title: FINANCE HR COORDINATOR - SYRIA
body:
**Position name:** Finance HR Coordinator  
**Duration**: 12 months renewable  
**Starting from**: ASAP  
**Duty Station**: Syria, Damascus, Aleppo, Amuda  
**Closing date of the vacancy**: 26/10/2026  
**Monthly gross salary**: 2.900-3.200

**Context Presentation**:  
Un Ponte Per (UPP) is an Italian NGO established in 1991. It started its activities as “Un ponte per Baghdad”, in the aftermath of the first Gulf war, with the aim of organizing solidarity initiatives in support of the Iraqi civilian population. In subsequent years, UPP missions expanded to include Serbia and other Middle Eastern and Mediterranean countries. The NGO aims at preventing armed conflicts, protecting human rights and supporting local civil society, especially in the Middle East, by promoting the nexus between its humanitarian, peacebuilding and development programs.

Since 2015, UPP has been one of the leading INGOs in the North East Syria (NES) response. Providing humanitarian aid and capacity building of local actors in Health and Protection as well as environmental health, including waste management. In partnership with local partners, UPP has been able to develop a comprehensive system of health services delivered in 26 facilities, including mobile units, hospitals, primary health care centres, and an ambulance network. For further information please refer to our website: [www.unponteper.it/en/](https://www.unponteper.it/en/)

**Tasks**

**Finance and administration**

- Definition of the financial strategy for the mission together with the Head of Mission/Country Representative and in collaboration with the technical referent at HQ
- Coordinate and supervise general cash and accounts of the mission
- Ensure and enforce compliance with the organization Anti-Fraud, Anti-Terrorism, Anti-Corruption policies and local financial laws and provisions
- Ensure proper implementation and respect of organization policies and guidelines, design or adapt relevant local policies, procedures and tools for optimized management of the mission financial resources
- Support HQ Administration department in preparing country’s yearly financial forecast of mission (staff, running, shared and indirect costs) and annual budget
- Support Head of mission/Country Representative in elaborating and consolidating the annual accounting of the mission and the report to the relevant authorities and donors
- Support external and internal audits
- Oversee banking relationships and signatory responsibilities delegated
- Monitor the overall financial management of the mission
- Is responsible for coordinating and ensuring effective treasury management for the smooth running of operations, while maintaining appropriate controls to mitigate security risks. Identify and promptly flag financial shortfalls or overspending in the mission's financial management and propose corrective measures.
- Ensure compliance with general accounting and project financial management principles, as well as with UPP's anti-fraud, anti-corruption and anti-terrorism policies and procedures.
- Provide training, orientation and tutoring for finance and logistics staff and partners where necessary and/or requested
- Assess and mitigate the financial risks on the mission, ensure that reliable internal control systems are in place, and financial ethics is respected
- Check that the administrative procedures related to taxes and payment of social security obligations are followed, and comply with established legal procedures in the country
- Monitor the payment of suppliers and staff salaries

**HR management**

- Together with the Senior Management Team (SMT) and the field managers, plan HR operational and budget needs, in order to efficiently ensure the required sizing and capabilities of the mission
- Support the coordination team and managers in the recruitment processes, ensuring a coherent management of administrative and legal procedures (recruitment, end of contract, payment of national and local taxes, proper upkeep of personnel files, management of extra hours and leaves, etc.), all across the mission in order to meet resources needs
- Support the Senior Management Team (SMT) and the field managers in detecting training needs according to operational requirements, in evaluating people’s performance and in implementing the associated action plans to improve people capabilities
- Is responsible for training and coaching all HR staff in the mission on the key Human Resources pillars, policies, procedures, and practices, as well as raising awareness among key management staff, including coordinators, on HR responsibilities, risks, and good practices
- Define and coordinate the local implementation, in accordance to UPP practices and local regulations, of a fair rewarding policy in order to ensure internal equity
- Coordinate the implementation of local HR administrative protocols and procedures, ensuring compliance with UPP policies and applicable legislation; monitor and mitigate related legal, compliance and operational risks, provide regular information and briefings to personnel, coordinators and managers, supervise expatriate administrative processes, and support management in addressing staff conflicts.
- Ensure the effective implementation of UPP's HR strategy and standards across the mission, adapting them where necessary to the local context and applicable legislation.
- Provide support and guidance to line management in handling staff (expat or national staff) conflicts
- Coordinate and oversee the preparation of the monthly payroll, ensuring accuracy and compliance with applicable local legislation on salaries, taxation and social security contributions.

**REQUIREMENTS**

- Essential degree in Economics/Finances/HR management, Psychology, International Relations, Political Science. Master in HR Management desirable
- Essential 3 years’ experience in Finance and HR Management with at least 2 in HR managerial positions in humanitarian contexts with NGOs
- Excellent oral and written English essential
- Essential computer literacy (word, excel and internet)
- Experience of financial reporting and grant management with a range of external donors using Excel and administrative software
- Financial management skills and knowledge of finance systems and procedures
- Strategic vision
- Leadership
- Team building and cooperation
- People management
- Ability to work in multicultural environment
- Non-discriminatory attitude
- Active listening and empathy
- Behavioural flexibility and stress management
- Planning
- Desirable experience in main donors funded project (EU, UN, USAID, AICS, CDCS etc.)
- Desirable knowledge of the Middle East context and relevant local actors
- Desirable knowledge of Arabic or Italian
- Ability to travel in Middle East and in Europe

**UPP requires criminal background check certificate (released max 3 months before the date of job offer) to confirm a job offer. We are aware that in some countries the release of criminal background certificate by the competent authorities might require several weeks. However, UPP runs selections to deploy staff in emergency programs and time-lapse between job offer and field deployment is often very short. Thus, we kindly ask all candidates to get prepared on time and be able to submit their certificate promptly in case of success in the selection.**

Un Ponte Per is an International NGO committed to diversity and inclusion within its teams, in line with the principle of non-discrimination. UPP encourages all candidates irrespective of gender, religion and ethnicity including persons with disabilities to apply and become part of the organization.

***Ethical Conduct & Safeguarding***

*UPP takes a **zero-tolerance** approach to any form of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (SEAH), Child Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation, and Physical/Emotional Harm, including online abuse, and is committed to recruiting only those suitable to work with children and the communities we serve. As a participant in the* [*Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme (MDS)*](https://misconduct-disclosure-scheme.org/)*, UPP systematically requests information from previous employers on any substantiated findings of SEAH or serious breaches of child safeguarding, reserves the right to contact any organisation a candidate has worked for, and requests data on investigations ongoing at the time of their departure. All posts are subject to vetting checks including criminal records disclosure and screening against anti-terrorism, anti-money-laundering, anti-corruption, and anti-fraud sanctions lists. Shortlisted candidates must provide a criminal background check certificate issued no more than three months before the job offer; candidates are encouraged to obtain this in advance as processing times vary. By submitting an application, candidates confirm their understanding of these procedures, authorise UPP to conduct all mandatory inquiries, declare that they have never committed or been subject to findings of SEAH or Child Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation, or Physical/Emotional Harm. All selected candidates are expected to work in accordance with UPP's Code of Conduct and all PSEAH and Child Safeguarding policies. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.*

title: Data Enumerator (DTM)
body:
Overview of position

Collect data and under the overall guidance of the DTM Program Officer, the technical supervision of the Senior Program Associate/ Project Assistant (Operations) and the direct supervision of the Team Leader, the successful candidate will be accountable and responsible for collecting data as part of the DTM mobility tracking, registration, flow monitoring points, surveys and among other tools and tasks. S / he will work in close collaboration with the field teams and partners in the areas (s) s/he has been assigned to. S/he will perform the under-listed functions, not limited to the following: provide support to relevant partners on data collection based on the DTM methodology and tools, following a pre-established schedule.

Role objectives

- Collect data and provide support to relevant partners on data collection based on the DTM methodology and tools, following a pre-established schedule.
- Maintain high-grade quality work and accountability during data collection/ interviews and/or entries by ensuring integrity and credibility.
- Monitor and evaluate the DTM operations in the field and identify areas of improvement and enhanced efficiency.
- Triangulating collected data based on DTM methodology with relevant partners.
- Responsible for sending the information collected in the field to the Team Leader/ Project Assistant promptly and according to the standards and requirements of the DTM program.
- Carry out rapid registration, other assessments, and surveys where needed.
- Ensure confidentiality and ethical consideration in line with the our client data protection principles and the humanitarian principles of do no harm.
- Promote effective partnership by collaborating with DTM partners in the field during data collection, including our client staff, to achieve shared goals and optimise results.
- Ensure respect, promote individual and cultural differences, encourage diversity, maintain high ethical standards, and act consistently with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- Work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercise careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges, including the flexibility to be deployed or redeployed on short notice deemed necessary.

Project reporting

This role will work under the overall guidance of the DTM Program Officer, the technical supervision of the Senior Program Associate / Project Assistant (Operations) and the direct supervision of the Team Leader

Key competencies

- Certificate / Diploma / Degree in relevant field.
- Minimum of two years for a University Diploma or one year for a degree.
- Experience in the field of humanitarian assistance is an advantage
- Experience in data collection and statistics is an advantage.
- Experience in the humanitarian field, NGO, or INGO is mandatory.
- Demonstrated ability to maintain integrity in performing responsibilities assigned.
- Trusted by the community, with certain maturity in making decisions, widely accepted and respected.
- Possess good leadership skills and the ability to explain instructions clearly.
- Respect and promote individual and cultural differences and encourage diversity.
- Integrity and transparency maintain high ethical standards and act in a manner consistent with organizational principles / rules and standards of conduct.
- The ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- Teamwork: develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimise results.
- Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner; is action-oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own action and delegated work.
- Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication; explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

Team management

The role has no managerial responsibility.

Further information

- Qualified female candidates are encouraged to apply for this role.
- Applicants with knowledge of the local context, terrain, language and culture are desirable
- Applicants with special needs who meet the requirement will be given due consideration
- The position on Call/Hourly

title: ICT END USER HW/SW SUPPORT (Network, Voice & Security (Cisco CUCM / Check Point)
body:

title: Liaison & Security Officer -Damascus
body:
**Background/Context:**

The IRC has operated in Syria since 2012, providing protection, health, economic recovery, and early childhood development programs in Idleb, Aleppo, Ar-Raqqa, Hasakeh, and Deir ez-Zor, with new programs expanding into Hama, rural Damascus, and Homs. With a team of over 350 members, the IRC has established trust and strong community relationships, ensuring access and effective service delivery.

Our longstanding experience in the country to date provides a strong foundation for the IRC to further adapt and expand its programming across Syria, to respond to the new realities – with a greater focus on resilience and recovery initiatives. Alongside this, the IRC also plays a significant role in Syria’s NGO, donor, and coordination forums, holding key positions and actively engaging in advocacy efforts.

 **Job overview:**

The Liaison and Security Officer, under the supervision of the Senior Humanitarian Access and Security Coordinator, serves as IRC’s focal point with relevant national and local authorities in Central and South Syria, support the SHASC to ensure organizational compliance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements, maintain registration status, secure timely governmental approvals, and facilitate sustained operational and programmatic access across IRC’s areas of implementation, and ensures that IRC activities are conducted in accordance with government regulations while upholding IRC’s humanitarian principles, organizational policies, and duty of care obligations. The Liaison and Security Officer is also responsible for supporting security management for IRC staff, premises, and assets in Central and South of Syria, ensuring compliance with IRC minimum security standards, contributing to security risk mitigation measures, and providing support to security incident reporting, response, and follow‑up processes.

**Responsibilities:**

## 1. Government Liaison & Humanitarian Access

- Under the supervision of the SHASC, act as IRC’s focal point with relevant Syrian ministries (e.g., Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Social Affairs and Labor) and local authorities across Central and South Syria.
- Support the SHASC to ensure timely renewal and maintenance of IRC registration, operational licenses, and other legal documentation required to operate in Syria.
- Ensure the submission, tracking, and follow-up of program approvals, activity permissions, and official correspondence with authorities in Central and South Syria.
- Establish and maintain effective, trust-based relationships with government counterparts and relevant external stakeholders.
- Support the SHASC to facilitate and coordinate visits of IRC visitors, senior management, and donors, including securing approvals and movement permissions.
- Support IRC staff movements through airports and official border crossing points, ensuring smooth entry and exit procedures.
- Under supervision of the SHASC, coordinate with IRC legal Representative and relevant authorities to obtain and renew visas for international staff and official visitors.
- Build and maintain professional relationships with key national and sub-national authorities to support sustained access and collaboration.
- Maintain a structured calendar and tracking system for approvals, renewals, registrations, and compliance deadlines.
- Ensure all official correspondence, permits, approvals, and meeting records are properly documented and securely archived.
- Monitor changes in Syrian laws, regulations, decrees, and administrative procedures affecting INGOs.

## 2. Security Risk Management 

- Conduct Premises Risk Assessments for IRC offices, guesthouses, and program implementation sites across Central and South Syria.
- Support the SHASC to review, updating and developing the Security Risk Assessment (SRAs) for IRC areas of operations across Central and South Syria.
- Support the review and updating of the Security Management Plan (SMP), SOPs, and contingency plans (hibernation, relocation, evacuation) in line with contextual changes.
- Conduct follow-up security visits to IRC premises and field locations to ensure compliance with security standards.
- Under supervision of the SHASC, develop, update, and test office and facility evacuation plans, including practical drills where feasible.
- Prepare and deliver security briefings for newly joined staff and visitors; ensure pre-arrival and on-arrival security documentation is relevant to the context.
- Ensure all security incidents are reported on time and all incident reports are submitted on IRC’s online reporting system.
- Support the SHASC to ensure IRC premises are equipped with appropriate safety and security equipment (fire extinguishers, first aid kits, emergency signage, etc.), and follow up with Supply Chain on fire, health, and vehicle safety issues.
- Monitor political, social, economic, media, and military developments relevant to security and access, and report to SHASC.
- Oversee and monitor visitor movements, including airport and Land BCPs pick-ups and drop-offs, and maintain up-to-date visitor tracking records.
- Maintain a structured tracking system for all IRC International Staff and IRC visitors.

## 3. Internal Coordination & Reporting

- Under supervision of the SHASC, work closely with program, field, Supply Chain, HR, and Finance teams to ensure all planned activities are legally cleared and aligned with government requirements.
- Provide regular written and verbal updates to the SHASC on access, registration, legal compliance, and security developments.

## 4. Staff Management & Team Oversight

- Recruit, supervise, and manage receptionists and security guards across Central and South Syria.
- Set clear objectives, provide regular feedback, and conduct performance reviews in line with IRC performance management standards.
- Support the SHASC to develop and implement capacity-building and on-the-job learning plans for direct reports.
- Ensure effective time, attendance, and leave management, and adequate staffing coverage at all times.
- Promote staff care, well-being, and adherence to duty of care principles.
- Address performance or conduct issues in coordination with Human Resources, in line with IRC policies.

 **Job Requirements:**

**Education:**

University degree in a relevant field such as law, public administration, international relations, security management, or related discipline. Equivalent professional experience will be considered.

 **Work Experience:**

- 2–3 years of relevant experience in liaison, government relations, legal affairs, access, and/or security roles with international NGOs, UN agencies, or diplomatic missions.
- 1-2 years of experience managing and supervising staff.
- Demonstrated experience working with Syrian authorities and navigating regulatory and administrative processes.
- Proven experience supporting security risk management, including SRAs, SMPs, SOPs, and contingency planning.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- A commitment to IRC’s mission, vision, values, and IRC Way – Professional Code of Conduct.
- High level of discretion, integrity, and cultural sensitivity.
- Credible written, presentation, and verbal communication skills; ability to convey information effectively and solid experience providing training and staff development.
- Validated sense of professional discretion, integrity, and ability to handle complex situations diplomatically and to achieve effective resolution.
- Excellent management and social skills and a proven ability to promote harmonious/cohesive teamwork across departments.
- Validated ability to plan long-term, organize priorities, and work under administrative and programmatic pressures with detail orientation and professional perseverance.
- Highly collaborative and resourceful; ability to establish positive working relationships with senior-level management and all other partners to improve collaboration and productivity.
- Curiosity, a desire to continually learn and develop.

**Language/Travel:**

- Fluent Arabic and English: Professional working proficiency
- Travel: 20% to field sites.

 **Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Senior Humanitarian Access and Security Coordinator  
**Position directly supervises:** Receptionists and Guards in Central and South Syria  
**Key Internal Contacts:** SeniorField Managers – Humanitarian Access and Security Manager

**Key External Contacts:** other non-governmental organizations

**Professional Standards:** IRC staff must adhere to the values and principles outlined in IRC Way – Global Standards for Professional Conduct. These are Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality. In accordance with these values, IRC operates and carries out policies on Beneficiary Protection from Exploitation and Abuse, Child Safeguarding, Anti-Workplace Harassment, Respect at Work Fiscal Integrity, and Anti-Retaliation.

**Returning National Candidates:** We strongly encourage national or returning national candidates to apply for this position. If you are a citizen of the country where this position is based and are currently residing outside of your home country, you may be eligible for an attractive relocation package. Eligibility is determined based on IRC's operational needs and specific role requirements. IRC strives to attract, motivate, and retain qualified national staff in our programs.

**Accountability to Clients:** IRC staff must adhere to the commitment of contributing to the sustainability and development of its (CR) Client Responsiveness Mechanisms, preserving the culture of prioritizing the needs of our clients and affected communities by systematically listening to their perspectives and using their feedback to make programmatic decisions and give them greater influence over program design and delivery.

title: Protection Officer (PRoL)-Daraa
body:
**Background/IRC Summary:** The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview/Summary:** The Protection Officer (PRoL) is responsible for overseeing the day-to-day implementation and technical quality of integrated protection programming delivered through partner organizations in Daraa and other assigned locations. The position has a primary focus on Protection and Rule of Law (PRoL) interventions, including legal awareness, legal assistance, civil documentation support, housing, land and property (HLP) issues, referrals, and community-based protection activities, while also supporting the quality and effective implementation of Child Protection (CP) and Women’s Protection and Empowerment (WPE) interventions delivered by partners.

The Protection Officer serves as the primary technical focal point for partner field teams, providing ongoing coaching, mentoring, capacity building, and technical guidance to ensure services are delivered in accordance with IRC standards, donor requirements, and international protection principles. The role includes conducting regular field visits, monitoring service quality, verifying program data and documentation, identifying implementation gaps, and working collaboratively with partners to strengthen program performance and accountability.

The Protection Officer supports the establishment and strengthening of community-based protection mechanisms, promotes meaningful participation of affected populations, and ensures that vulnerable individuals are safely identified and referred to appropriate services. The position works closely with partner staff, community structures, and IRC technical teams to promote integrated protection outcomes, strengthen referral pathways, enhance service quality, and ensure that protection interventions effectively address the needs of women, girls, boys, men, and individuals with specific needs.

The position also contributes to strengthening partner capacity, quality assurance processes, project reporting, coordination with stakeholders, and continuous improvement of protection programming to ensure the effective and accountable delivery of services across all project locations.

**Major Responsibilities:** Major responsibilities of the **Community-based Protection Officer** (not exhaustive) are listed below:

- Lead the day-to-day technical support and oversight of Protection and Rule of Law (PRoL) activities implemented through partners, ensuring adherence to IRC technical standards, donor requirements, and international protection principles.
- Support partners in the implementation of legal awareness, legal information dissemination, HLP-related activities, civil documentation support, protection advocacy, and referral services.
- Provide technical guidance to partner staff on protection case management principles, safe identification, referrals, protection mainstreaming, confidentiality, and survivor-centered approaches.
- Support the implementation and quality assurance of Child Protection (CP) and Women’s Protection and Empowerment (WPE) activities delivered by partners, ensuring compliance with sector standards and quality benchmarks.
- Ensure that integrated protection approaches are applied across all project interventions and that protection risks are systematically identified and addressed.
- Accompany partner teams during field visits and service delivery activities to provide mentoring, coaching, and technical support.

**Community Protection Systems Strengthening & Sustainability**

- Assess partner capacity gaps and develop capacity-strengthening plans in coordination with relevant technical coordinators and managers.
- Deliver training, coaching, mentoring, and on-the-job capacity-building for partner staff on PRoL, CP, WPE, safeguarding, protection mainstreaming, referrals, and case management principles.
- Facilitate regular technical review meetings with partner teams to discuss challenges, lessons learned, and corrective actions.
- Support partners in developing action plans to improve service quality and ensure timely implementation of recommendations.
- Support sustainable capacity strengthening and knowledge transfer initiatives to enhance partners’ long-term ability to deliver quality protection services independently.

**Referral & Coordination Oversight**

1. Oversee referral pathways to ensure effectiveness, continuity, and proper coordination with partners and service providers.
2. Work closely with the partner to ensure gradual handover of responsibilities and knowledge transfer.

**Data Validation, Compliance & Reporting**

1. Verify beneficiary data and ensure its accuracy and reliability.
2. Manage documentation and achieving in line with donor requirements.
3. Prepare impact reports, closure reports, and ensure full compliance with donor regulations and requirements.

**Program Closure & Transition Planning**

1. Support final evaluations and lessons learned exercises.
2. Lead or contribute to closure planning, ensuring safe and structured transition of activities to partners or communities.
3. Ensuring protection mainstreaming is integrated across remaining program activities.
4. **General**

- Perform any other duties as required by program needs or as requested by the supervisor.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- **Position Reports to:** Protection Senior Manager.
- **Position directly supervises:** Protection field staff – local partner activities.
- **Indirect Reporting:** IP Coordinator.
- **Other Internal and/or external contacts:**
- ***Internal:*** Protection Officers, Health team, WPE, and CP teams, ERD team. IP senior managers, IP Coordinator.
- ***External:*** INGOs, local actors, and local authorities.

 **Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- A bachelor's degree in social work, international relations, human rights, community development, or any other university degree.

***Work Experience:***

- Proven experience 2-4 yearsin Protection, PRoL, legal assistance, civil documentation, case management, or related humanitarian programming.
- Experience working with NGOs and implementing programs through partner organizations.
- Experience in providing technical support, coaching, and capacity strengthening to staff and partners.
- Experience in field monitoring, quality assurance, reporting, and compliance with donor and organizational standards.
- Knowledge of Child Protection (CP), Women’s Protection and Empowerment (WPE), referral pathways, and protection principles.
- Strong understanding of the Syrian humanitarian context and commitment to protection, inclusion, and gender equality.

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Strong management and organizational skills.
- Excellent time management skills and ability to meet deadlines.
- Strong communication, negotiation and persuasion skills
- Good interpersonal skills and ability to work as part of a team, as well as independently.
- Flexible and able to work in a dynamic and diverse environment.
- Experience in regular report writing.
- Good interpersonal skills and ability to work as part of a team, as well as independently.
- Flexible and able to work in a dynamic and diverse environment.
- Must be computer literate (Microsoft Word and Excel).

***Language Skills:***

- Arabic & English are required
- Travel: If requested

**Professional Standards:** IRC staff must adhere to the values and principles outlined in IRC Way – Global Standards for Professional Conduct. These are Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality. In accordance with these values, IRC operates and carries out policies on Beneficiary Protection from Exploitation and Abuse, Child Safeguarding, Anti-Workplace Harassment, Respect at Work Fiscal Integrity, and Anti-Retaliation.

**Returning National Candidates:** We strongly encourage national or returning national candidates to apply for this position. If you are a citizen of the Country in which this position is based and are currently located outside of your home country and possess over two years of international work experience, the Middle East Region has introduced an attractive remuneration package. The package includes competitive compensation, return flight to post, shipping allowance, temporary housing and a relocation allowance. Certain restrictions may apply. IRC strives to attract, motivate and retain qualified national staff in our programs.

**Accountability to Clients:** IRC staff must adhere to the commitment of contributing to the sustainability and development of its (CR) Client Responsiveness Mechanisms, preserving the culture of prioritizing the needs of our clients and affected communities by systematically listening to their perspectives and using their feedback to make programmatic decisions and give them greater influence over program design and delivery.

**Gender Equality:** IRC is committed to narrowing the gender gap in leadership positions. We offer benefits that provide an enabling environment for women to participate in our workforce including parental leave, gender-sensitive security protocols and other supportive benefits and allowances.

**Diversity and Inclusion:** at IRC MENA, we are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity. Organizations that are diverse in age, gender identity, race, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, ethnicity, nationality, and perspective are validated to be better organizations. More importantly, creating a safe workspace environment where everyone, from any background, can do their best is the right thing to do. So, bring your whole self to work.

title: Protection Officer (Child Protection)-Homs
body:
**Background/IRC Summary:** The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview/Summary:** The protection Officer (Child Protection) is responsible for overseeing the day-to-day implementation and technical quality of Child Protection programming delivered through partner organizations in Daraa and other assigned locations. The position has a primary focus on Child Protection interventions, including case management, psychosocial support, community-based child protection, safe identification and referral, parenting and caregiver support, and child safeguarding, while also supporting the quality and effective implementation of Women’s Protection and Empowerment (WPE) and Protection and Rule of Law (PRoL) interventions delivered by partners.

The Child Protection Officer serves as the primary technical focal point for partner field teams, providing ongoing coaching, mentoring, capacity building, and technical guidance to ensure services are delivered in accordance with IRC standards, donor requirements, child safeguarding principles, and international protection standards. The role includes conducting regular field visits, monitoring service quality, verifying program data and documentation, identifying implementation gaps, and working collaboratively with partners to strengthen program performance and accountability.

The Child Protection Officer supports the establishment and strengthening of community-based child protection mechanisms, promotes meaningful participation of children, caregivers, and communities, and ensures that vulnerable children are safely identified and referred to appropriate services. The position works closely with partner staff, community structures, and IRC technical teams to strengthen referral pathways, improve service quality, and ensure that protection interventions effectively address the needs of children and their caregivers while contributing to integrated protection outcomes.

The position also contributes to strengthening partner capacity, quality assurance processes, project reporting, coordination with stakeholders, and continuous improvement of protection programming to ensure the effective and accountable delivery of services across all project locations.

**Major Responsibilities:** Major responsibilities of the **Protection Officer** (Child Protection) are listed below:

- Lead the day-to-day technical support and oversight of Child Protection activities implemented through partners, ensuring adherence to IRC technical standards, donor requirements, and child protection principles.
- Support partners in the implementation of child protection case management, psychosocial support activities, parenting and caregiver support initiatives, community-based child protection mechanisms, and child safeguarding interventions.
- Provide technical guidance to partner staff on case management principles, best interests’ procedures, safe identification, referrals, confidentiality, child safeguarding, and mainstreaming protection.
- Support the implementation and quality assurance of WPE and PRoL activities delivered by partners to ensure integrated protection programming and effective referral pathways.
- Ensure that child protection risks are systematically identified, monitored, and addressed through project interventions.
- Accompany partner teams during field visits and service delivery activities to provide mentoring, coaching, and technical support.

**Community Protection Systems Strengthening & Sustainability**

- Assess partner capacity gaps and develop capacity-strengthening plans in coordination with relevant technical coordinators and managers.
- Deliver training, coaching, mentoring, and on-the-job capacity-building for partner staff on CP, safeguarding, case management, referrals, protection mainstreaming, and integrated protection approaches.
- Facilitate regular technical review meetings with partner teams to discuss challenges, lessons learned, and corrective actions.
- Support partners in developing action plans to improve service quality and ensure timely implementation of recommendations.
- Support sustainable capacity strengthening and knowledge transfer initiatives to enhance partners’ long-term ability to deliver quality protection services independently.

**Referral & Coordination Oversight**

1. Oversee referral pathways to ensure effectiveness, continuity, and proper coordination with partners and service providers.
2. Work closely with the partner to ensure gradual handover of responsibilities and knowledge transfer.

**Data Validation, Compliance & Reporting**

1. Verify beneficiary data and ensure its accuracy and reliability.
2. Manage documentation and achieving in line with donor requirements.
3. Prepare impact reports, closure reports, and ensure full compliance with donor regulations and requirements.

**Program Closure & Transition Planning**

1. Support final evaluations and lessons learned exercises.
2. Lead or contribute to closure planning, ensuring safe and structured transition of activities to partners or communities.
3. Ensuring protection mainstreaming is integrated across remaining program activities.

**General**

- Perform any other duties as required by program needs or as requested by the supervisor.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- **Position Reports to:** Protection Senior Manager (Child Protection).
- **Position directly supervises:** IRC’s activities and field staff – local partner activities.
- **Indirect Reporting:** IP Coordinator.
- **Other Internal and/or external contacts:**
- ***Internal:*** Protection Officers, IP Coordinator, WPE, and CP teams, ERD team. IP senior managers, and Health team.
- ***External:*** INGOs, local actors, and Local authorities.

 **Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- A bachelor's degree in social work, international relations, human rights, community development, or any other university degree.

***Work Experience:***

- Proven experience2-4 years in Child Protection, case management, psychosocial support, child safeguarding, or related humanitarian programming.
- Experience working with NGOs and implementing programs through partner organizations.
- Experience in providing technical support, coaching, and capacity strengthening to staff and partners.
- Experience in field monitoring, quality assurance, reporting, and compliance with donor and organizational standards.
- Knowledge of Women’s Protection and Empowerment (WPE), Protection and Rule of Law (PRoL), referral pathways, and protection principles.
- Strong understanding of the Syrian humanitarian context and commitment to child protection, inclusion, and gender equality.

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Strong management and organizational skills.
- Excellent time management skills and ability to meet deadlines.
- Strong communication, negotiation and persuasion skills
- Good interpersonal skills and ability to work as part of a team, as well as independently.
- Flexible and able to work in a dynamic and diverse environment.
- Experience in regular report writing.
- Good interpersonal skills and ability to work as part of a team, as well as independently.
- Flexible and able to work in a dynamic and diverse environment.
- Must be computer literate (Microsoft Word and Excel).

***Language Skills:***

- Arabic & English are required.
- Travel: If requested

**Professional Standards:** IRC staff must adhere to the values and principles outlined in IRC Way – Global Standards for Professional Conduct. These are Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality. In accordance with these values, IRC operates and carries out policies on Beneficiary Protection from Exploitation and Abuse, Child Safeguarding, Anti-Workplace Harassment, Respect at Work Fiscal Integrity, and Anti-Retaliation.

**Returning National Candidates:** We strongly encourage national or returning national candidates to apply for this position. If you are a citizen of the Country in which this position is based and are currently located outside of your home country and possess over two years of international work experience, the Middle East Region has introduced an attractive remuneration package. The package includes competitive compensation, return flight to post, shipping allowance, temporary housing and a relocation allowance. Certain restrictions may apply. IRC strives to attract, motivate and retain qualified national staff in our programs.

**Accountability to Clients:** IRC staff must adhere to the commitment of contributing to the sustainability and development of its (CR) Client Responsiveness Mechanisms, preserving the culture of prioritizing the needs of our clients and affected communities by systematically listening to their perspectives and using their feedback to make programmatic decisions and give them greater influence over program design and delivery.

**Gender Equality:** IRC is committed to narrowing the gender gap in leadership positions. We offer benefits that provide an enabling environment for women to participate in our workforce including parental leave, gender-sensitive security protocols and other supportive benefits and allowances.

**Diversity and Inclusion:** at IRC MENA, we are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity. Organizations that are diverse in age, gender identity, race, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, ethnicity, nationality, and perspective are validated to be better organizations. More importantly, creating a safe workspace environment where everyone, from any background, can do their best is the right thing to do. So, bring your whole self to work.

IRC is committed to creating a diverse, inclusive, respectful and safe work environment where all persons are treated fairly, with dignity and respect. In keeping with our core values of Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality, IRC strives to maintain a work environment built on mutual respect in which all individuals treat each other professionally, and free of bias, prejudice, and harassment. IRC expressly prohibits and will not tolerate discrimination, harassment, retaliation, or bullying of IRC Persons in any work setting. All IRC staff, wherever they are located, are accountable for creating an environment free of discrimination, harassment, bullying, and retaliation.

title: DIRECTRICE GÉNÉRALE OU DIRECTEUR GÉNÉRAL - FRANCE
body:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Rattaché·e à la Présidence, vous dirigez l'exécutif d'ACF France et animez le comité exécutif. Cette équipe regroupe actuellement les directions des opérations, de l'expertise et du plaidoyer, de la communication et du développement, administrative et financière, des ressources humaines, de la logistique, des systèmes d'information, et de l'audit, des risques et de la conformité, ainsi que l'unité stratégie et transformation. Vous êtes appuyé par des chargé·es de mission et une assistante de direction. Cette organisation est appelée à évoluer dans le cadre de la réorganisation globale qui a été engagée.  
Veiller au bon fonctionnement du lien avec la gouvernance associative: vous assurez l'articulation entre le CA et l'exécutif, participez aux réunions, aux temps forts de la vie associative et présentez chaque année les accomplissements de l'association.  
Fédérer l'équipe de direction : vous animez le comité exécutif, favorisez la prise de décision collégiale et accompagnez le développement de ses membres.  
Porter le cap stratégique : vous proposez au CA un plan d'action pluriannuel conforme aux orientations stratégiques, en pilotez la mise en oeuvre.  
Sécuriser les grands équilibres financiers : vous veillez au respect et à la viabilité du modèle économique , vous assurez le pilotage de la trajectoire financière et contrôlez la stabilité de la trésorerie au niveau global.  
Conduire la transformation : vous menez à bien la transformation organisationnelle engagée avec les équipes, en capitalisant sur le travail accompli et en l'ajustant lorsque nécessaire.  
Représenter Action contre la Faim : vous portez la parole de l'association auprès des partenaires, des bailleurs, des médias et des organisations internationales.  
Incarner ACF France au sein du réseau international : vous coordonnez l'action d'ACF France avec les membres du réseau et veillez au respect des valeurs et principes communs, à la cohérence des opérations, et des actions de plaidoyer ainsi qu'à la réputation d'ACF.  
Prendre soin du collectif : attentif·ve aux personnes, vous portez une culture managériale fondée sur la responsabilisation et la confiance. Vous entretenez l'engagement et une dynamique collective positive, y compris à distance, et conduisez un dialogue social avec les instances représentatives du personnel.  
Garantir la sécurité et la conformité : vous pilotez la gestion des crises et assumez la responsabilité légale de l'organisation.

  
Profile :

 Vous avez une solide expérience en ONG, en partie acquise sur le terrain. Vous avez dirigé une entité de grande envergure, en tant que DG ou directeur·rice pays, et avez exercé au sein d'une association en France. Une expérience au sein d'ACF serait un atout.  
Vous connaissez le fonctionnement des associations en France, notamment en matière de gouvernance et de dialogue social.  
Reconnu·e pour votre vision stratégique et votre capacité d'anticipation, vous analysez les évolutions géopolitiques et leurs effets sur l'action humanitaire.  
Vous avez déjà conduit une transformation organisationnelle et accompagné les équipes dans le changement.  
Doté·e d'un leadership fédérateur, vous portez une culture managériale fondée sur la responsabilisation. Vous savez animer une équipe de direction, décider en collectif et trancher lorsque la situation l'exige, avec courage, écoute et empathie.  
Vous vous exprimez avec aisance, y compris face aux médias.  
Solide, humble et optimiste, vous faites preuve d'endurance et de persévérance.  
Vous avez une parfaite maîtrise du français et de l'anglais.  
  
  
Conditions d'emploi  
  
Statut : Cadre dirigeant  
Lieu : Montreuil (Seine-Saint-Denis)  
Rémunération :De 87K à 100Keuros bruts annuels sur 13 mois selon expérience  
Avantages:30 jours par an de CP  
Couverture santé: Prise en charge à 80% par ACF  
Indemnités Transport : prise en charge à 50% du forfait entre le domicile et le lieu de travail  
Indemnités  
Tickets-restaurant: prise en charge à 60% par l'association pour une valeur de 8euros  
Ouvres sociales  
Télétravail :ACF dispose d'une politique de télétravail ouverte, depuis le territoire métropolitain.  
Une présence au siège de 8 jours/ mois est requise pour ce poste.  
Des temps de présence collective sont fixés par l'employeur pour les réunions collectives, jusqu'à 3 jours par mois.  
Une présence continue au siège sera requise pendant la période d'intégration.  
Indemnités de télétravail.  
Le poste implique des déplacements réguliers en France et à l'étranger.  
ACF s'engage pour les personnes en situation de handicap et lutte activement contre toutes les formes de discrimination.  
Cette offre d'emploi vous intéresse ?  
Ce recrutement est confié au cabinet Humanitalents, mandaté par ACF. Toutes les candidatures seront traitées dans la plus stricte confidentialité.   
Postulez par email à recrutement\[a\]humanitalents.com en précisant la référence DG/ACF en objet avant le 31/10/2026.

title: Caseworker Assistant
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position has an end date of 30 September 2027.***

**Job Overview:**

The Program for Initial Resettlement Caseworker Assistant supports refugee and other ORR-eligible populations during their integration into the United States by assisting with service delivery, client support, documentation, transportation, and resource coordination. Working under the guidance of the Cash and Medical and Initial Resettlement Coordinator, the Caseworker Assistant helps ensure clients have access to essential services and resources while promoting self-sufficiency, stability, and successful community integration.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Assist in coordinating pre-arrival and post-arrival services to ensure clients receive essential support upon arrival.
- Support airport pickups, housing setup, food assistance, transportation arrangements, and community orientation activities.
- Assist clients with navigating community resources and accessing essential services.
- Conduct client intake and assessment activities to help identify household strengths, needs, and priorities.
- Develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and SMART goals in partnership with each client.
- Provide referrals and follow up on service connections, appointments, and action items.
- Support the distribution of direct assistance and program-related resources according to organizational and funder requirements.
- Maintain regular communication with assigned clients to support progress toward established goals.
- Document client interactions, services provided, referrals, and outcomes accurately and timely.
- Enter and maintain client records in ETO and other required databases.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:** Associate degree in Social Work, Human Services, or a related field preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- At least 2 years’ experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations strongly preferred.
- Experience providing customer service, case management support, or community outreach preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Ability to learn to navigate or familiarity with database systems such as IRIS and Efforts to Outcomes (ETO)
- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluency in English, both spoken and written; proficiency in language(s) spoken by IRC’s clients is desired;
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research and problem-solving purposes.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- Will require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** ($18.45). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Asistente de Protección Santa Bárbara del Zulia - Personal Nacional
body:
Danish Refugee Council (DRC) es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, en el marco de la respuesta de emergencia al terremoto, DRC está buscando un/a Oficial de Protección altamente calificado/a con sede en Santa Bárbara del Zulia, Venezuela.

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC administra sus operaciones en Venezuela bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela implementa actividades de monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para personas con necesidades específicas (PWSN), sesiones informativas para personas de interés (PoC), prevención de la trata de personas y seguridad alimentaria.

**Objetivo general del puesto:**

Bajo la supervisión del Líder de equipo de Protección (Zulia), el Asistente de Protección apoyará la implementación en terreno de todos los objetivos de protección bajo los proyectos de DRC. El Asistente de Protección desarrollará y mantendrá buenas relaciones con las personas de interés, las partes interesadas relevantes y otros actores humanitarios, para apoyar la implementación y coordinación adecuadas de las actividades de Protección de DRC que se desarrollarán en el área de intervención. Apoyar la implementación de enfoques diferenciales, especialmente de edad, género, y diversidad en las actividades de protección.

**Responsabilidades:**

- Contribuir eficientemente a la implementación del proyecto de protección en los municipios del sur del lago del estado Zulia de acuerdo con los objetivos acordados.
- Implementar periódica el Monitoreo de Protección en las comunidades de intervención, incluyendo el levantamiento de datos cuantitativos y cualitativos sobre necesidades/riesgos de protección mediante la aplicación de entrevistas a unidades familiares, grupos focales e informantes claves.
- Contribuir al fortalecimiento del enfoque de edad, género y diversidad en las acciones de y respuestas de protección.
- Apoyar en la identificación y documentación sistemáticamente las necesidades específicas y riesgos de protección de las personas más vulnerables en las comunidades de intervención –a través del Monitoreo de Protección, actividades informativas realizadas en las comunidades y otros medios— a fin de referir y/o brindar una repuesta oportuna a las personas de interés.
- Participar en el Comité de Asistencia de Protección Individual (IPA), y contribuir con los planes de respuestas que respondan a las necesidades específicas protección de los casos, y apoyar con los planes de entrega de las asistencias y/o remisiones a servicios especializados internos y/o externos.
- Manejar la información confidencial de manera correcta, de acuerdo con las políticas de protección de datos de DRC, gestionando los archivos de protección de manera precisa, correcta y completa.
- Apoyar en la recopilación de información para la elaboración de reportes, informes, e insumos productos del Monitoreo de Protección.
- Asegurar la más alta calidad de las intervenciones de protección y la coherencia entre todos los proyectos, en curso y propuestos, de acuerdo con la estrategia general.
- Apoyar en la orientación de las personas de interés según las rutas de protección, el mapeo de servicios y de los actores humanitarios e institucionales.
- Apoyar en la organización y facilitación de grupos focales y sesiones informativas sobre temas de protección.
- Apoyar y asistir en conjunto con la línea supervisora en el desarrollo de actividades legales conforme a los objetivos y metas.
- Participar bajo supervisión en el asesoramiento individual de las principales necesidades legales identificadas.
- Acompañar a los beneficiarios a instituciones públicas según sea necesario.
- Participar en espacios de formación y retroalimentación de las acciones de protección.
- Participar de manera colaborativa en las acciones del equipo de protección y otras áreas.
- Participar activamente a las reuniones de equipo proporcionando insumos, desafíos y lecciones aprendidas.
- Contribuir al desarrollo de herramientas de procedimiento operativos estándar.

**Programación y Operaciones**

- Asegurar la implementación eficiente y efectiva de las actividades programática asignadas, mientras el plan de trabajo.
- Apoyar en la preparación de informes y presupuestos mensuales.

**Experiencia y competencias:**

- Mínimo 1 año de experiencia relevante en protección humanitaria, trabajo social, derechos humanos u otro trabajo similar de terreno, relacionado a una ONG u otra organización sin fines de lucro.
- Experiencia de terreno y de trabajo con comunidades urbanas, y/o rurales, y/o indígenas.
- Experiencia y capacidad para entrevistar a personas de todas las edades, género y diversidad.
- Buenas habilidades para trabajar con tabletas y computadores.
- Buenas habilidades en MS Word y Excel.
- Voluntad y habilidad de aprender.

**Educación:**

Título Universitario pertinente en logística y / o gestión de la cadena de suministro o cualificación profesional equivalente.

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: 6 meses con disponibilidad de extensión según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda I.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.
- Contratación nacional.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**: actuar de acuerdo con la visión y los valores de DRC.

**Proceso de solicitud:** Todos los solicitantes deben cargar una carta de presentación (máx. 1 página) y un CV actualizado (**máx. 2 páginas, sin soportes**) en español, en la plataforma de empleo de DRC. Las solicitudes enviadas por correo electrónico no serán consideradas.
