title: Senior Case Management Officer
source: International Network For Aid Relief and Assistance
body:
**GENERAL INFORMATION**

Job Title : Senior Case Management Officer

Location : Ankara, Türkiye (On-site)

Job Type : Full-time

Contract Duration : The contract is for an initial period of **one (1) year**, with the possibility of extension depending on the availability of funding and the continued need for the role.

**ABOUT INARA:**

International Network for Aid, Relief and Assistance (INARA) is a U.S.-registered 501(c)(3) humanitarian organization founded in 2015 by Arwa Damon. Established in response to critical gaps in the humanitarian system, INARA works to support children affected by conflict, displacement, and natural and human-induced disasters who are often unable to access sustained medical and psychosocial care.

INARA delivers integrated, child-centered programming that combines life-saving interventions with long-term recovery support. The organization focuses on children facing complex and overlapping vulnerabilities, including injury, trauma, disability, and exclusion from essential services. Through a multidisciplinary approach, INARA provides access to medical treatment, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), and coordinated case management, ensuring continuity of care beyond the immediate emergency phase.

INARA delivers integrated, child-centered programming across multiple sectors to support children affected by crisis. Its interventions include comprehensive medical and rehabilitative care, providing specialized treatment and long-term follow-up; mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), offering trauma-informed and community-based services; and livelihood and economic empowerment initiatives that strengthen household stability. INARA also supports education in emergencies by creating safe and inclusive learning environments, implements water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) interventions to improve health conditions, and maintains a rapid emergency response capacity to deliver immediate medical, psychosocial, food, and non-food assistance during acute crises.

**Vision**

A world where every child has the agency to create a dignified life.

**Mission**

Fostering a future where we empower children to shape their own dignified lives.

**Purpose**

Enhancing children’s capacity to shape their own fulfilling futures through integrated health, empowerment, and community-driven interventions.

**JOB SUMMARY:**

The Senior Case Management Officer is responsible for supervising and supporting INARA’s case management and MHPSS staff in Türkiye while directly managing and following up medical cases in Ankara. The position ensures that children and their families receive coordinated, timely, safe, and high-quality support throughout assessment, treatment, recovery, and case closure. The role provides day-to-day supervision to Case Management Officers and MHPSS Officers, reviews case documentation and service quality, coordinates closely with hospitals and service providers, and maintains an active caseload in Ankara. The position also verifies hospital and treatment-related expenses against services received, reconciles case expenditures and cash advances with Finance, prepares donor-required case and program reports, and works with Partnerships/Program Management and Communications to ensure reporting, case stories, and communication materials are accurate, timely, and appropriately documented.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Case Management, Medical Follow-up & Care Coordination**

- Manage an active caseload of children receiving medical support in Ankara, ensuring continuous follow-up from intake and assessment through treatment, rehabilitation, recovery, referral, and case closure.
- Conduct and/or review comprehensive assessments of children’s medical, psychosocial, protection, social, and practical needs and develop individualized care plans in coordination with children, caregivers, medical providers, and relevant INARA staff.
- Coordinate appointments, diagnostics, procedures, hospitalization, rehabilitation, medication, referrals, transportation, and other treatment-related needs, and follow up with hospitals and service providers to ensure continuity and quality of care.
- Maintain regular contact with children and caregivers, provide practical guidance and support, explain treatment pathways and next steps, and ensure that changes in needs or treatment plans are communicated promptly.
- Advocate for children and families with hospitals, healthcare providers, social services, and other relevant actors to address barriers to care and secure appropriate services.
- Ensure timely identification and escalation of safeguarding, protection, medical, or psychosocial concerns in accordance with INARA policies and referral pathways.
- Ensure medical and MHPSS services are coordinated as part of an integrated, child-centered case management approach.

**Team Supervision, Technical Oversight & Quality Assurance**

- Provide direct day-to-day supervision to Case Management Officers and MHPSS Officers, ensuring clear work planning, appropriate caseload allocation, service coverage, and accountability.
- Conduct regular team meetings, individual supervision, case review sessions, and multidisciplinary discussions to monitor progress, address complex cases, and support sound case management decisions.
- Review case files, assessments, care plans, follow-up notes, referrals, service records, and closure documentation to ensure completeness, accuracy, confidentiality, and compliance with INARA standards.
- Monitor staff caseloads, case progress, service timelines, and follow-up actions, and intervene where delays, gaps, risks, or quality concerns are identified.
- Provide coaching, technical guidance, and practical support to staff; identify capacity-building needs and support learning and consistent application of case management and MHPSS procedures.
- Promote a supportive, respectful, and accountable team environment and ensure adherence to safeguarding, confidentiality, data protection, professional boundaries, and organizational policies.
- Coordinate with relevant managers on staff performance, workload, operational challenges, and corrective actions where required.

**Hospital & Service Provider Coordination**

- Establish and maintain effective working relationships with hospitals, doctors, rehabilitation providers, pharmacies, laboratories, and other service providers supporting INARA children.
- Confirm treatment plans, services delivered, follow-up requirements, and relevant medical documentation with providers, while maintaining appropriate confidentiality and informed consent.
- Review hospital invoices, treatment bills, and related medical expenses against the treatment and services actually received by each child, flagging discrepancies or unclear charges for clarification before processing.
- Support resolution of service delivery issues, appointment delays, documentation gaps, or billing discrepancies in coordination with hospitals, Finance, and relevant INARA colleagues.

**Case-related Financial Reconciliation & Cash Advances**

- Work closely with Finance on a regular basis to reconcile medical and case-related expenditures with approved treatment plans, supporting documents, and services received.
- Maintain clear records of treatment-related expenses and provide the programmatic and case documentation required to validate hospital, pharmacy, transportation, accommodation, and other approved day-to-day medical costs.
- Manage and clear cash advances received for children’s treatment and day-to-day medical expenses in a timely manner, ensuring that receipts and supporting documentation are complete and submitted in accordance with INARA procedures.
- Follow up on outstanding advances, missing documentation, discrepancies, or corrections with Finance and relevant staff until fully reconciled and cleared.
- This role verifies and reconciles case-related costs but is not responsible for program budgeting, financial management, or budget ownership.

**Monitoring, Documentation & Donor Reporting**

- Maintain accurate, complete, and up-to-date beneficiary records, medical follow-up information, service documentation, consent records, and case progress notes in accordance with INARA’s data protection and confidentiality requirements.
- Track case progress, treatment status, outputs, outcomes, pending actions, and relevant indicators and ensure reliable information is available for internal monitoring and donor reporting.
- Prepare monthly and quarterly reports on children and case management activities using existing donor templates, ensuring that information is accurate, evidence-based, complete, and submitted on time.
- Share completed reporting inputs and supporting information with the Partnerships and Program Management Department for review, consolidation, and donor submission.
- Maintain and follow a clear calendar of donor reporting deadlines and required case-related deliverables, including narrative inputs, beneficiary information, case updates, and communication materials.
- Provide timely clarifications, case data, and supporting documentation requested by Partnerships/Program Management for donor reports, reviews, monitoring visits, or audits.

**Communications, Case Stories & Visibility**

- Work closely with the Communications Department to identify appropriate treatment journeys, case stories, milestones, and impact examples that can be documented in line with consent, safeguarding, confidentiality, and dignity standards.
    - Coordinate access to accurate case information and appropriate follow-up with children and caregivers so that treatment progress and case stories are captured responsibly and without disrupting care.
    - Review case-related facts in communication materials for accuracy and ensure that medical and treatment information reflects the services actually received.
    - Track and follow up on donor deadlines for required communication, visibility, case-story, photo, video, or other program materials, coordinating with Communications and Partnerships/Program Management to ensure timely completion.

**Cross-Departmental Coordination**

- Work closely with Program Management, Partnerships, Finance, Communications, Administration, and Operations to ensure coordinated support to children and timely completion of case-related actions.
- Participate in relevant internal meetings and provide concise updates on case progress, team workload, treatment challenges, reporting requirements, and issues requiring management attention.
- Support coordination with external service providers and relevant actors where this directly contributes to referral pathways, continuity of care, or improved services for children.

**REQUIREMENTS & QUALIFICATIONS**

**Qualification**

- Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, Psychology, Nursing, Public Health, or another relevant field; a Master’s degree is an asset.
- Strong understanding of child-centered case management, care coordination, safeguarding, confidentiality, and data protection.
- Strong organizational, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and sensitive cases.
- Fluency in Turkish and strong working proficiency in English are required; Arabic is a strong asset.
- Ability to work on-site in Ankara and to travel locally to hospitals and service providers as required.

**Experience**

- Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in case management, medical care coordination, protection, MHPSS, or humanitarian programming, preferably with an international NGO.
- Demonstrated experience supervising case management, MHPSS, social work, or multidisciplinary teams.
- Proven experience coordinating medical cases with hospitals and healthcare providers and following treatment pathways and patient needs.
- Experience reviewing case documentation and treatment-related supporting documents and coordinating expense reconciliation with Finance.
- Experience preparing accurate narrative or beneficiary-level reports using donor or organizational templates and working to fixed reporting deadlines.
- Experience working with children and families affected by conflict, displacement, disaster, or other vulnerabilities is strongly preferred.

**CONFIDENTIALITY AND SAFEGUARDING**

**Confidentiality**

As the position is involved in sensitive topics, he/she must observe absolute discretion within and outside the organization. Non-respect of this clause or any breach of responsibility may result in a written warning or immediate dismissal.

**Safeguarding**

INARA has zero tolerance for abuse, exploitation, or harm to children and vulnerable adults. INARA employees must adhere strictly to safeguarding policies, maintain professional boundaries, and report concerns immediately.

title: Partnerships and Engagement Officer - London, UK
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
**Location:** London, UK

**Position Status:** Full-time, Regular

**Salary:** starting £37,040 - commensurate with professional experience and internal equity.

**Closing date:** Please submit application by **October 14th**

[**Risk Level:**](https://library.mercycorps.org/record/47705?ln=en) **☐ Level 3 ☐Level 2** X **Level 1**

Level 1: Likely to have no contact with participants or sensitive data

## **About Prosper Global**

Barely enough is not enough for anyone. Prosper Global is a humanitarian organization working alongside communities facing conflict, climate change, and economic hardship to meet urgent needs and create the conditions for lasting progress. Today's challenges demand new solutions, so we pair local knowledge with global resources to help communities build what's needed, test what's possible, and scale what's proven so that people everywhere can pursue a full life on their own terms. In 2026, we changed our name from Mercy Corps to Prosper Global, to reflect our belief that when every community can prosper, all of humanity moves forward.

## **The Program / Department / Team**

The Philanthropic Growth and Engagement department (PG&E) raises private funds by cultivating and maintaining relationships with private donors; defines the agency's brand, raising our public profile and sharing stories about our work with the media, the public and our supporters; and produces a wide range of online and offline communications.

Within PG&E, the Corporate Partnerships team develops and executes partnership strategies to grow revenue from leading global companies. In Europe, the team manages Prosper Global's relationships with major UK and European companies, their corporate foundations and their employees, securing six and seven-figure investments, in-kind and pro bono support, brand visibility and thought partnership. We build meaningful partnerships through outstanding relationship management, co-creation and a focus on shared value, working closely with colleagues across programmes, marketing and communications, the executive office and our country teams around the world.

## **The Position**

## **The Partnerships and Engagement Officer supports the growth of Prosper Global's corporate partnerships across Europe in support of the Pathway to Prosperity (P2P). The postholder will manage a portfolio of European corporate partners and prospects, supporting the full partnership lifecycle from new business development through closing, stewardship and renewal, and will work closely with the Corporate Partnerships Manager to advance the team's highest-value relationships.**

## **Approximately 70% of the role focuses on corporate partnership development and portfolio management. The remaining 30% leads Prosper Global's employee impact work in Europe, identifying where employee engagement and workplace giving can deepen corporate relationships and grow unrestricted income. The successful candidate will bring relationship management and business development experience, an understanding of the European corporate giving landscape, excellent written and verbal communication skills, and the ability to manage complex projects across teams and time zones.**

## **Essential Responsibilities**

### **Portfolio and Relationship Management**

- Manage a portfolio of European corporate partners and prospects, supporting the full donor lifecycle, including business development, proposal development, closing, stewardship and renewal, to retain and grow giving levels.
- In collaboration with the Corporate Partnerships Manager, develop and implement plans for partnerships in the portfolio, aligned with P2P priorities and each partner's own business and social impact goals.
- Act as the primary point of contact for assigned partners, responding to outreach and questions and identifying wider opportunities for collaboration.
- Support the Corporate Partnerships Manager on key accounts, deputising where needed, and provide business development, stewardship and communications support to corporate donors and prospects beyond the assigned portfolio.

### **Business Development**

- Support research, strategy and planning to expand Prosper Global's corporate portfolio in the UK and Europe, including in priority thematic sectors and in response to emerging corporate funding and trends.
- Write, edit and project manage concepts, proposals, pitch decks, reports and stewardship materials tailored to corporate audiences.
- Collaborate with programme, technical and innovation colleagues to match programme needs with potential funders and develop successful proposals.
- Contribute to cross-team new business mapping and to research and preparation for key events and conferences.

### **Grants Management and Compliance**

- In partnership with the Award Management Team (AMT), ensure agreements across the portfolio are well managed from review through kick-off, reporting and close-out, coordinating with finance, compliance, desk, country and programme teams as needed.
- Ensure internal teams understand and meet partner funding requirements, and that reporting is accurate, timely and compelling.
- Maintain accurate partner and prospect records in Raiser's Edge NXT, SharePoint and other systems so that institutional knowledge is captured and accessible across the team.

### **External Engagement and Representation**

- Represent Prosper Global in partner and prospect meetings, communications and events, and within European corporate responsibility networks, for both fundraising and profile raising.
- Prepare briefing materials, talking points and other content to support colleagues and leadership in external engagement.
- Build and share knowledge of the European corporate philanthropy landscape, bringing the partner perspective into proposal and programme design.
- Support initiatives that deepen partner relationships, including trips, campaigns and profile-raising events.

### **Employee Impact**

- Manage Prosper Global's employee impact activity in Europe in support of global partnerships, engaging employees of European-headquartered companies worldwide as well as European-based employees of companies headquartered elsewhere, and focusing effort where employee engagement will most effectively deepen corporate partnerships and grow unrestricted income.
- Design and deliver employee engagement opportunities with corporate partners, including workplace giving, matching gifts, employee fundraising and emergency appeals.
- Manage relationships with key UK and European workplace giving platforms and partner contacts, prioritising the channels with the strongest potential return.
- Represent Prosper Global at employee engagement events, in person and virtually, as a presenter and facilitator, bringing our mission and impact to life.
- Work closely with the US-based Employee Impact team to adapt global tools, materials and best practice for European audiences, and with Fundraising Operations to track and report income.

### **Safeguarding Responsibilities**

- Actively learn about safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work.
- Practice the values of Prosper Global including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members.
- Encourage openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.

## **Supervisory Responsibility**

None.

## **Accountability**

- **Report directly to**: Senior Director, Corporate Partnerships (US-based)
- **Dotted lines to**: Corporate Partnerships Manager, Director, Corporate Partnerships and Employee Impact
- **Works directly with**: Directors of Corporate Partnerships, Senior Director of Corporate Partnerships, Employee Impact team, Award Management Team, Fundraising Operations, Marketing and Communications, and desk, country and programme teams.

## **Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders**

Prosper Global team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

## **Minimum Qualification and Transferable Skills**

- Minimum of five years' progressive experience in corporate fundraising, partnership development or corporate social responsibility, ideally within the international development or humanitarian sector.
- Demonstrated track record of securing, stewarding and growing six and seven-figure corporate partnerships, including closing new business.
- Strong understanding of the UK and European corporate giving landscape, the evolving ESG agenda, and corporate decision-making processes.
- Experience managing restricted funding agreements, including coordinating compliance, finance and reporting across teams.
- Excellent written communication skills, with proven experience writing compelling proposals, reports and pitch materials for corporate audiences.
- Excellent verbal and presentation skills, able to represent the organisation confidently to senior corporate stakeholders and employee audiences.
- Proven ability to manage complex projects and competing priorities with excellent attention to detail.
- Cross-cultural acumen and experience working cross-functionally in a global organisation.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office and relationship databases; experience with Raiser's Edge NXT desirable.
- Experience of employee engagement or workplace giving programmes desirable.
- Working proficiency in a European language in addition to English desirable.

## **Success Factors**

The successful Senior Partnerships and Engagement Officer is a strategic, creative relationship builder who takes genuine ownership of their portfolio and finds compelling ways to align partner interests with Prosper Global's priorities. They are confident representing the organisation to senior corporate audiences and equally comfortable energising employee groups. They work with a high degree of independence, use sound judgement about when to bring in leadership, and are highly organised, able to balance multiple priorities under pressure and adapt quickly when plans change. A natural collaborator, they build strong working relationships across teams and time zones, communicate clearly and proactively, and bring a solutions-oriented, professional approach to every partnership. They share a strong commitment to Prosper Global's mission and to the communities we serve.

## **Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions**

The position is based in London or Edinburgh on a remote basis and requires up to 20% travel, primarily within the UK and Europe, with occasional international travel, which may include visits to country programmes. Prosper Global team members represent the agency both during and outside work hours when deployed in a field posting or on a short-term assignment or trip to country offices. Team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs and Prosper Global policies, procedures and values at all times and in all Prosper Global locations. Candidates must have the right to work in the UK at the time of appointment.

## **Ongoing Learning**

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development

## **Team Engagement and Effectiveness**

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

## **Equal Employment Opportunity**

Prosper Global is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.

## **Safeguarding and Ethics**

Prosper Global is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC **and have signed on to** [**the Interagency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme**](https://www.schr.info/the-misconduct-disclosure-scheme). We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to [Prosper Global Code of Conduct Policies](https://www.mercycorps.org/who-we-are/ethics-policies) and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct elearning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Prosper Global Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@prosperglobal.org).

title: International call for MEAL consultancy - Outcome Harvesting Evaluation
body:
NOTE: only organisations registered outside of Denmark are eligible for this consultancy opportunity.

**Opportunity:** ActionAid Denmark (AADK) is seeking a consultant, or team of consultants, to complete an Outcome Harvesting Evaluation. This is a MEAL consultancy to support AADK to assess the impact of its programming and partnership with local organisations.

**About SPAII:** Since January 2022, AADK has implemented the Strategic Partnership Agreement II (SPAII) in partnership with 17 ActionAid countries as well as with partners at the international level. AADK made a significant change in programming strategy from SPAI to SPAII to align with the overall AADK strategy as well as the AA strategy, and the overall objective of the SPAII programme is ‘*Societies are transformed to become more just, feminist, green, and resilient.’* The thematic priorities are expressed through the following three strategic objectives:

- *Strategic Objective 1: Democracy Deliver* – young people, especially young women and those facing marginalisation or fragility, enjoy their rights to an open and enabling democratic space and access to well-resourced programmes and public services.
- *Strategic Objective 2: Resilient livelihoods and just transition* – young people, especially young women and those facing marginalisation or fragility, enjoy a just transition and their right to climate resilient livelihoods.
- *Strategic Objective 3: Youth Leadership in Crises* – young people, especially young women and those facing marginalisation, are resilient to shocks and enjoy their right to protection in fragile contexts, disasters, and protracted crises.

**Objectives of the Outcome Harvesting Evaluation:**

1. To provide AADK with a robust evaluation and verification of the breath of impact and outcomes, as ascertained from harvested outcomes and complementary desk research.
2. To provide data, evidence and impact pathways for a set number of in-depth, substantiated and verified harvested outcomes.
3. To provide a set number of case studies, derived from harvested outcomes, for external communication.
4. Identification of opportunities and strategic lessons for future outcome harvesting, outcomes and impact learning.

These objectives will support AADK in demonstrating accountability to right-holders, partners, donors, and other stakeholders in terms of evidence of results achievement as well as to contribute to evidence-based decision-making, fundraising, and support learning processes internally and with partners.

Based on the objectives above, the scope of this evaluation is a comprehensive review of outcomes harvested throughout the duration of SPAII and complementary desk research of SPAII evidences, case studies, etc. This should be completed for all outcomes harvested across the three strategic objectives, as well as cross-cutting outcomes.

The evaluation should draw lessons relating to the effectiveness, relevance, scalability and impact of the harvested outcomes. Attention should be given to principles of participation and inclusion, equality and non-discrimination, feminist leadership principles, feminist research principles as well as accountability and reciprocity as addressed in the programme interventions. Findings should be structured to inform the SPAII Final Narrative report and communicate both programme achievements and strategic learning.

**Evaluation Team:**

- Experience of outcome harvesting.
- Experience of feminist leadership processes, intersectional feminist analysis and understanding of decolonial and anti-racist approaches to evaluation.
- Proven experience in leading exercises similar in scope to the present task.
- Extensive experience in evaluations, reviews, and assessments or other formative exercises particularly for large-scale complex programmes, with evidence of understanding of global standards, theories, models, and methods related to assessing results achievements, effectiveness, and value-add of different actors.
- Experience of online group facilitation
- Experience and ability to communicate complex projects to a range of audiences.
- Experience with results assessing of human rights-based, policy-influencing and advocacy interventions and the work of NGOs, CSOs and social movements to influence change at various levels.
- Specific thematic experience in youth-led change, climate justice, humanitarian response and/or gender responsive public services.
- Ability to conduct participatory and inclusive collaborative processes across different organisations and countries – including the ability to engage with, listen to and learn from a broad range of stakeholders.
- Experience from working in context covered by the SPAII programme.
- Strong communication skills, both in writing and orally in English, and ability to produce high-quality products underpinned by rigorous critical analysis of collected data and assembled evidence. French and Arabic is an advantage.

This is a global competition open to bidders from all geographic areas except for Denmark, and following the technical review, the financial proposal will be reviewed for the best overall comparative value. The evaluation is expected to take place from October to December 2026.

title: Consultant.e Expert.e en Architecture et IA Générative – Projet HAVA
body:
**Titre : Consultant.e Expert.e en Architecture et IA Générative – Projet HAVA**  
**Date : 11/09/2029**  
**Projet :**  
**Référence : ​HULO-TDR-BAR-2026-001​**

Cet appel à candidatures est ouvert à tous les consultants éligibles, en accord avec les procédures et principes de hulo.

**Contexte de la consultance :**

La **Coopérative hulo**, créée en juin 2021, est la première Société Coopérative Européenne (SCE) opérant dans le secteur de l’humanitaire. En décembre 2025, hulo compte 16 organisations membres : ACTED, Action contre la Faim (ACF), Bioport, la Croix-Rouge française (CRF), Fleet Forum, Handicap International / Humanity & Inclusion (HI), International Federation of the Red Cross, International Rescue Committee (IRC), INTERSOS, Médecins du Monde (MDM), Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC), Oxfam Intermón, Plan International, Première Urgence International (PUI), Solidarités International (SI), et Welthungerhilfe (WHH).

Son objectif est d'accroître l'impact de l'aide humanitaire en renforçant les liens et la solidarité entre les acteurs de la logistique humanitaire et en améliorant les performances grâce à la mise en commun des ressources et de l'expertise en matière de logistique et de chaîne d'approvisionnement. Les « initiatives mutualisées » de hulo, sont déjà en cours dans 7 countries (Burkina Faso, République Centrafricaine, RDC, Liban, Jordanie pour la crise syrienne, Colombie, et Tchad). Les activités sur le terrain sont composées d'achats mutualisés, de ressources humaines partagées, d’une plateforme web permettant la mise en commun de ressources, et d’initiatives environnementales mutualisées. Ces initiatives permettent d'économiser du temps et de l'argent, d'améliorer la qualité des biens et des services fournis, et donc de fournir une aide plus efficace à ceux qui en ont le plus besoin.

Hulo développe actuellement son écosystème Data autour de Microsoft Fabric, avec l'objectif de renforcer ses capacités en matière de Data Science, Business Analytics et Business Intelligence.  
L'utilisation des outils d'Intelligence Artificielle Générative (GenAI) se développant rapidement en interne, cela crée de nouvelles opportunités pour les équipes de hulo, mais également des risques, notamment concernant le shadow AI.  
Hulo souhaite donc étudier et préparer la mise en place de HAVA (Hulo AI for Value-added Assistance), un assistant d'IA générative d'entreprise, sécurisé et gouverné.  
Le concept actuellement réfléchi repose sur une approche Hybrid Enterprise AI Assistant, combinant des modèles d'IA générative opensource et les documents et mécanismes de sécurité contrôlés par hulo.  
L'architecture envisagée s'appuie notamment sur :

- Azure OpenAI Service
- Microsoft Fabric
- Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
- Microsoft Entra ID
- Microsoft Purview
- Microsoft Defender
- les bases de données et modèles analytiques de hulo

Le concept HAVA et ses annexes constituent le premier kit de travail qui servira de base à la présente consultance.

**Perimètre général du travail attendu du.de la Consultant.e :**

L'objectif principal de cette consultance est d'accompagner hulo dans la revue, la validation et la finalisation du cahier des charges fonctionnel et technique du projet HAVA.  
Le.la consultant.e apportera une expertise indépendante en matière de :

- Generative AI
- Large Language Models (LLM)
- Architecture Cloud
- Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
- Sécurité des données
- Gouvernance de l'IA
- Microsoft Azure et Microsoft Fabric

Le.la consultant.e n'aura pas pour objectif de développer l'intégralité de HAVA pendant cette mission.

La mission devra permettre à hulo de disposer, à l'issue de 20 jours estimés (A confirmer dans la proposition), d'un cahier des charges suffisamment complet et robuste pour permettre la mise en œuvre ultérieure de HAVA, en interne et/ou avec l'appui d'un prestataire externe.

Cette mission de consultant sera mise en oeuvre en coordination avec le département Business Analytics & Research (BAR). Une personne ressource sera désignée par département pour identifier les enjeux et faciliter les échanges.

**Priorités et livrables :**

**Cahier des charges HAVA finalisé** **incluant** :

1\. Analyse de situation -

- Contexte et enjeux
- Besoins identifiés et priorisés par service
- Contraintes techniques et d’intégration
    - Analyse de l'architecture existante, points forts, limites et recommandations
    - Données disponibles et leur qualité
    - Exigences éthiques, réglementaires et de gouvernance
    - Budget, planning et modalités de collaboration

2\. Solution recommandée

- Périmètre -
    - Objectifs
    - Périmètre fonctionnel
- Proposition -
    - Recommandation sur les modèles IA (Comparaison et recommandation des modèles et stratégie de modèles)
    - Connexions / liens avec d’autres usages IA internes (ex. Usages spécialisés de certains départements)
    - Modèle de coûts et ressources (Coûts d'implémentation, coûts récurrents et ressources nécessaires)
    - Registre des risques (Risques techniques, sécurité, données, opérationnels et adoption)
    - Spécifications sécurité et gouvernance (Identité, accès, confidentialité, RAG sécurisé, logs, gouvernance et guardrails)
    - Architecture RAG (Ingestion documentaire, métadonnées, recherches web, embeddings)

3\. Préparation de la mise en oeuvre

- Déploiement - Livrables, calendrier et responsabilités
- Critères de réussites
- Maintenance, support et réévaluation après déploiement

**Qualifications et expérience:**

- Minimum 3 ans d'expérience dans les domaines de la Data, de l'IA ou de l'architecture Cloud ;
- Expérience démontrée dans la conception de solutions Enterprise Generative AI ;
- Solide connaissance des LLM et architectures RAG ;
- Expérience de l'écosystème Microsoft Azure ;
- Bonne connaissance de la sécurité des données ;
- Expérience en gouvernance de l'IA ;
- Expérience dans la conception de solutions utilisant des documents internes ;
- Capacité à transformer des besoins métier en spécifications techniques ;
- Expérience avec des environnements humanitaire contenant des données sensibles ou confidentielles.

**Management et lignes hiérarchiques**

Ce · tte consultant·e sera placé·e sous la responsabilité du directeur du département « Business Analytics & Research » et travaillera de concert avec un Data Scientist.

**Calendrier**

Mi-octobre – décembre 2026

title: Técnico/a Sanitario/a. Campamentos Saharauis
body:
## Misión

El puesto tiene por objeto apoyar en el diseño, desarrollo y supervisión de las acciones en apoyo a los programas de salud sexual y reproductiva (PNSR) y salud infantil (PISIS) de los proyectos que la organización desarrolla en los Campamentos de personas Refugiadas Saharauis enTindouf.

## Ámbito geográfico deIntervención

Campamentos de Población Refugiada Saharaui, Tindouf, Argelia.

## Organigrama

Trabajará bajo la supervisión técnica de la Coordinación Sanitaria y trabajará junto con todo el equipo de Médicos del Mundo en terreno para el logro de los objetivos.

## Responsabilidades

1. En coordinación con la Coordinación Sanitaria, realizar evaluaciones de necesidades en salud en las áreas de intervención para los proyectos en curso o posibles nuevas intervenciones y contribuir a la formulación de proyectos.
    - En coordinación con responsables del Ministerio de Salud Pública Saharaui (MSP), identificar las necesidades de productos farmacéuticos (medicamentos, material consumible y equipos médicos durables) para los programas PNSR PISIS.
    - Apoyar técnicamente en los procesos de formulación con enfoque de marco lógico relacionados con Salud Sexual y Reproductiva (SSR) / Salud Infantil (SI) de los proyectos de MdM en los CRS, asegurando la transversalización de los enfoques de género y antropológico
2. Promover, planificar y ejecutar actividades sanitarias y de fortalecimiento de los servicios públicos de salud:
    - Acompañar a los equipos del PNSR(coordinaciones nacionales, coordinaciones regionales, secretaría) de acuerdo con un ciclo de mejora continua (planificar, implementar, verificar, actuar)
    - Proporcionar apoyo técnico al personal de salud adherido al PNSR y PISIS de los tres niveles asistenciales: Hospital nacional, hospitales regionales y dispensarios.
    - Liderar la realización de estudios de corte de los programas PNSR y PISIS. Acompañar la recogida de datos del Sistema de Información Sanitaria. En colaboración con la Coordinación Sanitaria contribuir al análisis de indicadores de salud y a la propuesta de proponer soluciones de mejora al MSP.
    - Apoyar en la actualización, implementación y seguimiento de protocolos y procedimientos estándar del PNSR y PISIS para garantizar intervenciones de calidad. Monitorizar su implementación y acompañar a las responsables del MSP para fomentar su cumplimiento en los diferentes niveles asistenciales.
    - Verificar técnicamente dosieres de compras de medicamentos, equipos médicos y material consumible.
    - Promover el adecuado funcionamiento de herramientas de seguimiento y coordinación del MSP como la Plataforma del PNSR-PISIS, las reuniones de coordinaciones mensuales y con el resto de los programas prioritarios. Promover y acompañar la celebración del Comité de muerte materna. Participar en la organización de la Asamblea Anual de la Mesa de Concertación y Coordinación en salud y contribuir a la preparación de información para donantes.
    - Contribuir a la transversalización de género en salud, de acuerdo con el Plan de Género y Salud del MSP, las políticas de MDM y la orientación de la Coordinación de Género y Derechos humanos.
    - Apoyar técnicamente en el ciclo de gestión del voluntariado sanitario y pasantías en terreno.
    - Contribuir activamente en la respuesta humanitaria en caso de emergencias y catástrofes.
3. Acompañamiento y monitoreo del componente sanitario de los proyectos en curso considerando la lógica de intervención de los proyectos, así como su coherencia y complementariedad con otras acciones, productos y actividades
    - Dar seguimiento a las actividades sanitarias de los proyectos activos de la organización y en concreto en lo referido a laSSR ySI, incluyendo la malnutrición materno-infantil.
    - Recoger y sistematizar los datos e indicadores de salud / sanitarios del sistema de monitoreo de MDM, en concreto en lo referido a la SSR,SI y malnutrición materno-infantil y los programas PNSR y PISIS. Participar en el análisis de indicadores junto a la Coordinación Sanitaria.
    - Asegurar la disponibilidad de fuentes de verificación en especial en relación con SSR y SI. Contribuir a la justificación de los proyectos.
4. Apoyar en el ciclo de capacitación y formación del personal sanitario:

- Apoyar al MSP en la detección de necesidades de capacitación y formación del personal de salud, en relación con SSR/SI y Derechos sexuales y reproductivos (DDSSRR).
    - Dar apoyo técnico y promover la realización de formaciones periódicas al personal de salud adherido al PNSR y PISIS.
    - Apoyar en las evaluaciones de estudiantes de matrona y enfermería de la Escuela de Enfermería, y en su caso, en la revisión de programas y contenidos.
    - Acompañar en el desarrollo de habilidades/sensibilización de temas relevantes respecto a la SSR y Salud Infantil. Fomentar la sensibilización e integración del enfoque de género en salud.

1. Contribuir activamente a la sistematización y adopción de buenas prácticas en MDM:

- Contribuir a la articulación y coordinación con el resto de las áreas, y en concreto con logística, administración, género y derechos humanos, farmacia e incidencia política, participando activamente en las reuniones de equipo
    - Contribuir activamente a la transversalización de los enfoques de género, antropológico y medioambiental en las intervenciones de MDM.
    - Contribuir al seguimiento de la estrategia de la misión y la coherencia entre los diferentes proyectos en marcha desde las diferentes áreas sanitarias.
    - Participar en espacios técnico-sanitarios de discusión y coordinación regulares y transmitir a la Coordinación Sanitaria elementos que requieran atención y contribuir al análisis de alternativas.
    - Apoyar en la implementación y seguimiento de los protocolos y procedimientos de seguridad y salud para el personal contratado y voluntario de MDM.
    - Contribuir a la actualización de la Estrategia País.

Otras tareas que le puedan ser requeridas por la Coordinación Sanitaria en el ámbito de sus responsabilidades y funciones.

## Formación

### Titulación Académica:

Requerida: Enfermero/a especialista en Obstetricia y Ginecología/Matrona.

### Formación Adicional:

Altamente deseable: Formación complementaria vinculada al ejercicio de su profesión, género y antropología de la salud. Máster/Postgrado en Cooperación Internacional/ Acción Humanitaria/ Salud pública.

## Requisitos

**Idiomas**: Imprescindible excelente nivel de castellano Altamente deseable: inglés, francés y/o árabe

**Informática**: Imprescindible nivel usuario de Word, Excel, internet y correo electrónico. Deseable nivel medio de Excel.

## Experiencia

Imprescindible experiencia en terreno en cooperación internacional en las funciones mencionadas.

Deseable experiencia en contextos similares y contextos críticos de seguridad.

## Competencias

- Excelente capacidad de organización y planificación
- Capacidad de trabajo en equipo y en red
- Flexibilidad
- Capacidad de trabajo en condiciones difíciles
- Elevada capacidad de comunicación escrita y hablada
- Conciencia cultural y adaptabilidad. Facilidad para las relaciones interpersonales
- Cumplimiento estricto de los protocolos de seguridad establecidos para el país y la misión de MdM
- Identificación con principios y valores de Médicos del Mundo

## Retribución/Condiciones

Tablas salariales de Médicos del Mundo. Contrato Indefinido.

Jornada laboral: 40 horas.

Categoría: Grupo 1. Personalsanitario

Las personas interesadas pueden enviar el CV a través de nuestra página web:

**Nota:**

Médicos del Mundo promueve la igualdad de oportunidades de todas las personas y establece medidas de acción positiva para quienes por razón de diversidad funcional o de exclusión social y/o cultural pertenecen a grupos infrarrepresentados en los puestos que se ofertan. Por lo que ninguna candidatura con perfil válido será rechazada por su diversidad funcional o por estar cultural o socialmente excluida por razón de nacimiento, etnia, raza, sexo, género o cualquier otra condición o circunstancia personal, social o cultural.

title: Fertilizer Procurement Strategy Associate
body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

## **About the Role**

Seeking a procurement professional to lead fertilizer procurement, ensuring cost-efficient sourcing and reliable on-time delivery. Drive strong individual execution and contribute to team success. In this role, your focus will be dedicated to deep-dive data analysis to determine optimal purchasing windows, and managing and executing the entire procurement process independently.

## **Responsibilities**

Execute Procurement with Excellence

- Strategy & Delivery: Support the creation and execution of seasonal procurement strategies to deliver +90% OTIF (On-Time, In-Full) delivery, market-competitive costs, and 5% year-on-year cost savings.
- Quality Assurance: Ensure absolute quality control, achieving 0 quality issues reaching the farmer, and maintain an +80% on-time payment rate for suppliers.
- Supply Chain Reliability: Proactively address future supply gaps by evaluating farmer needs against global market trends, supplier capacity, and current inventory levels.
- Process Optimization: Drive lead-time improvements through streamlined delivery and process automation. Regularly improve key operations like the goods receipt process and loading quality control.
- Data & Analytics: Spend time developing, maintaining, and continuously improving complex Google Sheets data models to track global market trends and landed costs. Use this data to provide crucial decision support on when to purchase (or not purchase) fertilizers to maximize cost savings.

Build Partnerships & Market Liaisons

- Strategic Relationships: Help build and maintain deep partnerships with fertilizer suppliers and industry organizations beyond seasonal procurement needs.
- Country Team Collaboration: Act as a critical business partner for our country operations teams, actively identifying and sharing opportunities to improve our offering to farmers.
- Industry Representation: Serve as a representative for One Acre Fund externally with suppliers and market actors to drive long-term, systematic supply chain improvements.

People Management

- People Management: Manage and mentor a small team, setting clear goals, providing timely feedback, and conducting high-quality career coaching and performance reviews.
- Team Growth:Contribute to staffing, recruitment, and succession planning to build a high-performing procurement unit.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

Professional & Technical Competencies:

- Supply Chain Expertise: Solid foundational knowledge of global procurement processes, international shipping, and supply chain operations.
- Data Fluency: An advanced analytical mindset with high proficiency in Google Sheets to build pricing, forecasting, and decision-support models. Comfortable spending half of your time analyzing data to help make decisions.
- Language: Fluency in written and spoken English is required.

Management & Execution Skills:

- Relationship Builder: Exceptional collaboration and negotiation skills, with the ability to influence both internal stakeholders and external global suppliers.
- Project Management: Strong organizational skills with a proven track record of managing multiple projects simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.
- Solution-Oriented: An innovative thinker who approaches obstacles with a results-driven mindset and is comfortable making data-driven decisions under medium-risk conditions.

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Nairobi, Kenya

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

## **Eligibility**

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

## **Application Deadline**

16 October 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

title: FIELD COMMUNICATION OFFICER
Italian Teacher
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Background**

 In response to the increased refugee arrivals into Europe, the IRC established the program initially in Greece, which was expanded with programs in Serbia and wider Balkans and with programs in Germany. Following a first assessment conducted in January 2017 in Italy and another one in July 2017, several critical protection gaps were identified within assistance provided to refugees and migrants in Italy: mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), assistance to unaccompanied children, information provision and legal support. To respond to the identified gaps IRC established a small presence in Italy. The IRC in Italy provides essential safety, empowerment, education, livelihood and health services to migrants, refugees and asylum seekers. Our programs operate across the country, including in Trieste, Milan, Rome, Turin and various locations in Sicily and Calabria, with a strong focus on supporting the most vulnerable populations, such as women and children.

**Context of the Assignment**

IRC, in partnership with Ente Nazionale Acli Istruzione Professionale (E.N.A.I.P.) Piemonte, Ente Nazionale Acli Istruzione Professionale (E.N.A.I.P.) Friuli Venezia Giulia, Powercoders, Progetto Tenda, is implementing the **Digital Horizons projec**t in Turin and Trieste, since February 2025.  
Digital Horizons helps young refugees and migrants in Italy accessing sustainable employment through free software development training, job support, individual guidance and social support. The project focuses on youth aged 16–25, arrived in Italy in recent years, who are seeking to break down integration barriers, improve mental health and build pathways to long-term work opportunities.

By working with public job centers (PES), vocational training providers (VET), IT companies and employers, the project prepares participants for high-demand digital careers and supports them with mental health services, individual job counselling and psychosocial support, job placement, a safe and quiet space to study, access to social services, language training, and childcare.

Simultaneously, it also builds the capacity of institutions and employers to create more inclusive opportunities for the target population.

The Digital Horizons intensive (5hs day, monday-friday) training in software development has been delivered in Trieste since mid October 2025, by IRC partner ENAIP FVG. To support the group of participants with heterogeneous knowledge of Italian language, IRC is seeking a teacher for **italian classes (A2-B1-B2),** includingspecific IT **vocational language,** to support students learning outcomes, before the start of the IT training.

**Purpose of the Assignment**

**Job Overview**

The Digital Horizons Italian Teacher will be based in Trieste and will design and deliver middle advanced (A2-B1-B2 as needed) Italian language classes and IT vocational language, to a group of Digital Horizons students, in person. Under the Economic Wellbeing Manager’s supervision and in collaboration with the IRC Italy Integration Counselor and ENAIP FVG staff, the Italian teacher will conduct classroom teaching activities in Trieste, ensuring no student is left behind.

**SCOPE OF WORK**

**Specific Duties and Responsibilities:**

- **Plan, design, and deliver lessons** in Italian at A2-B1–B2 level, integrating IT-related terminology and vocational language relevant to software development.
- **Develop tailored teaching materials** that combine general Italian language learning with specialized IT vocabulary and contexts.
- **Address student questions** and provide clarification on both general and IT-specific language content.
- **Help develop students’ confidence and learning skills**, encouraging students to use Italian effectively in technical and professional settings.
- **Identify learning gaps** and adapt teaching strategies to meet diverse linguistic needs within the group.
- **Promote intercultural communication** by clarifying information and bridging cultural differences that may affect learning.
- **Manage classroom dynamics** and handle any critical issues that arise during sessions, ensuring a supportive learning environment.
- **Encourage collaborative learning** through peer-to-peer support and group exercises for language practice with IT-related content.
- **Maintain accurate records** of attendance, progress, and outcomes to support monitoring and reporting requirements.
- Collaborate with the IT trainer, other ENAIP vocational training staff and IRC Integration Counselor to achieve the course objectives.

The **Digital Horizons Italian teacher** will deliver updates to IRC Staff, on the classroom learning process and possible challenges identified.

**Deliverables**

- Italian classes sessions conducted (40 hs)
- Attendance Sheets signed

**Timeframe**
