title: Research Manager for Afghanistan, based in Kabul
body:
## BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the REACH Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis, GIS and remote sensing. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO with headquarters based in Paris and presence in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, which allows IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support in its fields of intervention.

### We are currently looking for a Research Manager to scope out and set-up a new Research Team focussing on the Economy, Markets, and Livelihoods

**Department**: IMPACT

**Position**: Research Manager

**Contract duration**: 4 months

**Starting Date**: 1st December 2026 (preferred); 1st January 2027 (latest)

**Location**: Kabul, Afghanistan.

## COUNTRY PROFILE

The humanitarian response in Afghanistan remains one of the largest in the world, with 21.9 million people identified as in need of assistance in the 2026 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan. The country is particularly vulnerable to climate change, with drought conditions affecting agriculture and livelihoods. Natural disasters, including flooding and earthquakes, remain prevalent – often causing displacement, damaging and destroying shelter and services, and disrupting livelihoods. Conflict remains a risk, with recent increase in conflict activity between Afghanistan and Pakistan. With millions of refugees in neighbouring countries, including Iran and Pakistan, forced return of refugees is also a driver of needs in the country.

Alongside this, since the De facto Authorities took control of the government in 2021, a range of restrictive policies have significantly restricted the rights of women and girls in society – leading to increased marginalisation and protection risks. The economic situation remains poor and authorities lack resources to run effective public services, with reliance on humanitarian assistance. As the USA was a major aid donor in Afghanistan, their withdrawal of all aid funding had a significant effect, for example on the closures of health centres. With political positioning of donor governments restricting a full development approach, a basic human needs response is increasingly complementing the humanitarian response across Afghanistan.

Against this backdrop, IMPACT Initiatives is planning a range of research activities to support an evidence- and needs-based humanitarian response. The IMPACT Deputy Country Representative (DCR) supports the Country Representative (CR) in overseeing programme strategy and implementation internally, as well as external representation of IMPACT.

## POSITION PROFILE

Following the development of our new Country Strategy, IMPACT Afghanistan is planning to establish a new research team with the aim of providing relevant information to humanitarian and basic human needs stakeholders linked to the economy, markets and livelihoods in Afghanistan.

IMPACT Afghanistan is therefore seeking an experienced Research Manager with knowledge of assessment and analysis, to scope out a programme of work for this new team, through internal and external consultations. The Research Manager will be responsible for drafting concept notes and research ToRs that can be used to solicit funding for the start-up of the team.

The Research Manager will be responsible for building an understanding of the relevant aid strategies existing in Afghanistan and identifying relevant data and research gaps that could be filled. This will involve connections with international and national NGOs (including members of Cash Consortium of Afghanistan), the UN, and donors. The Research Manager will review existing research in Afghanistan (including the MSNA and Joint Market Monitoring Initiative) and also connect across IMPACT to understand similar research being conducted elsewhere that could be adapted for the Afghanistan context.

## RESPONSIBILITIES

The Research Manager’s responsibilities will include:

***CONTEXTUAL UNDERSTANDING***

- Assess relevant strategic, analytical, and operational documents to develop an understanding of the current priorities relating to the economy, markets and livelihoods for the aid response in Afghanistan.
- Mapping existing IMPACT data, other research, and other relevant information sources to understand relevant areas for potential assessment and research.
- Connecting with national and international NGOs, UN colleagues, and the donor community to understand their priorities and to identify where IMPACT research could support their programmes and strategies.
- Provide SMT and other staff members with key updates from these efforts.

***DEPARTMENT STRATEGY DEVELOPMENT***

- Engage with IMPACT colleagues in HQ and in other country programmes to identify existing assessment and research tools that could be adapted for Afghanistan.
- Develop a series of concept notes that can be shared with prospective partners or donors, to seek funding for the set-up for the new team.
- Develop/draft relevant research ToRs, enabling technical discussion and approval of potential research projects.
- Develop a light-touch team strategy that could subsequently be further developed based on the eventual set-up and staffing of research activities.
- Coordinate with staff in the Cash Consortium of Afghanistan to identify potential assessment and research opportunities for the future of the Consortium.

***RESEARCH MANAGEMENT***

- As necessary, support the Humanitarian Coordination and Monitoring Unit in the delivery of research and analysis linked to Joint Market Monitoring Initiative and the Cash Consortium of Afghanistan.
- As required, work with the cross-cutting analysis team to support the develop of analysis products linked to the economy, markets, and livelihoods, which can better position IMPACT Afghanistan in this thematic field.

The Research Manager will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes. They will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to IMPACT and its partners or collected during his/her assignment with IMPACT.

## REQUIREMENTS

- **Work experience** Demonstratable relevant working experience in a humanitarian setting, such as programme management, evaluation and assessments. Experience working with development responses is an advantage;
- **Thematic experience** Able to showcase experience in working with economy and market data in an aid environment’
- **Research skills** Excellent quantitative and qualitative research design, data collection, and data analysis experience required;
- **Familiarity with aid system** Good understanding of the aid system and the research community.
- **Management experience** Demonstrated team management skills, including remote management;
- **Experience in geographical region** Past experience in the region/supporting is desirable;
- **Communication/reporting skills** Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting and reviewing;
- **Cross-cultural work environment** Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility and work independently;
- **Academic qualifications** A Master’s degree in a relevant discipline is preferred. However, significant relevant work experience can be considered.
- **Software skills** Proven knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite, to include Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Familiarity with R, SPSS and/or STATA or other statistical analysis software an asset
- **Security environment** Ability to operate in a complex and challenging security environment.
- **Language skills** Fluency in English required, competency in Dari or Pashto is an asset.

## COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

- For this position, salary between 3’050€ and 3’100 monthly before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD *NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.*
- Accommodation and food provided in the guesthouse.
- Affiliation to French Social security (CFE) + health Complementary (Mobility Benefits) + Repatriation assistance (SOS International) + Private Pension Fund.
- Flight tickets every six months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered).
- R&R after eight weeks, flight ticket up to 500$ + 200$ of living allowance
- Contribution to the transportation of luggage: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- Predeparture induction - three days at IMPACT Initiatives’ HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situ security training (depending on previous inductions and security trainings taken);
- IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

title: Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Officer - South (UA Nationals Only)
body:
**Job Title**: Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Officer - South (UA Nationals Only)

**Function**: Programme Development

**Job Group:** Programmes

**Duty Station**: Mykolaiv, Ukraine (with frequent travel to NP field sites)

**Line Manager:** Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Coordinator

**Technical Line Manager:** Programme Development Manager

**Line Management Responsibility:** N/A

Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP) is a dynamic, international non-governmental organisation. We work with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP). We work to reduce violence, protect civilians in countries affected by violent conflict and its aftermath, and help transform the world’s response to conflict situations.

**Overview:**

NP has been working in Ukraine since 2022 within conflict-affected communities and individuals across Odesa, Mykolaiv, Kherson, Donetsk, Dnipropetrovsk and Kharkiv Oblasts. Working through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP), NP centers local communities in preventing violence and promoting positive peace. NP’s programming focuses on building capacities within local communities to engage in nonviolent self-protection methods such as protective accompaniment/presence, community-led safety and security initiatives such as conflict de-escalation techniques and early warning/response mechanisms. Secured funding spans several years and offers an exciting opportunity to be at the forefront of sustainable, civilian protection.

The Monitoring and Evaluation Coordinator will be in the Program Development department and is responsible for overseeing Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) in Nonviolent Peaceforce in Ukraine (NPUA). This position is open to international and national candidates.

**Job Summary:**

The Monitoring and Evaluation Coordinator will be responsible for overseeing M&E processes and initiatives across NPUA programming functions. The role will contribute to strategic design which supports the continued relevance, effectiveness, and efficiency of NPUA programming. The M&E Coordinator will be responsible for NPUA’s assessments, knowledge products, and evaluations. This includes developing data collection protocol, data analysis, report writing, and internal and external dissemination of results. The M&E Coordinator will additionally lead and manage NPUA’s M&E and Assessment team.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Duties and Responsibilities**

- Work closely with the Programmes Department, and field teams to develop and strengthen monitoring and evaluation systems, including approaches and tools that facilitate the acquisition and aggregation of useful programming data.
- Act as a central focal point for monitoring and evaluation technical assistance and guidance, ensuring that NPUA maintains requisite levels of quality throughout programming.
- Guide the design of data quality assurance procedures and trainings to ensure accurate and consistent data collection among NPUA field teams.
- Manage processes related to internal monitoring, evaluation and information management including supporting the Programme Development Department develop logical frameworks and performance monitoring plans, review reporting protocols and conduct research activities.
- Manage processes related to external monitoring and evaluation activities including requests for applications, outsourcing of assessments and evaluations, providing technical input, and overseeing communications related to needs assessments, baseline, midterm, and end line studies, post, and other types of evaluations.
- Lead the dissemination of results and findings including developing external communications materials and advocacy.
- Produce high-quality reports on the results of projects against the project goals and objectives.
- Manage quantitative and qualitative data collection for the purposes of programme development and reporting including the design and deployment of innovative electronic data capture, data storage and data security systems.
- Undertake regular visits to the field to support implementation of monitoring and evaluation and to identify where adaptations might be needed.
- Develop an organizational training plan and strategy to support learning and capacity building efforts within NPUA.
- Guide the regular sharing of the outputs of monitoring and evaluation findings with management and field staff including reporting of assessments, evaluations, programme data, lessons learned and good practices.

**Duties Applicable to All Staff**

- Actively work towards the achievement of the goals and mandate of Nonviolent Peaceforce.
- Abide by and work in accordance with Nonviolent Peaceforce values and principles.

**QUALIFICATIONS REQUIREMENTS**  
**Education**

- Post-secondary Education or bachelor's degree in social sciences, Administration, Information Management, Project Management, or other relevant academic background (essential), master's degree (desirable).

**Experience**

- At least 3 years of relevant experience in monitoring, evaluation, learning, and research.
- Experience in designing, implementing, and operating project M&E systems from start to end of project.
- Experience in strategic planning and performance measurement, including indicator selection, target setting, reporting, database management and developing M&E and performance monitoring plans.
- Experience in facilitating and serving as focal person for externally managed evaluations.
- Knowledge of major evaluation methodologies (ex. Quantitative, qualitative, mixed-method, and impact) and data collection and analysis methodologies.

**Skills and Competencies**

- Good training and facilitation skills with experience providing relevant and appropriate capacity building for staff and partners.
- Proficient analysis and communication skills for the purpose of report writing and presentations.
- Experience in data entry and analysis software such as Salesforce, SPSS, STATA, and Microsoft Excel and Access.
- Familiarity and interest in humanitarian protection, peacebuilding, and violence prevention programming.
- Knowledge and understanding of the Ukrainian socio-economic, cultural, and political conditions.
- Self-motivated person able to work independently without close supervision.
- Able to work effectively in a diverse team environment.
- Comfortable with frequent travel to field locations and living / working in remote areas.
- Able to communicate in oral and written English, as well as Ukrainian and/or Russian

title: Programme Manager (South)
body:
**Job Title:** Programme Manager (South)

**Department:** Programming

**Division:** Programme implementation

**Duty Station:** Mykolaiv, Ukraine (with frequent travel to Odesa and Kherson)

**Line Manager:** Head of Programme (HoP)

**Line Management Responsibility:** Team Leaders (South – Odesa & Mykolaiv & Kherson)

**Position Type:** Full-Time

**ABOUT US**

Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP) reimagines security and civilian protection in areas most impacted by conflict by working alongside communities to interrupt and prevent violence. NP is a global civil society organization that works with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP) and by helping to transform the world’s response to conflict situations.

Programming is founded on unarmed civilian protection and is thematically focused on protection in displacement, child protection, gender-based violence protection and inter-communal violence reduction, social cohesion, and civic engagement.

NP first established a presence in Ukraine in 2014/2015 working on peacebuilding and conflict mediation. NP has had a sustained presence in Ukraine since April 2022. NP occupies a unique space in the protection response in Ukraine; simultaneously providing direct protection to at-risk civilians and providing hands-on support to front-line volunteer collectives to directly contribute to the sustainability and safety of their actions.

**JOB SUMMARY**

To manage the implementation of NP’s Programme, overseeing violence prevention programming in the South of Ukraine - covering Odesa, Mykolaiv and Kherson Oblasts - ensuring the project is implemented in accordance with NP’s mission and vision, compliances, and allocated budgets. The PM advances the collective effort of ensuring that programmes are evidence and needs driven, monitored closely, and are risk appropriate. The PM promotes and actively encourages coherency, quality assurance and crosspollination across field teams.

The PM will provide leadership for Team Leaders in close liaison with the HoP and will work directly with the Protection Advisor and Programme Development Team.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Programme Management**

- Responsible for the overall planning and effective delivery of the project(s) in areas of implementation through the application of Unarmed Civilian Protection approach.
- Provide technical advice and oversight for the field teams implementing violence reduction projects, either directly or through team leaders in field sites.
- Together with the SPM, guide teams in strategic planning, development of work plans and adapting implementation to address emerging protection needs and contextual or operational challenges.
- Provide oversight, monitoring and review of Salesforce reporting and contribute to internal reporting upon request (including context, programming, staffing and welfare). Highlight to SMT key points from Salesforce Activity Reporting.
- The PM will support field teams and serve as interlocutor with Management and the Programme Development team if programming has to be adapted to address dynamic contextual realities and/or if changing circumstances renders the project objectives irrelevant or impossible.
- Work very closely with MEL team to ensure the effective implementation of the monitoring, evaluation, and learning strategy of program in each of the program locations.
- Engage in direct programme implementation as needed, participate in integrated capacities and needs assessments and emergency response if needed. This may include direct support with in-house and partner technical trainings. Stand in as Acting Team Leader when necessary.
- Contribute to broader country programme strategy development together with the rest of the Programme and Management team.
- Participate in grant inception process with programme development, finance and operations and then lead grant inception process with field teams in partnership with Programme Development department.
- When requested, contribute to donor reporting for area of operations.
- When requested, support assessments and start-up in new areas of implementation.

**Representation and Advocacy**

- Represent NP in coordination and advocacy fora where appropriate and needed, including on issue-based advocacy in the South of Ukraine.
- Represent NP at the sub-national level (with local authorities in field locations) when Team Leaders request senior support.
- Provide guidance and direct support on access related negotiations in areas of operation as needed in close coordination with the SSA and HoM.
- In collaboration with the Programme Development team, represent NP in the South of Ukraine to donors, engaging in proactive communication to keep donors updated on the progress of the project and the evolving conflict and protection context.
- Represent NP in the South of Ukraine during donor visits to areas of operation and planning donor visits together with the Programme Development team and will whenever possible, accompany the donor on field visits.

**Financial & Operational Management**

- Supervise and ensure that teams comply with their internal and external reporting requirements.
- Support FPO and TL with field level budget management including coding of field level expenses in accordance with approved project budgets.
- Work directly with TLs to prepare monthly site forecasting and monthly reporting of actuals against forecasts and flag under/overspends and offer corrective measures.
- In coordination with SPM, establish site spending strategies to ensure best use of available funds as well as allocating team attention towards necessary budget line spending.
- Serve as interlocutor between field teams and programme support departments (HR, Finance and Operations), ensuring that the needs of field teams are met and that field teams are fully aware of what is happening operationally in the Country Office as it relates to their sites.

**Personnel Management**

- Serve as Line Manager for Team Leaders.
- Facilitate strong staff morale and positive working environment using and practicing the NP values as central guidance.
- Coach and guide team leaders on field-based personnel management, with the support of Human Resources colleagues, ensuring that labour law is adhered to, and NP Human Resources policies are known and implemented.
- Ensure sufficient level of staffing, identifying the need for new recruitment in a timely fashion.
- Participate in recruitment panels for South-based recruiting.
- Support Team Leaders to ensure that all field team staff (programme and programme support) receive timely performance reviews in close coordination with HR department.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

- Master’s degree in project management, conflict resolution, conflict transformation, peace studies, international relations, political science, negotiation, mediation, human security or related area of study.
- 4-6 years work experience in civilian protection, violence prevention, social cohesion, peacebuilding.
- Minimum 1 year experience as a Team Leader or similar position with Nonviolent Peaceforce
- Demonstrated management experience in working in complex security environment.
- Demonstrated experience working with state authorities and negotiation
- Demonstrated ability to live, work and solve problems independently and effectively in remote, highly challenging locations
- Demonstrated ability to analyse conflict, security and political contexts
- Identify with NP values and UCP principles

**SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES:**

***Independent Judgment/Analytical:***

- Ability to set priorities, solve problems and analyse data
- Ability to manage information with discretion
- Demonstrable conflict analysis skills, identify entry points and design prevention and protection strategies

***Interpersonal:***

- Ability to communicate effectively with individuals and motivate and provide leadership to team and to work in a multi-cultural environment
- Solutions focused, creative problem solver
- Proven ability to build relationships with the full range of actors including government, various community leaders, military, police and non state actors
- Genuine commitment and interest in living and working at the community level
- Flexibility and adaptability

***Language:***

- Ability to interact confidently in English with colleagues and external contacts, to write documents and reports, and to present effectively relevant information
- Working Ukrainian language skills are an added benefit

***Information Technology:***

- Good skills in Microsoft Office applications. Hardware IT skills a definite asset

**Other Specialized Requirements**

- Ukraine is a complex security environment where conditions change rapidly – experience in insecure environments is essential to success in this position

**Working Conditions:**

- This field position may include challenging living conditions, limited access to amenities, and potentially unstable security situations.
- You must be prepared to live in basic or non-traditional accommodation, which may include shared housing, camps, or field-based settings
- Demonstrated ability to adhere to strict security protocols.

**SPECIAL NOTICE**

Nonviolent Peaceforce is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against based on disability.

Nonviolent Peaceforce acknowledges the duty of care to safeguard and promote the welfare of employees, contractors, volunteers, interns, communities we work with, and other stakeholders and is committed to ensuring safeguarding practice reflects statutory responsibilities and government guidance and complies with best practices in the Humanitarian and Development sector. NP expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We prioritise ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work for us.

The post holder will undertake the appropriate level of training and is responsible for ensuring that they understand and work within the safeguarding policies of the organisation.

All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks. NP also participates in the [Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme](https://misconduct-disclosure-scheme.org/). In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.

**NO FEE**

**We never ask for payment as part of our selection process, and we always contact candidates via our corporate accounts and platforms. If you are approached for payment, this is likely to be fraudulent. Please check whether the role you are interested in is posted** [**here** ](https://nonviolentpeaceforce.org/work-with-us/)**on our website.**

title: Final Evaluation Consultancy – Strengthening Women and Girls with and without Disabilities in Gaza
body:
**CBM Christian Blind Mission e.V. (CBM) is looking for an experienced professional/professionals to conduct a Final Evaluation for a project in Gaza. This assignment will be based on consultancy work for approximately up to 30 working days in November 2026.**

**About the Project:**

The project “Strengthening women and girls with and without disabilities by enhancing an inclusive and safe environment in the Gaza Strip” aims to contribute to the long-term strengthening of the resilience capacity of women and girls with and without disability in Gaza through improved access to psychosocial well-being and physical recovery services, enhanced capacities of duty bearers and community to integrate inclusive services and take social and legal action to address GBV, especially against persons with disability.

The purpose of this End-term evaluation is to assess the overall performance of the project from its start to the time of evaluation. It will review the achievement of objectives and outcomes, highlight successes, and identify gaps and challenges. Findings and recommendations will inform future programming and strategic planning by CBM and its partners, and support accountability to all stakeholders.

For more information, please refer to the terms of reference here: [https://www.cbm.org/tors-eval-womengirls-gazaproject](https://www.cbm.org/tors-eval-womengirls-gazaproject)

title: Mama Lucy Eye Unit Design Consultancy
body:
**CBM Christoffel-Blindenmission Christian Blind Mission e.V. (CBM) is inviting qualified Architectural and Engineering Consultancy Firms to provide consultancy services for the detailed design of the proposed Eye Unit at Mama Lucy Eye Hospital, Nairobi. This assignment is expected to be undertaken over an approximately 8-week period and will result in a complete tender-ready package, detailed cost estimates, and procurement support documentation**

The proposed project involves the extension and refurbishment of Mama Lucy Eye Hospital to establish a modern eye care facility providing comprehensive ophthalmology services with a strong emphasis on paediatric eye care. The facility will be designed to create a child-friendly, inclusive, and accessible environment while supporting broader eye care services and future expansion requirements. The assignment includes detailed architectural and engineering design development, preparation of Bills of Quantities and cost estimates, tender documentation, and support for statutory approvals.

title: Electoral Inclusion and Accessibility Consultant
body:
**POSITION INFORMATION**

- Organization: UNDP Lebanon Through Stars Orbit Consultants and Management Development
- VA No.: UNDP/LBN/VA26/185
- Position Title: Electoral Inclusion and Accessibility Consultant
- Duty Station: work from home, with occasional meetings with UNDP
- Duration: 2 months (without exceeding 18 working days per month)
- Vacancy Date of Issue: 30 September 2026
- Vacancy Closure Date: 07 October 2026
- National or International consultancy: National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link: [https://drive.google.com/file/d/1k4qiQaXRNZG8iikxpxj80h4IFCVt95LK/view](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1k4qiQaXRNZG8iikxpxj80h4IFCVt95LK/view)

**BACKGROUND**

UNDP Lebanese Electoral Assistance and Parliament Support Project (LEAPS) has the main objective to achieve an enhanced efficiency, transparency, and inclusiveness of the electoral process in Lebanon towards the upcoming parliamentary elections through enhanced and efficient electoral processes, improved legislation, and inclusive public participation, addressing the challenges hampering the democratic consolidation in Lebanon.

Through a multi-component approach, the project has the intended outcomes of providing technical assistance and support in the following key electoral areas:

1. Enhanced efficiency, transparency and inclusiveness of the electoral management and administration through improved institutional capacity and legislative reforms;
2. Strengthened institutional capacity of the SCE to perform its mandate and attributions in a sustainable and independent manner;
3. Effectiveness and transparency of the EDR mechanism enhanced through technical assistance to the Constitutional Council,
4. Inclusiveness and participation of vulnerable and marginalized groups in the electoral processes enhanced and
5. Strengthened institutional capacity of the parliament to function, debate and adopt key reform legislation.

war operational context into a focused set of feasible institutional and policy measures ahead of the upcoming parliamentary elections.

The initiative responds to accessibility and electoral-continuity challenges arising from damaged public infrastructure, displacement and continued instability, particularly in the South. It focuses on four priority reforms:

1. Accessible Mega Centres;
2. Reactivation of the Administrative Committee established under Decree 2214/2009;
3. Pre-registration and choice of polling location, including displaced voters; and
4. Inclusive voting and candidacy procedures.

The consultancy will provide specialized technical expertise on electoral inclusion, accessibility and disability-inclusive electoral processes. It will support PWD NGOs in translating available evidence, legal and institutional

provisions, and identified barriers into practical policy proposals and an implementation roadmap for the upcoming parliamentary elections.

The assignment will support:

- Consolidation and analysis of evidence from the 2025 electoral monitoring exercise, previous UNDP-supported activities, relevant legal and institutional provisions, and available information on post-war polling-centre accessibility and availability.
- Development of four concise, evidence-based policy briefs covering the four priority reforms.
- Development or technical validation of minimum accessibility criteria for Mega Centres, covering physical access, transport and parking, internal circulation, voting facilities, signage, accessible information, communication support, emergency procedures and reasonable accommodation.
- Targeted institutional consultations with relevant electoral and government stakeholders, including documentation of responsibilities, feasible options, required data, agreements and outstanding issues.
- Technical input to accessible public communication products and the four short accessible videos, ensuring consistency with the proposed reforms.
- Technical support to the preparation of Commitment Day and the resulting commitment matrix, ensuring commitments are specific, attributable and suitable for follow-up.

**2. SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the general supervision of the UNDP Governance and Rule of Law CTA and in close coordination with the LEAPS team, the consultant shall:

**A. Evidence Review and Analysis**

- Consolidate evidence from PWD’s 2025 electoral monitoring, previous UNDP-supported work, relevant legal and institutional provisions, and available information on damaged or inaccessible polling centres.
- Identify key accessibility barriers affecting voters and candidates with disabilities, distinguishing verified evidence from information requiring validation.
- Assess the implications of displacement, damaged infrastructure and access constraints, particularly in the South.
- Identify relevant institutional mandates, coordination needs and priority actions.

**B. Policy Development and Accessibility Framework**

- Provide technical input to four concise policy briefs, outlining the issue, evidence, proposed solution, responsible institution and required action.
- Develop or validate minimum accessibility standards for Mega Centres, covering access, transport, circulation, voting facilities, signage, interpretation, communication support, emergencies and reasonable accommodation.
- Ensure recommendations are rights-based, practical and operationally feasible.
- Contribute to an implementation roadmap with responsible institutions, actions and indicative timelines.

**C. Institutional Consultation and Coordination**

- Support the preparation and technical facilitation of consultations with the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities and other relevant government and electoral stakeholders.
- Prepare briefing materials and technical inputs for consultations.
- Document agreed actions, responsibilities, required information and outstanding issues.

**D. Accessible Communication and Commitment Day**

- Provide technical input to four accessible videos, ensuring consistency with the policy recommendations.
- Coordinate with the Media and Communications Specialist on accessible and consistent public messaging.
- Support the preparation and delivery of Commitment Day, including presentation of the four reforms and supporting evidence.
- Contribute to a commitment matrix capturing stakeholders, commitments, next steps and indicative timelines.

**E. Quality Assurance and Reporting**

- Review outputs for technical accuracy, clarity, consistency and alignment with project objectives.
- Ensure recommendations clearly identify responsible institutions and required actions.
- Incorporate UNDP feedback and finalize outputs within agreed timelines.

**3. EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The Consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities within 2 months (without exceeding 18 working days per month).

**4. INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

With day-to-day management the designated project manager or institutional focal point.

UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely thorough and transparent manner. UNDP will be also responsible to provide clarifications and facilitation of the work.

Day-to-day transportation from home to office (and own means. The Consultant will rely on his own means of communication and transportation.

**5. DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 2 months without exceeding 18 working days per mo

**DUTY STATION**  
The consultant will work from home, with occasional meetings with UNDP.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- Education: A Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, Sociology, Humanities, International Relations, Development studies, social sciences, or a related field is required.
- Experience: A minimum eight (8) years of relevant experience in work related to Persons with Disabilities (PWDs), PWD-led organizations, civil society, human rights, social inclusion, participation, rights-based programming, or disability-related research and data.
- Language: Fluency in English and Arabic.

**“The Personnel will be covered with Health insurance and Personal accident insurance; the fees shall be deducted from personnel's monthly payment”.**

title: Clerk of Works
source: Mission for Essential Drugs and Supplies
body:
Mission for Essential Drugs and Supplies (MEDS) is a faith-based health solutions provider founded by an ecumenical partnership of the Kenya Conference of Catholic Bishops (KCCB) and the Christian Health Association of Kenya (CHAK). The Organization’s core mandate is being a reliable provider for quality and affordable Health Products and Technologies, Quality Assurance and Health Systems Strengthening Services. MEDS was established in 1986 and serves clients spread throughout Kenya, other regions in Africa and beyond.

Project Summary  
MEDS is undertaking a project for construction of a warehousing facility for handling of Health Products and Technologies (HPTs) and an office block in Kisumu County. The Clerk of Works reports to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO). This position is responsible for ensuring that construction work meets project plans, specifications, safety standards and quality requirements. Job holder will be on a fixed term contract of 12 months with possibility of extension.

Key Responsibilities:  
i) Supervise and monitor works on construction site to ensure compliance with approved drawings, specifications and quality standards  
ii) Inspect and verify materials delivered and used on site for conformity to specifications and quality standards  
iii) Monitor workmanship across architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical and plumbing works  
iv) Maintain detailed site records, including site daily diaries, defect registers and instruction book for architect and consultants  
v) Act as a liaison between architect, project manager, consultants, contractor(s) and Management, communicating instructions and resolving issues for smooth project execution  
vi) Report deviations, defects and non-conformities promptly and follow up on execution of corrective and preventive measures  
vii) Ensure that design and construction work comply with statutory and regulatory requirements for handling of HPTs, including but not limited to, Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), Good Storage Practices (GSP), Good Distribution Practices (GDP) as well as health and safety requirements  
viii) Identify potential problems proactively, advise on technical issues and help in solution development to support timely delivery of the project within budget and quality expectations  
ix) Prepare and submit progress reports to Management on work progress, quality and site conditions.

Candidate Profile:  
i) Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, construction management or related field from a recognized institution  
ii) Professional certification or membership with a relevant body (e.g., Institute of Clerk of Works, Engineers Board of Kenya, or equivalent)  
iii) Minimum five (5) years work experience in supervision of large-scale construction projects  
iv) Thorough understanding of construction drawings, specifications, and Bills of Quantities  
v) Strong knowledge of building codes, standards, statutory and regulatory requirements with emphasis on storage for HPTs  
vi) Familiarity with Health, Safety, and Environmental requirements on construction sites  
vii) Ability to monitor construction quality, materials, and workmanship against approved standards  
viii) Technical competencies: Record keeping, Report writing, Supervision of construction projects for pharma-grade warehouses, MS Office and knowledge of project management software (MS Project Primavera) are added advantages  
ix) Behavioural attributes; High level of integrity, strong communication and interpersonal skills, keen attention to detail and commitment of quality, ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.

If you fit the profile of this position, please submit your application including:  
• Detailed CV stating your current position and salary, email address and telephone contacts  
• Names and contacts of three (3) Referees (one of whom must be a professional who has supervised you at some point in your career and another one a Senior Religious Leader);  
• Copy of National Identity Card.

title: Especialista en Finanzas
body:
Miyamoto International es una firma global de ingeniería estructural y gestión de riesgo de desastres que trabaja en la reducción de riesgos sísmicos, la respuesta a emergencias y la reconstrucción resiliente en comunidades vulnerables alrededor del mundo. A través de su área humanitaria, Miyamoto apoya a gobiernos, organizaciones no gubernamentales y comunidades afectadas por desastres naturales, brindando asistencia técnica, evaluaciones estructurales y programas de recuperación.

Contexto del Puesto

En respuesta al terremoto en Venezuela, Miyamoto International busca incorporar a un(a) Especialista Financiero que brinde soporte administrativo-financiero a las actividades de respuesta y recuperación temprana del programa. Esta persona será clave para garantizar la correcta gestión, control y reporte de los recursos financieros destinados a las operaciones de emergencia, asegurando el cumplimiento de las políticas internas de Miyamoto y de los requisitos de los donantes.

**Responsabilidades Principales**

- Gestionar y supervisar las operaciones financieras diarias del programa de respuesta al terremoto en Venezuela.
- Preparar, revisar y consolidar presupuestos, proyecciones de flujo de caja y reportes financieros periódicos (mensuales, trimestrales y según requerimiento de donantes).
- Asegurar el cumplimiento de las normativas financieras locales, las políticas internas de Miyamoto International y los requisitos contractuales de los donantes.
- Procesar pagos, reembolsos y transacciones relacionadas con actividades de campo, logística y personal.
- Mantener registros contables precisos y actualizados, incluyendo la conciliación bancaria y el control de gastos por línea presupuestaria.
- Apoyar en la preparación de auditorías internas y externas, así como en la implementación de recomendaciones de auditoría.
- Coordinar con el equipo de logística y operaciones para garantizar controles financieros adecuados en la adquisición de bienes y servicios de emergencia.
- Capacitar y brindar acompañamiento al personal de campo en procedimientos financieros y administrativos.
- Identificar riesgos financieros y proponer medidas de mitigación, especialmente en un contexto de respuesta a emergencias.
- Elaborar informes financieros para donantes, autoridades locales y la sede de Miyamoto International, según sea requerido.
- Otras funciones relacionadas que se asignen según las necesidades del programa.

**Requisitos y Calificaciones**

**Formación académica:**

Título universitario en Contaduría Pública, Administración, Finanzas, Economía o carrera afín.

**Experiencia:**

Mínimo 10 años de experiencia en gestión financiera, preferiblemente en el sector humanitario, organizaciones sin fines de lucro o proyectos financiados por donantes internacionales.

Experiencia previa en contextos de emergencia o respuesta a desastres, deseable.

Conocimiento de normativas y requisitos financieros de donantes internacionales (USAID, ECHO, Naciones Unidas, entre otros) es una ventaja.

**Habilidades y competencias:**

Dominio de herramientas de contabilidad y hojas de cálculo (Excel avanzado; conocimiento de software contable como QuickBooks, SAP u otros).

Capacidad de trabajar bajo presión y en entornos de alta demanda, propios de contextos de emergencia.

Atención al detalle y fuerte capacidad analítica.

Habilidades de comunicación efectiva, tanto escrita como verbal.

Integridad, ética profesional y compromiso con la transparencia en el manejo de recursos.

Capacidad de trabajo en equipo y coordinación con actores locales e internacionales.

**Idiomas:**

Español fluido (nativo o equivalente).

Inglés intermedio-avanzado, deseable para la comunicación con la sede internacional.

**Otros requisitos:**

Disponibilidad para viajar a zonas afectadas por el terremoto según sea necesario.

Flexibilidad para adaptarse a un entorno de trabajo cambiante y de respuesta rápida.

title: Maestral Public Finance for Children (PF4C) Expert Cohort
body:
Maestral is inviting applications for the **Maestral Public Finance for Children (PF4C) Expert Cohort**—a small group of experienced Public Finance for Children professionals who will be among the first trained to use Maestral developed public finance and investment case tools. We are looking for experts who combine strong technical knowledge with the ability to communicate complex public finance concepts clearly and engage effectively with governments and partners.

Selected participants will receive direct training from Maestral President Philip Goldman and Senior Associates, preparing them to become PF4C Experts who can introduce the tools and support their application with governments, development agencies, and other partners.

**What Maestral provides:**

- Direct training on all Maestral public finance and investment case tools
- Recognition as a Maestral PF4C Expert, part of a small group trained to introduce and apply the tools
- Paid opportunities to introduce the tools through short webinars for governments, development partners, and other organizations
- The potential for paid technical assistance assignments through Maestral when governments or partners seek deeper support to adapt, learn, or apply the tools

**What we ask of PF4C Experts:**

- Participate fully in Maestral training on the tools
- Support the introduction of the tools through short webinars and presentations
- Be available for potential short-term technical assistance assignments through Maestral to help governments and organizations adapt and apply the tools

**Maestral’s Public Finance for Children Work**

Maestral works with governments and partners to strengthen the financing of systems and services for children. Our Public Finance for Children expertise spans macroeconomic modelling, national and subnational costing, service costing, investment cases and economic evaluation, public financial management, and coordinated financial planning. Our work combines rigorous analysis with practical tools that help governments understand what quality systems and services cost, identify financing needs and priorities, and make evidence-based decisions about investing in children.

**Qualifications**

We are seeking experienced professionals with:

- An advanced degree in economics, public finance, public policy, development economics, or a closely related field. Equivalent depth of professional experience will also be considered.
- At least five years of professional experience in public finance, costing, or applied economic analysis.
- Knowledge of Public Finance for Children approaches, investment case methodologies, costing, and/or economic evaluation.
- Advanced spreadsheet modelling skills, including the ability to develop transparent, auditable models with clearly documented assumptions and data sources.
- Experience working with national public finance data and relevant international economic, demographic, and social sector data sources.
- Strong analytical discipline, including the ability to distinguish evidence from assumptions, clearly communicate limitations, and defend analysis under external review.
- Strong communication skills, with the ability to make complex public finance concepts and findings accessible to non-technical audiences and engage effectively with government and development partners.
- Professional working proficiency in English is required. Proficiency in an additional language (such as: Arabic, Chinese, French, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish) is a strong advantage.
- Experience working in child protection, social welfare, social protection, the social service workforce, health, or education.
- Experience working directly with ministries of finance or planning, co-developing tools with government teams, delivering capacity strengthening, or reviewing economic and costing models.

*Participation in the Maestral PF4C Expert Cohort does not guarantee future assignments. It provides specialized training in Maestral’s tools and positions PF4C Experts for consideration as opportunities arise to introduce and apply them in different country contexts.*

title: Deputy Director, Corporate Partnerships - US
body:
**Location:** US

**Position Status:** Full-time, Exempt, Regular

**Salary :** range from $76,800 to $91,200 commensurate with professional experience and internal equity.

**Closing date:** Please submit application by **October 14th**

[**Risk Level:**](https://library.mercycorps.org/record/47705?ln=en) **☐ Level 3 ☐Level 2** X **Level 1**

Level 1: Likely to have no contact with participants or sensitive data

## **About Prosper Global**

Barely enough is not enough for anyone. Prosper Global is a humanitarian organization working alongside communities facing conflict, climate change, and economic hardship to meet urgent needs and create the conditions for lasting progress. Today's challenges demand new solutions, so we pair local knowledge with global resources to help communities build what's needed, test what's possible, and scale what's proven so that people everywhere can pursue a full life on their own terms. In 2026, we changed our name from Mercy Corps to Prosper Global, to reflect our belief that when every community can prosper, all of humanity moves forward.

## **The Program / Department / Team**

The Philanthropic Growth and Engagement department (PG&E) works to raise private funds, cultivating and maintaining relationships with private donors; define the agency’s brand, raising our public profile and sharing stories about our work by engaging with the media, the public, and our supporters; and produces a wide range of online and offline communications.

In support of that mission, the Corporate Partnerships team develops and executes partnership strategies and initiatives to support increased revenue from top fortune 500 corporate donors and prospects. The team manages Prosper Global’s relationships with major corporate social responsibility and corporate foundation teams focused on securing six and seven-figure gifts, in-kind/probono support, brand visibility, and thought partnership. We are passionate about Prosper Global’s mission and dedicated to supporting our worldwide team that is improving the lives of 30 million people in more than 30 countries.

## **The Position**

The Deputy Director is responsible for supporting private fundraising and partnership development in support of Prosper Global’s strategic priorities, as outlined in the Pathway to Prosperity (P2P). The Deputy Director will support Directors on the corporate partnerships team to advance strategic partnerships with top donors, prospects, and influencers. The successful candidate will have relationship management experience, an understanding of Prosper Global programming and trends in philanthropy, strong written and verbal communications, and experience in project management.

## **Essential Responsibilities**

### **PRIVATE FUNDRAISING & PROJECT MANAGEMENT**

- Own a portfolio of corporate partners and prospects that are appropriate for the deputy-level role. Create partnership strategies to secure new funding and renewals through adept management of the donor lifecycle, including new business development, proposal development, closing, ongoing stewardship efforts, and renewals.
- Outside of the deputy's assigned portfolio, provide business development, stewardship, and communications support to a range of corporate donors and prospects, in alignment with P2P priorities and emerging corporate funding trends.
- Support and project manage the business development process. Write/edit concepts, proposals, pitch decks, and other fundraising materials.
- Support and project manage the development and delivery of stewardship materials such as info sheets, program updates, and formal reports.
- Support and project manage initiatives in support of corporate partnerships, including trips and meetings, profile elevating events, campaigns, and communications.
- In partnership with the Employee Impact team, support employee engagement projects to drive awareness and increase unrestricted support through workplace giving.

### **INTERNAL COORDINATION**

- Support knowledge management by maintaining donor and prospect records in Raiser's Edge NXT (CRM), SharePoint, etc. ensuring institutional knowledge is captured, shared and accessible across the team.
- Collaborate with program, technical and innovation team members to match key program needs with potential funders and develop successful proposals.
- Coordinate with program, technical, innovation, communications, and leadership team members to ensure donor engagement strategies can be effectively implemented.

### **EXTERNAL ENGAGEMENT**

- Effectively represent Prosper Global in donor and prospect meetings, communications, and at events.
- Prepare briefing materials, talking points, and other content to support colleagues and leadership in external representation.
- Maintain a comprehensive understanding of strategic priorities, relevant technical areas, and key partnerships to represent the organization and programs to internal and external stakeholders.

### **SAFEGUARDING RESPONSIBILITIES**

- Actively learn about safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work.
- Practice the values of Prosper Global including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members.
- Encourage openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.

## **Supervisory Responsibility**

None.

## **Accountability**

- **Report directly to**: Director of Development & Engagement
- **Works directly with**: Directors of Corporate Partnerships, Senior Director of Corporate Partnerships, Employee Impact Officers, Country Program teams, Award Management Team

## **Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders**

Prosper Global team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

## **Minimum Qualification and Transferable Skills**

- Proven ability to manage projects and competing priorities
- 5 years increasing responsibility in corporate fundraising or corporate social responsibility strongly preferred
- Cross cultural acumen and proven abilities to work cross functionally in a global environment.
- Strong oral and written communications skills
- Ability to work in teams to develop and execute strategy for successful partnership experience and engagement
- Understanding of international aid and development preferred
- Understanding of corporate decision-making processes preferred

## **Success Factors**

- **An outstanding project manager and relationship builder** — equally effective navigating internal stakeholder relationships and external corporate partner relationships. Able to juggle competing priorities and deadlines across multiple partnerships simultaneously.
- **A skilled cross-functional coordinator** — able to pull together the people and pieces needed to move partnerships forward and hit team-wide fundraising and engagement goals.
- **Strategic and creative** — able to identify new employee-engagement and workplace-giving opportunities, and to bring innovative thinking to stewardship and partnership development.
- **A strong communicator** — skilled at writing and editing proposals, reports, pitch decks, and stewardship materials for varied audiences.
- **Emotionally intelligent and collaborative** — able to build trust quickly, read stakeholder needs, and work smoothly across teams and cultures.
- **Grants-management experience** — comfortable overseeing award review, kick-off, reporting, and compliance for a portfolio of corporate donors without losing sight of the relationship-building side of the job.
- **Knowledgeable about the corporate landscape** — fluent in corporate decision-making processes and current CSR/philanthropy trends, with a track record of securing philanthropic support.

## **Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions**

The position is a remote position based in the United States and it requires up to 10% travel to support prospect and partnership development.

## **Ongoing Learning**

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development

## **Team Engagement and Effectiveness**

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

## **Equal Employment Opportunity**

Prosper Global is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.

## **Safeguarding and Ethics**

Prosper Global is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC **and have signed on to** [**the Interagency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme**](https://www.schr.info/the-misconduct-disclosure-scheme). We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to [Prosper Global Code of Conduct Policies](https://www.mercycorps.org/who-we-are/ethics-policies) and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct elearning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Prosper Global Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@prosperglobal.org).

title: Conseiller en Pédagogie et Curriculum
body:
**Background**

La société de Développement International, un organisme de Recherche & Développement ayant son siège social au Canada est à la recherche de plusieurs experts pour la mise en œuvre d’un système intégré de gestion et d’amélioration des apprentissages dans l’enseignement primaire en Centrafrique.

**Objectifs de la mission**

L’objectif de la mission est d’établir et co-exploiter un **système éducatif intégré, axé sur les données**, afin d'améliorer la qualité de l'enseignement et les résultats d'apprentissage du CI au CM2, tout en renforçant la gouvernance, la transparence et la capacité institutionnelle du Ministère de l’éducation Nationale.

**Objectifs spécifiques**

- Déployer une plateforme technologique de bout en bout couvrant la planification pédagogique, le suivi de l'exécution, la redevabilité, la performance et le rapportage à plusieurs niveaux.
- Assurer l'assistance technique pour la co-production des ressources pédagogiques structurées alignées sur le programme national révisé et intégrées à la plateforme.
- Former et accompagner les enseignants, directeurs, conseillers pédagogiques et inspecteurs dans un cadre axé sur les données.
- Fournir un service de suivi académique et de monitoring de la mise en œuvre garantissant une exécution de haute-fidélité, avec des mécanismes de résolution d'incidents et d'assurance qualité.
- Établir les conditions d'une appropriation complète par le gouvernement (systèmes, transfert de compétences, gouvernance et financement), avec un plan de transition mesurable.

**Livrable attendus :**

Le prestataire d'assistance technique proposera (en collaboration avec les autres membre de l’équipe) une liste détaillée et un calendrier des livrables, comprenant au minimum :

- **Rapport de démarrage :** gouvernance, plan de travail, plan de déploiement, gestion des risques, méthodologie d'exécution de la mission co-conçue, Suivi & Évaluation (S&E), sauvegardes, plan de transition.
- **Plateforme opérationnelle :** modules activés, paramétrages, tableaux de bord, gestion des accès et documentation.
- **Infrastructures et équipements :** plan de passation des marchés pour les biens et services non-consultants destinés à la mise en œuvre par le MEN, si possible, gestion des appareils mobiles (MDM), inventaire, assistance et politique de remplacement.
- **Contenu pédagogique :** guides de l'enseignant numériques + supports imprimés, évaluations, plans de formation (initiale et continue).
- **Formation et coaching :** modules, sessions, rapports de participation/d'utilisation, plans de soutien basés sur la performance.
- **Supervision et qualité :** outils d'audit, rapports mensuels de fidélité d'exécution, résolution des tickets, recommandations.
- **Centre de commande :** conception, installation, tableau de bord d'aide à la décision, transfert de compétences et rapport d'initiative d'accompagnement de proximité (*hand-holding*).
- **Rapports périodiques :** mensuels/trimestriels (progrès, indicateurs clés de performance (KPI), enseignements tirés, assiduité, qualité, risques).
- **Plan de transition et d'appropriation co-développé :** feuille de route détaillée, jalons, indicateurs de transfert de préparation, mécanisme de certification et passation des responsabilités.

**Qualification d'ordre général**

- Diplôme : Master (BAC+5) en éducation, développement de curriculum ou domaine étroitement connexe
- Expérience professionnelle d'au moins10 ans dans le développement de curriculum, la conception de pédagogie structurée ou la formation des enseignants

**Compétence pertinente avec la mission**

- Expérience avérée dans la conception de guides de leçons structurés et de matériels d'enseignement et d'apprentissage pour des programmes gouvernementaux à grande échelle
- Connaissance des modèles de curriculum axés sur les compétences et de la conception d'évaluations formatives
- Expérience de travail dans le cadre des curricula nationaux

**Expérience de région et de la langue :** Avoir la maîtrise de la région et de la langue

La société de Développement International, un organisme de Recherche & Développement ayant son siège social au Canada est à la recherche de plusieurs experts pour la mise en œuvre d’un système intégré de gestion et d’amélioration des apprentissages dans l’enseignement primaire en Centrafrique.

**Objectifs de la mission**

L’objectif de la mission est d’établir et co-exploiter un **système éducatif intégré, axé sur les données**, afin d'améliorer la qualité de l'enseignement et les résultats d'apprentissage du CI au CM2, tout en renforçant la gouvernance, la transparence et la capacité institutionnelle du Ministère de l’éducation Nationale.

**Objectifs spécifiques**

- Déployer une plateforme technologique de bout en bout couvrant la planification pédagogique, le suivi de l'exécution, la redevabilité, la performance et le rapportage à plusieurs niveaux.
- Assurer l'assistance technique pour la co-production des ressources pédagogiques structurées alignées sur le programme national révisé et intégrées à la plateforme.
- Former et accompagner les enseignants, directeurs, conseillers pédagogiques et inspecteurs dans un cadre axé sur les données.
- Fournir un service de suivi académique et de monitoring de la mise en œuvre garantissant une exécution de haute-fidélité, avec des mécanismes de résolution d'incidents et d'assurance qualité.
- Établir les conditions d'une appropriation complète par le gouvernement (systèmes, transfert de compétences, gouvernance et financement), avec un plan de transition mesurable.

**Livrable attendus :**

Le prestataire d'assistance technique proposera (en collaboration avec les autres membre de l’équipe) une liste détaillée et un calendrier des livrables, comprenant au minimum :

- **Rapport de démarrage :** gouvernance, plan de travail, plan de déploiement, gestion des risques, méthodologie d'exécution de la mission co-conçue, Suivi & Évaluation (S&E), sauvegardes, plan de transition.
- **Plateforme opérationnelle :** modules activés, paramétrages, tableaux de bord, gestion des accès et documentation.
- **Infrastructures et équipements :** plan de passation des marchés pour les biens et services non-consultants destinés à la mise en œuvre par le MEN, si possible, gestion des appareils mobiles (MDM), inventaire, assistance et politique de remplacement.
- **Contenu pédagogique :** guides de l'enseignant numériques + supports imprimés, évaluations, plans de formation (initiale et continue).
- **Formation et coaching :** modules, sessions, rapports de participation/d'utilisation, plans de soutien basés sur la performance.
- **Supervision et qualité :** outils d'audit, rapports mensuels de fidélité d'exécution, résolution des tickets, recommandations.
- **Centre de commande :** conception, installation, tableau de bord d'aide à la décision, transfert de compétences et rapport d'initiative d'accompagnement de proximité (*hand-holding*).
- **Rapports périodiques :** mensuels/trimestriels (progrès, indicateurs clés de performance (KPI), enseignements tirés, assiduité, qualité, risques).
- **Plan de transition et d'appropriation co-développé :** feuille de route détaillée, jalons, indicateurs de transfert de préparation, mécanisme de certification et passation des responsabilités.

**Qualification d'ordre général**

- Diplôme : Master (BAC+5) en éducation, formation des enseignants, leadership éducatif ou domaine connexe
- Au moins 10 ans d'expérience dans le développement professionnel des enseignants, les systèmes d'accompagnement structuré ou l'amélioration des établissements scolaires

**Compétence pertinente avec la mission**

- Expérience avérée dans la conception et la mise en œuvre de programmes de Formation des Formateurs
- Expérience des cadres structurés d'observation en classe et de l'accompagnement fondé sur les données

**Expérience de région et de la langue :** Avoir la maîtrise de la région et de la langue

title: Rwanda Quantity Surveyor Lead (Fixed-Term)
body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Rwanda program, founded in 2007 is our largest and operates under the local brand Tubura. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chili.

## **About the Role**

Seeking an experienced Quantity Surveyor with over 5+ years to manage $8M+ USD in infrastructure projects at Rwanda Institute of Conservation Agriculture (RICA) in Bugesera/Rwanda, ensuring on-time and on-cost construction delivery for One Acre Fund.

## **Responsibilities**

Projects Cost Planning, Budget Control & Value Engineering

- Take ownership of cost control and financial performance for the RICA Seed Centre construction project, bulk utilities ( water and electricity) supply, and pivot center irrigation installation project, ensuring delivery within approved budgets and timelines.
- Lead cost planning, estimation, forecasting, and cost-to-complete assessments to support informed projects decisions.

Quantity Surveying, Tendering & Commercial Management

- Conduct market price surveys and engage suppliers, manufacturers, and dealers to validate pricing, assess market trends, and secure competitive rates.
- Maintain accurate commercial records and correspondence, ensuring compliance with contractual obligations, procurement procedures, and relevant construction regulations.

Construction Cost Monitoring & Implementation Oversight

- Monitor project expenditure, commitments, variations, and forecast costs against approved budgets, recommending corrective actions where necessary.
- Coordinate material ordering and cost oversight with the relevant project teams to support efficient utilisation, minimise waste, and maintain construction progress.

Financial Reporting, Payments & Contract Reconciliation

- Prepare and maintain project cash-flow forecasts, cost-to-complete projections, and regular financial reports highlighting variances, risks, and decisions required.
- Review contractor, consultant, and subcontractor payment claims with the project team, verifying completed works, contractual entitlements, and supporting documentation.

Inventory Control, Team Coordination & Compliance

- Supervise the Inventory Coordinator to ensure construction materials are accurately recorded, appropriately stored, and managed in line with project requirements.
- Monitor material receipts, issues, balances, and usage records through the Inventory Coordinator, investigating discrepancies and supporting accurate reconciliation.

People & Stakeholder Management

- Directly supervise and support the Inventory Coordinator, providing clear priorities, guidance, and accountability for accurate inventory management.
- Collaborate closely with the Construction Project Manager, construction supervision team, procurement colleagues, contractors, consultants, and suppliers to achieve project cost and delivery objectives.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Bachelor’s degree in Quantity Surveying or a closely related field.
- At least 5 years of relevant quantity surveying experience, including cost management on construction projects of comparable scale and complexity, with a value of approximately USD 8 million or RWF 12 billion.
- Registration with the Rwanda Institute of Quantity Surveyors or another recognised professional quantity surveying institution.
- Strong understanding of construction methods, measurement standards, contract administration, procurement processes, and applicable building regulations.
- Works effectively with project teams, contractors, consultants, suppliers, and procurement colleagues.
- Demonstrated experience in cost planning, budget monitoring, contractor claims, variation assessments, financial reporting, and commercial negotiations.
- Experience using relevant quantity surveying and cost-estimation software, spreadsheets, and project management tools.

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Bugesera, Rwanda

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits.

## **Contract Duration**

2 years.

## **Eligibility**

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Rwanda.

## **Application Deadline**

31 October 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

## **Why Work Here**

We’re one of the largest agricultural organizations in Africa, operating in ten countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers.  
Guided by our mission, we use the discipline of a business to deliver cost-effective services to millions of people. We believe that heart plus rigor can change the world. [Read more.](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here)

## **Job Application Process**

We use a unique, hands-on interview process to ensure a great match.  
We're constantly seeking exceptional leaders from a diversity of backgrounds and experiences. We strongly encourage applications from African professionals with deep local knowledge and investment in the communities we serve. [Read more.](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/applying-one-acre-fund/job-application-process)
