title: Oficial MEAL - Caracas (Personal Nacional)
body:
Danish Refugee Council (DRC) es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, en el marco de la respuesta de emergencia al terremoto, DRC está buscando un/a Oficial MEAL altamente calificado/a con sede en Caracas, Venezuela.

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC administra sus operaciones en Venezuela bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela implementa actividades de monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para personas con necesidades específicas (PWSN), sesiones informativas para personas de interés (PoC), prevención de la trata de personas y seguridad alimentaria.

En el marco de la respuesta de emergencia al terremoto ocurrido en el mes de junio 2026, DRC está abriendo una nueva oficina de implementación en Caracas, independiente de la oficina de país, para atender las necesidades de las poblaciones afectadas. Para ello, busca incorporar un/a Oficial MEAL, es requerida una alta eficacia en el monitoreo y evaluación de actividades para medir la calidad de implementación de DRC en el país.

**Objetivo general del puesto:**

El objetivo principal del Oficial MEAL (OMEAL) es apoyar en la implementación de la estrategia para monitorear y evaluar la calidad de los proyectos de DRC en Venezuela, incluyendo la acción en el marco de respuesta a la emergencia por los Terremotos, según indicadores internos, indicadores de donantes, y principios de monitoreo y evaluación estándar. Llevará a cabo actividades operativas de seguimiento a los indicadores, reportes en formatos de donante y control de medios de verificación digitales, levantar alertas de subejecución en el monitoreo mensual a la gerencia, mantener bases de datos y IPTTs actualizados mensualmente y de fácil acceso a los miembros del equipo del proyecto y de la oficina nacional. Bajo supervisión técnica del Gerente MEAL, tendrá que articularse con los equipos de terreno, gerentes técnicos de las bases y coordinadores técnicos programáticos de la oficina nacional de Caracas, para implementar las actividades de monitoreo, en el marco de la estrategia de MEAL.

**Responsabilidades:**

**Monitoreo y Evaluación:**

- Apoyar la implementación de la estrategia MEAL para los programas humanitarios de DRC de las bases a nivel nacional, con mayor énfasis en el apoyo para la respuesta a la emergencia por el terremoto.
- Diseño, implementación y seguimiento mensual de la Indicator Performance Tracking Table (IPTT) para mantener los proyectos asignados al día, con información actualizada y verificada.
- Llevar a cabo actividades de recopilación y análisis de datos cuantitativos y cualitativos de los proyectos asignados.
- Validar y resguardar adecuadamente cada medio de verificación de los proyectos asignados de manera digital y/o física, según corresponda.
- Garantizar la adecuada recolección de datos en los estudios realizados por la organización.
- Apoyar el diseño y la puesta a prueba de herramientas de seguimiento que se utilizarán durante las actividades y la asistencia.
- Apoyar en el diseño e implementación de metodologías de evaluación de los programas DRC.
- Levantar alertas mensuales conforme a la planificación de actividades de los proyectos asignados a la gerencia MEAL nacional.
- Seguimiento mensual a socios implementadores para garantizar un flujo de información bidireccional y una implementación limpia y actualizada de los proyectos asignados.
- Conocer los planes de trabajo de los proyectos asignados, para así proponer estudios de mediciones de evaluación, impacto, sostenibilidad, entre otros, necesarios para garantizar la calidad de los programas desarrollados por DRC en Venezuela.
- Alinearse en la revisión mensual nacional del doble conteo de beneficiarios en la BBDD nacional con el resto del equipo MEAL.
- Apoyar la recolección de datos para evaluaciones (línea base, intermedia y final).
- Coordinar logísticamente el desarrollo de aplicación de encuestas post distribución.
- Coordinar logísticamente encuestas, grupos focales, entrevistas en terreno con apoyo del equipo de las bases.
- Validar que los instrumentos se apliquen correctamente.
- Proveer contexto territorial para la interpretación de resultados.
- Visitas a terreno frecuentemente con el equipo para la validación del uso correcto de los verificadores y llenado adecuado de los mismos.

**Reporte y manejo de información**

- Responsable de la limpieza de las bases de datos construidas para para consolidación de datos a nivel nacional.
- Reportar avance en los indicadores de sus proyectos a la gerencia MEAL, Gerencias Bases, equipos de terreno, socios implementadores y a cualquier otro actor requerido mensualmente.
- Presentar informes mensuales a la unidad MEAL nacional sobre los logros y desafíos relacionados con el monitoreo de los proyectos asignados.
- Producir informes de seguimiento periódicos para garantizar que los programas tengan datos precisos y útiles para informar el desarrollo del proyecto.
- Participar en la evaluación interna del programa.
- Control de calidad y supervisión de los datos que se recogen, realizar visitas frecuentes a terreno para supervisar esta calidad. Identificar y abordar los errores en la recogida y/o en la introducción de datos.
- Participación de las reuniones de revisión de PiP, teniendo la información actualizada de los proyectos asignados, es decir, manteniendo el corte cuantitativo mensual limpio (IPTT) y al día en coordinación constante la Gerencia MEAL nacional.
- Diseño de herramientas visuales que permitan dar avance de las actividades desarrolladas de los proyectos asignados.
- Manejo de bases de datos de los proyectos asignados (query) y producción de información consolidada en power bi – Automatización de sistemas de información.

**Rendición de Cuentas (MPQR):**

- Asegurarse de que las actividades cumplan con los principios de rendición de cuentas a comunidades de DRC.
- Asegurar el uso adecuado de los medios de verificación, establecido para cada programa Humanitario del DRC.
- Apoyar la implementación de los mecanismos de retroalimentación y quejas del DRC Venezuela.
- Durante las actividades de seguimiento, garantizar que los beneficiarios sean tratados con respeto, confidencialidad y consentimiento informado.
- Tener dentro de los proyectos asignados el registro de retroalimentaciones recibidas para rendir cuentas a donantes al respecto.
- Visitas permanentes a actividades de terreno para la verificación de uso adecuado de los canales y la transmisión de mensajes claves.
- Apoyo en la sistematización mensual de las papeletas físicas de los buzones de retroalimentaciones que llegue pro valija a la base de datos nacional.

**Conocimiento de Indicadores del(los) Proyecto(s):**

- Revisar con regularidad el Plan MEAL con los indicadores de los proyectos asignados para verificar el cumplimiento metodológico de los mismos.
- Entender las diferencias entre los indicadores de productos y resultados de los proyectos asignados para poder generar herramientas de seguimiento y de recolección de información adecuadas para dar respuesta a dichos indicadores.
- Estar atento a los indicadores de productos generales de los proyectos asignados, que solicitan ser medidos a través de estudios de línea base, salida o en momentos específicos.

**Gestión y articulación:**

- Servir de enlace con los programas y operaciones para asegurar un seguimiento rápido de la retroalimentación y las quejas recibidas.
- Articularse con la unidad de gestión de la información IM, en el manejo de las bases de datos asignadas.
- Consolidar la base de datos y registros seguros y confidenciales de quejas y reclamos del DRC.
- Articularse con equipos de terreno de las bases a nivel nacional.
- Articulares y comunicarse periódicamente con el equipo MEAL – IM de la oficina nacional.
- Mantener comunicación constante con la línea técnica de la gerencia MEAL de la nacional.

**Experiencia y competencias:**

- Experiencia laboral de mínimo 3 años en actividades relacionadas con MEAL.

title: Agriculture, Market Systems and Climate Finance Senior Advisor, VisionFund International
body:
**Agriculture, Market Systems and Climate Finance Senior Advisor, VisionFund International**

VisionFund International is World Vision’s microfinance provider serving vulnerable clients through loans, savings, and insurance. We enable families to grow their livelihoods in hard to reach, rural locations in 28 countries so that caregivers can create secure futures for their children.

We believe in brighter futures for children; empowering families to create incomes and jobs; unlocking economic potential for communities to thrive.

Join VisionFund as we seek to end intergenerational poverty through microfinance.

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **Agriculture, Market Systems and Climate Finance Senior Advisor**, you will serve as the technical lead and focal point internally and externally for these three important, connected, and strategic areas of intervention for VisionFund. You will provide technical advice on current best practices, support the development of related products, guide strategy and organisational positioning, and support resource development and programme management for related Agricultural, Climate, and Market Systems initiatives and grants.

You will manage the CrediEnterprise credit product pilot project in nine countries in Africa and Central America as part of the THRIVE 2030 programme, ensuring it delivers on its targets while coordinating with and reporting to World Vision partners. You will oversee grant reporting, project management, operational delivery, capacity building of national staff, and integration of this component with other interventions within the THRIVE 2030 programme.

You will provide technical leadership to position VisionFund for institutional funding to support its growing Agricultural, Climate, and Market Systems interventions globally. You will support donor pre-positioning, grant writing, and the Resource Development team with technical content throughout proposal development processes.

**Technical Advisory**

You will provide technical advice to VisionFund Operations and MicroFinance Institutions across the network on Agricultural, Market Systems, and Climate industry best practices. You will lead VisionFund’s Internal Climate Financing working group, using your knowledge and experience to shape VisionFund strategy, products, and market positioning. You will also represent VisionFund in technical working groups, including Environmental and Climate Action forums, to communicate VisionFund strategy and strengthen brand visibility within the World Vision partnership.

**Resource Development**

You will support resource development activities for Agricultural, Climate, and Market Systems initiatives through grant writing, review, and donor positioning. You will provide technical advice and content for new and existing grant applications, lead VisionFund’s positioning with agricultural, climate, and market systems-focused donors and opportunities, and leverage learnings from the implementation of CrediEnterprise under THRIVE 2030 to pursue additional institutional funding.

You will represent the organization in technical grant calls and donor visits as needed, establish a mechanism for tracking ESCA climate-finance engagements and opportunities, and provide technical advisory support for the implementation of new and ongoing institutional funding in partnership with the Resource Development and Operations teams. You will also lead sector learning, evidence documentation, and dissemination to support VisionFund’s positioning and acquisition activities.

**Operational Delivery**

You will oversee the implementation of CrediEnterprise as part of the THRIVE 2030 programme and other relevant Agricultural, Climate, and Market Systems projects. You will manage CrediEnterprise implementation to achieve THRIVE 2030 targets, working closely with MFI Country Managers and World Vision field offices. You will supervise product training rollout and provide ongoing coaching and mentoring to MFI staff.

You will support the gathering of commodity profiles for the agrocalculator, lead the replication of standard tools and processes developed by Operations into CrediEnterprise projects, and ensure CrediEnterprise figures are accurately reflected in core banking and impact tracking systems. You will monitor performance metrics, assess progress, resolve implementation bottlenecks, and agree on corrective actions with MFIs, escalating issues to Regional and Operational Directors as needed.

You will ensure quality control of MFI partnerships supporting CrediEnterprise implementation, ensure integration with other financial products such as insurance and savings, and maintain coordination and differentiation between Savings Group linkage and the CrediEnterprise product. You will support MFIs in recruiting and developing Agri and Business Development Officers, provide training on THRIVE 2030, monitoring and evaluation, and reporting standards, and build the capacity of CrediEnterprise managers to use the e-THRIVE platform and other World Vision digital platforms for decision-making.

**Programme Reporting and Knowledge Management**

You will lead market systems, agricultural, and climate finance reporting, particularly for CrediEnterprise THRIVE 2030 programme reporting, learning, and knowledge management. You will establish a structured monitoring and evaluation framework, in collaboration with the VFI Global Impact team, to track product performance, gather field data, and assess client feedback.

You will coordinate technical input into VisionFund’s quarterly DME and narrative reporting for THRIVE 2030 quarterly AP and donor progress reports, aligned with THRIVE DME indicators. You will review quarterly THRIVE 2030 market systems reports to identify opportunities to scale CrediEnterprise financing across THRIVE countries and participate in regular country-specific quarterly THRIVE report reviews.

You will develop annual priorities, implementation plans, and budgets for the function in alignment with available resources. You will also develop case studies, implementation briefs, and other learning products to support Community of Practice learning.

**Requirements include:**

- 10 years' experience agri, climate and market systems finance, preferably in Africa
- Agricultural Economics or relevant agricultural degree (or equivalent practical experience). Post-graduate level degree
- Proven experience in market systems and agricultural lending i.e. understands farmer value chains production cycles and cashflows
- Able to communicate the fundamentals of market systems and climate resilience
- Proven ability to implement projects - action oriented, proven ability to implement and follow up
- Good communication skills with staff and partners
- Demonstrated experience in partnering, grant applications, reporting and other writing skills
- Experience across a range of countries (not limited to one or two places is a plus)
- Experience of Value chain/market systems financing or finance to agricultural cooperatives
- Demonstrated experience of working on and or designing programs with a climate change component
- Working level proficiency of written and verbal English. Spoken and written Spanish or French will be a plus

**Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement:** The position requires ability and willingness to travel domestically and internationally up to **35%** of the time.

title: Job Counselor
body:
**BACKGROUND**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries, the IRC aims to restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. In response to the arrival of refugees in Greece in 2015, the IRC has been offering SMS, WASH and Protection services. Among others, through its child protection programs, the IRC has been offering individual support through case management to vulnerable children and their families, non-formal educational activities for children through Safe Healing and Learning Spaces and emergency accommodation and protection to unaccompanied children.

**SCOPE OF WORK**

Since 2017, IRC Hellas supports vulnerable youth refugee and host communities in Athens to access income generation through employment and self-employment services and skills-building activities, directly and in collaboration with partners. Building on this experience, IRC Hellas, with the support of UNHCR and in partnership with the Municipality of Thessaloniki, is implementing the Youth Empowerment and Self-Reliance project for the third year to promote socio-economic equal access for vulnerable youth in Thessaloniki.

To support with the implementation of the project, IRC Hellas is recruiting a Job Counselor, to be responsible for the day-to-day implementation of employability activities, including service mapping, stakeholder engagement, job counseling and Job Readiness Trainings.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Organize needs assessment and service mapping activities related to employability and skills development programming for youth;
- Participate in stakeholder engagement activities;
- Support the project implementation by designing, organizing and leading Job Readiness Trainings and information sessions for youth;
- Support the project implementation by providing individual employment support/job counseling for youth;
- Proactively working to identify issues related to clients’ participation and report them to the Project Manager.
- Ensuring relevant project data is accurately collected and updated on a weekly and monthly basis.
- Coordinate closely with the team to ensure effective implementation of the provided activities;
- Participate in regular team meetings;
- Ensure regular reporting from the projects is compiled and reports are submitted to the Senior Livelihoods Manager on a weekly/monthly basis;
- Any other task designated by the Project Manager as requested.

**REQUIREMENTS**

BA/BS Degree in social sciences, education, project management, and/or related certification required. Master’s degree or additional certification in Job Counseling is strongly preferred.

- Minimum 2 years’ experience in training, employment support, counseling or project management, primarily in relation to refugee protection. NGO experience preferred.
- Strong interest in supporting refugees and vulnerable populations (experience supporting youth a plus)
- Demonstrated understanding and ability to maintain confidentiality and respect for clients and partners
- Good interpersonal and strong negotiation skills essential with experience in conflict resolution desirable
- Excellent verbal communication skills
- Strong liaison and diplomatic skills
- Punctuality and attention to detail
- Computer skills, in particular Excel
- Fluency in both Greek and English is mandatory

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**

**Working hours:** 9:00-17:00

**Travel and other requirements:** Occasionally to other areas of IRC programs in Greece.

**Disclaimer Clause:** This job description is not an exhaustive list of the skills, effort, duties and responsibilities associated with position.

Due to the expected high number of applications, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: €1,631/month). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Training Officer
body:
*This position is contingent on receipt of grant funding.*

**Job Overview**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the leading providers of high-quality programming for refugees resettling to the United States. The IRC is committed to developing innovative programs that respond to the refugees’ unique strengths and needs, using our learning and experience to shape policy and practice, and highlighting and promoting best practices in refugee services provision.

The IRC is seeking a Training Officer for Switchboard, a project that provides training and capacity-building services to service providers in the United States, including resettlement agencies and affiliates, state agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others. More information about Switchboard can be found at [www.SwitchboardTA.org](https://reliefweb.int/file:///C:/Users/TigestCo/AppData/Local/Microsoft/Olk/Attachments/ooa-fefcb179-4b91-4707-b044-59e9496f57fe/69780562696ebcadf2340c5c93711aeb96e9493d8b84ea912d714b7dd9c61fdb/www.SwitchboardTA.org).

The Training Officer will be responsible for leading the development and delivery of capacity-building initiatives related to newcomer and refugee services. This role includes providing training and technical assistance to service providers to support them in addressing the general resettlement and case management needs of refugees and newcomers. This role requires prior direct service experience working with clients, subject matter experts, and/or partners to develop culturally responsive service plans to address individual and family client needs utilizing a broad range of approaches, including client-centered, strength-focused, and trauma-informed to meet the social, safety and stability of newcomers.

This staff will be responsible for producing and maintaining high-quality performance by collaborating with experts, designing effective resources, and facilitating learning experiences that contribute to improving outcomes for children, adults, and families.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Training and Technical Assistance**

- Develop and deliver training related to refugee and newcomer services, to include webinars, self-paced, e-learning courses, online certificate courses, in-person training, etc.
- Provide consultation, guidance, and recommended resources via email and/or virtual meetings to refugee service providers across the U.S., in response to questions and technical assistance requests
- Produce written learning resources including blog posts, information guides and toolkits
- Incorporate feedback from internal and external reviewers
- Lead development of multimedia resources, including e-learning modules, videos, and podcasts, in collaboration with colleagues across teams
- Coordinate a monthly community of practice focused on refugee and newcomer emerging topic needs

**Project Management**

- Contribute to the creation of Switchboard’s annual training and technical assistance (TTA) workplan.
- Ensure related trainings and learning resources are developed and delivered on time and on budget.
- Use effective communication and collaborative skills with a wide range of stakeholders
- Manage external subject matter expert/consultant relationships and project plans as they contribute to the development of related TTA.

**Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E)**

- Oversee tracking of related TTA outputs and outcomes against targets (materials developed, trainings delivered, individuals participating, etc.)
- Together with Training Officers and Switchboard’s M&E team, review and analyze feedback data from related TTA participants
- Oversee provision of inputs into Switchboard reports, including monthly activity updates and semi-annual Performance Progress Reports.

*Other duties as assigned*

**Experience:**

**Required:**

- Master’s Degree in a relevant field, such as Master of Social Work (MSW) or equivalent experience.
- Minimum 6 years of direct service experience with refugees and/or other ORR-eligible populations
- Experience providing training and/or technical assistance to build the capacity of refugee service providers
- Experience providing client-centered, trauma-informed, and strength-based services for refugees
- Experience providing pre- and post-arrival services to newcomer clients, supporting their access to educational, financial, medical, social, and community resources while promoting self-sufficiency

**Preferred:**

- Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW), Master of Social Work (MSW), or equivalent experience

- Lived experience with forced displacement or shared background with newcomer populations

- Experience contributing to project M&E (data collection, management, and reporting)
- Experience with evidence-based programming

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:**

- Working knowledge of programs and services related to client-centered services for refugees and newcomer families
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with fluency in English; including engaging public speaking abilities
- Self-starter with ability to work both independently and collaboratively as a part of a team
- Capacity to give and receive constructive feedback
- Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple competing deadlines and efficient time management
- Adequate technology literacy including intermediate knowledge of MS Office Suite (Teams, Word, PowerPoint, Excel), and Zoom, with adaptability to learning new and innovative technology.

title: IT Business Relationship Director, Americas
body:
**Background/IRC Summary**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people worldwide for a better future.

The IRC's Technology department is the engine behind the organization’s ambition to reach 40 million clients by 2033. We are transforming how we work to reach more people through technology and enable faster, better decisions, whilst maintaining a reliable operational foundation that drives down the cost of delivery.

**Job Overview**

We are hiring an IT Business Relationship Director to ensure IT service delivery meets the operational needs of program offices across the Americas geography (US and LATAM), translating business needs into IT priorities and IT technical capability into business value. The role sits at the intersection of IT and program operations — building trust with leadership, diagnosing where IT processes break down, and brokering the cross-office knowledge and escalation paths that don't currently exist structurally.

This role will operate as the connective layer between IT and Resettlement, Asylum and Integration (RAI) and Crisis, Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) leadership across the US and LATAM, working alongside the Global IT Solutions team, the Americas IT Service Desk (POD) and RAI Operations staff. They will build a regular engagement cadence with RAI office and CRRD program leadership, develop enough programmatic fluency to judge whether an IT solution will work in the field, own escalations, knowing when an issue needs IT leadership, a vendor, or executive attention. The role embeds proactive communication and cross-office knowledge-sharing into how IT and program operations work together, so that consistency across offices is structural rather than dependent on individual relationships.

The ideal candidate has direct experience in complex, distributed program operations, and brings credibility with program leadership as a result — not just IT service management experience. They are equal parts relationship manager, translator, and escalation owner: able to build trust with operations staff, assess whether a proposed IT solution will hold up in the field, and judge when to resolve something directly versus route it structurally. They have a bias for proactive communication, a high bar for consistency across offices, and a clear instinct for equipping program and office staff with the tools, access, and know-how to handle their own work.

This role reports to the Senior Director, IT Business Relationship Management and partners closely with RAI and CRRD leadership through an agreed engagement model. The role will also work closely with the Global IT Solutions Team, including the Service Delivery Center of Excellence, Helpdesk team, Enterprise Applications and Infrastructure.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Relationship Management and Engagement**

- Serve as the senior IT partner to RAI office and CRRD program leadership, providing strategic guidance and thought partnership on IT service delivery performance, planned initiatives, and emerging risks across the US and LATAM
- Maintain a regular engagement cadence with RAI operations directors and senior CRRD leadership, ensuring IT priorities are aligned with program needs and that leadership has visibility of service delivery against commitments
- Act as the accountable IT point of contact for escalations from office and program leadership — owning the response, not just the routing
- Build sufficient familiarity with the programmatic context of each cluster to advise credibly on whether IT solutions will work in practice, and to represent office needs accurately to HQ IT
- Own cross-office knowledge brokering — surfacing what's working in one office to others, and serving as the connective point for "what are other offices doing on this?" questions that currently have no structural answer
- Act as the strategic focal point for IT initiative rollouts across RAI offices and CRRD programs in the Americas – shaping appropriate timing, delivery and relaying infrastructure, application, and programmatic IT needs from offices to HQ IT teams and vice versa.
- Support IT budget planning for the Americas region and ensure asset documentation, audit readiness, and regulatory compliance obligations are maintained

**Escalation, Risk Management and Service Performance**

- Own escalation pathways for issues that fall between the helpdesk and engineering teams, knowing when to involve specific IT leads, vendors, or procurement and following through to resolution
- Monitor service delivery performance and key performance indicators across the Americas region, identifying patterns and recurring issues that should trigger problem management review; escalate trending patterns as they emerge for either immediate action, system enhancement, or larger risk management
- Partner with the Global Service Desk Manager on T1/T2 technician performance, ensuring ticket priority logic and SLA adherence

**Job Requirements:**

**Knowledge & Experience**

- 6-8 years in a relationship management, business partnering, or program/operations role bridging technical and non-technical stakeholders — direct experience with humanitarian, nonprofit, or similarly complex distributed-operations environments strongly preferred
- Working knowledge of the IT service and technology lifecycle, from planning and delivery through operations and continuous improvement, sufficient to engage credibly with technical teams and evaluate whether a proposed solution is fit for purpose
- Familiarity with IT best-practice frameworks and delivery models (e.g., ITIL, Agile/Scrum, or equivalent project delivery methodologies) and how they apply to service management and technology rollouts; ITIL Foundation certification preferred, not required
- Demonstrated experience translating operational needs into technical priorities and representing technical capability back to non-technical leadership
- Experience defining and tracking performance metrics (KPIs, SLAs, or equivalent) and running a recurring review cadence with stakeholders

**Personal Attributes**

- Spanish language proficiency
- Builds credibility quickly with leadership
- Comfortable holding ambiguity and structuring it
- Strong written and verbal communication; able to translate fluently between technical and program audiences

**Working Environment**\*\*\*:\*\*\*

This position is based in the US – Hybrid. The role may require travel to US and LATAM Offices as necessary.

In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. title: Tupande Senior Quality Assurance Supervisor (Fixed-term)
body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

In Nairobi, around 50 staff support global functions like procurement, recruitment, government relations, and communications.

## About the Role

We are seeking a Senior Quality Assurance Supervisor with a minimum of 2 years experience who will support the daily compliance and quality assurance processes of the macadamia factory from receipt through processing to dispatch of products ensuring compliance to customer, internal, legal and statutory requirements

## Responsibilities

Materials Management (Raw & Processing Aids)

- Raw Material Intake: Oversee the Raw Material receiving checks. Verify the quality of incoming raw nuts (Good quality, SKR, Moisture content)
- Packaging Inventory: Manage the quality of packaging materials and other processing aids before acceptance to the processing factory

Product Integrity & Quality Assurance

- Finished Product Compliance: Oversee the grading and classification of macadamia kernels to ensure they meet international standards and customer specifications regarding size, color, and quality defect limits.
- In Process Quality Control: Manage the hourly sampling regime at key stages (Cracking, Sorting, Drying). Ensure operators are correctly identifying critical defects such as immature nuts, insect damage, and mold.
- Sensory Analysis: Enforce organoleptic testing protocols to detect early signs of rancidity (oxidative stability) or off-flavors caused by improper drying or storage.
- Hold & Release: Authority to place On Hold any batch of nuts that fails moisture specs or shows signs of contamination, preventing it from reaching the packing line.
- Verify monitoring records for defined Critical Control Points (e.g., drying temperatures for Salmonella control, metal detection for physical hazards).
- Conduct independent verification checks on CCP records to ensure accuracy and prevent record falsification
- Monitor Operational Prerequisite Programs (OPRPs) such as allergen controls (if applicable), sieving, or sorting performance.
- Immediately escalate deviations from critical limits and ensure corrective actions are implemented and documented.

Management of Team Performance (Quality of Inspectors)

- Monitoring the Monitors, You are responsible for the accuracy of your team.
    - QA Inspectors: Support in the incoming material checks, in process line checks, sorting/operators team quality of work against standards and final packing inspectors quality of work
    - Sanitation Inspectors: Inspect the cleaners work after they finish but before production starts. Provide immediate feedback if residue is found.
- Training & Competency: Maintain training matrices for both teams. Ensure sanitation staff understand Hygiene, sanitation and chemical safety and QA staff understand sampling validity, process checks and customer requirements
- Resource Allocation: Manage shift rotas to ensure coverage during peak seasons, ensuring no production line runs without QA presence and no cleanup happens without supervision.

Final Product Confirmation & Release Support

- Review laboratory results, moisture confirmations, grading reports, and packaging compliance before recommending product release
- Verify finished products meet internal specifications, export standards, and customer-specific requirements
- Ensure finished products are not dispatched without documented quality confirmation
- Maintain records of product approvals and quality release confirmations

Prerequisite Programs (PRP) Inspection & Reporting

- Conduct routine PRP inspections covering sanitation effectiveness, pest control trends, glass & hard plastic control, environmental monitoring, hygiene compliance, and waste management
- Review pest control service reports and escalate adverse trends
- Support zoning enforcement between Low Risk and High Care areas to prevent cross-contamination
- Document inspection findings and report gaps for corrective action

title: Humanitarian Access and Security Manager – Bunia / RDC
body:
Lieu : Bunia / RDC  
Date souhaitée de démarrage : Asap  
Durée de contrat : 2 mois renouvelable

Handicap International / Humanity & Inclusion (HI) est une association de solidarité internationale indépendante et impartiale, qui intervient dans les situations de pauvreté et d’exclusion, de conflits et de catastrophes. Œuvrant aux côtés des personnes handicapées et vulnérabilisées, elle agit et témoigne pour répondre à leurs besoins essentiels et améliorer leurs conditions de vie. Elle s’engage à promouvoir le respect de leur dignité et de leurs droits fondamentaux.

Depuis sa création en 1982, HI a mis en place des programmes de développement dans plus de 55 pays et intervient dans de nombreuses situations d’urgence. Aujourd'hui, nous avons un budget d'environ 200 millions d'euros, avec 4000 employés dans le monde.

Chez Handicap International, nous croyons fermement en l'importance de l'inclusion et de la diversité au sein de notre structure. C'est pourquoi nous sommes engagés dans une politique handicap afin de favoriser l'accueil et l'intégration de personnes en situation de handicap.

Merci d’indiquer si vous avez besoin d’un aménagement particulier, y compris pour participer aux 1ers entretiens. Retrouvez plus d’informations sur l’association : [www.hi.org](http://www.hi.org/).

**CONTEXTE :**   
Depuis la fin des années 1990, la RDC connaît une instabilité chronique, liée à des fragilités de gouvernance interne et à sa proximité avec des pays en crise. Cette situation limite l'accès à des services sociaux de qualité pour une population estimée entre 100 et 120 millions d'habitants. La faible gouvernance des ressources publiques affaiblit par ailleurs la gestion des risques de catastrophes : face aux crises, la réponse gouvernementale peine souvent à couvrir l'ensemble des besoins, un défi persistant pour la population.

La province de l'Ituri, à l'est du pays, illustre particulièrement cette complexité. Elle fait face à une situation humanitaire caractérisée par la persistance des conflits armés, d'importants déplacements de population et des besoins humanitaires élevés. À cette crise sécuritaire s'ajoute, depuis le 15 mai 2026, une 17ᵉ épidémie de maladie à virus Ebola déclarée dans la zone de santé de Mongbwalu. Cette flambée s'est rapidement propagée : au 21 septembre, 63 zones de santé (soit 37,7%) étaient touchées dans sept provinces, ce qui en fait, selon l'OMS et Africa CDC, la deuxième plus importante épidémie d'Ebola jamais documentée et la plus rapide en termes de croissance. La majorité des nouvelles infections provenant de chaînes de transmission non identifiées, les limites de la surveillance et du suivi des contacts demeurent un enjeu central de la réponse.

**VOTRE MISSION :**  
Dans le cadre de la réponse à l’épidémie d’Ebola, qui touche notamment l’Ituri, le Nord-Kivu, la Tshopo et le Haut-Uélé, la mission vise à accompagner l’ouverture de la base de Bunia et des installations logistiques ATLAS prévues à Nia-Nia, ainsi que, selon les besoins opérationnels, à Fataki ou dans une autre localité retenue. Elle appuiera le démarrage des activités en Ituri dans des conditions de sécurité et d’accès adaptées au contexte, tout en renforçant les capacités de l’équipe HAS locale pour assurer le suivi des opérations après le départ du Manager HAS d’appui.

Sous la responsabilité de l’area manager, vos principales responsabilités seront :

- **Sécuriser les installations HI/ATLAS :** évaluer les locaux prévus à Bunia, l’entrepôt de Nia-Nia et tout autre site logistique retenu selon les besoins opérationnels ; définir les mesures prioritaires de sûreté et de sécurité et accompagner leur mise en place avant utilisation.
- **Consolider les analyses des axes et des zones d’intervention :** exploiter les évaluations HAS existantes et les enseignements des opérations de transport déjà réalisées en Ituri, dans la Tshopo et au-delà ; formaliser les évaluations insuffisamment documentées, réévaluer les axes ou zones dont la situation a évolué, et évaluer les nouveaux axes et zones envisagés pour les opérations ATLAS.
- **Élaborer les documents HAS essentiels à l’ouverture de Bunia :** produire une version allégée et opérationnelle du plan de sécurité local, comprenant la grille complète d’analyse des risques ; un plan de contingence local et ses annexes (arbre de communication, scénarios critiques, options d’évacuation et liste de contacts) ; les principales procédures opérationnelles de sécurité (SOP) ; ainsi qu’un support de briefing sécurité pour toute personne arrivant sur la base.
- **Recruter et accompagner l’équipe HAS locale :** contribuer au recrutement des deux collaborateurs prévus, assurer leur formation pratique et les accompagner progressivement dans l’utilisation et la mise à jour des analyses, procédures et outils HAS.
- **Appuyer le démarrage et le suivi des opérations ATLAS :** conseiller les responsables opérationnels sur les conditions de sécurité et d’accès, soutenir la préparation et le suivi des mouvements, et formuler des recommandations lorsque les conditions d’une opération doivent être adaptées ou réexaminées.
- **Assurer la représentation et la coordination HAS en Ituri :** participer aux cadres locaux d’échange sur la sécurité et l’accès, notamment au Groupe de travail Accès Ituri et aux réunions hebdomadaires INSO ; entretenir les contacts utiles et partager les informations pertinentes avec les équipes HI/ATLAS.

**VOTRE PROFIL :**

- Vous possédez au moins 3 ans d’expérience sur le terrain au sein d’ONG humanitaires à des postes de Manager sécurité/ accès humanitaire en contextes d’urgence, complexes et instables ;
- Vous êtes expérimenté(e)s en gestion d’incident/de crise, en accès humanitaire et le renforcement des compétences.
- Vous maitrisez des concepts, outils et processus liés à la gestion de la sécurité et de l’accès humanitaire.
- Vous avez le sens des priorités, grande capacité d'organisation et d'autonomie ;

**CONDITIONS :**

Chez HI, les conditions de départ sont à la hauteur de votre engagement et adaptées au contexte de votre mission. Une attention particulière est portée aux questions de santé et à votre situation personnelle : [https://hi.org/fr/travailler-chez-hi](https://hi.org/fr/travailler-chez-hi)

Le poste est aussi ouvert localement.

- Contrat International de 2 mois à pourvoir rapidement basé à Bunia ;
- Le contrat international permet une couverture sociale adaptée aux besoins de chacun :
    - Assurance chômage prélevée uniquement pour les ressortissants de l’UE ;
    - Assurance retraite ;
    - Couverture santé, rapatriement, prévoyance prises en charge par HI et par l’employé ;
- **Salaire** : à partir de 2800 € brut/mois ;
- **Perdiem** : 684 € net/mois – versé en monnaie locale sur le terrain ;
- **Hardship :** 500 € net/mois
- **Congés payés** : 25 jours par an ;
- **R&R** : 5 Jours toutes les 8 semaines
- **Poste :** Non accompagné
- Logement : Collectif pris en charge par HI ;
- Si vous êtes résident(e) dans le pays : package local.

By partnering with local tree nursery operators, we raise and distribute agroforestry trees that enrich soils and build long-term financial resilience. Supported by a structured frontline field team across Central and Southern Provinces, we use rigorous, data-driven frameworks to measure our impact and ensure we drive meaningful improvements in farmer yields, asset accumulation, and food security.

## About the Role

In this role, you will establish and lead day-to-day operations for both inbound and outbound contact centre teams, drive overall Customer Experience (CX) strategies, manage SMS and external communications engagement campaigns, implement robust SOPs, and promote client protection compliance as a Customer Service Champion. You will oversee staffing, training, performance management, and KPI tracking to ensure every farmer receives high-quality, responsive, and supportive service

## Responsibilities

Contact Centre Operations & Management

- Oversee daily inbound and outbound call center operations to maintain service quality, achieve performance SLAs, and track operational KPIs.
- Manage workflows, agent scheduling, capacity planning, and operational queues for the new center.
- Develop, implement, and maintain Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for all contact center functions.

Drive Customer Experience (CX)

- Elevate CX performance through regular call monitoring, call shadowing, and structured quality assurance reviews.
- Analyze customer feedback and operational data to identify trends, pain points, and opportunities for service improvement.
- Manage and optimize client SMS and external communication campaigns to deliver timely, farmer-centered engagement.

Client Protection & Compliance

- Oversee the execution of seasonal Client Protection (CP) surveys to achieve target completion rates.
- Conduct regular quality checks on CP survey data to guarantee accuracy, completeness, and reliability.
- Monitor CP issues, manage risk escalations, and execute corrective action plans promptly.

Team Leadership & Coaching

- Directly supervise, mentor, and build capacity for inbound and outbound Contact Centre Agents.
- Conduct regular performance reviews, 1-on-1 check-ins, SLA monitoring, and targeted coaching to foster team growth.
- Lead agent onboarding, ongoing team training, and continuous skills development.

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Proven experience managing or supervising inbound and outbound contact center teams.
- Hands-on training experience designing and conducting team training programs.
- Solid background in workforce planning, scheduling, hiring, and implementing SOPs.
- Track record of driving customer experience strategies, managing external comms/SMS platforms, and innovating processes.
- Strong knowledge of client protection policies, fraud prevention, and data protection standards.
- Proficiency in Google Workspace (Google Sheets, Docs, Slides), Excel, call centre software (Zendesk, PBX, IVR), and SMS platforms
- Bachelor's degree in communications, sales, marketing, or a related field.

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Kabwe, Zambia

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Contract Duration

1 year

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Zambia.

## Application Deadline

23 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*
