Diversity and Inclusion: Lead and promote a culture of including the voices of older people across our support, convening and thought leadership roles, in a way that is transformative, empowering and highly inclusive of those marginalised by gender, economic status, disability and other factors of discrimination.

Leading Others(for managers): Demonstrate strong leadership to own unit/department and manage people in a well and reputable manner. Create an atmosphere of trust and an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential.

**Safeguarding**

HelpAge International is committed to safeguarding the communities with which we work, our partners, staff and any others who we come into contact with. The post holder will also be responsible for:

- Preventing harm and abuse from our people, operations and programmes to anyone that encounters our work.
    - Reporting all safeguarding incidents you see, hear, hear about or suspect, using our internal reporting mechanism.
    - Complying with all safeguarding framework policies and practices.
    - Completing mandatory training courses relating to our safeguarding policy framework and complying with HR vetting procedures.

**SAFER RECRUITMENT**

All employments at HelpAge International will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include misconduct disclosure schemes and terrorism finance checks.

title: Feasibility study of Integrated Transformation for Food and Nutrition Security, Resilient Livelihoods, and one Health systems in ASALs project
body:
**1.0 Background**

Malteser International (MI) is the worldwide relief agency of the Sovereign Order of Malta that has for over 60 years provided relief and recovery during and following conflicts and disasters. MI also works alongside vulnerable communities on long-term programs to deliver lasting change. Christian values and humanitarian principles form the foundations of our work: bringing aid to people regardless of their religion, background, or political convictions at over 100 Projects in more than 20 countries. MI’s vision is a life in health and dignity for all; its mission is to provide emergency relief in crises such as natural disasters, epidemics, or armed conflicts and carry out programs that enable people transform their lives for the better. The approach is to protect health by ensuring people have access to functioning medical structures, adequate nutrition, clean water, sanitation, and hygiene as well as strengthen the resilience of people in especially vulnerable regions against future crises.

**2.0 Scope of the project**

**2.1.1 Scope of the Project**

The proposed 36-month project Titled\*: Integrated Transformation for Food and Nutrition Security, Resilient Livelihoods, and One Health Systems in ASALs\* will be implemented across the Kenya–Ethiopia cross-border region, covering selected areas of Marsabit and Turkana Counties in Kenya and Dasannech Woreda in the South Omo ZoneofSouthern Ethiopia. In Marsabit County, the proposed target areas include North Horr, Maikona and Illeret Wards, together with cross-border Dasannech communities adjoining. In Turkana County, the project will cover Turkana North, Kibish and Turkana Border areas, including Nyangatom communities and cross-border areas adjoining Dasannech Woreda in South Omo, Ethiopia.

The feasibility study will assess the proposed project within its broader social, economic, institutional, environmental, operational and cross-border context. The consultant will assess conditions at macro, meso and micro levels to determine the relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, impact, coherence, and sustainability implementation requirements of the proposed interventions. Emphasis will be given to cross-border dynamics, institutional and coordination arrangements, service delivery systems, community structures, local capacities and the factors influencing health and nutrition, WASH, livelihoods, peace and social cohesion, early warning, anticipatory action and climate resilience.

At community level, the consultant will engage households, community leaders, local institutions, civil society organizations, government actors and other relevant stakeholders to assess the nature, scale and underlying drivers of food and nutrition insecurity, climate-related shocks, livestock losses, limited access to safe water, poverty, displacement, conflict and associated health and livelihood risks. Consultant will assess how these challenges are interconnected, how they affect pastoralist and agropastoral groups, and how risks and vulnerabilities are experienced across communities on both sides of the border. It will also provide an opportunity to listen to communities, local authorities, civil society organizations, and other key stakeholders and understand their priorities, capacities, and concerns.

The proposed project will apply a Humanitarian–Development–Peace (HDP) Nexus approach, recognizing the need for complementary and coordinated interventions that address immediate needs while strengthening longer-term resilience and social cohesion. The thematic scope will include Health and Nutrition, One-health, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), climate resilient livelihoods, peacebuilding and social cohesion, Early warning and anticipatory action and Institutional and technical capacity strengthening. The findings will inform areas of amendment before the full proposal is developed because of identified changes needed to the **project design, targets, indicators, roles and responsibilities, risk management, cross-border coordination, and sustainability approach** by ensuring that the final project is practical, relevant, and responsive to the context prior to submission of the project proposal to BMZ.

**2.1.2 Implementing Partners**

**PACIDA** will lead implementation in Marsabit County (North Horr, Maikona and Illeret ward) and the adjoining areas of Southern Ethiopia (Dasannech Woreda) building on its long-standing presence and operational experience in the region. **SAPCONE** will lead implementations in Turkana County (Turkana North and Kibish) and neighboring cross-border areas (South Omo region). While each organization will have a defined geographical and technical role, they will work closely together on issues that require a coordinated cross-border response.

Consultant will also assess the capacity and readiness of PACIDA and SAPCONE, as the proposed local implementing partners, to deliver the programme within their respective geographical areas and work effectively across the border. This will include their technical and operational capacity, community relationships, coordination mechanisms, existing partnerships and ability to support locally led and sustainable approaches. These findings will help ensure that the proposed programme is grounded in the realities of cross-border communities and has a realistic pathway towards achieving improved health and well-being, resilient livelihoods, stronger social cohesion, and functional early warning and anticipatory action systems.

**3.0 Rationale of the assignment**

The cross-border region of Turkana, Marsabit, and southern Ethiopia faces acute food and nutrition insecurity, with 60% of the population in IPC Phase 2–4, GAM rates of 15–25%, over 50% livestock losses, and limited access to safe water, driving poverty, displacement, conflict, and mortality risks. Communities living in cross-border areas face a combination of challenges that continue to undermine their livelihoods, health, food security, and ability to cope with shocks. Recurrent droughts, floods, conflict, livestock losses, poverty, displacement, and pressure on natural resources have made many households more vulnerable. These challenges are closely linked and often reinforce each other, making it difficult for communities to recover from recurrent shocks.

Food and nutrition insecurity remain major concerns, particularly among vulnerable households. Recurrent climate shocks affect food production and livestock, while limited livelihood opportunities and access to markets further reduce household food security. The proposed project will help communities to strengthen their ability to produce and access nutritious food, while improving access to nutrition services and promoting healthier practices at household and community level.

Health and nutrition challenges are also compounded by limited access to services in remote and conflict-affected areas. Communities, particularly vulnerable groups, have difficulty accessing timely health, nutrition and disease-prevention services. The project will therefore strengthen facility- and community-based nutrition services, One Health approaches, outreach, and disease-prevention practices, recognizes the close relationship between human, animal and environmental health in these communities.

Water insecurity is another major constraint to households. In most areas, communities face unreliable water sources, poorly functioning water systems, concerns about water quality, and limited access to sanitation and hygiene facilities. The project will address these challenges through the rehabilitation and construction of water systems, improved water governance and operation and maintenance, and sustained hygiene and sanitation behavior change.

Livelihoods are particularly vulnerable to climate variability and recurrent drought. Many households depend heavily on livestock and rain-fed agriculture, leaving them exposed to crop failure, livestock losses and declining income. The project will support more resilient livelihood options, including drought-tolerant crop and fodder production, climate-smart agriculture, sustainable rangeland management, improved livestock husbandry and diversification. It will also strengthen household economic opportunities through savings and loan groups, financial literacy, entrepreneurship, business development and improved access to markets, including linkages between local producers and schools.

Conflict and competition over natural resources further affect livelihoods, mobility and social cohesion across the border. Climate pressures increase competition over water, pasture and other resources, while existing tensions can make it more difficult for communities to respond collectively to shocks. The project will therefore strengthen local mechanisms for peacebuilding through climate and conflict analysis, gender and social inclusion approaches, stronger community peace committees, scenario and response planning, safe spaces, and youth-led cross-border peace initiatives.

Given the frequency and unpredictability of climate and conflict-related shocks, there is also a need to move beyond responding to crises after they occur. The project will strengthen early warning and anticipatory action systems, including community-based mechanisms and digital tools for monitoring climate, markets and nutrition trends. A crisis modifier will provide flexibility to redirect resources quickly when agreed triggers indicate an emerging crisis, while protecting longer-term development investments and gains.

Finally, the proposed project will respond to the interconnected nature of the challenges facing cross-border communities rather than addressing food security, health, WASH, livelihoods, peace and climate resilience separately. It will adopt Humanitarian–Development–Peace Nexus through a locally led approach.

**4.0 Scope of the assignment**

Guided by MI’s Program Team, the consultant will undertake a comprehensive feasibility study to assess the relevance, coherence, efficiency, effectiveness, impact, and sustainability of implementing the proposed project. The assignment will operationalize the feasibility dimensions required under the BENGO guidelines that are technical, financial, institutional, and socio-cultural focusing on how the project can be effectively integrated within existing health systems. Consultant will assess whether the proposed approach is relevant, realistic and responsive to the needs of communities, while identifying the capacities, systems, partnerships and resources required to achieve the intended results.

The consultant will report to MI and coordinate closely with contact with people from PACIDA and SAPCONE. The consultant will maintain professional independence in data collection, analysis, findings, conclusions and recommendations

The scope of the assignment will be guided by the four main outcomes and specific objectives proposed under the project.

**4.1.1 Specific Objectives**

To strengthen the capacity of local civil society organizations to deliver integrated, sustainable solutions for food security, peacebuilding and climate resilience in fragile ASAL cross-border regions.

**4.1.1.2 Outcomes**

**Oct.1**: Communities have improved health, nutrition and One Health systems for enhanced resilience and well-being.

**Oct.2**: Households adopt diversified climate-resilient food production systems and access sustainable income opportunities.

**Oct.3**: Capacities of formal and informal cross-border stakeholders in conflict prevention and management and social cohesion building, with particular focus on climate and women and youth, are enhanced

**Oct.4**: Early warning and anticipatory action systems are functional and responsive.

Across all the four outcomes, the consultant will consider gender equality, social inclusion, conflict sensitivity, climate change, local ownership and sustainability with particular attention to the experiences and priorities of women, youth, children, persons with disabilities, pastoralist households and other groups that may face greater barriers to services, livelihoods and decision-making.

**5.0 Methodology of Assignment**

The study will provide an opportunity to test and refine the proposed approach before the full proposal is developed. As part of this process, the proposed results framework will be reviewed to ensure that the indicators and targets are measurable, realistic and supported by available data. It will identify any gaps in baseline information and determine where additional data may be required to establish realistic targets and support effective monitoring.

The study will use a cross-sectional mixed-methods and context-sensitive approach to understand the realities of communities and institutions across Turkana and Marsabit Counties in Kenya and Daassenach Woreda, South Omo region in Southern Ethiopia using the OECD DAC criteria of relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability.

The methodology will employ desk review, quantitative and qualitative data collection, stakeholder consultations and field observations. The approach will be designed to capture both the similarities and differences across the three geographical areas, while paying particular attention to the cross-border nature of the proposed programme.

**5.1.1 Desk review and context analysis**

Consultant will begin with a review of relevant project documents, assessments, policies, strategies, and available secondary data. This will help establish a clear understanding of the social, economic, environmental, institutional, climate and conflict context in the proposed areas in relation to food and nutrition security, health and One Health, WASH, livelihoods, climate risks, livestock, conflict and social cohesion, early warning and anticipatory action.

The review will also map existing government and community systems and identify lessons from similar interventions implemented in the target areas. The analysis will be presented in macro, meso and micro levels, linking county-level policies and systems with local institutional arrangements and the experiences and priorities of communities.

**5.1.2 Stakeholder and institutional Engagements**

Consultants will engage key stakeholders at county, woreda and community levels, including government departments, local authorities, civil society organizations, community structures, private-sector actors, peacebuilding organizations, health and nutrition actors, WASH stakeholders and cross-border institutions.

The assessment will examine the roles, technical capacities, relationships and readiness of PACIDA and SAPCONE to contribute to implementation within the geographical areas as well as their ability to coordinate and work effectively across the Kenya–Ethiopia border.

**5.1.3 Community consultations**

Consultants will engage directly with communities to understand their needs, priorities, experiences and proposed solutions. Vulnerable pastoralist and agro-pastoralist will be consulted to ensure that the perspectives of women, youth, pastoralist households, persons with disabilities and other potentially vulnerable groups are adequately represented.

Qualitative methods such as focus group discussions, key informant interviews and community consultations will be used to explore issues that may not be fully captured through secondary data. In addition, early warning information will be assessed whether suitable triggers, information sources, decision-making structures and response mechanisms are available to enable timely action when climate or conflict-related risks increase.

The study will also validate the proposed figures and clarify the relationship between the household targets and the proposed overall reach of approximately 30,000 people directly and 150,000 people indirectly

**5.1.4 Proposed intervention package**

Consultant will assess whether the proposed interventions are relevant, complementary and realistic within the Marsabit, Turkana and Southern Ethiopia, Daassenach Woreda. It will identify potential gaps, overlaps or duplications, as well as activities that may need to be refined to ensure that the project remains focused, practical and manageable. The study will also examine whether the proposed implementation model is feasible given the geographical distances, infrastructure, security conditions, population mobility, institutional arrangements and cross-border dynamics in the target areas.

The study will further undertake a systematic risk and assumptions analysis and consider how these factors could affect implementation and identify appropriate mitigation measures and adjustments to the project design.

Preliminary findings will be shared with key stakeholders through a validation process to confirm that the assessment accurately reflects the realities of the target areas. Stakeholders will have an opportunity to clarify information, provide additional evidence, raise concerns and contribute to the refinement of the findings and recommendations. Feedback from the validation process will be incorporated into the final recommendations and be translated into practical actions to strengthen the project design.

The final recommendations will focus on practical adjustments to interventions, targeting, geographical coverage, indicators and targets, implementation arrangements, partnership roles, risk management, cross-border coordination and sustainability mechanisms in line with OECD DAC criteria (Relevance, coherence, sustainability, impact, effectiveness and efficiency). This will ensure that the final project design is evidence-informed, contextually appropriate and feasible to implement.

**6.0** **Ethical consideration**

Consultant will be conducted in accordance with accepted ethical principles, such as respect for participants, informed consent, confidentiality of data, maintaining privacy, voluntary participation and do no harm. Before data collection, the consultant will obtain the necessary approvals and permissions from relevant authorities and institutions in the target areas.

All participants also will be provided with clear information about the purpose of the study, why they are participating, how the information will be used, and their right to decline or withdraw from the study at any time without any negative consequences. consent will be obtained prior before interviews, focus group discussions and key informant interviews. Households with limited literacy, the information will be explained and verbally consent will be documented in an ethically appropriate manner.

Since the study will involve cross-border communities and institutions, the consultant will respect applicable national requirements, local governance structures and community protocols in both countries. The study will ensure that participation does not create unrealistic expectations regarding future programme support.

**7.0 Time frame and expectation**

Consultant is expected to complete the feasibility study within a proposed timeframe of 26 days. The final schedule will be agreed upon with MI at the contractual stage.

**7.1** **Deliverables**

- Inception report with detailed methodology, data collection tools in alignment to OECD DAC Criteria, sampling strategy, workplan and question matrix linking questions to data sources and tools.
- Final feasibility study report, presenting the methodology, findings, analysis, conclusions, risks, assumptions and practical recommendations.
- Any datasets generated and analyzed for the study, with appropriate disaggregation where available and consistent with confidentiality requirements.
- Recommendations on the project proposal, intervention logic, results framework, indicators, targets, assumptions and monitoring framework.
- Summary PowerPoint presentation highlighting key findings and recommendations.
- Presentation and discussion of findings with PACIDA, SAPCONE and Malteser International and relevant partners through a validation meeting/workshop.

**7.2** **Application and selection procedure**

**7.2.1** **Skills and Experience of Study Team**

The consultant or consulting team should collectively demonstrate the following:

- Advanced university degree in development studies, public health, agriculture, livestock development, climate change, natural resource management, peace and conflict studies, social sciences, economics, programme management or a related field.
- Proven minimum seven (7) years' experience conducting feasibility studies, assessments, evaluations or applied research for humanitarian, development, resilience or integrated programme in a cross-border setting.
- Demonstrated experience working in Kenya and Ethiopia, pastoralist or agro-pastoralist contexts.
- Relevant technical experience in food and nutrition security, livelihoods, WASH, One Health, climate resilience, peacebuilding, early warning and/or anticipatory action.
- Experience with mixed-methods studies, using qualitative and quantitative approaches, participatory community engagement and stakeholder consultation.
- Experience in undertaking organizational and institutional capacity of local civil society organizations.
- Understanding of cross-border programming, conflict sensitivity and community-based systems.
- Excellent command of written and spoken English.
- Where team is involved, the consultant should clearly state the role and responsibility of each team member and demonstrate how the combined expertise covers the scope of the assignment.

**7.3 Safeguarding and Professional Conduct**

The consultant(s) shall comply with applicable safeguarding, confidentiality, ethical and professional requirements of PACIDA, SAPCONE and Malteser International throughout the assignment. Any safeguarding concern arising during the study shall be handled through the agreed reporting channels.

title: Manager Ingénierie des Technologies de Réseau - Millennium Challenge Account (MCA) - Côte d’Ivoire Régional
body:
## À propos de MCA – Côte d’Ivoire Régional

Le Millennium Challenge Account (MCA-Côte d’Ivoire Régional), en collaboration avec le Gouvernement de la République de Côte d’Ivoire (GoCI) et le Millennium Challenge Corporation (“MCC”) du Gouvernement des États-Unis d’Amérique, met en œuvre un projet dans le cadre du Compact d’un montant de 322,5 millions de dollars. Ce programme vise à renforcer la sécurité énergétique régionale, à réduire les coûts de l’énergie et à favoriser l’accès à une électricité fiable et abordable en Afrique de l’Ouest, en améliorant la capacité de la Côte d’Ivoire à échanger de l’électricité sur le marché régional.

## Objectif du poste

Le Manager Ingénierie des Technologies de Réseau de MCA-Côte d’Ivoire relève du Directeur Infrastructure et Programmes et joue un rôle essentiel dans la mise en œuvre réussie des différents projets d’ingénierie des technologies de réseau financés dans le cadre du Compact et visant à relever les défis de développement en Côte d’Ivoire. À ce titre, il collabore étroitement avec le Gouvernement de Côte d’Ivoire, le MCA-Côte d’Ivoire, la MCC et les parties prenantes des projets (notamment CI-ENERGIES, CIE, DGE et ANARECI) afin de garantir que les solutions techniques soient conçues et mises en œuvre de manière efficace, efficiente et conforme aux normes et réglementations applicables. Il supervise les équipes chargées de la mise en œuvre des activités techniques et d’ingénierie des projets, veille à une collaboration efficace entre les équipes, à une coordination étroite avec les autres départements impliqués dans l’exécution des projets (notamment les Directeurs support WAPP et Support ERERA, la passation des marchés, les sauvegardes environnementales et sociales), ainsi qu’à une gestion rigoureuse des risques. Il s’assure également du respect des plans de travail, des budgets et des résultats attendus. Enfin, il veille à l’alignement de l’exécution des projets avec les objectifs globaux du Compact et à l’utilisation efficiente des ressources mises à disposition.

## Principales responsabilités

- Superviser la planification, la conception et la mise en œuvre des projets d’ingénierie relevant du Compact régional de MCA-Côte d’Ivoire, en veillant à leur alignement avec les objectifs du programme ainsi qu’au respect des politiques et procédures de la MCC.
- Diriger les analyses techniques, évaluations et études de faisabilité nécessaires à la conception des projets et à la prise de décision, en tenant compte des aspects environnementaux, sociaux et économiques.
- Superviser l’élaboration, la revue et la mise à jour des spécifications techniques, plans, schémas et autres documents d’ingénierie, en veillant à leur conformité aux normes et standards applicables.
- Collaborer avec l’équipe de Passation des Marchés dans la préparation et l’évaluation des dossiers d’appel d’offres, des propositions techniques et du processus de sélection des prestataires, afin de garantir la prise en compte des exigences techniques des projets.
- Représenter les projets de MCA-Côte d’Ivoire lors de réunions, conférences, ateliers et autres événements pertinents, en valorisant les réalisations, les bonnes pratiques et les résultats obtenus.
- Évaluer les composantes du projet et leurs impacts au regard des stratégies et cadres du Compact, afin de garantir l’atteinte et la pérennisation des objectifs de qualité, conformément aux exigences de Performance Environnementale et Sociale (ESP), d’Analyse Sociale (SA), de Suivi-Évaluation et Analyse Économique (MEEA), ainsi qu’aux standards de la MCC.
- Représenter les projets de MCA-Côte d’Ivoire lors de réunions, conférences et autres événements, en promouvant leurs réalisations, les bonnes pratiques mises en œuvre et leur contribution au développement du secteur.
- Veiller au respect des exigences applicables aux projets financés par les bailleurs de fonds, notamment en matière de passation des marchés, de gestion financière, de sauvegardes environnementales et sociales, ainsi que des politiques et procédures en vigueur.
- Assurer le suivi et l’évaluation de la performance des projets, proposer les ajustements nécessaires pour faire face aux risques, défis ou opportunités identifiés, et garantir l’atteinte des objectifs et résultats attendus.
- Superviser les activités de construction et de déploiement des infrastructures de réseau, en veillant au respect du périmètre des travaux, des normes de qualité, des délais contractuels et des exigences de sécurité.
- Coordonner les actions avec les responsables de MCA-Côte d’Ivoire, les administrations publiques et les autres parties prenantes afin d’assurer une communication et une collaboration efficaces tout au long de la mise en œuvre des projets.
- Fournir un appui technique et des orientations aux équipes de MCA-Côte d’Ivoire, aux représentants du Gouvernement et aux partenaires du projet sur les questions d’ingénierie et d’infrastructures de réseau.
- Superviser la préparation des rapports d’avancement, présentations et autres documents techniques relatifs aux projets, à destination des parties prenantes internes et externes.
- Conseiller les équipes sur les meilleures approches en matière de gestion des ressources, de planification et d’exécution des projets, en cohérence avec les stratégies, cadres de référence et budgets du programme MCA.
- Assurer le suivi de la performance des contrats attribués, notamment par l’examen et l’approbation des plans de travail et de mobilisation des ressources des prestataires, ainsi que par la négociation des ajustements nécessaires aux livrables contractuels.
- Se tenir continuellement informé(e) des tendances émergentes, des meilleures pratiques et des innovations dans le domaine de l’ingénierie, et contribuer au partage des connaissances au sein de l’équipe de MCA-Côte d’Ivoire Régional.

## Compétences requises

- Diplôme universitaire en ingénierie ou dans un domaine connexe. Une spécialisation en ingénierie des technologies de réseau, ingénierie des infrastructures, génie civil ou génie électrique est fortement souhaitée.
- Au moins huit (8) années d’expérience pertinente dans la planification, la conception et la mise en œuvre de projets d’ingénierie, de préférence dans le cadre de programmes de développement de grande envergure, de projets énergétiques ou de projets liés aux technologies de réseau.
- Expérience avérée de collaboration avec des administrations publiques, des agences bilatérales ou multilatérales et d’autres institutions de développement dans la mise en œuvre de projets d’ingénierie, idéalement dans les secteurs de l’énergie ou des technologies de réseau.
- Capacité à encadrer, accompagner et motiver les équipes, notamment à travers le coaching et le développement des compétences, afin d’optimiser la performance, la qualité du travail et l’atteinte des objectifs.
- Capacité démontrée à instaurer un climat de confiance au sein des équipes et à favoriser une culture de résultats et d’amélioration continue orientée vers l’impact.
- Une expérience dans le secteur de l’ingénierie en Afrique de l’Ouest subsaharienne, notamment en Côte d’Ivoire, constitue un atout ; une expérience dans les secteurs de l’énergie ou des technologies de réseau est fortement souhaitée.
- Expérience avérée dans la gestion et la livraison de projets de haute qualité, dans le respect des délais et des budgets.
- Expérience démontrée dans la gestion de projets complexes et de grande envergure, idéalement au sein d’organisations ou d’agences de développement international.
- Bonne connaissance des normes et standards internationaux applicables à la gestion des projets financés par les bailleurs de fonds, notamment la MCC, la Banque mondiale, l’USAID ou des institutions similaires.
- Expérience dans le suivi des performances et le reporting des résultats sur la base d’indicateurs et de cibles prédéfinis.
- Capacité démontrée à coordonner et fédérer des parties prenantes variées afin d’atteindre les objectifs du projet.
- Une certification en gestion de projet constitue un atout important.
- Excellente maîtrise du français à l’écrit et à l’oral ; la maîtrise de l’anglais professionnel est fortement souhaitée.

title: Subawards Compliance Finance Officer, Puerto Rico or Colombia
country: Puerto Rico (The United States of America)
body:
**Location:** Puerto Rico or Colombia  
Valid unrestricted work authorization in the country in which you will be based is required at the time of application for this position.

**Position Status:** Full-time

**Duration:** until end September 2027

**Salary Level:** Puerto Rico: $46,000 to $54,625 ; Colombia to be benchmarked on local scale - commensurate on professional experience -

**closing date:** posting closing October 8th - please submit application documents in English

[**Risk Level:**](https://library.mercycorps.org/record/47705?ln=en) ☐ **Level 3** ☐**Level 2** ☐**Level 1**

(Level 3: Frequent contact with participants, direct contact with children, access to sensitive data, and/or high level of accountability.

Level 2: Some contact with participants; unplanned non-direct contact with children.

Level 1: Likely to have no contact with participants or sensitive data)

## **About Prosper Global**

Barely enough is not enough for anyone. Prosper Global is a humanitarian organization working alongside communities facing conflict, climate change, and economic hardship to meet urgent needs and create the conditions for lasting progress. Today's challenges demand new solutions, so we pair local knowledge with global resources to help communities build what's needed, test what's possible, and scale what's proven so that people everywhere can pursue a full life on their own terms. In 2026, we changed our name from Mercy Corps to Prosper Global, to reflect our belief that when every community can prosper, all of humanity moves forward.

### **The Program / Department / Team**

Prosper Global is implementing a three-year Department of State-funded project called **Strengthening Caribbean Economic Growth (SCEG)** aimed at improving employability and entrepreneurship across the Caribbean. To achieve this, Mercy Corps will provide small grants to 12 local organizations across the region as well as provide recipients with capacity building and learning opportunities: Antigua and Barbuda, Barbados, The Bahamas, Dominica, Grenada, Dominican Republic, Jamaica, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the 5 Grenadines, Suriname, and Trinidad and Tobago.

### **The Position**

Working in the Finance Department under the direction of the Finance Manager, the Subawards Compliance Finance Officer is responsible for monitoring partners actual expenditure is in line with the agreed award and works with sub-awardees to review their due diligence and financial reporting, to ensure the projects are being implemented with minimal risk.

### **Essential Responsibilities**

## **SUBAWARD MANAGEMENT**

- Responsible for the review of subrecipient budgets and budget narratives for completeness, as well as financial supporting documentation, accounting records, and expenditures to verify reasonableness, allowability, allocability and overall cost realism in compliance with MC and donor budget requirements.
- Review pre-award due diligence assessments of prospective subrecipients are conducted in accordance with the Mercy Corps Subaward Policy and Procedures (SPP) and donor requirements.
- Recommend appropriate risk mitigation measures, including the incorporation of special award conditions, to the subgrant agreement and/or monitoring plan to lessen financial and compliance risks.
- Review sub-award modifications by reviewing partner budget modification templates.
- Prepare Financial Monitoring Reports, document findings, communicate recommendations, and monitor implementation of corrective action plans until resolution.
- Review subrecipient fund requests and liquidation reports to verify supporting documentation including programmatic requirements are met.
- Prior to subaward close-out, conduct final financial reconciliation of subawards, ensuring all expenditures have been properly reported, liquidated, and reconciled prior to close-out and all requirements of the subaward agreement have been met and that subaward funds have been properly settled, respective reporting documentation and project-related documentation is documented and filed on the Share Point in full.
- Maintain complete, organized, and audit-ready subaward financial files throughout the entire subaward life cycle in accordance with the MC subaward Manual and Field Finance Manual.

## **SUBAWARD CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT**

- Develop subrecipient monitoring plans, conduct financial monitoring and prepare financial monitoring visit reports.
- Provide on-going training and support to subrecipients in Mercy Corps subaward financial management procedures and assist in conducting formal subrecipients training workshops and “kick-off” meetings prior to subaward implementation.
- Conduct partner visits as required by the financial monitoring plan to evaluate subrecipients financial management systems, internal controls, supporting documentation, procurement practices, cash management, and compliance with applicable donor regulations.
- Review partner policies and suggest improvements.
- Draft guidelines for partner organizational management, specific to each grant.

### **Safeguarding Responsibilities**

- Actively learns about safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work.
- Practices the values of Prosper Global including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members.
- Encourages openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.

### **Supervisory Responsibility**

N/A.

### **Accountability**

- **Report directly to**: Finance Manager
- **Works directly with**: Resilient Communities Program Manager, Finance Officer, MCG Compliance Teams, other International Finance staff.

### **Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders**

Prosper Global team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

### **Minimum Qualification and Transferable Skills**

- Prior experience in finance, procurement, operations, or any organizational field is preferred.
- A university degree in finance, accounting or other fields is preferred
- Basic computer skills in MS Office programs, particularly Excel and Word
- Ability to work effectively with an ethnically diverse team in a sensitive environment.
- Willingness to learn and adapt.
- Fluent verbal and written English skills required, working proficiency in verbal Spanish required.
- Ability to work effectively with an ethnically diverse team in a sensitive environment.

### **Success Factors**

The ability to effectively interact with colleagues and partners. A high professional standard and work ethic, with the ability to learn new systems and processes. This job will offer an opportunity to learn various aspects of the organization, gaining knowledge in several departments, it will allow the candidate to grow and expand their career.

### **Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions**

The position is based in Colombia or Puerto Rico and it requires up occasional travel to support country programs, which may include travel to insecure locations where freedom of movement is limited and areas where amenities are limited.

### **Ongoing Learning**

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development

### **Team Engagement and Effectiveness**

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

### **Equal Employment Opportunity**

Prosper Global is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.

### **Safeguarding and Ethics**

Prosper Global is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC **and have signed on to** [**the Interagency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme**](https://www.schr.info/the-misconduct-disclosure-scheme). We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to [Prosper Global Code of Conduct Policies](https://www.mercycorps.org/who-we-are/ethics-policies) and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct elearning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Prosper Global Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@prosperglobal.org).

title: Consultancy Opportunity – Water Sector Specialists | Somalia
body:
**Important notice**

This recruitment is being conducted in connection with a **competitive proposal currently under preparation**. Inclusion of a candidate in the proposed team does not constitute an offer of employment or guarantee of an assignment. Any engagement will be subject to successful contract award, final client requirements, verification of qualifications and experience, availability, and agreement on contractual terms.

**About Accord Worldwide, Inc.**  
Accord Worldwide, Inc., through its professional training brand Accordemy®, provides training, capacity development, institutional strengthening and consulting services to organizations internationally.

**About The Opportunity**

**Location:** Somalia, with field travel to project locations  
**Contract Type:** Short-term consultancy / project-based  
**Status:** Proposal-stage recruitment  
**Sector:** WASH / Water Resources / Institutional Capacity Development  
**Application Deadline:** As soon as possible / applications reviewed on a rolling basis

Accord Worldwide, Inc. is inviting expressions of interest from qualified water-sector professionals for a proposed institutional capacity-building assignment in **Somalia**. The assignment relates to institutional capacity assessment, training needs assessment and curriculum development supporting water and sanitation institutions at federal and Federal Member State levels.

We are currently seeking specialists for the following **two positions**:

## 1. Water Utility & Institutional Finance Specialist

The specialist will support assessment of the institutional and financial capacity of water utilities/agencies, including financial sustainability, revenue collection, tariff structures, contract management, organizational arrangements, and readiness for Public-Private Partnership (PPP) and sustainable water-utility business models.

**Minimum profile:**

- University degree in **Public Finance, Corporate Finance, Business Administration, or a related field**.
- At least **7 years of relevant professional experience**.
- Demonstrated experience assessing water-utility financial sustainability, revenue collection and/or tariff structures.
- Experience with contract management, PPP arrangements and/or utility business models.
- Experience in WASH, water utilities, institutional strengthening or public-sector capacity development is highly desirable.
- Experience in Somalia or another fragile/conflict-affected environment is an advantage.
- Experience with UN agencies, multilateral development banks or international development organizations is desirable.

## 2. Groundwater, Water Quality & M&E Specialist

The specialist will assess institutional and technical capacity related to groundwater and water-quality monitoring, digital monitoring and data-management systems, and monitoring and evaluation frameworks.

**Minimum profile:**

- University degree in **Hydrogeology, Water Resources Engineering, or a closely related discipline**.
- At least **7 years of relevant professional experience**.
- Demonstrated experience in groundwater and/or water-quality monitoring systems.
- Experience with water-sector data management, digital monitoring platforms and/or M&E frameworks.
- Experience in WASH, water-resource management and institutional capacity development is highly desirable.
- Experience in Somalia, the Horn of Africa or another fragile/conflict-affected environment is an advantage.
- Experience with UN agencies, multilateral development banks or international development organizations is desirable.

## Assignment requirements

Candidates should be willing and able to undertake **field travel in Somalia**. The anticipated assignment involves engagement with government institutions, Federal Member States, water utilities/agencies and other stakeholders, including activities associated with **Dollow (Jubaland), Qardho (Puntland), and South Galkayo (Galmudug)**.

Candidates with broader expertise spanning both technical water-sector management and institutional/utility capacity development are encouraged to apply and may indicate interest in **either or both positions**. Applications will nevertheless be assessed separately against the requirements of each specialist role.
