body:
**Team Leader – Evaluation on Humanitarian Assistance, Recovery and Protection in Ukraine / Kyiv | Project-based consultancy | Anticipated end 2026–mid 2027**

**About Voluntas (Latin: will, goal, purpose, meaning)**

Voluntas was created from the fundamental belief that all human beings have the inherent right to live a meaningful life.

**That is why we exist: to realize human potential in all corridors of life** – making every workplace, community, and country on the planet full of hope and dignity. Philosophers by heart and advisors by profession, we use our insights to provide evidence-based inspiration, tools and recommendations for our partners around the world.

Voluntas has established offices in Beirut, Copenhagen, Dakar, Kyiv, Mumbai, Nairobi, Port Sudan, and Tunis. We build on a track record of over 270 projects across Africa, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia, serving more than 150 clients. We advise private and public sector actors, including international organizations, government agencies, civil society and foundations, on how to drive meaningful change in societies and organizations.

Our field of expertise is providing fact-based recommendations and policy options grounded in extensive research and data collection in volatile regions and tailored to increase the impact and sustainability of our partners’ efforts.

Voluntas offers a wide range of services across research, policy and governance, including context and thematic analysis, public perception surveys and policy briefs. Under monitoring and social impact, we provide program design, third-party monitoring, evaluations and social impact measurement. We work across thematic areas including agriculture and food, children and youth, economic development, education, gender, health, migration, governance, media, peace and security, and sustainability.

**About the Role**

Voluntas is preparing a tender for an Evaluation on Humanitarian Assistance, Recovery and Protection for an international organization in Ukraine.

We are seeking an experienced **Evaluation Team Leader** to provide overall technical and strategic leadership for the assignment.

The assignment is expected to run from end 2026 to mid 2027 and will assess not only the programme itself, but also the client’s wider contribution to humanitarian, recovery and protection objectives in Ukraine, including areas such as localization, social protection, government leadership, civil society engagement, coordination, and the transition from emergency assistance towards longer-term recovery and resilience. The evaluation will use a theory-based, mixed-methods and contribution-focused approach, with at least four case studies and primary data collection in Ukraine.

**Your Responsibilities**

- Lead the overall evaluation design and implementation.
- Develop the methodology, evaluation matrix, analytical framework and data collection approach.
- Lead theory-based and contribution-focused analysis.
- Oversee qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis.
- Guide case study design and stakeholder engagement in Ukraine.
- Ensure strong triangulation, quality assurance and evidence-based conclusions.
- Integrate gender, disability, vulnerability, ethics and safeguarding considerations.
- Lead key deliverables, including the inception and final evaluation reports.
- Present findings and recommendations to the client and relevant stakeholders.
- Lead and coordinate the wider evaluation team.

**Main Competencies**

- Professional proficiency in Ukrainian is required.
- Minimum 12 years' relevant experience.
- Extensive experience leading complex evaluations in humanitarian, development, recovery, resilience and/or social protection contexts, including conflict-affected settings.
- Strong knowledge of the Ukrainian humanitarian and recovery context.
- Experience with theory-based and mixed-methods evaluation approaches, including contribution analysis, outcome harvesting or process tracing, and international standards.
- Expertise in humanitarian protection, social protection, cash assistance, and/or localization.
- Strong qualitative and quantitative research skills.
- Experience designing inclusive, ethical, trauma-informed data collection with vulnerable populations.
- Experience working with government, civil society, international organizations and donors.
- Proven experience managing multidisciplinary evaluation teams and delivering high-quality evaluations to demanding timelines.
- Excellent analytical, report-writing and presentation skills, including facilitating workshops with senior audiences.
- Excellent written and spoken English.

title: Request for Proposal County Coordination Consultant (Individual Consultant) Nakuru County - Kenya
body:
**Request for Proposal**

**County Coordination Consultant (Individual Consultant)**

**Nakuru County - Kenya**

**September 2026**

## **Procurement Summary**

**Item Details**

RFP Title County Coordination Consultant – Nakuru County

Consultant Type Individual Consultant

Location Nakuru County, Kenya, with regular field presence

Contract Period 12 months

Reporting To Designated Programme Manager

Proposal Deadline 10th October

Submission Email suppliers@girleffect.org

Anticipated Start November

## **Who We Are**

Girl Effect is an international non-profit that builds media and technology that girls want, trust and need. From chatbots and social media to television dramas and community engagement, our work helps adolescent girls and young women access trusted information, build confidence and make informed choices about their health, education, relationships and futures.

Girl Effect creates safe and relevant spaces for girls, online and offline, and works with communities, service providers and public systems so that girls can act on the information they receive. Our programmes place girls' voices, safety, agency and lived realities at the centre of design and delivery.

## **Background**

Girl Effect Kenya is implementing an integrated programme in Nakuru County to improve sexual and reproductive health (SRH) and maternal and child health (MCH) outcomes for adolescents and young people, with adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) aged 15 to 24 as the priority beneficiaries. The programme combines social and behaviour change communication, personalised digital decision support, community engagement, service navigation, referral, and follow-up support.

The programme will use an integrated, youth-centered multimedia ecosystem and digital platform to improve maternal and newborn health, as well as broader sexual and reproductive health outcomes. Key programme areas will include group antenatal care (G-ANC), contraception, including DMPA-SC and self-injection, heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB), sexually transmitted infections (STIs), and related health concerns. Community screenings and facilitated dialogue sessions will connect participants to adolescent-responsive services delivered by qualified public and private healthcare providers, community health promoters, and mobile outreach teams.

Implementation in Nakuru will require close coordination with the County Government, sub-county health management teams, health facilities, pharmacies, community health structures, implementing partners, community-based organisations, youth and community champions, and other relevant actors. Girl Effect therefore seeks a county-based consultant who will serve as its principal coordination and implementation focal point in Nakuru.

## **Objective of the Consultancy**

The purpose of the consultancy is to provide sustained county-level leadership, coordination and operational oversight for Girl Effect’s SRH and MCH programmes in Nakuru County.

The consultant will act as Girl Effect’s eyes and boots on the ground, ensuring that county plans are translated into timely, safe and high-quality implementation; partners remain aligned; implementation risks and service-delivery bottlenecks are identified and addressed early; and accurate, timely implementation information reaches the wider Girl Effect team to inform decision-making.

The consultant will work closely with the Programme Managers, Programme Lead and Country Director, as well as other members of the Girl Effect Kenya team as required.

## **What You will do**

The consultant will perform the following responsibilities in close collaboration with the Girl Effect Kenya team and designated county and implementation partners.

### **County planning and implementation coordination**

- Develop and maintain the county implementation plan, activity calendar and stakeholder engagement plan in line with the approved programme strategy, workplan and budget.
- Coordinate the day-to-day delivery and logistical arrangements for all county activities with Girl Effect and implementing partners.
- Convene regular partner check-ins, track agreed actions, dependencies and decisions, and follow through to completion.
- Monitor county milestones and promptly escalate delays, implementation risks, quality concerns and decisions requiring Girl Effect’s input.

### **County government and stakeholder engagement**

- Serve as Girl Effect’s primary county liaison and maintain effective working relationships with relevant county and sub-county government departments, health teams and focal persons.
- Coordinate county entry processes, approvals and meeting arrangements, ensuring programme activities align with county priorities, plans and reporting structures.
- Represent Girl Effect at approved county forums and technical working groups, prepare the required meeting materials, document agreed actions and provide timely updates to the Girl Effect team.
- Promote county ownership, programme integration and sustainability while avoiding unauthorised financial, contractual or policy commitments on behalf of Girl Effect.

### **Partner coordination and performance follow-up**

- Map and maintain an up-to-date directory of implementing partners, health and community actors, related programmes and referral resources in Nakuru County.
- Coordinate collaboration among Girl Effect, county teams and implementing partners, ensuring clear roles, aligned activity schedules and effective information sharing.
- Monitor partner performance through routine support visits, track delivery against agreed plans and standards, follow up on corrective actions and escalate persistent implementation or compliance issues.

### **Service mapping, referral and quality coordination**

- With guidance from county teams and partner organizations, identify, map, assess and periodically validate public and private referral sites, including health facilities, clinics and pharmacies providing adolescent-responsive SRH and MCH services, and maintain an up-to-date service directory.
- Work with county teams and technical partners to verify provider readiness, including trained staff, service availability, commodities, accessibility and referral procedures.
- Monitor referral pathways and barriers such as stock-outs, cost, stigma, confidentiality and poor client experience, and coordinate timely corrective action or alternative referrals.
- Link community activities and participants to vetted providers, community health promoters and mobile outreach teams for appropriate services and follow-up.

### **Community engagement and field delivery**

- Support the recruitment, training, deployment and supervision of champions, facilitators, community health promoters and other field actors.
- In collaboration with community health promoters and partner CBOs, coordinate the selection of safe, accessible community venues and mobilise AGYW, adolescents, young people, caregivers and other community stakeholders to participate in programme activities.
- Ensure community screenings, dialogue sessions and outreach activities follow approved content, tools and referral protocols, while providing field teams with routine coaching and quality support.
- Promote meaningful adolescent and youth participation, maintain complete activity records and feedback, and ensure participant insights inform programme adaptation.

### **Monitoring, evaluation, research and learning**

- Track agreed county indicators and maintain complete, accurate and timely records on programme activities, reach, referrals, service access, quality and partner performance.
- Conduct routine data-quality checks, reconcile discrepancies, maintain supporting documentation and assist with approved data-verification exercises.
- Gather and document participant and partner feedback, implementation insights, emerging trends and stories of change to inform programme learning and adaptation.

### **Safeguarding, accountability and reporting**

- Ensure all county activities comply with Girl Effect’s safeguarding, ethical and data-protection requirements, and promptly report concerns or serious incidents through approved channels.
- Use programme resources responsibly and ensure activities and supporting documentation comply with approved plans, budgets and procedures.
- Provide timely implementation updates and reports, maintaining accurate and organised records of county activities, stakeholder engagement, risks and agreed actions.
- Monitor the county operating context and promptly escalate significant risks, delays, quality concerns or issues requiring Girl Effect’s attention.

## **Deliverables**

- County plans, activities and logistical arrangements are completed on time and in accordance with approved workplans, budgets, technical guidance and county protocols.
- County government and stakeholder relationships are professionally managed, required approvals are secured, commitments are documented and agreed actions are followed through.
- Partner roles and schedules remain aligned, performance is regularly monitored, and delivery gaps and corrective actions are identified, followed up and escalated when necessary.
- Service directories and referral information remain accurate and current, provider readiness is regularly verified, and referral barriers are promptly addressed with the responsible partners.
- Community activities are delivered safely and consistently using approved content, tools and referral protocols, with meaningful youth participation and appropriate support to field teams.
- Programme data, records and reports are accurate, complete and timely; data-quality issues are resolved; and participant and partner feedback informs programme learning and adaptation.
- Safeguarding concerns, implementation risks and critical incidents are promptly escalated through approved procedures, while programme resources and information are handled responsibly and confidentially.

Deliverables will be reviewed and approved by the designated Programme Manager. Final dates and reporting formats will be agreed during contracting.

## **Duration, Location and Level of Effort**

The consultancy is expected to run for 12 months.

The consultant must be based in Nakuru County and maintain a regular field presence across programme locations.

This is a high-level-of-effort assignment requiring consistent availability and responsiveness. The consultant will manage their time and approach against agreed workplans, milestones and outputs.

Occasional travel within or outside Nakuru County may be required with reasonable notice and prior approval.

## **Management and Working Arrangement**

The consultant will report to the designated Programme Manager, who will provide overall direction and approve deliverables.

The consultant will collaborate with relevant Girl Effect Kenya teams, including:

- Programmes;
- Partnerships;
- Evidence and Insights;
- Safeguarding;
- Youth Engagement;
- Finance and Operations;
- Digital Delivery; and
- Social and Behaviour Change.

The consultant will also work closely with county government teams, technical partners, implementing partners and community stakeholders.

## **Who You Are**

The successful consultant should demonstrate:

- Bachelor's degree in public health, reproductive health, nursing, community health, social sciences, development studies, project management or another relevant field. Relevant postgraduate qualifications are an advantage.
- At least five years of progressively responsible experience coordinating public health, SRH, RMNCAH, adolescent and youth health, community health or related programmes.
- Demonstrated experience working with county and sub-county government health structures in Kenya. Strong professional networks and recent work experience in Nakuru County are highly desirable.
- Experience coordinating multiple implementing partners, community-based organisations, health facilities, community health promoters and community actors against a common workplan.
- Practical understanding of adolescent-responsive SRH and MCH programming, including contraception, referral systems, community mobilisation, service delivery linkages and quality improvement. Familiarity with DMPA-SC, self-injection, heavy menstrual bleeding or STI programming is an advantage.
- Experience supporting programme monitoring, routine data collection, data-quality checks, research or evaluation fieldwork, and preparation of clear analytical reports.
- Strong knowledge of safeguarding, informed consent, confidentiality and data protection in programmes involving adolescents and young people.
- Strong planning, facilitation, negotiation, problem-solving and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to work independently and manage competing priorities.
- Excellent written and spoken English and Kiswahili.
- High integrity, discretion and commitment to gender equality, inclusion, youth participation and Girl Effect's values.

## **Proposal Submission**

Applicants should submit a concise technical proposal of no more than five pages together with a separate financial proposal.

The application should include:

- A cover letter explaining the applicant’s suitability, availability for the 12-month assignment and ability to maintain a regular presence in Nakuru County.
- A technical approach explaining how the applicant will coordinate county stakeholders, partners, field delivery, referrals, monitoring, safeguarding and risk management.
- A current CV highlighting relevant assignments and county-level experience.
- Three professional references, including name, organisation, position, email address and telephone number.
- A separate financial proposal in Kenya shillings **(KES)** showing:
    - The proposed all-inclusive monthly professional fee;
    - The underlying daily rate or estimated level of effort;
    - Applicable taxes

## **Evaluation Criteria**

Proposals will be evaluated in the following order:

- Pre-screening;
- Technical evaluation; and
- Financial evaluation.

Girl Effect may establish a minimum technical score that applicants must achieve before their financial proposals are considered.

Assessment area Weight

Relevant qualifications and overall experience 15%

Experience in SRH, MCH, adolescent and youth health, community health or related programmes 20%

Experience engaging county government and coordinating partners, preferably in Nakuru 20%

Quality and practicality of the proposed technical approach 15%

Safeguarding, monitoring, reporting and risk-management capability 10%

Value for money and clarity of the financial proposal 20%

**Girl Effect may request interviews, written clarifications, reference checks or a best-and-final financial proposal.**

## **Procurement Timelines**

- Terms of reference published: 28th September, 2026
- Deadline for proposal submission: 10th October 2025

## **General and Commercial Terms**

- **Contracting and Payment:** The successful consultant will sign Girl Effect’s standard consultancy agreement. Payment will be linked to the satisfactory delivery and approval of agreed outputs and supporting documentation.
- **Pricing, Taxes and Expenses:** Fees must be quoted in Kenya shillings, with applicable taxes shown separately. Girl Effect will deduct taxes where required by law. Only reasonable expenses approved in writing in advance will be reimbursable in accordance with the final agreement.
- **Confidentiality, Data and Intellectual Property:** The consultant must protect all confidential, personal and sensitive information. Deliverables and materials produced under the consultancy will be governed by Girl Effect’s intellectual-property, confidentiality and data-protection provisions.
- **Safeguarding and Conduct:** Appointment is subject to satisfactory due diligence, reference and safeguarding checks. The consultant must comply with Girl Effect’s safeguarding, ethical, anti-fraud, information-security and code-of-conduct requirements.
- **Conflicts of Interest:** Applicants must disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest.
- **Equal Opportunity:** Girl Effect welcomes applications from qualified individuals of all backgrounds and particularly encourages candidates based in or with strong working knowledge of Nakuru County.
- **Right to Award:** Girl Effect may seek clarification, interview or negotiate with applicants, amend or cancel the process, reject any or all proposals, or make no award. Girl Effect is not liable for costs incurred in preparing an application.
- **Proposal Validity:** Proposals must remain valid for 90 days from the submission deadline.

title: Psychosocial Support Expert - Consultancy
body:
**Keeping the Story Alive: Strategic Citizen Journalism in Sudan**

## **Project Background**

Sudan’s information ecosystem faces severe challenges amidst ongoing conflict. Professional journalists and citizen reporters operating inside Sudan document critical field realities under extreme pressure, insecurity, and personal risk. Exposure to conflict, displacement, and traumatic events creates a significant psychological burden and complex mental health challenges for frontline reporters.

**Role Objective**

The Psychosocial Support Expert provides mental health and group therapy expertise, designing, facilitating, and delivering virtual group psychosocial support sessions for program participants to process stress and trauma, build coping mechanisms, prevent burnout, and foster peer solidarity in a safe and confidential environment.

## **Key Responsibilities & Scope of Work**

- **Session Design & Preparation:** Tailor group therapy methodologies to the realities of journalists in active conflict zones. Develop sensitive, culturally appropriate, and trauma-informed session outlines focusing on trauma handling, stress management, burnout prevention, and self-care strategies.
- **Facilitation & Group Therapy Delivery:** Facilitate up to 50 virtual group support sessions across designated participant cohorts via secure, encrypted digital tools (e.g., Signal, Zoom, WhatsApp), addressing acute fear, secondary trauma, emotional exhaustion, and operational isolation.
- **Confidentiality, Safeguarding & Risk Mitigation:** Enforce strict participant confidentiality and anonymity protocols. Establish clear referral pathways for individual cases requiring advanced clinical care or specialized psychiatric intervention beyond the scope of group therapy.
- **Reporting & Monitoring:** Provide brief, anonymized quarterly progress summaries and structural feedback to project management (MiCT and Ayin Network), documenting overarching mental health trends and operational observations without revealing identifying details.

## **Key Deliverables**

1. Inception Plan & Session Framework detailing session methodologies, confidentiality protocols, and tailored topic breakdown.
2. Delivery of up to 50 scheduled virtual group therapy and psychosocial support sessions across cohort cycles.
3. Anonymized quarterly progress reports outlining completed sessions, general emotional themes, participant engagement levels, and risk mitigation steps.

## **Qualifications & Requirements**

- Advanced university degree (Master's or equivalent) in Clinical Psychology, Psychotherapy, Trauma Counseling, Social Work, or a related mental health discipline.
- Minimum 5 years of professional clinical experience in providing trauma-informed therapy or crisis counseling.
- Demonstrated experience supporting journalists, human rights defenders, or individuals operating in high-risk conflict settings (prior context experience in Sudan or the MENA region highly preferred).
- Native or professional Arabic fluency (spoken and written) for session facilitation, along with professional working proficiency in English for project reporting and coordination.

Technical competence in digital security practices, safe online facilitation, and managing remote group dynamics in low-bandwidth environments.

title: Adjoint.e à la Coordination du Territoire Europe (CDD 12 mois)
body:
Action Education — anciennement Aide et Action — est une association internationale de développement par l’éducation, libre de toute attache politique et religieuse. Depuis 1981, elle agit pour garantir l’accès à une éducation de qualité aux populations les plus vulnérables et marginalisées, en particulier les enfants, les filles et les femmes, afin que toutes et tous puissent maîtriser leur propre développement et contribuer à un monde plus juste, pacifique et durable.

Parce que l’accès à une éducation de qualité constitue un levier essentiel pour lutter contre la pauvreté, les inégalités, les discriminations et les exclusions, Action Education favorise l’apprentissage tout au long de la vie. L’association porte ainsi une attention particulière à l’éducation et à la protection de la petite enfance, à l’accès et à la qualité de l’éducation aux niveaux primaire et secondaire, à la formation professionnelle, à l’insertion sociale, à l’éducation inclusive, à la citoyenneté et au développement durable.

Fondant son intervention sur les valeurs de dignité, d’inclusion et d’intégrité, ainsi que sur les principes d’action de transparence, de redevabilité et de solidarité, Action Education mène aujourd’hui, grâce au soutien de ses 51 122 marraines, parrains et donateurs, 69 projets dans 16 pays d’Afrique, d’Asie et d’Europe, au bénéfice de plus de 1,1 million de personnes.

En Europe, Action Education agit plus particulièrement auprès des populations exposées à la précarité, aux discriminations et aux ruptures de parcours éducatif. L’association accompagne notamment les enfants, les jeunes et les familles vivant en habitat précaire, et travaille avec les acteurs socio-éducatifs afin de favoriser la scolarisation, le maintien dans les apprentissages, le renforcement du pouvoir d’agir des publics accompagnés et l’amélioration des dispositifs d’accueil et d’accompagnement.

Ces dernières années, l’organisation a connu des évolutions structurelles importantes, dans la gestion de ses opérations comme dans sa gouvernance. Les bases de cette transformation sont aujourd’hui posées, et sa mise en œuvre opérationnelle se poursuit à travers la déclinaison de son nouveau plan stratégique pour la période 2025-2029.

C’est dans ce contexte interne riche en perspectives, mais aussi dans un environnement externe mouvant et marqué par de nombreux défis, qu’Action Education recrute son/sa futur·e **Adjoint·e à la coordination du Territoire Europe**.

**MISSIONS**

Sous la responsabilité de la Coordinatrice du Territoire Europe, l’adjoint.e à la coordination joue un rôle clé dans le soutien à la coordination et aux projets d’Action Education en France et en Europe. Il/elle appuie la Coordinatrice dans la conduite des opérations, en adéquation avec les orientations stratégiques globales, ainsi que le plan stratégique 25-29 du Territoire. Il a également à sa charge directe le pilotage de certains projets. L’adjoint.e assure un rôle de management fonctionnel pour accompagner les chef.fe.s de projets dans leurs missions.

**Responsabilités principales**

**Appui à la coordination et à la mise en œuvre des projets (40%) :**

- Appuyer la Coordinatrice sur le pilotage du Territoire Europe : reporting interne, gestion budgétaire, suivi de la planification annuelle, mise en œuvre et appropriation par l’équipe de l’ensemble des politiques et procédures de l’organisation ;
- Appuyer la mise en œuvre des projets en adéquation avec les standards de qualité attendus ;
- Accompagner les chef.fe.s de projet dans la réalisation de leurs missions ;
- Veiller à la transversalité dans la mise en œuvre des projets au sein des différentes échelles d’intervention (local, régional, national, européen) ;
- Veiller au respect de la politique SERA de l’association pour le pilotage global des projets mis en œuvre ainsi qu’à l'utilisation efficace des ressources et des moyens alloués à la mise en œuvre des actions.

**Pilotage, déploiement et développement de projets (40%)**

- Assurer la coordination opérationnelle ainsi que la chefferie de projet sur les projets, activités, et chantiers internes du Territoire Europe. Notamment un projet à venir en lien avec l’analyse des politiques publiques en Europe et la mobilisation institutionnelle à destination des élèves à besoins éducatifs particuliers ;
- Rechercher et déposer de nouveaux projets liés à cette thématique spécifiquement, et plus largement en lien avec les axes stratégiques de l’organisation ;
- Lorsque nécessaire, assurer les RDV avec les bailleurs de fonds identifiés.

**Représentation institutionnelle, Lien Partenarial et Plaidoyer (20%)**

- Représenter Action Education dans différents forums et se tenir au courant des tendances dans les domaines liés aux thématiques d’intervention du territoire ;
- Établir des relations institutionnelles et promouvoir les initiatives /approches développées au sein des projets du Territoire Europe ;
- Impulser la dynamique prospective permettant le développement du territoire (identifier ou approfondir de nouveaux projets ou partenariats, notamment au niveau européen).

**PROFIL RECHERCHÉ**

- Diplôme niveau Bac + 5 en Sciences humaines, Sciences sociales, Sciences de Gestion, Economie, ou équivalent
- Au moins 8 ans d’expérience avérée dans des programmes/projets de développement en France et/ou à l’étranger (Europe un plus)
- Expérience dans la coordination fonctionnelle avec des équipes projets
- Expérience en pilotage et gestion de projets
- Expérience en projets et financements européens
- Bon communicateur (oral et écrit)
- Leadership et capacité d’influence
- Bonne connaissance des différentes problématiques liées à l’inclusion, l’éducation populaire, et la citoyenneté
- Capacités d’initiatives et d’adaptation à des situations changeantes
- Maîtrise des outils informatiques
- Maîtrise de l’anglais
- Capacité d’organisation et de planification

**ASPECTS PRATIQUES**

- Durée : **CDD 12 mois**
- Prise de poste **: dès que possible**
- 39 heures avec 23 JRTT au prorata temporis
- Lieu : Poste basé à Paris (11ème)
- Possibilité de 2 jours de TT / semaine
- Déplacements ponctuels à prévoir en France et/ou en Europe.
- Avantages : Prise en charge par l’employeur de l’abonnement de transport (à 50%), tickets restaurant de 10 € (à 60%) et de la mutuelle (à 75%)
- Rémunération : entre 41 et 46K€

title: Compliance Coordinator (Temporary)
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
We are currently recruiting an interim **Compliance Coordinator** to join our Legal, Ethics & Compliance team.

This is a remote, temporary 3-month position open to candidates based in the UK. The role will be full-time, offering a salary of circa. £36k per annum.

At Relief International, we are committed to building a representative, inclusive and authentic workplace. We strongly encourage applications from candidates from minoritized backgrounds and those who bring lived experience of the contexts in which we work.

This role is classified as requiring standard pre-employment checks.

**About Relief International**

Relief International is an international non-profit organization that partners with communities impacted by conflict, climate change and disaster to save lives, build greater resilience and promote long-term health and wellbeing. Our teams work across Africa, Asia and the Middle East, delivering Health and Nutrition, WASH (Water, Sanitation and Hygiene), Education and Livelihoods programming that creates the foundation for community resilience. We work alongside local actors to develop safe, inclusive and evidence-based programmes that reach those most in need.

**About the Opportunity**

The Compliance Coordinator plays an important role in supporting Relief International's Legal, Ethics and Compliance function and helping ensure the organization maintains robust systems for incident management, ethics reporting and risk management. Working closely with the Global Investigations Director and colleagues across Human Resources, Security, Country Offices and senior leadership teams, you will help strengthen accountability and support the effective management of incidents across our global operations.

This role combines incident management coordination, compliance monitoring, reporting, policy support and data analysis. You will maintain incident management systems, track investigation recommendations, support policy implementation and produce high-quality reporting and analysis that helps inform decision-making at both management and board level. The successful candidate will be highly organized, analytical and detail-oriented, with a strong commitment to ethics, accountability and humanitarian principles.

**Your Responsibilities**

This role includes the following responsibilities.

- Coordinate and maintain Relief International's incident management system, ensuring incidents are accurately logged, triaged, documented and managed in accordance with policy requirements.
- Support global and country-level incident management processes, working with Incident Management Teams and technical case leads to promote timely case resolution.
- Track and monitor implementation of recommendations arising from investigations and support follow-up activities across the organization.
- Contribute to a culture of accountability by supporting ethical incident reporting and helping strengthen internal systems and processes.
- Produce reports and analysis on incident management trends for senior leadership, governance bodies and other stakeholders.
- Support compliance with donor, regulatory and organizational reporting obligations relating to ethics, safeguarding and security incidents.
- Assist with policy development, updates and implementation across the Legal, Ethics and Compliance function.
- Work collaboratively with Human Resources, Safety & Security, Country Offices and other departments to strengthen ethical incident management and organizational compliance.

**About You**

You will bring the following experience and skills.

- Experience working in compliance, incident management, whistleblowing, investigations support, governance, risk management or another related function.
- Strong organizational skills and exceptional attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
- Experience supporting case management processes or working within incident management systems including triage.
- Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.
- Strong analytical capabilities and confidence working with data, reporting tools and information management systems.
- Experience using Microsoft Office applications. Experience using Navex Ethicspoint is a plus.
- Demonstrated ability to work effectively with colleagues from diverse cultural and professional backgrounds.
- Understanding of governance, accountability, ethics or compliance principles within international organizations is highly desirable. Previous experience in the humanitarian or development sector and Arabic or French language skills would be an advantage.

Relief International is an international non-profit organization that partners with communities impacted by conflict, climate change and disaster to save lives, build greater resilience and promote long-term health and wellbeing. title: Senior Health Technical Lead/Specialist
body:
**BACKGROUND**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGOs), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities, helping people survive, reclaim control of their futures, and strengthen their communities.

The IRC was present in Sudan from 1981 to 2009. In November 2019, the IRC re-registered in Sudan and, with the wider IRC-led Consortium (CARE International, Catholic Relief Services, Medical Teams International, Relief International, and local partners), currently delivers integrated health and nutrition services across 11 states, supporting 640 health facilities and service delivery points nationwide and reaching over four million beneficiaries in 2025.

Since the outbreak of war in April 2023 between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), the country has spiraled into relentless violence, institutional collapse, and mass displacement, and is facing one of the most complex and devastating humanitarian crises in the world today. More than 30 million people now require humanitarian assistance, and around 25 million people face acute food insecurity, including 770,000 children suffering from severe acute malnutrition.

The project is expected to run for the duration of the World Bank-financed award (exact start date and duration to be confirmed on award).

**Senior Health Technical Lead Scope of Work**

The IRC is seeking a Senior Health Technical Lead for an upcoming World Bank-funded health project in Sudan. The project is intended to restore access to a basic package of health and nutrition services and preserve the main elements of essential public health functions in Sudan.

The project is expected to run from February 2027 for 3 years.

The Senior Health Technical Lead provides technical leadership and quality assurance across SHARE II's health and nutrition service delivery and health system strengthening activities including primary health care and hospital services, nutrition programming (CMAM/IYCF), communicable and non-communicable disease management, reproductive, maternal and newborn health, disease surveillance and outbreak preparedness, health information systems (DHIS2/EWARS/HMIS), and facility-level WASH and infection prevention and control. They will ensure service delivery is technically sound, aligned with national health strategies and World Bank requirements. SHARE II will sustain and maintain SHARE I’s existing footprint in delivering a basic package of health services to 420 PHCs and 10 hospitals and also expand access to essential health services in prioritized high-need localities. The project will be delivered nationwide across multiple states including RSF and SAF controlled areas and many areas with severe to catastrophic health needs.

The postholder will lead facility readiness assessments and IPC protocols; oversees nutrition programming and evidence generation; supports health workforce strengthening, referral pathways, and differentiated delivery models; and provides technical guidance on DHIS2/HMIS, disease surveillance, outbreak preparedness and emergency response, climate-resilient facility and WASH improvements, laboratory and blood systems, digital health, and supply chain/pharmaceutical management, coordinating closely with Consortium partners.

The Senior Health Technical Lead represents the IRC-led consortium in relevant technical coordination mechanisms (Health, Nutrition and WASH Clusters, Strategic Advisory Group, technical working groups), liaising with WHO, UNICEF, and Federal/State Ministries of Health, and reinforcing government-led systems. They ensure technical activities comply with World Bank Operational Policy 7.30, the Procurement Regulations, and the Environmental and Social Framework, including SEA/SH prevention and response; supports the Third-Party Monitoring mechanism, IRC's Community Feedback Mechanisms and the project's Grievance Redress Mechanism; and supports continuity of SRH and GBV services across the Consortium.

The Senior Health Technical Lead supports the phased, consultative handover of SHARE I sites into SHARE II, ensuring continuity of services, staffing, incentives, commodities and data systems during transition, and contributes to sustainability and responsible exit planning, including integration into MoH plans. The Senior Health Technical Lead provides technical inputs to project reporting, including results framework/indicator tracking for submission to the Project Director and the World Bank, and supports capacity building of MoH and local partner staff consistent with IRC's Partnership Excellence for Equality and Results System (PEERS).

**Requirements**

- Medical degree (MD/MBBS) or an advanced degree (Master's) in public health, health systems management, or a related field.
- Minimum 10-15 years' progressive experience in health systems strengthening and/or PHC and hospital service delivery programming, including significant experience in Sudan or comparable fragile, conflict-affected, or access-constrained settings.
- Demonstrated technical expertise in health and nutrition and relevant technical areas including PHC/hospital service delivery, nutrition (CMAM/IYCF), communicable and non-communicable disease management, reproductive/maternal/newborn health, GBV/SRH, mental health, disease surveillance and outbreak response and health information system.
- Prior experience on large health and nutrition projects financed by the World Bank or other major institutional donors; familiarity with health cluster coordination.
- Experience working with, or through, Ministry of Health structures and health-sector coordination mechanisms (Health Cluster, WHO, UNICEF).
- Strong data analysis, facility assessment (HeRAMS), and technical report writing skills, and demonstrated experience supporting multi-partner consortium coordination.
- Fluency in English required; Arabic strongly preferred, given the requirement for field-facing engagement with MoH/SMoH counterparts and communities.
- Ability to travel to field locations across Sudan, including hard-to-reach and access-constrained areas, and to operate effectively under insecure or volatile conditions, in line with IRC and UNDSS security protocols.

Please note that this position will be contingent on the outcome of the bid.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: EMERGENCY PROGRAMME COORDINATOR
body:
About : Action contre la Faim

Created in 1979, Action contre la Faim is a non-governmental organization that fights against hunger. Its charter of humanitarian principals- independence, neutrality, non-discrimination, free and direct access to victims, professionalism, transparency - has been part of its identity for 45 years. Its mission is to save lives by eliminating hunger through the prevention, detection and treatment of under-nutrition, particularly during and after emergency situations linked to conflicts or natural disasters. Action contre la Faim focuses its actions on 7 main areas of expertise: Nutrition and Health - Mental Health, Psychosocial Support - Food Security and Livelihoods - Water, Sanitation and Hygiene - Advocacy - Climate - Research. In 2024, Action contre la Faim provided aid to more than 26 million people in 57 countries worldwide. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Under the supervision of the Deputy Country Director for Programmes, your mission will be to strengthen the country office's emergency preparedness and response capacities to ensure timely, effective, and coordinated emergency responses, and lead the implementation of emergency responses across all areas of intervention of ACF in Yemen.  
The main responsibilities and challenges of the position will be as follows:  
Strengthen and operationalize the country office's emergency preparedness and response system to ensure readiness for emergenciesDevelop and maintain up to date emergency preparedness and contingency plans  
Design, maintain up to date and lead the implementation of emergency response standard operating procedures in line with ACF programme, finance, logistics, human resources, and security policies and procedures  
Lead and coordinate emergency responses implemented by the country office to ensure providing timely and quality humanitarian assistance to populations affected by crisesEnsure continuous monitoring and analysis of the humanitarian, political, and operational context to identify emerging risks and response opportunities  
Lead the activation of emergency responses in line with ACF's procedures and agreed decision-making mechanisms  
Strengthen ACF's engagement with donors, partners, and through coordination mechanisms to enhance ACF's emergency positioning and resource mobilization capacityMonitor key humanitarian developments, donor priorities, and funding opportunities relevant to emergency preparedness and response  
Represent ACF in humanitarian coordination fora: clusters, working groups and inter-agency fora etc.  
Promote ACF's emergency response capacities, experience, and strategic priorities to external stakeholders (donors, partners etc.)

  
Profile :

 You hold a Master's Degree in International relations/humanitarian work or any other related field.  
You have at least 5 years of professional experience in the humanitarian sector, with a minimum of 3 years managing emergency response programmes.  
You demonstrate a strong leadership and decision-making abilities, good communication, representation, and negotiation skills. You are recognised for your ability to work effectively under pressure and adapt to changing circumstances.  
You master English (written and spoken)  
Having a previous experience in Yemen is an asset.  
  
Conditions d'emploi  
  
Fixed term contract under French legislation: 6 months  
Monthly gross salary from 2597 to 2968euros upon experience, including 13th month   
Reimbursement of the pension insurance for non-French citizens: 16% of the gross monthly salary  
Annual salary increase: 6% increase after and each 12 months of continuous contract  
Monthly per diem and living allowance: 730 USD net, field paid  
Monthly country allowance: 450euros   
Child allowance: 1500euros per year per child present in the country of origin (maximum 6000euros/year)  
Transportation and accommodation: Coverage of transportation costs and guest house  
Medical coverage: ACF covers 100% of the health and repatriation insurance agreement fees, for your medical expenses (as well as your dependents if you have a family post), and up to 1 month after the end of your contract.  
Salary sustainment measures (sickness, paternity, maternity)  
Leaves and RnR: 25 days of paid leaves per year, 20 RnR per year, airfare reimbursement with a ceiling to get to the chosen break destination, and 215 euros for each RnR period  
Accompaniment and trainings:Follow-up and support for career development  
Free and unlimited access to the e-learning platform Talentsoft  
ACF is committed to people with disabilities and actively fights against all forms of discrimination.

title: Especialista en Grants e Informes (National/International)
body:
El **Consejo Danés para los Refugiados (DRC)** es una de las principales ONG humanitarias del mundo, que trabaja en más de 30 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, personas retornadas, personas en movilidad y poblaciones locales/comunidades de acogida en situación de vulnerabilidad. Actualmente, **DRC** busca un(a) **Especialista en Grants e Informes** altamente calificado(a) con sede en **Caracas, Venezuela**.

**Acerca del Puesto:** El/la Especialista en Grants e Informes es responsable de apoyar la gestión de subvenciones del portafolio de la Oficina de País de Venezuela, de acuerdo con las normativas del donante y de DRC. Esto incluye apoyar el desarrollo efectivo de propuestas, el cumplimiento con los donantes y la entrega oportuna de informes. El puesto reporta al Grants Management Manager y colabora de cerca con el equipo de Programas (Líderes Técnicos, MEAL, Alianzas, etc.), Servicios de Apoyo (Finanzas, Logística, RRHH) y el Senior Management Team en todos los asuntos relacionados con grants y cumplimiento. El puesto se encuentra en el centro de un portafolio multi-donante (ECHO, GFFO, SDC, OCHA CBPF, WFP) que abarca Protección, Seguridad Alimentaria y Medios de Vida, WASH y Acción Anticipatoria, ofreciendo una fuerte exposición a donantes institucionales.

**Responsabilidades:**

***Monitoreo de la Gestión de Grants, Cumplimiento, Aseguramiento de Calidad y Administración***

- Asegurar una gestión contractual de alta calidad en estrecha coordinación con el Grants Management Manager, señalando cualquier problema o riesgo potencial;
- Apoyar las enmiendas contractuales, incluyendo extensiones con y sin costo y revisiones de proyecto, en coordinación con el Grants Management Manager y las partes internas relevantes;
- Coordinar y facilitar las reuniones de arranque/apertura, revisión y cierre de grants, incluyendo el seguimiento del avance frente a los plazos y puntos de acción;
- Monitorear, actualizar y asegurar que los sistemas de Grants Management y documentación interna de DRC (Dynamics y SharePoint) estén completamente actualizados, trabajando con el/la Grants Management Specialist de HQ para resolver cualquier inconveniente;
- Revisar y actualizar el grants tracker;
- Apoyar en el monitoreo del portafolio de grants, trabajando directamente con los equipos de implementación, asegurando una sólida comprensión de las obligaciones y normativas contractuales, solicitando el apoyo del Grants Management Manager cuando sea necesario.
- Asegurar que las obligaciones contractuales sean conocidas y cumplidas por los equipos de Programas, M&E y Operaciones.
- Resolver las brechas identificadas para el cumplimiento de los entregables dentro del plazo y presupuesto establecidos, informando al personal correspondiente en el país y solicitando asesoría al Departamento de Programas de DRC HQ sobre posibles soluciones que cumplan con las normas del donante.

***Reportes y Desarrollo de Nuevos Negocios***

- Coordinar la preparación de informes de proyecto de acuerdo con los requisitos del donante, trabajando directamente con otros departamentos de DRC en Venezuela;
- Apoyar en la provisión de capacitaciones sobre desarrollo de propuestas e informes para los equipos, según sea necesario;
- Apoyar al Grants Management Manager en la actualización del mapeo de donantes y el funding tracker, manteniéndose al tanto de las tendencias de financiamiento y las estrategias de los donantes, prestando especial atención a la diversificación del portafolio de financiamiento y las estrategias de recaudación de fondos de la Oficina de País;
- Apoyar al Grants Management Manager en el mantenimiento de una comunicación activa y regular con los donantes, asegurando respuestas oportunas a sus comunicaciones y coordinando con los miembros relevantes del equipo país para brindar retroalimentación de alta calidad;
- Apoyar al Grants Management Manager en las reuniones de Go-No-Go para nuevos grants y contribuir en la reunión de planificación de propuestas.
- Coordinar con los coordinadores técnicos de programas, gerentes de base, servicios de apoyo y socios implementadores para recopilar sus insumos para el desarrollo de propuestas. Compilar el borrador final de la propuesta y sus anexos, asegurando que cumplan con los estándares de calidad requeridos, con supervisión mínima del Grants Management Manager.
- En colaboración con el equipo de MEAL, asegurar que el desarrollo de propuestas de proyecto y los informes a donantes estén basados en datos organizacionales confiables y aprendizajes.
- Asegurar la participación de DRC HQ en el aseguramiento de calidad de informes o propuestas cuando sea necesario, particularmente para grants estratégicos.
- Apoyar en la comunicación, negociaciones y coordinación con donantes y partes interesadas externas.
- Apoyar en la preparación de fichas informativas, sitreps/informes flash, declaraciones de capacidad, entre otros.
- ***Cualquier tarea ad hoc asignada por el Grants Management Manager***

**Experiencia y competencias técnicas:**

- Al menos 2 años de experiencia en gestión de grants/proyectos, desarrollo de propuestas o informes a donantes, con una ONG internacional, agencia de la ONU u otra organización financiada por donantes.
- Se prefiere conocimiento y experiencia trabajando en múltiples sectores, incluyendo protección, seguridad alimentaria y medios de vida, WASH y Acción Anticipatoria.
- Dominio de Microsoft Office y otros programas relevantes, incluyendo Word, Excel y PowerPoint.
- Sólida experiencia en la redacción y compilación de propuestas e informes a donantes, con fuertes habilidades de redacción y edición.
- Familiaridad con las normas y regulaciones de los donantes, o capacidad demostrada para aprenderlas rápidamente.
- Capacidad demostrada para priorizar grandes cargas de trabajo, cumplir sistemáticamente con los plazos y adaptarse a un entorno de trabajo complejo y desafiante.
- Excelentes habilidades de comunicación, coordinación, influencia e interpersonales.
- Demostrar capacidad de pensamiento creativo y práctico para mejorar la calidad de los proyectos.
- Capacidad para trabajar dentro de un equipo multicultural/diverso.
- Compromiso con los principios humanitarios y los valores de DRC.

**Deseable:**

- Experiencia práctica con donantes de la ONU (UNHCR, WFP, OCHA), ECHO, GFFO, SDC y/o fundaciones privadas, incluyendo solicitudes de modificación y extensiones con y sin costo.
- Experiencia con Microsoft Dynamics, SharePoint o sistemas similares de gestión de grants / ERP.

**Educación**:

- Título universitario en Ciencias Sociales, Desarrollo Internacional, Administración de Empresas, Economía o campos relacionados.

**Idiomas:**

- Es indispensable un inglés escrito sólido (una prueba escrita formará parte del proceso de selección); buen nivel de inglés oral.
- Habilidades de comunicación en español son obligatorias.

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de formar parte de una de las mejores ONG del mundo.
- Acceso a más de 1.000 capacitaciones y certificaciones gratuitas en línea.
- Duración del contrato: sujeta a la disponibilidad presupuestaria.
- Salario: Banda G2 / Cargo no gerencial. Contrato nacional.
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.

**Competencias Fundamentales de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia:** enfocarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y fomentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa:** asumir responsabilidad e iniciativa, promoviendo la innovación.
- **Comunicación:** escuchar y expresarse de manera eficaz y honesta.
- **Demostrar integridad:** actuar de acuerdo con la visión y los valores de DRC.

**Proceso de postulación:**

Todos los postulantes deben adjuntar una **carta de presentación** (máximo 1 página) y un **currículum vitae actualizado** (máximo 2 páginas, sin anexos), en inglés o español, en la plataforma de empleo de DRC. Las solicitudes enviadas por correo electrónico no serán consideradas.

Fecha límite de postulación: **Domingo 11 de octubre a las 11:59 p. m. (hora local).** Tenga en cuenta que las postulaciones serán revisadas de manera continua y las entrevistas se programarán tan pronto como se identifique a un candidato adecuado. DRC se reserva el derecho de cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha límite una vez que se haya identificado a un candidato idóneo.

Fecha de inicio: **Octubre de 2026.**

title: Youth Education Specialist (YESOL)
body:
This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.

**Background/IRC Summary:**  
The International Rescue Committee responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic well-being, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is at work in over 40 countries and 25 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. Since 1999, the IRC has developed partnerships with New York City public schools, community-based organizations and local colleges and universities to support the positive development of refugee youth and their communities in New York City. The Education and Learning Program provides year-round programming working directly with refugee youth, their parents and families, and their schools.

**Job Overview/Summary:**  
The Youth Education Specialist (YESOL) will work closely with the Youth Programs Supervisor to support high-quality programming for refugee and immigrant youth in New York City. The specialist will be working on a team that works on youth programs including, but not limited to, Youth Tutoring, online Youth English for Speakers of Other Languages (YESOL) classes, Leaders in Training (LIT), a college access and career readiness program for high school juniors and seniors, World Explorers, a cultural awareness program, and sports programming. During the annual Newcomer Youth Summer Academy (NYSA), the Youth Education Specialist will provide logistical support to teaching staff, coordinate instructional coaching, coordinate classroom assessment materials, and collect, enter, and analyze assessment data, ensuring the overall day-to-day classroom needs of the Academy are met. The specialist will also support with instruction and field trips during Mini-NYSA programs, which occur during school breaks in the middle of the school year.

**Major Responsibilities:**

This position will lead Youth English for Speakers of Other Languages (YESOL) classes:

**Curriculum Preparation**

- Create and improve YESOL curriculum to meet the needs of current student population, including academic English and test preparation
- Prepare slideshows for each class
- Update syllabi for each group as semester progresses

**Intake and Assessment**

- Manage new referral and contact information, outreach to potential families and students
- Administer baseline, midline and endline English assessments, coordinate intake process
- Collaborate with parents and teachers to identify specific student needs

**Teach YESOL Classes**

- 2-3 groups of Middle School: Beginner and Intermediate
- 2 groups of High School: Beginner and Intermediate
- Additional groups based on student need and program capacity

**YESOL Program Monitoring & Evaluation**

- Track class attendance and document daily individual and class case notes
- Gather qualitative data of program impact through student surveys and staff observations
- Synthesize and present data for annual reports

**Intern Management**

- Recruit and hire Youth ESOL interns
- Delegate weekly tasks and review submitted projects and tasks
- Provide opportunities for leadership and professional development

**Saturday Parent ESOL Classes**

- Take lead on managing ESOL classes for parents of youth programs students

**Mini Newcomer Youth Spring Academy (Mini NYSA) and Newcomer Youth Summer Academy (NYSA) Support** — direct responsibility for the academic program

- Support NYSA program planning, including staff and volunteer recruitment, hiring, and training
- Plan and instruct lessons on ESOL and other topics to groups of up to 25 students
- Participate in all Meet & Greets, staff trainings, program meetings, and staff development activities thereafter
- Assist the Dean of Instruction in the implementation and analysis of various student assessment initiatives, including but not limited to content area assessments, progress reports, and report cards
- Monitor submission of, enter, and analyze student assessment data
- Assist in the timely production and dissemination of necessary assessments and resources for all teaching staff
- Assist in the coordination and set up of caregiver-teacher conferences
- Assist in the coordination and implementation of school-wide Multi-Tiered Systems of Support (MTSS)
- Lead the coordination and implementation of all staff-appreciation events and initiatives
- Lead groups of students for off-site field trips
- Perform other duties as assigned

**Key Working Relationships:**

- Position reports to: Youth Programs Supervisor
- Position directly supervises: Interns
- Other internal and/or external contacts: Other youth program staff

**Job Requirements:**

- Bachelor's degree in education or relevant field; Master's degree candidate in education preferred
- Must be available for Saturdays to run programming
- Strong command of Microsoft Suite, G Suite, Canva, and other digital platforms required
- Classroom teaching experience preferred (both in-person and online, especially TESOL experience)
- Experience with data collection and analysis
- Strong organizational skills and meticulous attention to detail
- Strong written and oral communication skills
- Cultural competence and cross-cultural or overseas experience required
- Experience working with immigrant populations, highly desirable
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team
- Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, adapting programming to shifting client needs and relevant government policy changes
- Fluency in written and spoken English required. Second language proficiency in relevant language highly desirable (including Spanish, French, Dari, Farsi, Pashto, Arabic, Tibetan, Russian, Haitian Creole, Ukrainian, Mandarin, etc.)
- Flexibility to work on Saturdays and evenings based on program requirements

**Working Environment:**

- All applicants must be based in or willing to work from our New York City office
- The IRC NYC RAI office currently operates on a hybrid schedule (3 days in office, 2 remote)
- During Mini-NYSA and NYSA, the specialist is expected to work in-person Monday–Friday at a centrally located public school in New York City
- During school-year programming, the specialist will be expected to work Tuesday–Saturday
- Online ESOL classes during the school year take place after school hours; specialists should expect school-year hours of 11am–7pm, Tuesday–Friday
- Saturdays are in-person at the IRC office from 9am–5pm

***This position is expected to end on August 31, 2027.***

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $27.50/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Head of Programme Nigeria Abuja
body:
**About the Context**

Nigeria continues to face a complex and protracted humanitarian crisis driven by armed conflict, insecurity, climate-related shocks, displacement, and economic challenges.

The Northeast remains the epicenter of the crisis, where years of conflict have displaced millions of people and disrupted access to basic services, livelihoods, and protection. In addition, increasing levels of violence and displacement in the Northwest and North Central regions, alongside recurrent flooding and food insecurity, have further exacerbated protection and humanitarian needs across the country.

The 2026 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan estimates that 5.9 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance.

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) has been operating in Nigeria since 2015, delivering humanitarian assistance and durable solutions to conflict-affected and displaced populations. NRC works across multiple core competencies, including Education, Information, Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA), Shelter, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), and Protection from Violence. Through direct implementation and partnerships, NRC supports displaced persons, returnees, and vulnerable host communities to meet their immediate needs, strengthen resilience, and pursue long-term recovery and self-reliance.

NRC is committed to principled humanitarian action, safeguarding, accountability to affected populations, and ensuring that assistance reaches those most in need**.**

Find out more about NRC [https://www.nrc.no/](https://www.nrc.no/%22%20/t%20%22_blank) and Watch this short video to see NRC in action [https://vimeo.com/736782633](https://vimeo.com/736782633%22%20/t%20%22_blank)

**What we are looking for**

The purpose of the Head of Programme position is to develop and ensure implementation of holistic high-quality programmes. In this role you will provide strategic leadership and oversight for the Country Office’s programme portfolio, ensuring that projects and interventions are effectively designed, implemented, monitored, and aligned with the organization's mission, strategy, and donor requirements. Additionally, you will be responsible for driving programme quality, impact, accountability, and growth while ensuring efficient use of resources and compliance with organizational policies.

**What you will do**

1. In collaboration with the Programme Unit, lead the development of the Country Office fundraising strategy. This includes the mapping of donor policy and priorities and their alignment with NRC’s programmatic and advocacy goals.
2. Lead the development and implementation of NRC’s partnership strategy in Nigeria, ensuring effective collaboration with national and international partners, strengthening partner capacity, and promoting principled, equitable partnerships in line with NRC’s partnership framework.
3. Responsible for contributing to the development and implementation of country strategy.
4. Responsible for the coherence and quality of core competency programmatic input to all relevant processes and documents;
5. Responsible for strengthening our collaboration with other actors through building and strengthening networks, cooperation and implementing partnerships
6. Responsible for ensuring sound and timely grants management through NRC’s Project Cycle Management (PCM) framework and in line with donor requirements and best practice.
7. Responsible for ensuring consistency and promoting synergy between programme and support units
8. Acting Country Director (CD) when delegated

**What you will bring**

**1.Professional Competencies**

- A bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (programme management, business or a social science related). An advanced academic qualification will be an added advantage.
- Minimum 5 years’ experience from a senior management position in a humanitarian/ recovery context with responsibility for programme and/or project management
- Experience in NRC Core Competency programming is an asset.
- Experience of working on, coordinating or leading consortia or other forms of partnership implementation.
- Experience in MEAL systems and approaches, and accountability mechanisms and frameworks.
- Experience from working in complex and volatile contexts.
- Documented results related to the position’s responsibilities.
- Knowledge about own leadership skills/profile.
- Fluency in English, both written and verbal and excellent drafting skills.

***Context related skills, knowledge and experience***

- Knowledge of the Central and West Africa context and crisis;
- Experience with start-up, scale-up projects, emergency and early recovery contexts.
- Experience of mainstreaming evidence-based approaches to programme quality throughout the project cycle.
- Experience of working in integrated programmes.
- Knowledge of donor landscape, priorities and conditions.
- Effective team building, cross-cultural communication and conflict resolution skills;
- Experience in the design and delivery of team capacity strengthening, including remote coaching, mentoring and training.

**2.Behavioural competencies**

- Strategic thinking.
- Initiating action and change.
- Empowering and building trust.
- Managing resources to optimize results.
- Handling insecure environments.
- Deliver Results
- Act with Integrity

Find more details [Job Description\_Head of Programme Nigeria.pdf](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQAppsIWsn8pSrnsXD_8p7suATL_WSPKx1hUS6Wuia5fbLw?e=1wfFUD)

**What we offer**

- Duty station: Abuja, Nigeria
- Contract: 24 months
- Salary&benefits: grade 11 on NRC’s salary scale (The contract can be national/resident and/or international/mobile depending on final selected profile)
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.
- Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC [https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)
- Kindly send any questions about the application process to: ***cwa.recruitment@nrc.no***. *Applications sent via email will not be accepted. Please check your application status on your NRC application profile.*
