International Consultant/Consultancy Firm - CLIMATE RESILIENCE AND ADAPTATION & SOCIAL PROTECTION
body:
Midline Evaluation of: BUILDING CLIMATE RESILIENCE BY LINKING CLIMATE ADAPTATION AND SOCIAL PROTECTION THROUGH DECENTRALISED PLANNING IN MOZAMBIQUE  
•Short-term consultancy assignment  
•Evaluation period: October 2026 – July 2027  
•Period to be evaluated: 23 October 2024 – 31 March 2027  
•Consultancy location: Mozambique – Gaza, Manica and Tete Provinces

**Save the Children** believes every child deserves a future. We work to ensure children survive, learn, and are protected, particularly those living in the most vulnerable circumstances. Our work brings together local and global expertise to support communities, strengthen systems, and create lasting change for children and their families.

**About the project**  
The Building Climate Resilience by Linking Climate Adaptation and Social Protection through Decentralised Planning in Mozambique (LINK) is a five-year initiative supported by the Green Climate Fund (GCF) and approved by the GCF Board on 18 July 2024. The project is implemented from **23 October 2024 to 22 October 2029**, with Save the Children Australia serving as the GCF Accredited Entity.

The project seeks to strengthen the resilience of vulnerable children, households, and communities to climate-related risks by linking climate change adaptation, social protection, and decentralised planning. It aims to strengthen the capacity of communities and local institutions to anticipate, prepare for, and respond to climate-related shocks while improving food and water security, livelihoods, health and well-being, and resilient infrastructure.

The project is being implemented across three provinces—**Gaza, Manica and Tete**—and nine districts: Massangena, Mabalane and Mapai in Gaza; Machaze, Guro and Tambara in Manica; and Doa, Moatize and Mutarara in Tete.  
Implementation is undertaken through a partnership between Save the Children International Mozambique (SCIMOZ), the Ministry of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries (MAAP), and Save the Children Norway (SCN), under the overall accreditation of Save the Children Australia.

The project contributes to the GCF adaptation result areas of increased resilience of vulnerable people, communities and regions, and increased resilience of health and well-being, food and water security.

**The intervention is structured around three key result areas:**  
**Outcome 1**: Strengthened institutional and community capacity at district and provincial level on climate resilient measures that meet local needs  
**Outcome 2**: Priority locally led adaptation actions and social protection support identified in Local Adaptation Plans (LAPs) implemented by communities and local governments  
**Outcome 3:** Improved enabling environment through climate change adaptation mainstreaming into district development planning and budgeting, policy dialogue, dissemination, and learning

The project is expected to reach approximately 414,857 direct beneficiaries, including 233,116 women and girls, and approximately 559,863 indirect beneficiaries, including an estimated 285,530 women and girls.  
By connecting climate adaptation with social protection and decentralised planning, LINK seeks to contribute to more inclusive, locally relevant and sustainable approaches to climate resilience in Mozambique.

**A place to make a difference**  
Save the Children is seeking an international independent consultant or consultancy team to lead the midline evaluation of the LINK project, covering the implementation period from 23 October 2024 to 31 March 2027.  
As the project will continue until October 2029, this evaluation will be primarily formative and provides an opportunity to assess progress at an early stage of implementation and generate evidence and learning to inform adaptive management, programme improvement, accountability and strategic decision-making during the remaining project period.

The evaluation will assess the relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, emerging outcomes, sustainability and inclusiveness of the project, while examining the extent to which the intervention is contributing to strengthened climate resilience through the integration of climate adaptation, social protection and decentralised planning.  
The consultant will work closely with Save the Children, government counterparts, implementing partners, communities and other relevant stakeholders to generate credible evidence, identify lessons, and develop practical recommendations for strengthening implementation and sustainability.

In this consulting assignment you will:  
• Lead the design and delivery of the project evaluation, including development of the inception report, evaluation matrix, methodology, sampling approach and data collection tools.  
• Review relevant project documentation, monitoring data, baseline and other available evidence to assess progress towards intended results and identify key evidence gaps.  
• Conduct quantitative and qualitative data collection in selected project locations, including key informant interviews, focus group discussions, community consultations and other appropriate methods.  
• Engage with project participants, communities, government stakeholders, implementing partners and Save the Children teams at relevant national, provincial and district levels.  
• Assess the project's contribution to climate resilience, social protection, decentralised planning, food and water security, livelihoods, health and well-being, and resilient infrastructure.  
• Assess the extent to which the project is addressing the needs of women, girls, children, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups, including consideration of gender and social inclusion.  
• Analyse and triangulate quantitative and qualitative evidence to identify results, emerging outcomes, good practices, implementation challenges and factors influencing project performance.  
• Facilitate stakeholder reflection and validation of emerging findings and recommendations.  
• Produce a high-quality draft and final evaluation report, including clear, prioritised and actionable recommendations.  
• Develop an accessible evaluation summary/learning brief highlighting key findings, lessons and recommendations for programme and stakeholder use.  
• Ensure that all evaluation activities comply with Save the Children safeguarding, ethical, data protection and research standards.

**This consultancy requires:**  
• Minimum 7 years of demonstrated international experience conducting evaluations, research or learning assignments, preferably involving complex, multi-sector development, climate resilience, social protection or humanitarian programmes.  
• Demonstrated expertise in climate change adaptation, climate resilience and/or social protection, preferably in the context of decentralized planning and local governance.  
• Proven experience in designing and implementing mixed-methods evaluations, including quantitative and qualitative data collection and analysis.  
• Strong experience in conducting field-based research and consultations with communities, including vulnerable and marginalized populations.  
• Demonstrated ability to analyze programme performance and generate evidence-based, practical and actionable recommendations.  
• Experience working with government institutions, development partners, NGOs and community structures in Mozambique or similar contexts.  
• Strong understanding of gender equality, disability inclusion, child-sensitive programming and social inclusion.  
• Excellent analytical, report-writing and communication skills, with the ability to present complex findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.  
• Fluency in English and Portuguese is required. Knowledge of relevant local languages used in the project areas will be considered an advantage.  
• Previous experience evaluating projects funded by the Green Climate Fund or other climate finance mechanisms is highly desirable.  
• Willingness and ability to comply with Save the Children safeguarding policies, Code of Conduct and ethical requirements.

**Does this sound like the place for you?**  
We welcome applications from qualified consultants or consultancy teams with the relevant experience and expertise to undertake this important assignment.

  
**SUBMISSION OF APPLICATION**  
**Application and Submission Requirements**  
Interested candidates should submit a complete application package comprising the following:  
1.Cover letter outlining the candidate’s understanding of the assignment, relevant qualifications, and experience.  
2.Technical proposal The should demonstrate a clear understanding of the evaluation objectives and present the proposed evaluation design and methodology (maximum 10 pages, excluding annexes, CVs, references, sample assignments, and the Financial Proposal).  
3.Financial proposal, in USD with all costs envisaged including: Consultancy fees clearly separate from all other technical, logistics and admin costs.  
4.Annex: Team member composition and CVs of proposed consultancies, two to three sample assignment; contact details for three professional references with previous relevant assignment.

The technical and financial proposals will be evaluated based on both technical quality and financial value, with particular consideration given to the proposed methodology, relevant experience, feasibility of the approach, and the clarity and completeness of the financial proposal.

title: Intern - Information Management
source: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
body:
**Work Location**

Istanbul (in-person, remotely or hybrid); Full-time/Part-time

**Expected duration**

October - March 2026

**Duties and Responsibilities**

The Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) is the part of the UN Secretariat responsible for bringing together humanitarian actors to ensure a coherent response to emergencies. OCHA's mission is to mobilize and coordinate effective and principled humanitarian action in partnership with national and international actors in order to alleviate human suffering in disasters and emergencies; advocate the rights of people in need; promote preparedness and prevention and facilitate sustainable solutions. The Strategic Prioritization and Practices Branch (SPPB) helps OCHA and partners deliver more effective joint responses using innovative, state of the art coordination tools and services. The work of the Branch focuses on the key activities which enable effective coordination: needs assessment and analysis, humanitarian response planning and continuous response monitoring. SPPB aims to ensure OCHA and partner staff have the skills, tools and technical support needed to meet the needs of people affected by crises through a well- coordinated collective response effort, within the framework of a rigorous Humanitarian Programme Cycle (HPC). The intern will be located in the Humanitarian Programme Cycle Section (HPCS) within SPPB. Daily responsibilities will depend on the individual's background and duties may include but are not limited to providing assistance with the design and preparation of studies on humanitarian response, emergency relief and other related issues and in various follow-up activities; researching, analyzing and presenting information gathered from diverse sources on assigned topics/ issues; assisting with the preparation of various written documents, e.g. drafts sections of studies, background papers, policy guidelines, parliamentary documents etc.; assisting in the maintenance of reference/ resource information on specific topics or policy related issues; providing support with the organization of meetings, seminars, conferences, work-shops, etc., and serving as note-taker to such events; maintains awareness of current humanitarian affairs and related issues, to include relevant political, policy, gender considerations or other developments in specific subject area and/or country or region concerned and; performs other tasks requested by supervisor, as appropriate. In addition, the intern shall be given specific tasks related to Strategic Prioritization and Practices Branch (SPPB)’s work on response monitoring. Key Tasks • Provide field support to country offices and regional offices on response monitoring, including on the use of HPC (Humanitarian Programme Cycle) tools. • Support data collection and data analysis including identifying trends and patterns related to response monitoring to inform operational and strategic decision-making. • Support the management and maintenance of databases and content management systems, ensuring humanitarian information is well-organized, accurate and easily accessible. • Provide support related to the management of population figures (People in Need, People Targeted, People Reached, People Covered). • Support the Humanitarian Plans History project recovering historical data on past humanitarian response plans, reviewing and cleaning the data. • Manage spreadsheets and other data tools; understand, document, and ensure the quality of high-value humanitarian data for accuracy, consistency and comparability. • Conduct literature reviews and desk research on good practices and innovations in humanitarian response monitoring. • Support in production and update of information products such as reports and charts by analyzing trends and turning data into graphical products. Internships are designed to be full-time or part-time and may be conducted in person, remotely, or in a hybrid format, with the modality adjustable based on the request of the successful candidate. This internship is offered at full-time, for a maximum period of six (6) months, beginning at a mutually agreed time, in person, based in Istanbul (Türkiye), though remote or hybrid arrangements may also be explored.

**Qualifications/special skills**

Applicants must meet one of the following requirements: • Be enrolled in, or have completed, a graduate school programme (second university degree or equivalent, or higher); • Be enrolled in, or have completed, the final academic year of a first university degree programme (minimum bachelor's level or equivalent), Preferably in areas related to political science, social science, humanitarian affairs, international studies, public administration, economics, engineering, earth sciences or in a related field. • Applicants to the UN Internship Programme are not required to have professional work experience. However, a field of study that is closely related to the type of internship that you are applying for is required. Your training, education, advanced course work or skills should benefit the United Nations during your internship. • Skills in information management, data analysis, database management, cleaning, treating, analyzing and presenting data and content management systems are required. • A keen interest in identifying trends and patterns in humanitarian data and data visualization is required. • Demonstrates strong attention to detail and a commitment to precision is desirable. • Keen interest in humanitarian coordination architecture is desirable. • Excellent writing and communication skills are desirable.

**Languages**

English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this internship fluency in English (both oral and written) is required. Knowledge of French and/or Spanish is desirable.

**Additional Information**

Not available.

**Intern Specific text**

Interns are not financially remunerated by the United Nations. Costs and arrangements for travel, visas, accommodation and living expenses are the responsibility of interns or their sponsoring institutions. Interns who are not citizens or permanent residents of the country where the internship is undertaken, may be required to obtain the appropriate visa and work/employment authorization. Successful candidates should discuss their specific visa requirements before accepting the internship offer.

**No Fee**

THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CHARGE A FEE AT ANY STAGE OF THE RECRUITMENT PROCESS (APPLICATION, INTERVIEW MEETING, PROCESSING, OR TRAINING). THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CONCERN ITSELF WITH INFORMATION ON APPLICANTS’ BANK ACCOUNTS.

title: Chef de projet de services logistiques ATLAS – Bunia / RDC
body:
Lieu : Bunia / RDC  
Date souhaitée de démarrage : Début novembre 2026  
Durée de contrat : 5 mois

Handicap International / Humanity & Inclusion (HI) est une association de solidarité internationale indépendante et impartiale, qui intervient dans les situations de pauvreté et d’exclusion, de conflits et de catastrophes. Œuvrant aux côtés des personnes handicapées et vulnérabilisées, elle agit et témoigne pour répondre à leurs besoins essentiels et améliorer leurs conditions de vie. Elle s’engage à promouvoir le respect de leur dignité et de leurs droits fondamentaux.

Depuis sa création en 1982, HI a mis en place des programmes de développement dans plus de 55 pays et intervient dans de nombreuses situations d’urgence. Aujourd'hui, nous avons un budget d'environ 200 millions d'euros, avec 4000 employés dans le monde.

Chez Handicap International, nous croyons fermement en l'importance de l'inclusion et de la diversité au sein de notre structure. C'est pourquoi nous sommes engagés dans une politique handicap afin de favoriser l'accueil et l'intégration de personnes en situation de handicap.

Merci d’indiquer si vous avez besoin d’un aménagement particulier, y compris pour participer aux 1ers entretiens. Retrouvez plus d’informations sur l’association : [www.hi.org](http://www.hi.org/).

**CONTEXTE :**   
Depuis la fin des années 1990, la RDC connaît une instabilité chronique, liée à des fragilités de gouvernance interne et à sa proximité avec des pays en crise. Cette situation limite l'accès à des services sociaux de qualité pour une population estimée entre 100 et 120 millions d'habitants. La faible gouvernance des ressources publiques affaiblit par ailleurs la gestion des risques de catastrophes : face aux crises, la réponse gouvernementale peine souvent à couvrir l'ensemble des besoins, un défi persistant pour la population.

La province de l'Ituri, à l'est du pays, illustre particulièrement cette complexité. Elle fait face à une situation humanitaire caractérisée par la persistance des conflits armés, d'importants déplacements de population et des besoins humanitaires élevés. À cette crise sécuritaire s'ajoute, depuis le 15 mai 2026, une 17ᵉ épidémie de maladie à virus Ebola déclarée dans la zone de santé de Mongbwalu. Cette flambée s'est rapidement propagée : au 21 septembre, 63 zones de santé (soit 37,7%) étaient touchées dans sept provinces, ce qui en fait, selon l'OMS et Africa CDC, la deuxième plus importante épidémie d'Ebola jamais documentée et la plus rapide en termes de croissance. La majorité des nouvelles infections provenant de chaînes de transmission non identifiées, les limites de la surveillance et du suivi des contacts demeurent un enjeu central de la réponse.

Cette situation exerce une forte pression sur les capacités logistiques, notamment à Bunia mais également dans certaines zones de santé, où les besoins en transport, en stockage sec et en stockage à température contrôlée dépassent largement les capacités locales disponibles. C'est dans ce contexte exigeant, à l'intersection des enjeux sécuritaires, humanitaires et épidémiologiques, que Handicap International souhaite relancer ses activités dans cette zone en renforçant et en facilitant le stockage et l’acheminement de l’aide humanitaire fournie par les acteurs humanitaires.

Ainsi, le projet Atlas Logistique lance des activités de stockage et de transport afin d’appuyer la réponse logistique de la riposte. Celles-ci comprendront :

- L’opérationnalisation d’une capacité de stockage médical (15°-25°C / 2° - 8°C) et le renforcement des opérations de transport au départ de ce site à destination des centres de santé Ebola (CTE),
- L’opérationnalisation de plusieurs capacités de stockage avancées en région et le renforcement des opérations de transport au départ de ces hubs afin de répondre aux besoins identifiés par l’ensemble des acteurs humanitaires.

Ce projet s’inscrit dans le cadre de l’ouverture actuelle d’une sous-base Handicap International à Bunia et tend à positionner Atlas Logistique comme un acteur logistique majeur de la riposte à la MVE.

**VOTRE MISSION :**  
Sous la responsabilité du Manager des Opérations, le Chef de Projet contribue au sein de son pays de rattachement à la mise en œuvre du mandat et de la stratégie d’Humanité & Inclusion. Il est responsable de la mise en œuvre de son projet. Dans ce cadre-là, il veille à l’optimisation de la qualité et de l’impact du projet, par le biais d’un système de délégation avec des mécanismes de contrôle appropriés. Il partage avec tous les autres responsables HI la charge d’une gestion saine et d’un bon fonctionnement de l’organisation globale

Vos principales responsabilités seront :

1\) Management

2\) Stratégie et pilotage

3\) Mise en œuvre opérationnelle

Veille au respect des normes et standards techniques globaux HI/Atlas en communiquant et en impliquant les conseillers et spécialistes techniques compétents Atlas sur les thématiques du projet.

\- Accompagne la finalisation de la phase d’ouverture et la mise en opération des différents hubs avancés, conformément au cadre logique et au budget alloué

\- Assure la continuité du projet, conformément au cadre logique et au budget alloué

\- S’assure que la mise en œuvre du projet est conforme aux cadres existants

\- En lien avec l’équipe MEAL et le plan MEAL établi pour le projet, assure le suivi, l’évaluation, la redevabilité et l’apprentissage du projet

\- Assure la gestion des données projet

\- Assure l’animation fonctionnelle des équipes sur son projet

\- Contribue à la communication sur le projet en externe

4\) : Préparation et réponse aux urgences

Vos responsabilités spécifiques Atlas seront notamment :

\- Supervise la gestion de l’entrepôt : allocation des espaces de stockage, suivi des stocks partenaires, inventaires périodiques et respect des procédures AL.

\- Planifie et coordonne les convois mutualisés pour les partenaires humanitaires en respectant les priorités et les contraintes sécuritaires.

\- Valide la planification des opérations de transport et s’assure du suivi de la flotte de véhicules

\- Met à jour et exploite les outils de suivi du projet (PM Box, planning de transport, OFU, tableau de priorisation, indicateurs de performance).

\- Collecte et analyse les données de transport (volumes, délais, taux de satisfaction des partenaires) et de stockage (occupation, rotation).

\- S’assure de la bonne application des SOP sécurité transport et entrepôt par l’équipe (briefings chauffeurs, suivi radio, rapports d’incidents).

\- Coordonne les relations avec les partenaires utilisateurs, assurer le suivi des demandes de service et la redevabilité (feedbacks).

**VOTRE PROFIL :**

- Vous avez au moins 2 ans d’expérience professionnelle dans le secteur du transport, une expérience en gestion de projet est vivement recommandée
- Vous avez au moins 1 an d’expérience en gestion d’équipe
- Vous êtes en capacité de travailler sous pression et dans un contexte de sécurité volatile, vous avez un excellent sens de la communication et maîtrisez parfaitement le français, l’anglais est vivement souhaité.

**CONDITIONS :**

Chez HI, les conditions de départ sont à la hauteur de votre engagement et adaptées au contexte de votre mission. Une attention particulière est portée aux questions de santé et à votre situation personnelle : [https://hi.org/fr/travailler-chez-hi](https://hi.org/fr/travailler-chez-hi)

Le poste est aussi ouvert localement.

- Contrat International de 5 mois à compter idéalement de début novembre 2026 basé à Bunia ;
- Le contrat international permet une couverture sociale adaptée aux besoins de chacun :
    - Assurance chômage prélevée uniquement pour les ressortissants de l’UE ;
    - Assurance retraite ;
    - Couverture santé, rapatriement, prévoyance prises en charge par HI et par l’employé ;
- **Salaire** : à partir de 2757 € brut/mois ;
- **Perdiem** : 684 € net/mois – versé en monnaie locale sur le terrain ;
- **Hardship :** 500 € net/mois
- **Congés payés** : 25 jours par an ;
- **R&R** : 5 Jours toutes les 8 semaines
- **Poste :** Non accompagné
- Logement : Collectif pris en charge par HI ;
- Si vous êtes résident(e) dans le pays : package local.
