PROVISION OF CLEANING INTERNAL, EXTERNAL FACILITIES AND TEA STEWARD SERVICE
body:
**1. INTRODUCTION**  
Heifer International is a global nonprofit organization working to end hunger and poverty while caring for the Earth. Since its establishment in 1944, Heifer International has supported millions of farming families by strengthening sustainable agriculture, improving livelihoods, and building resilient communities. Heifer International has been implementing development programmes in Kenya since 1981, working with smallholder farmers and communities to improve agricultural productivity, incomes, food security, and livelihoods.

Heifer International Kenya invites qualified and experienced service providers to submit proposals for the provision of professional cleaning and gardening services at the Heifer International Kenya office located at Ndama Place, Nairobi.  
The selected service provider will be expected to provide reliable, professional, safe, and high-quality cleaning and tea service in accordance with the requirements outlined in this request for proposal and applicable Kenyan laws and regulations.

**2. RATIONALE**  
The provision of high-quality cleaning, facilities management, and tea steward services is essential to maintaining a clean, hygienic, safe, well-organized, and conducive working environment for staff, partners, visitors, and other stakeholders.  
The successful service provider shall be responsible for delivering professional cleaning and facilities support, and providing professional tea steward services to support the daily preparation, serving, and management of refreshments for staff, visitors, meetings, and official office functions. The services will include maintaining high standards of hygiene, cleanliness, food safety, and courteous service, and properly caring for kitchen equipment and supplies at the Heifer International Kenya Country Office on scheduled working days and at agreed times, in accordance with the required service standards, scope of work, and contractual terms.  
The service provider shall:  
• Provide professional cleaning facilities management services with due care, diligence, efficiency, and attention to detail. The service provider shall ensure that all internal and external areas are maintained in a clean, hygienic, safe, and presentable condition;  
• The service provide will ensure tea and refreshments are prepared and served promptly and professionally; and facilities-related tasks are undertaken effectively. All services shall comply with agreed service standards, schedules, occupational health and safety requirements, and applicable organizational policies.  
• Be responsible for the recruitment, employment, remuneration, statutory compliance, supervision, welfare, and performance management of its personnel.  
• Comply with applicable Kenyan labour laws, statutory requirements, minimum wage regulations, working hours, leave provisions, occupational health and safety requirements, and other applicable employment obligations.  
• Provide competent relief or replacement personnel during annual leave, sick leave, planned or unplanned absence, at no additional cost to Heifer International Kenya.  
• Ensure all personnel deployed are suitably qualified, trained, instructed, supervised, and equipped to perform their duties.  
• Provide appropriate uniforms and personal protective equipment (PPE), where applicable.

**3. OBJECTIVES OF THE ASSIGNMENT**  
The main objectives of the assignment are to:

- Maintain a clean, hygienic, safe, and professional office environment.
- Ensure effective cleaning and sanitation of offices, meeting rooms, washrooms, kitchen areas, corridors, and common areas.
- Provide adequately trained, supervised, and properly equipped cleaning and tea service personnel.
- continuity and reliability of services throughout the contract period.
- Promote compliance with applicable health, safety, labour, and environmental requirements. .

**4. EXPECTED DELIVERABLES**  
4.1 Cleaning Services  
The service provider shall undertake, but not be limited to:  
• Daily cleaning of offices and workspaces.  
• Cleaning and disinfecting washrooms and sanitary facilities.  
• Cleaning floors, corridors, stairways, and common areas.  
• Cleaning and polishing office furniture and surfaces.  
• Cleaning and preparation of meeting and conference rooms.  
• Emptying and cleaning of waste bins.  
• Collection and appropriate disposal of waste.  
• Cleaning windows, glass surfaces, doors, and other accessible areas.  
• Quarterly deep cleaning as required.  
• Additional cleaning support during meetings, events, or other official activities where required.  
4.2 Supervision and Quality Control The service provider shall:  
• Provide adequate supervision of deployed personnel.  
• Monitor service quality and compliance with the agreed work programme.  
• Address service deficiencies promptly.  
• Maintain appropriate attendance and service records.  
• Coordinate with the designated Heifer International Kenya Contract Manager.

**5. QUALIFICATIONS OF THE SERVICE PROVIDER**  
The service provider should demonstrate:  
Valid legal registration and statutory compliance in Kenya.

- At least three years' relevant experience in the provision of cleaning, tea service and facility management services.
- Capacity to recruit, deploy, supervise, and replace personnel as required.
- Availability of appropriate cleaning equipment, materials, chemicals, and PPE for deployed staff.
- Commitment to professional conduct, safeguarding, confidentiality, and occupational health and safety. .

**6. EVALUATION CRITERIA**  
Mandatory Evaluation  
• Current Tax Compliance Certificate  
• KRA PIN  
• Certificate of Business Registration  
• Business Permit.  
• Bank Account Details  
• CR12  
• Physical address, contact person, telephone number and email address.  
• Signed written declaration of Labour Laws and Minimum Wage Compliance  
• Three recommendation letters from firms/organizations to which the bidder has provided or is currently providing similar services within the last three years.  
• Company profile  
• Technical proposal for service provision  
• Financial proposal detailed with a monthly cost breakdown.

Note: Failure to provide any mandatory document or evidence may result in disqualification.  
Technical Evaluation  
• Cleaning Equipment and Accessories – List of at least five equipment/accessories owned by the firm, including vacuum cleaners, with intended use.  
• List of detergents and chemicals to be used.  
• Detailed cleaning work programme/schedule.  
Requirements Prior to Contract Signing  
• Certificate of good conduct provision for deployed staff.  
• Valid Food Handler’s Medical Certificate for kitchen staff.

**7. LATE SUBMISSIONS AND MODIFICATIONS**  
Proposals received after the submission deadline will not be considered. Applicants are responsible for ensuring that their proposals are submitted in accordance with the instructions stated herein. Heifer reserves the right to terminate this request for proposals or modify the requirements upon notice to applicants.

**8. VALIDITY OF PROPOSALS**  
Proposals submitted shall remain open for acceptance for Thirty (30) days from the last date specified for receipt of the proposal. This includes, but is not limited to, pricing, terms and conditions, service levels, and all other information. If your organization is selected, all information in this document and the negotiation process is contractually binding.

**9. LIMITATIONS**  
This Request for Proposal does not represent a commitment to award a contract, to pay  
any costs incurred in the preparation of a response to this RFP, or to procure or to contract for services or supplies. Heifer reserves the right to fund any or none of the applications submitted and reserves the right to accept or reject in its entirety and absolute discretion any proposal received because of the request for the proposal.

**10. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY**  
Section 1. Ownership Generally. Subject to Section 2 below, any intellectual property (including but not limited to copyrights, trademarks, service marks, and patents), intellectual property rights, deliverables, manuals, works, ideas, discoveries, inventions, products, writings, photographs, videos, drawings, lists, data, strategies, materials, processes, procedures, systems, programs, devices, operations, or information developed in whole or in part by or on behalf of Contractor or its employees or agents in connection with the Services and/or Goods (collectively, the "Work Product") shall be the exclusive property of HPI. Upon request, the  
Contractor shall sign all documents and take all actions necessary to confirm or perfect HPI's exclusive ownership of the Work Product.  
Section 2. Prior-Owned Intellectual Property. Any intellectual property owned by a Party before the Effective Date ("Prior-Owned IP") shall remain that Party's sole and exclusive property. Regarding any of Contractor's Prior-Owned IP included in the Work Product, Contractor shall retain ownership, and hereby grants HPI a permanent, nonexclusive, royalty-free, worldwide, irrevocable right and license to use, copy, reproduce, publicly display, edit, revise, perform, and distribute said intellectual property, in any format or any medium, as part of the Work Product.  
Section 3. Work Made for Hire. To the extent copyright laws apply to the Work Product, the Parties agree that (a) HPI specially ordered or commissioned the Work Product, (b) the Work Product is a "work made for hire" under United States copyright laws, and (c) HPI shall be deemed the author thereof and shall own all right, title, and interest therein. To the extent such rights, in whole or in part, do not vest in HPI as a "work made for hire", Contractor hereby irrevocably grants, assigns, and transfers to HPI, exclusively and in perpetuity, all of the Contractor's rights of any kind or nature, now known or hereafter devised, in, too, and in connection with the Work Product, and HPI shall solely and exclusively own any rights therein, and in the elements thereof, including but not limited to any allied, ancillary, subsidiary, incidental, and adaptation rights. The Contractor hereby waives all rights known as "moral rights" and any similar rights that the Contractor may have in connection with the Work Product. The description of Services and/or Goods provided in this Agreement shall in no way limit the way HPI may use the Work Product.

**11. DIVERSITY AND INCLUSION**  
Heifer International values diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging (“DEIB”) and believes that effectively accessing and managing diverse talent leads to improved outcomes. HPI takes a broad view of diversity and is inclusive of varied backgrounds, including, but not limited to, age, experience, race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, disability status, national origin, and culture. HPI expect third-party providers to respect and reflect HPI’s value of DEIB. HPI’s ongoing monitoring of third-party service providers incorporates an assessment of vendors’ commitment to, adherence with, and track record of accessing and retaining diverse and inclusive workforces.

title: International Education Expert
body:
**About STOOS**

STOOS is an international research and consulting firm providing **evaluations, assessments, research, capacity building and project management** services across humanitarian and development settings. We work with NGOs, international organizations and other partners to generate evidence, strengthen programmes and improve outcomes for communities across the Middle East, Africa, Eastern Europe and beyond.

STOOS invites applications from experienced **international Education Experts** to collaborate on education-related consultancy assignments. **Experts based in any country are welcome to apply.** Assignments will be **primarily remote**, with occasional travel depending on project requirements and agreed availability.

**Role Overview**

The Education Expert will provide technical and strategic support to education assignments, drawing on substantial experience in **managing and implementing education projects internationally**. The role will include contributing to programme design, evaluations, assessments, research and capacity building, working closely with STOOS teams, clients and national partners.

We are particularly interested in experts who combine **practical programme management experience with strong research, evaluation and analytical skills**, and can translate evidence into feasible recommendations for education programming.

**Key Responsibilities**

- **Programme design and technical support:** Contribute to education strategies, theories of change, results frameworks and implementation approaches that improve access, quality, equity and learning outcomes.
- **Project management and implementation:** Provide guidance on work planning, implementation quality, partner coordination, monitoring and adaptive management.
- **Evaluations, assessments and research:** Lead or contribute to education evaluations, needs assessments, feasibility studies and thematic research, including methodology development, sampling and research tool design.
- **Technical analysis:** Assess issues relating to formal and non-formal education, teacher development, inclusive education, education systems and **Education in Emergencies (EiE)**.
- **Data analysis and reporting:** Review programme documentation, analyse qualitative and quantitative findings, and produce clear reports with practical recommendations.
- **Stakeholder engagement:** Facilitate consultations, interviews and workshops with education authorities, donors, implementing partners, teachers, learners and community representatives.
- **Capacity building:** Develop training resources and strengthen the capacities of project teams, local partners and researchers through coaching and technical guidance.
- **Quality assurance and safeguarding:** Ensure deliverables meet agreed standards and integrate **child safeguarding, research ethics, gender equality, disability inclusion and conflict sensitivity**.
- **Proposal development:** Contribute technical inputs to education-related proposals, including approaches, methodologies, workplans and deliverable frameworks.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- A **Master’s degree or higher in Education, International Education, Education Policy, International Development** or a closely related discipline.

**International Professional Experience**

- **At least eight years of professional experience in managing and implementing education projects internationally**, including work across different country contexts.
- Demonstrated responsibility for education programme planning, delivery, team or partner coordination, monitoring and quality assurance.
- Experience working with **international NGOs, UN agencies, donors, government institutions or international consulting organizations**.
- Strong understanding of challenges affecting education access, participation, retention and learning outcomes, particularly for marginalized and crisis-affected populations.
- Demonstrated experience conducting or contributing to **education evaluations, assessments or research**, using qualitative and quantitative methods.
- Experience translating programme evidence into actionable recommendations for implementing organizations, policymakers and development partners.

**Technical and Collaboration Skills**

- Strong analytical skills and the ability to produce **clear, well-structured reports**.
- Ability to develop research tools, review data quality and synthesize findings from multiple sources.
- Proven ability to collaborate with **multicultural teams and national partners**, including through remote working arrangements.
- Strong organizational skills, responsiveness and the ability to deliver high-quality outputs within agreed deadlines.
- Commitment to safeguarding, ethical research and culturally appropriate engagement with children, young people and communities.

**Languages**

- **Fluency in English is mandatory**, including excellent speaking, analytical writing and report-writing skills.
- **Proficiency in additional languages is an asset.**

**Areas of Expertise of Particular Interest**

Applicants may bring expertise in one or more of the following areas:

- **Education in Emergencies** and education in conflict or displacement settings.
- Inclusive education, disability inclusion and gender-responsive programming.
- Teacher professional development, pedagogy and teaching quality.
- Foundational literacy and numeracy, learning assessment and learning recovery.
- Non-formal education, accelerated education and pathways back into formal schooling.
- Education systems strengthening, policy analysis and institutional capacity development.
- Early childhood education and development.
- Integration of child protection, psychosocial support and wellbeing within education programmes.

**Working Arrangements**

Engagements will be **consultancy-based and linked to specific assignments**. Most activities—including document review, methodology development, remote consultations, analysis, reporting and technical coordination—will be undertaken remotely.

The scope, duration, level of effort and fees will be agreed for each assignment. Where travel is required, arrangements will be discussed in advance.

title: Project Manager - West Africa
body:
**Position Summary:**

Shelter For Life International (SFL) is anticipating a project in West Africa with a focus on managing the flow of migrants into the region. Included in the Project’s objectives will be structured movement and resettlement of migrants within and outside Guinea Bissau, while providing basic food, shelter and other humanitarian assistance.

Shelter For Life is seeking a Project Manager to lead an anticipated program in West Africa. The Project Manager will be responsible for the overall implementation, oversight, and successful achievement of project goals. The Project Manager will provide quality assurance and control of all program deliverables as well as provide leadership, supervision, and direction to the project’s field staff and operations. The position will be based in Bissau city, Guinea Bissau.

**Areas of Responsibility:**

*Strategic Leadership*

- Provide supervision, support, and direction to field staff
- Lead a multi-national, multi-lingual, and multi-skilled group of professionals
- Establish relationships with various partners and stakeholders, such as the donor organization, governmental ministries, national, regional and local authorities, partner organizations, and represent SFL at key meetings
- Bring focus and determination to the project staff to ensure high-quality results, and prioritize the achievement of the program’s goals

*Quality Project Management*

- Develop and oversee detailed regular, periodic work plans and ensure the project meets all deliverables
- Provide quality reports on project progress to SFL headquarters and the project donor
- Carefully monitor project performance and document progress on project indicators
- Provide oversight and guidance to the project’s finance department to maintain adherence to the

program’s budget and financial plans in accordance with donor requirements and SFL’s internal controls

- Coordinate and communicate activities with SFL HQ, PRM, the US Embassy, and local government officials
- Implement and enforce procedures that ensure compliance with US Government rules and regulations
- Enforce SFL’s internal control procedures, outlined by SFL’s Field Operations Manual, Employee Handbook and the Who we Are, What we Believe, and How we Serve documents.

*Technical Oversight*

- Responsible for strategy, logistics, technical oversight and guidance of project components
- Provide overall responsibility for all data collection, monitoring and evaluation
- Oversee a range of activities for coherence and harmonious operation of the program’s activities

## Education and Experience Requirements:

- Master’s degree in project management, or related fields.
- Demonstrated track record in managing logistics, project-indicators and project objectives within insecure areas and fragile markets.
- Thorough and demonstrated understanding of population management and migrant resettlement.
- A minimum of eight years of relevant professional management level experience in logistics, particularly in fragile and unstable environments.
- A minimum of five years of work experience as Logistics Manager, Project Manager, or similar level management position.
- Prior work experience with UNHCR and/or IOM-funded or similar international donor-funded programs is preferred and advantageous.
- Demonstrated experience in reporting project progress in adherence with donor guidelines.
- Strong leadership and administrative skills, problem-solving management ability in a cross-cultural environment.
- Strong communications and interpersonal skills with evidence of ability to productively interact with a variety of stakeholders and organizations.
- Prior work experience in Africa required; specific experience in West African countries preferred.

## Personal Skills & Abilities:

- Proven leadership skills with ability to maintain a positive work environment with professionalism.
- Strong teamwork and listening skills combined with excellent interpersonal skills and cross-cultural sensitivity.
- Ability to analyze, coordinate, and plan, both strategically andinnovatively.
- Ability to quickly assess complex situations and form accurate understanding.
- Ability to respond practically, using adaptive management to operate successfully in difficult field conditions
- Willingness to adopt the use of locally appropriate technologies.
- Ability to be flexible, persistent, and diplomatic to gain respect among staff and diverse stakeholders including local community leaders, governmental ministries, and the donor organization.
- Proficiency in written and spoken English required; strong command of Portuguese is strongly preferred; knowledge of French is a plus.

SFL is interested in applicants whose professional ethics, values, and determination to achieve impact are evident and aligned with organizational priorities.

## Additional notes:

- A minimum of 12+ months commitment to live and work in Guinea Bissau is required.
- Applicants must be comfortable with frequent travel, especially in West Africa.
- Competitive pay and generous benefits including six weeks of paid time off, two weeks of R&R, ACA compliant health insurance, and allowances for housing, food, and communication.

**About Us:**

Shelter For Life International (SFL) is an international faith-based relief and development organization with over 30 years’ experience in providing sustainable development and humanitarian assistance to post-conflict countries around the world. We are currently operational in Afghanistan, The Gambia, and Ukraine, with headquarters located in Minnetonka, MN, USA. Our team provides support and assistance in the following areas:

1. Population Movement and Settlement
2. Public Infrastructure Reconstruction
3. Economic and Social Development

Our mission is to demonstrate God’s love by enabling people affected by conflict and disaster to restore their lives and rebuild their communities. To learn more about us, please visit [www.shelter.org](http://www.shelter.org/)

title: Complaints and PSEA Advisor
body:
Location: home-based; ideally South Africa or another location in similar time-zone  
Duration of contract: 1 year (possibility for extension)  
Supervisor: Global Coordinator PMER, Complaints and Safeguarding  
Start date: as soon as possible

**Lutheran World Federation (LWF) World Service**  
LWF World Service is the humanitarian and development arm of the Lutheran World Federation. We are a widely recognized, international, faith-based organization working in more than 20 countries globally. We seek to bring people of all backgrounds together in the common quest for justice, peace, and reconciliation in an increasingly complex and fragmented world. A commitment to the human rights of every individual, regardless of their status, guides our work, actions, and operations. We are particularly known for our timely, compassionate, and professional humanitarian work, and for our field presence in hard-to-reach areas. Our work is people-centered and community-based. Above all, we work with the most vulnerable, and to claim and uphold their rights, we engage proactively with local government and community structures. For additional information, please see LWF World Service.

**Purpose**  
Complaints and PSEA Advisor supports the Global Coordinator PMER, Complaints and Safeguarding in the implementation and strengthening of complaints handling and PSEA systems across LWF World Service.  
The position provides operational and technical support in complaint intake and case management, investigations, CRM monitoring and reporting, PSEA, capacity strengthening, and digital and knowledge management. The position requires a high level of confidentiality, sound judgment and the ability to work independently while knowing when matters need to be escalated to the Global Coordinator.  
The Advisor works closely with CRM and PSEA Focal Points in LWF Country Programs to support consistent implementation of LWF policies, systems and requirements across the Country Programs. The position also works with relevant Geneva-based functions, when required.

**Required qualifications**  
University degree in a relevant field such as social sciences, law, human rights, international development or another related field.  
Recognized training or certification in investigations.

**Knowledge and experience**  
At least 3 years of relevant professional experience in complaints handling, investigations, PSEA, safeguarding or related areas.  
Practical experience in complaint intake, assessment, referral and case management.  
Good knowledge of complaints handling, PSEA and safeguarding standards and practices in humanitarian and development contexts.  
Experience conducting workplace or misconduct investigations, including interviews, evidence review and investigation reporting.  
Experience providing training, coaching or technical support, preferably in humanitarian or development settings.  
Experience working with digital information systems, databases or collaboration platforms.

**Language skills**  
English required: fluency  
French and/or Spanish are an asset

**LWF Core Skills**  
Achieving results – advanced\*  
Accountability – resourced  
Working effectively with others - advanced  
Analytical thinking - advanced  
Initiative - advanced  
Leadership - resourced

**LWF Functional Skills**  
Attention to detail - advanced  
Capacity building / Training – advanced  
Confidentiality Management – advanced  
Analytical Thinking - resourced  
Information Management – advanced

\*LWF 3 skills levels are: basic - advanced – resourced

The LWF and LWF workers must adhere to the values and principles outlined in the Code of Conduct as well as the Core Humanitarian Standard and relevant LWF policies such as Protection from Sexual Abuse, Exploitation and Harassment (PSEAH), Child Protection and Gender Justice Policy. The staff member must conduct himself/herself both professionally and personally in such a manner as to bring credit to the LWF and to not jeopardize its humanitarian mission.

**Main duties**  
**Complaints Handling and Investigations**  
Supports the day-to-day management of the LWF Complaint mailbox, including acknowledgment, initial assessment, referral, intake analysis, registration and follow-up of complaints.  
Reviews and analyses complaints and recommends appropriate handling or escalation in line with LWF policies and procedures.  
Maintains accurate and confidential case information in the complaints database and supports CRM Focal Points with complaint handling and documentation.  
Conducts or supports investigations when assigned, including planning, interviews, evidence review and preparation of investigation reports.  
Acts as the designated backup for the LWF Complaint mailbox during the absence of the Global Coordinator and ensures continuity of complaint handling.

**CRM Monitoring, Systems and Implementation**  
Supports the monitoring of CRM implementation across Country Programs and follows up identified gaps with CRM Focal Points.  
Coordinates the quarterly CRM reporting process, reviews the quality and completeness of submissions and follows up where information is missing or incomplete.  
Supports the review and improvement of the CRM quarterly reporting tool and process.  
Supports the rollout and consistent use of ActivityInfo for complaint recording and monitors the quality and completeness of information recorded by Country Programs.  
Reviews CRM information and complaint data to identify recurring gaps, trends and areas requiring additional support.

**PSEA**  
Supports the Global Coordinator with the review, update and rollout of the LWF World Service PSEA Policy.  
Provides technical support to PSEA and CRM Focal Points on the implementation of PSEA requirements at Country Program level.  
Supports and follows up PSEA self-assessments and UN PSEA assessments, including review of evidence, identification of gaps and follow-up of agreed actions.  
Develops and delivers PSEA induction, training and refresher sessions and supports focal points in strengthening staff awareness.  
Identifies recurring PSEA gaps and brings significant or systemic issues to the attention of the Global Coordinator.

**Capacity Strengthening and Technical Support**  
Supports the induction and onboarding of new CRM Focal Points and provides ongoing coaching and technical support to CRM and PSEA Focal Points.  
Develops and delivers practical training and refresher sessions on complaint handling and CRM based on identified needs.  
Supports focal points in strengthening complaint mechanisms and related processes and facilitates learning and exchange between focal points when useful.

**Digital Systems and Knowledge Management**  
Reviews and organizes existing CRM, complaints, investigation and PSEA resources, helping to reduce duplication, archive outdated materials and simplify the resources available to Country Programs.  
Supports the development and maintenance of a structured SharePoint site where Country Programs can easily access current guidance, templates, training materials and other resources related to Complaint and PSEA.  
Supports the effective use of ActivityInfo, SharePoint and other relevant digital systems and works with Data & Analytics and other colleagues when technical support is required.

**Major Challenges**  
Handling sensitive and confidential information while managing several priorities at the same time.  
Supporting more consistent implementation of CRM and PSEA requirements across different Country Program contexts.  
Turning policies and technical requirements into practical and user-friendly approaches.  
Managing multiple priorities, taking initiative and ensuring timely coordination on sensitive or complex matters.

title: Recruitment for Multiple (Senior) Analyst Positions Across Multiple Regions & Countries: Acute Needs Analysis, Multiple Locations
body:
*Veuillez trouver la version française ci-dessous*

*PLEASE NOTE: This is a global call for applications to fill multiple Analyst and Senior Analyst vacancies hosted across various IMPACT country offices in Latin America & the Caribbean (LAC), Middle East & North Africa (MENA), and Sub-Saharan Africa. Candidates should indicate their preferred analysis context (see table below) on the application form. In your cover letter, please provide your motivation for the top 3 analysis context preferences you select on the application form*

## **BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH**

Founded in 2010 and headquartered in Geneva, [IMPACT Initiatives](https://www.impact-initiatives.org/what-we-do/) is a leading applied research organization and the largest independent provider of data in crisis-affected contexts. Through our initiatives—REACH, AGORA, and PANDA—we enable humanitarian and other aid actors to make better, evidence-based decisions by delivering timely, relevant, and methodologically rigorous data and analysis. Our extensive presence across crisis-contexts allows us to collect data directly from crisis-affected people wherever needed, including among the most vulnerable and hard-to-reach. [REACH](https://www.impact-initiatives.org/what-we-do/reach/), initiative of IMPACT, strengthens evidence-based humanitarian decision-making through efficient data collection, management, and analysis – before, during, and after an emergency.

All of IMPACT’s programs are implemented in support of humanitarian coordination structures. IMPACT’s team comprises specialists in data collection, management, and analysis, as well as experts in humanitarian response, GIS, and remote sensing.

### We are currently looking for various (Senior) Analysts – Acute Needs Analysis to support our teams in multiple locations.

**Position:** (Senior) Analyst – Acute Needs Analysis

**Contract duration**: Up to 6 months

**Starting Date**: Mid-September 2026

**Location**: Multiple country office locations across **LAC**, **MENA**, **Sub-Saharan Africa** (see below location preference to be indicated on applicant form).

### POSITION PROFILE

In response to the shifting humanitarian financing landscape, IMPACT is placing greater emphasis on producing **comparable, decision-oriented analysis products to inform humanitarian prioritization.** This position will be working on the second round of the Acute Needs Analysis (ANA) - a flagship analytical output that summarizes available data to provides a concise, actionable understanding of **risk of loss of life** across geographies and population groups within a crisis **in order to feed into key decision-points, such as the HPC and donor allocations.**

The **(Senior) Analyst – Acute Needs Analysis** will be responsible for producing this analytical product at country level. This includes reviewing and synthesizing data, conducting structured analysis using IMPACT’s global analytical guidance, and producing a short, high-impact external brief. The analyst will work closely with GIS, data, and design colleagues to incorporate visual elements into the final output. The final analytical product will play a key role in informing humanitarian prioritization decisions.

### RESPONSIBILITIES

#### DEVELOPMENT OF ANALYTICAL PRODUCT - ACUTE NEEDS ANALYSIS

- Lead the implementation and delivery of the analysis project at the country level, in coordination with the HQ programme team.
- Align the rollout with global schedules and ensure adherence to IMPACT’s analytical standards.
- Develop and maintain a strong stakeholder mapping and a network of collaborators at country level to enhance contextual understanding / monitoring.
- Ensure development of user-centered products and, where relevant, support joint analysis with relevant stakeholders.

#### DATA REVIEW AND CONSOLIDATION

- Collect and synthesize relevant secondary data from REACH assessments, UN agencies, INGOs, and public datasets (e.g., OCHA, FEWS NET, IPC), including via building and maintaining necessary relationships.
- Evaluate data reliability and identify critical gaps.
- Support decisions on the need for targeted, light-touch primary data collection.

#### ANALYTICAL PROCESS AND INTERPRETATION

- Apply IMPACT’s global analytical guidance to produce structured, consistent, and context-relevant analysis of acute needs analysis.
- Use defined frameworks (e.g. Risk of Excess Mortality) to identify areas at risk of large-scale loss of life and estimate the number of people experiencing life-threatening conditions
- Clearly document assumptions, limitations, and analytical reasoning.

#### OUTPUT PRODUCTION AND DISSEMINATION

- Draft the Acute Needs Analysis brief using standardized global templates and language.
- Collaborate with GIS and design colleagues to include maps, caseload tables, and other visual aids.
- Ensure internal review and validation of the product before dissemination.
- Present findings to clusters, working groups, and donors as needed.
- As needed, support the development of Global Key Messages based on country level findings.

#### LEARNING, INNOVATION, AND QUALITY ASSURANCE

- Participate in lessons-learned reviews and propose improvements to global analysis processes and guidance.
- Contribute to organisational learning on running analysis workstreams and contribute to reflections and development of additional analytical workstreams, in collaboration with country and global counterparts.
- Support internal knowledge sharing and analytical training at the country level.
- Stay updated on sectoral best practices and innovations in humanitarian analysis.
- The (Senior) Analyst will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes. They will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to IMPACT and its partners, or collected during his/her assignment with IMPACT.

### REQUIREMENTS

Note, roles can be at Senior Analyst or Analyst level, based on the experience of the candidate.

#### REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- **3** **years of relevant working experience** in a humanitarian setting, such as analysis, assessments, monitoring and evaluation and research design etc. with direct in-country experience;
- **Excellent academic qualifications**, including a master’s degree or equivalent in a relevant discipline (e.g. international development studies / international relations, humanitarian response, data science, political science, etc.);

#### TECHNICAL SKILLS:

- **Excellent analytical and critical thinking skills** with experience of interpreting complex data and producing clear, actionable insights.
- **Strong writing skills** and experience producing clear, concise briefs for external audiences.
- **Proficiency in Excel**, with experience of an additional analytical tool (e.g. PowerBI, SPSS, R, STATA, or Python) and an understanding of basic GIS processes and outputs an asset.
- **Familiarity with different qualitative and quantitative research methods**, with the ability to evaluate the quality of different data sources.
- **Understanding of humanitarian coordination systems**, including HPC and inter-agency needs analysis and assessments.
- **Contextual knowledge** is an asset. Please highlight in your application if you have experience working in one or more of the potential contexts listed below

#### COMMUNICATION AND ORGANIZATIONAL SKILLS

- **Ability to manage complex workflows** and deliver high-quality outputs under tight deadlines.
- **Experience engaging with external stakeholders** (e.g. clusters, donors, UN agencies).
- **Fluency in English required**; additional languages required based on location (see ‘Additional Requirements’).
- **Comfortable working** in cross-cultural, fast-paced environments.
- **Sound judgment and emotional intelligence** in high-pressure or sensitive situations, strong interpersonal awareness and the ability to respond constructively to feedback and shifting priorities.
- **Please indicate in the applicant form if you have completed a HEAT training.**

#### ANALYSIS CONTEXT LOCATIONS AND ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

The exact locations where the ANA will be conducted in 2026 will be confirmed pending funding The below is a tentative *list of possible* crises to be analysed.

### COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

- For this position, depending on the seniority of the role and the location salary between 2’100 CHF and 3'120 CHF monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD
- *NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined based on our salary grid, which takes into account both the grade of the position and the staff member’s level of education. In addition, a location-specific security and/or isolation allowance may be applied to acknowledge the challenging living and working conditions in certain duty stations.*
- Accommodation and food provided in the guesthouse.
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary, employer-funded in addition to gross salary), MSH health insurance, life insurance and ISOS repatriation assistance.
- Flight tickets at the beginning and at the end of the contract & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered).
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: 23 kg of luggage allowance (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

### \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

*VEUILLEZ NOTER : il s’agit d’un appel à candidatures global visant à pourvoir plusieurs postes d’Analyste et d’Analyste Senior au sein de différents bureaux pays d’IMPACT en Amérique latine et aux Caraïbes (ALC), au Moyen-Orient et en Afrique du Nord (MENA), ainsi qu’en Afrique subsaharienne. Les candidat·e·s sont invité·e·s à indiquer leur contexte d’analyse préféré (voir tableau ci-dessous) sur le formulaire de candidature. Dans votre lettre de motivation, veuillez indiquer les raisons de vos trois principales préférences de contexte d'analyse sélectionnées sur le formulaire de candidature.*

## CONTEXTE SUR IMPACT ET REACH

Fondée en 2010 et basée à Genève, [IMPACT Initiatives](https://www.impact-initiatives.org/what-we-do/) est une organisation de recherche appliquée de référence et le principal fournisseur indépendant de données dans les contextes de crise. À travers ses initiatives (REACH, AGORA et PANDA), IMPACT permet aux acteurs humanitaires et autres acteurs de l’aide de prendre de meilleures décisions fondées sur des données probantes, en leur fournissant des données et analyses rigoureuses, pertinentes et livrées en temps utile. Notre présence étendue dans les contextes de crise nous permet de collecter des données directement auprès des populations affectées, y compris les plus vulnérables et les plus difficiles à atteindre. [REACH](https://www.impact-initiatives.org/what-we-do/reach/), une initiative d’IMPACT, renforce la prise de décision humanitaire fondée sur des données probantes grâce à une collecte, une gestion et une analyse efficaces des données, avant, pendant et après une urgence.

L’ensemble des programmes d’IMPACT est mis en œuvre à l’appui des structures de coordination humanitaire. L’équipe d’IMPACT est composée de spécialistes en collecte, gestion et analyse de données, ainsi que d’expert·e·s en réponse humanitaire, SIG et télédétection.

### Nous recherchons actuellement plusieurs (Senior) Analystes en Besoins Aigus pour rejoindre nos équipes dans plusieurs lieux d’affectation.

**Poste :** (**Senior) Analyste en Besoins Aigus (ANA)**

**Durée du contrat** : Jusqu’à 6 mois

**Date de début** : Mi-septembre 2026

**Lieu** : Plusieurs bureaux pays en **ALC**, **MENA** et en **Afrique subsaharienne** (voir ci-dessous la localisation à indiquer sur le formulaire de candidature).

### PROFIL DU POSTE

Face à l’évolution du paysage du financement humanitaire, IMPACT met davantage l’accent sur la production de **produits d’analyse comparables et orientés vers la décision, au service de la priorisation humanitaire.** Ce poste portera sur le deuxième cycle de l’Analyse des Besoins Aigus (ANA), un produit analytique phare qui synthétise les données disponibles afin de fournir une compréhension claire et exploitable du **risque de perte de vies humaines** à travers les zones géographiques et les groupes de population au sein d’une crise, **afin d’alimenter des points de décision clés, tels que le HPC et les allocations des bailleurs de fonds.**

L’**Analyste (Senior) en Besoins Humanitaires Aigus** sera chargé·e de produire ce produit analytique au niveau pays. Cela inclut la revue et la synthèse des données, la conduite d’une analyse structurée à l’aide des orientations analytiques globales d’IMPACT, ainsi que la production d’une note externe courte et à fort impact. L’analyste travaillera en étroite collaboration avec les équipes Data, SIG et design pour intégrer des éléments visuels au produit final. Le produit analytique final jouera un rôle clé dans les décisions de priorisation humanitaire.

### RESPONSABILITÉS

#### ÉLABORATION DU PRODUIT ANALYTIQUE : BESOINS HUMANITAIRES AIGUS

- Piloter la mise en œuvre et la livraison du projet d’analyse au niveau pays, en coordination avec l’équipe programme du siège.
- Aligner le déploiement sur les calendriers globaux et veiller au respect des standards analytiques d’IMPACT.
- Développer et entretenir une cartographie solide des parties prenantes ainsi qu’un réseau de collaborateur·rice·s au niveau pays afin de renforcer la compréhension du contexte et le suivi.
- Assurer le développement de produits centrés sur les utilisateur·rice·s et, le cas échéant, appuyer les analyses conjointes avec les parties prenantes concernées.
- REVUE ET CONSOLIDATION DES DONNÉES
- Collecter et synthétiser les données secondaires pertinentes issues des évaluations REACH, des agences des Nations Unies, des ONG internationales et des bases de données publiques (par ex. OCHA, FEWS NET, IPC), notamment en développant et entretenant les relations nécessaires.
- Évaluer la fiabilité des données et identifier les lacunes critiques.
- Appuyer les décisions relatives à la nécessité d’une collecte de données primaires ciblée et légère.

#### PROCESSUS ANALYTIQUE ET INTERPRÉTATION

- Appliquer les orientations analytiques globales d’IMPACT afin de produire une analyse structurée, cohérente et adaptée au contexte des besoins humanitaires aigus.
- Utiliser des cadres définis (par ex. le risque de surmortalité) pour identifier les zones à risque de pertes de vies humaines à grande échelle et estimer le nombre de personnes en situation de menace vitale
- Documenter clairement les hypothèses, les limites et le raisonnement analytique.

#### PRODUCTION ET DIFFUSION DES LIVRABLES

- Rédiger la note de l’Analyse des Besoins Aigus à l’aide des modèles et du langage standardisés au niveau global.
- Collaborer avec les équipes SIG et design afin d’intégrer cartes, tableaux de caseload et autres supports visuels.
- Assurer la revue et la validation internes du produit avant sa diffusion.
- Présenter les résultats aux clusters, groupes de travail et bailleurs de fonds selon les besoins.
- Selon les besoins, appuyer le développement des messages clés globaux sur la base des résultats au niveau pays.

#### APPRENTISSAGE, INNOVATION ET ASSURANCE QUALITÉ

- Participer aux revues de leçons apprises et proposer des améliorations aux processus et orientations d’analyse globaux.
- Contribuer à l’apprentissage organisationnel sur la conduite des chantiers d’analyse et participer aux réflexions et au développement de nouveaux chantiers analytiques, en collaboration avec les équipes pays et le siège.
- Appuyer le partage interne de connaissances et les formations analytiques au niveau pays.
- Se tenir informé·e des bonnes pratiques sectorielles et des innovations en matière d’analyse humanitaire.
- L’(Senior) Analyste maintiendra la plus stricte confidentialité sur l’ensemble des données collectées et des processus associés. Il/elle prendra activement des mesures pour prévenir tout partage non autorisé d’informations et de données appartenant à IMPACT et à ses partenaires, ou collectées au cours de sa mission avec IMPACT.

### PROFIL REQUIS

À noter : le poste peut être pourvu au niveau Analyste ou Analyste Senior, en fonction de l’expérience du/de la candidat·e.

#### QUALIFICATIONS REQUISES

- **3** **ans d’expérience professionnelle pertinente** dans un contexte humanitaire, telle que l’analyse, les évaluations, le suivi-évaluation et la conception de recherche, etc. avec une expérience directe sur le terrain ;
- **D’excellentes qualifications académiques**, comprenant de préférence un master ou équivalent dans une discipline pertinente (par ex. études du développement international / relations internationales, action humanitaire, data science, sciences politiques, etc.) ;

### COMPÉTENCES TECHNIQUES :

- **D’excellentes compétences analytiques et de réflexion critique**, avec une expérience de l’interprétation de données complexes et de la production de résultats clairs et exploitables.
- **De solides compétences rédactionnelles** et une expérience dans la production de notes claires et concises destinées à des publics externes.
- **Maîtrise d’Excel**, avec une expérience d’un outil d’analyse supplémentaire (par ex. PowerBI, SPSS, R, STATA ou Python) ; une compréhension des processus SIG de base et de leurs livrables est un atout.
- **Bonne connaissance des différentes méthodes de recherche qualitatives et quantitatives**, avec la capacité d’évaluer la qualité de différentes sources de données.
- **Compréhension des systèmes de coordination humanitaire**, y compris le HPC et les analyses et évaluations des besoins inter-agences.
- **La connaissance du contexte** est un atout. Merci de préciser dans votre candidature si vous avez une expérience de travail dans l’un ou plusieurs des contextes potentiels listés ci-dessous

#### COMPÉTENCES EN COMMUNICATION ET EN ORGANISATION

- **Capacité à gérer des flux de travail complexes** et à produire des livrables de qualité dans des délais serrés.
- **Expérience de collaboration avec des parties prenantes externes** (par ex. clusters, bailleurs de fonds, agences des Nations Unies).
- **Maîtrise de l’anglais requise** ; des langues supplémentaires peuvent être requises selon la localisation (voir « Exigences supplémentaires »).
- **À l’aise pour** travailler dans des environnements interculturels et à rythme soutenu.
- **Bon jugement et intelligence émotionnelle** dans des situations sous pression ou sensibles, solide sens relationnel et capacité à réagir de manière constructive aux retours et aux priorités changeantes.
- **Merci d’indiquer dans le formulaire de candidature si vous avez suivi une formation HEAT.**

#### CONTEXTES D’ANALYSE, LOCALISATIONS ET EXIGENCES SUPPLÉMENTAIRES

Les localisations exactes où l’ANA sera menée en 2026 seront confirmées sous réserve du financement. Voici une *liste provisoire* des crises susceptibles d’être analysées.

### REMUNERATION ET AVANTAGES

- Pour ce poste, selon le niveau de séniorité et la localisation, le salaire mensuel se situe entre 2’100 CHF et 3’120 CHF (avant impôt sur le revenu), etc., ainsi qu’une allocation de subsistance mensuelle de 300 USD
- *NB : les salaires d’IMPACT sont strictement déterminés selon notre grille salariale, qui prend en compte à la fois le grade du poste et le niveau d’éducation du/de la salarié·e. Une allocation de sécurité et/ou d’isolement spécifique à la localisation peut également être appliquée afin de tenir compte des conditions de vie et de travail difficiles dans certains lieux d’affectation.*
- Hébergement et repas fournis en guesthouse.
- Affiliation à la caisse de pension privée suisse (Swisslife, environ 9,975 % du salaire brut, financé par l’employeur en plus du salaire brut), assurance santé MSH, assurance vie et assistance de rapatriement ISOS.
- Billets d’avion au début et à la fin du contrat, ainsi que frais de visa pris en charge (les frais de déplacement dans le pays et les dépenses professionnelles sont intégralement couverts).
- Contribution au transport des bagages : franchise de 23 kg (+ assurance bagages et effets personnels)
- 36 jours de congés annuels par an. Jours fériés du pays d’affectation. Congé familial/pour raisons personnelles lorsque applicable.
- IMPACT accorde une priorité à la sécurité psychologique de son personnel ; l’assurance santé fournie couvre, entre autres, jusqu’à 1000 € par an de frais de soutien psychosocial.

title: Chief Audit Executive (CAE) / Head of Internal Audit
body:
**Background:**

The Asian Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC) is an autonomous international organization working to build the resilience of people and institutions to disasters and climate change in Asia and the Pacific. ADPC operates through partnerships with governments, development partners, donors, civil society, academia, and other stakeholders, and manages programs, grants, projects, country operations, procurement, finance, human resources, information systems, and other institutional functions.

ADPC has adopted the Three Lines Governance Model. Management owns and manages risks; Risk Management, Compliance, Legal, Quality Assurance and other oversight functions form the second line; and Internal Audit provides independent assurance as the third line. The Internal Audit function is intended to strengthen ADPC’s ability to create, protect, and sustain value through independent, risk-based and objective assurance, advice, insight and foresight.

ADPC’s Board of Trustees approved the Internal Audit Policy in August 2026. The Policy requires the Internal Audit function to operate in conformance with The Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA) Global Internal Audit Standards and establishes the organizational independence, authority, reporting relationships, responsibilities, and quality requirements of the function.

ADPC therefore seeks a highly qualified and experienced Chief Audit Executive (CAE) to establish, lead and continuously strengthen an independent and risk-based Internal Audit function appropriate to ADPC’s mandate, operating environment, donor-funded portfolio, governance arrangements, and risk profile.

**Purpose and Objectives:**

The Chief Audit Executive will provide strategic leadership and effective management of ADPC’s Internal Audit function and provide the Board of Trustees and Executive Committee with independent, objective and risk-based assurance and advisory services on the adequacy and effectiveness of governance, risk management and internal control.

The CAE will ensure that the Internal Audit function is established and operated in accordance with ADPC’s Internal Audit Policy and the applicable IIA Global Internal Audit Standards, while maintaining independence, objectivity, professional judgment, confidentiality, and due professional care.

**Organizational Independence and Reporting:**

- The CAE shall report functionally to the Board of Trustees. Where the Board establishes an Audit Committee and delegates relevant oversight responsibilities to it, the CAE shall work directly with the Audit Committee within that delegated authority.
- The CAE shall report administratively to the Executive Director for day-to-day administrative matters.
- The CAE shall have direct and unrestricted access to the Board of Trustees and, where applicable, the Audit Committee, including the ability to communicate in private without management present.
- The CAE shall be free from interference in determining the scope of internal auditing, performing work, communicating results, allocating resources, selecting subjects, and applying audit techniques.
- The CAE shall promptly disclose any actual, potential, or perceived impairment to independence or objectivity, as well as any inappropriate scope or resource limitation, to the appropriate governance body.

**Scope of Work and Key Responsibilities:**

1\. Establish and Manage the Internal Audit Function

- Establish and maintain the Internal Audit function, methodologies, procedures, templates, documentation standards, and operating arrangements in accordance with ADPC’s Internal Audit Policy and applicable professional standards.
- Develop and periodically update an Internal Audit Universe covering ADPC’s significant activities, processes, risks, systems, programs and entities, including governance, finance, procurement, human resources, information technology and cybersecurity, project management, country offices, grants management, safeguarding, business continuity, climate and environmental risks, and third-party management.
- Develop a risk-based annual Internal Audit Plan and a rolling three-year strategic Internal Audit Plan, taking into account ADPC’s objectives, risk profile, donor obligations, governance priorities, management input, and emerging risks.
- Present the proposed audit plans, resource requirements and material revisions for review and approval by the Board of Trustees/Audit Committee, as applicable.
- Ensure that Internal Audit collectively possesses or obtains the knowledge, skills and competencies necessary to fulfil its mandate, including through specialist or co-sourced support where required.

2\. Perform and Oversee Internal Audit Engagements

- Plan and conduct risk-based assurance and advisory engagements across ADPC in accordance with the approved Internal Audit Plan.
- For each engagement, hold an opening meeting with the relevant process owner; perform walkthroughs and understand key processes and controls; obtain and assess relevant documents and evidence; test the design and operating effectiveness of controls; identify root causes, risks and control gaps; and develop practical, risk-based recommendations.
- Validate observations and factual accuracy with process owners and responsible management before finalization.
- Prepare clear, concise and evidence-based draft and final internal audit reports, obtain management responses and agreed action plans, and communicate significant matters to senior management and the Board/Audit Committee as appropriate.
- Conduct closing meetings with process owners and management and follow up on agreed corrective actions until appropriately resolved or formally accepted.
- Undertake advisory assignments where requested and appropriate, without assuming management responsibility or impairing Internal Audit independence.

3\. Governance, Risk, Control and Donor Assurance

- Assess the adequacy and effectiveness of ADPC’s governance, enterprise risk management and internal control arrangements.
- Assess compliance with ADPC policies and procedures, contractual obligations, donor requirements, applicable laws and regulations, and relevant governance standards.
- Review fiduciary risk areas relevant to an international and donor-funded organization, including financial management, procurement, grants and sub-grants, project management, third-party management, fraud risk, safeguarding, information technology, cybersecurity, and data governance.
- Evaluate whether resources and assets are acquired economically, used efficiently and sustainably, and adequately safeguarded.
- Identify significant or emerging risk exposures, control weaknesses, fraud risks, governance issues, and other matters requiring Board or management attention.

4\. Quality Assurance and Improvement

- Develop, implement and maintain a Quality Assurance and Improvement Program (QAIP) covering all aspects of the Internal Audit function.
- Conduct ongoing monitoring and periodic internal self-assessments of conformance with the Global Internal Audit Standards and the achievement of Internal Audit performance objectives.
- Establish appropriate performance measures and stakeholder feedback mechanisms for the Internal Audit function.
- Report the results of internal quality assessments and improvement actions to the Board/Audit Committee and Executive Committee at least annually.
- Support arrangements for an independent external quality assessment at least once every five years, in accordance with the Global Internal Audit Standards and ADPC’s Internal Audit Policy.

5\. Reporting and Stakeholder Engagement

- Provide periodic and annual reporting to the Board/Audit Committee and Executive Committee on the Internal Audit mandate, plan implementation, significant findings, management action status, resource requirements, budget, quality, conformance, and matters affecting independence.
- Maintain constructive professional relationships with the Board, Executive Director, Executive Committee, management, external auditors, donors, assurance providers, and other relevant stakeholders while preserving Internal Audit independence.
- Coordinate, where appropriate, with internal and external assurance providers to reduce unnecessary duplication and improve assurance coverage.

**Expected Outputs / Deliverables:**

**Deliverable 1 – Internal Audit Framework and Planning**

**Establishment of the Internal Audit framework and risk-based planning package**, including:

(i) initial assessment of the Internal Audit function, governance arrangements, assurance coverage and priority institutional risks, including inception/work plan;

(ii) comprehensive Internal Audit Universe and documented risk assessment methodology; and (iii) risk-based one-year Internal Audit Plan and rolling three-year strategic Internal Audit Plan for Board/Audit Committee review and approval.

**Timeline: November 2026** – to be completed in time for the relevant BoT meeting

**Deliverable 2 – Implementation**

**Implementation of the approved risk-based Internal Audit Plan**, including conduct of planned audit engagements, preparation and maintenance of appropriate working papers, issuance of engagement-level reports, follow-up of recommendations and provision of periodic updates, as required. This phase shall also include development and application of Internal Audit methodology, engagement procedures, working-paper/reporting templates, recommendation follow-up mechanisms, supporting tools, and the Quality Assurance and Improvement Program (QAIP) including a competency development/ training plan for personnel supporting Internal Audit, and implementation of the approved risk-based Internal Audit Plan through individual audit engagements.

**Timeline: December 2026 – December 2027**

**Deliverable 3 – Reporting, Knowledge Transfer and Close-out**

Establishment/finalization of the **Quality Assurance and Improvement Program (QAIP)**, including periodic internal self-assessments against applicable **Global Internal Audit Standards (GIA)**, defined performance indicators, stakeholder feedback and continuous improvement arrangements. Preparation of a **consolidated/annual Internal Audit report** covering work performed, key findings and recommendations, implementation/follow-up status and overall outcomes; presentation/reporting to the BoT/Audit Committee, as applicable; and completion of knowledge transfer and capacity development.

**Timeline: December 2027 – January 2028**, aligned with the relevant BoT/Audit Committee reporting

**Note:** The above deliverables, sequencing and timelines are indicative and may be adjusted and finalized in consultation with the selected service provider and relevant ADPC stakeholders, taking into account the approved Internal Audit Plan, operational requirements, and the applicable BoT/Audit Committee meeting and reporting schedule.

**Working Principles:**

The Consultant, acting as the **Chief Audit Executive (CAE)/ Internal Audit Lead,** shall perform the assignment independently and objectively. The Consultant shall **functionally report to the Board of Trustees (BoT) or the Audit Committee, if established,** including on the risk-based Internal Audit Plan, significant audit findings, Internal Audit performance, and the results of the Quality Assurance and Improvement Program (QAIP). The Consultant shall have direct access to the BoT/Audit Committee as required. For administrative and day-to-day coordination, the Consultant shall liaise with the **Executive Director and designated ADPC focal point(s).** Such coordination shall facilitate access to relevant personnel, records, systems, meetings and other information necessary for the assignment and shall not affect the independence, professional judgment, scope, findings or reporting of the Internal Audit function.

During individual audit engagements, the Consultant shall work directly with the relevant **Directors, Unit Heads, process owners and designated counterparts** for engagement planning, process walkthroughs, document review and testing, validation of findings and recommendations, management responses, and follow-up actions. The Consultant shall participate in and present to the **BoT and/or Audit Committee,** as required, including for approval of the Internal Audit Plan and reporting of Internal Audit results and QAIP outcomes.

**Qualifications and Competencies:**

1\. Minimum Academic Qualification

- Master’s degree in Accounting, Auditing, Finance, Business Administration, Public Administration, Risk Management, or another relevant field.

2\. Professional Certification

- An active Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) designation is required for the candidate.   
    The individual performing the CAE role must hold an active Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) designation.
- Additional relevant professional credentials such as CPA/CA, CISA, CFE, CRMA, ACCA or equivalent will be an advantage.

3\. Professional Experience

- Minimum of ten (10) years of progressively responsible professional experience in internal audit, assurance, governance, risk management, controls or closely related areas, with substantial experience in internal audit.
- Demonstrated experience leading, managing and developing an Internal Audit function or audit teams, including risk-based planning, engagement oversight, reporting, follow-up and quality management.
- Demonstrated experience reporting to, or interacting directly with, an Audit Committee, Board of Directors/Trustees or equivalent governing body.
- Experience developing strategic and annual risk-based audit plans aligned with organizational objectives and risk profiles.
- Experience in international organizations, multilateral development organizations, United Nations agencies, INGOs, or donor-funded programs/projects is highly desirable.
- Demonstrated understanding of donor compliance, grant management, fiduciary risk management and accountability frameworks is highly desirable.

4\. Technical Knowledge

- Comprehensive knowledge and practical application of the IIA Global Internal Audit Standards and the International Professional Practices Framework (IPPF).
- Strong knowledge of governance, enterprise risk management, internal control frameworks including COSO, and the Three Lines Model.
- Demonstrated competence in risk-based auditing, performance auditing, fraud risk management and investigation concepts, information technology/cybersecurity auditing, and data analytics for audit and assurance.
- Ability to assess complex institutional, operational, financial, compliance, project and donor-related risks and translate audit findings into practical and proportionate recommendations.
- Sound understanding of quality assurance and improvement requirements for Internal Audit.

5\. Leadership, Communication and Personal Competencies

- High degree of integrity, independence, objectivity, professional courage and sound judgment.
- Strong strategic leadership, change management, stakeholder engagement and negotiation skills.
- Excellent analytical, critical-thinking and problem-solving abilities.
- Excellent report writing, presentation and communication skills, including the ability to communicate sensitive or significant audit matters effectively to senior management and governing bodies.
- Excellent command of written and spoken English.

**Independence and Conflict of Interest:**

- The candidate/engagement lead must be free from any actual, potential or perceived conflict of interest that could impair independent professional judgment.
- The CAE shall have no direct operational or management responsibility for activities subject to Internal Audit review.
- Any actual or potential conflict, prior responsibility for an activity under review, or other impairment to independence or objectivity must be disclosed promptly and appropriate safeguards applied.
- The CAE shall comply with the ethics and professionalism requirements of the Global Internal Audit Standards and ADPC’s applicable policies.

**Evaluation Criteria:**

Candidates/proposals that do not meet any mandatory eligibility requirement may be determined non-responsive before weighted scoring. Subject to confirmation in the solicitation document, responsive candidates/proposals may be evaluated using the following indicative weighted criteria

- Curriculum Vitae of the candidate or designated engagement lead, clearly demonstrating the required qualifications and experience.
- Copy/evidence of active CIA certification and any other relevant professional credentials.
- Brief technical approach describing how the candidate/firm would establish and manage the Internal Audit function, develop the risk-based audit plan, conduct engagements, report to governance bodies, and implement QAIP if applicable.
- Disclosure of any actual, potential or perceived conflicts of interest and confirmation of independence.
- Financial proposal in the format required by ADPC.

**Confidentiality and Ownership:**

The CAE and any personnel supporting the Internal Audit function shall maintain strict confidentiality over information obtained in the course of the assignment and shall safeguard ADPC records and information. All internal audit working papers, reports, risk assessments, plans, methodologies and other outputs produced specifically for ADPC under the engagement shall be handled and owned in accordance with the applicable contract and ADPC policies.

**Performance and Review:**

Performance will be assessed against the approved Internal Audit Plan, quality and timeliness of engagements and reporting, implementation of the Internal Audit strategy and QAIP, stakeholder and Board/Audit Committee feedback, adherence to professional standards, and the CAE’s effectiveness in maintaining independence and providing relevant risk-based assurance and advice.

**Duty Station:**

ADPC Headquarters, Bangkok, Thailand, with travel as required.

**Itinerary:**  Any travel required for the assignment shall be undertaken only with the prior approval of ADPC and shall be arranged and/or reimbursed in accordance with applicable ADPC policies, rules, and procedures.

**Condition of payment:** Indicate whether the payment will be phased, based on completion of outputs.

title: Infection Prevention Control (IPC) Manager - DRC - French proficiency mandatory
body:
**INFECTION PREVENTION CONTROL MANAGER – EBOLA EMERGENCY RESPONSE**

**PURPOSE**

Responsible for the Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) activities and leads the development & maintenance of an infection control program, according to **MSF** protocols and standards in order to ensure the quality of care and safety of patients, caretakers and staff

**WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR IPC MANAGER IN THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO – EBOLA EMERGENCY RESPONSE**

- Available for deployment within the next 3 months for your first rotation of 12-16 weeks, followed by a mandatory 21-day post-deployment monitoring period.
- French proficiency (at least B2)
- Experienced in Ebola response, VHF, outbreak, or emergency response (strong asset)
- Flexible and adaptable in fast-changing environments
- Resilient under high-pressure humanitarian conditions
- Committed to teamwork and MSF principles
- Ready for remote and resource-limited field settings
- Nursing / MD / EPI / pharmacist diplomas
- Essential: IPC diploma (validated by the OC IPC advisor)
- Desirable: Tropical Medicine

**Accountabilities**

· Participating in the definition of the IPC objectives and in collaboration with the IPC committee, defining, implementing and monitoring the IPC annual plan Based on a Stepwise Infection Prevention and Control Approach (SIPCA) assessment (together with the IPC supervisor)

· Setting up regular monitoring mechanisms for IPC activities, analyzing the results, identifying priorities and proposing solutions when necessary. Establishing, maintaining and improving surveillance systems for health care associated infections in the facility. Participating and contributing in the elaboration of the contingency plan and EPREP regarding the IPC aspects depending on context and possible scenarios

· In collaboration with each service activity manager, ensuring and maintaining the implementation of the standard precautions and transmission-based precautions in health structures in all departments including sterilization, laundry, kitchen, hygiene agents and providing technical supervision and expertise, support, training and guidance to the staff on IPC related issues using existing tools such as audits, checklist, surveillance, etc. and developing training plan and materials as required.

· Setting up mechanisms for the implementation and monitoring of the adherence to additional precautions for air, droplet and contact transmissible diseases when indicated, adapting general guidelines to the health facility realities, putting isolation algorithms in place and ensuring adequate nosocomial outbreak detection and response.

· Designing and ensuring the implementation of correct ‘clean and dirty flows’ inside the health facility. Ensuring that the environmental standards in the facility are respected and together with the Hospital Facilities Manager and WHS Supervisor, that the essential requirements are available in the health structures

· Guaranteeing compliance to aseptic care techniques and to the correct use of antiseptics, disinfectants and detergents.

· Monitoring and analyzing the consumption and the quality of IPC materials and equipment

· Planning and supervising, with the support of HR department, the associated HR processes (recruitment, training/induction, evaluation, potential detection, motivation, development and internal communication) of the staff in the project under his/her responsibility, in order to ensure having the appropriate team in terms of size, capabilities and skills.

· Reporting any irregularities to the PMR (as functional manager) in addition to NAM, MAM, supervisors… and proposes immediate actions when necessary. Producing reports with information and recommendations for the monthly medical reporting. Follows up and consolidates data from different departments.

Note:

· IPC standard precautions include Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), hand hygiene, prevention of accidental exposure to body fluids, safe and appropriate treatment of re-usable medical devices, waste management, cleaning and disinfection of surface and environment, respiratory hygiene and individual hygiene for staff, caretakers and patients IPC essential requirements include water supply, solid waste and waste water treatment/disposal, latrines and shower facilities, dead bodies management, vector control and medical waste management.

· Transmission-based Precautions (TBP): are the second level of basic infection control and are to be used in addition to standard precautions for patients who may be infected or colonized with certain infectious agents for which additional precautions are needed to prevent infection transmission (contact, droplet, airborne).

**What MSF Offers:**

- A fixed-term contract for deployment assignments and additional 21 days
- Travel, accommodation, and medical coverage during missions.
- Daily allowances in line with MSF policies.
- Access to training and professional development opportunities.

title: Laboratory Manager - DRC - French proficiency mandatory
body:
**LABORATORY MANAGER – EBOLA EMERGENCY POOL**

**PURPOSE**

Defining, implementing and monitoring all laboratory activities in the project area including management of relevant staff, according to **MSF** protocols in order to ensure the quality of the laboratory work

**WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR LABORATORY MANAGER IN THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO – EBOLA EMERGENCY RESPONSE**

- Available for deployment within the next 3 months for your first rotation of 12-16 weeks, followed by a mandatory 21-day post-deployment monitoring period.
- French proficiency (at least B2)
- Experienced in Ebola response, VHF, outbreak, or emergency response (strong asset)
- Flexible and adaptable in fast-changing environments
- Resilient under high-pressure humanitarian conditions
- Committed to teamwork and MSF principles
- Ready for remote and resource-limited field settings
- Essential laboratory technician diploma, desirable specialization or training in tropical diseases or other laboratory domains
- At least 2-year experience as a lab tech. Also, desirable experience in developing countries

**Accountabilities**

- Participating in the definition and update of the laboratory activities, including its budget, and assisting in the medical diagnosis and the treatment of diseases of the patients. Supervising laboratory activities in health facilities.
- Performing quality control tests and analysis, ensuring the compliance to the basic plans of the laboratory and that all tests (serology, hematology, biochemistry, bacteriology, parasitology, compatibility, etc.) are done correctly and according to prescriptions
- Ensuring that the hygiene and safety protocols both for individual as well as for collective protection (i.e. required clothes and equipment, hygiene and universal precautions, etc.) are implemented in laboratories and that the cleaning personnel is informed about biohazards.
- Ensuring proper registration and records of all lab related activities, implementing a correct use of the associated management (EpyTryp. etc.), in order to have proper records of laboratory activities. Preparing and sending slides/samples for external quality control
- Ensuring confidentiality of all patients’ laboratory results at any time, according to protocols in place
- In coordination with the project biomedical service supervising the appropriate use of medical devices under his/her responsibility so they can be used at any time (e.g. correct automatic instrument calibrations and correct and updated inventories of laboratory material and equipment) anticipating and communicating future needs.
- Planning and supervising, in close coordination with the HR department, the associated processes (recruitment, training, performance evaluation, development and internal/external communication) of the laboratory staff of the project in order to improve staff capabilities and to ensure both the sizing and the amount of knowledge required
- Compiling, analyzing and reporting on lab activities and results to the medical staff and the immediate supervisor providing data on complications, the total number and types of tests and in general, any problem with the staff and / or laboratory material. Also participating in the development of epidemiological reports relating to MSF health services.

**What MSF Offers:**

- A fixed-term contract for deployment assignments and additional 21 days
- Travel, accommodation, and medical coverage during missions.
- Daily allowances in line with MSF policies.
- Access to training and professional development opportunities.

title: Project Pharmacy Manager - DRC - French proficiency mandatory
body:
