**Accountabilities**

- Participating actively in the definition and update of the annual planning and budgets of the pharmacy activities in the project.
- Supervising the functioning and organization of the project central pharmacy and other peripheral units, setting the protocols and procedures to be followed by all staff in order to ensure the quality of the service provided to the population, including pharmaco vigilance in case of need.
- Defining storage, stock management and supply processes, as well as hygiene and security procedures, tools, and protocols (controlling pests and rodents) in order to ensure good storage conditions (temperatures, humidity and light exposure) and the accurate handling of the products and equipment in terms of hygiene and that all hygiene and security procedures are followed in project pharmacies (cleaning, controlling pests and rodents, etc.)
- Giving support in the ordering and supply process of medicines and medical devices. Monitoring correct stock management across pharmacies within project area, to guarantee a good control and up to date data of stock levels and avoid expiries, overstocks and stock outs. Reporting on drug consumptions and medical devices dispensed according to protocols, informing on unusual patterns.

- Ensuring the collection of data for monitoring and surveillance of optimal quantity & quality of medicine use. Supporting activities at service level for effective drug distribution and control, quality prescription (analyzing rational drug use), medicines reconciliation, antibiotic stewardship interventions such as restricted use antibiotic review, follow up of pharmaceutical care plans, patient counseling, good dispensing practices and safe medication practices.

Ensuring that all pharmacy staff uses required clothes and equipment according to protocols, i.e. white coat, gloves, etc.

title: Projects Coordinator
body:
**About World Vision**

For more than 75 years, World Vision has been committed to making a positive and lasting difference in the world. We have become a global leader in improving and transforming the lives of children, their families, and their communities. We help children, families, and communities overcome poverty and injustice, irrespective of religion, race, ethnicity, or gender. Every child deserves a life rich in meaning and purpose. We work with the most vulnerable children in the world so they can experience life in all its fullness.

**Location: Syria – Hassakeh and Raqqa**

**Job purpose:**

The Project Coordinator (PC) – GFFO Project will provide overall leadership in managing, implementing, and overseeing the GFFO-funded project in Northeast Syria. The PC will ensure high-quality, timely, and donor-compliant delivery of activities across WASH, Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL), Protection, and Health, implemented both directly by World Vision International (WVI) and through local partners.

The PC will work closely across all departments, including Technical Advisors, Grant Acquisition and Management (GAM), Finance, People and Culture (PnC), Partnerships, Security, Program Support, to ensure the project is donor-compliant and implemented well and on time.

The PM will work closely across all departments, including Technical Advisors, Grant Acquisition and Management (GAM), Finance, People and Culture (PnC), Partnerships, Security, Program Support, to ensure the project is donor-compliant and implemented well and on time.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**1. Project Implementation and Quality Assurance**

- Collaborate with the NES Area Manager to develop and supervise project activities. Ensure alignment with project/program goals and objectives.
- Following up monthly on the Detailed Implementation Plan (DIP) aligned to the project, and quality assurance checks across activities, ensuring adherence to technical standards, MEAL frameworks, and accountability principles.
- Plan and oversees of WASH, FSL, health, and protection activities and interventions in the targeted locations according to project timelines and objectives.
- Coordinate with partners and stakeholders to ensure smooth implementation of activities.
- Monitor project progress and make adjustments as necessary to achieve.
- Build and sustain working relationships with authorities and health directorate counterparts, with regular follow-up and engagement, recognizing that government partnership is essential for effective implementation and sustainability
- Communicate logistical, administrative, or safety needs clearly and follow up to ensure timely resolution.
- Ensure all project activities adhere to internal policies, donor regulations, and humanitarian standards

**2. Financial and Operational Management**

- Ensure sound financial management and expenditure tracking for assigned projects, in collaboration with the Finance and Operations teams.
- Monitor burn rates and ensure proactive measures are taken to achieve financial performance within donor-approved limits.
- Monitor burn rates and ensure proactive measures are taken to achieve financial performance within donor-approved limits.
- Support operational efficiency by coordinating with Supply Chain, PnC, and MEAL units to resolve bottlenecks and maintain smooth implementation flow.

**3. Reporting and Learning**

- Ensure timely and accurate submission of narrative and financial reports in line with donor requirements as per the MoU and WVI standards.
- Maintain comprehensive project documentation, including activity reports, PMIS updates, meeting minutes, incident reports, and other relevant records.
- Support the development and periodic update of project work plans/PIP, procurement plans, budget plans, and logical frameworks.
- Support data collection and documentation of lessons learned and challenges in collaboration with the MEAL team.
- Work with the Communications team to document success stories and best practices to inform future programming and contribute to organizational learning.
- Contribute to internal and donor reports as required, ensuring accuracy and consistency in coordination with NES AM, MEAL, Finance, Communications, GAM and other.

**4. Teams & Partners Management**

- Collaborate closely with the staff, implementing partners, and service providers to ensure that project activities are kept on track.
- Lead, monitor & maintain relationships with partners; Regularly engage with field staff/partners to ensure quality design, implementation, and flow on project goals;
- Lead information-sharing systems (regular meetings, visits, shared web‐engines, etc.);
- Supervise, mentor, and build the capacity of project officers and field teams, promoting teamwork, accountability, and professional growth.
- Lead coordination with cross-functional teams to ensure integrated and coherent project delivery.
- Support the Area Manager in identifying staffing needs and contributing to performance management processes.
- Provide input into partnership assessments, capacity building plans, and performance reviews.

**5.Coordination & Stakeholder Engagement**

**Externally**:

- Coordinate operations under the project externally with other local stakeholders and NGOs operating in the area of project implementation;
- Liaise with local partners, authorities, and relevant stakeholders to ensure coordinated implementation and strong community engagement.
- Represent the organization in sectoral or coordination meetings as delegated by the Area Manager.

**Internally**:

- Coordinate operations internally for the projects with all relevant departments;
- Engage with Technical Advisors to ensure project alignment with technical standards and best practices.
- Regularly engage with GAM at the design and acquisition stage to ensure GAM has all the needed inputs and information from the donors.
- Lead the donor’s operational communication after the signing of the agreement while keeping the GAM involved.
- Other tasks assigned by line manager or higher management.

**Knowledge/Qualifications for the Role**

 **Required Professional Experience**

- Experience in the Syria-NES context is required.
- Experience in management of multi-sectoral projects including at least two of the following sectors WASH, FSL/Cash, Health, Nutrition, or Protection
- Cultural sensitivity and adaptability;
- Strong communication skills with the ability to express ideas and concepts clearly and persuasively with senior members of the humanitarian community as well as with field practitioners;
- Ability to work with a reasonable level of comfort in high tension and high security risk situations;
- Ability to maintain performance expectations in diverse cultural contexts, psychologically stressful environment and physical hardships;
    
    **Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification:**
- Bachelor’s degree in International Development, Business Administration, Engineering, Social Sciences, or a related field.
- Proven training in humanitarian standards (Sphere, Core Humanitarian Standards, or similar).
- Strong knowledge of project cycle management and budget monitoring tools.
- Strong English and Arabic communication skills (oral and written);
- A minimum of 4-6 years operational management humanitarian experience with preference given to project management experience in an emergency context.

 **Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications**

- Excellent analytical skills and ability to think strategically, innovatively, and practically
- Excellent budget management and development skills
- Experience in mainstreaming cross‐cutting issues into organizations, change management, and/or organizational development
- Understanding of the Humanitarian Coordination architecture.

 **Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement**

- The position will be based in Syria NES-Hassakeh and travel to Raqqa
- The PC MUST travel to the project location in Hassakeh and Raqqa (within the same governorates at least once every 2 weeks), or as requested by the line manager.
    
    **Physical Requirements**:
- Ability to work under pressure with tight timelines.
- Ability to travel between projects locations
    
    **Language Requirements**
- Essential: Strong English communication skills (oral and written)
- Essential: Strong working knowledge of Arabic (oral and written)

body:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. Prise en charge à hauteur de 50 % des frais de transport en commun.

Une présence régulière au siège de Montreuil est ainsi prévue, selon une fréquence définie avec ton manager. À cela s'ajoutent environ trois jours par mois dédiés aux réunions et événements collectifs.

title: Humanitarian AI Research Fellowship
body:
**About the Fellowship**

NetHope is piloting a new, short-term Humanitarian AI Research Fellowship to grow the pool of researchers and practitioners who understand how AI can responsibly advance humanitarian and development work, and to produce research findings that NetHope's Member organizations and the wider nonprofit community can put to immediate, practical use.

This is a part-time, remote, internationally open opportunity for individuals who bring rigor, curiosity, and a genuine interest in responsible AI for humanitarian impact.

**About NetHope**

NetHope brings together leading humanitarian, development, and conservation organizations to create a more connected and equitable world through the power of technology. At the intersection of the nonprofit, private, and technology sectors, NetHope unites more than 60 Member organizations working in over 190 countries. In collaboration with over 70 of the world’s top technology companies, we design innovative, scalable solutions to global challenges, helping our Members and the wider nonprofit sector better serve people and communities in need.

**Two Research Streams**

The fellowship will run two parallel streams. Fellows will work independently within a stream, with guidance and support from the AI Fellowship Lead and periodic check-ins with NetHope subject-matter experts.

**Stream 1: AI Adoption & Governance**

Focused on at least two case studies of how humanitarian and nonprofit organizations are adopting, governing, and managing risk around AI tools in their operations and programs. Illustrative project areas include:

- Documenting real-world lessons and practices, helpful or cautionary from organizations integrating AI tools into their operations
- Building on NetHope's AI readiness work to better capture what adoption looks like in practice at the level of individual implementing partners
- Comparing organizational strategies for AI adoption (direct vendor partnerships, open-source and in-house builds, or off-the-shelf tools) and factors that may drive the choice
- Identifying priority AI safety and governance risks across humanitarian organizations, and practices for risk identification, mitigation, and incident response

**Stream 2: AI Systems & Localization**

Focused on the technical side of AI for humanitarian use, particularly where localized, offline, or low-connectivity deployment matters. Illustrative project areas include:

- Evaluating open-source and open-weight models, including localized or fine-tuned versions, for humanitarian use cases
- Assessing the relative risks and advantages of local/open systems versus closed, proprietary systems for humanitarian contexts
- Surfacing practical use cases and readiness gaps for AI deployment in resource-constrained or low-connectivity settings; developing a small library of simple, user-friendly tools to solve specific problems
- Contributing to a library of supervised fine-tuning prompts and datasets for humanitarian contexts

**Research Standards**

- Case studies involving NetHope Members or partners require their consent, and NetHope will review all findings before publication.
- Fellows will follow NetHope's AI Policy, including completing an AI Disclosure Form before starting, and NetHope's Data Protection Policy.
- Research involving personal data or affected communities must meet NetHope's data protection and research ethics requirements.

**Who Should Apply**

We welcome applicants from mid-career to seasoned practitioners who bring strong writing and analytical skills and a genuine interest in responsible AI's role in humanitarian impact.

- Stream 1 (Adoption & Governance): background in policy, program evaluation, or humanitarian/international development systems; experience with technology adoption or organizational change is a plus
- Stream 2 (AI Systems & Localization): background in computer science, machine learning, or applied data science, with knowledge of or interest in the humanitarian sector. Experience in model evaluation and/or red teaming a plus.
- Across both streams: strong written communication, self-direction, and the ability to sustain an independent research project on a fixed timeline

**Fellowship Details**

- Format: Remote, internationally open, part-time (approximately 10 hours/week)
- Duration: Mid-November 2026 through February 2027
- Cohort size: 4-6 fellows
- NetHope owns all research outputs and related intellectual property, including any datasets, prompts, tools, and code. Fellows are credited as named authors. Release and licensing terms will be set out in the fellowship agreement.
- Fellows receive a stipend in recognition of their time and contributions. Details will be shared with selected fellows and set out in the fellowship agreement.
- All fellows must pass an OFAC screening before starting.

title: MEL Lead (FCDO GOAL)
body:
**About the GOAL Opportunity**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is preparing to bid for FCDO's Girls and Out-of-School Children: Action for Learning Programme (GOAL) Long-Term Technical Assistance (LTTA) contract in Pakistan, following release of FCDO's Terms of Reference (ITT 7863). GOAL builds on more than a decade of UK-funded education reform in Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), delivered through the Punjab Education Support Programme (PESP, 2013–2022) and the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Education Sector Programme (KESP, 2012–2022), and on two live GOAL components: the Bridging Technical Assistance grant (B-TAG, ending March 2027) and the ILMpact remedial learning grant (ending September 2026), both of which the incoming Supplier will need to review and build on during inception.

The LTTA contract will run for up to 38 months (December 2026 – January 2030), comprising a 4-month inception period, a 32-month implementation period, and a 2-month closure phase, with a budget of up to £13 million and an extension option of up to £6.5 million and 18 months at FCDO's discretion. It will deliver systems-strengthening, politically informed technical assistance to provincial education departments in Punjab and KP, with Sindh included as a limited, capped scope (up to £1 million) focused on scoping, needs analysis and possibly Teacher Licensing support; the remaining budget is split equally between Punjab and KP.

The programme's three outcomes are:

- **Foundational Learning (30%):** strengthened provincial delivery of early and inclusive Foundational Learning.
- **Teacher Professionalisation (40%):** improved teacher professionalisation, including standards, licensing, and performance and support systems.
- **Education Financing Governance (30%):** improved governance and accountability of education financing, including public financial management and innovative financing.

The Terms of Reference place strong emphasis on systems thinking and a Thinking and Working Politically (TWP) approach, including a 'coalitions for change' lens that looks beyond government departments to civil society, philanthropy and the private sector, and on strengthening how provincial governments manage the rapid growth of outsourced and Public-Private Partnership (PPP) schools across Punjab and KP. Equity, inclusion and safeguarding are cross-cutting requirements throughout.

FCDO requires a lean Core Team of a Project Director (the only role not required to be full-time; at least 20% of days in Pakistan), a Team Leader, a Technical Assistance Lead, two Outcome Leads (one covering teaching and learning, one covering PFM and innovative financing), and two Provincial Leads (Punjab and KP) from contract commencement, with a third for Sindh only if FCDO later approves a Sindh implementation phase. The named Table 1 Core Team positions must be full-time and exclusive to the contract; any additional Core Team positions a bidder proposes do not have to be full-time, but are still subject to the same exclusivity requirement while engaged. IRC is proposing to strengthen this structure with a dedicated MEL Lead. FCDO's Terms of Reference confirm that GOAL's programme-wide MEL component is not being separately procured, and para 13.5 explicitly invites bidders to propose additional Core Team expertise beyond FCDO's named positions — this role is IRC's response to that invitation, not a named Table 1 position.

**Background of the role:**

The MEL Lead is a core team position responsible for the production, budgeting and implementation of the programme's Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) strategy. The MEL strategy must set out the approach to data collection, management and analysis; evidence use and generation; use of innovation and technology; Value for Money (VFM); and dissemination — and must align with the Theory of Change, logframe and VFM monitoring for the overall GOAL programme.

The MEL Lead will report to the Team Lead, working closely with the Technical Assistance Lead to ensure MEL evidence informs technical decision-making, and with the GESI Specialist to ensure GESI-disaggregated data collection and analysis.

**Roles and Responsibilities**

- Lead production of the programme's MEL strategy covering data collection/management/analysis, evidence use and generation, use of innovation and technology, VFM, and dissemination, aligned with the Theory of Change, logframe and VFM monitoring for the wider GOAL programme.
- Propose and apply MEL methodologies and methods capable of capturing progress in systems thinking and Thinking and Working Politically (TWP) — for example Developmental Evaluation or Systems Thinking MEL, using methods such as outcome mapping or process tracing — rather than relying on conventional summative M&E alone.
- Lead development and updating of the programme's logframe and maintain the change log recording all logframe amendments throughout the life of the contract.
- Establish required quantitative and qualitative baseline data before the end of the inception period, in collaboration with SED Punjab, ESED KP and other GOAL component partners, drawing on existing B-TAG, ILMpact, DARE-RC and RSPN knowledge products rather than starting from scratch.
- Design monitoring activities that are real-time wherever possible, use community-driven modes of monitoring and appropriate technology, integrate into government systems rather than creating parallel ones, and remain accessible and easy to understand by all partners.
- Ensure the MEL system can track plausible contribution pathways to FCDO's wider education portfolio milestones — for example, the Foundational Learning milestone of a 5% increase in Grade 5 reading in Urdu and English in KP and Punjab by 2029 against the 2023 ASER baseline — using agreed indicators and available data sources including Annual School Census data, ASER and relevant provincial/national assessments.
- Propose an incremental, additive approach to evaluation that builds up a picture over the life of the contract, rather than relying on a single summative report at the end of the TA.
- Own the evidence base for KPI 5 (acting on lessons learnt), ensuring lessons from partners are systematically captured, analysed and reflected in quarterly reporting and adaptive management decisions; contribute quality-assured MEL and logframe products that support KPI 2 (quality of implementation deliverables).
- Lead preparation of the annual MEL Strategy document and annual Results KPIs reporting, and contribute the MEL sections of the Exit Plan (first drafted in the inception phase, updated annually, finalised January 2029) and of quarterly Progress Reports to FCDO and to SED Punjab/ESED KP/SELD Sindh.
- Ensure MEL data collection is disaggregated by gender, disability, poverty and geography, working closely with the GESI Specialist to identify and target the most marginalised children.
- Track and report on Value for Money, supporting the Team Lead's quarterly financial and progress reporting and the programme's fee-retention/KPI-linked payment model.
- Build the MEL capacity of provincial government counterparts as part of the programme's systems-strengthening approach, consistent with the ToR's expectation that TA strengthens government routines rather than substituting for them.

**Qualification, experience and Skills will include:**

**Essential:**

- Advanced degree in monitoring and evaluation, statistics, social science, education, or a related field.
- Substantial senior MEL leadership experience (indicatively 8-10+ years) on FCDO- or similarly funded, complex donor programmes, ideally involving adaptive, politically informed programming.
- Demonstrated expertise in adaptive/developmental MEL methodologies (e.g. Developmental Evaluation, Systems Thinking MEL) and methods (e.g. outcome mapping, process tracing), rather than conventional logframe-only M&E.
- Strong experience developing and managing logframes, Theories of Change, and Value for Money monitoring frameworks nested within a wider programme logframe.
- Experience with KPI-linked, fee-retention payment structures and donor reporting requirements, ideally FCDO's.
- Experience with education data systems and sources (e.g. EMIS, Annual School Census, ASER) in Pakistan or a similar context strongly preferred.
- Experience building MEL capacity within government counterparts.
- Excellent written and spoken English; Urdu and/or other relevant regional languages an advantage.

**Collaboration with Other Team Members**

- **Team Lead:** provide regular MEL evidence and VfM reporting to inform programme management and donor reporting.
- **Technical Assistance Lead:** ensure MEL findings inform technical decision-making and quality assurance across outcome areas.
- **Outcome Leads (Teaching & Learning; PFM & Innovative Financing) and Provincial Leads:** coordinate data collection, monitoring and process evaluation across outcome areas and provinces.
- **GESI Specialist:** ensure MEL data and analysis are disaggregated by gender, disability, poverty and geography to identify and target the most marginalised children.
- **SED Punjab / ESED KP:** support provincial government counterparts to strengthen their own MEL and data systems, in alignment with DARE.

*This JD reflects FCDO's Terms of Reference for the GOAL LTTA contract (ITT 7863) and associated bidder clarifications, and remains subject to change until contract award. This position is contingent on the outcome of the bid.*

title: Program Officer, Instructional Design & Multimedia
body:
*This position is contingent on receipt of grant funding.*

**Job Overview:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the leading providers of high-quality programming for refugees resettling to the United States. The IRC is committed to developing innovative programs that respond to the refugees’ unique strengths and needs, using our learning and experience to shape policy and practice, and highlighting and promoting best practices in refugee services provision.

The IRC is seeking a Program Officer for Instructional Design and Multimedia for Settle In, a program providing information and support for newcomers in multiple languages through its website (SettleInUS.org), mobile app, and social media platforms. More information on Settle In can be found on https://www.settleinus.org.

This position designs and produces the learning experiences newcomers encounter across Settle In’s platforms. The role combines two areas of practice: instructional design—structuring multilingual, self-paced learning journeys that help newcomers build knowledge over time—and multimedia production—creating videos, graphics, and other assets that support the full range of Settle In content.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Design multilingual, self-paced learning journeys for newcomer audiences, including learning objectives, sequencing, knowledge checks, and reinforcement. Apply instructional design, adult learning principles, plain language standards, and translation-ready structure so that content is usable by newcomers with varying levels of literacy, digital literacy, and prior exposure to U.S. systems.
- In partnership with Switchboard’s Senior Program Officer, Instructional Design, establish instructional design standards for Settle In content and review materials developed by team members, subject matter experts, and contractors against those standards.
- Incorporating Switchboard’s established instructional design standards, recommend and implement improvements to Settle In’s instructional design practice, and update previously developed Settle In learning resources on an established review cycle.
- Create compelling, in-language multimedia content, including short-form video, infographics, motion graphics, and social media assets.
- Manage post-production of all finalized work, including Adobe Premiere project organization, color correction and grading, sound design, motion graphics, music editing, sequencing, export and compression for multiple platforms, and archiving.
- Coordinate with the multilingual Digital Community team on content creation, voiceover, subtitling, and translation review, and advise colleagues on audio and video recording tools and practices.
- Ensure final products are easy to understand, culturally appropriate, linguistically and factually accurate, accessible across web and mobile, and aligned with Settle In standards, newcomer needs, and funder requirements.
- Ensure all learning experiences and multimedia content meet accessibility standards (e.g., captions, alt text, screen-reader compatibility)
- Maintain visual and instructional consistency across Settle In's platforms (website, mobile app, social media)
- Coordinate and incorporate feedback across teams and projects and participate in user testing and other methods for optimization of content.
- Manage production timelines across concurrent projects and coordinate the work of external contractors, including videographers, designers, and translation vendors.
- Use platform data and user insights to set measurable goals for content and assess performance, and contribute to project reports, including monthly activity updates and performance monitoring reports.

*Other duties as assigned.*

**Job Requirements:**

- Bachelor’s degree in instructional design, education, communications, or other relevant field (or equivalent experience).
- Minimum four years of professional experience combining instructional design and multimedia production, including creating multilingual digital content for diverse populations.
- Demonstrated experience designing self-paced learning for adult audiences, including experience with e-learning tools.
- Excellent command of video editing (Adobe Premiere) and graphic design software (Adobe InDesign, Canva), and knowledge of social media platforms, especially Facebook.
- Working knowledge of plain language principles and digital accessibility standards.
- Experience contributing to project M&E (data collection, management, and reporting).
- Ability to manage complex projects on strict timelines, with excellent written and oral communication skills and strong attention to detail.
- Fluency in at least one of Settle In’s supported languages (Dari, Pashto, Spanish, and Haitian Creole) preferred.
- Previous experience working with refugee resettlement or other immigration pathways, and familiarity with ORR-funded programs.
- Ability to translate complex or technical information into clear, visual, and easy-to-understand learning content
- Experience engaging with external subject matter experts, consultants, or production vendors.

**Working Environment:**  This position is a remote working environment. Required domestic travel up to 20%.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $80,000 - $85,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. title: Case Coordination Caseworker
body:
**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other ORR qualified immigrants to support a positive integration experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with each client. Provide individualized support through direct services, referrals, and advocacy.
- Receive referrals for case management for ORR-eligible and TANF-eligible clients and participate in any needed case conference meetings to assure continuity of care.
- Assess client needs, creates Family Self-Sufficiency Plans (FSSPs) and Individual Employability Plans (IEPs), focusing on removing employment barriers, stabilizing, and obtaining and retaining employment.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized. Follow up with any referrals made to other programs.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Conduct outreach to case management staff, refugee-serving agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others to inform service providers and refugees of programs and services.
- Complete eligibility screenings for all referral and enrollment paperwork for all eligible Program participants.
- Provide comprehensive case management services, including assisting with benefits applications as appropriate.
- Guide/assist participants to establish contact and receive support services in the community based on their service plan.
- Ensure all services are linguistically appropriate and help advocate with mainstream service providers for linguistically appropriate services.
- Complete case notes in a detailed and timely fashion.
- Ensure all family data is entered into data management system in a timely manner.
- Assist with the preparation of donor funding reports and new funding proposals.
- Participate in all program meetings, staff development activities, and fully engages as a member of the team.
- Follow all IRC policies, procedures and protocols including adherence to the IRC Way and Child Safeguarding.
- Other related duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:**  Case Coordination Supervisor

**Indirect Reporting:** Interns/Volunteers

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Undergraduate degree Social Work or similar field strongly preferred; comparable related work experience may be substituted.

***Work Experience:***

- 2+ years of case management experience in a social services environment.
- Experience working with vulnerable or under served populations preferred

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Computer proficiency with an emphasis on Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook).
- Strong organizational skills and detail-oriented
- Public Speaking and/or presentation experience preferred
- Ability to effectively communicate and work as a team member with collaborative partners, the community, and clients in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment.
- Ability and willingness to drive 15 passenger van.
- Strong attention to detail with the ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Problem solver capable of working well independently and as a part of a team.

***Language Skills:***

- Proficiency in written and spoken English, bilingual ability preferred in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French or other refugee/immigrant language used in Arizona. Cross-cultural understanding and strong communication skills, both written and verbal.

***Certificates or Licenses:***

title: Safeguarding Specialist
body:
## **MSF Eastern Africa is looking for a Safeguarding Specialist**

*Do your skills and experience not precisely match the requirements? At MSF EA, we strive to create a safe, diverse and inclusive workplace, recognizing the need to increase access to professional opportunities for historically underrepresented groups. If you're interested in this position but your experience doesn't align perfectly with the selection criteria, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might be the ideal candidate for this or other positions.*

*Firmly committed to safeguarding patients, community members, staff, and all those in contact with the organization from all forms of abuse, including sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEAH), we will take all necessary steps, through rigorous vetting processes, to ensure that confirmed perpetrators of abuse do not join the organization.*

*For this position, contact level with patients and children is categorized as **High** risk and will be monitored with this in regard.*

## ***Introduction***

Médecins Sans Frontières/Doctors Without Borders (MSF) is an international independent medical humanitarian organisation that provides assistance to people affected by conflicts, epidemics, and natural or human-made disasters and excluded from healthcare. We provide this assistance without discrimination, irrespective of race, religion, creed or political affiliation.

## ***About MSF Eastern Africa***

MSF Eastern Africa is the regional institutional office of MSF. It focuses on representation and networking, recruiting and supporting staff from the region, communications and fundraising, as well as working on other dossiers of importance to MSF such as Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI), Data Protection, mutualization, training, medical operational support and environmental health.

## ***Rationale/Objective for Position***

The Safeguarding Specialist is responsible for supporting and implementing safeguarding policies and procedures at programming location in collaboration with different MSF Operational Entities.

This position will be **hierarchically** and **functionally** accountable to the **Head of EDI & Safeguarding**.

## ***Tasks & Responsibilities***

- Lead or support on administrative workplace investigations at HQ and/or programming context.
- Follow up and address safeguarding concerns and challenges as they may occur.
- Build capacity for staff and affiliated members on safeguarding, including risk assessments, through trainings, workshops and alternative measures.
- Identify and develop necessary materials in collaboration with the behaviour /safeguarding Unit team to support the capacity building processes.
- Carry out safeguarding audits and provide support on self-assessments for programming context.
- Carry out field visit and/or audit reports after travel to programming context to contribute to the review of existing safeguarding policies and procedures.
- Follow up on safeguarding concerns and conduct lessons learnt exercise as preventative measure.
- Carry out surveys in relation to every workshop/training conducted.
- Support on mainstreaming of safeguarding capacity at MSF EA HQ and/or programming context though newly developed tools and practices.
- Contribute to the development of the Unit’s Annual Plan and support on internal monitoring of objectives set for the role.
- Support on regional networking strategies to ensure accountability through partnerships and best practices.

**Other Responsibilities**

- Recognize, respond, and document any form of abuse or inappropriate behavior and alert the safeguarding unit of any suspected potential abuse.
- Engage in on-going self-reflection and proactive approach to advance on EDI & Safeguarding related knowledge and skills.
- Integrate EDI & Safeguarding strategies and practices in area of work responsibility, while utilizing relevant available data to gain insights for informed decision making at all levels.
- Compliance assurance - Ensure that all data processing activities within the unit comply with relevant data protection laws and regulations in your area of operation, including the Data Protection Act, 2019 and support your team to receive necessary training in this area.
- Policy adherence - Enforce data protection policies, procedures, and guidelines within the unit, ensuring that all team members are aware of and adhere to these protocols.
- Proactively participate in the individual performance management process including objective setting, performance monitoring and performance evaluation.

## ***Qualifications***

**Education**

- A bachelor’s degree in behavioral science, social or organizational science, human rights, international development, law, education, or similar field from a recognized institution.
- Specific education/certification related to Safeguarding is a strong and added advantage.
- Knowledge of Safeguarding principles and capacity to use it in trainings and audits.
- Ability to develop case strategies, conduct investigative interviews and deliver investigation reports of high quality and within short deadlines
- Fluency in English and French is required, and knowledge of Kiswahili and/or other language is an added advantage.
- Cultural knowledge and competence of the African context is highly desirable.

**Experience**

- At least 5 years of experience in Safeguarding, Protection or GBV.
- Proven track record in leading and conducting workplace administrative investigations in the Humanitarian sector.
- Experience in supporting Safeguarding training/workshops.
- Experience conducting Safeguarding audits and/or self-assessments is desirable.
- Work experience from East or Central Africa is highly desirable.
- Experience advising on risks and risk mitigation regarding investigations into allegations of abuse.

**Competencies**

- ***Technical Competencies***
    - Ability to conduct workplace administrative investigations, following due process and in a timely manner.
    - Strong analytical and advisory skills and the ability to translate complex analysis into concise, clear, and actionable conclusions and recommendations
    - Ability to conduct Safeguarding audits with support and guidance from the Unit team.
    - Ability to facilitate trainings/workshops on Safeguarding related topics with support and guidance from the Unit team.
- ***Behavioral /General Competencies***
    - Respectful and appropriate behavior in support of MSF Behavioral Commitments.
    - Commitment to MSF’s Values and Principles, to our vision and mission of promoting the rights and well-being of patients and community members at risk.
    - Ability to work in a multicultural environment successfully and to demonstrate commitment and support for diversity, gender-responsive, inclusive, and non-discriminatory behavior and attitudes.
    - Ability to inspire and build collaborative working relationships.
    - Ability to handle highly sensitive situations and confidential information diplomatically and discreetly.
    - Ability to work independently and take initiatives.
    - Ability to manage conflict constructively and effectively.
    - Excellent listening and organizational skills.
    - Excellent written and verbal communications skills.
    - Results and Quality Oriented.
    - Ethics: High ethical standards and a commitment to protecting the data of individuals and furthering MSF mandate.

## ***Conditions and Benefits:*** 

- **Job Location**: MSF Eastern Africa office in Nairobi (Kenya).
- **Contract**: 2 years (renewable), full-time contract.
- **Start date**: January 2027.
- **Salary:** An annual salary of **EUR 27,145 at HQ Grade 8** based on a full-time appointment with an annual increment of 2% every year up to a maximum of 10 years.
- **Work-life balance financial benefit;** ranging between **EUR 620 to 1,159/month** based on individual & administrative status. This amount may be used to cover accommodation and utilities, transportation, etc.
- **Other benefits include;**
    - **Annual Leave:** 25 days of annual leave per year.
    - **Other Holidays:** sick leave, circumstantial leave, maternity leave (21 weeks), paternity leave (4 weeks), own affairs days off, etc.

title: Consultance sur l'analyse et l’amélioration de la gestion des déchets de soins de santé dans les délégations internationales de la CRF
body:
## **Contexte de la mission de consultance**

La Croix-Rouge Française (CRF) met en œuvre des projets internationaux principalement dans les domaines de la santé et de la gestion des risques de catastrophes (GRC). Au sein de la Direction des Opérations Internationales (DOI), le Département Santé et Gestion des Risques de Catastrophe intervient notamment dans le renforcement des systèmes de santé, la réponse aux épidémies, la santé communautaire et la formation paramédicale. La CRF intervient également en situation d’urgence, notamment à travers son Pôle Urgence International (PUI), qui contribue au déploiement de capacités de réponse adaptées aux crises et aux besoins humanitaires.

La gestion des déchets de soins de santé dans ces différents contextes constitue un enjeu transversal de qualité des soins, de prévention des risques, de sécurité, de respect de la dignité des personnes et de protection de l’environnement.

Une attention particulière devra être portée à la gestion des déchets pharmaceutiques, compte tenu des risques sanitaires, environnementaux, réglementaires et de détournement associés. Leur gestion sera analysée depuis leur identification et leur mise à l'écart jusqu'à leur traitement et leur élimination finale, en incluant les modalités de stockage temporaire, de traçabilité, de transport et de destruction.

La gestion des déchets de soins de santé participe directement à la perception de la qualité des soins et à la crédibilité de la CRF et du Mouvement.

La présente consultance vise à analyser les pratiques de gestion des déchets de soins de santé au sein des délégations internationales de la CRF concernées, au regard des cadres réglementaires nationaux applicables, des pratiques des Sociétés Nationales Hôtes, des standards internationaux, des évolutions techniques du domaine et des contraintes propres aux différents contextes d’intervention.

Une attention particulière sera portée à la gestion des déchets de soins de santé en contexte d’urgence aiguë, notamment dans le cadre du déploiement de dispositifs de réponse aux épidémies et aux crises sanitaires tels que les Centres de Traitement du Choléra (CTC) et les Centres de Traitement Ebola (CTE) et plus largement les cliniques d’urgence déployables par la CRF lors de ce type de réponse. La consultance devra notamment analyser les besoins, contraintes et modalités opérationnelles spécifiques à ces contextes, notamment en matière de gestion des déchets infectieux et de prévention et contrôle des infections (PCI). Ce travail devra en particulier contribuer au processus en cours de la CRF relatif à la certification EMT de l’OMS, en identifiant les principes, procédures, équipements et capacités nécessaires à une gestion sûre et opérationnelle des déchets dans le cadre du déploiement d’une équipe médicale d’urgence.

Sur la base de l’état des lieux, la consultance formulera des recommandations opérationnelles, réalistes et contextualisées pour renforcer la qualité, la sécurité et la cohérence des pratiques de gestion des déchets de soins de santé.

## **Objectif général de la mission de consultance**

Analyser les pratiques de gestion des déchets de soins de santé dans les délégations internationales de la CRF et proposer des recommandations opérationnelles, priorisées et adaptées aux contextes d’intervention, en intégrant les exigences réglementaires, les standards internationaux, les innovations techniques et les contraintes opérationnelles.

## **Objectifs spécifiques de la mission de consultance**

Les objectifs spécifiques de la mission sont les suivants :

- **Réaliser un état des lieux des pratiques** de gestion des déchets de soins de santé dans les délégations concernées et, lorsque pertinent, dans les structures de santé appuyées, incluant, lorsque les données disponibles le permettent, une caractérisation des principaux flux de déchets de soins de santé et pharmaceutiques observés, de leur nature, de leur importance relative et des contextes dans lesquels ils sont générés, y compris la gestion en situation d’urgence aiguë ;
- **Conduire une revue de littérature et des pratiques internationales** afin d’identifier les évolutions, innovations et bonnes pratiques pertinentes ;
- **Analyser les cadres légaux et réglementaires applicables** et les mettre en perspective avec les pratiques observées au sein de la CRF et des systèmes nationaux de santé ;
- **Identifier les écarts, contraintes opérationnelles et risques associés** aux circuits de tri, stockage, transport, traitement et élimination ;
- **Proposer des recommandations opérationnelles** et priorisées permettant d’améliorer les pratiques de la CRF et, lorsque pertinent, des structures de santé appuyées, en distinguant, les principes ou standards minimaux applicables et les options devant être adaptées aux différents contextes d’intervention ;
- **Identifier, lorsque la qualité des données le permet, les éléments susceptibles d’alimenter une production scientifique** (publication ou poster) à soumettre à une conférence internationale ou un support de capitalisation.

## Méthodologie de la mission de consultance

La méthodologie sera proposée par le/la consultant·e et validée avec la CRF au démarrage de la mission. Elle devra notamment combiner :

- **Une phase de cadrage**, permettant de préciser le périmètre, les délégations concernées, les sources de données disponibles et les modalités de collecte ;
- **Une revue documentaire et bibliographique**, incluant les références réglementaires, les standards internationaux, les pratiques des Sociétés Nationales Hôtes (SNH), ainsi que les évolutions, innovations et bonnes pratiques récentes en matière de gestion des déchets de soins de santé ;
- **La conception des outils de collecte et d’analyse**, notamment questionnaires, guides d’entretien et/ou grilles d’analyse ;
- **La collecte et la consolidation des données** auprès des délégations concernées, à travers l’analyse documentaire, des entretiens avec les équipes et, lorsque pertinent, des observations de terrain. La gestion des déchets en situation d’urgence devra également être prise en compte ;
- **L’analyse des pratiques et des circuits de gestion des déchets de soins de santé**, notamment le tri, le stockage, le transport, le traitement et l’élimination, au regard des cadres réglementaires nationaux, des standards internationaux et des pratiques de référence, en intégrant, pour les solutions de traitement et d’élimination et lorsque pertinent, leurs consommations énergétiques, émissions et rejets, résidus générés, besoins de maintenance et de consommables, ainsi que leur adéquation aux capacités techniques locales ;
- **Une analyse spécifique du circuit des déchets pharmaceutiques**, comprenant a minima les modalités d'identification, de mise à l'écart, de stockage temporaire, de sécurisation, de traçabilité, de transport et de destruction, ainsi que les responsabilités des différents acteurs impliqués ;
- **L’identification des écarts, risques et contraintes opérationnelles**, en tenant compte des capacités disponibles et des spécificités des différents contextes d’intervention, ainsi que, lorsque ces éléments ressortent des données collectées, des principaux facteurs contribuant à la génération des déchets observés, afin de pouvoir alimenter les réflexions ultérieures sur leur prévention et leur réduction à la source ;
- **Des échanges réguliers avec la CRF**, notamment avec le Référent EHA, la fonction Environnement, les équipes concernées par l’EMT et, selon les sujets analysés, les autres fonctions métiers concernées, afin de partager les constats et d’alimenter l’analyse ;
- **La formulation de recommandations opérationnelles et priorisées**, tenant compte de leur pertinence, de leur faisabilité et des contraintes propres aux différents contextes d’intervention ;
- **L’identification des possibilités de valorisation des résultats**, notamment sous la forme d’une production scientifique ou d’un support de capitalisation, lorsque la qualité et la quantité des données le permettent.

## **Livrables attendus**

**Rapport de cadrage**

• Compréhension du besoin et du périmètre ; méthodologie détaillée ; outils de collecte ; délégations/contextes ciblés ; chronogramme indicatif ; modalités d’échanges et de validation.

**Livrable intermédiaire – état des lieux et analyses**

• Données consolidées et analysées ; synthèse des pratiques observées ; analyse des circuits de gestion ; principaux écarts, risques et contraintes ; premiers constats sur la gestion en urgence.

**Note de synthèse sur la littérature, les standards et les pratiques internationales**

• Synthèse des références examinées ; évolutions et innovations ; bonnes pratiques ; éléments transférables ou adaptables à la CRF.

• La note de synthèse comprendra une section dédiée présentant les principes et modalités opérationnelles applicables aux dispositifs de réponse sanitaire d’urgence, ainsi que les recommandations spécifiques pour le déploiement d’une EMT, incluant les besoins en équipements, consommables, organisation des circuits, traitement et élimination des déchets.

**Proposition d'un outil pratique d'aide à la décision pour la gestion des déchets de soins de santé et pharmaceutiques** (grille, arbre décisionnel, fiche pratique ou format équivalent), permettant aux délégations et, lorsque pertinent, aux structures de santé appuyées, à partir de la nature du déchet, des risques associés et des solutions disponibles localement, d’identifier les modalités recommandées de tri, stockage, transport, traitement et élimination. L’outil sera conçu dans un format modulaire permettant son adaptation aux différents contextes et son enrichissement ultérieur, notamment sur les dimensions de prévention et de réduction à la source

**Rapport final de consultance**

• État des lieux consolidé ; analyse réglementaire et comparative ; résultats de terrain le cas échéant ; recommandations opérationnelles priorisées, accompagnées, lorsque pertinent, d’éléments sur leur temporalité, les acteurs et responsabilités concernés, les principaux prérequis et les éventuels besoins d’investissement ; annexes avec outils et éléments utiles à la capitalisation.

**Support(s) de valorisation, si pertinent**

• Proposition de note technique, poster, communication institutionnelle ou contribution scientifique, selon la qualité des données et validation de la CRF.

## Organisation de la consultance et chronogramme

### **Phases de la consultance**

Phase 0 – Cadrage de la mission : validation du périmètre, revue documentaire initiale, méthodologie, outils de collecte et chronogramme.

Phase 1 – État des lieux et collecte : collecte documentaire, questionnaires/entretiens, consolidation des données et analyse des pratiques.

Phase 2 – Analyse comparative et terrain : revue de littérature, analyse réglementaire et des standards, comparaison des pratiques ; mission(s) terrain si retenue(s).

Phase 3 – Recommandations et capitalisation : formulation et priorisation des recommandations, restitution intermédiaire/finale, finalisation des livrables et propositions de valorisation.

Des temps d’échanges avec le/la consultant·e seront prévus entre et pendant les différentes phases.

### **Chronogramme**

La mission se déroulera entre novembre 2026 et avril 2027, selon une durée et un calendrier détaillé à proposer par le/la consultant·e dans son offre, selon le périmètre validé et la proposition méthodologique du/de la consultant·e. Le calendrier détaillé sera arrêté avec la CRF au démarrage de la mission.

Phase 0 : Cadrage et méthodologie – durée à proposer

Phase 1 : Collecte et état des lieux – durée à proposer

Phase 2 : Analyse comparative et terrain – durée à proposer

Phase 3 : Recommandations, restitution et finalisation – durée à proposer

Ce chronogramme constitue une base de structuration de la mission et sera finalisé avec le/la consultant·e retenu·e.

title: Operations Manager ATLAS logistique - RDC
body:
**Lieu : Bunia RDC**  
**Date souhaitée de démarrage : début novembre 2026**  
**Durée de contrat : 5 mois**

Handicap International / Humanity & Inclusion (HI) est une association de solidarité internationale indépendante et impartiale, qui intervient dans les situations de pauvreté et d’exclusion, de conflits et de catastrophes. Œuvrant aux côtés des personnes handicapées et vulnérabilisées, elle agit et témoigne pour répondre à leurs besoins essentiels et améliorer leurs conditions de vie. Elle s’engage à promouvoir le respect de leur dignité et de leurs droits fondamentaux.

Chez Handicap International, nous croyons fermement en l'importance de l'inclusion et de la diversité au sein de notre structure. C'est pourquoi nous sommes engagés dans une politique handicap afin de favoriser l'accueil et l'intégration de personnes en situation de handicap.

Merci d’indiquer si vous avez besoin d’un aménagement particulier, y compris pour participer aux 1ers entretiens. Retrouvez plus d’informations sur l’association : [www.hi.org](http://www.hi.org).

**CONTEXTE :**   
Depuis la fin des années 1990, la RDC connaît une instabilité chronique, liée à des fragilités de gouvernance interne et à sa proximité avec des pays en crise. Cette situation limite l'accès à des services sociaux de qualité pour une population estimée entre 100 et 120 millions d'habitants. La faible gouvernance des ressources publiques affaiblit par ailleurs la gestion des risques de catastrophes : face aux crises, la réponse gouvernementale peine souvent à couvrir l'ensemble des besoins, un défi persistant pour la population.

La province de l'Ituri, à l'est du pays, illustre particulièrement cette complexité. Elle fait face à une situation humanitaire caractérisée par la persistance des conflits armés, d'importants déplacements de population et des besoins humanitaires élevés. À cette crise sécuritaire s'ajoute, depuis le 15 mai 2026, une 17ᵉ épidémie de maladie à virus Ebola déclarée dans la zone de santé de Mongbwalu. Cette flambée s'est rapidement propagée : au 21 septembre, 63 zones de santé (soit 37,7%) étaient touchées dans sept provinces, ce qui en fait, selon l'OMS et Africa CDC, la deuxième plus importante épidémie d'Ebola jamais documentée et la plus rapide en termes de croissance. La majorité des nouvelles infections provenant de chaînes de transmission non identifiées, les limites de la surveillance et du suivi des contacts demeurent un enjeu central de la réponse.

Cette situation exerce une forte pression sur les capacités logistiques, notamment à Bunia mais également dans certaines zones de santé, où les besoins en transport, en stockage sec et en stockage à température contrôlée dépassent largement les capacités locales disponibles. C'est dans ce contexte exigeant, à l'intersection des enjeux sécuritaires, humanitaires et épidémiologiques, que Handicap International souhaite relancer ses activités dans cette zone en renforçant et en facilitant le stockage et l’acheminement de l’aide humanitaire fournie par les acteurs humanitaires.

Ainsi, le projet Atlas Logistique lance des activités de stockage et de transport afin d’appuyer la réponse logistique de la riposte. Celles-ci comprendront :

• L’opérationnalisation d’une capacité de stockage médical (15°-25°C / 2° - 8°C) et le renforcement des opérations de transport au départ de ce site à destination des centres de santé Ebola (CTE),

• L’opérationnalisation de plusieurs capacités de stockage avancées en région et le renforcement des opérations de transport au départ de ces hubs afin de répondre aux besoins identifiés par l’ensemble des acteurs humanitaires.

Ce projet s’inscrit dans le cadre de l’ouverture actuelle d’une sous-base Handicap International à Bunia et tend à positionner Atlas Logistique comme un acteur logistique majeur de la riposte à la MVE.

**VOTRE MISSION :**  
Sous la responsabilité du Directeur Programme, le Manager des Opérations contribue au sein de la zone où il est basé à la mise en œuvre du mandat et de la stratégie d’Humanité & Inclusion. Il veille à l’optimisation de la qualité et de l’impact des projets mis en œuvre dans la zone, par le biais d’un système de délégation avec des mécanismes de contrôle appropriés. Il partage avec tous les autres responsables de HI la charge d’une gestion saine et d’un bon fonctionnement de l’organisation globale. Il est le manager, dans son pays, d’une équipe composée de chefs de projet.

Vos principales missions seront :

Mission 1 : Stratégie et pilotage

- Contribue au développement de la stratégie opérationnelle du programme, ainsi qu’à sa mise en œuvre et à son suivi annuel :
- Met en œuvre la partie projet de la stratégie opérationnelle du programme
- Contribue à la transformation organisationnelle, en particulier par le biais de changements des pratiques managériales, d’amélioration continue et contribue à l’amélioration des processus de travail

Mission 2 : Standards et expertises

Assure le déploiement et la conformité avec les cadres globaux, les politiques institutionnelles et les normes de HI. Cela inclut : les cadres de référence obligatoires (comme la mission et les valeurs de HI ou la théorie du changement de HI : l’accès aux services), la Politique Qualité des Projets de HI (y compris ses 6 engagements minimaux et son cadre de qualité), toutes les politiques institutionnelles de HI (Sécurité/Code de conduite et PSEAH / Prévention contre la fraude / Age-genre-handicap), l’ensemble des directives et processus institutionnels ; seuils de délégation ; niveaux de sécurité

Mission 3 : Mises en œuvre opérationnelle

- Veille à la bonne gestion et au suivi des projets sous sa responsabilité :
- En gardant à l’esprit les opportunités potentielles et les risques, contribue au suivi et à l’analyse des évolutions fait par son responsable hiérarchique, et proposer des mesures de mitigation le cas échéant :
- Assure l’animation fonctionnelle des équipes sur sa zone
- Préparation et réponse aux urgences

Vos responsabilités spécifiques Atlas :

- Collabore à la définition de la stratégie post-acheminement en coordination avec les clusters.
- Mener l’écriture du projet, en lien avec l’équipe terrain et siège.
- S’assure de la compatibilité de la stratégie terrain avec le mandat de la plateforme.
- Veiller et suivre pro activement les opportunités de financement : bailleurs, fondations, fonds propres, etc.
- Représente le projet au niveau local, national ainsi qu’au niveau des bailleurs de fonds.
- Participe activement aux réunions des clusters logistiques et autres.
- Présente et promeut les activités de la plateforme aux acteurs humanitaires, être le point focal pour les partenaires en capitale.
- Soutient les N-1 dans leurs activités de représentation externe.
- En lien avec les équipes HAS, s’assurer de la formation des équipes sur les procédures de sécurité liées aux mouvements des personnes
- Participe à la collecte d’informations et à l’analyse sur le contexte, les besoins humanitaires et la sécurité des zones de convois et d’activités.
- Participe à la planification et priorisation des activités, en collaboration avec les clusters.

**VOTRE PROFIL :**

· Vous avez au moins 3 ans d'expérience en gestion de projet, avec au moins une certaine expérience en coordination de projet

· Vous avez de l’expérience en management et savez travailler au sein d’une équipe multiculturelle,

· Vous êtes reconnu pour votre capacité à développer des partenariats et avez une bonne connaissance des mécanismes de coordination humanitaire,

. Vous avez de l’expérience sur la gestion de services de type logistique, compréhension du mandat Atlas

. Vous avez de bonnes aptitudes à la négociation, à la représentation externe et à la coordination

· Vous maitrisez le français et l’anglais

**CONDITIONS :**

Chez HI, les conditions de départ sont à la hauteur de votre engagement et adaptées au contexte de votre mission. Une attention particulière est portée aux questions de santé et à votre situation personnelle : [https://hi.org/fr/travailler-chez-hi](https://hi.org/fr/travailler-chez-hi)

- Contrat International de 5 mois à compter de début novembre 2026, poste basé à Bunia
- Le contrat international permet une couverture sociale adaptée aux besoins de chacun :
    - Assurance chômage prélevée uniquement pour les ressortissants de l’UE ;
    - Assurance retraite ;
    - Couverture santé, rapatriement, prévoyance prises en charge par HI et par l’employé ;
- **Salaire** : à partir de 2860 € brut/mois ;
- **Perdiem** : 677 € net/mois – versé en monnaie locale sur le terrain ;
- **Hardship :** 500 € net/mois
- **Congés payés** : 25 jours par an ;
- **R&R** : 5 Jours toutes les 8 semaines
- **Poste :** Non accompagné
- Logement : Collectif pris en charge par HI ;
- Si vous êtes résident(e) dans le pays : package local.

title: RFP- Donor Landscape Assessment in Kenya
body:
## Request for Proposal (RFP)

Issued on: September 25, 2026

Solicitation Number: **51495**

For: Donor Landscape Assessment

Quotes Deadline: October 9, 2026

1. **Background**

 For nearly 70 years, Pathfinder International has been a catalyst for systems transformation, inclusive growth, and resilient communities. With a global footprint spanning Africa, South Asia, and the Middle East, we invest in women and girls by expanding access to essential health products and services, unlocking leadership pathways, and strengthening economic participation. By partnering with civil society, governments, and the private sector, we scale women-led innovations that deliver sustainable systems of support, while generating measurable impact with the goal to ensure every woman has the agency to shape her future and lead a healthy, fulfilling life.

 Pathfinder International Kenya - a registered Non-Governmental Organization under Kenya PBO Act seeks to strengthen its sustainability and diversify its funding base in response to the evolving development financing landscape. While it has extensive experience working with all kinds of donors, , Pathfinder International Kenya aims to expand and diversify its funding portfolio by exploring opportunities within philanthropy, corporate social investment, and foundations in Kenya.

 To support this ambition, Pathfinder International Kenya is seeking an external consultant to conduct a market assessment of various donor segments and provide strategic recommendations on engagement, investment requirements, and expected returns.

 2. **Objectives of the Assignment**

- Assess the scope and size of the philanthropic, corporate social investment, and foundations targeting not-for-profit, Non-Governmental Organizations registered and implementing development projects in Kenya.
- Identify high-potential donors and funding mechanisms aligned with Pathfinder International strategic priorities and operational presence.
- Determine the investment (financial, human, operational) required to effectively engage all donor segments and the expected timeline for return on investment.
- Recommend realistic funding targets for the 2027–2033 for these donor segments.
- Assess the feasibility and competitive advantage of operating as a local organization versus an INGO.
- Identify potential opportunities for local NGOs versus INGOs.

**3. Scope of Work**

The consultant will:

**a. Review Pathfinder International Kenya’s historical and current funding trends,** with a specific focus on performance and lessons learned within philanthropy, corporate social investment, and foundations

**b. Conduct market research** to:

- Map the landscape of current donors in Kenya specifically relevant to Pathfinder International Kenya’s work.
- Identify key active bilateral, corporate donors, foundations, and social enterprises with strategic alignment to Pathfinder International and the type of organizations (local Vs International) they currently prefer to fund.
- Understand giving behaviors, motivations, and barriers for philanthropic giving in Kenya (specifically relevant to strategic interventions aligned with Pathfinder’s work in Kenya)

**c. Benchmark peer organizations** to understand:

- Who is accessing these funds?
- How much funding is being secured?
- What investments were required to achieve success.
- What is their legal status: Local versus International organizations.

**d. Analyze investment requirements**:

- Financial resources, staffing, systems, partnerships, and leadership support.
- Timeline and risk factors for return on investment.

**e. Recommend funding targets** for the 2027–2033 for these donor segments.

**4. Deliverables**

- **Inception Report**: Detailing methodology, work plan, and stakeholder engagement strategy.
- **Market Assessment Report**: Comprehensive analysis of donor segments, investment requirements, and strategic recommendations including type of registration recommended for Pathfinder.
- **Funding Target Recommendations**: Scenario-based projections for CS 2027–2033.
- **Presentation to Pathfinder International Management**: Summary of findings and recommendations.

**5. Duration and Timeline**

- **Estimated Duration**: 15 working days
- **Timeline**: October-November 2026
- **Budget**: Proposals should demonstrate a clear value-for-money approach. The total budget will be a key factor in the selection process.

**6. Consultant Profile**

- Proven experience in resource mobilization, donor landscape analysis, and strategic planning in Kenya and East Africa.
- Very strong understanding of Kenya’s donor landscape, including philanthropic, private sector and corporate giving environment.
- Experience working with NGOs or development organizations in Kenya.
- Excellent analytical, communication, presentation and stakeholder engagement skills.

**7. Management and Reporting**

The consultant will report to the Business Development Director or his appointee at Pathfinder International, who will be the primary point of contact. Key milestones and findings will be shared with the Country Management Team (CMT) and presented to the Board of Directors at the conclusion of the assignment for strategic approval.

**8. Payment Schedule**

All payments will be tied to the successful completion and approval of deliverables, ensuring accountability for outputs and quality.

**Key Milestones and Deliverables**

**Milestone / Deliverable(s) / Payment %**

Upon approval of Inception Report/ Inception Report (methodology, work plan, stakeholder engagement plan) / 30%

Upon approval of Draft Market Assessment / Draft Market Assessment Report (including donor analysis, investment requirements, operational & supply chain readiness) / 30%

Upon approval of Final Deliverables / Final Report, Annual Funding Target Recommendations for Pathfinder International Kenya, Dataset, and Presentation to Pathfinder International Management / 40%

- The consultant is responsible for managing all expenses within the agreed total budget.
- Payment tranches are fixed percentages of the total contract value and will not be adjusted based on actual spending differences.
- The consultant must arrange their own insurance coverage (including health and travel insurance) and ensure compliance with national tax laws (e.g., VAT or income tax obligations).

**Proposal Guidelines and Instructions**

Offerors will be required to submit two electronically sealed proposals, one a technical proposal and the other a cost proposal. All proposals must be signed and valid for a minimum of sixty (60) days.

Your proposal should provide basic information about your Company/Individual and relevant service offerings. It should have a section addressing each of the following areas:

Responses should include the following information:

**A, Technical Proposal**

1. **Technical Proposal** (offeror will be evaluated based on their responsiveness to the Scope of Work)
    - Overview of the proposed approach and methodology.
    - Description of tools and techniques for data collection and analysis
    - Outline of key activities and timeline.
    - Summary of relevant experience in similar assignments.
2. **Consultant/Firm Profile**
    - Summary of qualifications and expertise, including experience working with NGOs and the philanthropic/corporate sector in Kenya.
    - Key personnel and roles (include brief bios or CV highlights).
3. **References**
    - At least two references from previous clients for similar assignments.
    - Contact details and brief description of the work undertaken.

**B. Cost/Financial Proposal**

Provide detailed and complete information on the cost that will be incurred by Pathfinder International. Such costs must include all items and not limited to the following:

- Detailed budget breakdown including daily rates, number of days, and any anticipated reimbursable expenses.
- Budget must be inclusive of all taxes.

### Evaluation Criteria

In evaluating the proposals, Pathfinder International will seek the **best value for money**

rather than the lowest priced proposal. Pathfinder will use a two-stage selection procedure:

- the first stage will evaluate the Technical Proposal. The technical proposal opening will be attended only by Pathfinders, as no information other than who submitted an offer will be read out at this stage.
- the second stage will evaluate the Cost Proposal for proposals that pass the Technical Proposal evaluation. Only proposals with an average score of 70 and above will be considered eligible for stage 2

Specifically, the selection committee will evaluate each proposal upon the following criteria:

**Evaluation Criteria / Total Weight 100 points.**

**Bid Submission - Pass/Fail**

1. Bid submitted on time
2. Offeror is eligible to receive funding per background checks
3. Any potential conflict of interest is sufficiently mitigated

**Technical Proposal - 40 points**

- Overview of the proposed approach and methodology.
- Description of tools and techniques for data collection and analysis
- Outline of key activities and timeline.
- Summary of relevant experience in similar assignments.

**Consultant/Firm Profile - 30 points**

- Summary of qualifications and expertise, including experience working with NGOs and the philanthropic/corporate sector in Kenya.
- Key personnel and roles (include brief bios or CV highlights).

**References - 30 points**

- At least two references from previous clients for similar assignments.
- Contact details and brief description of the work undertaken.
- Provide any other information to demonstrate the Contractor’s capability in relation to the Scope of Work.

Pathfinder is not bound to accept the lowest or any proposal and reserves the right to accept any proposal in whole or in part and to reject any or all proposals.

Pathfinder shall not be legally bound by any award notice issued for this RFP until a contract is duly signed and executed with the winning offeror.

The evaluator will tally all the individual scores for each section and calculate the total score. If the total number points meet or exceeds the 70 point threshold, the suppliers cost proposal will be eligible for consideration.

The score for the cost proposal will be calculated in the following manner:

Cost proposal score = 100 x Lowest cost/ cost of the proposal under consideration. The lowest cost proposal will receive the full 100 points.

The total score will be calculated as follows:

Total Score= Technical proposal score of the proposal under consideration multiplied by 70 plus (+) Cost proposal score of the proposal under consideration multiplied by 30.

### Inquiries

If you have any questions/inquiries, please e-mail nairobiprocurement@pathfinder.org no later than close of business **October 1, 2026.** The solicitation number indicated above must be included in the subject line. Responses will be posted to all known offerors.

As part of this RFP process, Pathfinder reserves the right to conduct interviews with bidders.

### Proposal Deadline

All written responses to this RFP must be received by Pathfinder no later than **17:00hrs EAT** on **October 9, 2026**. The solicitation number indicated above must be included in the subject line/on the envelope.

Please email the quote and other information directly to: nairobiprocurement@pathfinder.org

Pathfinder International, Kenya.

Please label each proposal attachment. One should be labeled technical proposal and the other

Cost proposal. The solicitation number indicated above must be included in the reference line.

Late submissions will not be considered. Shortlisted candidates may be invited for an interview or presentation to further discuss their proposed approach. The successful applicant will be selected based on technical expertise, relevant experience, value for money, and demonstrated capacity to comply with Pathfinder Kenya’s ethical and safeguarding standards

### Modification

If at any time prior to award Pathfinder deems there to be a need for a significant modification to the terms and conditions of this RFP, Pathfinder will issue such a modification as a written RFP amendment to all competing offerors. No oral statement of any person shall in any manner be deemed to modify or otherwise affect any RFP term or condition, and no offeror shall rely on any such statement. Such amendments are the exclusive method for this purpose.

### Resulting Award

Single contract: As a result of this solicitation, Pathfinder anticipates engaging a single independent contractor/company. Pathfinder reserves the right to split the SOW and make multiple awards.

Any resulting contract will be subject to the terms and conditions contained in Annex A. Part A of this annex will only apply to USG-funded assignments.

### Payment Terms

Pathfinder anticipates entering into a cost-reimbursable fixed-cost contract with the selected contractor.

### Terms

Pathfinder reserves the right to cancel this solicitation at any point and is under no obligation to issue a subcontract as a result of this solicitation.

Pathfinder will not reimburse any expenses related to the preparation of any proposal related materials or delivery.

### Confidentiality

All information disclosed by either party regarding this RFP is confidential and shall be treated as such.

### Agreement

Any resulting contract will be subject to the terms and conditions contained in the annex. See Annex A

title: Head of Finance Department (NIGERIAN NATIONALS ONLY)
body:
SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI) is an international humanitarian NGO which, for more than 40 years, has been  
providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their vital needs  
for food, water and shelter. Particularly involved in the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the first cause  
of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and
