title: APS Program Analyst
body:
**Overview**

Join a team where innovation meets mission. Our AI, cloud, cyber, and modernization solutions save agencies thousands of hours, safeguard national security, and strengthen health and humanitarian missions worldwide. With 1,700+ team members, 1,500+ AI/data experts, and 100+ prime contracts, we deliver at scale and with purpose.

We’ve been recognized as a Top Workplace by The Washington Post for six consecutive years and named to the Inc. 5000 Fastest Growing Private Companies list in 13 of the past 14 years. Credence is a welcoming environment for those looking to grow and make a meaningful impact. We encourage employees to push boundaries and engage in solving critical, world-changing federal challenges.

**Position Summary**

The Humanitarian Assistance Support Contract (HASC) combines deep institutional expertise, technical leadership, and a strong commitment to U.S. missions. Through HASC, Team Credence provides operational and administrative support to the U.S. Department of State (DOS) to coordinate humanitarian assistance, disaster response, and foreign assistance efforts across multiple bureaus, maintaining a 24/7 response capability.

The Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy (GHSD) administers a substantial portion of its discretionary grant and cooperative agreement portfolio through an Annual Program Statement (APS). The APS is a bureau-wide solicitation framework governing the full federal assistance lifecycle: development and publication of Addenda; receipt and Technical Eligibility Review (TER) of Statements of Interest (SOIs); merit review and selection; Consultative Program Design (CPD); issuance of directed Notices of Funding Opportunity (NOFOs); review of full applications; and award.

The APS is implemented through multiple concurrent Addenda and country- or program-specific award processes. Its scale and pace require disciplined central tracking, document control, deadline management, applicant correspondence, and records management. Under the FAPD-approved GHSD APS Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), the FA Hub Program Analyst provides the administrative and analytical infrastructure that allows the APS Manager, Merit Review Panels (MRPs), technical offices, posts, and Grants Officers (GOs) to execute each stage consistently, transparently, and in accordance with the Federal Assistance Directive (FAD), 2 CFR 200, and Department policy.

Credence is seeking experienced APS Program Analyst to maintain the authoritative operational record for the APS, coordinate recurring review and award-development workflows, and provide timely, accurate information across simultaneous APS processes.

**Application Closing Date:** The closing date for applications is **Wednesday, October 7, 2026**.

**The objectives of APS Program Analyst are :**

- Maintain a complete, accurate, and current bureau-wide record of all APS Addenda, SOIs, full applications, review stages, decisions, and awards
- Coordinate schedules, documentation, and communications across multiple concurrent APS processes
- Support consistent execution of TER, merit review, CPD, directed NOFO, full application review, and award transition activities
- Ensure APS files and applicant correspondence are controlled, traceable, procurement-sensitive, and archived in accordance with Department requirements
- Provide reliable analysis, status reporting, and process tools that enable the APS Manager and other authorized officials to identify delays, risks, and required actions

**Responsibilities include, but are not limited to the duties listed below:**

The APS Program Analyst will operate under the direction of the FA Hub APS Manager and in coordination with MRP Chairs and members, GOs, Grants Officer Representatives (GORs), technical offices, posts, and other authorized stakeholders. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:

***APS Planning, Scheduling, and Addenda Support***

- Maintain the APS Planning Tracker and integrated calendar for annual APS actions, quarterly Addenda, review milestones, CPD periods, directed NOFOs, full application deadlines, and anticipated awards
- Track dependencies, decision points, clearances, and responsible parties; issue reminders and follow up on overdue or at-risk actions
- Maintain current templates, checklists, standard correspondence, naming conventions, and folder structures approved for APS use
- Support administrative coordination of Addenda development, clearance, publication, amendments, and Q&A cycles, including version control and compilation of comments.
- Prepare routine status summaries, action lists, and process dashboards for the APS Manager and FA Hub leadership

***Submission Intake and Technical Eligibility Review***

- Monitor designated submission channels and coordinate retrieval of submissions from Grants.gov, MyGrants, or other approved Department systems
- Assign and maintain unique tracking numbers; log submission date, organization, Addendum or NOFO reference, file status, reviewer assignment, and disposition in the APS Master Tracker
- Conduct completeness and administrative checks using approved TER tools and criteria, and compile TER results for APS Manager review and certification
- Prepare TER summary sheets documenting totals received, pass/fail results, and standardized reasons for technical ineligibility
- Draft acknowledgment receipts and applicant notifications using approved templates; route correspondence for APS Manager and GO review or clearance, as required
- Maintain a complete, auditable record of original submissions, eligibility determinations, supporting documentation, and final correspondence

***Merit Review and Selection Process Support***

- Establish and maintain procurement-sensitive workspaces for each MRP and confirm that required conflict-of-interest and non-disclosure documentation is complete before access is provided
- Prepare review rosters, scoring workbooks, orientation materials, submission packages, and standardized Selection Memorandum templates
- Track completion of individual reviews, consensus sessions, scoring documentation, written strengths and weaknesses, and Selection Memoranda
- Maintain the APS Selection Log and reconcile panel decisions, leadership approvals, GO actions, and applicant notifications against the Master Tracker
- Provide real-time administrative and analytical support during consensus meetings, including document management, decision tracking, and quality checks for completeness and internal consistency
- Support controlled transmission of procurement-sensitive records only to authorized individuals

***Consultative Program Design Support***

- Coordinate CPD schedules, participant lists, invitations, pre-reads, approved facilitation materials, deliverable trackers, and secure document repositories
- Track completion and version history of CPD outputs, including workplans, budgets, risk matrices, timelines, security plans, pitch decks, and other required program design products
- Maintain records of decisions, open issues, and action items and ensure that materials required for revised Selection Memoranda and directed NOFOs are complete and readily accessible
- Support workshop logistics and documentation while maintaining neutrality and consistent treatment across participating applicants

***Directed NOFO, Full Application, and Award Support***

- Track preparation, review, clearance, issuance, and amendment of directed NOFOs and ensure the administrative record links each NOFO to the applicable approved selection and CPD documentation
- Log full applications, support TER and MRP document preparation, and track Award Recommendation Memoranda through required reviews and GO action
- Prepare applicant correspondence and award-process notifications using approved language and routing protocols
- Compile and archive final award documentation and support orderly handoff of complete records to the designated GOR and other authorized post-award officials
- Update the APS Master Tracker with final award data, including recipient, award number, value, period of performance, program area, geography, and responsible office.
- Data Quality, Records Management, and Continuous Improvement
- Serve as the day-to-day custodian of the APS Master Tracker, Planning Tracker, Selection Log, and associated process records
- Conduct routine data-quality checks and reconcile trackers against SharePoint, MyGrants, Grants.gov, selection records, and award documentation
- Maintain standardized electronic files and ensure required records are uploaded, named, versioned, and archived within established timelines
- Produce portfolio metrics and analyses, including submission volumes, eligibility outcomes, review status, processing time, applicant characteristics, award distribution, and recurring bottlenecks
- Identify process gaps and recommend practical improvements to templates, trackers, workflows, and internal guidance for APS Manager approval
- Support training, onboarding, and calibration activities by maintaining current job aids and process materials

## **Requirements**

- Bachelor’s degree in public administration, international affairs, public health, business administration, data management, or a related field, or equivalent relevant professional experience
- At least five years of progressively responsible experience supporting U.S. government foreign assistance, grants, cooperative agreements, and/or contracts
- Demonstrated experience managing high-volume, deadline-driven workflows with multiple concurrent workstreams and interdependent stakeholders
- Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including formulas, linked workbooks, data validation, filters, pivot tables, and quality control of large tracking datasets
- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Word, Outlook, Teams, and SharePoint, including document formatting, mail merge, version control, permissions, and records organization
- Demonstrated ability to produce accurate trackers, correspondence, review materials, summaries, and decision-support products with close attention to detail
- Working knowledge of federal assistance processes and the solicitation-to-award lifecycle, including eligibility screening, merit review, selection documentation, and award records
- Ability to handle procurement-sensitive and other controlled information with discretion and to comply with conflict-of-interest, non-disclosure, and access-control requirements
- Strong written and oral communication skills and the judgment to distinguish routine process support from matters requiring elevation to the APS Manager or GO
- Ability to work independently, anticipate operational needs, prioritize competing deadlines, and maintain accuracy in a high-tempo environment
- French language fluency
- U.S. citizenship with the ability to obtain and maintain a Secret Clearance required.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Experience supporting Department of State or another U.S. government foreign assistance program.
- Familiarity with the Department of State Federal Assistance Directive, 2 CFR 200, Grants.gov, MyGrants, and federal records-management requirements
- Experience supporting technical eligibility reviews, merit review panels, co-creation or consultative program design, NOFO development, or award recommendation processes
- Experience developing dashboards, automating routine reporting, or improving data and document workflows
- Knowledge of global health security, health diplomacy, or other international health and development programs
- Spanish language fluency

**Reporting and Coordination**

- *Receives technical directions from*: FA Hub APS Manager
- *Coordinates routinely with*: FA Hub leadership and team members; MRP Chairs and members Grants Officers and Grants Officer Representatives; GHSD technical offices and Front Office U.S. embassies and posts, as appropriate; CPD facilitators, subject-matter experts, and other authorized support personnel

**Procurement Integrity and Guardrails**

- The APS Program Analyst provides administrative, analytical, and process support. The individual must preserve the integrity of the competition, apply approved procedures consistently, and promptly elevate questions involving eligibility, policy, selection, or award authority.

**The APS Program Analyst may:**

- Apply approved administrative checklists and compile information for government review.
- Prepare trackers, correspondence, review packages, summaries, and draft process documentation.
- Coordinate schedules, records, controlled access, and routine communications.
- Identify discrepancies, missing documentation, approaching deadlines, and process risks for resolution by authorized officials.

**The APS Program Analyst may not:**

- Establish final federal program priorities or make policy determinations
- Make final eligibility, applicant selection, funding, cost allowability, or award decisions
- Change published evaluation criteria or direct MRP scoring or recommendations
- Provide preferential information, proposal advice, or assurances of funding to an applicant
- Approve, obligate, execute, modify, or terminate a federal award or perform any other inherently governmental function
- All work must comply with applicable conflict-of-interest requirements, non-disclosure agreements, procurement-sensitive communication protocols, records-management requirements, and access controls

**Place of Performance**

- Washington, DC / hybrid / remote with regular availability during Department of State business hours and in-person participation as required for merit review, CPD, and other APS activities.

**Salary Range:** $102,000–$158,000 per year. Actual compensation will be determined based on the selected candidate's experience, education, certifications, skills, and overall qualifications.

title: Administrative Assistant (GS-5)
body:
The IMF Resident Representative office in Jordan is seeking to hire a highly qualified **Administrative Assistant** to join its team, preferably starting on **December 1, 2026 or earlier.**

The position is offered as a one-year local contractual appointment, with the possibility of renewal for successive terms of up to three years, subject to continued need and satisfactory performance.

Candidates must be **nationals or residents of Jordan** or be able to independently obtain a valid work permit before starting employment with the Fund to be considered. Proof of nationality, residency, and/or work authorization will be required prior to starting employment. The IMF will not sponsor or assist with obtaining work permits.

**Job Summary**  
Responsibilities are performed under the general guidance of the Head of Office and the supervision of the Office Manager. Administrative Assistant (AA) contributes to the smooth operation of the office support work and related systems by assuming responsibility for organizing and coordinating workflow. Under the general guidance of the Head of Office and the supervision of the Office Manager, and as a member of the management team, contributes to overseeing delegated activities in the unit. AAs may supervise other support staff in the team. The AA is expected to back up others during absences and periods of heavy workload and perform similar assigned work.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

Within limits of delegated authority, the Administrative Assistant (AA) undertakes the following duties and responsibilities:

- Provides full range of office support services to the manager, including organizing and maintaining the Head of Office/Economists’ calendars.
- Contributes to operation of office support work and related systems by taking responsibility for organizing and coordinating workflow.
- Mentors, trains, resolve conflicts, and supervises support staff as appropriate.
- Ensures timely delivery and quality of outputs.
- Participates in preparation of staffing plans and contributes to the performance management process.
- Supports the Head of Office with respect to staff recruitment, contract and salary issues.
- Monitors and reviews work program and budgets. Processes and follows up on all budget related issues, e.g., consultant contracts, travel arrangements, payment requests, etc.
- Prepares budgetary information required for quarterly reviews.
- Researches information using IMF’s systems, databases, and internet.
- Prepares and coordinates logistics for conferences, workshops, document review, meetings, etc. This includes logistical support for incoming missions, e.g., mission schedules, travel arrangements, drivers, etc.
- Interprets rules and regulations with respect to domestic/international travel. Takes responsibility for coordinating the same.
- Takes responsibility for maintaining institutional filing systems and databases.
- Performs basic troubleshooting of hardware problems (e.g., printer interface, modem, cable connections, etc.) and operating system level problems (e.g., directory creation, printer setup, server connections, virus checks, etc.). Facilitates exchange of office technology information.
- Maintains an effective network of contacts with government officials, donors, civil society, academia, business, media, HQ, and other country offices. Works with COM staff in the development/maintenance of COM Country web site.
- Provides informational and logistical support with respect to the Head of Office’s contacts with officials at senior levels, both internally and externally in the country of operation.
- Routinely reviews/gathers information from newspapers, press releases, newsletters, clipping services, and media sources pertaining to the IMF and its work or policies. Highlights/conveys appropriate information to the Head of Office/Economists.
- Acts as a conduit between management and other staff.
- Performs other ad hoc duties as required.

Note: This list of duties is illustrative of regular and recurring functions, however the AA is expected to back up others and perform similar assigned work.

**Qualifications**

- Completion of a bachelor’s level degree; training in business administration or experience in a variety of fields, e.g., basic finance and accounting, human resources, audit, administrative, or other related fields is desirable.
- Five or more years of relevant experience.

Skills:

- Demonstrate administrative abilities in planning, organizing, problem-solving, personnel management, decision-making, personal organization, and time management skills.
- Ability to follow through on team priorities and respond to requests for information.
- Ability to produce high-quality work under pressure.
- Thorough knowledge and experience working with Microsoft Office applications (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, etc).
- Demonstrated attention to detail. Ability to manage multiple tasks and complete tasks within agreed schedule.
- Ability to communicate clearly—to expresses ideas and concerns openly and constructively and delivers verbal and written information effectively.

Language Requirements

- Fluency in **oral and written Arabic is required. Proficiency in English is also essential.**

title: Finance, Compliance and Grants Coordinator - GORS
body:
**Location:** Remote

**Consultancy**: part-time, 30 hours per week, for 3 months with the possibility of extension

**Compensation:** US$50 -$60 per hour, depending on experience

**Background**

Global Outbreak Response Support (GORS) delivered by Global Emergency Group, Inc. (GEG), under a cooperative agreement with the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy (GHSD), provides rapid activation, surge response, and transition support enabling countries to detect, contain, and recover from infectious disease outbreaks. GEG leads GORS as the prime recipient, building on its ongoing role as Field Programs Support lead for Team Credence on the Humanitarian Assistance Support Contract (HASC). Founded in 2007, GEG delivers GORS through a global network of regional response hubs, a pre-vetted surge roster, and embedded in-country teams that mobilize within hours of an authorized outbreak response.

**Reporting/Communication Lines**

The Finance, Compliance and Grants Coordinator reports functionally to the GEG Finance Manager and operationally supports the GORS Program Director and GORS Senior Operations Lead. Works closely with Operations, Senior Technical Director/subaward managers, Intelligence-to-Action Hub Lead and MEL Officer.

**Scope of Work**

**Position Description**

The Finance, Compliance and Grants Coordinator is responsible for accurate, compliant and decision-useful financial management for readiness, activations, partners, technology and expenditure-to-results reporting.

*The Finance, Compliance and Grants Coordinator will:*

- Maintain the program budget, forecasts, burn rate, activation scenarios and cost allocation across fixed and activation-dependent activities.
- Ensure every material cost links to an approved activity, output, result and responsible function.
- Support rapid activation budgeting, travel advances, procurement, vendor and partner payments and financial controls.
- Financial onboarding for new personnel.
- Manage payroll and expense processing for personnel including performing monthly reconciliations for any credit card company charges.
- Financial management for all GORS personnel, including adherence to local labor laws, managing financial aspects including taxes (employee and employer), severance, leave, overtime, corporate requirements, timesheets, holidays, creating policies for travel/expenses/work schedules/etc.
- Monitor subaward/subcontract budgets, invoicing, supporting documentation, budget vs actuals, variances and compliance.
- Produce timely financial reports and decision briefs for the GORS Program Director, Senior Operations Lead and GEG Finance Manager.
- Produce requests for funding from GHSD.
- Produce monthly accounting of all expenses for submission to GHSD.
- Support expenditure-to-results reviews and flag where spending, delivery and performance diverge.
- Maintain audit-ready records, segregation of duties, fraud controls and close-out/reconciliation processes.
- Support lifecycle-cost modelling for Intelligence-to-Action Hub and costed continuation/scale planning.
- Ensure compliance with all USG financial requirements.

**Required Position Qualifications**

- Relevant degree/professional qualification in finance, accounting, grants management or a related field.
- At least 5–8 years of donor-funded program finance, preferably including USG and emergency operations.
- Strong experience in budgeting, forecasting, subaward monitoring, audit readiness and rapid-response finance.
- Ability to translate financial data into clear management decisions under time pressure
- Excellent attention to detail in maintaining organized and accurate financial records across multiple projects and countries.
- Fluent professional English; additional languages and international experience are assets.

**Competencies/Performance Criteria**

Adherence and promotion of the GEG Way.

**Travel Frequency**

The Finance, Compliance and Grants Coordinator will conduct planned travel as required.

**Working Conditions**

The Finance, Compliance and Grants Coordinator will work remotely from their home base on a 9am to 5pm eastern time zone basis and will be available during emergencies or to meet critical client requirements. The Finance, Compliance and Grants Coordinator adheres to GEG security management directives and policies as prescribed by GEG.

**Benefits & Leave**

As personnel dedicated to GORS delivery, the Finance, Compliance and Grants Coordinator will have access to those Global Emergency Group benefits available in their country’s home of record.

**ABOUT GLOBAL EMERGENCY GROUP**

Founded in 2007, GEG is a benefit corporation that supports vulnerable people affected by crisis in more than 52 countries by providing a broad range of humanitarian support services to a wide range of organizations, including the United Nations, the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, donor governments, companies, major international and national NGO’s and local communities. Every day, these organizations and communities rely on GEG’s emergency response expertise, and on the combined capabilities and dedication of its people to implement strategies, find solutions and seize opportunities to assist the world’s most vulnerable people.

Global Emergency Group is committed to being an equal opportunity employer and recruiting people of diverse backgrounds and experiences. GEG does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion or belief, color, gender, sex, sexual orientation, marital status, family structure, age, medical condition, disability, ancestry, national origin or ethnic group. All recruitment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications, merit and business need.

title: Expression of Interest: Board Member(s) for RET Americas
body:
**Location:** Worldwide, with preference for US-based candidates

**Term:** 3 years, renewable by mutual agreement – Unpaid (reasonable travel expenses can be claimed)

**Closing date:** Friday, October 16

**About RET Americas**

RET Americas is an independent 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization headquartered in Washington, D.C. We are part of the RET Alliance, a global network dedicated to alleviating suffering and catalyzing sustainable development in crises, conflicts, and fragile contexts.

Founded in 2000 by Sadako Ogata, the trailblazing former UN High Commissioner for Refugees, RET has implemented more than 460 projects across 35 countries and provided critical programming to over 2.5 million program participants. Today, our mission is more urgent than ever.

The world is facing intersecting crises: Displacement, conflict, unpredictable weather and increasingly devastating disasters. These fall disproportionately on the populations RET Americas serves: Youth, women, and girls in Latin America, the Caribbean, Africa, the Middle East and beyond. We are at a pivotal moment, actively growing our board, deepening our resource base, and expanding our impact.

We are looking for board members who bring strategic thinking, professional networks, and a genuine commitment to humanitarian values. This is an opportunity not just to govern but to shape the future of a high-impact organization at a critical moment.

If you believe in the power of education, protection, and community resilience to transform lives, we would love to hear from you.

**Purpose of the Board**

The RET Americas Board of Directors is the governing body of the organization. It is responsible for the strategic direction of RET Americas, ensuring fiscal integrity, and overseeing the CEO and senior management. The Board meets quarterly with the Executive Leadership Team to review progress, ensure organizational health, and guide long-term strategy.

As an independent 501(c)(3), RET Americas Board members carry full legal fiduciary responsibility under U.S. nonprofit law and are expected to act in the best interests of the organization and the communities it serves.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Fulfill the statutory duties of a nonprofit board director under U.S. law and IRS requirements.
- Approve and monitor organizational strategy, annual plans, and major policies.
- Appoint, support, and evaluate the CEO, and ensure appropriate succession planning.
- Attend and actively contribute to quarterly board meetings and relevant committee sessions.
- Fulfill the annual Give/Get obligation and serve as an ambassador for RET Americas.
- Review financial statements, the annual audit, and key compliance documents.
- Serve on or contribute to a relevant task force or working group based on professional expertise.
- Maintain confidentiality and adhere to the organization’s Conflict of Interest Policy.
- Advocate for RET Americas’ mission within your professional and personal networks.

**Priority Expertise Areas**

We are currently recruiting for board members with experience in one or more of the following sectors:

- Legal – Particularly international law, nonprofit governance, compliance, or human rights law
- Communications and media – Public relations, graphics, marketing, or social media
- Finance & Accounting – Financial oversight, audit, investment, or endowment management
- Corporate – Technology, media, finance, business development, extractive industries, agricultural or pharmaceutical sectors
- Government & Diplomacy – Including bilateral relations, international development policy, US Department of State networks
- Philanthropy & Fundraising – Major donor cultivation, foundation relations, or corporate social responsibility

**Skills & Abilities**

We are seeking board members who possess one or more of the following talents:

- Strategic thinker with the ability to contribute to long-term organizational planning and evaluate competing priorities.
- Inspirational communicator who can serve as a credible ambassador for RET Americas in professional and public settings.
- Collaborative team player with strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills.
- Financially literate with the ability to review budgets, audited financials, and organizational performance data.
- Curious and willing to probe, challenge constructively, and inquire deeply on behalf of the organization.
- Committed to good governance, including legal and fiduciary obligations of a nonprofit director.

**Personal Style & Attributes**

- Alignment with RET Americas' values: Accountability, transparency, and humanitarian commitment.
- Demonstrated engagement in the humanitarian, development, or social impact sector, whether through prior board service, philanthropy, or advocacy.
- Ability to fulfill the Give/Get commitment (details provided during initial vetting and meeting) and bring a meaningful network to the organization's resource development.
- Available to prioritize RET Americas board duties, including quarterly meetings and task force engagement.
- Self-aware, principled, and consistent; someone who models the right behaviors and treats all colleagues with respect.
- Meetings & Attendance
- Board meetings are held four times per year (quarterly), conducted virtually and/or in person.
- Board members are expected to review all pre-meeting materials at least 48 hours before each meeting.
- Ad hoc working sessions or committee calls may be convened between quarterly meetings.

**Term & Renewal**

- Initial board terms are three years, renewable by mutual agreement with the Board Chair.
- Renewals are subject to a brief annual review of Give/Get fulfillment and overall engagement.
- Board members wishing to step down should provide a minimum of 60 days' written notice.

title: Country Financial Controller
body:
**Role Purpose**

As a member of Concern Sierra Leone Country Management Team, the Country Financial Controller (CFC) is responsible for the effective management of Concern Sierra Leone’s finance function. This will include ensuring internal controls are in place, managing the finance team, partner finance oversight, training, treasury management, financial planning and reporting. The successful candidate will be responsible for ensuring proper financial management and reporting on all grants received by Concern Sierra Leone.

**Reports to:** Country Director

**Terms:** Two-year Fixed Term, Full time, Accompanied, fully office based

**Location:** Freetown, Sierra Leone

**Salary:** GB7 €51,861 - €57,623

**Requirements:** This role is based in Freetown, Sierra Leone with regular travel to other programme locations within Sierra Leone.

**Responsibilities**

*Financial Systems and Controls*

- Ensure that country financial management systems and records are adequate in order to identify and protect the assets and interests of the organization.
- Ensure that the systems and procedures in place enhance, as far as possible, the efficiency and effectiveness of the manner in which assets are utilized.
- Maintaining and monitoring an effective and efficient system of internal controls (i.e. ledger, cashbooks, balance sheet reconciliations, cash and bank management etc.) which comply with Concern Worldwide’s financial guidelines and minimise the risk of fraud or misappropriation.
- Undertaking regular field visits to assess the financial systems in place and implement improvements wherever needed.
- Closely monitor all financial activities and keep the CD/Country Management Team advised of all situations that have the potential for a negative impact on internal controls or financial management performance.
- Responsible for maintaining financial documents and back up at field level so that all transactions contain sufficient audit trail. This includes all back up details to the support cost allocation, donor reporting, quarterly and year-end reporting.

*Financial Reporting and Donor Reporting*

- Lead the preparation of new, annual & revised Country budget and donor budgets with the support of CD and budget holders and in line with strategic plans and organizational objectives including budget template preparation, consolidation of the budget packs, completion of the budget submission to Dublin complete the responses on budget feedback from Dublin jointly with Shared Services Accountant.
- Reconcile all balance sheet items on a monthly basis, in accordance with Concern Worldwide policies & procedures, with the support of International Accounting Services if applicable.
- Produce timely & accurate preparation of data for monthly management accounts for International Accounting Services, budget-holders, and Country Management to ensure that they can monitor the budget utilization and take appropriate action on any significant variances. Present comments and major variances to CMT
- Oversee the timely & accurate preparation of donor reports for external donors / agencies.
- Ensure timely and accurate preparation of financial reports for Concern’s Head Office (Financial Reporting Pack including country commentary) and deal with feedback from Head Office
- Maintain a donor financial management system in order to optimize funding and to ensure efficient and accurate reporting to donors, including donor compliance.

*Staff Management and Capacity Building*

- Providing leadership and direction for the in-country Finance Team
- Develop a second layer of staff who can fill the gap whenever any position is vacant in the finance team
- Undertake specific training, capacity building and other relevant initiatives to ensure national staff perform their roles and responsibilities with accuracy and professionalism and also create the space for national staff to develop into credible candidates to fill vacant positions in the finance team and to provide strong cover for leave.
- Provide training and support to finance and non-finance staff regarding Concern’s financial procedures and internal controls
- Undertake financial training of budget-holders, to assist them in enforcing financial controls and making decisions based on financial reports.
- Ensure that Performance Development Reviews (PDRs) are completed for all country finance staff at least annually and that feedback on performance is provided routinely.

*Budget, Financial Management and Compliance*

- Responsible for overall financial management including participatory budget preparation, revision and monitoring and timely submission of Budgets and reports to HQ.
- Develop and implement work and expenditure plans and ensure that the country programmes are implemented within agreed and approved budget through undertaking regular budget monitoring of expenditure against budget.

*Partnership Accounting*

- Undertake the financial component of Concern Integrated Local Partner Assessment tool (CILPAT) with potential Partners on a timely and comprehensive basis in collaboration with Programmes and Systems departments.
- Summarise CILPAT findings and develop action plans to address financial weaknesses where partnership is workable with available resources.

**Role Holder Requirements**

- Accountancy Qualification (e.g. CPA, ACA, ACCA)
- 3 years post qualification experience in Concern or a similar organization preferably as international staff
- Experience in developing staff capacity both on technical and management aspects
- Experience managing large and multi donor (especially ECHO, OCHA, etc.) programme budgets

*We would also like:*

- Knowledge of development issues and concepts
- Academic background of or strong practical experience in macro-economic and/or fiscal policy
- Ability to work under pressure to meet tight deadlines
- Good team worker
- Good communication and negotiation skills
- A good understanding of computer applications i.e. Microsoft word, Excel, communications systems and basic trouble shooting skills
- Familiarity with ERP systems including Unit4 (formerly Aggresso).
- Cross cultural awareness and sensitivity
- Empathy with Concern’s goals and a commitment to capacity building, protection and participation
- Good communication and training / capacity building skills
- Proven organization, planning and management skills
- Ability to work on own initiative and lead diverse teams
- Flexible and adaptable to a changing environment

title: Labour Mobility Communications and Creative Content Specialist (Consultant A)
body:
Job Identification (Reference Number): **23923**  
Position Title: **Labour Mobility Communications and Creative Content Specialist (Consultant A)**  
Duty Station City: **Honiara**  
Duty Station Country: **Solomon Islands**  
Contract Type: **Consultant A**  
*Recruiting Type:* **Consultancy**  
*Vacancy Type:* **Call for Applications**  
Initial duration: **9 months**  
Closing date: **8 October 2026**

**Nature of the consultancy:**

Technical Assistance on Communications and Creative Content to the Labour Mobility Unit (LMU) of the Government of Solomon Islands (Category A Consultancy).

**Context:**

Labour mobility has become a key income and skills pathway for Solomon Islanders, with over 9,000 nationals participating in the Pacific Australia Labour Mobility (PALM) and New Zealand Recognized Seasonal Employer (RSE) schemes in 2025 alone. As participation grows, so does the need for stronger, more structured reintegration support. A 2023–2024 survey of 500 returned migrants found that returned migrant workers frequently faced limited access to employment, skills utilization, business support and financial services — highlighting the need for structured programmes that translate overseas experience and savings into sustainable livelihoods.

The proposed 12-month pilot project will contribute to improving sustainable economic reintegration outcomes for returned migrant workers in Solomon Islands (objective). The intervention has one outcome: The Labour Mobility Unit (LMU) provides enhanced, gender-sensitive economic reintegration support services to returned migrant workers, to facilitate their sustainable return and reintegration into their communities. This will be achieved through two complementary outputs: A comprehensive findings report on the sustainable reintegration of returned migrant workers, in support of implementing the Labour Mobility Policy and Action Plan 2024-2028, is available to the LMU (Output 1.1); and the LMU has enhanced capacity to deliver gender-sensitive economic reintegration support, particularly skills-building, networking and career opportunities for returned migrant workers (Output 1.2).

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing:**

From Return to Resilience: Strengthening Economic Reintegration of Returned Migrant Workers in Solomon Islands (RR0593); Labour Mobility Unit (LMU), Ministry of Foreign Affairs and External Trade (MFAET) with the Government of Solomon Islands.

**Description for Internal Candidates**

**Responsibilities for Internal Candidates**

The locally recruited Consultant will lead the implementation of Activity 1.2.3 and undertake other related tasks as requested by the Labour Mobility Unit (LMU). The Consultant will support the full process of developing and delivering gender-sensitive information, education and communication (IEC) materials for returning migrant workers, from information gathering and stakeholder consultation through to content development, production, dissemination, monitoring and adaptation.

The Consultant will undertake the following tasks:

1\. Gather information and undertake research

Conduct research to identify relevant information, resources, opportunities and good practices that can inform IEC materials for returning migrant workers in Solomon Islands. The IEC materials will primarily focus on economic reintegration, including information that supports returning migrant workers to access employment, develop livelihoods, pursue investment or entrepreneurship opportunities, and strengthen their financial resilience. Where relevant to sustainable reintegration, the materials may also incorporate information on social, psychosocial and other aspects of reintegration, including linkages to relevant services, resources and support available to returning migrant workers.

Information covered by the IEC materials may include, but is not limited to:

- Local employment and potential investment opportunities;
- Skills development, training and other education opportunities;
- CV and cover letter preparation, job search and interview preparation;
- Entrepreneurship, business development and financial literacy;
- Upcoming events and opportunities for returning migrant workers, including activities supported under the project;
- Pre-return counselling and other relevant information; and
- Relevant social, psychosocial and other support services or resources that may contribute to sustainable reintegration.

The Consultant will also research relevant good practices and examples from the Pacific region on engaging returning migrant workers and strengthening economic reintegration outcomes through awareness-raising and information interventions.

2\. Consult with stakeholders and target audiences

Consult with relevant stakeholders, LMU and target audiences, as appropriate, to validate information needs, identify key messages and ensure that the proposed IEC materials are relevant, accessible and responsive to the needs of returning migrant workers. The Consultant will communicate relevant findings and recommendations to LMU and incorporate feedback into the development of the materials.

3\. Advise on content and communication approaches

Provide technical and expert advice to LMU on the content, format, design, accessibility and communication approach for the IEC materials, including recommendations on appropriate channels and methods for effectively reaching returning migrant workers.

4\. Develop and produce IEC materials

Based on the information gathered, research undertaken, stakeholder consultations and agreed communication approach, support LMU in the development and production of high-quality IEC materials. Materials may include printed, digital, audio-visual and other creative communication resources, as appropriate to the target audience and intended purpose.

5\. Support dissemination of IEC materials

Support LMU, as required, in the dissemination of completed IEC materials through appropriate channels. These may include printed materials and direct sharing through in-person engagement and email; online platforms, including the [Labour Mobility Unit Facebook page](https://www.facebook.com/people/Labour-Mobility-Unit-Solomon-Islands/61566025701376/) and official website channels; radio; and other appropriate and creative communication mediums.

6\. Monitor engagement and gather feedback

Track engagement with the IEC materials and gather feedback from target audiences and relevant stakeholders to assess the relevance, accessibility and effectiveness of the materials and dissemination approaches.

7\. Recommend adaptations and improvements

Based on monitoring, feedback and lessons learned, provide timely recommendations to LMU on adaptations or adjustments to the IEC materials, content or dissemination approaches. Findings and feedback will be used to inform subsequent material development, production and dissemination.

8\. Handover and knowledge sharing

Ensure that all materials, content, templates and relevant resources developed under the assignment are provided to LMU for ongoing use, adaptation and dissemination. The Consultant will also share relevant knowledge, findings and lessons learned with LMU to support continued development and dissemination of reintegration information beyond the assignment.

9\. Other related support

Provide other related technical assistance and support as reasonably required by the LMU and IOM Project Manager, within the scope of the assignment.

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

- Complete all activities by no later than 31 July 2027
- Document and share with LMU and IOM relevant best practices and lessons learned on engaging returning migrant workers through gender-sensitive and inclusive IEC materials.
- Consult relevant stakeholders and target audiences and provide technical support to LMU in the development and production of at least 10 IEC materials, primarily focused on improving economic reintegration outcomes for return migrant workers
- Disseminate IEC materials through appropriate channels and engage at least 100 returning migrant workers
- Monitor engagement, collect feedback and provide recommendations to inform adaptation and improvement of IEC materials
- Handover all final materials, templates and source files to LMU and provide a final summary report of activities, results and lessons learned to LMU and IOM.

**Qualifications for Internal Candidates**

University degree or equivalent qualification in Graphic Design, Communications, Media, Marketing, Journalism, or another relevant creative or communications field; relevant professional experience may be considered in lieu.

**Experience**

- Demonstrated experience in graphic design, content writing and development of professional IEC and communication materials, including print, digital, audio-visual and social media content.
- Proficiency in relevant creative and digital applications, including Adobe Creative Suite (e.g. Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign and/or Premiere Pro), video editing software and other digital content creation tools.

**Skills**

- trong written, verbal and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build effective working relationships with colleagues, government counterparts, stakeholders and target audiences.
- Demonstrated ability to think creatively, work independently with limited supervision, adapt outputs in response to feedback and changing requirements, and manage multiple tasks and deadlines effectively
- Strong organizational and file-management skills, including maintaining well-organized records of materials, source files and other project resources. Experience working with government, international organizations or development partners, particularly in the Pacific, would be an advantage.

**Languages**

- Required for this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written). Working knowledge of Pijin is desirable.
- IOM’s official languages are English, French and Spanish.
- Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at [this link](https://www.iom.int/sites/g/files/tmzbdl486/files/about-iom/Competency_Framework-EN.pdf). Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these three values:

- Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators (Level 1)

- Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

**Notes**

- Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.
- This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.
- This post is subject to only those holding a valid residence and work permit for the country where this position is based will be eligible for consideration.
- Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, verification of residency, visa, and authorizations by the concerned Government, where applicable.
- IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.
- IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.
- IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM online recruitment system. The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.
- For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: [IOM Careers and Job Vacancies](https://www.iom.int/careers)

title: Financial Capabilities Coordinator
body:
**Job Overview:** Under the supervision of the Senior Program Manager, the IRC seeks a Financial Capabilities Coordinator to support the development and implementation of career pathways services in its Economic Empowerment program for refugees and other immigrants in Tucson. This position is responsible for assisting clients in developing plans that help them reach their goals and achieve financial stability, and for ensuring IRC achieves program targets relating to enrollment, economic empowerment outcomes, and connection to community benefits and resources. The Coordinator is to tangibly connect working clients on their journey to a higher paying job to resources and certifications. It is expected to focus services in a one-on-one career counseling format in tandem with conducting classes and workshops on topics such as budgeting, credit building, banking, and financial products.

**Responsibilities: Include, but are not limited to:**

**Client Services:**

- Assist clients in assessing and resolving current financial challenges, while providing a wide lens on their financial health to shift the approach to proactive financial management
- Administer intake and assessment for enrolled participants and co-develop an Individualized Career Development Plan (ICDP) with each participant to guide training, employment, and follow-up activities.
- Coordinate case-managed wraparound supports, including interpretation, transportation and childcare stipends, work supplies, and emergency assistance, tied to each participant's documented barriers and ICDP.
- Connect participants to local occupational training, apprenticeships, or certification programs, and to employer partners for job upgrades or career-related employment.
- Conduct 6- and 12-month follow-up with participants and, when applicable, their employers to assess job retention, wages, advancement, job quality, benefits, and household financial stability.
- Ensure that changes (new job, new benefit, and change in credit score) are properly documented in relevant systems.
- Capture client success stories
- Develop workshop materials or tailor existing materials to meet the needs of the community. Workshop topics may include the following: budgeting, savings, banking products, credit building, and identity theft.

**Program Coordination:**

- Ensure compliance with all policies, procedures, and protocols of the agency.
- Ensure that information required for program eligibility for all career programs and reporting purposes is collected and that accurate records are maintained, including case files and client data entry.
- Work as part of a team to provide comprehensive strength-based services to IRC clients through coordination of cases and effective communication between team members and departments.
- Design, implement, and provide monitoring and evaluation oversight for career and industry-specific programming;
- Train, and supervise interns and volunteers providing career support services to clients enrolled in career programs;
- Participate in IRC network-wide initiatives to understand and share best-practices relating to career pathways programming;
- Build and maintain partnerships with community-based organizations, career service providers, and small business and corporate entities for advanced career opportunities;
- Coordinate corporate and employer engagement opportunities and events.
- Participate in program meetings and staff development activities.
- Coordinate quality assurance efforts by conducting periodic case file and electronic data reviews.
- Produce high-quality program reports for IRC headquarters and funders and ensure programs fulfill funder and agency requirements.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

- 2+ years of related professional experience in financial capabilities and/or career development
- Experience in a non-profit setting and/or financial coaching services a plus
- Experience working in a diverse, and non-traditional setting with diverse staff and client base
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills and an overall ability to be clear and concise in all communications
- Exceptional organizational skills with proven attention to detail.

**CDD | 12 mois | ASAP**

## **Acted**

***Qui sommes-nous***

Acted travaille avec 19 millions de personnes dans 43 pays au carrefour de l’humanitaire, du développement, et des programmes climatiques et environnementaux. Grâce à une connaissance poussée des contextes et l’adoption de technologies émergentes, nous sauvons des vies, allégeons les souffrances, et protégeons et restaurons notre planète. Travaillant avec un écosystème croissant de partenaires locaux, nationaux et internationaux, nous poursuivons un objectif commun : un monde 3Zéro : Zéro Exclusion, Zéro Carbone, Zéro Pauvreté.

***Qui cherchons-nous***

Vous apportez les compétences clefs attendues d’un travailleur humanitaire et de développement, mais également une conscience climatique et environnementale active, et vous pouvez naviguez les défis qui émergent lorsque les souffrances environnementale et humaine se rencontrent. Vous avez l’esprit entrepreneurial : vous décelez les opportunités, connectez les points, adaptez votre approche aux différents environnements, et vous prenez des risques mesurés dans la poursuite de résultats. Vous alliez les principes au pragmatisme, et l’ambition à l’humilité.

## **Acted Tchad**

Présente au Tchad, Acted intervient en faveur des populations vulnérables des Provinces du Lac et du Ouaddai, et à Ndjamena. En 2025, l’organisation a mis en oeuvre 11 projets pour un budget de 10.5 millions d’euros. Ses opérations sont coordonnées depuis NDjamena et implémentées à travers 4 bases terrain à Bol et Daboua au Lac, Adré et Chokoyan au Ouaddai.

Au Lac, Acted soutient les personnes déplacées internes suite aux attaques des groupes armés à travers le mécanisme RRM, dont elle est co-lead, et assure l’assistance en sécurité alimentaire. Elle participe aussi à renforcer la résilience des populations dans le cadre de projets d’éducation, d’eau hygiène assainissement ou de moyens d’existence.

Au Ouaddai, Acted s’est redéployée dès avril 2023 pour répondre à l’afflux sans précédent de réfugiés soudanais et retournés tchadiens fuyant les combats au Soudan. A travers une approche multisectorielle d’urgence en abris/AME, CCCM et Protection, Acted répond aux besoins vitaux des déplacés sur les sites informels et les camps d’accueil. Depuis 2025, Acted participe à renforcer la résilience économique des réfugiés Soudanais avec l’aide des communautés hôtes dans la préfecture de Chokoyan.

Les actions d’Acted au Tchad reposent sur une expertise technique multisectorielle reconnue, une capacité de déploiement rapide, une approche basée sur les données, une forte acceptance locale, et la participation accrue des communautés.

Au Ouaddai, Acted s’est redéployée dès avril 2023 pour répondre à l’afflux sans précédent de réfugiés soudanais et retournés tchadiens fuyant les combats au Soudan. A travers une approche multisectorielle d’urgence en abris/AME, CCCM et Protection, Acted répond aux besoins vitaux des déplacés sur les sites informels et les camps d’accueil.

Enfin, Acted intervient régulièrement en réponse aux chocs cycliques, tels que la soudure et les inondations, particulièrement dévastatrices.

Les actions d’Acted au Tchad reposent sur une expertise technique multisectorielle reconnue, une capacité de déploiement rapide, une approche basée sur les données, une forte acceptance locale, et la participation accrue des communautés.

## **Rôle et responsabilités principales**

Le/la Responsable projet, sous la conduite opérationnelle du Coordinateur de zone et la conduite technique du Coordinateur technique des programmes est responsable d’assurer la mise en œuvre du projet d’Acted. Le/la Responsable projet supervise les opérations de terrain et assure l’achèvement effectif et dans les délais des activités ; il/elle assure également des restitutions de qualité et la réalisation des résultats avec un maximum d’impact pour les bénéficiaires. Le/la Responsable projet supervise le staff projet, dans la gestion au jour le jour de tous les aspects du projet et fait le lien avec les départements internes pertinents, les partenaires externes et les parties prenantes du projet.

***Principales Responsabilités***

1\. Planification des projets

2\. Suivi de mise en œuvre des projets

3\. Administration et gestion opérationnelle de mise en œuvre du projet

- *Finances*
- *Logistique*
- *Administration/RH*
- *Transparence*
- *Sécurité*

4\. Relations externes

5\. Contrôle qualité

6\. Rapports

## **Qualifications et compétences requises**

- Expérience en lien avec le type de projet requise, dans un contexte d’urgence et/ou de développement
- Une expérience de travail avec des bailleurs de fond institutionnels est un plus
- Expérience en gestion de budget
- Capacité à coordonner et gérer une équipe
- Capacité à travailler de manière indépendante et créative sur le terrain et en capitale
- Excellente expression orale et écrite
- Forte habilité à travailler dans un contexte interculturel

## **Termes de référence**

Pour plus d'informations sur le poste, [cliquez ici ](https://www.acted.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/candidate-pack-pm-tcd.pdf).

## **Conditions**

- Salaire défini par la grille des salaires Acted en fonction du niveau d’études, de l’expertise, du niveau de sécurité et du niveau d’expérience
- Indemnité mensuelle de frais de vie 300$
- Logement en guesthouse et nourriture pris en charge par Acted
- Sécurité sociale, mutuelle (MSH) et assistance rapatriement (SOS International) pris en charge par Acted
- Transport vers la mission et billet retour totalement pris en charge tous les 6 mois (vers l’adresse spécifiée sur le contrat de travail)
- Frais de visa pris en charge par Acted
- R&R tous les 3 mois (billet d’avion pris en charge jusqu’à 500$ + indemnité supplémentaire de 200$)
- Une semaine de préparation au départ comprenant 4 jours de formation sécurité en immersion
- Possibilité d’avoir un appel de 30minutes avec un.e consultant.e en fiscalité
- Soutien psychologique (rendez-vous avec un.e professionnel.le)
- Ce poste est classé comme un poste international dans la grille de recrutement d’Acted. L’éligibilité à un contrat international est donc requise.

title: République Démocratique du Congo : Responsable MEAL Pays - Kinshasa

**CDD | 6 mois | Octobre 2026**

## **Acted**

***Qui sommes-nous***

Acted travaille avec 19 millions de personnes dans 43 pays au carrefour de l’humanitaire, du développement, et des programmes climatiques et environnementaux. Grâce à une connaissance poussée des contextes et l’adoption de technologies émergentes, nous sauvons des vies, allégeons les souffrances, et protégeons et restaurons notre planète. Travaillant avec un écosystème croissant de partenaires locaux, nationaux et internationaux, nous poursuivons un objectif commun : un monde 3Zéro : Zéro Exclusion, Zéro Carbone, Zéro Pauvreté.

***Qui cherchons-nous***

Vous apportez les compétences clefs attendues d’un travailleur humanitaire et de développement, mais également une conscience climatique et environnementale active, et vous pouvez naviguez les défis qui émergent lorsque les souffrances environnementale et humaine se rencontrent. Vous avez l’esprit entrepreneurial : vous décelez les opportunités, connectez les points, adaptez votre approche aux différents environnements, et vous prenez des risques mesurés dans la poursuite de résultats. Vous alliez les principes au pragmatisme, et l’ambition à l’humilité.

## **Acted République Démocratique du Congo**

La République Démocratique du Congo fait face à une crise humanitaire prolongée, marquée par la persistance des conflits armés, des déplacements massifs de populations, des chocs climatiques et des chocs épidémiques récurrents, tels que le choléra, le mpox ou la rougeole. Ces dynamiques combinées affectent durablement les conditions de vie des populations déplacées, retournées et hôtes, en particulier dans les provinces de l’Est et certaines zones de l’Ouest du pays.

Dans ce contexte, Acted intervient principalement dans les provinces du Sud-Kivu, Nord-Kivu, Tanganyika, Nord-Ubangi et Sud-Ubangi, à travers des projets financés notamment par le Department of State / US, ECHO, FCDO, SDC, le Fonds Humanitaire, ainsi que le CDCS, afin de répondre aux besoins humanitaires immédiats et aux vulnérabilités persistantes des populations les plus affectées. Afin de renforcer la couverture et la complémentarité de ses interventions, Acted intervient en coordination avec plusieurs partenaires opérationnels, et est membre de consortiums humanitaires.

Cette coordination permet à Acted de mettre en œuvre des réponses d’urgence rapides et multisectorielles pour couvrir les besoins vitaux liés aux conflits, aux déplacements forcés, aux catastrophes naturelles et aux crises sanitaires. Les interventions portent notamment sur l’assistance alimentaire, les abris et articles ménagers essentiels, l’Eau, Hygiène et Assainissement (EHA), la gestion et coordination des sites (CCCM) ainsi que l’éducation en situation d’urgence, avec une attention particulière portée, dès le premier kilomètre humanitaire, à la protection et à la dignité des personnes vulnérables. Au Sud-Kivu, Acted est par ailleurs un acteur clé du Mécanisme de Réponse Rapide (RRM), contribuant à des réponses rapides et coordonnées en lien avec les déplacements de populations et aux chocs soudains.

En parallèle, Acted développe des interventions visant à renforcer la résilience des communautés, à travers le soutien aux moyens d’existence, la relance agricole, la sécurité alimentaire et la relance économique locale, afin de réduire la vulnérabilité face aux chocs récurrents.

Acted apporte également un appui structurant aux organisations de la société civile (OSC) en renforçant leurs capacités organisationnelles et opérationnelles. Cet accompagnement inclut l’appui à la structuration des initiatives locales ainsi que la mise en place de mécanismes de financement en cascade, permettant aux OSC de développer des activités directement liées aux problématiques locales et aux priorités identifiées par les communautés.

Enfin, Acted intègre progressivement dans ses programmes des approches sensibles à l’environnement, visant à la préservation des écosystèmes et des aires protégées, à la réduction de l’empreinte environnementale des interventions et à la promotion de solutions à faible émission de carbone. À travers l’appui aux communautés, Acted encourage le développement d’activités génératrices de revenus durables et d’une économie locale plus verte, contribuant à la protection des ressources naturelles tout en renforçant les moyens d’existence.

## **Rôle et responsabilités principales**

Le/la responsable pays Enquêtes, Suivi, Contrôle et Évaluation est responsable de l’élaboration du développement et de la mise en œuvre d’un système d’enquêtes, de suivi, de contrôle et d’évaluation approprié et viable en ligne avec les procédures MEAL (Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning) de la stratégie globale d’Acted et s’assure que les projets et programmes d’Acted sont réalisés tel que planifiés.

***Principales Responsabilités :***

1\. Coordination des activités MEAL

2\. Gestion du département et de l’équipe MEAL

3\. Renforcement des compétences et formation

4\. Développement de procédures

5\. Capitalisation

6\. Mettre en œuvre le mécanisme de réponse aux plaintes des bénéficiaires

7\. Autres

## **Qualifications et compétences requises**

- Diplôme Supérieur en Sciences Politiques, Relations Internationales, Développement International, Economie ou équivalent (anthropologie, sociologie, statistiques) ;
- Au moins 2 à 5 ans d’expérience en monitoring et évaluation de projets dans l’humanitaire et/ou le développement ;
- Expérience en évaluations participatives et en gestion du cycle de projet ;
- Excellent niveau de communication à l’écrit comme à l’oral en français et en anglais ;
- Bonnes capacités d’organisation et de communication avec le personnel international et national et les communautés rurales ;
- Capacité à coordonner et gérer une équipe ;
- Travail en équipe, capacité à créer un esprit d’équipe et à faire monter en compétences ;
- Flexibilité, capacité d’adaptation, capacité d’organisation, prise d’initiative.

Pour plus d'informations sur le poste, [cliquez ici ](https://www.acted.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/mealm-rdc-2026.pdf).

## **Conditions**

body:
***Marketing and Business*** ***Development Intern***

**Reporting to:** SBC Design and Partnerships Officer

**Start date:** 1 February 2026

**Duration:** 12 Months

**Location:** The position will be based in Amman, Jordan. Please note that MAGENTA’s teams work from home with in-person meetings and events as required, including regular colocation with colleagues in hubs.

**Remuneration:** A stipend of 1,000.00 USD per month

MAGENTA is a leading Social and Behavioural Change (SBC) agency that specialises in understanding human decision-making processes in order to design solutions for relevant and impactful solutions to some of the most challenging problems of our time. We implement programmes across the Middle East & North Africa, Africa, Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean using the latest in behavioural science principles and a rigorous approach to research, strategy, campaign design and implementation.

Our client base includes UN agencies, INGOs, the FCDO, the US government and the private sector. We aim to amplify the voices of local actors while bringing international expertise and methodological rigour. To do so, we partner with civil society, creative agencies, media and academics to design innovative, relevant and impactful solutions to some of the most challenging problems of our time. Whether we are aiming to shift parenting practices to improve children’s outcomes or to understand how social norms underpin corruption, we always go the extra mile to ensure we can create positive impact for some of the most underserved populations in the world.

MAGENTA is made up of five business units and three operating departments: Middle East & North Africa, Asia, Africa, Latin America & the Caribbean, the MAGENTA Lab, Corporate Services, Growth & Marketing and Technical & Programme.

The Marketing and Business Development Intern will play an important role in supporting MAGENTA’s marketing and new business efforts. This internship offers an opportunity to gain hands-on experience in a dynamic and mission-driven environment.

***RESPONSIBILITIES***

**Marketing and Communications**

- Manage and expand MAGENTA’s social media presence (LinkedIn and Facebook), including planning, creation, and scheduling of posts, monitoring engagement metrics, and pinpointing areas for content enhancement.
- Contribute to developing and designing compelling marketing materials, including case studies, capability statements, brochures, and bi-monthly newsletter.
- Ensure that MAGENTA’s marketing collateral is kept up-to-date across four languages, and implement updates and edits as required.
- Maintain strict compliance with the company’s branding directives across all marketing materials and communications, maintaining a consistent visual and messaging identity.
- Maintain and update MAGENTA’s website, ensuring it accurately reflects the most recent projects, initiatives, and team.
- Maintain MAGENTA’s databases including YouTube channel, tender monitoring tracker, past performance database, close-out tracker, and contact lists.
- Generate routine reports detailing marketing performance, including website traffic, social media engagement, and provide recommendations for enhancement.
- Research and monitor thought leadership opportunities and support program teams to prepare and submit applications to conferences, summits, and other thought leadership events.
- Provide occasional training and guidance to MAGENTA teams on how to use Canva and YouTube platforms for marketing and business development tasks.

**Business Development**

- Facilitate proposal development by conducting research on thematic areas related to specific bids, donor strategies, and competitor analysis.
- Collaborate with bid writing teams by providing desk research support and helping draft proposal sections as required.
- Support programme teams on proposal submissions by gathering and uploading necessary documents, formatting proposals, and providing additional technical support as required.
- Monitor business development platforms to identify relevant tenders to be shared with the programme teams twice a week.

***REQUIREMENTS***

**Education:**

- Recently completed a bachelor’s or master’s degree programme, ideally in a field related to international development, business development, or marketing.

**Experience:**

- Prior marketing-related and or business development internships, coursework, or relevant extracurricular activities preferred.
- Impeccable written and verbal communication skills in English and Arabic. One additional MAGENTA language (French or Spanish) is highly desirable.
- Strong organisational, writing, formatting, and presentation skills.
- A creative mindset for generating innovative marketing ideas and content.
- Basic understanding of analytics tools and data interpretation.
- Familiarity with digital marketing concepts, including conducting social media analytics and SEO.
- Familiarity with social media content creation and digital communication trends.
- Ability to follow branding guidelines and maintaining brand consistency.
- Ability to manage multiple tasks, meet deadlines and prioritise tasks as needed.
- Ability to work effectively in a team.
- Proficiency with Office tools, especially Word, PowerPoint, and Excel.
- Proficiency with Canva or other online graphic design tools.
- Demonstrated curiosity about AI and emerging technologies, with hands-on experience applying them to real work - e.g. using AI for research synthesis, drafting, data analysis, workflow automation, or "vibe coding" simple tools/prototypes - and a track record of proactively teaching yourself new digital skills
- Flexibility to changing needs and priorities.

***COMPETENCIES***

The following are key competencies required for this position.

• Innovative

• Reliable

A fast, self-directed learner who actively builds new skills rather than waiting to be trained - comfortable experimenting with AI, no-code and "vibe coding" tools to solve problems and work smarter

***CULTURAL FIT***

Curiosity: Challenge the obvious, reflect and then act.

Transparency: Hold yourself and those around you accountable

Authenticity: Walk the talk

Innovation: Think bold, think big, think broad

• Good sense of humour, personable and demonstrated ability to build networks.

MAGENTA has a flexible working policy which promotes periods of remote working in the year.
