title: AI Product Manager - CLEAR Project
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
**What we’re looking for**

Help build NRC’s future of AI-enabled humanitarian response.

NRC is hiring an experienced **Product Manager** for the CLEAR Initiative to help build the next generation of humanitarian information systems and turn complex, fragmented crisis data into insights that enable humanitarian teams to act earlier - and potentially save lives.

CLEAR is building open infrastructure for crisis emergency response and anticipatory action. Across the humanitarian sector, critical signals such as earth observation data, conflict feeds, field reports, and market information often sit across dozens of disconnected tools and formats. By the time these signals are brought together, the window for early action may already have passed. CLEAR is designed to change that. The initiative is developing a shared, open and federated platform built for - and owned by - the humanitarian sector. By connecting diverse data sources and transforming them into actionable insights, CLEAR aims to close the gap between insight and action when every moment matters.

As AI Product Manager, you will be at the heart of turning this vision into reality. Working under the strategic direction of the AI Lead, you will translate CLEAR’s objectives into practical digital products that support real-world humanitarian crisis response. This is an opportunity to work at the intersection of AI, product development, data and humanitarian action - helping build technology that enables the sector to see emerging risks sooner, make better-informed decisions and act within the critical window before a crisis peaks.

If you are passionate about turning emerging technology into practical solutions for humanitarian impact, we would like to hear from you.

**What you will do:**

- Drive product delivery and adoption - own the coordination, sequencing, prioritiziation and rollout CLEAR’s multiple products.
- Turn strategy into action - translate the project’s vision and objectives into clear product priorities, requirements and deliverables.
- Connect research and engineering - create a seamless bridge between emerging research, technical development and practical humanitarian applications.
- Bring people together - align internal and external stakeholders around priorities, timelines and product outcomes.
- Keep delivery moving - manage the operational aspects of product development, identify dependencies and remove barriers to progress.
- Build for humanitarian impact - ensure that CLEAR’s digital solutions are not only technically strong, but genuinely useful to the teams responding to crises on the ground.

Please download a more detailed[ **JOB DESCRIPTION**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQAZg2AJ8T3cSYY2XR6G_W3NAQEQDwRvqW61xN3MUO7JKwk?e=gdvKOU) for more specific duties and responsibilities.

**What you will bring:**

- 5–7 years’ product management experience in technology, data or digital transformation.
- Proven success launching and scaling complex digital products from concept to implementation.
- Strong ability to bridge technical and non-technical teams, translating technology into user needs and operational requirements into technical solutions.
- Practical knowledge of Agile, APIs, cloud platforms and modern software development.
- Proficiency in product management frameworks and tools, including user story mapping, prioritisation and OKRs.
- Experience with user research, usability testing and human-centred design.
- Strong data literacy, including defining metrics, interpreting analytics and making data-informed decisions.
- Experience leading multi-stakeholder projects and managing diverse technical and non-technical audiences.
- Proven programme/delivery management experience across areas such as adoption, measurement, governance and partnerships.
- Experience managing external suppliers, including scope, quality and handover.
- Working knowledge of data science, machine learning and AI.
- Understanding of data ethics, privacy and responsible AI, particularly when working with vulnerable populations.
- Experience in humanitarian operations and an understanding of field realities and coordination mechanisms is an asset.
- Familiarity with open-source licensing and digital public goods is an asset.

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: NRC Head Office in Oslo, NRC Representation Offices (excluding Geneva and Washington, DC), approved Employer of Record (EoR) countries, and other countries where NRC operates, provided they are within ±2 hours of Oslo time.
- Contract: Temporary Cover (2 years).
- Travel: Up to 10%.
- Salary/benefits: grade 9 on NRC’s Resident salary scale, with accompanying terms and conditions.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity Market Place.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

If you have any questions about this role, please email **ho.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

title: Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Lead
body:
**Program Background**

Partnerships for Infrastructure (P4I) Phase 2 is an Australian Government initiative to support quality infrastructure development that drives inclusive growth in Southeast Asia. P4I-2 is a 10-year initiative to December 2035, with an initial period of five years from January 2026 to December 2030. P4I works with partners to strengthen policy and regulatory frameworks related to infrastructure development. It also addresses obstacles to project development, including through advice on financing strategies (with an emphasis on mobilising private finance). P4I works closely with Australian Government and industry to help bring relevant solutions to Southeast Asia’s infrastructure development challenges, in line with Australia's Southeast Asia Economic Strategy to 2040. P4I currently works in four sectors: land transport resilience, maritime decarbonisation, integration of renewables into energy systems, and telecommunications. P4I incorporates inclusion (gender equality, disability and social inclusion) and climate (mitigation and adaptation) across these four sectors.

More information about P4I is available at [**www.partnershipsforinfrastructure.org**](https://www.partnershipsforinfrastructure.org/)

**The Role**

The M&E Lead is responsible for the implementation, and periodic refinement, of P4I’s Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning System. Working under the guidance of the MEL Director and closely with the program Learning Lead, the M&E Lead ensures performance data collection, analysis, reporting and management is robust and in line with program and DFAT requirements.

**Responsibilities**

The **M&E Lead** will:

- Lead the implementation and periodic refinement of P4I’s Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Systems, including the MEL Framework, Performance Assessment Framework indicators, data collection tools and analytical methodologies, ensuring alignment with DFAT requirements and evolving program needs. This will include the effective integration of inclusion, climate and other cross-cutting priorities.
- Lead program performance monitoring, mobilising P4I colleagues and subcontractors to contribute to the collection, quality assurance and analysis of performance data, and that the program Management Information System (MIS) is generating reliable and accessible data to inform program management decision-making.
- Lead the preparation and quality assurance of program reporting products, including periodic DFAT progress reports, dashboards, presentations and other performance reporting requirements, ensuring evidence-based data and analysis is communicated clearly and effectively to diverse audiences.
- In close consultation with the program Learning Lead, contribute to reviews, research and learning processes as needed, synthesising evidence, stakeholder feedback and contextual analysis into practical insights that inform strategy, adaptive management and program performance.
- Provide MEL technical leadership, guidance and skills development across program teams, partners and advisers, raising the profile of MEL and fostering evidence-informed decision-making to maximise progress towards P4I’s End of Program Outcomes (EOPOs).

Click on the link or copy paste it to access the full Terms of Reference for this position: [**https://tinyurl.com/yszmnuax**](https://tinyurl.com/yszmnuax)

**About You**

**Selection Criteria**

**Qualifications**

- Tertiary qualifications in a relevant field such as international development, monitoring, evaluation and learning, public policy, social research, economics, governance, infrastructure, or a related discipline; or equivalent professional experience.

**Technical**

- Demonstrated experience leading MEL systems for large, complex donor-funded programs, including performance monitoring frameworks, data quality assurance processes, Management Information Systems (MIS), and donor reporting.
- Strong understanding of MEL methodologies and development effectiveness approaches, including performance measurement, evaluation, adaptive management, learning and evidence-informed decision-making.
- Understanding of DFAT MEL Standards and broader development effectiveness principles, or the demonstrated ability to apply comparable donor requirements in complex program settings.
- Strong qualitative and quantitative analytical skills, with the ability to synthesise data, evidence and stakeholder insights into practical recommendations for program management and decision-making.
- Experience working in Southeast Asia and/or within infrastructure, climate, inclusion, governance or related development programming is desirable.

**Leadership, Communication and Collaboration**

- Excellent written, verbal and facilitation skills, with the ability to communicate complex information clearly and effectively to technical and non-technical audiences.
- Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills, with a demonstrated ability to build productive partnerships with donors, government counterparts, program teams, subcontractors, consultants and technical advisers.
- Demonstrated ability to provide technical leadership, mentoring and capacity strengthening, building MEL understanding, capability and buy-in across diverse teams and partners.
- Demonstrated ability to work effectively within multidisciplinary, multicultural and geographically dispersed teams, balancing competing priorities and delivering high-quality outputs to agreed timeframes.

**Personal Attributes**

- Sound judgement, initiative, professionalism and integrity, with high levels of cultural awareness and commitment to safeguarding, inclusion, ethical practice and respectful engagement.

title: Project Quality, Reporting and Implementation Advisor
body:
**Country Programme:** Angola

**Contract Length:** 1 year, with the possibility of extension

**Base**: Luanda, Angola

**Starting date:** upon agreement

**Line Manager:** Country Director for Angola

**People in Need** (PIN) is a Czech-based international non-governmental organization (NGO) that has provided humanitarian and development assistance across more than 20 countries since 1992. Today, PIN stands as one of the largest organizations of its kind in Central and Eastern Europe, supporting vulnerable communities in Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Eastern Europe. PIN empowers civil society, advocates for human rights, and promotes social inclusion both at home and abroad.

**About the Angola Programme of People in Need:**

**PIN has been in Angola since 2006**, initially through education projects and subsequently expanding its programming across agriculture and livelihoods, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), community health and nutrition, gender, civil society strengthening, child protection and human rights. Over the years, PIN has worked across several provinces, including Bié, Huambo, Huíla, Namibe, Luanda, Uíge, Moxico and Kwanza Sul. Today, PIN’s work in Angola combines longer-term development and resilience building with support to communities affected by climate-related and other shocks, with particular expertise in climate-resilient livelihoods, WASH, nutrition, civil society strengthening and inclusive governance.

**PARS Programme**

PIN is the executing entity for the **PARS Angola project**, "**Promoting climate adaptation and resilience through innovation and entrepreneurship for green jobs in Angola**". A **five-year project** funded by the **Global Environement Fund (GEF)** and iimplemented in partnership with the **Angolan Ministry of Environment** and **UNIDO**. The project is part of the six-country GEN-funded PARS programme and aims to reduce climate vulnerability and strenghten the resilience of communities in Angola´s southern and coastal provinces by promoting innovation, technology transfer and private-sector-led adaptation solutions through support of Angolan MSMEs.

## **About the role:**

The Project Quality, Reporting and Implementation Advisor supports the effective and high-quality implementation of the **PARS Angola – Promoting climate adaptation and resilience through innovation and entrepreneurship for green jobs in Angola** project implemented by People in Need (PIN) in partnership with the Ministry of Environment of Angola and UN Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO).

The position provides dedicated support to the PARS Angola Project Management Unit (PMU), with a particular focus on **project cycle management, planning, monitoring of implementation, donor reporting, documentation and compliance**, complemented by operational support required for timely project delivery.

The Advisor works closely with the Project Manager to ensure that activities, outputs, targets, budget, procurement and implementation milestones remain aligned; that implementation progress and risks are systematically tracked; and that reporting to UNIDO is timely, accurate, evidence-based and compliant with the Project Document, Implementing Partner Agreement, Terms of Reference and Operational Guidelines.

The position also helps maintain effective coordination between programme, MEAL, finance, procurement, logistics and other support functions involved in project implementation.

## **Main Duties & Responsibilities:** 

- **Project Cycle Management, Planning and Coordination**Support the PMU in the day-to-day coordination and follow-up of project implementation across all PARS Angola components.
    - Support preparation and regular updating of Annual Work Plans, reporting-period workplans, implementation schedules and other project management tools.
    - Maintain an integrated project implementation tracker covering activities, deliverables, indicators, procurement and other milestones, responsible persons and deadlines.
    - Regularly follow up with technical and support teams on agreed actions, deliverables and implementation deadlines; identify delays, bottlenecks or non-compliance with agreed processes; seek timely clarification and corrective action from responsible colleagues; and escalate unresolved or recurring issues to the Head of Programmes and/or Country Director, as appropriate.
    - Support the organization and preparation of regular internal project coordination and review meetings.
    - Support preparation for bi-weekly coordination meetings with UNIDO and monthly implementation reviews, including consolidation of information on implementation progress, budget execution, procurement and recruitment, safeguards, risks and upcoming priorities.
    - Support preparation and follow-up of Project Steering Committee meetings, including background documents, presentations, minutes and agreed actions.
    - Support coordination across programme, MEAL, Finance, Procurement/Logistics and other relevant functions to ensure that implementation remains aligned with approved workplans and project requirements.
- **Reporting and Documentation**
    - Coordinate the internal process for preparation of project reports and ensure that inputs are requested, received and consolidated according to agreed internal deadlines.
    - Draft and/or consolidate technical sections of the **Kick-off Report, interim and annual technical progress reports, Project Implementation Reports (PIRs), final report and other reports required by UNIDO and GEF**.
    - Work closely with MEAL colleagues to ensure that reported results are supported by up-to-date indicator data, monitoring evidence and appropriate means of verification.
    - Work closely with Finance to ensure consistency between narrative reporting, implementation progress, expenditure and financial reporting.
    - Verify that reports clearly describe progress against outputs, activities, indicators and targets and adequately explain delays, challenges, risks and corrective measures.
    - Coordinate internal review and quality assurance of reports before submission to UNIDO.
    - Maintain a structured repository of project achievements, lessons learned, case studies and other evidence that can feed into reporting and knowledge products.
- **Monitoring, Quality and Adaptive Management**
    - Support regular monitoring of implementation against the Project Results Framework, Annual Work Plan, milestones and contractual commitments.
    - Work with the MEAL team and technical staff to ensure that project monitoring data and supporting evidence are collected and available for management and reporting purposes.
    - Support the PMU in monitoring project risks and maintaining an up-to-date Project Risk Register.
    - Track agreed risk mitigation and corrective measures, follow up with responsible colleagues on their implementation, and escalate overdue or insufficiently addressed actions where they may affect project results, compliance, budget execution or contractual commitments.
    - Maintain a clear escalation pathway for significant or recurring implementation issues, including delays, compliance gaps, unresolved risks and deviations from approved workplans or project requirements. Ensure that such issues are documented, brought to the attention of the appropriate decision-maker in a timely manner, and followed up until a decision or corrective action is agreed.
- **Operational and Implementation Support**
    - Provide practical support to the PMU and technical teams in translating approved workplans into concrete implementation steps and timelines.
    - Coordinate with Procurement/Logistics and programme teams to follow the status of procurement processes required for planned activities and flag potential delays.
    - Support preparation and updating of procurement planning information required for Annual Work Plans and implementation reviews, while respecting the responsibilities of dedicated Finance and Procurement staff.
    - Support preparation of ToRs, scopes of work and other documentation for consultants, service providers and technical assignments.
- **Procurement Planning and Technical Procurement Support**
    - Support the preparation of procurement documentation required for project implementation, particularly for consultant recruitments, technical service contracts, studies, assessments and other specialized assignments.
    - Coordinate the provision of technical inputs required for procurement processes and ensure that Terms of Reference (ToRs), scopes of work, technical specifications and expected deliverables are prepared in a timely and high-quality manner.
    - Support programme and technical teams in the development and review of tender documentation and procurement packages in line with project requirements and PIN procedures.
    - Follow up with responsible colleagues to ensure that procurement processes are initiated sufficiently in advance and remain aligned with implementation timelines and workplans.
    - Participate in the technical evaluation of bids, proposals and consultant applications where relevant and support the documentation of evaluation processes.
    - Coordinate with Procurement/Logistics colleagues to monitor the status of key procurements and help address bottlenecks that may affect project implementation.
    - Ensure that procurement-related documentation and decisions are properly documented and accessible for project management, reporting and audit purposes.
- **Knowledge Management, Communication and Learning**
    - Support systematic documentation of project results, lessons learned, good practices and implementation experiences.
    - Contribute to preparation of project presentations, briefs, case studies and other knowledge products.
    - Support exchange of relevant information and learning with the PARS Global Coordination Project and other PARS country projects.

## **Main requirements:** 

- At least **5 years of relevant professional experience** in project/programme management, reporting, programme quality, MEAL or a related area; experience with large institutional donor-funded projects is strongly preferred.
- Strong command of **English and Portuguese**, both written and spoken
- Demonstrated experience in donor reporting and preparation of high-quality narrative reports.
- Good understanding of project cycle management, work planning, monitoring and risk management.
- Experience coordinating inputs from programme, MEAL, finance, procurement and other functions is an advantage.
- Experience with UN agencies, GEF-funded programmes or other complex institutional donors would be a strong advantage.
- Experience in climate adaptation, private-sector/MSME development, green entrepreneurship or related programming is desirable but not essential.
- Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple deadlines and streams of information simultaneously.
- Excellent analytical, drafting and editing skills.
- Advanced user of MS Office, particularly Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
- Willingness to travel within Angola as required.

## **We offer:** 

- Working environment in a well-established humanitarian organization;
- *Salary & Benefits*: Salary based on PIN’s salary scale and HR policies; expected salary range between 2900 - 3300 EUR super gross (based on experience).
- Additional allowances include: 
    - Monthly Subsistence Allowance of 1440 EUR;
    - Accommodation provided by PIN/Monthly Housing Allowance;
    - *Time off and Rest:*
    - 25 days of holiday annually;
    - 10 sick days
- *Travel benefits:*
    - Reimbursement of travel expenses with travel to the country of residence once every 6 months of work;
    - Reimbursement of costs of visas and vaccinations; assistance with the visa application procedure;
    - Reimbursement for the medical check-up before and after the deployment;
    - Travel health insurance covering medical care, incl. the repatriation;
    - *Health and Well-being:*
    - 24/7 Medical Support available online;
    - Free psychological consultations available online;
    - *Professional Development:* Free access to e-learning platforms and PIN Learning Hub; PIN’s global Induction Training, and tailored capacity-building opportunities

title: Manager - Health Supply Chain Transformation (Kenya Nationals Only)
body:
**Hiring Unit**:[ inSupply Health](https://insupplyhealth.com/)

**Organization Overview:**

[**inSupply Health**](https://insupplyhealth.com/insupply-overview/) is an East African health advisory firm that designs people-centered, scalable, sustainable supply chain solutions. We focus on optimizing data visibility and use, workforce development, and continuous performance improvement. inSupply operates as a social enterprise, aiming to achieve business sustainability while advancing our social mission. We aim to transition short-term supply chain fixes into sustainable solutions that transcend specific projects or funding streams. Our work focuses on democratizing access to quality, affordable, and context-specific supply chain learning and innovations so that local and regional supply chain actors can improve the performance and efficiency of their supply chains and health systems, towards better health outcomes.

inSupply Health is headquartered in Nairobi, with offices in Dar es Salaam and across East Africa, and is affiliated with JSI Research & Training Institute, Inc. (JSI). We collaborate closely with public and private-sector clients to design optimized, responsive, and resilient supply chain systems. Our dynamic team of local consultants delivers critical services supporting essential health products, adapting proven methodologies to local contexts for long-term impact. This is a hands-on management leadership role that requires strong experience in public health systems, digital health implementation, and data-to-decision approaches in low-resource settings.

**Job Summary**

inSupply Health is seeking an experienced and dynamic **Manager –Health Supply Chain Transformation** to lead and support the design and implementation of innovative health supply chain interventions across our operating countries.

The Manager will work closely with Ministries of Health, government agencies, private-sector clients, NGOs, donors and other partners to identify supply chain challenges and co-design practical, sustainable solutions that improve the efficiency, effectiveness and resilience of health supply chains.

The role will provide technical and functional leadership to Analysts and Senior Analysts working across health supply chain projects, while providing coaching, mentorship and quality assurance to ensure high-quality technical delivery. The successful candidate will also contribute to business development by identifying new opportunities, developing technical approaches and supporting proposals and other business development activities.

**Responsibilities:**

**1. Project Implementation and Coordination:**

Manage in-country project implementation, identify supply chain challenges, and co-design solutions with MOH, clients, and other stakeholders to enhance supply chain performance, ensuring appropriate use of resources to deliver quality outcomes and milestones in a timely, cost-effective, and responsive manner.

**2. Functional Leadership, Team Development and Technical Quality Assurance:**

Provide functional and technical leadership to Analysts and Senior Analysts working across projects, coordinate domain inputs, and provide coaching, mentorship and guidance to maintain high standards of technical delivery. Support staff performance, career development and capability building, and provide technical quality assurance at key project milestones to ensure that work meets inSupply Health's standards and client expectations.

**3. Data Utilization and Analysis:**

Lead data-driven problem-solving initiatives, analyse qualitative and quantitative data, and present findings to diverse audiences to inform supply chain improvements and project decision-making. Implement IMPACT team models and frameworks in data review meetings and promote the use of evidence and insights to support adaptive management and improved supply chain performance.

**4. Stakeholder and Client Engagement:**

Build and maintain effective relationships with Ministries of Health, government institutions, NGOs, donors, clients and other partners to promote data utilisation and evidence-based decision-making. Advocate for the adoption of innovative and sustainable approaches to improve supply chain performance and efficiency, and support the Project Director/Lead and Project Manager in managing significant client issues and escalations.

**5. Innovation and Continuous Improvement:**

Foster a culture of innovation and continuous improvement, integrating human-centred design, quality improvement and other appropriate methodologies to strengthen tools, approaches and strategies.

- Identify opportunities for digitalisation, including transitioning to digitised LMIS and dashboards.
- Explore advanced quantification tools and health products and technologies distribution models.
- Support integration with national health supply chains.
- Surface potential innovations and advanced technical insights for consideration by the PMU.

**6. Business Development and Growth:**

Lead in scouting for new projects and business opportunities within the health supply chain and health systems transformation space, contributing to responses to RFPs, proposals, concept notes and other business development activities. Develop technical approaches and solutions for new opportunities, build relationships with potential clients and partners, and identify opportunities to expand existing engagements and contribute to inSupply Health's growth and reputation.

**7. Performance Monitoring and Adaptive Learning:**

Oversee and support data collection, regular data review and analysis of project and programme monitoring indicators, facilitating adaptive learning sessions and evidence-based decision-making. When assigned as Project Manager, monitor overall project implementation progress, delivery risks, budget performance and achievement of results, ensuring timely corrective actions and escalation where required.

**8. Knowledge Management and Technical Thought Leadership:**

Capture, document and share technical insights, lessons learned, good practices and innovations across projects. Contribute to the development of technical tools, methodologies, reports, knowledge products and presentations that strengthen the Supply Chain Transformation function and inSupply Health's technical reputation.

**9. Project Management:**

When assigned as Project Manager, the position will assume responsibility for day-to-day project delivery, coordination, performance and achievement of results. The role will also contribute to business development, stakeholder engagement, innovation and continuous improvement to strengthen the growth, impact and reputation of inSupply Health.

**Qualifications:**

- **A Bachelor's degree** in Pharmacy, Public Health, Healthcare Supply Chain or a related field. A **Master's degree** in a health-related field is preferred.
- At least 7 years of experience in global health or development, including at least 5 years of experience in health supply chain management.
- Demonstrated experience across a range of health supply chain programmes.
- Strong technical experience in areas such as:
    - Forecasting and supply planning
    - Health Supply chain assessments
    - Logistics Management Information Systems (LMIS)
    - Inventory management
    - Storage and distribution solutions
    - Health supply chain strengthening
- Experience working with Ministries of Health, NGOs, donors and other development partners.
- Relevant professional certification in supply chain management, project management or a related field, such as APICS CSCP or PMP, is preferred; membership in a relevant professional body is required where applicable
- Experience in social marketing, healthcare social enterprise, start-up or NGO health programmes is highly desirable.
- Demonstrated experience in project management, business development and/or client relationship management.
- Excellent oral and written communication, influencing, networking and relationship-building skills.

**What We Are Looking For**

- Passion for improving supply chains and health systems, with a strong understanding of market dynamics.
- Self-driven, creative, and flexible, with a focus on finding innovative solutions to complex problems.
- Outcome-oriented, with a proven track record in effective management and driving business development.
- Ability to work collaboratively while independently managing time and results, and to provide mentorship and coaching to team members.
- Experience negotiating and advocating with private- and public-sector clients for the uptake of new approaches and strategies.
- Awareness of private-sector trends and the ability to leverage this knowledge to support organisational success.
- Commitment to continuous learning and professional growth.
- Enthusiasm for actively contributing to inSupply Health's growth and reputation.

## **Why Join Us?**

At inSupply Health, you’ll work with a bold, collaborative team passionate about transforming health systems. You’ll lead flagship projects, co-create innovative solutions, and influence national and regional policies through evidence. We offer a flexible, learning-driven work environment with opportunities for professional growth and leadership.

title: Consultancy – Strategic Expert, Libya
body:
**DUTY STATION: Libya**

**Expected Start Date: ASAP**

**REPORTING TO: Regional Head of Programme — MENA**

## **BACKGROUND:**

Libya, serving as a transit, destination and influence hub, plays a central role in North Africa. Beyond internal political divisions and localised security tensions, the impact of potential tensions within the country extends across its national borders and could result in heightened protection risks and humanitarian needs.

Having said that, Geneva Call remained fully operational in Libya from 2019 until 2023 and since then Geneva Call has been in contact with key interlocutors and regularly monitoring the situation. Geneva Call’s programme was focused on engaging, in both in Tripoli and Benghazi, with the different governmental departments, namely with the ministries of defence and interior, as well as their associated civilian offices and supporting forces on the ground. Moreover, engagements were conducted with influential actors such as tribal and community leaders in selected areas.

In light of the evolving context and the emerging protection priorities on the ground, Geneva Call is aiming to conduct a strategic assessment exercise in Libya to further capitalize on its previous engagements with various state and non-state actors. Geneva Call is planning to explore opportunities for stronger programming and deeper engagement with key stakeholders in Libya, by focusing on the factors that may trigger or fuel violent extremism, radicalisation and disruptions to social cohesion and comprehension by key actors of humanitarian norms, paying particular attention to both internal and cross-border dynamics.

For this purpose, Geneva Call is seeking to contract a strategic expert on a consultancy basis to support this assessment and deliver on the sub-objectives detailed below.

## **OBJECTIVES**

Under the direct supervision of the Regional Head of Programme – MENA, the main objectives of the assignment to be conducted by the Libya Strategic Expert are the following:

- Develop comprehensive contextual analysis on political, security and social dynamics relevant to current dynamics in Libya and potential conflict links and spillover from neighbouring countries (Sahel and Sudan). This will include regional and cross-regional external factors that exacerbate extremism.
- Identify and map out different state and other stakeholders’ relevant promotion of protection, social cohesion and prevention of extremism on the ground.
- Analyse the Protection of Civilians (PoC) landscape in Libya, identifying emerging **protection issues, emerging risks, response gaps and priority geographical areas** to inform future programming.
- Identify strategic and programmatic opportunities directly and through partners, potential entry points and areas for engagement to inform future interventions in Libya, with a focus on returns, reintegration, protection of social cohesion, and prevention of violent extremism.

## **METHODS AND DELIVERABLES**

The consultancy will run for a period of **six weeks (30 days)** staring as soon as possible. The consultant is expected to adopt mixed-methods approach combining desk research with field-level engagement and will deliver:

- Inception report and work plan outlining the proposed methodology, assessment questions, scope, key activities and approach to field-level engagement and data collection.
- A comprehensive protection and strategic contextual analysis covering key protection risks, emerging trends, geographical hotspots, response gaps and relevant stakeholders.
- Final report presenting key findings, conflict analysis, strategic opportunities and recommendations.
- An executive summary (max 10 pages) summarizing key findings and recommendations for senior management, relevant interlocutors, and donors;
- A PowerPoint presentation summarizing the key findings and recommendations.

**Management of the consultancy**

- The consultant will report to the Regional Head of Programme – MENA who will provide the necessary guidance and support in the completion of agreed outcomes.
- The payment of the consultancy will be based on outcomes and will be settled in two tranches:
- Inception report and approved work plan (20%)
- Delivery of consultancy report by the end of the consultancy (80%)
- The total time allocated for the delivery of these outcomes should not exceed six weeks.

## **Qualifications, Skills and Experience**

The selected consultant must meet the following criteria:

- Hold a master’s degree, PhD or equivalent work experience, in social sciences, political science, conflict resolution or any other related field that applies to the assessment.
- Deep understanding of conflict analysis methodologies (including conflict systems mapping, actors’ analysis), and the specific context of Libya. This expertise enables him/her to guide the team in aligning the assessment with the country’s unique challenges and priorities.
- Demonstrated track record in delivery of similar actions research consultancies in related thematic areas and in similar contexts.
- Proven track record of working in Libya and maintained relevant networks in country as well as the wider region of MENA.
- Excellent writing and communication skills in Arabic and English.

## **EXPRESSION OF INTEREST**

Interested and qualified consultants **must submit their application**, no later than **12.10.2026** with the following in one pdf document:

- An updated curriculum vitae highlighting relevant professional experience and qualifications for this consultancy.
- Three- page technical proposal document outlining their proposed approach to the assessment, methodological approach and proposed timeline, with reference to the research scope outlined in the ToR. Additionally, candidate is expected to provide examples of previous work preferably related to similar topic.
- A financial proposal with a detailed budget
- Full contact information for at least two recent clients as references, if possible.

title: Stagiaire Grands Donateurs - H/F - Paris
body:
**PRÉSENTATION ALIMA**

**L’ESPRIT ALIMA :** La raison d’être d’ALIMA est de sauver des vies et de soigner les populations les plus vulnérables, sans aucune discrimination identitaire, religieuse ou politique, à travers des actions basées sur la proximité, l’innovation et l’alliance d’organisations et d’individus. Nous agissons avec humanisme, impartialité et dans le respect de l’éthique médicale universelle. Pour accéder aux patients, nous nous engageons à intervenir de façon neutre et indépendante.

**LES VALEURS et PRINCIPES de notre action, inscrits au sein de notre CHARTE :**

1\. Le patient d’abord

2\. Révolutionner la médecine humanitaire

3\. Responsabilité et liberté

4\. Améliorer la qualité de nos actions

5\. Faire confiance

6\. L’intelligence collective

7\. La responsabilité environnementale

ALIMA promeut et défend les principes des droits humains fondamentaux. ALIMA a une approche de tolérance zéro envers les personnes coupables d’actes de violences sexistes et sexuelles ainsi qu’envers l’inaction face à des faits de violence supposée ou avérée. La protection des personnes bénéficiant et impactées par notre intervention est notre priorité absolue dans tout ce que nous faisons. Toute personne collaborant avec ALIMA s’engage à :

● Respecter la charte, le code de conduite, les politiques institutionnelles incluant la politique de protection contre les abus de pouvoir et les violences sexistes et sexuelles, la politique de prévention de la corruption et de la fraude ;

● Signaler toute violation aux politiques, documents, cadre et procédure à un supérieur, à un référent.

**SOIGNER - INNOVER – ENSEMBLE :** Depuis sa création en 2009, ALIMA a soigné plus de 13 millions de patients dans 15 pays, et déploie aujourd’hui ses opérations dans 12 pays d’Afrique et Haïti. En 2022, nous avons développé 62 projets de réponse médicale humanitaire pour répondre aux besoins de populations touchées par les conflits, les épidémies et l’extrême pauvreté. L’ensemble de ces projets se font en appui aux autorités sanitaires nationales à travers près de 511 structures de santé. Nous travaillons en partenariat, notamment avec des ONGs locales, dès que cela est possible afin de nous assurer que nos patients bénéficient de l’expertise, que ce soit au niveau de leur pays ou du reste du monde. Par ailleurs, pour améliorer la réponse humanitaire, nous menons des projets de recherches opérationnelles et cliniques, particulièrement pour lutter contre la malnutrition et les fièvres hémorragiques virales.

**NOS THÉMATIQUES PROJET :** Malnutrition, Santé sexuelle et reproductive incluant les violences basées sur le genre, Santé Primaire et secondaire, Pédiatrie, Paludisme, Épidémies (Fièvres hémorragiques, méningite, Choléra, Rougeole, Dengue, COVID-19).

**L'ÉQUIPE ALIMA :** plus de 2000 personnes œuvrent actuellement pour ALIMA. Les équipes terrain, au plus proche des patients, reçoivent leur support des équipes de coordination, généralement basées en capitale des pays d’intervention. Celles-ci reçoivent le support des 4 équipes desk et de l’équipe du service urgences et ouvertures basées au siège opérationnel de Dakar, Sénégal. Les équipes de Paris et New-York travaillent activement à la collecte de fonds ainsi qu’à la représentation d’ALIMA. Le reste de la Galaxie ALIMA comprend des individus et des équipes partenaires qui travaillent pour le compte d’autres organisations telles que les ONGs médicales BEFEN, ALERTE Santé, SOS Médecins / KEOOGO, AMCP, les organismes de recherche PACCI, INSERM, les Universités de Bordeaux ou de Copenhague, l’ONG Solidarités International et bien d’autres.

**NOS PAYS D’INTERVENTIONS :** Mali, Burkina Faso, République Centrafricaine, Nigeria, Niger, Tchad, République Démocratique du Congo, Cameroun, Guinée, Soudan, Mauritanie, Éthiopie, Haïti.

**PROTECTION DES BÉNÉFICIAIRES ET DES MEMBRES DE LA COMMUNAUTÉ**

Niveau 3: Dans le cadre de ses fonctions, le ou la titulaire du poste sera amené·e à visiter les programmes et être en contact avec des enfants ou/et des adultes vulnérables. Par conséquent, la vérification du casier judiciaire ou la présentation d'un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs sera nécessaire. Dans les situations où l’impossibilité de fournir un casier judiciaire ou un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs est constatée, une déclaration sur l’honneur sera demandée.

CONTEXTE

ALIMA souhaite poursuivre son action de mobilisation de ressources externes pour assurer son développement. À ce titre, l’ONG recrute un.e stagiaire en philanthropie et grands donateurs. Basé.e à Paris au sein de l’équipe grands donateurs, vous contribuerez au développement des ressources privées d’ALIMA en appuyant les activités de prospection, de suivi des donateurs et d’organisation, des actions de collecte. Ce stage vous permettra d’acquérir une vision complète des enjeux de la

philanthropie au sein d’une ONG médicale internationale.

MISSIONS

Rattaché.e à l’équipe Grands donateurs et partenariats au bureau de Paris (20e arrondissement),

vous assistez le/la Chargé.e de Relations Grands Donateurs dans le déploiement de la stratégie de levée de fonds auprès des grands donateurs notamment en France et éventuellement en Europe.

Il/elle :

● Réalise des recherches et analyses sur des prospects grands donateurs et réseaux

philanthropiques

● Contribue à l’identification et à la qualification de nouveaux prospects en lien avec les priorités de développement du service et les réseaux du comité de campagne

● Prépare des fiches de briefing, notes de rendez-vous et supports destinés aux activités de prospection et de fidélisation

● Participe à la mise à jour et à la qualité des données dans les outils de suivi de la relation donateurs

● Contribue à la préparation des campagnes de collecte et des actions de communication destinées aux grands donateurs

● Participe à la préparation des rapports, bilans et supports de valorisation destinés aux donateurs

● Appuie l’organisation logistique des événements de prospection, de fidélisation et de collecte

## Expériences et Compétences

- Étudiant.e en Master 2 (université, IEP, école de commerce ou de communication) avec une spécialisation en solidarité internationale, management des ONG, Marketing/Communication ou gestion de projets.
- ● Une première expérience associative ou un premier stage dans le secteur de la solidarité internationale est un véritable atout.
- ● Maîtrise des outils bureautiques courants (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) ou de la suite Google
- (Docs, Sheets, Slides). L'aisance avec un CRM ou des outils graphiques (Canva) est appréciée.
- ● Sensibilité marquée pour l'action humanitaire et/ou la mission médicale.
- ● Excellentes capacités rédactionnelles
- ● Très bonnes capacités de recherche et d’analyse
- ● Capacité de synthèse
- ● Anglais niveau B2
- ● Rigueur, curiosité intellectuelle
- ● Excellent relationnel et esprit d'équipe développé

## Conditions

Type de contrat : Stage conventionné (Convention de stage obligatoire)

- Durée : 6 mois
- Lieu : Paris 20e arrondissement
- Gratification : Gratification légale en vigueur (environ 4,35 €/heure, soit 650 € à 700 € nets mensuels selon les mois)
- Avantages : Prise en charge à 50% des titres de transport (Navigo) + Tickets-restaurant

title: HR Assistant
body:
DEPARTMENT PURPOSE: The Human Resources department is responsible for people strategy; ensuring efficiency and effectiveness in delivery of Oxfam’s human resource operations, whilst ensuring consistency and transparency in line with OGB policies, procedures and systems.

  
TEAM PURPOSE: The HR team is responsible for providing quality HR services support to Oxfam’s Syria Program. Working with other members of the HR team, the post holder role will be responsible for contributing to the objectives and delivery of HR Function. The Country HR Manager provides matrix line management to all field location HR teams.  
Ensuring implementation of OGB HR approved policies, procedures and processes, compliance of HR minimum standards and delivery of agreed Key Performance Indicators.

  
JOB PURPOSE: Provides administrative support for HR and related projects, whilst coordinating and analysing information and trends related to staffing, organizational effectiveness, training and development, reward and benefits compensation.  
  
Establish, administer, and communicate sound policies and practices that treat employees with dignity and equality while maintaining compliance with applicable law, policy and regulation.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES (Technical, Leadership, People and Resource management)  
Induction:  
•Support HR Manager in scheduling induction for new joiners.  
•Monitor and ensure that induction meetings are done timely and induction checklist is updated, signed and filed in personal file.  
•Ensure file management is properly done, personal files and HR files are maintained and secured.  
•Manage and maintain staff leave, R&R, time sheets and attendance schedules.  
•Share joiner leavers list with security on regular basis.  
  
Recruitment, Contract Management:  
•Support recruitment for vacancies, including but not limited to, ensuring prompt long listing and short-listing; screening CV’s; preparing written tests, scheduling interviews; contacting candidates, and writing regrets when needed.  
•Ensure that all necessary and related documents for every recruitment is properly gathered and put in relevant file (requisition, job profile, short list, CVs, written tests, regret letters, recruitment summary).  
•Ensure that all employment contract templates are updated, in line with the local labour law and Oxfam’s policy.  
•Coordinate and facilitate all on boarding processes and have signed completed schedule filed for reference. This include ensure new staff undertake all mandatory courses. Welcome new and transferred employees ensuring that they have the tools and knowledge needed to perform their job properly and get engaged within the Organization, Assuring the proper arrangements of new staff equipment’s (ID, laptop, phone …Where applicable).  
•Responsible for the essential part of reference checks in coordination with Oxfam HR Accredited Referee and OGB Reference Team.  
•Support in the management and administration of volunteers’ contracts.

Medical:  
•Support in ensuring that employee medical records are up to date and that arrangements are facilitated if necessary for any medical treatment that is required.  
•Manage relations with medical service providers, monitors medical expenses and ensures medical staff records are handled and kept in a confidential manner.

GOLD:  
•Update medicals in GOLD and run GOLD reports for medicals.  
•Update GOLD completely, timely and accurately in absence of HR Officer.  
•Ensure GOLD reports are provided whenever needed.

Absence Management:  
•Ensure that absence (including annual leave and sick leave) is proactively managed.  
•Provide leaves record report to Managers on monthly basis.  
•Conduct regular quality control checks to ensure data accuracy.  
•Coordinate absence data across hubs.

Performance Management:  
•Provide support to HR Manager to collect objectives and performance reviews.  
•Support in creating awareness and understanding among current and new staff on the code of conduct and safeguarding.

Project support:  
•Supporting the HR Manager with key projects as required.  
•Ensuring all leavers complete exit interview, analyse trends and make recommendations to the HR manager.  
•Any other duties that may be reasonably required of the postholder.  
•Required to adhere to Oxfam’s principles and values as well as the promotion of gender justice and women's rights.  
•Understanding of and commitment to adhere to equity, diversity, gender, child safety and staff health and wellbeing principles.

  
EXPERIENCE, KNOWLEDGE & COMPETENCIES

Essential:  
•Self-Awareness  
•Systems Thinking  
•Enabling

In addition:  
•Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field.  
•Bachelor's degree holder Minimum of 2 years of experience in HR role in private or humanitarian sectors, or High secondary education 5 years of experience.  
This experience should include HR related roles within the preferably humanitarian or development sector, at either national or international levels.  
•Experience in data base and absence management.  
•Competency in use of relevant technology systems (MS Office suite, HRIS).  
•Well-developed interpersonal and team skills and proven ability to be flexible in demanding situations.  
•Commitment to humanitarian principles and action.  
•Commitment to Oxfam’s equal opportunity and gender policies.  
•Flexibility & adaptability with the ability to work under pressure and in insecure areas.  
•Proficiency in English and Arabic both written and verbal.  
•Flexibility and willingness to travel up to 75% within Syria as required.  
•Pleasant and courteous personality.  
•Efficient and organized.  
•Possesses initiative, patience, tact, and able to work with minimum supervision  
•Sympathy with the aims and objectives of Oxfam.

title: Program Director (Contractor Representative)
body:
This position is open for Indonesian nationals only. The Program Director leads the successful delivery of development programs, managing performance, risk, client relationships, and team capability to achieve strategic and operational outcomes. About DT Global Asia Pacific At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.

For more information, please see [www.dt-global.com](http://www.dt-global.com)

**The Role**

The Program Director oversees the implementation of development programs in Asia Pacific, ensuring effective management of contractual and financial performance and risk to support strong outcomes and contribute to DT Global’s performance and growth. They build strong client relationships to understand goals, facilitate program adaptability and ensure deliverables meet expectations. They ensure that program teams have the skills, experience and tools they need to deliver program outcomes. By aligning decisions with strategic priorities, addressing challenges proactively, and driving continuous improvement, they lead teams to enhance program quality and outcomes.

Click on the link or copy paste it to access the full Terms of Reference for this position: [https://tinyurl.com/programdirector-cr](https://tinyurl.com/programdirector-cr)

**Main Accountabilities**

**People & Leadership**

o Ensure the program has the leadership, skills, expertise and tools to achieve end of program outcomes and meet client and stakeholder expectations.

o Manage the Program Team Leader, fostering a collaborative environment for effective leadership. Provide support and intervention as required to address challenges.

o Foster collaboration between program and corporate teams and proactively promote company culture and values to ensure there are replicated by the program.

o Oversee program resourcing to ensure optimal performance and value, supporting or leading performance management when needed.

o Participate in recruiting senior program staff to meet strategic resourcing needs.

o Lead a team of corporate resources, offering support, mentoring, and capability building to ensure success and build succession.

**Contractual Program Management**

o Ensure all contractual requirements, obligations and deliverables in program Head Contracts are being met and effectively delivered.

o Lead the review of Head Contracts, Service Orders and amendments to identify and mitigate areas of risk and ensuring compliance with the corporate legal process.

• **Client Engagement**

o Maintain a collaborative relationship by understanding the client's goals to ensure the program remains adaptable to emerging opportunities and shifting priorities.

o Resolve client concerns promptly while aligning solutions with company values and objectives.

o Ensure program personnel maintain collaborative relationships with the client, counterpart agencies and stakeholders, stepping in to address challenges as needed.

**Development Effectiveness / Strategic Management**

o Oversee the strategic direction of the program, continuously monitoring project progress and client feedback. Consults with stakeholders to make strategic decisions to address anticipated implementation challenges.

o Assist the Team Leader with change management to realign the program’s strategic direction as required.

**Financial Management**

o Oversee and/ or manage the financial performance and profitability of the program, including monitoring margin variations, justifying any discrepancies.

o Oversee and/ or manage the accuracy and timeliness of forecasting, reporting and invoicing to our client, ensuring justification is provided for changes in project forecasts.

o Oversee the accuracy and maintenance of the project Lifetime Budget (LTB), Annual Corporate Budget and Cash Flow Forecasting, providing clear explanation for significant discrepancies; and provide approval of client invoices, project advance requests and project budgets and forecasts for corporate.

o Ensure client invoice sampling process is managed efficiently to minimise any disruption or delay to payment, including follow up with client for certification where delays occur.

o Active participation and oversight of response to financial audits, including accountability for the completion of any corrective actions identified.

o Be the key escalation point to address any financial concerns with the Client Activity Manager.

**Program Operations**

o Oversee program start-up activities, transition and mobilisation phases, and ensure effective handover and closure at project completion.

o Ensure head contract requirements are integrated into program operational manuals, personnel and partner agreements, and decision-making processes.

o Ensure due diligence is conducted, documented and monitored for all personnel, subcontractors, and grantees.

o Review and approve recruitment, procurement, subcontract and grant agreements in accordance with DT Global’s QF1-1 Level of Authority and all other DT Global processes and client policies.

**Risk, Compliance, Safeguards & Integrity**

o Ensure all program personnel and partners comply with DT Global’s Safeguarding and Integrity policies and procedures (including Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (SEAH), Child Protection, Environmental Protection, Modern Slavery, Fraud, Anti-Corruption, Anti-Bribery, Conflicts of

o Interest, sanctions screening, etc.) and all other DT Global policies, procedures and requirements.

o Identify, assess and mitigate program risks by facilitating risk management processes, implementing controls, escalating emerging risks.

o Report any actual or suspected policy breaches or incidents promptly (e.g. such as those related to Safeguards, Integrity, Security, HSE, HR, IT, Cybersecurity, Data, Privacy), support investigations and ensure corrective actions are documented and implemented.

o Maintain exemplary personal behaviour in interactions with children and vulnerable people and adhere to all DT Global policies to uphold the highest standards of compliance and integrity.

**Reporting**

o Oversee the timeliness and quality of all contractual reporting requirements and other deliverables to meet client standards.

o Provide internal reporting on project and commercial performance, key achievements, and risk.

**Business Development**

o Leverage client relationships, market/country intelligence, and networks to identify and recommend new business opportunities that align with DT Global’s strategic goals.

o Contribute to proposal writing and/ or the identification of skilled candidates for named positions in proposals as needed.

**Quality Management**

o Implement DT Global Asia Pacific’s Quality Management System, ensuring compliance and suggesting improvements.

o Participate in audits and ensure timely implementation and documentation of corrective actions and improvements.

**HSE & Security**

o Ensure the program, including its personnel and partners operate in compliance with DT Global’s HSE and Security policies and procedures, legislation, and client contracts.

o Prepare and maintain up to date program HSE and security management plans and risk registers / assessments.

o Ensure all program staff are actively involved in risk identification and hazard reporting process.

o Take reasonable care of your own and others health and safety, seeking assistance when needed.

o Adhere to all other HSE instructions and responsibilities outlined in the HSE management system documentation.

**Knowledge, Skills, Experience and Qualifications**

• Bachelor's degree in International Development, Business Administration, Law, or a related field.

• Demonstrated experience managing complex development programs, including deliverables, timelines, budgets, and stakeholder engagement.

• Strong understanding of contract management, financial management, and donor-funded program requirements.

• Proven leadership experience, including managing diverse and geographically dispersed teams.

• Excellent stakeholder management, communication, and influencing skills, with the ability to build effective relationships across sectors.

• Strong strategic planning, program oversight, and problem-solving capabilities.

• Excellent report writing, editing, and presentation skills.

• Demonstrated understanding of development sector priorities, socio-political contexts, and cross-cultural environments.

• Commitment to ethical conduct, integrity, sustainability, equity, and Do No Harm principles.

• Knowledge of donor policies, frameworks, and relevant thematic areas is desirable.

• Successful candidates must provide certified qualifications, complete criminal record checks, and undergo satisfactory reference checks.

title: COORDINATEUR.ICE PAIE ET ADMINISTRATION DU PERSONNEL TERRAIN (HOMERE)
body:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Sous la supervision de la Responsable de Service RH Régionales, votre rôle sera d'apporter un support aux RH des 21 pays d'intervention afin d'assurer le bon déroulement du processus de paie (logiciel Homère) et aux révisions de la rémunération, ainsi qu'un support au pilotage et au suivi des Ressources Humaines nationales.  
Plus précisément, vos missions seront les suivantes :  
Appuyer au déploiement et à la révision des processus de paie et rémunération en collaboration avec l'équipe RH Régionales et les Coordinateurs ou Coordinatrices Fonctionnelles SIRHAccompagner les Responsables RH dans la formalisation de leurs demandes de paramétrages du SIRH  
Appuyer les RH des Bureaux Pays à la formalisation de leur processus de paie et à son suivi  
Participer à l'appui technique sur aux outils d'administration à destination des utilisateurs dans les pays d'intervention en lien avec l'équipe SIRH  
Apporter un support au pilotage et au suivi des Ressources Humaines nationalesAppuyer à la création et la mise à jour des cadrages d'administration du personnel national et à leur dissémination  
Appuyer à la mise à jour des outils d'administration du personnel  
Appuyer le suivi des audits siège  
Assurer le contrôle interne sur la paie, la gestion administrative du personnel et la mise en oeuvre des politiques de rémunération  
Appuyer à la définition des indicateurs RH

  
Profile :

 Vous êtes titulaire d'un diplôme supérieur en Ressources Humaines (RH) et/ou en paie, vous une avez une solide expérience RH au sein d'une ONG international (siège ou terrain).  
Autonome et force de proposition, vous avez une bonne connaissance de la réglementation de la paie, des charges sociales et des méthodes de calcul des cotisations sociales et fiscales. Vous avez une appétence pour les chiffres, les fonctions avancées d'Excel et vous pouvez vous appuyer sur vos connaissances en paramétrage de paie.  
Vous êtes reconnu.e pour vos capacités à identifier, analyser les problématiques RH et formuler à vos interlocuteur·rice·s des recommandations, des alertes et/ou trouver des solutions.  
Doté·e d'un excellent relationnel, vous êtes capable de vous adapter aux problématiques nationales et internationales du secteur humanitaire. Vous êtes également capable d'animer une séquence de formation.  
Une expérience dans l'utilisation du logiciel Homère et une connaissance du logiciel NIBELIS (logiciel de paie) sont de vrais atouts.  
Vous maîtrisez le français et l'anglais à l'oral comme à l'écrit.  
Une expérience ACF est un atout.  
  
Conditions d'emploi  
Statut:Cadre Intégré - CDD de 4 mois - Temps plein  
Lieu: Montreuil (Seine-Saint-Denis)  
Rémunération :De 46K à 55Keuros bruts annuels sur 13 mois selon expérience  
Avantages:25 jours par an de CP et 21 jours de RTT  
Couverture santé, prévoyance : Prise en charge à 80% par ACF

Prise en charge à 60% par l'association pour une valeur de 8euros  
Ouvres sociales du CSE (chèques cadeaux, remboursement activités culturelles, ...)

title: Various Countries - Head of Programmes
Program Lead, Ebola Response
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**BACKGROUND:**

Responding to the world’s worst humanitarian crises in a great variety of roles, the International Rescue Committee’s staff is a force for humanity and hope. If you’re skilled and passionate, we would like to add your energy to ours.

Through its Emergency Unit (EmU), the IRC is one of the world’s largest humanitarian agencies, leading rapid emergency responses that provide life-saving assistance, early recovery, and stabilization support to people affected by conflict, displacement, natural disasters, and complex emergencies across multiple contexts worldwide. We are committed to innovation, agility, and strong partnerships to deliver timely and effective humanitarian action.

Active in public health, education in emergencies, cash and basic needs and protection and promotion of rights, we assist people from harm to home. The IRC recognizes that people affected by crisis and the actors closest to them are best placed, have the right, and should have the power and resources to respond and drive lasting change. We commit to increasing the share of funding channeled to local actors in emergencies, ask ‘Why not partner?’ whenever we plan programming, and partner as equals.

**CONTEXT:**

The Ministry of Public Health of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) declared the country's 17th Ebola outbreak on May 15, 2026, following laboratory confirmation of Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) in Ituri Province. On May 17, 2026, WHO declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC), and it has since become the largest Ebola outbreak ever reported in DRC and the fastest-expanding on record. The outbreak is unfolding in a highly complex humanitarian and security context marked by chronic insecurity, armed group activity, repeated population displacement, and high levels of cross-border movement, particularly with Uganda and South Sudan.

The IRC is supporting containment of the outbreak in Ituri and North Kivu. IRC's primary focus is to support existing primary health care (PHC) facilities to ensure safe continuity of services, strengthen infection prevention and control (IPC) practices and infrastructure, raise community awareness of behaviors that limit further spread, and reinforce the protective environment, including through MHPSS support.

**JOB OVERVIEW:**

The position of **Program Lead, Ebola Response** (PL) is a member of the Ebola Response Senior Management Team and is integral to the successful implementation of IRC's programs in the affected provinces. Working under the direction of the Ebola Response Director, the PL will be responsible for overall leadership in the design, implementation, and management of the Ebola Response’s programs to address clients’ needs and priorities. She/he will be responsible for providing strategic direction of programs, conceptualizing and promoting innovations, and continuing to deepen the impact of IRC’s programs on the ground.

The PL assists the Ebola Response Director in the integrated planning and implementation of activities crucial to the success of local programs. This includes internal and external coordination and stakeholder engagement, including with donors, government and non-government partners, and IRC technical and regional support teams; overseeing multi-sector project design and implementation; managing sector teams to propose, coordinate, and deliver quality programs aligned with strategic priorities and beneficiary needs; and managing strategic funding opportunity tracking, partnering and pre-positioning decisions.

**MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:**

***Program Strategy, Design and Fundraising***

- Lead the operationalization of IRC's current Ebola Response strategy and actively engage in strategic planning processes to shape the response's longer-term direction.
- Perform regular analysis of the outbreak and ensure IRC's strategy and operational presence is responsive to those needs and highly mobile program models.
- Work closely with Coordinators and HQ-based Emergency Unit and Technical Unit staff to ensure that project design reflects IRC's program quality standards and adheres to industry best practices.
- Lead efforts to achieve sustainable program growth, proactively identifying opportunities for new programming initiatives and placing particular emphasis on securing multi-year funding to sustain them.
- Provide leadership and strategic support to program and grants teams as they develop competitive, evidence-based, and cost-effective funding applications.
- Provide guidance, strategies, and tools to ensure that program choices are grounded in the findings of needs assessments (drawing on both primary and secondary data), rigorous analysis, meaningful input from affected communities, a thorough understanding of context, technical best practices, and operational viability.
- Formulate integrated program initiatives that allow technical sectors to complement one another, while promoting the mainstreaming of protection principles and gender-responsive approaches throughout programming.

***Program Management — Implementation, Monitoring and Evaluation***

- Provide overall leadership of IRC's Ebola Response program portfolio, ensuring strategic coherence, well-managed growth, and full compliance with IRC and donor regulations.
- Build the capacity of program team members, both individually and as a team.
- Work with Program Coordinators and the Operations team to develop and adapt detailed, realistic, and feasible implementation plans.
- Collaborate with the Senior Management Team to uphold management, compliance, and performance standards, and to maintain effective systems for budget, knowledge, and risk management.
- Support program staff in capturing, documenting, and disseminating lessons learned and best practices, feeding them into future project design.
- Work with program staff to develop robust monitoring and evaluation (M&E) plans, including methodologies and tools that strengthen data collection, analysis, and reporting quality.
- Review M&E and accountability data with program staff to identify and address gaps in operational performance.
- Champion IRC's "partner first" approach, building strategic, respectful, and empowering relationships with local organizations, and ensuring partners are actively engaged in decision-making, program design, and service delivery, positioning IRC as a partner of choice.
- Ensure partnership management is high-quality, accountable, and collaborative, including oversight of partner-led delivery, adaptive technical support, and consistent application of IRC's partnership framework and principles.

**Grants Management**

- Provide strategic leadership in developing and executing a comprehensive funding strategy: expanding and strengthening the donor base, driving excellence in grants management and compliance, strengthening program and grants information systems, and contributing to high-quality proposals and reporting.
- Oversee internal and external reporting in coordination with the Ebola Response Director across programs and finance, ensuring reports are well-written, timely, and meet donor, IRC, and partner requirements; conduct thorough review of all external reports compiled by the Grants Coordinator.
- Ensure Program Coordinators conduct routine monitoring visits to implementation sites to verify donor compliance and program quality.
- Work with Program Coordinators and the Grants and Finance teams to maintain sound budget management, expense control, and timely contractual documentation.
- Support the Grants Coordinator in leading Grant Opening, Monitoring and Closing Meetings with relevant departments, ensuring these occur on schedule, and that programming staff are well equipped to manage project budgets.
- Ensure Program Coordinators review Budget vs. Actual reports regularly, and provide the leadership needed for effective monthly grant review meetings.
- Mitigate financial risk by working with the Finance Department to ensure programming staff fully understand the financial and administrative processes involved across project budget cycles.
- Integrate partnership considerations into program design and Go/No-Go funding decisions, engaging partners proactively throughout program and project development.

**External Representation and Advocacy**

- Maintain a strong working knowledge of IRC's programming in the epicenter zones to represent IRC credibly in coordination forums and with implementing partners, authorities, and donors.
- Support the Ebola Response Director in cultivating donor relationships, including donor visits and the development of targeted advocacy.
- Build and sustain strong partnerships with implementing organizations through regular communication, cooperation, and joint decision-making where appropriate.
- Serve as the focal point for program-related communication between IRC's regional and global country programs.
- Identify and track funding opportunities in collaboration with technical teams.
- Guide programmatic input into advocacy and communications efforts, both in-country and globally.

**Staff Management and Development**

- Supervise Program Coordinators and program staff, setting clear expectations and objectives, providing proactive wellbeing support, and delivering timely, constructive feedback.
- Foster an inclusive team culture centered on achieving individual and team results, grounded in mutual respect, inclusion, trust, active listening, ownership, learning, accountability, and openness.
- Apply IRC's performance management system consistently, providing regular, thoughtful coaching, feedback, and professional development to direct reports, and ensuring they do the same for their own teams.
- Strengthen programming staff's project management skills and ensure new capabilities are applied on the job.
- Lead recruitment, hiring, and development of high-performing staff, preparing them for greater responsibility.
- Provide leadership to ensure successful rollout of and adherence to IRC's Global People and Culture Operating Policies and Procedures.
- Hold regular, high-quality 1:1s with each direct report (at least biweekly) balancing interpersonal connection with work priorities.
- Model and reinforce healthy work-life balance practices to support staff well-being.

**KEY WORKING RELATIONSHIPS**

- **Position Reports to:** Ebola Response Director
- **Position directly supervises:** Ebola Response Program Coordinators (5)
