title: Housing Specialist
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future

**Job Overview:** The UHP Housing Specialist secures and coordinates the furnishing of safe, sanitary, and affordable housing for newly arriving humanitarian parolees and refugees and provides related logistical support. This role will work with staff, clients, and community partners to stabilize humanitarian parolees/refugee and client households by connecting them with long-term resources for low-income and designated affordable housing opportunities. In coordination with the UHP Team, the UHP Housing Specialist will be responsible for locating housing for UHP clients and other vulnerable populations. The UHP Housing Specialist also participates, as required, in program planning and service developments through teams, committees and work groups. The UHP Housing Specialist operates under moderate supervision with latitude for the use of independent judgment and initiative.  
  
***This position has an end date of September, 30, 2027.***

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Identify and secure safe, sanitary, and affordable housing for newly arriving refugees in compliance with established program requirements.
- Conduct ongoing outreach to current and potential landlords and property managers, building strong working relationships with the goal of increasing access to housing for refugee families and to coordinate client home repair requests as needed. Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations to support a positive resettlement experience.
- Coordinate logistics of housing set-ups including ordering furniture and supplies and arranging delivery, arranging utility hook-ups, facilitating lease signings and renewals, arranging payments, and conducting home safety inspections.
- Implement a high-quality procurement protocol including researching potential new vendors, following appropriate financial and purchasing procedures, and maintaining required documentation.
- Deliver orientations to clients independently or in collaboration with housing caseworkers; may support other pre- and post-arrival activities such as airport pick-ups.
- Satisfy recordkeeping requirements.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of support staff, volunteers, and interns.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

- Bachelor’s degree
- Minimum of 1 year of housing related professional experience required
- Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations preferred

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment
- Proven ability to contribute both independently and as a key team member
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively
- Superb organization, planning, and logistical skills
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product
- Ability to regularly lift ~50 lbs
- Fluent in English, both spoken and written; proficiency in Ukrainian and/or Russian language(s) spoken by IRC’s clients is preferred.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research and problem-solving purposes
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work

**Compensation:** ($26/hr-$27/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

Cookies: [https://careers.rescue.org/us/en/cookiesettings](https://careers.rescue.org/us/en/cookiesettings)

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: REQUEST FOR KRA LEDGER RECONCILAITION SERVICES TO CHILDFUND KENYA
body:
**Introduction**

The purpose of this TOR is to request a financial proposal for the provision of KRA tax ledger reconciliation services.

**About ChildFund:**

ChildFund is a child-focused international development organization that works with children living in extreme poverty, reaching 17.6 million children and family members in 26 counties. With primary funding from sponsors and from government, corporate and individual donors, we work long-term in communities to help them transform themselves into places where children have what they need to live at their potential throughout their lives: access to health care, nutrition, learning opportunities, safety and caregivers equipped to ensure these essentials are in place.

**Background:**

ChildFund Kenya is seeking a qualified agent to reconcile its KRA ITAX ledger entries. This involves ensuring accuracy and alignment between the legacy system entries and the iTax system entries. This reconciliation is essential for maintaining compliance with Kenyan tax regulations.

**Objectives:**

1. To reconcile the ChildFund Kenya KRA ledger.
2. To identify and correct any discrepancies or errors in the KRA ledger.
3. Working with KRA officials, to propose and implement necessary amendments to the KRA ledger to ensure accuracy and compliance.

**Scope of Services:**

Data Collection and Analysis:

- Gather relevant data from the ChildFund Kenya KRA Legacy and iTax ledger entries.
- Analyze the data to identify discrepancies, errors, or inconsistencies.

Ledger Reconciliation:

- Compare and reconcile the two ledgers, ensuring that entries align and balance.
- Identify and document any discrepancies or errors.

Error Correction and Amendments:

- Propose and implement necessary corrections or amendments to the CFK KRA ledger.

**Deliverables:**

A fully reconciled KRA ledger report, reflecting all approved corrections and amendments to eliminate discrepancies and ensure alignment between the legacy system and the iTax system. This will address any long-standing issues related to contentious amounts between ChildFund and KRA.

The vendor will provide verifiable documentation supporting all final to be reviewed and approved by the designated ChildFund technical lead as evidence of satisfactory completion of the assignment and shall form part of the supporting documentation required for payment processing.

**Qualifications and Experience:**

The consultant should have the following qualifications and experience:

- Strong knowledge of the KRA system.
- Evidence of relevant experience and client testimonials from similar assignments.
- Be an approved KRA Agent of good standing.

**Data Protection and Confidentiality**

The consultant/service provider shall comply with all applicable data protection and privacy laws, regulations, and ChildFund policies relating to the collection, access, use, processing, storage, retention, and disclosure of personal data obtained or handled during the assignment.

Note- Due to the large number of applications received, only shortlisted tax agents will be contacted.

title: Project Manager
body:
**Miyamoto International** is a global engineering and disaster management firm, delivering expert solutions to sustain industries and safeguard humanity. We are a purpose-driven company with a mission to make the world a better, safer place.

We are seeking a dedicated, highly organized, and results-oriented **Project Manager** to join our global Disaster Risk Management group, which specializes in disaster risk reduction, response, reconstruction, and urban resilience. With experience responding to over 100 global and U.S. disasters, our data-driven, multidisciplinary approach addresses economic, political, socio-cultural, sustainability, and technical challenges in some of the world's most demanding environments. We excel at developing strategies for post-conflict and disaster recovery, including creating resilient, affordable housing systems that empower communities to rebuild and thrive.

This position is to be based in our **Los Angeles** office. No relocation or sponsorship is provided.

**Position Summary**

The Project Manager will oversee the implementation of complex global disaster preparedness, response, recovery, and resilience programs, with a strong focus on effective **contract/award management**. Working under the direction of Miyamoto’s Senior Principals overseeing global disaster response and preparedness work, the Project Manager will work closely with technical specialists, country teams, finance, operations, and project coordination staff to ensure programs are delivered effectively, on time, within budget, and in accordance with donor requirements.

The role will provide day-to-day oversight of program implementation, including work planning, budget and expenditure management, reporting, compliance, procurement and contracting coordination, risk management, and contract/award administration. The Project Manager will support multiple country programs and help teams translate program objectives and award requirements into practical implementation.

The position will require flexibility to deploy to disaster-affected countries as needed. During emergency responses, the Project Manager may support the rapid establishment and management of project systems, budgets, reporting, coordination, and other operational requirements.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Manage the day-to-day implementation of global disaster preparedness, response, recovery, and reconstruction programs, ensuring activities are delivered on time, within budget, and in accordance with program and donor requirements.

title: Operations Coordinator
body:

The role will support a broad range of operational needs, including procurement, contracting, consultant recruitment and management, logistics, travel and deployments, IT and equipment, finance coordination, and project start-up and closeout. The Operations Coordinator will also support the development of scopes of work, identification and mobilization of specialized consultants and service providers, and management of consultant rosters and other operational resources that can be leveraged across projects and disaster responses.

This is a hands-on role requiring strong judgment, initiative, and follow-through. The successful candidate will be comfortable taking ownership of operational needs from identification through completion, while recognizing when specialized expertise or management guidance is required. The position requires the ability to work across multiple projects and countries, respond quickly to changing priorities, and develop practical solutions and systems without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Provide day-to-day operational support across global disaster preparedness, response, recovery, and resilience programs.
- Coordinate procurement of goods and services, including supporting development of specifications and scopes of work, identifying vendors and service providers, obtaining and documenting quotations, coordinating required reviews and approvals, and tracking procurement through delivery.
- Support consultant and contractor engagement, including development of scopes of work, identification and recruitment of qualified experts, contracting, onboarding, assignment tracking, and coordination of invoicing and other administrative requirements.
- Develop and maintain rosters of specialized technical and operational consultants and service providers and support their efficient mobilization across projects and disaster responses.
- Work with Project Managers, technical teams, and country teams to identify operational and specialized expertise required for program implementation and help determine practical approaches to meeting those needs.
- Coordinate operational aspects of project and country start-up and closeout, including consultant and staff mobilization, procurement, contracting, equipment, IT, travel, documentation, and other implementation requirements.
- Coordinate international and in-country travel and deployment logistics, including flights, accommodation, ground transportation, visas, insurance, communications, equipment, and other mobilization requirements.
- Coordinate IT, communications, software, equipment, and other operational requirements for project teams and deployed personnel, working with internal or external specialists as needed.

- Maintain procurement, contracting, consultant, vendor, equipment, travel, and other operational records and trackers, ensuring documentation is complete, organized, and readily accessible.
- Coordinate with specialized consultants and advisors in areas such as procurement, safety and security, legal and compliance, logistics, IT, and other operational functions, helping translate specialist guidance into practical actions for project and country teams.
- Support development and continuous improvement of practical operational procedures, templates, tools, and workflows that enable teams to work efficiently while meeting organizational and donor requirements.
- Proactively identify operational needs, bottlenecks, and risks and work with Project Managers, country teams, leadership, and specialist advisors to develop and implement practical solutions.
- Support emergency operations and rapid-response activations, including mobilization, logistics, procurement, contracting, information management, equipment, and other immediate operational priorities.
- Provide operational support across other global initiatives and responses as organizational priorities and needs evolve.

As needed, this role may require international travel and deployment to disaster-affected locations to provide direct operational and logistical support.

**Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**:

Bachelor’s degree in business, operations, international relations, emergency management, supply chain, logistics, or another relevant field. Equivalent relevant professional experience will also be considered.

**Experience**:

- Approximately 4–7 years of relevant professional experience in operations, project coordination, procurement, logistics, contracting, business administration, or related functions.
- Demonstrated experience independently managing operational processes and taking responsibility for complex tasks from planning through completion is important.
- Experience supporting complex, international, or fast-moving operations is highly desirable.
- Experience in humanitarian assistance, disaster response, international development, or other rapidly changing operational environments is an advantage but not required.

**Knowledge**:

- Strong understanding of operational and project administration processes, with familiarity across areas such as procurement, contracting, logistics, budgeting, financial administration, IT, and operational support.
- Experience with donor-funded programs is desirable, as is familiarity with U.S. Government-funded programs and 2 CFR / U.S. federal award requirements.

**Skills**:

- Excellent organizational and problem-solving skills, strong attention to detail, and demonstrated ability to exercise sound judgment and independently manage multiple operational priorities.
- Ability to identify what needs to be done, determine a practical path forward, seek specialized guidance when appropriate, and follow through to completion.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills and confidence working with vendors, consultants, technical specialists, and teams across different countries and functions.
- Strong proficiency in Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and digital and AI-enabled tools for organization and administration.
- Ability to appropriately handle sensitive and confidential information.

**Languages**: Professional fluency in English required. Spanish highly preferred. Additional languages are an advantage.

**Remote Work and Travel Requirements**:

Willingness to travel internationally and deploy to disaster-affected locations as needed.

We work in complex and rapidly changing environments where there is rarely a single blueprint for how work should be done. We minimize bureaucracy while maintaining strong, adaptive systems that support accountability, quality, and compliance. We look for smart, resourceful individuals who are comfortable taking ownership, navigating ambiguity, working collaboratively, and finding practical solutions in a fast-moving environment. Successful candidates share our passion for helping others and strive to improve the quality of their work with each new challenge. This is an opportunity to expand your creativity and build your expertise in the field.

title: Coordinateur Géographique H/F
body:
**Aperçu**

Nous recrutons actuellement un **Coordinateur Géographique H/F** pour rejoindre notre équipe **Développement des Ressources et Mise en Oeuvre des Programmes**.

Il s'agit de postes en télétravail, ouverts aux candidat·es basé·es dans l'un des pays où Relief International opère, dans une zone comprise entre les fuseaux horaires du Royaume-Uni et du Pakistan.  
Des déplacements pouvant représenter jusqu'à 30 % du temps sont à prévoir dans les bureaux pays et sur les sites d'intervention, selon les besoins.

Nous sommes fiers de recruter à l'échelle internationale et d'accueillir des collaborateurs et collaboratrices du monde entier. Nous proposons à l'ensemble de notre personnel des salaires et des avantages sociaux compétitifs, selon des principes d'équité et de transparence.  
Les fourchettes de rémunération variant selon les marchés locaux, les candidat·es présélectionné·es seront informé·es de la fourchette applicable au cours du processus de recrutement.

Ce poste est soumis à des vérifications préalables à l'embauche renforcées.

**À propos de Relief International**

Relief International (RI) est une organisation internationale à but non lucratif qui œuvre aux côtés des communautés touchées par les conflits, le changement climatique et les catastrophes, afin de sauver des vies, renforcer la résilience et promouvoir la santé et le bien-être à long terme.

Notre équipe, composée de plus de 6 000 collaborateurs et bénévoles locaux, intervient en Afrique, Asie et Moyen-Orient, à travers des programmes de Santé et Nutrition, d'Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène (EAH), d'Éducation et de Moyens de subsistance, qui posent les bases de la résilience communautaire.

Pour cela, nous travaillons avec les acteurs locaux afin de développer des programmes sûrs et inclusifs, fondés sur des données probantes, sensibles aux enjeux de conflit, adaptés au climat et répondant aux besoins des populations concernées.

Relief International est un Réseau de trois organisations partageant une mission commune: Relief International, Inc., Relief International-France et Relief International-UK

**À propos du poste**

En tant que membre clé de l'équipe Développement des ressources et Mise en œuvre des programmes, le/la Coordinateur·rice Géographique joue un rôle essentiel pour aider Relief International à mobiliser les ressources nécessaires à la mise en œuvre de programmes humanitaires et de développement à fort impact dans plusieurs bureaux pays.

En étroite collaboration avec les Responsables Géographiques, les bureaux pays et les équipes techniques, vous contribuerez aux relations avec les bailleurs de fonds, au positionnement stratégique et aux efforts de développement de financements auprès d'un éventail diversifié de bailleurs, notamment les bailleurs européens, le gouvernement des États-Unis, les agences des Nations Unies, les fondations, les entreprises et d'autres partenaires institutionnels de financement.

Vous piloterez et coordonnerez l'ensemble du processus d'élaboration des propositions, depuis l'identification des opportunités jusqu'à leur soumission, en veillant à produire des propositions de grande qualité, conformes aux exigences des bailleurs et compétitives.

Ce poste s'adresse à un·e professionnel·le expérimenté·e en développement de financements, appréciant le travail interculturel, la coordination de processus complexes d'élaboration de propositions et l'appui aux programmes pour mobiliser des financements permettant d'avoir un impact significatif dans certains des contextes humanitaires les plus difficiles au monde.

**Vos responsabilités**

Ce poste comprend les responsabilités suivantes :

- Suivre les tendances des bailleurs de fonds, les opportunités de financement et les priorités stratégiques, et partager les informations pertinentes ainsi que les opportunités de positionnement avec les équipes pays et les équipes du siège.
- Soutenir les démarches auprès des bailleurs et les efforts de positionnement stratégique en élaborant des notes conceptuelles, des argumentaires et des approches de financement pour les opportunités prioritaires.
- Piloter et coordonner l'ensemble du processus d'élaboration des propositions, afin de garantir des soumissions de grande qualité, remises dans les délais, compétitives et conformes aux exigences des bailleurs.
- Coordonner les ateliers de conception des propositions, les processus de constitution de consortiums et les mécanismes de revue interne impliquant les parties prenantes des programmes, de la finance, des équipes techniques et des opérations.
- Apporter un appui technique et des conseils aux bureaux pays sur les exigences des bailleurs, l'élaboration des propositions, la budgétisation et les processus de développement de financements.
- Faciliter les processus de décision « go/no-go » et tenir à jour avec précision le pipeline de financements ainsi que les outils de suivi des opportunités.
- Développer et renforcer les capacités des équipes pays en matière de conception de programmes, d'élaboration de propositions et de relations avec les bailleurs.
- Participer, le cas échéant, aux soumissions auprès des bailleurs et à l'utilisation de leurs plateformes en ligne, notamment APPEL, GMS et UNPP.
- Soutenir la coordination transversale entre les équipes Développement des ressources, Mise en œuvre des programmes, Gestion des subventions, Finance et équipes techniques, ainsi que les bureaux pays.

**Votre profil**

Vous disposez de l'expérience et des compétences suivantes :

- Une maîtrise professionnelle de l'anglais est indispensable.
- Une maîtrise professionnelle du français est requise.
- Expérience avérée dans la mobilisation de financements auprès de bailleurs institutionnels et non institutionnels, ainsi que dans l'accompagnement d'opportunités de financement complexes dans les secteurs humanitaire et du développement.
- Solide expérience des mécanismes de financement de bailleurs tels qu'ECHO, le FCDO, les institutions de l'Union européenne, les agences des Nations Unies, les bailleurs du gouvernement des États-Unis, les fondations et d'autres partenaires internationaux de financement.
- Expérience dans le pilotage de processus complexes d'élaboration de propositions, y compris en consortium, depuis l'identification de l'opportunité jusqu'à la soumission au bailleur.
- Bonne maîtrise des exigences de conformité des bailleurs, de la budgétisation des propositions, du recouvrement des coûts indirects et des principes de gestion financière.
- Diplôme en relations internationales, administration des affaires ou dans un autre domaine pertinent, ou expérience professionnelle équivalente.
- Excellentes compétences rédactionnelles, de relecture et de communication, avec la capacité à élaborer, dans des délais serrés, des documents convaincants destinés aux bailleurs.
- Excellentes capacités d'organisation et de gestion des parties prenantes, avec la capacité de gérer plusieurs priorités dans différents pays et fuseaux horaires.
- Une expérience dans des contextes humanitaires ou affectés par des conflits, ainsi qu'une bonne connaissance du système humanitaire international, seraient fortement appréciées.

title: NTS/EORE Team Member / Aleppo, Raqqa & Hasakah
body:
**DanChurchAid (DCA) Syria** invites applications for an experienced **NTS/EORE Team Member** to join our dedicated team.

- Under the supervision of the NTS/EORE Team Leader, undertake assigned Non-Technical Survey (NTS) and Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE) activities in accordance with applicable DCA procedures and operational tasking.
- Conduct NTS through the systematic collection, recording and reporting of information from communities, authorities and other relevant sources relating to suspected explosive ordnance contamination and humanitarian impact, without independently determining land classification or land-release outcomes.
- Deliver EORE using approved DCA messages, materials and methodologies to increase awareness of explosive ordnance risks and promote safer behaviour, while supporting appropriate community engagement, data collection and reporting.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

- Conduct assigned NTS activities through the systematic collection and recording of information from relevant sources using approved DCA NTS formats and procedures.
- Deliver assigned EORE sessions using approved DCA messages, educational materials and methodologies to promote awareness of explosive ordnance risks and safer behaviour.
- Conduct NTS and EORE activities in accordance with applicable DCA procedures and operational tasking.
- Support EORE community outreach activities, campaigns and special awareness events as assigned.
- Adapt EORE communication methods to suit different target groups and literacy levels while maintaining accurate and consistent delivery of approved risk-education messages.
- Build positive working relationships with communities, authorities and other relevant stakeholders and information sources in support of assigned NTS and EORE activities.
- Facilitate appropriate community engagement and participation in assigned NTS and EORE activities.
- Recognise and report community concerns or information relating to suspected explosive ordnance contamination through the appropriate DCA reporting channels.
- Support inclusive engagement and appropriate access to women, men, girls, boys and other relevant community members and information sources during assigned activities.
- Work collaboratively with other team members and follow the guidance and instructions of the NTS/EORE Team Leader and relevant HMA management.
- Maintain professional conduct as a representative of DCA and contribute to continuous improvement and a positive, inclusive and professional team environment.
- Apply approved navigation, map-reading and Global Positioning System (GPS) techniques during assigned NTS activities.
- Use approved DCA systems and tools to accurately record and manage NTS information and EORE activity data.
- Complete required NTS and EORE records and reports accurately and on time.
- Use and care for assigned equipment, IT equipment and applications appropriately in support of assigned NTS and EORE activities.
- Operate safely in field environments and comply with all applicable safety and security procedures.

**MINIMUM REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE**

- Educational Level: Primary School Certificate, a high school degree will be an added asset.
- Years of work experience: Minimum one year of relevant experience in NTS and/or EORE, community liaison or other relevant humanitarian mine action activities.
- Language skills and local knowledge: Appropriate language skills and local knowledge relevant to the areas and communities in which assigned activities are undertaken.
- Field requirements: Able and willing to undertake field travel as required.
- Relevant technical capabilities: Following appointment, personnel must successfully complete required DCA NTS and EORE training, DCA competency verification and applicable induction, refresher and mandatory pre-deployment training before operational deployment.

**About ZOA**

***We are here for people who have lost everything due to armed conflict or natural disaster.***

ZOA, as an international NGO, supports people who have lost everything due to armed conflict or natural disaster. Together, we can come to their aid in emergencies and remain faithful to communities as they recover – providing new opportunities for them to help themselves again. The work of ZOA is coordinated from the Netherlands. We are active in multiple countries in Africa, South America, the Middle East Region, and Asia. We work with approximately 900 employees worldwide and with (local) partners. We invite you to join our team of committed colleagues.

**Our work in Uganda**

In Uganda, ZOA has offices in Kampala, West Nile (Arua), Acholi (Gulu), and Karamoja (Amudat). ZOA Uganda works both in relief and recovery on the themes of food security & livelihoods, education, and conflict management with a special focus on land Rights.

**About the OCHA Project**

From October 2026 to July 2027, ZOA will implement WASH activities as a consortium partner with other partners implementing Protection and Nutrition related activities. The funding from OCHA will be used to meet immediate life saving needs including:

- Extending water supply systems
- Rehabilitating reserve tanks and water system components
- Support operations of motorised water supply systems
- Rehabilitate water points
- Facecal desludging
- Support to household latrine construction
- Latrine block construction
- Emergency preparedness and response in flood prone areas.

ZOA is looking for a MEAL Officer to be based in Arua.

**Your challenge**

The MEAL Officer has the responsibility of undertaking all MEAL activities to document output, outcome and impact changes as defined in the MEAL Framework for the OCHA WASH project. S/he will identify information gaps and make recommendations for the collection of data on all indicators as checks against processes and contexts to measure progress, results, and impact.

The MEAL Officer will ensure that all OCHA WASH project MEAL activities shall result in timely tracking and documentation for project activities, quality data generated and processed in support of project reporting, increased accountability to different stakeholders, facilitates and upholds learning within the OCHA WASH project and across the organization as described in the project MEAL Plan.

The MEAL Officer WASH will support MEAL for WASH activities under the OCHA funded humanitarian project in Kiryandongo, Palorinya and Rhino Camp refugee settlements. He/She will oversee implementation of activities in two Outcome areas:

- Improved access to safe, reliable and equitable water supply for vulnerable communities in Palorinya, Rhino Camp and Kiryandongo refugee settlements.
- Reduced risk of WASH-related disease outbreaks through emergency sanitation and hygiene support for vulnerable refugee and host-community communities in Palorinya, Rhino Camp and Kiryandongo refugee settlements.

**Your main tasks and responsibilities**

***Monitoring***

- The MEAL Officer works closely with the project and other MEAL colleagues as well as partners to create and operate a functional MEAL framework, system, tools and processes in alignment with ZOA guidelines, standards and localized MEAL contexts to gather performance data at output, outcome and impact level based on objectives and indicators contained in the MEAL Frameworks.
- Leads in the drafting and development of the project MEAL plan, Indicator tracking table, field Data Protocols/SOPs, ToRs, and data collection tools to facilitate field procedures and execution.
- Work with Project staff to ensure the collection of relevant and appropriate data for Knowledge Management and Learning.
- Organise joint project monitoring with other stakeholders, partners and project teams
- Strengthen the utilization of technology and where feasible enhance data collection, analysis, and reporting considering the limited infrastructure and internet connectivity challenges of ZOA operation areas.
- Lead and facilitates local analysis, visualization, presentations and interpretation of contextualized MEAL information as inputs to regular narrative reports covering progress.
- Facilitate capacity building initiatives on MEAL for project staffs and partners ensuring they have the skills and knowledge necessary to effectively apply and implement MEAL system, frameworks, tools, and other MEAL processes to enhance activities, data collection, analysis, application of data and information for measuring progress, reporting, making necessary adjustments and improving programme impact(s).
- In coordination with MEAL Coordinator, plan and undertake Data Quality Audits and Assessment exercises to ensure data quality.
- Ensure visibility materials (pop ups, team clothing, project sheets, flyers, leaflets) to be used for meetings, contact with communities, donors, and partners are produced to high quality.

***Evaluation***

- Get involved in the drafting and design of ToRs for project assessments, evaluations and other studies
- Participate in the evaluation of proposal bids and selection of individual consultants and firms for consultancy assignments.
- Coordinate internal and external assessments, studies, evaluations and other research for the project in close collaboration with the MEAL Coordinator, PGM, Coordinators, Project Manager, and PQ team.
- Drafting and/or reviewing evaluation reports for internal and external use.
- The MEAL Officer acts as the main contact person for the MEAL related support in the OCHA WASH project

***Accountability***

- Oversee ZOA’s commitments to the Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS) in line with the project, ensuring that the Feedback and Complaints Mechanism (FCM) operated either at ZOA or project partner is fit for purpose and that complaints and feedback received are monitored and followed up appropriately.
- Promote participatory approaches and methodologies, engaging affected population to ensure their voices and perspectives are captured in order to address specific needs and expectations.
- Sensitise and educate team members and stakeholders (beneficiaries, service providers, partners, government authorities and others) on Feedback and Complaint Mechanisms implemented by ZOA Uganda.
- Ensure appropriate documentation of feedback and complaints received following correct reporting procedures and tools.
- In coordination with MEAL Coordinator conduct regular analysis and presentation of feedback and complaints portraying context and trends in the project implementation to guide necessary improvements.
- Promote understanding to ZOA’s Code of Conduct and Safeguarding policies, ensuring adherence to these policies at all times and that project activities are implemented with a “Do No Harm” approach.

***Learning***

- Lead drafting and development of Project level Learning Agendas and Questions to guide relevant data collection and learning activities.
- Promote a culture of learning and knowledge sharing through utilization of project/programme data collected, key assessments, evaluations, any other study findings and lessons learned for adaptive management, adjustments and improving impact(s).
- Documentation of good practices, success stories, innovative approaches and learning products to be utilized for programming, advocacy and other dissemination.
- Planning and organising joint project monitoring, reviews, and learning workshops/events internally and externally sharing results with programme teams and other stakeholders.
- Convene and chair regular meetings with project team involving other MEAL colleagues as well as partners using available platforms to collectively analyse and interpret MEAL information, discuss MEAL related issues, exchange MEAL expertise and experiences.
- Foster coordination and collaboration between project and MEAL teams as well as with key stakeholders (government authorities, UN agencies, NGOs, and implementing partners) in order to enhance MEAL practices such as MEAL coordination mechanisms, networks, and working groups.

***Any other***

- Perform any other duties as assigned.

**Your profile**

Identity

- The candidate is expected to fully support the vision, mission and Christian values 0f ZOA (see [https://www.zoa-international.com/corporate-identity](https://www.zoa-international.com/corporate-identity))

***Knowledge, Skills & Experience:***

- Bachelor degree in a relevant discipline (e.g., Statistics, Quantitative Economics, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Population Studies, Anthropology, etc.)
- Postgraduate diploma in Monitoring and Evaluation is advantageous.
- At least three (3) years’ of experience in:
- MEAL system design, rollout and implementation in multisectoral projects with International organizations
- Online data collection tools such as Kobo collect, Commcare, ODK, etc.
- (Computerized) data processing and analysis, e.g. statistical software such as SPSS, STATA, etc) and report writing tailored to suit donor requirements and other stakeholders.
- Training of team, individuals and groups (e.g. for data collection)
- Participatory assessment and monitoring
- Training of individuals and groups (e.g. for data collection)
- Good understanding of the Uganda context; experience in Kiryandongo and/or refugee operations
- Experience working in projects working in WASH is desirable
- Excellent facilitation and communication skills
- Ability to organise and train MEAL staff in ZOA, and within partner organisations
- Good contextual knowledge related to civil society/community assessment (i.e. Local community priorities, social and cultural constraints and local political and economic environment)
- Experience working with vulnerable people.
- Experience of working with People with Disabilities and/or Refugees is a plus

***Attitude/behaviour:***

- Good interpersonal, organizational and intercultural sensitivity
- Able to plan and coordinate and work in an organized manner
- Able to bridge differences and bring people together
- High integrity
- Motivated
- Able to work independently
- Commitment to ZOA’s mission, vision and values (see [https://www.zoa-international.com/corporate-identity](https://www.zoa-international.com/corporate-identity))

**Special conditions/circumstances**

The MEAL Officer will be based in Kiryandongo , Palorinya & Rhino Camp Programme Area Office with field visit within the Project locations to provide real time monitoring.

The MEAL officer may also visit other ZOA programme Offices and Country Office for learning purposes and or interaction with other MEAL staffs within the organization for information sharing, training etc.

The role is 1.0 FTE (40 hrs/ week). Working hours are outlined in the ZOA Uganda Employee Handbook. Some flexibility on working hours may be required, e.g. for travel at weekends, or during reporting times.

**Our offer**

- ZOA offers a challenging role in a dynamic context, and you will be part of an inspiring and motivated team.
- We offer good benefits and remuneration which suits the NGO sector.

Do you need more information?

For more information about ZOA, please visit our website [www.zoa-international.com](http://www.zoa-international.com/).

title: NTS/EORE Team Leader / Aleppo, Raqqa & Hasakah
body:
**DanChurchAid (DCA) Syria** invites applications for an experienced **NTS/EORE Team Leader** to join our dedicated team.

Under the supervision of the NTS/EORE Coordinator, the NTS/EORE Team Leader is responsible for planning, coordinating, supervising and monitoring Non-Technical Survey (NTS) and Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE) activities implemented by the assigned NTS/EORE team. The position ensures that NTS and EORE activities are delivered effectively, safely and in accordance with DCA policies, SOPs and applicable humanitarian mine action standards.

The NTS/EORE Team Leader supervises assigned NTS/EORE Team Members, ensures the quality of NTS and EORE activities, data collection and reporting, and supports operational and community liaison with local authorities, community representatives and other relevant stakeholders.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

- Lead and supervise assigned NTS/EORE Team Members.
- Plan daily, weekly and monthly NTS and EORE activities, including appropriate preparation for assigned NTS tasks.
- Allocate responsibilities and field tasks and monitor team performance.
- Supervise the implementation of assigned NTS activities and oversee the collection and review of relevant information and evidence by the team.
- Conduct briefings, debriefings, and regular coaching sessions.
- Ensure staff compliance with organisational procedures, code of conduct, and safeguarding policies.
- Foster a positive, inclusive, and professional team environment.
- Coordinate liaison and engagement with affected communities, community representatives and other relevant stakeholders to support assigned NTS activities and facilitate access to relevant information sources.
- Organise and oversee the delivery of EORE sessions for affected communities.
- Ensure EORE messages are appropriate for women, men, girls, boys, and vulnerable groups.
- Coordinate EORE awareness campaigns, community meetings, school sessions, and outreach activities.
- Support the appropriate contextual adaptation of approved EORE materials and provide feedback on identified community needs and explosive ordnance threats.
- Establish and maintain productive relationships with community representatives, local authorities, schools, and other relevant stakeholders to support NTS and EORE activities.
- Review NTS and EORE field records, data and reports produced by Team Members for completeness, accuracy and consistency, and ensure their timely submission through approved DCA processes.
- Maintain organised records of NTS and EORE activities conducted by the assigned team.
- Use approved DCA systems and tools to review and manage NTS information and EORE activity data.
- Ensure relevant NTS and EORE information and data are communicated to the NTS/EORE Coordinator and relevant DCA information-management functions through approved processes.
- Use DCA-provided IT equipment and applications appropriately in support of assigned activities.
- Ensure the assigned team operates safely in field environments and complies with all applicable safety and security procedures.

**MINIMUM REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE**

- Educational Level: Primary School Certificate, a high school degree will be an added asset.
- Years of work experience: Minimum one year of relevant experience in NTS and/or EORE, community liaison or other relevant humanitarian mine action activities. Previous supervisory or team leadership experience is preferred.
- Relevant Technical Capabilities: Demonstrated ability to lead and supervise NTS and/or EORE activities, including community engagement, information and data collection, documentation and reporting.
- Relevant Technical Knowledge: Working knowledge of applicable NTS and EORE procedures, DCA SOPs and relevant humanitarian mine action standards.
- Language skills and local knowledge: Appropriate language skills and local knowledge relevant to the areas and communities in which assigned activities are undertaken.
- Field requirements: Able and willing to undertake field travel as required.

**Following appointment, the NTS/EORE Team Leader must successfully complete required DCA NTS and EORE training, DCA competency verification and applicable induction, refresher and mandatory pre-deployment training before operational deployment.**

**Before operational deployment, the NTS/EORE Team Leader must demonstrate sufficient competence to supervise the approved navigation, map-reading and Global Positioning System (GPS) techniques used during NTS activities.**

**Team deployment consideration: NTS/EORE team composition and deployment should support appropriate access to women, men, girls and boys within targeted communities.**

In Uganda, ZOA has offices in Kampala, West Nile (Arua), Acholi (Gulu), and Karamoja (Amudat). ZOA Uganda works both in relief and recovery on the themes of food security & livelihoods, education, and conflict management with a special focus on land Rights.

**About the OCHA Project**

From October 2026 to July 2027, ZOA will implement WASH activities as a consortium partner with other partners implementing Protection and Nutrition related activities. The funding from OCHA will be used to meet immediate life saving needs including:

- Extending water supply systems
- Rehabilitating reserve tanks and water system components
- Support operations of motorised water supply systems
- Rehabilitate water points
- Facecal desludging
- Support to household latrine construction
- Latrine block construction
- Emergency preparedness and response in flood prone areas

ZOA Uganda is looking for a Project Officer to be based in Kiryandongo, Palorinya & Rhino Camp Settlements Office.

**Your challenge**

The Project Officer WASH, with support from the Project Coordinator WASH is responsible for the day-to-day implementation of WASH activities under the OCHA funded humanitarian project in Kiryandongo, Palorinya or Rhino Camp refugee settlements. He/She will oversee implementation of activities in two Outcome areas:

- Improved access to safe, reliable and equitable water supply for vulnerable communities in Palorinya, Rhino Camp and Kiryandongo refugee settlements.
- Reduced risk of WASH-related disease outbreaks through emergency sanitation and hygiene support for vulnerable refugee and host-community communities in Palorinya, Rhino Camp and Kiryandongo refugee settlements.

ZOA is hiring three positions under this advert. A WASH Officer will be based in each target location.

**Your main tasks and responsibilities**

**General**

- Implement project activities in the assigned refugee settlement, ensuring alignment with the approved workplan, budget, donor requirements and ZOA procedures.
- Carry out field assessments of water sources, sanitation facilities and WASH service gaps, and contribute to technical planning, activity design, procurement planning and implementation schedules.
- Monitor contractors, service providers, hand pump mechanics and community volunteers to ensure works are completed safely, on time and according to agreed technical standards and specifications.
- Support implementation of sanitation activities such as household latrine construction, latrine block construction, faecal desludging, waste management and handwashing facility installation.
- Plan and supervise hygiene promotion, community sensitisation, behaviour change campaigns and distribution of hygiene materials to reduce risks of WASH-related disease outbreaks.
- Establish, train and mentor water user committees, hygiene promoters, sanitation committees and hand pump mechanics to promote community ownership, sustainability and operation and maintenance.
- Work closely with OPM, UNHCR, district local government, settlement leadership, consortium partners, WASH partners and community structures to harmonise interventions and avoid duplication.
- Collect and verify WASH monitoring data, track progress against indicators, document lessons learned and success stories, and contribute to monthly, internal and donor reports.
- Ensure WASH activities are inclusive, safe and accessible for vulnerable groups, including persons with disabilities, women, children and older persons; support feedback and complaint mechanisms and uphold safeguarding standards.

**Water Supply and Infrastructure**

- Conduct technical assessments of water sources (boreholes, wells, piped systems) to determine functionality, repair needs, and rehabilitation feasibility.
- Support the design, planning and supervision of WASH infrastructure construction and rehabilitation works, including boreholes, piped schemes, and water storage systems.
- Monitor contractors, hand pump mechanics and community volunteers to ensure quality workmanship and adherence to technical standards.
- Maintain updated inventories and mapping of water sources within the implementation area.
- Closely work with the district water officials and other stakeholders during joint assessments and technical verification missions.

**Sanitation and Hygiene Promotion.**

- Support the design and implementation of sanitation improvements such as latrine construction, waste management, and hand washing station installation.
- Deliver hygiene promotion activities, including community sensitisations, behavioural change campaigns and distribution of hygiene kits.
- Collaborate with health department and partners to improve sanitation and infection prevention.

**Community Engagement and Capacity Strengthening.**

- Facilitate training and follow-up of water user committees to strengthen community based management of water points.
- Promote community contributions for operation and maintenance in line with local regulations and sustainability plans.
- Conduct community mobilisation during WASH campaigns, project launches and emergency response activities.

**Coordination and Partnership Engagement**

- Represent the organisation in district and subcounty WASH coordination meetings.
- Participate in project inception meetings, planning workshops, and joint monitoring missions.
- Provide technical feedback to partners and ensure alignment with national WASH Policy.

**Reporting /Monitoring and Data Management.**

- Provide inputs to implementation plans and activity/monthly reports;
- Identify, document lessons learned and best practices;
- Prepare and submit well written success stories;
- Contribute to project reports or implementation plans as required by supervisor;
- Collect monitoring data according to ZOA’s systems and activities in the project;
- Representation and coordination with relevant partners in Kiryandongo context on issues around WASH
- Actively participate in the required and relevant technical working groups;
- Participate in relevant coordination meetings concerning the project.
- Regular coordination with local government actors and relevant district offices; OPM, UNHCR and other NGO partners.
- Contact with other project specific actors, e.g. consultants or service providers.

**Accountability**

- Sensitise all stakeholders (beneficiaries, service providers, partners, government and other) on feedback and complaint mechanisms implemented by ZOA Uganda
- Upon receipt of a complaint or feedback, ensure that it is documented following correct reporting procedures

Identity

- The candidate is expected to fully support the vision, mission and Christian values 0f ZOA (see [https://www.zoa-international.com/corporate-identity](https://www.zoa-international.com/corporate-identity))

***Knowledge & Experience:***

- Minimum of a Diploma or degree in Hydraulic Engineering, Water Resource Engineering, environmental or public health or other related fields.
- 2 + years’ experience in WASH, preferably in a humanitarian setting (refugee camps, rural development, or emergency response).
- Experience in localisation approaches and working with local organizations
- A good command of English, including written reporting and activity reporting
- Experience of working with People with Disabilities is a plus
- Experience working in the refugee settlement context is advantageous
- Experience of working with OCHA or on emergency projects is desired

***Skills:***

- High level of networking capacities
- Experience of Engineering Software (Watercad, Epanet and Auto CAD etc)
- Experience with WASH Software components (hygiene promotion, Menstrual hygiene management and community sanitation approaches)
- Knowledge of domestic water supply system hydraulic design
- Excellent communication and interpersonal
- Able to bridge differences and bring people together from different backgrounds
- Motivated to work independently / self-managing
- Good computer skills: Ms Excel and Ms Word;
- Self-motivator, able to take initiatives with limited supervision;
- Ability to drive a motorcycle with valid driving/riding license is a MUST.

***Attitude/behaviour:***

- High level of personal integrity;
- Flexibility and adaptability;
- Interpersonal and cross-cultural sensitivity;
- Able to work under pressures and meet deadlines;
- Able to work in a sometimes fluid and innovative environment
- Commitment to ZOA’s mission, vision and values (see [https://www.zoa-international.com/corporate-identity](https://www.zoa-international.com/corporate-identity))

**Special conditions/circumstances**

The Project Officer will be based at the ZOA field office in either Kiryandongo, Palorinya, or Rhino Camp refugee settlements..

Regular travel to field locations, sub counties and for meetings with project stakeholders is expected. The postholder is expected to regularly ride a motorcycle in rural conditions/on unmade roads.

The role is 1.0 FTW (40 hrs./week). Working hours and benefits are outlined in the ZOA Uganda Employee Handbook. Some flexibility on working hours may be required, e.g. for travel at weekends, or during reporting times.

**Our offer**

- ZOA offers a challenging role in a dynamic context, and you will be part of an inspiring and motivated team.
- We offer good benefits and remuneration which suits the NGO sector.

Do you need more information?

For more information about ZOA, please visit our website [www.zoa-international.com](http://www.zoa-international.com/).

ZOA Uganda is looking for a Project Manager to be based in Arua Office.

**Your challenge**

The **Project Manager – WASH** with support from the Programme Manager West Nile , is responsible for oversight of the OCHA WASH project. The Project Manager will provide overall leadership, strategic direction, and operational oversight of the OCHA-funded WASH project, ensuring timely delivery of quality, accountable, and inclusive WASH services to refugees and host communities in accordance with donor requirements, Sphere standards, national policies, and organizational procedures. They will manage project resources, supervise staff, coordinate stakeholders, oversee monitoring and reporting, and ensure effective integration of protection, gender, disability inclusion, safeguarding, and accountability to affected populations throughout project implementation.

The PM will support and motivate 3 Project Coordinators and 3 Project Officers to deliver quality implementation in all WASH activities. The PM will also work closely with the consortium partners, building a collaborative and accountable working relationship.

The PM is overall accountable and responsible for implementation of WASH activities under the OCHA funded humanitarian project in Kiryandongo, Palorinya and Rhino Camp refugee settlements. He/She will oversee implementation of activities in two Outcome areas:

- Improved access to safe, reliable and equitable water supply for vulnerable communities in Palorinya, Rhino Camp and Kiryandongo refugee settlements.
- Reduced risk of WASH-related disease outbreaks through emergency sanitation and hygiene support for vulnerable refugee and host-community communities in Palorinya, Rhino Camp and Kiryandongo refugee settlements.

- Develop detailed work plans, procurement plans, spending forecasts, and activity schedules.
- Ensure implementation is aligned with project objectives, targets, and timelines.
- Conduct regular meetings and direct day-to-day supervision of the field staff to ensure the project is on track towards meeting the work plan requirements, ensuring targets and deliverables are completed by established deadlines.

***Donor Compliance and Grant Management***

- Ensure compliance with OCHA Humanitarian Financing guidelines, partner agreements, and organisational policies.
- Monitor project deliverables, indicators, and reporting obligations.
- Maintain adequate project documentation and audit-ready records.

***Budget and Financial Oversight***

- Manage project budgets in collaboration with finance staff.
- Monitor expenditure against approved budgets and spending plans.
- Ensure efficient use of resources and timely budget utilisation.
- Identify and address budget variances and financial risks.

***Technical Oversight of WASH Interventions***

- Provide overall supervision of WASH activities, including water supply systems, sanitation facilities, hygiene promotion, and operation and maintenance mechanisms.
- Ensure interventions comply with Sphere standards, Uganda Refugee Response standards, and government regulations.
- Promote quality, sustainability, and accountability in service delivery.

***Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement***

- Represent the organisation in WASH Sector Working Groups, refugee response coordination meetings, and district-level forums.
- Maintain effective collaboration with UN agencies, local authorities, implementing partners, refugee welfare councils, and host community leaders.
- Foster complementarity and avoid duplication of services.

***Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL)***

- Ensure routine monitoring of project indicators and progress against targets.
- Review activity reports, field assessments, and monitoring data.
- Support learning, adaptive management, and evidence-based decision-making.
- Ensure community feedback and complaint mechanisms are functional and responsive.

***Team Leadership and Performance Management***

- Supervise project staff, consultants, and field teams.
- Set performance objectives and provide coaching and technical support.
- Promote teamwork, staff wellbeing, and adherence to organisational values and safeguarding standards.
- Ensure the project team has clear objectives, with weekly and monthly targets, to ensure quality implementation of project outputs and outcomes, with regular face to face meetings (weekly or monthly)
- Ensure that project staff are conversant with their job description, ZOA’s internal regulations, standards, policies and donor regulations;
- Supervises and carries out periodical evaluation of the performance of the staff assigned to the project(s) against established performance objectives in a timely manner
- Ensures capacity building on key project concepts and approaches with support from PQ department and/or other ZOA and partner staff; recommends strategic training opportunities for the team;
- Ensures effective leave management within the project team, in liaison with the field Finance and Administration Associate Manager;

***Finance and procurement***

- Uses ZOA’s ERP system to track and maintain oversight of project expenditure (including partner finances), rregularly monitor projects expenditures (using the BVA) to ensure spending is made in line with the budget approved with the donor
- Ensure timely initiation of procurement requests and follow up on progress
- Provide appropriate code for expenses
- Ensure full utilization of the project approved budget, and timely adjustments and communication with the finance team to ensure good budget management.

**Risk Management and Safeguarding**

- Identify operational, financial, security, environmental, and safeguarding risks.
- Develop and monitor mitigation measures.
- Ensure safeguarding, protection mainstreaming, and prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA) are integrated into all project activities.

***Reporting and Communication***

- Prepare and submit timely, accurate, and high-quality narrative reports for the donor and internally.
- Document project achievements, challenges, lessons learned, and success stories.
- Provide regular updates on project progress, risks, and corrective actions.

***Mainstreaming Cross-Cutting Themes***

- Ensure gender, age, disability inclusion, conflict sensitivity, environmental sustainability, and protection principles are integrated throughout the project cycle.
- Promote meaningful participation of women, persons with disabilities, older persons, youth, refugees, and host communities in project planning and implementation.
- Monitor equitable access to WASH services and address barriers to inclusion.

- Sensitize all stakeholders (participants, service providers, partners, government and other) on feedback and complaint mechanisms implemented by ZOA Uganda;
- Upon receipt of a complaint or feedback, ensure that it is correctly documented following correct reporting procedures;

Identity

***Knowledge & Experience:***

- University degree in Hydraulic Engineering, Water Resource Engineering, environmental or public health or other related fields.
- At least 5 years successful project cycle management experience in a similar position; - Experience managing large programmes for INGOs is an added advantage;
- Experience managing large projects funded by institutional donors is an added advantage;
- Having led a project in partnership with a local NGO is an added advantage;
- Excellent spoken and written command of English;
- Language skills in relevant local languages of the duty station is an added advantage.

- Experience working in the refugee settlement context is advantageous

- Participative leadership with clear command of overall operations;
- Sensitive towards HRM and organizational issues;.
- Good communication, writing and facilitation skills;
- Innovative, creative and enthusiastic;
- Good computer skills: Ms Excel and Ms Word;
- Self-motivator, able to work with limited supervision;
- Able to ride a motorbike in field conditions, holding a valid driving license.

- Commitment to inclusion for People with Disabilities
