title: Project Coordinator, WASH (OCHA Project) - National Position
body:
**Position: Project Coordinator, WASH (OCHA Project) - National Position**

**Reports to:** Project Manager, WASH

**Job location:** Kiryandongo, Palorinya & Rhino Camp (1 per location)

**Starting date:** November 2025

**Vacancy closing date:** 6th October 2026

**Duration position:** 10 months contract

**Working hours:** Fulltime (40 hours per week)

**Please note:** The recruitment for this position is contingent upon confirmation of project funding. The position will only be filled subject to the availability and confirmation of the required funding.

**About ZOA**

***We are here for people who have lost everything due to armed conflict or natural disaster.***

ZOA, as an international NGO, supports people who have lost everything due to armed conflict or natural disaster. Together, we can come to their aid in emergencies and remain faithful to communities as they recover – providing new opportunities for them to help themselves again. The work of ZOA is coordinated from the Netherlands. We are active in multiple countries in Africa, South America, the Middle East Region, and Asia. We work with approximately 900 employees worldwide and with (local) partners. We invite you to join our team of committed colleagues.

**Our work in Uganda**

In Uganda, ZOA has offices in Kampala, West Nile (Arua), Acholi (Gulu), and Karamoja (Amudat). ZOA Uganda works both in relief and recovery on the themes of food security & livelihoods, education, and conflict management with a special focus on land Rights.

**About the OCHA Project**

From October 2026 to July 2027, ZOA will implement WASH activities as a consortium partner with other partners implementing Protection and Nutrition related activities. The funding from OCHA will be used to meet immediate life saving needs including:

- Extending water supply systems
- Rehabilitating reserve tanks and water system components
- Support operations of motorised water supply systems
- Rehabilitate water points
- Facecal desludging
- Support to household latrine construction
- Latrine block construction
- Emergency preparedness and response in flood prone areas

ZOA Uganda is looking for a Project Coordinator to be based in Kiryandongo, Palorinya & Rhino Camp (1 per location).

**Your challenge**

The Project Coordinator, with support from the Project Manager WASH is responsible for the day-to-day coordination around the planning and implementation of WASH activities under the OCHA funded humanitarian project in Kiryandongo, Palorinya or Rhino Camp refugee settlements. He/She will oversee implementation of activities in two Outcome areas:

- Improved access to safe, reliable and equitable water supply for vulnerable communities in Palorinya, Rhino Camp and Kiryandongo refugee settlements.
- Reduced risk of WASH-related disease outbreaks through emergency sanitation and hygiene support for vulnerable refugee and host-community communities in Palorinya, Rhino Camp and Kiryandongo refugee settlements.

**Your main tasks and responsibilities**

**General**

- Support needs assessments, project reviews, and post-project impact assessments as needed and advised;
- Actively participate in preparation of proposals, CN, technical description, and budget development jointly with the project team members .
- Produce detail implementation plan for the WASH component of the project in the host community and refugees. Periodically, update and ensure that progress in accordance with the plan.
- Ensure that WASH projects are implemented in a timely and professional manner, according to goal, objectives, and indicators and in line with ZOA, Ugandan government and donor requirements.
- Ensure proper documentation of WASH activities/data and experiences by the local partner and the community structure.
- Conduct regular monitoring and technical support visits to project sites and camps;
- Actively participate in the review of WASH activity plan, Spending plan and procurement plan and ensure timely delivery.
- Coordinates project activities in line with the workplan to achieve optimal project outputs and outcomes in line with ZOA/donor procedures and targets;
- Support the Deputy program manager in conducting WASH capacity needs assessment with the local partner organization implementing the wash component of the project

**Reporting**

- Provide inputs to implementation plans and activity/monthly reports;
- Identify, document lessons learned and best practices;
- Prepare and submit well written success stories;
- Contribute to project reports or implementation plans as required by supervisor;
- Collect monitoring data according to ZOA’s systems and activities in the project;
- Representation and coordination with relevant partners in Kiryandongo context on issues around WASH
- Actively participate in the required and relevant technical working groups;
- Participate in relevant coordination meetings concerning the project.
- Regular coordination with local government actors and relevant district offices; OPM, UNHCR and other NGO partners.
- Contact with other project specific actors, e.g. consultants or service providers.

**Human Resource Management**

- Ensure the Hygiene promoters have weekly and monthly targets;
- Conduct weekly or monthly meeting to achieve targets;
- Provide technical support through coaching and mentorship of hygiene promoters for quality implementation of project activities.
- Ensure procurement request are put on system for approval and finance requested accordingly
- Initiate timely purchase requisition of project goods/services;
- Ensure expenses within outcome 3 are in line with approved budget;
- Provide appropriate codes for expenses.

**Accountability**

- Sensitize all stakeholders (beneficiaries, service providers, partners, government and other) on feedback and complaint mechanisms implemented by ZOA Uganda
- Upon receipt of a complaint or feedback, ensure that it is correctly documented following correct reporting procedures
- Understand ZOA’s code of conduct and safeguarding policies, ensure adherence to these policies and that project activities are implemented with a “Do No Harm” approach

**Your profile**

Identity

- The candidate is expected to fully support the vision, mission and Christian values 0f ZOA (see [https://www.zoa-international.com/corporate-identity](https://www.zoa-international.com/corporate-identity))

***Knowledge & Experience:***

- University degree in Hydraulic Engineering, Water Resource Engineering, environmental or public health or other related fields.
- 4+ years’ experience in WASH, preferably in a humanitarian setting (refugee camps, rural development, or emergency response) for first degree
- Experience in localisation approaches and working with local organisations
- A good command of English, including written reporting and activity reporting
- Experience of working with People with Disabilities is a plus
- Experience working in the refugee settlement context is advantageous
- Experience of working with OCHA or on emergency projects is desired

***Skills:***

- High level of networking capacities
- Experience of data analysis software (Arc GIS and SPSS) is an asset
- Experience of Engineering Software (Watercad, Epanet and Auto CAD etc)
- Knowledge of domestic water supply system hydraulic design
- Excellent communication and interpersonal
- Able to bridge differences and bring people together from different backgrounds
- Motivated to work independently / self-managing
- Good computer skills: Ms Excel and Ms Word;
- Self-motivator, able to take initiatives with limited supervision;
- Ability to drive a motorcycle with valid driving/riding license is a MUST.

***Attitude/behaviour:***

- High level of personal integrity;
- Flexibility and adaptability;
- Interpersonal and cross-cultural sensitivity;
- Able to work under pressures and meet deadlines;
- Able to work in a sometimes fluid and innovative environment;
- Commitment to ZOA’s mission, vision and values (see [https://www.zoa-international.com/corporate-identity](https://www.zoa-international.com/corporate-identity))

**Special conditions/circumstances**

The Project Coordinator WASH will be based in either Kiryandongo, Palorinya, or Rhino Camp refugee settlements.

Regular travel to field locations, sub counties and for meetings with project stakeholders is expected. The postholder is expected to regularly ride a motorcycle in rural conditions/on unmade roads.

The role is 1.0 FTE (40 hrs/ week). Working hours are outlined in the ZOA Uganda Employee Handbook. Some flexibility on working hours may be required, e.g. for travel at weekends, or during reporting times.

**Our offer**

- ZOA offers a challenging role in a dynamic context, and you will be part of an inspiring and motivated team.
- We offer good benefits and remuneration which suits the NGO sector.

Do you need more information?

For more information about ZOA, please visit our website [www.zoa-international.com](http://www.zoa-international.com/).

title: Adjoint·e Directeur Pays aux Programmes Tchad-Cameroun – basé à N’Djaména
body:
## **Contrat à durée déterminée : 6 mois à compter du 21/12/2026**

## **PUI aux quatre coins du monde**

**Forte de ses 40 années d’expérience, Première Urgence Internationale :**

- Vient en aide à près de **6** millions de bénéficiaires
- Avec un budget de plus de **100** millions € par an
- Répartis dans **22** pays, sur **5** continents

Grâce à l’implication et l’engagement de :

- Plus de **2000** collaborateurs nationaux
- Environ **200** expatriés de 45 nationalités différentes
- Et **90** salariés au siège

PUI œuvre dans 10 secteurs d’intervention et se distingue par la mise en place d’une approche intégrée dans sa réponse. Cette méthode vise à identifier et comprendre l’ensemble des besoins des personnes touchées par une crise. Nos équipes se mobilisent pour apporter une réponse globale à l’ensemble des besoins fondamentaux des populations victimes de crises humanitaires dans l’urgence jusqu’à leur permettre de retrouver autonomie et dignité.

Pour en savoir plus sur [notre histoire](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/notre-histoire/), [nos valeurs](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/notre-valeurs/), [nos domaines d’intervention.](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/nos-domaines-d-intervention/)

## **Et le.la Adjoint·e Directeur Pays aux Programmes dans tout ça?**

En tant qu’Adjoint·e Directeur Pays aux Programmes, vous serez responsable de la mise en œuvre des programmes à travers les différentes bases, en assurant le pilotage et le développement d’une stratégie de programme pertinente, appropriée et techniquement solide. A cet effet, vos responsabilités seront les suivantes :

- **Programmes :** Vous serez en charge de la mise en œuvre des programmes, en vous assurant que les programmes se déroulent conformément à la charte PUI et en respectant les directives techniques internes et les procédures contractuelles. Vous serez responsable du suivi de la réalisation des programmes au niveau de la mission. Vous serez en charge d’interpeller les bases sur les besoins d’amélioration de la qualité.
- **Développement/Stratégie :** Vous dirigerez l’analyse des besoins et des lacunes, et proposerez de nouvelles opérations en fonction des besoins identifiés, en coordination directe avec les Coordinateurs Terrain et les Coordinateurs Techniques. Vous dirigerez la cartographie des donateurs pour développer la stratégie de collecte de fonds.
- **Ressources Humaines :** Vous gèrerez directement l’équipe de coordination technique et vous assurerez que les Coordinateurs Terrain et les Coordinateurs Terrain Adjoints bénéficient de leur soutien.
- **Représentation :** Par délégation du Directeur Pays, vous assurerez et coordonnerez la représentation de PUI au niveau national auprès des partenaires, bailleurs et autorités. Vous participerez aux forums techniques (groupes de travail).
- **Coordination:** Vous assurerez l’interaction efficace entre l’équipe de coordination technique et les bases. Vous vous assurerez également que le département de coordination technique assure une liaison adéquate avec les Coordinateurs Supports.
- **Suivi logistique, administratif et financier:** Vous participerez, en collaboration directe avec les coordinateurs techniques, à la supervision globale des liens entre le département de coordination technique et les départements logistique, RH et administratif. Vous garantirez que la mise en œuvre de toutes les activités se fait dans le respect des cadres logistiques et administratifs internes et externes.

## **Les défis qui vous attendent**

- Assurer le financement des programmes au Cameroun et au Tchad pour 2027
- Renforcer les pratiques et les systèmes MEAL
- Consolider les relations avec nos partenaires locaux.

## **Ce qu’il vous faudra pour réussir**

- **Formation** : Vous pouvez justifier d’un diplôme supérieur (Master 2 ou équivalent) dans un domaine lié à la gestion de projet, au développement international et/ou aux sciences sociales.
- **Expérience** : Fort d’au moins quatre ans de gestion de projets humanitaires multisectoriels (dont au moins deux ans en position de coordination), vous avez également de l’expérience en gestion de projet, en évaluation des besoins et élaboration de propositions, en matière de représentation externe, et en gestion d’une équipe. Vous avez déjà travaillé avec Première Urgence Internationale ? Ce sera un atout indéniable !
- **Compétences** : Vous maitrisez la gestion de projet, la gestion d’équipe, ainsi que les logiciels de gestion de base de données et les progiciels statistiques. Vous avec une connaissance approfondie des exigences et des attentes des donateurs, en particulier ECHO, BHA, PAM, UNHCR, CDCS, AFD et BPRM, ainsi que d’excellentes compétences rédactionnelles (notamment pour les propositions et les rapports).
- **Qualités requises** : Vous montrez de solides compétences en matière de leadership et de prise de décisions. Vous disposez de bonnes capacités d’analyse et de synthèse, êtes un bon négociateur et un bon communiquant, autant à l’écrit qu’à l’oral, et savez garantir des résultats efficaces sous la pression des délais. Vous faites preuve d’organisation, de rigueur, de flexibilité et d’une forte résistance au stress.
- **Langues** : Le français et l’anglais n’ont aucun secret pour vous ? Tant mieux, c’est indispensable pour ce poste ! Si vous parlez aussi l’arabe, cela représentera un atout indéniable.

## **Le mot du manager**

*« PUI est présent au Tchad depuis plus de 20 ans à l’est du pays et au Cameroun depuis plus de 15 ans avec une présence dans l’Extrême Nord. En 2025, les deux bureaux-pays fusionnent avec une coordination basée à N’Djamena. Dans un contexte humanitaire complexe, nous recherchons un.e Adjoint.e Directeur de Pays passionné.e et expérimenté.e pour faire avancer les programmes de ces deux pays. »*

## **PUI vous proposera**

- **Statut :** Cadre en Contrat à Durée Déterminée
- **Salaire brut mensuel :** 2 970,00 – 3 330,00 EUR selon votre expérience en solidarité internationale + 50€ par semestre d’ancienneté avec PUI
- **Assurance** comprenant couverture médicale et complémentaire santé, assistance 24h/24, rapatriement et prévoyance
- **Hébergement** en maison collective
- **Frais de vie** (« Per Diem »)
- **Régime de breaks :** 5 jours ouvrés à 3 mois de mission
- **Régime de Congés Payés :** 5 semaines de CP/an

## **Nos engagements**

PUI s’engage à prévenir tout type de comportement indésirable au travail, y compris le harcèlement, l’exploitation et l’abus sexuels, le manque d’intégrité et l’inconduite financière, et à promouvoir le bien-être des enfants et des adultes avec lesquels PUI est en contact. PUI attend de toutes les personnes employées qu’elles s’acquittent de leurs tâches et responsabilités professionnelles conformément au Cadre Éthique de PUI.

Toutes les personnes employées par PUI suivront des formations appropriées, et s’engagent dans la promotion, la diffusion et le respect des principes édictés dans sa charte éthique.

Le/la titulaire de ce poste aura potentiellement accès à des données personnelles concernant des enfants et des adultes vulnérables dans le cadre de son travail (catégorie 2 dans la classification de risques du recrutement sûr). Ainsi, toutes les offres d’emploi seront soumises à des références satisfaisantes et à des vérifications appropriées, qui peuvent incluront des vérifications du casier judiciaire et du financement du terrorisme.

Première Urgence Internationale considère la diversité des nationalités, genres, croyances, profils et statuts au sein de ses Ressources Humaines comme un atout majeur pour son action humanitaire, et s’astreint donc au strict respect du principe de non-discrimination tout au long de son processus de recrutement. Nous encourageons les personnes candidates issues de milieux divers à postuler.

Veuillez noter que Première Urgence Internationale ne sollicitera en aucun cas une participation financière pour des frais administratifs liés au recrutement. Toute information allant dans ce sens serait frauduleuse, merci de ne pas en tenir compte.

**Nous vous encourageons à postuler au plus vite si le poste vous intéresse, car nous pourrions mettre fin au processus avant la date mentionnée ci-dessus si un candidat approprié est identifié.**

Vous vous reconnaissez dans ce profil et vous adhérez à nos engagements ? Vous vous sentez prêt·e à relever le **challenge** et à rejoindre la **grande famille PUI ?**

title: Medical Director
body:
We are looking for our next inspirational and impactful medical leader to fill the role of **Medical Director at MSF-OCA**. This position is central to the steering and implementation of our medical, humanitarian action, ensuring that our medical programming is responsive and adaptive, able to deliver the healthcare that is most needed where people are experiencing conflict, medical crises, social violence and healthcare exclusion and natural and environmental disasters.

As the **Medical Director**, you will be responsible for leading the organization’s overall medical strategy and medical quality agenda. You will ensure that MSF has the medical leadership and expertise, standards, policies and support systems needed to deliver safe, effective and dignified person-centred healthcare.

You directly report to the General Director of MSF Netherlands / OCA Management Team Chair and are member of the Management Team meetings of Operational Centre Amsterdam and MSF Netherlands, contributing to the overall strategic direction of the organization. As part of MSF’s international Medical Director platform, you participate in the medical leadership of the MSF movement.

**Key Responsibilities**

- You lead the public health department and the medical, humanitarian operations in OCA, steering by leading the development of medical strategy and assuring the comprehensive nature and quality of medical and public health policies.
- You enable the execution of programmes, you ensure the quality and professional range of medical leadership needed for this and drive innovation, monitoring, accountability and learning.
- You work with the Operations Director to steer the allocation of resouces to a diverse range of crises. You oversee the relationship and processes with other departments to realize synergy, effectiveness and efficiency. You both steer and participate in relevant OCA and NL management platforms.
- You are responsible for the integrity of MSF OCA’s medical programmes, including adherence to medical ethics and upkeep the principle of ‘do no harm’, providing the leadership towards medical ethical dilemmas, and the management of medical risks, in alignment with OCA’s overall risk appetite.
- You collaborate with Operations and other departments to ensure safeguarding considerations are embedded in MSF OCA’s medical programmes and ensure optimal use of information, technology and data in our medical programmes, in collaboration with ITD.
- You collaborate with other OCs, promoting mutual accountability and an optimal use of MSF resources via mutualisation and interoperability where it is effective and efficient to do so. You participate in the international MedDir platform, MedOps platform overseeing delegated intersectional medical platforms.
- You undertake external representation, towards relevant interlocuters in our countries of operations and at a global level, in pursuit of our medical strategic objectives.

**Who you are**

You are motivated by the work that MSF does, standing in solidarity with people experiencing medical, humanitarian crises, adapting as needs evolve and the provision of quality medical care. You are a strategic thinker with the ability to translate vision into actionable plans. You inspire your teams and model an organisational culture which is informed by our values, a transparent and learning culture. You build strong medical leadership, focusing on development and performance in a multicultural environment. You are collaborative, able to build consensus, and work effectively with diverse stakeholders. You maintain your focus on the overall objective while being pragmatic in the process. A position that balances hands-on leadership with strategic vision.

**Essential:**

- Medical Doctor with post-graduate training in public health.
- Professional proficiency in English.
- Strong communication skills: able to navigate through a complex organization.
- **12+ years of experience** in medical, humanitarian programming, senior management experience
- Broad knowledge of humanitarian medicine, health programming and research
- Demonstrated experience in strategic planning, budgeting.

**Desirable:**

- Professional proficiency in French, Arabic or Spanish.
- Experience working in an international or humanitarian context, with an understanding of the challenges of operating in low-resource settings.
- A deep commitment to the principles and values of Médecins Sans Frontières.

**What we offer**

- A fixed-term, 3 years contract with renewal option for another 3 years. This position is mandated to be 6 years maximum.
- Gross monthly salary between € 7,987 – € 10,996 scaling within the range depending on experience.
- 30 days annual leave (full-time) plus 8% holiday allowance.
- A competitive pension scheme.
- Commuting allowance.
- Access to a large variety of internal training.
- An inclusive workplace with colleagues from around the globe.

title: Global Supply Chain Localisation Advisor
body:
Every year, humanitarian organisations rely on supply chains to deliver life-saving assistance to people affected by conflict, displacement, disasters and crises around the world. Strengthening the role of local actors within these supply chains — and how international and local actors plan, coordinate and deliver together — is a key part of building more sustainable and locally led humanitarian responses

The Danish Refugee Council (DRC), one of the world's leading humanitarian NGOs, is looking for a highly qualified and experienced supply chain professional to help drive this agenda at a global level. In this role, you will contribute to shaping how humanitarian organisations work with local actors and communities, helping ensure that critical humanitarian assistance can be delivered more effectively, efficiently and sustainably where it is needed most

**About the job**

DRC is committed to advancing supply chain localisation as a key strategic objective, working together with the Humanitarian Leadership Group on Supply Chain (HLGSC), a cross-sector initiative bringing together humanitarian organisations, donors and partners to strengthen end-to-end supply chains across the system.

As Global Supply Chain Localisation Advisor, you will provide strategic and technical leadership for the localisation workstream on behalf of DRC, acting as DRC's lead technical representative within HLGSC and working closely with UNICEF and other partners to shape, develop and strengthen the sector's approach to supply chain localisation. You will report to the Director of Supply Chain.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

- Provide technical leadership for the localisation workstream, helping shape the humanitarian sector's approach to supply chain localisation and supporting the delivery of agreed workstream objectives.
- Co-lead the development, testing and refinement of the Supply Chain Maturity Model, assessment methodology and associated guidance in collaboration with UNICEF and other workstream partners.
- Translate concepts, operational experience and stakeholder inputs into practical frameworks, guidance and tools that support localisation objectives across the sector.
- Act as DRC's lead technical representative within HLGSC, bringing DRC's operational experience, NGO perspectives, lessons learned and technical expertise to sector-wide discussions.
- Ensure alignment between the localisation workstream and DRC's wider localisation and supply chain priorities, including partner tiering approaches and partner supply chain management initiatives.
- Work collaboratively with UNICEF, co-lead organisations and technical experts to shape technical direction, build consensus and strengthen workstream outputs.
- Co-lead the technical content and preparation of expert group and technical working group engagements, including consultation materials, draft outputs and decision points for review.
- Provide technical guidance and thought leadership to stakeholders engaged in the workstream, ensuring existing initiatives, evidence and lessons learned are leveraged and duplication of effort is avoided.
- Review, validate and synthesise inputs from expert consultations, technical working groups, bilateral exchanges and testing activities, translating findings into strengthened methodologies, frameworks and recommendations.
- Support the preparation of outputs, recommendations and technical products for governance review, decision-making and endorsement.
- Lead the documentation of lessons learned, evidence gaps, limitations and considerations for the future stewardship, maintenance and evolution of the Supply Chain Maturity Model

To be successful in this role we expect you to bring substantial supply chain experience across HQ and country-office settings, strong technical credibility on maturity and capacity assessments, and the ability to lead and influence across organisations without formal line authority. Moreover, we also expect the following:

**Required**

- 7-10 years of experience working in HQ and Country Offices, especially in supply chain and related support functions.
- Supply Chain master's degree or equivalent academic qualification.
- Demonstrated ability to lead technical content development, working within a collaborative co-lead model and influencing, convening and synthesising across organisations without formal line authority.
- Strong track record of representing an organisation in external, multi-stakeholder technical forums.
- Fluency in English is required.

**Desirable**

- Experience working with local partners.
- Experience related to maturity assessments and capacity assessments of partners or markets.
- Familiarity with localisation initiatives (e.g. Grand Bargain / IASC localisation commitments).
- Working knowledge of French.

All employees are expected to demonstrate DRC's five core competencies:

**Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

  
**We offer**

**Contract length:** 12 months, in line with the current implementation period of the HLGSC localisation workstream action — any extension subject is to continued funding and workstream priorities.

**Work location:** Lyngbyvej 100, 2100 Copenhagen Ø, just by Ryparken station. The role requires travel as needed, estimated at once every 3 months.

**Start date:** 1st November 2026

The position is temporary, based on project employment linked to the current 12-month HLGSC localisation workstream action and its funding.

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with the agreement between DRC and AC. This is a national position for which local terms and conditions apply.

We welcome all nationalities to apply for the role. If you do not have the existing right to work in Denmark, DRC will support with applying and paying for a work permit.

  
**Further information**

For questions regarding the vacancy please contact Gaurav Verma at **Gaurav.verma@drc.ngo** . We will do our best to respond to as many inquiries as possible.

For more information about the Danish Refugee Council, please visit our website [**drc.ngo**](https://drc.ngo/).

**Danish Refugee Council is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and positive work environment based on mutual respect for all employees. All applicants are considered for employment regardless of personal characteristics or attributes.**

title: BURKINA FASO / MALI - COORDINATEUR.TRICE GRANT ET PARTENARIAT (H/F) - OUAGADOUGOU
body:
## Que faisons nous ...

**Date de début souhaitée :** 07/10/2026  
**Durée de la mission :** 6 mois   
**Localisation:** Ouagadougou

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL** (SI) est une association d’aide humanitaire internationale qui, depuis plus de 40 ans, porte secours aux populations victimes de conflits armés et de catastrophes naturelles en répondant aux besoins vitaux, boire, manger, s’abriter. Particulièrement engagée dans le combat contre les maladies liées à l’eau insalubre, première cause de mortalité au monde, SI met en œuvre par ses interventions une expertise dans le domaine de l’accès à l’eau potable, l’assainissement et la promotion de l’hygiène mais également dans celui, essentiel, de la sécurité alimentaire et moyen d’existence. Présentes dans 26 pays, les équipes de SI - 3 200 personnes au total composées d’expatriés, de salariés nationaux, de permanents au siège, de quelques bénévoles…- interviennent avec professionnalisme et engagement dans le respect des cultures.

## La mission

Solidarités International a ouvert fin 2018 pour répondre aux besoins urgents des personnes déplacées par la crise sécuritaire frappant initialement les régions du Sahel et du Centre Nord au Burkina Faso. En 2024 l'empreinte humanitaire de Solidarités International s'est étendue avec des opérations au Centre nord, au Nord, au Sahel et dans la Boucle du Mouhoun.   
En 2025, le bureau pays est composé d’une coordination à Ouagadougou, de 2 bases terrains, une base Grand Nord à Ouahigouya- région du Nord qui couvre une sous-base à Kongoussi au Centre-Nord, et des interventions également dans la Boucle du Mouhoun avec notamment un bureau à Tougan ; ainsi qu' une base Sahel à Dori qui couvre les sous-bases de Djibo et de Sebba.  
SI a diversifié son portefeuille d’interventions pour adresser à la fois les besoins vitaux en EHA, abris et nourriture des populations récemment déplacées par le conflit (mécanisme RRM et autres interventions d’urgence) et l’impact du conflit sur l’accès aux services publics EHA et aux moyens d’existence, intégrant également le renforcement des institutions et les enjeux de cohésion sociale.  
La plupart des projets sont mis en œuvre en consortium avec des ONGI et sur certains projets avec des partenaires locaux  
SI fait partie de plusieurs consortiums tels que : RRM-Frontline (avec ACF comme lead), Réponse multisectorielle Santé Nut EHA SAME intégrée dans le Yagha (PUI lead du consortium)  
La mission Burkina Faso a un volume budgétaire de 4 millions d'euros essentiellement financé par : ECHO essentiellement.. Les activités sont mises en oeuvre avec un partenaire local, SOLIDEV et AFDR

En sep 2026, la mission est composée :

\- 1 bureau de Coordination à Ouagadougou : 3 expatriés (Coordo Log, Coordo Grants, Grants Manager, Coordo Pays HULO) et 50 employés nationaux dont le Directeur Pays, le Directeur Pays Adjoint aux Programmes ; la Responsable conformité, risques et transparence ; le Responsable des Partenariats Locaux ; le Coo RH et Coo admin ; la Coo Lead Cluster EHA ; le Coo EHA ; Coo SAME, le Coo SERA ; et les adjoint.e.s de chaque département

\- 2 bases composées de 1 expatriés et d’environ 60 staffs nationaux.

L'équipe Grants est basée à la coordination à Ouagadougou et est composée de 3 personnes : Coordinateur.trice Grants et Partenariats, Grants Manager et Responsable des Partenariats locaux.

La coordination du BFA appui la mission mali composé d'une cooRdination et d'une base (un coordination de zone)

## Descriptif de l'offre

**OBJECTIF GENERAL :**

Le/la Coordinateur/trice Grants et Partenariat pilote la stratégie partenariale et financière de la mission. Il/elle assure la coordination interdépartementale et apporte un appui stratégique sur les relations bailleurs, le cycle contractuel, les partenariats de mise en œuvre, la conformité et la redevabilité. Il/elle manage un Responsable partenarial local et une Grant Manager expatriée, en lien étroit avec le/la Directeur/trice Pays.

**ENJEUX ET DEFIS SPECIFIQUES :**

- Gestion d’un volume important de projets et de contrats bailleurs (6 en cours) ;
- Renforcement du reporting interne et des capacités des RP/RA, notamment sur les APU et la coordination PROG/SERA ;
- Mise en place de formations au reporting en capitale et sur les bases, selon le contexte sécuritaire ;
- Renforcement de la gestion des partenariats : plans de renforcement de capacités, pré-évaluation des partenaires et maintien du poste de Responsable partenarial ;
- Renforcement de la gestion des risques, audits et redevabilité bailleurs avec une ressource dédiée ;
- Appui à la mission MALI.

**PRIORITES SUR LES 2-3 PREMIERS MOIS :**

**Relations bailleurs :**  
Cartographier les bailleurs, assurer une veille sur les opportunités de financement et maintenir une communication régulière avec les bailleurs.

**Stratégie de financement :**  
Coordonner les besoins de financement entre mission et siège, contribuer à la stratégie financière et partenariale et suivre les plans d’action associés.

**Développement des documents de projet :**  
Coordonner les départements dans la préparation des propositions, rapports et demandes de modification contractuelle, en garantissant leur qualité.

**Gestion contractuelle :**  
Vérifier la faisabilité des termes contractuels, assurer le respect des procédures bailleurs, renforcer les capacités des équipes et suivre les demandes de versement jusqu’à la clôture des subventions, avec le coordinateur financier.

**Gestion des partenariats de mise en œuvre :**  
Identifier les partenaires, superviser les due diligences et contractualisations et assurer la coordination avec eux.

**Conformité externe et audits :**  
Coordonner les due diligences et audits externes, animer les formations sur les procédures bailleurs et assurer le lien avec les départements et le siège.

**Communication externe :**  
Transmettre au service communication du siège les contenus conformes aux obligations contractuelles.

**CONTRAINTES SECURITAIRES :**

Des restrictions de circulation s’appliquent dans certaines zones et quartiers. Le poste bénéficie d’un logement SI en guest partagé, avec eau, électricité et internet. Canal+ et du personnel de maison (agent d’entretien et cuisinier) sont également disponibles.

## Votre profil

**DIPLÔME ET EXPERIENCES**

Diplôme : Bac + 4/5 en Sciences politiques, Relations Internationales, Développement International ou équivalent.

- Expérience dans le secteur humanitaire : + de 5ans
- Expérience sur un poste similaire : 3/4ans

**SKILLS**

**Compétences techniques**

1. Bonne connaissance du fonctionnement, règles et procédures des bailleurs de fonds.
2. Expérience en reporting/propositions de projet
3. Grandes compétences en gestion d'équipes, hiérarchique et en renforcement de capacités
4. Capacités rédactionnelles, analyse et synthèse
5. Capacités d'initiative, rigueur et autonomie

**Compétence transcverses**

1. Adaptabilité
2. Management
3. Coordination

**Langues**

1. Français
2. Anglais

## SI vous offrira les conditions suivantes

**Un poste salarié :** Selon l'expérience, à partir de EUR 2860 bruts par mois (2600 salaire de base + 10% d'indemnité de congé annuel versée mensuellement) et un Per Diem mensuel de USD 550.

SI couvre également les frais de logement et les frais de déplacement entre le pays d'origine de l'expatrié et le lieu d'affectation.

**Breaks :** Pendant la mission, un système d'alternance entre travail et congés est mis en place à raison de 7 jours ouvrables tous les trois mois (avec USD 850 alloués par Solidarités International). A ces périodes de pause, s'ajoute un jour de repos supplémentaire par mois travaillé.

**Couverture sociale et médicale :** Les expatriés bénéficient d'une assurance qui rembourse tous les frais de santé (y compris les frais médicaux et chirurgicaux, les soins dentaires et ophtalmologiques, le rapatriement) et d'un système de prévoyance incluant les risques de guerre. Les frais de vaccination et de traitement antipaludéen indispensables sont remboursés.

**CONDITIONS DE VIE :**

La ville de Ouagadougou est la capitale du Burkina Faso et la plus grande ville du pays. La vie y est agréable. La ville bénéficie de nombreux restaurants et lieux de sortie. La vie culturelle y est très animée.  
Les expatriés ne sont pas autorisés à conduire leur véhicule personnel.  
La ville bénéficie d’une très bonne couverture téléphonique et internet, avec plusieurs opérateurs.

title: Area Manager
body:
Hoffnungszeichen | Sign of Hope e.V. (SoH) is a Christian-motivated international organization working in humanitarian relief, development cooperation and human rights. The organization was founded and is headquartered in Germany. SoH thematic focus areas include Health and Nutrition, WASH, Food Security and Sustainable Livelihoods, Access to Basic Education, Human Rights, Emergency Relief and Resilience Building through directly implemented and partner-implemented projects and programmes. SoH provides emergency relief worldwide and regionally while linking relief, rehabilitation and development measures.

The organization’s East Africa Branch (EAB) office is located in Nairobi, Kenya, with country offices across the East Africa Region. In South Sudan, SoH supports humanitarian, development and human rights programming through direct engagement and partnerships with local actors, with the Country Office based in Rumbek, Lakes State.

**Job Title:** **Area Manager**

**Reports to: Country Representative - South Sudan**

**Job Location: Unity State, South Sudan, with frequent travel to Rumbek, Lakes State, and other project locations. On request, the postholder may also be required to travel to neighbouring areas of Sudan, subject to security clearance, applicable permissions and SoH travel procedures.**

**Start Date:** **19th October 2026**

**Contract:** **11 months & 2 weeks (renewable subject to satisfactory performance and available project funding)**

**Summary of the job title**

The Area Manager will support the Country Representative - South Sudan in strengthening programme and project oversight across SoH-supported humanitarian, development and human rights programming in South Sudan, including resilience, recovery and nexus interventions where applicable. Based primarily in Unity State, the position will provide hands-on support to project implementation, project cycle and grant management, partner capacity assessment and strengthening, partner coordination and management, stakeholder engagement, monitoring, reporting, documentation, learning and compliance. The Area Manager will work closely with SoH partner organizations, Country Office colleagues, the East Africa Branch, Headquarters and relevant government, community, humanitarian, development and human rights stakeholders.

The role requires a highly organized, self-driven and adaptable professional who can work with minimal supervision, exercise sound judgement and manage multiple priorities in remote and complex operating environments. In addition to programme oversight, the Area Manager will support SoH visibility, communications and fundraising by identifying compelling and ethically documented programme results, human-interest stories, case studies and potential fundraising opportunities, and by developing high-quality content that demonstrates the impact of SoH-supported interventions. The position may support any SoH-funded or SoH-supported humanitarian, development or human rights project in South Sudan, depending on programme needs and priorities.

**Core duties**

1. **Programme, Project Cycle and Grant Oversight**

- Support day-to-day oversight of SoH-supported humanitarian, development and human rights projects in South Sudan, ensuring implementation remains aligned with approved proposals, workplans, budgets, donor requirements and SoH policies and procedures.
- Maintain regular follow-up with implementing partners and project teams on activity progress, deliverables, implementation challenges, agreed actions and reporting deadlines, and support preparation and updating of implementation plans, milestone trackers, risk registers and other project management tools.
- Undertake regular field monitoring visits to assess implementation progress, quality, relevance, accountability and emerging operational issues; identify bottlenecks and risks early and support timely corrective action in consultation with the Country Representative and relevant colleagues.
- Apply sound project cycle management across assessment, design, planning, implementation, monitoring, adaptation, reporting, evaluation and project closure, and support concept note and proposal development, project reviews and evaluations as requested.
- Support compliance with institutional donor requirements and SoH internal procedures, including review of partner deliverables, supporting documentation, project files and grant management records.
- Work closely with Finance and partners to monitor budget utilization and budget-versus-actual performance, identify significant variances, and contribute to project and partner budgets, procurement plans, forecasts and budget revisions where required.
- Support preparation of timely, high-quality donor reports and inputs for grant reviews, audits, monitoring visits and donor or management requests for information, while maintaining complete and audit-ready project documentation.
- Support humanitarian needs assessments, preparedness, emergency response coordination and monitoring when required, and provide practical programme support during evolving crises.

**2. Partner Capacity, Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement**

- Undertake and coordinate organizational and project-specific capacity assessments of current and prospective local implementing partners using SoH tools and agreed due-diligence processes.
- Support development and follow-up of partner capacity-strengthening plans covering programme and grant management, financial management, monitoring and evaluation, safeguarding, accountability, human rights and protection-sensitive programming, documentation and reporting.
- Maintain structured communication with partners, facilitate coordination and review meetings, document agreed actions, follow up commitments and support partner performance monitoring against contractual obligations, workplans, budgets and quality standards.
- Support the Country Representative in maintaining effective relationships with government authorities, local administrations, communities, civil society and human rights actors, humanitarian and development coordination structures, UN agencies, NGOs/INGOs, donors and other relevant stakeholders.
- Participate in and, when delegated, represent SoH in coordination meetings, technical forums, project reviews, partner meetings and stakeholder engagements, ensuring relevant information and agreed actions are communicated and followed up internally.
- Support stakeholder mapping and maintain an up-to-date understanding of key actors, coordination platforms, programme and funding opportunities, operational constraints and emerging needs relevant to SoH programming.
- Promote respectful, transparent and mutually accountable partnerships consistent with SoH’s localization approach and facilitate effective information flow between field locations, partners, the South Sudan Country Office, the East Africa Branch and Headquarters.
    
    **3. Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, Learning and Reporting**
- Support establishment and use of practical project monitoring systems and tools, including indicator tracking, activity and output monitoring, partner reporting schedules and field monitoring plans.
- Review partner narrative and monitoring reports for completeness, accuracy and consistency with agreed indicators, targets, workplans and project results, and support data quality verification where required.
- Ensure monitoring findings, community feedback, implementation evidence and lessons learned are documented and used to improve programme quality, decision-making and adaptive management.
- Prepare, consolidate and contribute to clear, analytical and high-quality internal, donor and management reports, briefing notes, field visit reports, presentations, case studies and other programme documentation.
- Facilitate documentation and sharing of lessons learned, good practices, challenges and innovations across projects, partners and relevant SoH teams.
    
    **4 . Human Rights, Humanitarian Quality and Accountability**
- Support implementation and monitoring of SoH-supported human rights projects and the application of rights-based approaches where relevant, including participation, inclusion, non-discrimination and accountability.
- Promote adherence to humanitarian principles, accountability to affected populations, safeguarding, protection mainstreaming, conflict sensitivity and do-no-harm approaches across programme implementation.
- Ensure sensitive human rights, protection and community information is handled with appropriate confidentiality, informed consent, dignity, data protection and referral considerations in line with SoH procedures.
- Identify significant programme, protection, human rights, partner or operational concerns requiring escalation or technical support and communicate them promptly to the Country Representative.

**5. Visibility, Communications and Fundraising Support**

- Proactively identify strong programme results, human-interest stories, case studies and community perspectives that demonstrate the relevance and impact of SoH-supported humanitarian, development and human rights interventions.
- Identify potential fundraising stories, cases, programme needs and funding opportunities that can be developed further for institutional, private or public fundraising, and communicate these promptly to the Country Representative and relevant SoH fundraising or communications colleagues.
- Develop high-quality written content including success stories, case studies, project updates, field briefs, captions, quotations and other materials for donor engagement, fundraising, reporting, organizational learning and external communication.
- Support collection and management of appropriate photographs, video clips, testimonials and other communication materials in accordance with informed consent, safeguarding, dignity, confidentiality, security and data protection requirements, with particular care in human rights and protection-related contexts.
- Support compliance with donor visibility and branding requirements, maintain an organized bank of approved communication materials, and contribute to donor, partner, media or stakeholder visits, presentations and visibility activities when requested.

The duties and responsibilities set out above are not exhaustive. The Area Manager may be required to undertake other reasonable assignments consistent with their skills and experience and with SoH programme priorities in South Sudan.

**Candidates’ profile**

- A minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in International Development, Project Management, Humanitarian Action, Development Studies, Human Rights, Law, Disaster Risk Management, Social Sciences, Public Health, Agriculture, Natural Resources Management or another relevant field.
- A minimum of five years of progressively responsible experience in project or programme implementation, coordination or management, preferably in humanitarian, development and/or human rights programming in fragile or crisis-affected contexts.
- Demonstrated practical experience in humanitarian programming, including emergency response, recovery, resilience or humanitarian-development nexus programming. Experience with human rights or rights-based programming is an added advantage.
- Strong practical knowledge of the project management cycle, including assessment, design, planning, budgeting, implementation, monitoring, reporting, evaluation and project closure.
- Demonstrated experience working with institutional donor grants. Experience with German institutional donors, particularly BMZ and GFFO, is strongly preferred; relevant experience with other institutional donors will also be considered.
- Proven experience in partner coordination and management, including partner capacity assessment, accompaniment, performance follow-up and capacity strengthening, together with strong stakeholder engagement and facilitation skills.
- Good understanding of grant compliance, budget monitoring, results-based monitoring and evaluation, data quality, financial follow-up and use of evidence to improve programme implementation.
- Excellent written and verbal communication and report-writing skills, with demonstrated ability to produce clear, analytical and high-quality donor and management reports and to engage effectively with diverse stakeholders.
- Strong organizational, analytical and problem-solving skills, with demonstrated ability to work with minimal supervision, exercise sound judgement, manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines in demanding environments.
- Experience supporting organizational visibility, communications or development of human-interest stories and case studies is desirable. Previous involvement in identifying fundraising-ready stories, cases or programme opportunities is an added advantage.
- Knowledge of humanitarian principles, accountability to affected populations, safeguarding, protection mainstreaming, conflict sensitivity and rights-based approaches.
- Advanced working knowledge of MS Word, Excel and PowerPoint, including effective use of spreadsheets for project tracking, budget follow-up and reporting.
- Excellent spoken and written English. Knowledge of relevant local languages is an advantage.
- Willingness and ability to travel frequently to remote project locations in South Sudan and, when formally requested and authorized, to neighbouring areas of Sudan, and to work effectively in multicultural, insecure and resource-constrained environments.

**Conditions:**

• Duration of contract: 11 months & 2 weeks (renewable subject to satisfactory performance and available project funding)

• Salary according to qualification and experience

title: ICLA Project Manager South Central Syria
body:
**Background**

As the Syrian crisis has entered its 14th year, a record-level 16.7 million people, over 71% of the population, needs humanitarian assistance. Almost half are children. The former government's change in December 2024 sparked hope for the country’s future and for those in need of aid. However, ongoing conflict, economic collapse and record-high humanitarian needs persist throughout the country, coinciding with unprecedented cuts to humanitarian aid globally at a time when aid resources for Syria were already stretched thin.

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) has been a leading humanitarian actor in the response to the Syria crisis, in Syria and across the region, since 2012. Against a backdrop of conflict, socioeconomic and environmental deterioration, climate change and natural disasters, we provide emergency, transitional, early recovery and resilience programmes to people in need. We lead advocacy to promote unimpeded and sustained access to assistance for people across Syria and we call for increased humanitarian funding, resilience and early recovery support to alleviate the hardships of the Syrian people.

**What we are looking for**

NRC Syria looking for an ICLA Project Manager to join the **South-Central Area Office**. The role holder will be responsible for responsible for managing the overall NRC ICLA project portfolio and staffing in South and Central Syria. They will also contribute to the broader country-level programme development in collaboration with the ICLA Specialist. Additionally, they will contribute to the broader country level programme development in collaboration with the ICLA Specialist.

\*\***\*\*Please note for this role, applicants must be legally eligible to work in Syria. We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position. \*\***

**What you will do**

**The role will have some of the following main specific responsibilities:**

- Lead strategic planning for the ICLA programme in South and Central Syria, including legal needs assessments, gap analyses, and prioritisation.
- Review referral mechanisms for ICLA interventions in South and Central Syria and propose improvements aligned with area office response priorities.
- In close coordination with the ICLA Specialist, review ICLA field team structures and job descriptions to align with strategic objectives, and lead recruitment processes as needed.
- Ensure consistent quality and legal compliance across all ICLA services (legal counselling, information provision, representation, and referrals).
- Ensure accurate and consistent use of ICLA case management and M&E tools and integrate evidence and learning into programme development.
- Oversee legal accuracy of information and advice provided to project participants.
- Support the ICLA specialist in developing and adapting legal tools, case management systems, and training materials.
- Support the ICLA specialist to guide legal research, analysis, and advocacy messaging in line with field evidence and ICLA’s strategic objectives.
- Actively participate in relevant humanitarian coordination forums, including leading the Housing, Land and Property (HLP) Technical Working Group (where relevant).
- Strengthen collaboration with protection actors, legal aid providers, justice sector stakeholders, and local authorities.
- Promote operational synergies between ICLA and other NRC core competencies/programmes.
- Identify staff training needs and coordinate the delivery of legal and soft skills capacity building.
- Participate in and support project start-up, progress review, and closure meetings with relevant inputs and documentation.
- Coordinate new emergency response in Area, and approve existing ones
- Carry out any other task relevant to the position as requested by the Area Programme Manager or ICLA Specialist.

Please download the complete Job Description [here](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQAof5x3mHr9Q6lZZ_cV0uFGAd_6avh3Szy0B9zaEF7i0CA?e=Tbejqs) to learn more about the position.

**What you will bring**

- **Relevant university degree**, preferably law, human rights or social studies, master’s degree is an added value.
- **Minimum 3 years of experience** in a senior-level legal assistance (or Protection project with significant legal assistance component) project management position in a humanitarian/ recovery context.
- **ICLA (Legal) technical expertise**, including knowledge of **Housing, Land & Property and/or civil documentation issues.**
- Experience working in **complex and volatile contexts.**
- **Fluency in English**, both written and verbal.
- Knowledge of the **displacement context in Syria and the Middle East.**
- Experience with **Legal programming and Legal case management**
- Fluency in **Arabic is a MUST.**

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: **Homs**, Syria.
- \*\*\*\***Please note for this role, applicants must be legally eligible to work in Syria. We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.** \*\*
- Contract: Fixed Term
- Travel: **30-40%** within areas of operation
- Salary/benefits: Grade 8 on NRC’s national salary scale
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity Marketplace.
- For internal candidates please use your official email address when applying
- Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- If you have any questions about this role, please email **mero.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

NRC currently has over 3,000 staff across the Middle East dedicated to assisting people affected by conflict in Jordan, Syria, Lebanon, Iraq, Libya and Palestine. Its humanitarian interventions are based upon its programming expertise in the Core Competencies of Shelter, Education, WASH, Livelihoods and Food Security, and Information Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA) to vulnerable displaced people that were forced to flee.

 [Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

Learn more about NRC's operations in Syria [here.](https://www.nrc.no/countries/middle-east/Syria)

title: Head of Communications and Engagement
body:
**EXTERNAL ANNOUNCEMENT**

**TITLE: Head of Communications and Engagement**

**Contract Type: National**

**TEAM/PROGRAMME: Advocacy, Campaign, Communications and Media (ACCM)**

**LOCATION: Bangkok, Thailand**

**CONTRACT LENGTH: Open-ended**

**ROLE PURPOSE:**

The Head of Communications and Engagement will provide overall leadership, management and strategic direction to Save the Children’s communications, campaigns, media, brand, and broader audience engagement work in Thailand. S/he will oversee the development and implementation of communication strategies that strengthen Save the Children’s reputation, increase public awareness of children’s issues, enhance audience engagement, and support communications for fundraising.

The post holder will ensure Save the Children’s representation, communications activities, content and products are coherent, creative, impactful and effective in order to achieve policy change, public awareness and behavioural shifts that improve the lives and uphold the rights of vulnerable and marginalised children in Thailand, in line with the organisation’s strategic priorities. Working closely with the Strategy, Programme Quality and Impact (SPQI) Director and Executive Director (ED), the post holder plays a critical role in networking and relationship building with relevant external stakeholders and represents the organisation’s views as needed. The post holder will also develop and implement effective communications and media strategies that increase visibility, supporter engagement and public trust.

The post holder will play a key role in developing compelling content and engagement strategies across digital, media and public channels, while supporting donor visibility, resource mobilisation and individual giving initiatives.

The post holder will report directly to the Executive Director and work closely with the SPQI Director, fundraising teams and programme teams, to identify influencing and communication opportunities as well as proposals that will require inputs on campaigns, visibility and communications. This role will collaborate closely with the relevant colleagues in global teams as well as other Save the Children organisations in the region to ensure the effective delivery of campaign and communication strategies.

**SCOPE OF ROLE:**

**Reports to:** Executive Director

**Staff reporting to this post:** Communications and Multimedia Coordinator, Communications officer, Brand and Media Coordinator, Comms and Engagement intern.

**Role Dimensions:** Regular contact with content, campaign and communications staff in other organisations, local implementing partners, and Save the Children staff from global, member and regional teams. This post holder will manage project specific comms and engagement budgets.

**KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY:**

**Communications and Media**

- Ensure good external representation of Save the Children through communications materials and the management of Save the Children's online and offline presence for Thailand.
- Ensure safeguarding in content collection and dissemination and guide the creation compelling content that elevates the voices of communities especially children and showcases Save the Children's impact.
- Develop and lead a communications strategy that identifies key audiences and develops key messages and products
- Ensure communication products effectively communicate programme impact to supporters, donors and the wider public.
- Oversee production of high-quality, accurate, clear and consistent information and communications outputs that highlight the situation in Thailand for children, including case studies, feature stories, and blogs with support from Communication Coordinator
- Ensure brand consistency and integrity across all platforms and products.
- Oversee production of high-quality information and education materials, and/or visually appealing and brand-aligned external marketing materials for programme teams according to strategic priorities with support from Communication Officer/Consultant
- Support the development of communication strategic plans for programme teams
- Support Business Development and Fundraising teams through donor-facing communications materials, campaign messaging and stewardship content.
- Lead Thailand’s media strategy for both national and international media (based in Thailand) where appropriate to ensure that Save the Children is front and centre of issues in the news spotlight that concern children in Thailand.
- Build, maintain and grow relationships with legacy media and new media in Thailand and support the team to ensure timely and effective media coverage.
- Aim to make Save the Children the Number 1 share of voice in the media whenever possible on high visibility issues and crises impacting children in Thailand.
- Support the team to ensure a strong bench of trained and capable media spokespeople who can speak confidently to national and international media about our responses and programmes.
- Oversee regular monitoring of local media coverage of key issues related to children and Save the Children in Thailand. Ensure team oversight of media field visits in Thailand. Support local media monitoring in Thailand as appropriate.
- Oversee website content strategy and digital content optimisation to improve audience engagement and supporter conversion.

**Campaigns**

- Support the development of clear and realistic communications and content to support campaign initiatives by thematic sectors.
- Support program, project staff and partner organisations to articulate their priority campaign objectives and develop realistic strategies and plans for achieving programs’ objectives.
- Ensure that the Executive and SPQI Directors are equipped with up-to-date key messages and tools to inform their dialogue and representation.
- In collaboration with the Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) team and relevant programme staff, establish monitoring and evaluation mechanisms for campaigns and ensure that implementation and impact are effectively monitored and evaluated, and lessons documented and shared.
- Lead in identifying and managing potential risks associated with Save the Children's public positions on issues and design strategies to mitigate the risks that have been identified.
- Work with Save the Children regional and global Advocacy, Campaign, Communication and Media (ACCM) teams to ensure linkages of local, national and global communications and campaign issues in a manner that informs Save the Children at all levels to ensure coherence of messaging.

**Management and Capacity Building**

- Supervise Comms and Engagement team members and consultants to achieve results. Provide mentoring, coaching and structured professional development. Resolve any conflicts or issues in individual and/or team performance and ensure staff wellbeing.
- Provide regular reports on Comms and Engagement activities and relevant KPIs to Executive and SPQI Directors when appropriate.
- Ensure regular reports are produced highlighting communication performance, audience engagement, digital growth, media reach and fundraising-related communications outcomes.
- Build capacity of programme staff and partners to contribute high-quality stories, content and communication products that strengthen organisational visibility and engagement.

**Emergencies**

- In times of crisis, be ready to change priorities rapidly and support an emergency response including by working outside of normal business hours and days, and deploying to field locations
- Collaborate with regional and global teams to ensure the timely capture, processing, and coordination of emergency-related content

**BEHAVIOURS (Values in Practice):**

**Accountability:**

- Holds self-accountable for making decisions, managing resources efficiently, achieving and role modelling Save the Children values
- Holds the team and partners accountable to deliver on their responsibilities - giving them the freedom to deliver in the best way they see fit, providing the necessary development to improve performance and applying appropriate consequences when results are not achieved.

**Ambition:**

- Sets ambitious and challenging goals for themselves and their team, takes responsibility for their own personal development and encourages their team to do the same
- Widely shares their personal vision for Save the Children, engages and motivates others
- Future orientated, thinks strategically and on a global scale.

**Collaboration:**

- Builds and maintains effective relationships, with their team, colleagues, Members and external partners and supporters
- Values diversity, sees it as a source of competitive strength
- Approachable, good listener, easy to talk to.

**Creativity:**

- Develops and encourages new and innovative solutions
- Willing to take disciplined risks.

**Integrity:**

- Honest, encourages openness and transparency; demonstrates highest levels of integrity

**QUALIFICATIONS**:

- At least 10 years' experience in communications, media management, brand management, public engagement, digital communications, fundraising communications or related fields within NGOs, INGOs, development organisations or the private sector.
- Priority will be given to Thai nationals
- Experience in digital audience engagement, supporter communications, fundraising communications or brand management is an advantage.
- Fluent in both spoken and written English and Thai (highly desirable)
- Relevant bachelor’s degree

**EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS**

**Essential**

- Experience developing and implementing integrated communications, brand and audience engagement strategies.
- Experience of working on human development, social justice, or rights-based issues
- Experience in both pro-active and re-active media management (crisis comms)
- Experience developing and implementing digital marketing strategies
- Experience in storytelling through multimedia and writing.
- Excellent personal organisational skills, including time management, and ability to meet deadlines and work under pressure
- Good coordination and networking skills
- Proven ability to encourage innovation and teamwork.
- Ability to work collaboratively with colleagues across the organisation developing effective working relationships
- Excellent English communications skills, both written and oral
- Commitment to and understanding of Save the Children’s aims, values and principles.

**Desirable**

- Experience of working in collaboration with programme teams across one or more of Save the Children\*\*’\*\*s sectors i.e.child poverty, child protection, child rights governance, education, health and nutrition, child safety or for similar cause-based agencies.
- Experience working with or alongside creative marketing agencies
- Direct experience as a journalist, or skills in design, videography or photography.
- Self-starter and be able to initiate ideas

**Additional job responsibilities**

Lead organisational communication strategies, brand visibility initiatives, supporter engagement activities and national public launches. Support proposal development through communications and visibility planning. Oversee communications, media, digital engagement and fundraising communications functions.

title: EMERGENCY PROGRAMME COORDINATOR
body:
About : Action contre la Faim

Created in 1979, Action contre la Faim is a non-governmental organization that fights against hunger. Its charter of humanitarian principals- independence, neutrality, non-discrimination, free and direct access to victims, professionalism, transparency - has been part of its identity for 45 years. Its mission is to save lives by eliminating hunger through the prevention, detection and treatment of under-nutrition, particularly during and after emergency situations linked to conflicts or natural disasters. Action contre la Faim focuses its actions on 7 main areas of expertise: Nutrition and Health - Mental Health, Psychosocial Support - Food Security and Livelihoods - Water, Sanitation and Hygiene - Advocacy - Climate - Research. In 2024, Action contre la Faim provided aid to more than 26 million people in 57 countries worldwide. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Under the supervision of the Deputy Country Director for Programmes, your mission will be to strengthen the country office's emergency preparedness and response capacities to ensure timely, effective, and coordinated emergency responses, and lead the implementation of emergency responses across all areas of intervention of ACF in Yemen.  
The main responsibilities and challenges of the position will be as follows:  
Strengthen and operationalize the country office's emergency preparedness and response system to ensure readiness for emergenciesDevelop and maintain up to date emergency preparedness and contingency plans  
Design, maintain up to date and lead the implementation of emergency response standard operating procedures in line with ACF programme, finance, logistics, human resources, and security policies and procedures  
Lead and coordinate emergency responses implemented by the country office to ensure providing timely and quality humanitarian assistance to populations affected by crisesEnsure continuous monitoring and analysis of the humanitarian, political, and operational context to identify emerging risks and response opportunities  
Lead the activation of emergency responses in line with ACF's procedures and agreed decision-making mechanisms  
Strengthen ACF's engagement with donors, partners, and through coordination mechanisms to enhance ACF's emergency positioning and resource mobilization capacityMonitor key humanitarian developments, donor priorities, and funding opportunities relevant to emergency preparedness and response  
Represent ACF in humanitarian coordination fora: clusters, working groups and inter-agency fora etc.  
Promote ACF's emergency response capacities, experience, and strategic priorities to external stakeholders (donors, partners etc.)

  
Profile :

 You hold a Master's Degree in International relations/humanitarian work or any other related field.

You master English (written and spoken)  
Having a previous experience in Yemen is an asset.

Monthly gross salary from 2597 to 2968euros upon experience, including 13th month
