title: Director, Medical
body:
**JOB SUMMARY:** The Medical Director is primarily responsible for technical vision, strategy, design, implementation and management of the health programs at senior management level. The Medical Director will work in collaboration with the senior management team and health teams in the field to deliver high-quality health services to the targeted beneficiaries. The Medical Director will make frequent visits to the field sites to ensure the highest standards of service delivery. This role will ensure high-quality clinical services in all IMC-supported health facilities. The role will monitor service quality, ensure that all staff are trained and well-supported, pharmaceuticals and other medical supplies are properly managed, and apply clinical-level data to national-level quality improvement efforts. The Medical Director will represent IMC in the national Health Cluster, Health Forum and other technical and health-strategic inputs during proposal development periods.

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential function with or without reasonable accommodation.

**MAIN TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Technical Monitoring and Program Quality**

- Provide technical supervision of, and technical support to the organization’s health programming activities.
- Ensure activities are consistent with established best practices, acceptable international (WHO/Sphere) and national standards as well as ensure programs across different sites in the country are of comparable quality by encouraging transfer of good practices from one field site to another.
- Ensure health programs utilize standardized protocols, policies and guidelines according to the Ministry of Health and WHO.
- Work closely with the country director, senior management and field teams to determine the operational needs of the medical program within the scope of the grants;
- Oversee the collection and timely reporting of data and statistics for all programs (including objectives, indicators and outcomes of health programs) according to internal and donor requirements
- Review monthly field and donor reports and ensure appropriate follow-up and decision making on data relevant to the organization’s health programs;
- Where feasible work with government health authorities and international agencies such as WHO to ensure implementation of standardized national health information systems
- Work with field teams, partner agencies (when applicable) and national health authorities for outbreak preparedness and contingency planning
- Ensure timely and adequate provision of supplies and drugs through review of pharmacy consumption reports, national drug protocols, program budgets, acquisition of partner agency and UN drug kits, and health information materials.
- Ensure all stakeholders, including senior management team, the Technical Unit and donors are provided with updates, following the established reporting structures.
- Ensure all IMC staff are trained on the IMC Accountability Code;
- Inform beneficiaries about their rights and the existence of the circuit to formulate complaints in case of non-satisfaction so that corrective measures are applied;
- Assist staff in charge of satisfaction questionnaire administration to perform their work independently without interference;
- Collaborate with M/E department to enable the proper implementation of the complaint management mechanism and its functioning;
- Work with M/E department to ensure that feedback from communities is part of the M/E exercises, and features in M/E and program reports;

**Program Development**

- Establish and build the capacity of a country technical unit which should include program and sector leads to be engaged in business strategic planning and development
- Work with senior management team, field teams, regional desk and the Technical Unit in strategic planning for future health programs.
- Work with Programs Director and management team to draft concepts for future funding following the protocols and formats of each relevant donor.
- Provide technical input during proposal development and technical reviews, and feedback to the field to improve the quality of the final proposals;
- Strive to ensure as much as possible different health related sectors (Mental health, Nutrition, and VAWG) are integrated into proposed programs.
- Work with senior management team to improve understanding of and engagement with donors to improve awareness of IMC’s activities, capacity and strategy and understand donor priorities

**Representation**

- Represent the organization to UN, health cluster, international and national NGOs and Ministry of Health at health coordination meetings as well as other meetings which are relevant to country programs and enhance the organization’s visibility (i.e. task force meetings, assessment missions, camp coordination meetings, UN coordination meetings, INGO coordination meetings)
- Serve as the principal liaison with MOH on matters related to the program to ensure programmatic accountability contributes to the creation of a positive image and overall credibility of the organization, notably through the application of the organizations Code of Conduct, ethics, values and standpoint regarding internal and external actors.
- Represent IMC and its health programs at donor meetings and with other stakeholders as needed
- Promote health programming and staff at senior management team meetings, pipeline meetings and other internal forums as needed

**Human Resources Management**

- Assist in the recruitment, selection and training of qualified program health staff.
- Maintain open lines of communication with all field staff
- Train senior national staff to increase their responsibilities to build capacity and ensure sustainability of programs.
- Ensure professional development for expat and national health staff through assessment of training needs and capacity building activities.
- Work closely with the health teams to determine the training needs of the medical staff.
- Overseeing trainings of all national healthcare staff, including national Doctors, non-physician clinicians, nurses, midwives and other technical staff to ensure that the provided trainings are of acceptable quality and address the identified needs and to ensure sustainability of programs

**Working Relationships**

- Work closely with country senior management team and the Health Technical Unit
- Ensure program process through communication with country team to ensure coordination of programs supplies are consistent with management of budgets, including budget forecasting, development of spending plans.

**Security**

- Collaborate with security officer/CD to maintain security of health staff in the field
- Ensure application and compliance of security protocols and policies

Perform other duties as assigned. The duties and responsibilities listed in this document are representative of the nature and level of work assigned and not necessarily comprehensive.

Job Requirements

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- A Medical degree, with a master's degree in public health preferred. An equivalent combination of relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate.
- Typically, 10+ years of relevant and progressive experience in health programs (preferably developing country or low-resource setting with an NGO) and at least 7+ years at the senior management level with project design, development of concept notes and technical proposals, and the management of projects relating to primary health care, maternal and child health, maternal and newborn health (MNH), infectious diseases, non-communicable diseases, emergency response, public health or other aspects of health programming as appropriate to the context
- Experience in effectively dealing with international and headquarters staff, as well as donor agencies, government officials, and other NGO’s
- Experience managing multiple projects across several grants in a complex and dynamic country context
- Must have excellent communications skills, both oral and written
- Excellent organizational skills and ability to handle multiple tasks in a dynamic environment
- Ability to relate to and motivate staff effectively
- Creativity and the ability to work with limited resources
- Able to analyze and interpret data and track program performance against program indicators
- Possess excellent facilitation skills
- Ability to effectively present information and respond appropriately to questions from various stakeholders (i.e.: senior managers, counterparts, senior government and rebel leaders and other related regional players)
- Ability to work with a broad spectrum of people

Additional Technical or Language Requirements

## Ethical Conduct at International Medical Corps

As part of a global, humanitarian team dedicated to saving lives, easing suffering, and building self-reliance, International Medical Corps staff are responsible for adhering to our Code of Conduct and Ethics and for knowing and abiding by International Medical Corps policies and standards. All staff play a vital role in preventing violations of our Code of Conduct and Ethics, including conflicts of interest, fraud, corruption, and any kind of exploitation or abuse. International Medical Corps is also committed to providing a safe and healthy work environment free of harassment, bullying, and other misconduct, enabling staff to build and maintain professional, respectful working relationships.

International Medical Corps prioritizes safeguarding the populations with whom we work from exploitation, neglect, or abuse of children and adults at risk, and/or any form of trafficking in persons. International Medical Corps is committed to engaging members of crisis-affected communities to participate in meaningful ways in a crisis response, including making informed decisions about the assistance they receive, mitigating potential risks, and holding us accountable for the commitments we make. All staff are expected to support International Medical Corps’ culture of accountability toward our stakeholders, particularly the crisis-affected communities and individuals we serve.

As part of International Medical Corps’ commitment to a speak-up culture and as one of the primary ways we collectively hold ourselves accountable for complying with the ethical principles and standards of conduct outlined in the Code of Conduct and Ethics, all staff are required to report suspected or actual misconduct or violations of organizational policies. Our Code of Conduct and Ethics and Whistleblower Policy prohibit any form of retaliation against whistleblowers or individuals who report a concern in good faith. Staff who violate these protections may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment or contractual relationship with International Medical Corps.

## Equal Opportunities

International Medical Corps is proud to provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, age, disability or status as a veteran.

## Misconduct Disclosure Scheme

All offers of employment at International Medical Corps are subject to satisfactory references and background checks. International Medical Corps participates in the Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme from the Steering Committee for Humanitarian Response (SCHR). In accordance with this, we will request information from an applicant’s previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her understanding of these recruitment procedures.

UKRAINE - HEAD OF SECURITY & HUMANITARIAN ACCESS (M/F) - KYIV
body:
**Desired start date:** ASAP  
**Duration of the mission:** 5 months  
**Location:** Kyiv

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

**ABOUT THE MISSION**

Since the beginning of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine by Russian forces, SI has been responding to the needs of the population living in areas under Government control. While programming in 2022 and 2023 was—rightly—focused on immediate emergency response, the year 2024 marked a transition toward a more balanced approach, combining both emergency and early recovery interventions.  
SI’s main strategic objective for 2026 is to strengthen and clearly position its comparative advantage in Ukraine. The ambition is for SI to build a recognized and demonstrable expertise in WASH and Shelter. The program strategy for 2026 therefore focuses on two core sectors—WASH and Shelter—and is structured around two strategic axes:  
1\. Respond to both acute and chronic emergencies  
2\. Contribute to creating the conditions for dignified return or sustainable stay in stable areas through a recovery-oriented approach  
To maximize the impact of its interventions, SI aims to further enhance sectoral integration and promote localized approaches.  
In 2026, SI’s country program in Ukraine is expected to operate with a budget of approximately 10 million euros, with three field bases (Mykolaiv, Dnipro, Kharkiv), one coordination office in Kyiv, and a total of 110 staff, including around 15 expatriates.  
The main donors in 2026 are CDCS, AFD, and ECHO. Additional donors have been approached to expand and diversify the portfolio further, in line with SI’s programmatic priorities.

**ABOUT THE JOB**

SIZING OF THE TEAM ON THE BASE / IN COORDINATION :

Direct report to Country Director  
Functional link with Field Coordinators and Field Coordinator Assistants  
Direct line management of Deputy Access and Liaison Coordinator and Fire Safety officer  
SI in Ukraine is composed of about 15 expatriates and 90 national staff

GENERAL OBJECTIVES :

On behalf of the Country Director, the Head of Security and Humanitarian Department oversees the definition of access, safety and security strategies, as well as the implementation of information gathering, analysis and the necessary frameworks, both at base level and in coordination.   
They support the development of a network of reliable information and key contacts. They ensure compliance with the overall SI regulatory framework in their area and ensures the proper implementation of the Minimum Operational Standards for Security and Access.

ISSUES AND SPECIFIC CHALLENGES :

Static frontline but dynamic and volatile security context  
Increasing range of drones, systemic targeting of critical infrastructures and logistical nods and massive attacks in areas of presence  
Decreasing humanitarian access and challenged humanitarian principles

PRIORITIES ON THE 2-3 FIRST MONTHS :

Contribute to SI's access strategy in Sumy oblast and Kherson city, if applicable  
Maintain a high level of standard in security management throughout the Country program, regardless of HR turnovers and gaps  
Ensure dynamic risk assessments despite the routine  
Participate to the capacity-building of local partners

SECURITY CONSTRAINTS :

Existing curfew from 01 am to 05 am  
Frequent massive attacks targeting Kyiv  
Daily drones presence leading to air alarms and often, the need to shelter  
Adaptability of both sides to the conflict leading to frequent adaptative measures required

**YOUR PROFIL**

DIPLOMAS : Master in a humanitarian or security-related field

EXPERIMENT IN THE HUMANITARIAN SECTOR : more than 5 years

EXPERIMENT ON SIMILAR POSITIONS : 3-4 years

TECHNICAL SKILLS :

-Knowledge of standard corpus of security tools and documents in a country security pack

-Risk assessment and mitigation

-Staff training, development, coaching, and mentoring expertise

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS :

-Leadership and decision-making capacity

-Ability to work under pressure in a volatile security environment

-Strong inter-personal and analytical skills

LANGUAGES :

-English is Mandatory

-Ukrainian or Russian is a strong asset

**SI WILL OFFER YOU**

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2860 gross per month (2600 EUR base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of EUR 700.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

title: Tupande Export Logistics Senior Specialist
body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Kenya program, founded in 2006, operates under the local brand Tupande. Close to 500 staff in our Kakamega headquarters support 1,747 field staff and serve more than 1 million farmers. In Nairobi, around 50 staff support global functions like procurement, recruitment, government relations, and communications.

## **About the Role**

The Export Logistics Specialist oversees and manages end-to-end export operations to ensure that goods leave the organization’s facilities and reach international vendors on time, within budget and in full compliance of all agreed regulations; including safety standards.

The role is focused on planning, coordination, documentation & stakeholder management for all exports handled by Soko.

## **Responsibilities**

Export Operations & Coordination

- Plan, organize, and oversee the entire export process from order placement to delivery at the destination.
- Coordinate with production, warehousing, and procurement teams to ensure accurate and timely order fulfillment.
- Liaise with freight forwarders, carriers, and third-party logistics providers to schedule shipments.
- Track shipments, resolve delays, and ensure smooth cargo movement.

Documentation & Compliance

- Prepare and review all required export documentation (invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, certificates of origin, export licenses, etc.).
- Ensure compliance with international trade laws, customs regulations, and organizational policies.
- Maintain accurate records of shipments for audit and reporting purposes.
- Stay updated on changes in export/import regulations, customs procedures, and trade agreements.

Customer & Stakeholder Management

- Act as the primary point of contact for clients regarding export logistics inquiries.
- Provide timely updates to customers on order and shipment status.
- Resolve customer complaints, shipment issues, or documentation errors promptly.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with shipping agents, port authorities, and regulatory agencies.

Performance Management

- Negotiate shipping rates and terms with carriers and freight forwarders to optimize costs.
- Analyze export logistics performance and recommend process improvements for efficiency and cost savings.

Reconditioning

- Support and coordinate container reconditioning logistics when overseas regulators identify non-compliance issues.
- Ensure all reconditioning processes follow approved SOPs and documentation standards before goods are released to buyers.
- Maintain close communication with third-party service providers managing sterilization or product rework.

Supply Chain Traceability

- Ensure all exported goods have a clear, verifiable origin and traceable supply chain documentation.
- Work with sourcing and quality teams to build systems that enable end-to-end traceability of export products.
- Maintain audit-ready export documentation, certifications, and inspection records in compliance with global regulatory standards.

Cost efficiency

- Monitor freight costs, customs duties, and tariffs to control budgets.
- Identify opportunities for cost reduction across shipping, warehousing, and handling processes.
- Implement strategies that improve container utilization, reduce demurrage/detention, and optimize route planning.
- Regularly review freight spend and propose cost-saving initiatives without compromising quality or timelines.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- 5+ years of experience in Supply chain, with at least 3 years focusing on Exports.
- Proficiency in export management systems and tracking tools.
- Proficiency in building complex formulas and functions in Google Sheets to support data analysis and reporting.
- Language requirement: English is required. Working knowledge of Swahili is also useful
- Strong planning and organizational skills.
- Excellent communication and coordination abilities.
- Proficient in export management systems and tracking tools.
- Analytical mindset for cost projections and performance tracking.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and work under pressure.

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Nairobi, Kenya

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, paid time off

## **Eligibility**

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

## **Application Deadline**

16 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis, which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

title: Senior Data Engineer (Maternity Cover)
body:
**What we are looking for:**

NRC Norway is looking for an experienced **Senior Data Engineer** for a maternity cover position.

You’ll play a key role in building and optimising the data infrastructure that enables NRC to turn complex data into actionable insights. You will design and maintain scalable data pipelines and ETL processes in Microsoft Fabric across data lakes and data warehouses, ensuring that data remains accessible, reliable, and secure. You will also advise on the use of alternative data products when Microsoft Fabric is not the most suitable solution. Working closely with data product managers, analysts and other stakeholders, you’ll translate business needs into effective data solutions, strengthen data quality and governance, and champion modern engineering practices, automation and innovation.

If you’re passionate about data, technology and meaningful humanitarian impact, we’d like to hear from you.

**What you will do:**

- Ensure that data at NRC is accessible and optimized for use in the organisation.
- Instigate collaboration with program managers and field staff to understand their data needs and ensure that data systems are aligned with operational goals.
- Provide technical leadership, support and guidance to non-technical teams on data processing methods and infrastructure setup.
- Implement best practices for data governance, ensuring compliance with relevant regulations and ethical standards.
- Compliance and adherence to NRC policies, guidance and procedures, and a specific responsibility for the functions policies and procedures.
- Build data pipelines in Fabric to integrate internal and external data based on existing internal best

practices. This should reflect the current data needs set by SPK, other operational departments and field operations.

- Contribute to the design and continuous improvement of the Fabric environment, supporting secure data sharing across NRC.
- Contribute to developing the infrastructure, governance, and standards required to make data more discoverable and accessible.
- Build and evaluate systems and data pipelines on Microsoft infrastructure, including Azure and Power Apps, for use cases that fall outside Fabric’s scope, such as archiving solutions, and integrations with other NRC systems.
- Architect the data infrastructure inside and outside of Fabric to ensure it is optimized for performance and can handle the (large-scale) data requirements of the organisation.
- Proactively implement data validation checks, monitoring and error-handling processes to ensure the accuracy, consistency, and integrity of data.

Please download a more detailed [**JOB DESCRIPTION**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQDKrCT2JlDJS5Zf-TA--9IIAa-KD3fwrJv9-NbZF3szXNU?e=LUSMGu) to learn more about the position.

**What you will bring:**

- Proven experience with IT projects.
- Bachelor’s degree in computer science, software engineering, or related subjects, or demonstrable expertise in the field.
- Advanced analytical skills and problem-solving attitude.
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, comfortable working with a geographically distributed team, and can easily work with non-technical colleagues
- Capable of operating in an "Agile" environment
- Fluency in written and spoken English. Other languages are an asset.
- Proactive in keeping up to date with industry trends and innovation.
- 5+ years of experience shipping and maintaining code in production.
- Experience working with Microsoft Fabric or other Microsoft reporting tools.
- Experience or deep understanding of data architecture and data modelling.
- Solid knowledge of programming in Python, fundamentals of API design and security, familiarity with basic DevOps is a plus.
- In depth knowledge and comfortable working with relational databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL) and nonrelational data (JSON format) including building, optimizing, debugging, and creating queries and safe migration scripts.
- Familiarity in working with enterprise information systems in general, and especially ERP and CRM, are desirable.

**What we offer:**

title: Country Director, South Sudan
body:
## **Background:**

The humanitarian situation in South Sudan remains one of the most severe and complex crises driven by conflict, economic collapse, climate shocks, disease outbreaks, mass displacement, and shrinking humanitarian funding. An estimated 10 million people will experience critical needs in 2026.

The conflict in neighbouring Sudan continues to drive refugee inflows and returnee movements into South Sudan, placing additional pressure on already overstretched services and humanitarian systems. Over 1 million people have crossed into South Sudan since the Sudan conflict began. Access remains one of the most significant operational challenges due to active conflict, insecurity and bureaucratic impediments making it difficult for aid organizations to reach those in need.

NRC has been present in South Sudan since 2004. Today, it operates in Upper Nile State, Northern Bahr el Ghazal state, Warrap State, Western Bahr el Ghazal Sate, Jonglei State, Unity State and Central Equatoria State

NRC delivers programmes in the areas of Rapid Response to emergencies, Multipurpose Cash Assistance, Legal assistance and Protection, Education, Shelter, Water and hygiene promotion, and places a high importance upon advocacy. NRC co-leads different clusters and working groups (Protection, WASH, Shelter, Land, and Site Coordination Clusters, including HLP and Durable Solutions Working Groups).

**What we are looking for:**

**As Country Director, you will provide overall leadership and responsibility for the country operation. This includes:**

- **provide strategic direction and management to the country programme**
- **drive effective programme delivery**
- **strong external representation, including active engagement in inter-agency coordination**
- **lead resource mobilisation and advocacy efforts**
- **building high-performing teams to deliver accountable, high-impact humanitarian response**

The Country Director has overall responsibility for the country operation, providing both strategic direction and operational leadership. S/He leads the Country Management Group (CMG) and is a member of the Regional Management Team, under the leadership of the East and Southern Africa (ESA) Regional Director.

The Country Director provides vision, promotes ideas, gains agreement and acts as a role model. S/he ensures NRC’s continued relevance and position as a principled humanitarian actor in South Sudan.

- Prioritise continuous improvement and innovation to ensure the highest quality of humanitarian and protection programming with a focus on timely delivery

- In close collaboration with both the Regional Team and NRC CDs from neighbouring countries, jointly set the strategic direction of the regional displacement crisis and ensure close cooperation on developing response modalities.

title: Regional Head of Operational Support
body:
## **Background:**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation dedicated to protecting the rights of displaced and affected people during crises. NRC delivers high-quality programmes to support people forced to flee, helping them rebuild their lives and establish a new future. NRC provides immediate humanitarian assistance, prevents further displacement, and contributes to durable solutions. It operates across both new and protracted crises across 40 countries.

The country programmes in the East and Southern Africa region incorporate Ethiopia, Uganda, South Sudan, Sudan, Somalia, Kenya, and Mozambique. NRC exited from Tanzania in 2026.

NRC has a simplified organisational structure with a leaner Head Office in Oslo and Representation Offices and smaller Regional Teams. Global support structures are established for functions previously managed by the Regional Offices, including Finance, Risk & Compliance, People & Organisation, Media and Communication, PCM & Grants Management. The Regional Team and Country Offices will access support capacity from these Global Resource Pools.

Resource Pools (hereafter pool) gather staff in one common team which is organised and managed (but not necessarily physically located) at Head Office. The purpose of pooling is to improve efficiency, equity, access and flexibility. The teams should ensure predictable access to the same services and deliver them in an efficient way.

In Nairobi Kenya, several members of the different pools are physically located in the regional office, the Regional Head of Operational Support ensures streamlining of hosting arrangements and a conducive working environment for all.

**What we are looking for:**

The Regional Head of Operational Support will ensure an integrated approach to operational management, supporting the quality and timeliness of NRC's response in the region.

The role is responsible for enabling support needs in countries across HR, Risk and Compliance, Humanitarian Access and Safety (HAS), Finance, ICT, Logistics and Administration, ensuring compliance with NRC policies.

The Regional Head of Operational Support plays a crucial role in ensuring that the region is accountable for the performance of country offices, ensuring they meet operational standards and deliver on strategic objectives.

The role ensures a conducive working environment for all teams, including members of different global teams physically located in the regional office in Nairobi.

This role is a member of the Regional Management Team and the Global Support Advisory Group (GSAG) led by the deputy SG/ CFO.

**What you will do:**

- Ensure that support functions within the regional team operate efficiently, fostering a collaborative and effective working environment.
- Hold country offices accountable for progress on their operations by leveraging reports, analyses, and compliance data from NRC’s global resource and pools.
- Support country directors and heads of support, HAS Managers with capacity building and problem-solving related to operational challenges.
- Provide advice and mentorship to country office operational support teams, fostering capacity building and skills development.
- Participate in global discussions on planning and strategy relating to support functions.
- Review of finance, HR and logistics requirements related to regional grants in collaboration with the Global PCM and Grants Management facility.
- Streamline the hosting arrangements for members of global pools physically located in the regional office and ensure a conducive working environment

title: Senior Finance Officer
body:
**Assignment**

The IMPACT/REACH Syria mission, present in Damascus since 2025 and with activities in Syria since 2012, has traditionally had finance support from both the Acted Syria mission as well as dedicated IMPACT/REACH support in Amman. Since a shift in activities and location to Damascus, IMPACT/REACH is in the process of setting up a more independent finance structure to support activities in Syria. As such, IMPACT/REACH is looking for an experienced Senior Finance Officer, with ability to lead and advise on financial priorities, think critically about and manage financial workflows, meet financial deadlines, and oversee relevant finance staff.

Prior experience in managing finances for NGOs is essential, including budget development (with ability to proactively consult relevant team members to develop a high quality budget), financial reports, budget follow up (with ability to analyze and forecast spending, as well as advise senior management on financial decisions), and financial allocations and transactions. We are looking for someone who has an excellent finance background with experience in use of Excel and financial management software, and an ability to think creatively, lead independently, and advise senior managers in making wise financial decisions.

Under the supervision of the IMPACT Country Representative and the IMPACT Regional Finance Manager, the Senior Finance Officer is responsible for all financial tasks related to supporting the IMPACT/REACH Syria mission.

## OBJECTIVES

Provides leadership to the IMPACT/REACH Syria finance team in ensuring that financial workflows are established, efficient, and effective

Acts as a senior advisor to the IMPACT/REACH senior management in ensuring that financial decisions are based on accurate, up-to-date financial information

Ensures that all financial budgeting and reporting deadlines are met on time

Works closely with Acted Syria finance and IMPACT regional finance to ensure that all financial processes are followed according to compliant procedures

## FUNCTIONS

**General financial management and leadership**

- Supports IMPACT/REACH management as relevant in coordinating finance-related activities with relevant stakeholders, and provides guidance in setting objectives and implementing workflows that allow the team to be efficient and effective
- Conducts regular financial analysis and updates and advises IMPACT Country Representative on key financial decisions, including highlighting spending status and offering solutions if needed
- Contributes to the development of financial strategies to optimize profitability and minimize risks
- Acts as focal point for coordinating inputs or submission to Acted and IMPACT senior management and HQ teams in a timely manner and independently without requiring follow up, may manage 1-2 additional finance staff

**Budget management**

- In coordination with the IMPACT CR, IMPACT RFM, and Acted CFM, lead in the preparation of budget proposals based on allocation tables, forecasting, and consultations with relevant program and finance teams
- Ensure that budgets are submitted on time, quickly, and are presented in both internal format and converted accurately into donor formats when required
- Follow up on validation of budget and make changes to budget as required by HQs or country management
- Check, manage, and follow up on project follow up documents on a monthly basis to ensure that spending and financial allocations match the allocation tables
- Lead in updating monthly allocation tables, timesheets, and running cost tables on time and accurately, in coordination with program, operations, and finance teams on spending plans

**Accounting management**

- Ensure all financial and accountancy procedures are implemented and respected at the area level
- Check the coherence of the cashbook, saga, and cash balance before closing the accountancy for each week and the end of each month
- Ensure that all documentation (programmatic, procurement, or otherwise), is as per policy and in accordance with external donor regulations, before preparing any financial payments

**Financial reporting**

- In coordination with relevant focal points, ensure that monthly follow up reports are completed accurately and on time
- Close accurately the final expenditure report and ensure its adherence to the project plan before sharing with HQ for final reporting
- Prepare accurately and in a timely manner all financial reports in the correct donor format and coordinate validation and approval from all stakeholders within Acted and IMPACT

**Reporting and audit support**

- Ensure financial oversight and ensure that all IMPACT processes are compliant with audit processes
- Attend audits as requested by Acted finance and compliance team and be prepared to lead on accurate responses regarding IMPACT finances
- Prepare IMPACT inputs and coordinate with IMPACT HQ to provide inputs as requested by Acted finance team in preparation for audit

**Other financial tasks**

Support on any other financial task related to IMPACT Syria’s financial health

**KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS**

- Accurate and on time financial analysis provided monthly to senior management
- Accurate and on time budgets are prepared in coordination with country teams
- Accurate and on time reporting and follow up processes are executed each month
- Proactivity and leadership in ensuring finance tasks are executed at high quality

**QUALIFICATIONS**

- University degree in accounting, finance, economics, business administration or equivalent
- At least 4 years of experience progressively managing financial tasks and analysis required
- Strong leadership skills in financial management and analysis
- Excellent knowledge of excel, word, and outlook
- Familiarity with accounting software (e.g. 1C; SAGA, QuickBooks)
- Extreme attention to detail, with an ability to spot numerical errors and fix formulas
- Self-organizational skills and ability to identify necessary taskswork independently
- Previous experience in NGO/INGO preferred
- Ability to communicate in both Arabic and English

title: HRIS Product Owner
body:
**Join MSF OCG as a HRIS Product Owner!**

**We are looking for passionate candidates ready to contribute to our humanitarian mission.**

**Below, you will find the job details and the qualifications we are looking for.**

## Inclusivity and Diversity at MSF

Do your qualifications and experience not exactly match all requirements of the job?

At MSF OCG, we are committed to an inclusive culture that supports and amplifies the diverse voices of our staff members. We strive to create workplaces where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together to advance MSF's social mission and create better outcomes for our patients and the communities we work with.

We understand that some people may hesitate to apply for employment if they don't meet all listed job requirements. Research shows that this is especially true for women. If you believe your profile is a good match for this position, we invite you to apply even if you don’t fulfil every listed qualification.

We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment. All selected candidates will undergo reference checks.

## Context & mission

Médecins Sans Frontières is an independent, international medical and humanitarian organization that provides care to people in need, people affected by natural or man-made disasters, and victims of armed conflict, without discrimination and without regard to race, religion, creed or political affiliation (MSF Charter).

The MSF movement is built around 5 operational centers supported by 24 sections and offices worldwide. MSF Operational Center Geneva (MSF OCG) is one of these centers.

The HRIS Product Owner leads the LIGO RUN (Workday) team and ensures stable, effective and user-centred HRIS services for OCG, in alignment with the OCG Strategy and broader HR Transformation objectives.

The role is responsible for service delivery, product ownership, roadmap and backlog management, activity as well as budget planning, team management, shared tenant collaboration and continuous improvement of LIGO / Workday, which was recently deployed within OCG.

As LIGO is a core pillar of OCG HR Transformation, the role translates strategic objectives into sustainable operational delivery, while progressively building the governance, capacity and ways of working required for long-term service continuity and a future transition under IT.

## Tasks & Responsibilities

*HRIS Service Delivery and Product Ownership*

- Act as Product Owner for LIGO from an OCG perspective, managing the roadmap and backlog in line with HR strategic priorities, user needs, operational requirements and shared tenant constraints.
- Prioritise system evolutions, enhancements and corrective actions based on business value, service impact, feasibility, risks, resources and budget.
- Ensure continuity, stability and quality of LIGO services across support, incident management, service requests, functional administration, integrations, releases, enhancements and continuous improvement.
- Coordinate with HR stakeholders, user groups, IT, TMA (Tierce Maintenance Applicative) providers, global LIGO roles and other partners to ensure effective delivery and resolution of issues.

*User Experience, Adoption, Data and Continuous Improvement*

- Ensure that user experience, adoption and change management are embedded in the design, delivery and evolution of LIGO services.
- Oversee communication, training, user support, feedback collection and adoption activities to improve effective use of LIGO by HR teams, managers and employees.
- Promote reliable, consistent and usable HR data, ensuring that data quality, reporting and downstream impacts are considered in system changes.
- Support simplification, harmonisation, automation and improvement of HR processes through LIGO.
- Monitor service performance, user feedback, recurring issues and improvement opportunities, and translate them into concrete actions.

*Team Management and Capacity Building*

- Manage, organize and coordinate the multidisciplinary LIGO service delivery team, including HR functional referents, functional administration, IT business analysis, integration, support, user experience and adoption roles.
- Define clear roles, responsibilities, priorities, ways of working and escalation paths within the team.
- Plan and monitor workload, team capacity and delivery priorities across RUN, roadmap, support, adoption, integration, data and governance activities.
- Support the professional development of team members and strengthen collective expertise, autonomy, documentation and knowledge sharing.
- Build a collaborative team culture focused on service quality, accountability, user impact, continuous improvement and sustainable support.

*Activity Planning, Resource and Budget Management*

- Lead annual and multi-year activity planning for the LIGO service delivery scope, translating HR Transformation priorities into operational plans, milestones and measurable outcomes.
- Prepare, manage and monitor the LIGO service delivery budget, including internal resources, external support, TMA services, maintenance, enhancements, training and adoption activities, taking into account constraints (resource, budget, shared tenant).
- Contribute to defining a sustainable resourcing and funding model for LIGO as the service matures and prepares for a future IT-based operating model.

*Governance, Collaboration and Future Operating Model*

- Represent OCG in shared Workday tenant governance and contribute to a coherent, sustainable and collaborative operating model with other MSF entities, representing the broader OCG stakeholders
- Define and promote clear ways of working for prioritisation, impact assessment, decision-making, releases, testing, tenant administration, data, security and change management.
- Collaborate with IT, global LIGO roles, TMA (Tierce Maintenance Applicative) provider, HR stakeholders, user groups representatives and other application managers / product owners across the wider system architecture.
- Prepare the progressive transition of LIGO service delivery from HR Transformation towards a future IT-based operating model, while preserving business proximity and HR strategic alignment.)

## Your profile

*Experience and Knowledge*

- Significant understanding of MSF, and/ or humanitarian settings constraints and operations centred service orientation mindset.
- Significant experience in HRIS service delivery, product ownership, application management or HR transformation, ideally with Workday or another integrated HRIS.
- Strong understanding of HR processes, HR operating models, digital HR services and post-go-live / RUN environments.
- Experience leading multidisciplinary teams across business, functional, technical, support, user experience and adoption roles.
- Experience in roadmap management, backlog prioritisation, stakeholder arbitration, activity planning, budget monitoring and resource management.
- Good understanding of IT service management, application governance, integrations, data governance, security principles and multi-entity/shared system environments.
- English and French are the working languages of MSF Switzerland.

*Skills/ Technical competencies*

- HRIS service delivery and product ownership.
- Team leadership, coordination and capacity building.
- Activity planning, budget management and resource planning.
- Prioritisation, decision-making and stakeholder arbitration.
- Strong communication, facilitation, documentation and synthesis skills.

*Personal Abilities/Qualities*

- Strategic and operational mindset.
- Strong service orientation and user focus.
- Collaborative leadership style.
- Ability to create structure in a complex and evolving environment.

*Languages*

- Fluent English and French required; other MSF working languages are an asset.

## Terms of employment

- Full-time position 100% (40h/week)
- Fixed-term contract, until December 31st, 2027
- Working place: Geneva, Switzerland
- Ideal start date: As soon as possible
- Gross annual salary (for 100%): from CHF 110’652.- to CHF 126’228.- (salary commensurate with equivalent experience and internal salary grid)
- Paid vacation: 25 days per year, prorate temporis, plus any Swiss public holidays falling within the contract period.
- Pension plan: pension contribution covered 3/4 by MSF, 1/4 by staff member.
- Relocation support available for eligible candidates.

title: Senior Programme Manager, Academic Pillar (Refugee-Led Research Hub)
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
**Role:** Senior Programme Manager, Academic Pillar (Refugee-Led Research Hub)

**Grade and salary:** Grade 8, £49,119 - £58,265

**Hours:** Full-time 37.5 hours per week

**Location:** Oxford, United Kingdom (minimum 3 days in office)

**Contract type:** Fixed term until 30 September 2028 (with possibility of extension subject to further funding)

**Reporting to:** Head of Programmes (postholder to be appointed, in the interim you would report to the Executive Director)

**Start Date:** 1st January 2026 (desired) but flexible

\*\*Closing date:\*\*19th October (midday UK time) 2026

## **About the Refugee-Led Research Hub**

The Refugee-Led Research Hub (RLRH) supports individuals with lived experience of displacement to become leaders in fields related to human rights, forced migration, humanitarian response and development, politics, and law, among other areas. We do so by delivering academic and professional development programming to a global cohort of students who have been affected by displacement—as refugees, asylum seekers, IDPs, stateless, and beyond—supporting access to graduate degrees and advanced career opportunities. RLRH also creates opportunities for researchers with displacement backgrounds to lead primary and secondary research studies, from start to finish.

RLRH’s team is comprised of colleagues who are deeply committed to advancing refugee leadership, the majority of whom have lived experience of displacement. Our network of staff, researchers, students, and other affiliates is made up of 1,400+ individuals across 80+ countries. RLRH has six active offices: our first was established in Nairobi in 2020, we have had an office at the University of Oxford since 2021, and we have since developed physical hubs in Kakuma refugee camp (Kenya), Kuala Lumpur (Malaysia), Kampala (Uganda), and in the Oxfordshire community (UK).

From October 2025 RLRH is funded to serve as a technical partner for the Mastercard Foundations Scholars Program network, advancing an ambitious global agenda to support displacement-affected learners to access 1,000+ graduate-level scholarships at partner universities around the world. RLRH provides expert guidance and implements specialised programmes to help these learners enter university, thrive on course, and pursue meaningful and enduring careers on completion of their degrees. A complementary, refugee-led research agenda designed by RLRH colleagues produces insights to help Scholars Program partner universities and other stakeholders accelerate positive, long-lasting systems change.

## **The Role**

**Overview of the Academic Pillar:**

The Academic Pillar (AP) manages globally accessible education programmes that reach thousands of bachelors degree-holding refugees, asylum seekers, and others affected by displacement to strengthen their academic credentials and preparedness so they can access postgraduate degrees worldwide. A large, though not exclusive, proportion of the Pillar’s efforts are dedicated to recruiting and preparing African displacement-affected students for Mastercard Foundation’s Scholars Program graduate-level courses at 30+ partner universities. The AP team runs three hallmark programmes to support these prospective students:

**Graduate Horizons** provides learners with comprehensive postgraduate application and admissions support, from selecting right-fit universities and scholarships to crafting compelling personal statements and research proposals. The programme offers hands-on workshops, intensive writing boot camps, one-to-one application feedback, dedicated office hours, and mentorship designed to maximise each student’s academic potential. RLRH actively advocates for students, working directly with universities to eliminate barriers that impede their progress.

A complementary bridging programme that can be completed before or during Horizons is **Graduate Admissions Essentials,** a three-month self-guided programme designed by RLRH to help learners strengthen their academic and professional profiles across the core admissions areas that universities assess for postgraduate study. A wide range of thoughtfully curated resources are available, meeting learners where they are in their tertiary education journeys.

Finally, **RLRH Foundations: Refugee and Forced Migration Studies,** is an intensive nine-module online course that supports students to develop academic skills in the Social Sciences. The interdisciplinary curriculum exposes learners to International Humanitarian Law, Anthropology, Political Theory, Gender Studies, International Relations, and more, preparing participants for study across a wide range of fields of interest. In the near future, RLRH will be developing new Foundations courses, catering to a wider range of subject areas of interest as members of our community prepare for postgraduate degrees.

**Overview of Position:**

RLRH is in an exciting phase of strategic growth. . As the organisation expands its global reach, programme portfolio and operational capacity, we are seeking an experienced senior leader to oversee and further develop our Academic Pillar. The **Senior Programme Manager, Academic Success** will oversee a team of 8+ colleagues across multiple locations, with responsibility for achieving RLRH’s sector-leading objective of supporting **1,000 refugee and displacement-affected learners to enrol in master’s degrees worldwide by 2028**.

The **Senior Programme Manager** will provide strategic, operational and people leadership for RLRH’s Academic Pillar, ensuring that its programmes are coherent, high-quality, inclusive, scalable, data-informed, and delivered with measurable impact. The post-holder will oversee the planning, delivery, governance and continuous improvement of complex academic access programmes, ensuring objectives are achieved on time, within budget and in line with RLRH and University standards.

Working closely with the Head of Programmes, Academic Pillar staff, hub-based colleagues, the MEL team, and other RLRH pillars, the post-holder will lead the operational scaling and strategic development of RLRH’s academic access portfolio. This includes overseeing the effective delivery and expansion of **Graduate Horizons**, **RLRH Foundations**, and **Graduate Admissions Essentials**, with a particular focus on supporting African displacement-affected learners to access postgraduate opportunities across Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program partner universities.

The role will directly manage four Academic Pillar staff: the **Mentoring and Student Success Manager**, **Academic Partnerships and Outreach Manager**, **Academic Content and Facilitation Manager**, and **Senior** **Academic Project Officer**. Through these colleagues, the Senior Programme Manager will oversee the full Academic Pillar learner journey, from outreach and recruitment through academic preparation, mentoring, application support, admissions, transition into study, and longer-term academic progression.

The post-holder will be responsible for strengthening the systems, structures, and ways of working that enable Academic Pillar programmes to operate effectively at scale. This includes ensuring robust programme planning, financial oversight, risk management, data governance, reporting, stakeholder coordination, and quality assurance. The role will be instrumental in embedding a culture of accountability, transparency, collaboration and continuous improvement across RLRH’s academic portfolio.

**Responsibilities**

*Programme Planning, Delivery and Quality Assurance (35%)*

1. Provide end-to-end leadership for the planning, delivery and continuous improvement of RLRH’s Academic Pillar programmes.
2. Ensure that Academic Pillar programmes are delivered on time, to a high standard, within agreed resources, and in line with RLRH’s strategic objectives and University standards.
3. Oversee the full learner journey across the Academic Pillar, from outreach and recruitment through onboarding, academic preparation, mentoring, application support, admissions, transition into postgraduate study and longer-term academic progression.
4. Identify and resolve cross-programme delivery challenges, including timeline clashes, learner engagement risks, communication gaps, capacity constraints and operational bottlenecks.
5. Ensure that programme delivery is coherent across the Academic Pillar’s core areas: outreach and recruitment, academic facilitation, and mentoring.
6. Develop and maintain quality assurance processes across Academic Pillar programmes, including programme reviews, learner feedback loops, delivery check-ins, and mechanisms for continuous improvement.
7. identify opportunities for innovation and future programme development.

*People Management and Coordination (25%)*

1. Line-manage and support a team composed of the Mentoring and Student Success Manager, Academic Partnerships and Outreach Manager, Academic Content and Facilitation Manager, Senior Academic Project Officer and additional support staff based across RLRH's global hubs, setting clear expectations, monitoring performance and providing regular supervision and feedback.
2. Set clear expectations, objectives, and priorities for direct reports, ensuring each colleague has the guidance and support needed to lead their area of work effectively.
3. Convene regular one-to-one and team meetings to support decision-making, resolve challenges and maintain shared accountability across the Academic Pillar.
4. Foster a supportive, inclusive and reflective team culture that values lived experience, professional development, collaboration, mutual accountability and learner-centred practice.
5. Support staff development by identifying learning needs and strengthening colleagues’ skills in programme management, data use, facilitation, partnership management, team coordination and strategic planning through regular performance reviews and professional development conversations.
6. Lead workforce planning for the Academic Pillar, overseeing recruitment, onboarding, succession planning and team development to ensure sustainable organisational growth.

*Strategic Growth and Cross-Pillar Integration (20%)*

1. Translate RLRH’s organisational strategy, Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program commitments and 2028 objective into clear Academic Pillar priorities, annual plans, delivery models and growth pathways.
2. Lead the strategic development and scaling of the Academic Pillar’s programme portfolio, ensuring that growth is realistic, well-sequenced, properly resourced and aligned with learner needs.
3. Advise the Head of Programmes on Academic Pillar priorities, risks, strategic opportunities, partner developments and resourcing needs.
4. Collaborate with peer programmatic leaders across RLRH’s Research and Professional Pathways Pillars to ensure that Academic Pillar programmes connect effectively with research, professional development, alumni and career pathways.

*MEL, Operations, and Budget Management (15%)*

1. Contribute to the development of RLRH’s Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) portfolio, supporting data-driven insights from pillar activities that improve internal programming and contribute to MEL objectives.
2. Lead financial planning, resource allocation and budget oversight for the Academic Pillar, ensuring resources are used responsibly, strategically and in line with grant commitments and organisational procedures.
3. Strengthen operational systems, documentation and knowledge management across the Academic Pillar, including templates, guidance documents, process notes, and playbooks.
4. Ensure that Academic Pillar operations comply with relevant organisational and University policies, including safeguarding, data protection, accessibility, financial management and ethical practice.

*Organisation-wide strategy, learning, and documentation (5%)*

1. Coordinate with Head of Programmes, Director of Operations and Strategy, and Executive Director to input on annual organisation planning.
2. Participate in weekly leadership convenings to influence the strategic direction of the organisation.
3. Represent RLRH at meetings, conferences, partnerships and external stakeholder forums.
4. Contribute to organisation and pillar fundraising and wider grant management needs, as relevant.

## **Selection criteria**

### Required qualifications:

1. A postgraduate degree (or equivalent professional experience). No particular field is expected, but familiarity with (Refugee and Forced) Migration Studies, Education, International Development, and related disciplines can be an advantage.
2. Substantial experience leading complex, multi-stakeholder education, higher education access, widening participation or refugee education programmes, with demonstrated experience managing programme delivery and influencing multidisciplinary teams through line management and/or matrix structures.
3. Demonstrated experience translating organisational strategy into operational delivery through programme design, organisational planning, resource allocation and performance management.
4. Significant experience leading and developing high-performing multidisciplinary teams across multiple geographical locations.
5. Experience working with data, monitoring, and evaluation systems, reporting processes and programme improvement cycles.
6. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to produce clear reports, guidance documents, plans and external-facing materials.
7. Experience building strategic relationships with universities, scholarship providers, NGOs, funders and other senior stakeholders that translate into sustainable programme outcomes and institutional partnerships.
8. Experience supporting programme operations, financial planning, budget management, grant delivery and organisational governance.
9. Commitment to refugee leadership, equity, inclusion and ethical practice.
10. Excellent cultural competence and cultural humility, with experience working effectively across cultures, institutional settings and international teams.
11. Experience working with a high degree of autonomy, exercising sound judgement and accountability within specialist programme areas.

### Desired qualifications:

1. Familiarity with the African education ecosystem and the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program.
2. Fluency in additional languages spoken by RLRH learners and affiliates, such as Kiswahili, Arabic, or French.
3. Working comfort with Google Suites, Microsoft Outlook, Slack, WhatsApp Business, Project Management tools, and/or CRM platforms.

title: COORDINATEUR.ICE PAIE ET ADMINISTRATION DU PERSONNEL TERRAIN (HOMERE)
body:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Sous la supervision de la Responsable de Service RH Régionales, votre rôle sera d'apporter un support aux RH des 21 pays d'intervention afin d'assurer le bon déroulement du processus de paie (logiciel Homère) et aux révisions de la rémunération, ainsi qu'un support au pilotage et au suivi des Ressources Humaines nationales.  
Plus précisément, vos missions seront les suivantes :  
Appuyer au déploiement et à la révision des processus de paie et rémunération en collaboration avec l'équipe RH Régionales et les Coordinateurs ou Coordinatrices Fonctionnelles SIRHAccompagner les Responsables RH dans la formalisation de leurs demandes de paramétrages du SIRH  
Appuyer les RH des Bureaux Pays à la formalisation de leur processus de paie et à son suivi  
Participer à l'appui technique sur aux outils d'administration à destination des utilisateurs dans les pays d'intervention en lien avec l'équipe SIRH  
Apporter un support au pilotage et au suivi des Ressources Humaines nationalesAppuyer à la création et la mise à jour des cadrages d'administration du personnel national et à leur dissémination  
Appuyer à la mise à jour des outils d'administration du personnel  
Appuyer le suivi des audits siège  
Assurer le contrôle interne sur la paie, la gestion administrative du personnel et la mise en oeuvre des politiques de rémunération  
Appuyer à la définition des indicateurs RH

  
Profile :

 Vous êtes titulaire d'un diplôme supérieur en Ressources Humaines (RH) et/ou en paie, vous une avez une solide expérience RH au sein d'une ONG international (siège ou terrain).  
Autonome et force de proposition, vous avez une bonne connaissance de la réglementation de la paie, des charges sociales et des méthodes de calcul des cotisations sociales et fiscales. Vous avez une appétence pour les chiffres, les fonctions avancées d'Excel et vous pouvez vous appuyer sur vos connaissances en paramétrage de paie.  
Vous êtes reconnu.e pour vos capacités à identifier, analyser les problématiques RH et formuler à vos interlocuteur·rice·s des recommandations, des alertes et/ou trouver des solutions.  
Doté·e d'un excellent relationnel, vous êtes capable de vous adapter aux problématiques nationales et internationales du secteur humanitaire. Vous êtes également capable d'animer une séquence de formation.  
Une expérience dans l'utilisation du logiciel Homère et une connaissance du logiciel NIBELIS (logiciel de paie) sont de vrais atouts.  
Vous maîtrisez le français et l'anglais à l'oral comme à l'écrit.  
Une expérience ACF est un atout.  
  
Conditions d'emploi  
Statut:Cadre Intégré - CDD de 12 mois - Temps plein  
Lieu: Montreuil (Seine-Saint-Denis)  
Rémunération :De 41K à 50Keuros bruts annuels sur 13 mois selon expérience  
Avantages:25 jours par an de CP et 21 jours de RTT  
Couverture santé, prévoyance : Prise en charge à 80% par ACF  
Dispositifs de maintien de salaire (maladie, maternité, paternité)  
Indemnités Transport : Prise en charge à 50% du forfait entre le domicile et le lieu de travail

Prise en charge à 60% par l'association pour une valeur de 8euros  
Ouvres sociales du CSE (chèques cadeaux, remboursement activités culturelles, ...)

Il a été défini pour ce poste une présence obligatoire au siège de 1 jour par mois  
Temps de présentiels collectifs imposés / également obligatoires par l'employeur : pour les réunions et événements collectifs (jusqu'à 3 jours par mois) et 2 jours de présence obligatoire lors de votre intégration dans l'équipe  
Indemnités de télétravail
