title: Immigrant Youth Program Coordinator
body:
**Job Overview:** The Immigrant Youth Program Coordinator or Success Coach will coordinate the services provided to immigrant children and their families to ensure they have access to basic needs, education, community resources, and other services crucial to their well-being and stability. The Program Coordinator will function as the primary case manager for the family and coordinate services with other IRC partners and subgrantees, as well as help expand the network of service providers to strengthen services and improve the family’s success. Additionally, the Program Coordinator is responsible for attending local events and cultivating community partnerships and other community resources. The Program Coordinator will provide technical assistance and leadership to a team of interns and volunteers and will help with the selection of candidates during each cohort recruitment period. This position will report to the Immigrant Youth Program Supervisor. Travel within Miami-Dade County.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Provide comprehensive wrap-around case management services to immigrant children and their families, ensuring individualized support and advocacy.
- Conduct thorough needs assessments and ongoing evaluations to develop and implement tailored service plans that promote client safety, stability, and well-being.
- Empower clients by connecting them with appropriate resources and services and ensuring they have the tools to achieve their personal goals.
- Coordinate referrals and service planning with relevant stakeholders, ensuring a client-centered approach across all service areas.
- Serve as the primary point of contact for each family's case, maintaining strong working relationships with legal service providers, community partners, and other stakeholders.
- Deliver orientation services and ensure families understand available resources and program expectations.
- Provide crisis intervention, including mandated reporting to Child Protective Services when necessary.
- Participate actively in case management and staffing meetings to ensure consistent and informed client care.
- Meet regularly with Case Aide/Natural Helper to collaborate on relevant urgent cases and projects related to program implementation.

- Ensure high-quality data collection across all cases and contribute to data reporting and program development efforts.
- Promote program enrollment through client referrals and partnerships with other community providers.
- Collect client satisfaction surveys at case closure to track program success.
- Submit required reports and documentation in a timely and organized manner.
- Lead and supervise a team of interns and volunteers, including:

    - Support for professional development and training
- Represent the IRC at community meetings and public forums, strengthening partnerships with local service providers and promoting program visibility.

title: Caseworker (Ukrainian or Russian speaking)
body:
**IRC Background:** The mission of the International Rescue Committee (IRC) is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933, the IRC has a presence in over 40 countries and 27 offices in the United States; the IRC leads the way from harm to home. Domestically, our offices across the U.S. ensure new arrivals have food, shelter, and clothing, and work with refugees to help them gain self-sufficiency.

**Job Overview:** The UHP Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other qualified immigrants to support a positive resettlement experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The UHP Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

title: P&C Design and Change Management Specialist
body:
**Job Overview:**

The P&C Design and Change Management Specialist ensures that P&C transformation initiatives — Workday enhancements, process redesigns, and digital rollouts — are genuinely adopted across IRC's global workforce, not just technically delivered. This role owns the people-readiness side of transformation: understanding who's affected, how ready they are, what could go wrong, and how to address it before it does.

Working closely with the Training & Learning Delivery Specialist, Business Analysts, and P&C Partners, this role designs the change management approach for every initiative and embeds it from day one — from stakeholder impact assessments through go-live readiness and post-launch adoption tracking. The findings from this role directly feed the training design work led by the Training & Learning Delivery Specialist, ensuring training is built on a real understanding of who needs what.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Change Management**

- Design and execute structured change management plans and approaches for assigned P&C transformation initiatives, applying recognized methodologies such as ADKAR or Prosci, using templates and planning tools needed to do this consistently across projects
- Design and conduct stakeholder impact assessments at the start of every initiative, using a repeatable approach that captures affected populations, scale of change, adoption risks, and readiness gaps
- Develop stakeholder engagement plans for each initiative, determining the right messages, channels, and timing for each audience
- Build and execute communication plans for transformation initiatives, drafting audience-appropriate content in coordination with the Transformation & Digital Delivery Manager and relevant P&C teams
- Identify and proactively manage change resistance, developing approaches to address blockers and escalating significant risks with clear recommendations
- Establish change readiness checkpoints ahead of go-live, using tools and criteria to assess whether affected teams are prepared before launch
- Define and track adoption readiness metrics, identifying where adoption is lagging and recommending targeted interventions
- Identify and document change risks as part of regular project governance, with clear recommendations

**Partnership & Knowledge Management**

- Partner closely with the Training & Learning Delivery Specialist to ensure stakeholder impact assessments and readiness findings directly inform training design and sequencing
- Document change approaches, decisions, and lessons learned, contributing to the team's shared knowledge base
- Conduct post-implementation reviews on change effectiveness for every major initiative
- Stay current on change management best practices and organizational readiness approaches

**Job Requirements:**

**Work Experience**

- 3–5 years of experience in change management or P&C/HR transformation roles
- Demonstrated experience executing structured change management on P&C technology or business transformation projects
- Experience using or adapting change management tools, templates, or frameworks
- Solid working knowledge of Workday from an end-user or project delivery perspective is a strong advantage
- Change management certification (Prosci, CCMP, or equivalent) is an advantage
- Experience in a complex, matrixed organization preferred

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies**

- Solid working knowledge of change management methodologies (ADKAR, Prosci, or equivalent), applied practically
- Clear and adaptable communicator across audiences, from frontline users to senior stakeholders
- Data-aware: able to define readiness and adoption metrics, interpret findings, and recommend action
- Skilled at identifying and addressing resistance and readiness gaps
- Comfortable executing established methodology with precision and consistency, while identifying gaps or improvements to flag upward

**Working Environment:**

Standard office working environment with the ability to work remote 2-3 days per week

***This is a remote position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

title: Haiti : Directeur.rice Adjoint.e Pays – Port-au-Prince
source: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
body:
**CDD | 12 mois | ASAP**

## Acted

***Qui sommes-nous***

Acted travaille avec 19 millions de personnes dans 43 pays au carrefour de l’humanitaire, du développement, et des programmes climatiques et environnementaux. Grâce à une connaissance poussée des contextes et l’adoption de technologies émergentes, nous sauvons des vies, allégeons les souffrances, et protégeons et restaurons notre planète. Travaillant avec un écosystème croissant de partenaires locaux, nationaux et internationaux, nous poursuivons un objectif commun : un monde 3Zéro : Zéro Exclusion, Zéro Carbone, Zéro Pauvreté.

***Qui cherchons-nous***

Vous apportez les compétences clefs attendues d’un travailleur humanitaire et de développement, mais également une conscience climatique et environnementale active, et vous pouvez naviguez les défis qui émergent lorsque les souffrances environnementale et humaine se rencontrent. Vous avez l’esprit entrepreneurial : vous décelez les opportunités, connectez les points, adaptez votre approche aux différents environnements, et vous prenez des risques mesurés dans la poursuite de résultats. Vous alliez les principes au pragmatisme, et l’ambition à l’humilité.

## Acted Haïti

Présente en Haïti depuis 2004, Acted répond aux urgences et soutien le relèvement des populations dans le besoin, notamment dans les domaines de l’eau, l’hygiène et l’assainissement, de la sécurité alimentaire et de la reconstruction. En collaboration avec la société civile et les institutions, Acted développe et met aussi en œuvre des programmes axés sur le développement socio-économique et l’adaptation au changement climatique. Acted travaille actuellement dans 5 départements en Haïti à savoir la Grand’Anse, le Sud, le Sud-Est, l’Ouest, et le Centre, et prochainement dans les Nippes.

Concernant les réalisations majeures d’Acted en 2020-2021 :

• 5 562 personnes ont reçu une assistance monétaire afin de subvenir à leurs besoins prioritaires  
• 12 centres de santé réhabilités et soutenus afin de répondre à la pandémie de COVID-19  
• 35 réseaux d’eau et infrastructures réhabilités pour améliorer l’accès à l’eau, l’hygiène et l’assainissement  
• 1 125 personnes relogées grâce à la reconstruction de leur maison  
• 394 532 personnes sensibilisées aux mesures de prévention contre la Covid-19

Suite au tremblement de terre du 14 aout 2021 qui a dévasté les départements du Sud, de la Grande Anse et des Nippes en Haïti, Acted recrute. Acted a été une des première organisation humanitaire à mener des évaluations rapides pour déterminer l’ampleur des dégâts et des besoins, et est déjà fortement mobilisée pour apporter une aide d’urgence aux victimes du séisme, en étroite collaboration avec les autorités haïtiennes. Les activités menées actuellement concernent l’acheminement d’eau potable, la distribution de kits d’hygiène et la conduite de travaux d’assainissement et de réhabilitation des réseaux d’eau, mais aussi la distribution de nourriture, le versement d’aides financières d’urgence, la distribution de biens de première nécessité et, prochainement, la mise en place de solutions de logement pour les personnes les plus vulnérables, dans 12 communes des 3 départements.

## Rôle et responsabilités principales

Le/la Directeur.rice Pays Adjoint soutient le/la Directeur.rice Pays en représentant les intérêts d’Acted dans le pays vis à vis du gouvernement, des bailleurs et autres partenaires clef. Le/la Directeur.rice Pays Adjoint.e participe à l’élaboration du profil du Programme en accord avec la stratégie régionale et globale d’Acted . Le/la Directeur.rice Pays Adjoint.e soutient les équipes pour atteindre l’excellence dans le programme et assure les plus hauts niveaux de redevabilité.

***Principales Responsabilités :***

1\. Positionnement et fundraising

- *Analyse du contexte ;*
- *Développement et déploiement de la stratégie ;*
- *Networking, positionnement et représentation générale ;*
- *Relation avec les bailleurs et élaboration de propositions de projets ;*
- *Plaidoyer : (Co-)produire des notes stratégiques, des notes de plaidoyer, communiqués de presse pertinents sur les questions humanitaires et de développement.*

title: Logistics Officer
body:
Overview of position

To contribute to daily planning and coordination of WFP logistics operations including monitoring of services provided by contracted external organizations to ensure cost-effective operations and that set objectives are achieved in full.

Role objectives

- Contribute towards the development of logistics plans and processes ensuring compliance with wider logistics policies and WFP standards.
- Support or manage logistics projects or operational activities following standard processes and contributing, directly or indirectly, to the effective delivery of food assistance to beneficiaries.
- Collect and analyse data through research and networking with colleagues to recommend actions to senior staff to improve performance of local logistics operations.
- Conduct regular financial analysis and budget reviews, drawing out insights and recommending actions to senior staff to optimise use of available funds.
- Contribute to consolidation and preparation of operational pipeline planning, and to the management of operational aspects of the supply chain (procurement, shipping, port operation), including checking document and customs clearance readiness, loading and discharging operations and contracting of applicable transport, warehouse and any relevant logistics services.
- Contribute to supply chain by providing technical support and guidance to other CO unit/ services, divisions, particularly for emergency response.
- Guide and supervise more junior staff, acting as a point of referral and supporting them with more complex analysis and queries.
- Collate data and contribute to preparation of accurate and timely reporting, including Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), supporting a WFP-wide view of logistics activities that enables informed decision-making and consistency of information presented to stakeholders.
- Support the capacity building of WFP staff and partners for efficient and effective delivery of food assistance to beneficiaries (e.g. through the design and review of training materials).
- Identify and build productive relationships with logistics colleagues and staff within the area of assignment to support an integrated approach to food assistance.
- Follow emergency logistics preparedness practices, participate in preparation of CO Logistics Capacity Assessment (LCA), to ensure WFP are able to quickly respond and deploy food and needed resources to affected areas at the onset of the crisis.
- Participate in the on-going review of internal processes and procedures and identify ways to increase the day-to-day efficiencies.
- Act in an assigned emergency response capacity as required to meet emergency food assistance needs.
- Other as required.

Project reporting

This role reports to the line manager.

Key competencies

Education:

- Advanced University degree in Transport Economics, Supply Chain, Logistics, Engineering, Business Management, Mathematics or other related field, or First University degree with additional years of related work experience. Professional certification in SCM (Supply Chain Management) is an advantage.

Desired experiences for entry into the role:

- 3 years of post-graduate relevant professional / managerial experience with Master’s degree or 5 years of post-graduate relevant professional / managerial experience with Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain-related industry, Logistics, Shipping, Procurement.
- Experience in commercial or humanitarian transportation sectors.
- Experience monitoring and reporting on transport and freight market conditions and trends.
- Experience in dealing with shipments and clearing imports/exports with customs officials.
- Experience coordinating procurement and transportation processes with other units/ teams.
- Experience in warehouse and commodity management.
- Experience working with corporate systems (databases, software)

Language:

- Fluency (level C) in English language and the duty station’s language, if different.

Team management

This role has no team management responsibility.

Further information

- This Vacancy Announcement is for Pakistan Nationals Only.
- This vacancy announcement will be used to build a roster of prequalified applicants for future opportunities within same job profile at the current or lower level in Pakistan.

title: Logistics Associate / Logistics Assistant
body:
Overview of position

To provide specialized support functions and/or supervise staff performing standard logistics/supply chain processes and activities to enable effective delivery of goods and services for all delivery modalities.

title: Analyst - Compliance Solutions
body:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

This Analyst position will work with affiliates that pose a significant risk to this ministry. The primary responsibility will be working with affiliates to monitor compliance, conduct risk assessments, outline action steps, and make referrals for disciplinary action. Will cross train for other work areas on the team to provide back up when required due to heavy workload.

**Key Responsibilities:**

## **Analyst- Compliance Solutions**

**Remote (U.S.) | Habitat for Humanity International**

### Help strengthen Habitat’s global network while supporting affiliates through meaningful change.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we believe every family deserves a safe, affordable place to call home. Our affiliates are at the heart of that mission, and we’re looking for a thoughtful, analytical professional who can help ensure they have the leadership, systems, and support needed to thrive.

As our Analyst- Compliance Solutions, you’ll partner with affiliates facing operational or governance challenges, helping them assess risk, develop corrective action plans, and build long-term sustainability. This role requires equal parts relationship management, strategic thinking, project management, and sound judgment.

If you’re passionate about nonprofit excellence, enjoy solving complex organizational challenges, and can balance accountability with compassion, we’d love to hear from you.

### **What You’ll Do**

You’ll serve as a trusted advisor to affiliates while helping Habitat maintain strong organizational standards by:

- Conducting comprehensive risk assessments for at-risk affiliates.
- Partnering with affiliate leadership to develop practical corrective action plans.
- Monitoring compliance with Habitat policies and ministry requirements.
- Evaluating affiliate submissions and presenting recommendations to the Compliance Committee.
- Developing measurable improvement plans for affiliates on probation.
- Tracking organizational risk trends and preparing reports for leadership.
- Designing and improving systems, tools, and processes that strengthen affiliate oversight.
- Collaborating across teams to solve complex organizational challenges.
- Supporting additional compliance functions through cross-training and team collaboration.

### **What You Bring**

#### Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.
- 3–5 years of experience working with Habitat for Humanity or a similar nonprofit organization.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Strong project management and organizational skills.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities with minimal supervision.
- Excellent analytical and critical thinking abilities.
- Experience building collaborative relationships while navigating sensitive situations.
- Compassion, patience, persistence, and sound judgment.

### **Preferred Qualifications**

We’re especially interested in candidates with experience in:

- Nonprofit organizational risk assessments
- Compliance or governance
- Conflict resolution or mediation
- Organizational development
- Change management
- Continuous process improvement
- Performance monitoring and reporting
- Knowledge of Habitat for Humanity’s mission and affiliate model is highly preferred.

### **Why You’ll Love This Role**

This position offers the opportunity to:

- Protect and strengthen Habitat’s global ministry.
- Partner with nonprofit leaders across the country.
- Solve meaningful organizational challenges.
- Influence process improvements that impact affiliates nationwide.
- Work remotely while collaborating with an experienced, mission-driven team.

Location: Remote U.S. - work from anywhere

**Employees located near Atlanta, Americus, GA, or Washington, DC offices who are hired in a hybrid capacity report to the office on Tuesdays.**

### **Our Values**

At Habitat, our work is guided by three core values:

- Accountability — We take personal responsibility for Habitat’s mission.
- Courage — We do what’s right, even when it’s difficult.
- Humility — We recognize we are part of something bigger than ourselves.

***Safeguarding: HFHI requires that all employees take seriously their ethical responsibilities to safeguarding our intended beneficiaries, their communities, and all those with whom we work. Managers at all levels have responsibilities to support and develop systems that create and maintain an environment that prevents harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, safeguards the rights of beneficiaries and community members (especially children), and promotes the implementation of Habitat for Humanity’s code of conduct.***

### **Ready to Build Something Bigger?**

**If you’re passionate about strengthening nonprofit organizations, solving complex challenges, and advancing Habitat’s mission, we encourage you to apply.**

**Together, we can help more families build strength, stability, and self-reliance through shelter.**

**Hiring Range:**

The actual salary offered for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including location, internal equity and the candidate’s qualifications and professional experience. HFHI offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package that varies by country and typically includes vacation leave, sick leave, personal days, health insurance options, retirement plan contributions and life insurance. For work locations in the US, the annual hiring range for this position is:

$63,900.00

$95,100 USD

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

title: Consultancy to Develop a Western Indian Ocean Regional 30x30 Strategy and Regenerative Seascapes Toolkit
source: International Union for Conservation of Nature
body:
**Consultancy to Develop a Western Indian Ocean Regional 30x30 Strategy and Regenerative Seascapes Toolkit**

## Objective of the Consultancy

The objective of this consultancy is to support IUCN and its partners to develop a practical, ambitious and action-oriented Western Indian Ocean (WIO) Regional 30x30 Strategy and Roadmap, identifying tangible and scalable pathways through which the region can accelerate progress towards conserving and effectively managing at least 30% of marine and coastal areas by 2030.

With only four years remaining to achieve the 2030 target, the consultancy will build on the substantial work already undertaken through the Regenerative Seascapes for People, Climate and Nature (ReSea) project, including regional learning exchanges, national roadmaps and strategic discussions involving governments, local communities and key stakeholders from Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique, Madagascar and Comoros.

The consultant will review and capitalise on this existing work, assess lessons learned and progress to date, and propose concrete actions and mechanisms for accelerating implementation. The consultancy will assess a range of potential pathways towards 30x30, including Regenerative Marine Seascapes and, separately, Large Marine Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measures (OECMs), as well as Locally Managed Marine Areas (LMMAs), community-based marine conservation, marine protected areas and other relevant approaches.

The consultancy will also develop a practical and visually engaging Regenerative Seascapes Toolkit, building on lessons and experience from the ReSea project and the IUCN ESARO Coastal and Ocean Resilience Programme.

Ultimately, the assignment should result in a practical package of strategy, roadmap, tools and tangible recommendations that can support governments, communities, IUCN and regional partners in accelerating meaningful progress towards 30x30 over the remaining years to 2030.

### About IUCN

IUCN is a membership Union uniquely composed of both government and civil society organisations. It provides public, private and non-governmental organisations with the knowledge and tools that enable human progress, economic development and nature conservation to take place together.

Created in 1948, IUCN is now the world's largest and most diverse environmental network, harnessing the knowledge, resources and reach of more than 1,400 Member organisations and around 15,000 experts. It is a leading provider of conservation data, assessments and analysis. Its broad membership enables IUCN to fill the role of incubator and trusted repository of best practices, tools and international standards.

IUCN provides a neutral space in which diverse stakeholders—including governments, NGOs, scientists, businesses, local communities, Indigenous Peoples' organisations and others—can work together to forge and implement solutions to environmental challenges and achieve sustainable development.

### About the Project

In support of the establishment of sustainable, resilient and inclusive seascapes in the Western Indian Ocean, Mission Inclusion (Mi) and the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) implement the Regenerative Seascapes for People, Climate and Nature (ReSea) project in partnership with local feminist organisations in Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique, Madagascar and Comoros. The project is funded by Global Affairs Canada as part of the Partnering for Climate initiative. Its broader goal is to enhance the physical and socioeconomic resilience of coastal communities in these five countries by accelerating the uptake of Nature-based Solutions and gender-responsive conservation practices to protect, restore and sustainably manage marine and coastal ecosystems and unlock a regenerative blue economy. The ReSea project contributes to the Western Indian Ocean-led Great Blue Wall initiative by supporting the development of a network of sustainable, resilient and inclusive seascapes through a people-centred approach.

The Great Blue Wall initiative is built around four key pillars that align with the Global Biodiversity Framework and the Paris Climate Agreement. Blue Planet focuses on scaling and improving the management and governance of protected and conserved marine areas, with a strong emphasis on equity, gender-responsiveness and local stewardship. Blue Nature aims to restore and conserve critical ecosystems through gender-responsive Nature-based Solutions. Blue People promotes a regenerative and inclusive Blue Economy by empowering local communities, especially women and youth. Blue Partnerships is a cross-cutting pillar focusing on strengthening connectivity at all levels and across social, ecological, institutional and geographical dimensions.

Within this broader context, the ReSea project contributes to the Great Blue Wall's ambition for transformative and inclusive ocean governance by strengthening regenerative seascapes, community-led marine governance and other effective and sustainable approaches to marine and coastal conservation. The project is generating practical experience, lessons and evidence across Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique, Madagascar and Comoros on how conservation and sustainable management can be strengthened through integrated, people-centred and gender-responsive approaches. As the project moves towards its final phase, there is an important opportunity to capitalise on these experiences and translate them into practical pathways, tools and recommendations that can accelerate progress towards the 30x30 target and support the scaling and replication of regenerative seascapes across the Western Indian Ocean.

### Existing work on Regenerative Seascapes

As part of this work, IUCN ESARO brought together government representatives, local communities and key stakeholders from Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique, Madagascar and Comoros to learn from international experiences in the establishment and governance of marine seascapes. A regional learning exchange took place in Fiji in May 2025, followed by a second exchange in Indonesia in February 2026, undertaken in collaboration with Conservation International, which hosted the learning processes. The exchanges explored, among other experiences, the Lau Seascape in Fiji and the Bird's Head Seascape in Indonesia. Building on these learning exchanges, participating countries developed national roadmaps and a regional strategic framework to guide further engagement and action. Since then, some countries have made further progress and demonstrated interest in the establishment of marine seascapes, including Madagascar and Comoros. There is now a need to review and capitalise on the work undertaken to date, document lessons learned and identify practical and strategic pathways for moving from planning and learning towards implementation.

### Other pathways towards 30x30

Regenerative Seascapes are designed to deliver holistic outcomes across biodiversity conservation, sustainable livelihoods, climate resilience and inclusive ocean governance, contributing to multiple targets under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, as well as relevant Sustainable Development Goals and climate commitments. Within this broader contribution, Regenerative Seascapes have strong potential to support delivery of the 30x30 target. One potential pathway is through the formal recognition and reporting of qualifying areas as large-scale marine Other Effective Area-Based Conservation Measures (OECMs). Further work is therefore needed to define practical pathways through which Regenerative Seascapes could be recognised as direct contributions to 30x30, including by drawing lessons from emerging experiences such as the Philippines' approach to reporting large-scale marine OECMs.

International experience, including from the Philippines, provides important lessons on how networks of locally managed and conserved marine areas, supported by overarching governance and management arrangements, can create the conditions for recognition and reporting as large-scale marine OECMs and thereby contribute significantly to progress towards Target 3 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF), commonly referred to as the 30x30 target. Building on these lessons, the consultancy will assess how Regenerative Seascapes could create the enabling conditions for such recognition in the WIO, including through strengthened ecological connectivity, coordinated governance and management, and integration of locally managed and conserved areas within the wider seascape.

This will include assessing the legal, governance, institutional, technical and reporting conditions required for all or part of a Regenerative Seascape to qualify and be reported as a large-scale marine OECM. The consultancy will also examine how existing approaches, including LMMAs, community-based marine conservation and governance systems, marine protected areas, other OECMs, and relevant legal and financing mechanisms, can act as foundations or complementary components of a Regenerative Seascape and support its contribution to 30x30.

The consultant will create a report based on these findings.

### Regenerative Seascapes Toolkit

A further major output of the consultancy will be the development of a practical Regenerative Seascapes Toolkit. The toolkit will build on lessons from the ReSea project and the experience of the IUCN ESARO Coastal and Ocean Resilience Programme in Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique, Madagascar and Comoros, while also capitalising on relevant work and practical experience on seascapes undertaken by key stakeholders across the WIO. The consultant will work closely with relevant IUCN teams and stakeholders to consolidate practical experience and develop a usable methodology for the establishment, governance, implementation and scaling of regenerative seascapes. The toolkit should move beyond a conceptual publication and provide practical guidance and tools, including lessons, approaches, methodologies, examples and practical steps that can support replication and scaling.

## Description of the Assignment

- The consultant will design and implement an intensive and participatory consultation and engagement process with key stakeholders across the Western Indian Ocean.
- The consultation process will involve, as appropriate, government representatives, local communities and their organisations, civil society organisations, technical experts, regional institutions, conservation practitioners and other key stakeholders across Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique, Comoros and Madagascar.
- The consultant will review and capitalise on existing regional and national work related to 30x30, including strategies, roadmaps, frameworks, initiatives and relevant policy and planning processes, in order to ensure that the consultancy builds on existing efforts rather than duplicating them.
- The consultant will also identify, review and capitalise on work undertaken by key stakeholders across the region on seascapes, including existing seascape approaches, frameworks, methodologies, governance models, initiatives and practical experiences.
- The consultant will use consultations, interviews, group discussions, targeted workshops or virtual meetings and other appropriate engagement methods to validate lessons learned, identify barriers and opportunities, assess the feasibility of different pathways and ensure that the proposed strategy, roadmap and toolkit are informed by regional priorities and experience.
- The consultant will develop a WIO Regional 30x30 Strategy and Roadmap based on the above work and create methodologies/guidance for a practical Regenerative Seascapes Toolkit.

The consultancy will undertake the following four areas of work:

### 1. Review and capitalise on existing work

The consultant will review, map and consolidate relevant work undertaken through the ReSea project and other relevant initiatives, as well as existing 30x30-related strategies, roadmaps, plans, frameworks and initiatives developed at both regional and national levels across the Western Indian Ocean. This should include, among others, the Fiji and Indonesia learning exchanges; experiences from the Lau Seascape and Bird's Head Seascape; national roadmaps developed by the five ReSea countries; the regional strategic framework; existing national 30x30 strategies and roadmaps, including the Madagascar 30x30 strategy; progress made since these processes; existing lessons, challenges and opportunities; and relevant work undertaken by IUCN, governments, communities and other key partners.

The consultant will also identify, review and capitalise on relevant work undertaken by key stakeholders across the region on seascapes, including existing seascape approaches, frameworks, methodologies, governance models, initiatives and practical experiences. The consultant will undertake targeted and intensive consultations with relevant stakeholders to identify remaining gaps, emerging opportunities and priority areas for action and to ensure that the consultancy builds on, rather than duplicates, existing regional and national work.

### 2. Assess strategic pathways for accelerating 30x30

The consultant will assess the different practical and scalable pathways through which the WIO region can accelerate progress towards 30x30 during the remaining years to 2030.

Large Marine Seascapes: The consultant will review the existing work undertaken through ReSea and assess the practical way forward for the establishment and scaling of Large Marine Seascapes in the WIO. This should include lessons from Fiji and Indonesia; lessons from existing WIO work; assessment of national progress; potential governance models; legal and institutional requirements; financing and sustainability mechanisms; potential pilot opportunities; and practical recommendations for interested countries.

Large Marine OECMs: As a separate pathway, the consultant will assess the feasibility and potential contribution of Large Marine OECMs towards achieving meaningful progress towards 30x30. The work should draw on relevant international experience, particularly the Philippines, and assess relevant legal and policy frameworks; governance and management arrangements; technical and scientific requirements; spatial and data requirements; assessment and recognition processes; national and international reporting requirements; and potential opportunities in the WIO. The consultancy should propose practical next steps and a potential roadmap for governments interested in exploring this pathway.

Other pathways: The consultant will also assess other relevant pathways, including LMMAs; community-based marine conservation and governance; marine protected areas; other OECMs; legal and policy reforms; governance innovations; financing mechanisms; and other practical approaches capable of accelerating progress towards 30x30.

### 3. Develop the Regenerative Seascapes Toolkit

The consultant will work closely with the IUCN ESARO Coastal and Ocean Resilience Programme and relevant teams in Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique, Madagascar and Comoros.

The consultant will consult relevant teams and stakeholders and document practical lessons regarding the definition and understanding of regenerative seascapes; approaches applied across the ReSea portfolio; successes and challenges; governance models; community participation and ownership; conservation and sustainable-use approaches; financing and investment; policy and institutional arrangements; and opportunities for replication and scaling.

The toolkit will provide practical, step-by-step guidance across the different stages of regenerative seascape development, using an accessible “recipe card” methodology or similar approach. It will be designed for a broad audience (including local communities, practitioners, policymakers, scientists and other stakeholders) who are interested in learning from, adapting and applying approaches that have contributed to successful regenerative seascapes. The toolkit will allow users to draw on individual methods relevant to their context, rather than requiring adoption of the full approach.

The toolkit should be professionally designed and visually engaging.

### 4. Develop the WIO Regional 30x30 Strategy and Roadmap

Building on the above work, the consultant will develop a practical and action-oriented WIO Regional 30x30 Strategy and Roadmap.

The strategy should provide a clear regional vision; identify priority strategic pathways; propose tangible actions; identify national and regional priorities; propose legal and policy actions; recommend governance and institutional mechanisms; identify financing and investment opportunities; propose priority pilots and demonstration opportunities; identify key actors and partnerships; establish milestones and sequencing; and provide a practical roadmap towards 2030.

The strategy should focus on concrete and implementable actions rather than broad recommendations alone.

Deliverable/Activity - Description - Deadline

**Deliverable 1 - WIO 30x30 and Seascapes Stocktake, Lessons Learned and Strategic Assessment, including a comprehensive review and mapping of relevant regional and national 30x30 strategies, roadmaps, frameworks and initiatives; relevant ReSea work; the Fiji and Indonesia learning exchanges; national roadmaps; the regional strategic framework; existing work by key stakeholders on seascapes; progress to date; lessons learned; stakeholder mapping; and a detailed methodology for the consultancy. 31 October 2026**

Activity 1A - Review and synthesise existing ReSea documentation, regional and national 30x30 strategies, roadmaps, frameworks and initiatives, national roadmaps, the regional strategic framework and other relevant materials, including the Madagascar 30x30 strategy and other relevant national processes.

Activity 1B - Review and document lessons from the Fiji and Indonesia learning exchanges, relevant international experiences and existing work undertaken by key stakeholders in the WIO on seascapes, including approaches, frameworks, methodologies, governance models and practical initiatives.

Activity 1C - Assess progress, barriers, opportunities and priority gaps across the five countries and at regional level.

Activity 1D - Design and initiate an intensive stakeholder consultation process across the WIO, including targeted consultations with relevant government representatives, local communities and their organisations, civil society, technical experts, regional institutions and other key stakeholders.

Deliverable 2 - WIO 30x30 Pathways and Opportunities Assessment, including separate assessments of Large Marine Seascapes and Large Marine OECMs, as well as LMMAs, community-based conservation, other OECMs, marine protected areas and other relevant legal, governance, policy and financing pathways. - 20 November 2026

Activity 2A - Assess practical opportunities, requirements and next steps for Large Marine Seascapes in the WIO.

**Activity 2B - Assess the feasibility and potential contribution of Large Marine OECMs, including lessons from the Philippines and other relevant experience.**

Activity 2C - Assess opportunities to scale LMMAs, community-based marine conservation and other area-based conservation approaches.

Activity 2D - Identify legal, policy, governance, institutional and financing opportunities required to accelerate progress towards 30x30.

Activity 2E - Continue intensive consultations and validation with key stakeholders across the five ReSea countries and at regional level to assess, prioritise and validate the different strategic pathways towards achieving 30x30.

**Deliverable 3 - Draft Regenerative Seascapes Toolkit, including a practical and visually designed methodology documenting ReSea lessons and providing guidance and tools for the design, establishment, governance, implementation, financing and scaling of regenerative seascapes. - 5 December 2026**

Activity 3A - Undertake intensive consultations with the IUCN ESARO COR Seascape Team across Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique, Comoros and Madagascar, as well as relevant stakeholders and practitioners, to collect lessons, best practices, challenges and practical experience for the toolkit.

Activity 3B -Consolidate practical lessons, best practices, challenges and enabling conditions from the five ReSea countries.

Activity 3C - Develop the practical methodology, tools and case examples for the toolkit.

Activity 3D - Produce the draft professionally designed and visually engaging toolkit for review and validation.

**Deliverable 4 - Final WIO Regional 30x30 Strategy and Implementation Roadmap and Final Regenerative Seascapes Toolkit, including a prioritised four-year roadmap, recommendations on the different strategic pathways, proposed legal and governance actions, financing opportunities, priority pilots and tangible next steps towards 2030. - 15 December 2026**

Activity 4A - Develop and validate the final WIO Regional 30x30 Strategy and implementation roadmap.

Activity 4B - Finalise recommendations and proposed next steps for Large Marine Seascapes and Large Marine OECMs as distinct pathways.

Activity 4C - Finalise recommendations on other priority pathways, including LMMAs and community-based marine conservation.

Activity 4D - Incorporate stakeholder feedback and finalise the Regenerative Seascapes Toolkit.

Activity 4E - Submit all final editable documents, supporting materials and agreed knowledge products to IUCN.

Activity 4F - Organise and facilitate a regional webinar to present the final WIO Regional 30x30 Strategy and Implementation Roadmap and the Regenerative Seascapes Toolkit, share the key findings and recommendations, and facilitate discussion and initial socialisation with key stakeholders.

## Payment Schedule

The Timetable below summarises the chronological order of deliverables and indicates milestones at which IUCN will pay the Consultant.

Deliverable 1 - 20%

Deliverable 2 - 25%

Deliverable 3 - 25%

Deliverable 4 - 30%

## Skills and Experience

The ideal group of consultants for this consultancy should demonstrate a strong combination of technical expertise, regional knowledge and practical experience in marine conservation, seascape approaches and area-based conservation. The team should collectively demonstrate the following qualifications:

### Technical skills

- A senior Team Leader with demonstrated expertise in large-scale marine seascapes and seascape approaches.
- Extensive experience in marine conservation, ocean governance and area-based conservation.
- Demonstrated experience in the development, governance and implementation of large marine seascapes.
- Strong knowledge and practical experience of the Western Indian Ocean region.
- Demonstrated experience working with governments, local communities, civil society and regional organisations.
- Strong knowledge of the Global Biodiversity Framework and the 30x30 target.
- Demonstrated expertise in OECMs, protected and conserved areas and other area-based conservation approaches.
- Knowledge of community-led conservation, LMMAs and community-based marine governance.
- Expertise in marine policy, law and institutional frameworks.
- Experience in strategic planning and the development of practical implementation roadmaps.
- Strong experience in multi-stakeholder consultations, facilitation and participatory processes.
- Experience developing practical knowledge products, methodologies and toolkits.

It will be considered a strong asset for the proposed team to include an expert with direct experience of the Philippines' approach to Large Marine OECMs, or a team member with demonstrated in-depth knowledge of the Philippine large marine OECM experience and its relevance to other regions.

### Communications and design expertise

The team should include a communications, knowledge management and/or visual design specialist with demonstrated experience in developing high-quality and visually engaging toolkits, knowledge products, practical guides, publications and visual communication materials. This expertise will be essential for the development and professional design of the Regenerative Seascapes Toolkit.

### Other qualifications

- Excellent analytical and writing skills.
- Demonstrated ability to synthesise complex technical and stakeholder inputs into practical and actionable strategies and recommendations.
- Strong project management and coordination capacity.
- Excellent English language skills.
- Working knowledge of French and/or Portuguese would be an asset given the linguistic diversity of the WIO region.
- Relevant advanced university degree in marine conservation, ocean governance, environmental policy, natural resource management, geography, ecology or a related field.
- The proposed team should collectively demonstrate the full range of expertise required to undertake the assignment.

## Supervision and Coordination

The consultancy will be jointly supervised by the IUCN Regional Coastal and Ocean Governance Manager and the IUCN Regional Blue Science and Business Innovation Manager.

The consultant will work very closely with the IUCN ESARO Coastal and Ocean Resilience (COR) Seascape Team across the five ReSea countries: Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique, Comoros and Madagascar throughout the development of the WIO Regional 30x30 Strategy and the Regenerative Seascapes Toolkit.

For the development and design of the Regenerative Seascapes Toolkit, the consultant will also work closely with the IUCN ESARO COR Impact Officer and the Regional Ocean Communications Officer, particularly to ensure that the toolkit appropriately reflects IUCN experience and lessons, is practical and accessible to its intended audiences, and meets the required communication and visual design standards.

The consultant will also be expected to engage and consult with relevant government representatives, local communities, national and regional stakeholders and technical partners as required for the assignment.

## Timeframe and Location

The main consultancy period will run from 9 October 2026 to 15 December 2026.

All four deliverables, including the final WIO Regional 30x30 Strategy and Implementation Roadmap and the final Regenerative Seascapes Toolkit, must be submitted by 15 December 2026.

Following the submission of the final deliverable, the consultant will continue to provide agreed technical and implementation support until 28 February 2027. This support will focus on the early socialisation and implementation of the strategy and its priority actions, including follow-up with IUCN and relevant partners, as agreed with the supervising team.

The consultancy may be undertaken remotely. Any travel requirements will be agreed in advance with IUCN.

title: Graphic Design and Visualisation of the IslandPlas Plastic Waste Profiles
source: International Union for Conservation of Nature
body:
**Terms of Reference for IUCN Consultancy**

**Title: Graphic Design and Visualisation of the IslandPlas Plastic Waste Profiles**

**Objective of the Consultancy**

The objective of this consultancy is to engage an experienced graphic designer or design agency to develop an understandable, engaging and accessible visual identity for the seven IslandPlas national Plastic Waste Profiles (PWPs), covering Cabo Verde, Comoros, Madagascar, Mauritius, São Tomé and Príncipe, Seychelles, and Zanzibar.

IUCN holds in its possession the draft PWP reports, and the aim of this consultancy is to transform these technically detailed reports into clear, visually compelling and easy-to-navigate publications. The assignment will focus on professional publication layout, information design, infographics, diagrams, maps, icons and data visualisations, while ensuring that all seven reports are aesthetically consistent and recognisable as one IslandPlas publication series.

**About IUCN**

IUCN is a membership Union uniquely composed of both government and civil society organisations. It provides public, private and non-governmental organisations with the knowledge and tools that enable human progress, economic development and nature conservation to take place together.

Created in 1948, IUCN is now the world’s largest and most diverse environmental network, harnessing the knowledge, resources and reach of more than 1,400 Member organisations and around 15,000 experts. It is a leading provider of conservation data, assessments and analysis. Its broad membership enables IUCN to fill the role of incubator and trusted repository of best practices, tools and international standards.

IUCN provides a neutral space in which diverse stakeholders including governments, NGOs, scientists, businesses, local communities, indigenous peoples organisations and others can work together to forge and implement solutions to environmental challenges and achieve sustainable development.

Working with many partners and supporters, IUCN implements a large and diverse portfolio of conservation projects worldwide. Combining the latest science with the traditional knowledge of local communities, these projects work to reverse habitat loss, restore ecosystems and improve people’s well-being.

[www.iucn.org](http://www.iucn.org)

[https://twitter.com/IUCN/](https://twitter.com/IUCN/)

**About the Project**

The IslandPlas project is an IUCN-led initiative, supported by The Coca-Cola Foundation, that targets seven African Islands; Cabo Verde, Comoros, Madagascar, Mauritius, São Tomé and Príncipe, Seychelles, and Zanzibar. The project, running until end of 2027 envisions African Islands that are free from plastic waste in the environment, and in which circular measures are in place to prevent plastic leakage into the ocean. The project actions are designed to reduce and prevent plastic pollution into the environment through demonstrating effective, quantifiable solutions to addressing plastic leakage.

Among others, the project contributes to achieving the objectives prescribed in the Declaration adopted by the Ministerial Conference on the Blue and Circular Economy in the Island States of Africa and the Indian Ocean (September 2023), that advocates for a blue and circular economy, enabled through circular entrepreneurship, skills development, increased investment towards science, research and development, and legal and policy reforms. The project is designed to strengthen understanding of national plastic material flows and waste and pollution footprint, integrate and support informal waste sector actors and local communities, support local ventures for innovation to reduce plastic pollution using locally-appropriate solutions, strengthen institutional capacities (governmental, municipal, community level) to catalyse change, and explore potential for an inter-regional recycling hub.

At the regional level, the project aims to achieve three main outcomes:

1. Sustainable and improved livelihoods of informal waste sector actors engaged in a circular plastics economy (9,600 beneficiaries);
2. Quantifiable regeneration of plastic waste material through circular approaches, including through plastic material recovery (14,000 tons), recycling (5,600 tons) and upcycling; and
3. Strengthened sector innovation and enterprise development with new growth opportunities through direct capital investments to locally-appropriate solutions (US $2 million).

As part of the project, IslandPlas is developing a national Plastic Waste Profile for each of the seven project countries. The profiles bring together technical evidence on plastic material flows, waste generation and management, collection and recycling systems, plastic leakage, policy and governance, stakeholders, infrastructure, data gaps, challenges and opportunities for action. The technical content will be developed and quality-assured separately by IUCN and its technical consultants; this consultancy therefore focuses on visual communication, information design and final publication production.

**Description of the Assignment**

The selected consultant will be responsible for the graphic design, information visualisation and final layout of seven national IslandPlas Plastic Waste Profiles, whose draft reports exist. The consultant will work from technical content supplied and approved by IUCN and will be expected to identify opportunities to communicate complex information more effectively through visual design.

The assignment should go beyond formatting text. The consultant should actively identify what information can be communicated more clearly through infographics, diagrams, charts, maps, visual summaries, pull-out statistics and other information-design techniques, without changing the scientific meaning of the content.

***1. Develop a common visual identity and report template***

• Develop a professional visual approach for the IslandPlas Plastic Waste Profile series in consultation with IUCN.

• Establish consistent publication layout and page architecture, cover design, typography, section hierarchy, colour palette, tables, charts, maps, photographs, call-out boxes, references, iconography and illustration style, in accordance with the IslandPlas brand guidelines, and the IUCN Great Blue Wall Style Guide.

• Create standard approaches for highlighting key statistics, findings, recommendations, uncertainty and data gaps.

• Ensure all seven reports are aesthetically consistent and immediately recognisable as part of one IslandPlas publication series, while allowing appropriate country-specific identity through photography, maps and other visual elements.

***2. Design and layout seven national Plastic Waste Profiles***

• Apply the approved visual identity to the national profiles for Cabo Verde, Comoros, Madagascar, Mauritius, São Tomé and Príncipe, Seychelles, and Zanzibar.

• Convert the supplied technical content into professionally designed publications with a consistent structure, visual hierarchy and reader experience across all seven reports.

• Where report structures or information vary between countries, propose appropriate design solutions while maintaining overall consistency and comparability.

***3. Develop infographics and data visualisations***

• Translate complex quantitative and qualitative information into clear, accurate and engaging visual communication.

• Potential visual products may include plastic material flow diagrams; waste generation, collection and recycling statistics; plastic leakage pathways; waste management system diagrams; value chain diagrams; stakeholder maps; policy timelines; geographic maps; plastic waste composition; sources and destinations of plastic material; data gap summaries; and visual presentation of priority actions or recommendations.

• Develop clear country-level headline statistics and visual summaries that allow readers to quickly understand the most important findings.

• Simplify and clarify information without changing its scientific meaning. The consultant will not be expected to undertake new scientific analysis and should seek clarification from IUCN where any modification or interpretation is required.

***4. Improve accessibility of complex technical information***

• Use design to create a clear hierarchy between headline findings, key statistics, supporting evidence, technical detail, data limitations and recommendations.

• Where appropriate, break up dense sections using visual summaries, pull-out statistics, diagrams, icons, illustrations or other information design approaches.

• Ensure the profiles remain technically robust while being accessible to both specialist and non-specialist audiences, including government decision-makers, waste management practitioners, private sector actors, development partners, researchers and communities.

***5. Maintain consistency and comparability across countries***

• Use consistent terminology, visualisation formats, icons, graph styles, units, page structures and visual hierarchy for comparable indicators across the seven reports wherever possible.

• Develop the visual system so that it can support future regional comparison and synthesis of IslandPlas results.

***6. Image selection and visual assets***

• Work with project photographs and other visual assets supplied by IUCN and recommend where photography or illustration would strengthen the publications.

• Ensure captions and image credits are correctly assigned and consistently presented and develop icons or simple illustrations where required.

• Any externally sourced visual material must have appropriate permissions and licensing for IUCN use.

***7. Review, revision and final production***

• Develop an initial draft design concept and representative sample pages for IUCN approval before full production begins.

• Apply the agreed approach to one complete country profile as a prototype to test the full design system, including infographics and data visualisation.

• Roll out the approved design system across all seven country profiles and incorporate consolidated feedback from IUCN.

• Provide final publication-ready, web-optimised and editable/source files, including editable versions of original infographics, illustrations and graphic assets created through the consultancy.

**Duration of the Assignment**

The consultancy is expected to run for approximately eight (8) weeks from contract signature spread out over three months. The final schedule will be agreed during the inception phase and may be adapted according to the readiness of individual country reports and the timing of consolidated IUCN feedback.

The assignment will cover design concept development, production of a complete prototype profile, rollout across all seven countries, revisions and final publication production.

**Deliverables and activities**

The consultant will provide the following deliverables and carry out the following activities:

**Deliverable / Activity - Description - Indicative Timeline**

**1. Inception and Design Concept - Kick-off meeting with IUCN and submission of the proposed creative direction, visual identity, typography, colour palette, report structure and proposed approaches to data visualisation. - Week 1**

**2. Sample Report Pages / Visual System - Design approximately 5–10 representative pages demonstrating the cover, contents, section pages, body text, data visualisations, tables, photography, call-out statistics and other core design elements. - Week 2**

**3. First Complete PWP Prototype - Design and layout one complete country Plastic Waste Profile, including proposed infographics and data visualisations, for IUCN review before rolling out the design across the remaining profiles. - Weeks 2–3**

**4. Seven Draft Plastic Waste Profiles - Complete the first design and layout of all seven country reports using the approved visual system. - Weeks 4–6**

**5. Revised Final Reports - Incorporate consolidated IUCN technical, communications and country team feedback and deliver seven final designed reports. - Weeks 7**

**6. Final Publication Package - Deliver final high-resolution and web-optimised PDFs (including French and Portuguese versions), editable/source design files and editable versions of all original infographics, illustrations and graphic assets created through the consultancy. - Week 8**

**Payment Schedule**

The Timetable below summarises the chronological order of deliverables and indicates milestones at which IUCN will pay the Consultant.

**Deliverable - Milestone payment**

IUCN approval of the inception/design concept and representative sample pages. - 20%

Submission of the complete first design/layout of all seven country Plastic Waste Profiles - 30%

IUCN approval of all seven final reports and receipt of the complete final publication package, including editable/source files and graphic assets. - 50%

title: REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP): MIDLINE EVALUATION OF THE USDA-FUNDED TIWOLOKA PROGRAM IN MALAWI
body:
CARE Malawi seeks a qualified consulting firm to conduct a Midline Evaluation for the USDA-funded Tiwoloka Program (2024-2029), implemented across six districts in Malawi. The evaluation will assess progress in literacy, nutrition, health, hygiene, school feeding, and government systems strengthening using a mixed-methods, quasi-experimental approach.

The selected firm will be responsible for data collection, analysis, reporting, and presentation of findings, generating evidence to inform project implementation, learning, and policy decisions. Firms with demonstrated experience in large-scale evaluations, education, nutrition, school feeding and advanced quantitative and qualitative research methodologies are encouraged to apply.

**Application Deadline:** 23 October 2026

title: Transformation Manager
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
**Position Title**: Transformation Manager

**Location**: UK, Ireland, Belgium, Germany, Switzerland, Australia, New Zealand, Burkina Faso, Zimbabwe, Kenya, Nigeria, Madagascar, Indonesia, Nepal, Bangladesh, Philippines or Laos.

**Reports to**: International Director

**Application Deadline**: 11 October 2026

**Contract Type**: Fixed term – 3 years  
  
**? About CBM Global**

CBM Global works alongside people with disabilities in low- and middle-income countries to fight poverty and exclusion and transform lives. Check out our website and LinkedIn profile to learn more. Drawing on over 100 years of experience and driven by Christian values, we work with the most marginalised in society to:

- Break the cycle of poverty and disability
- Treat and prevent conditions that lead to disability; and
- Build inclusive communities where everyone can enjoy their human rights and achieve their full potential.

We work in over 20 countries, investing in long-term, authentic partnerships with the Disability Movement and multiplying our impact by delivering a combination of inclusive community-based programmes, advocacy for national and global policy change and inclusion advice to other organisations. CBM Global is a worldwide federation with the following Members: CBM Australia, CBM Ireland, CBM Kenya, CBM New Zealand, CBM Switzerland, and CBM UK.

**? About the Role**

CBM Global is embarking on a change process called ‘Building Together’ which seeks to:

- Accelerate the shifting of power to our partners and project participants.
- Increase the impact of our work
- Generate efficiencies in our systems and ways of working

Core to this change, the organisation is aiming to evolve the roles it plays as an international NGO to focus on those roles where we add the most value in our work alongside our partners and which enable the power shift we are seeking. Alongside this, in our country level work we are seeking to shift away from a deep seated project based approach, towards an approach that seeks to facilitate programmatic, systems level change.

We will initially pilot these new ways of working in two countries before planning a wider role out. During these pilots we will:

- Explore further the new roles we can play as an international NGO and sharpen / refine these, before a wider roll out.
- Develop our programmatic approach and develop initial systems level programmes that align with this approach.
- Develop learning products, guidance and tools for use by teams within CBM Global when we roll out our approach more widely.
- Explore and review the roles and responsibilities of different teams within CBM Global and develop efficient systems, processes and procedures related to aspects of programme oversight and management.
- Assess the capacity of teams within CBM Global to undertake the revised roles and responsibilities and determine changes required within teams to undertake these new roles in the future.

Towards the end of the pilots, we will then develop a roll out plan, which building upon the learning will map out the wider roll out across all CBM Global teams.

The proposed change process will be complex and will impact on many different teams and entities across CBM Global. The Transformation Manager will lead and coordinate this work. They will be required to gain an in-depth understanding of current ways of working; identify changes needed; design and lead a change process; and directly deliver key tasks within it, whilst also coordinating tasks undertaken by relevant teams across the Federation.

**Job overview and core purpose**

Working within the CBM Global Secretariat, the Transformation Manager will be responsible for day-to-day leadership, coordination and delivery of the Building Together change process.

A steering committee chaired by the International Director, has been established for strategic oversight. Reporting to the International Director, but accountable to the Steering committee, the Transformation Manager will be responsible for project managing the overall change process as well as for undertaking some specific tasks that are part of the project plan.

**Key Responsibilities:**

1\. Overall project management of the Building Together change process, including of the 2 pilots. This will require:

a) A detailed project plan to be maintained and updated as necessary, with timelines, responsibilities, dependabilities and deliverables clearly articulated and understood

b) Close coordination and follow up with internal stakeholders / teams responsible for different tasks, to enable progress to be tracked, the coherence of the overall plan to be maintained and plans to be revised where necessary

c) The identification of risks and mitigating actions

d) The production of periodic progress reports/updates

e) Support the governance of the Building Together change process, facilitating connections and communications between stakeholders and operating as the Secretary to the steering committee, arranging meetings, agendas and notes

2\. Leading and supporting the development of the necessary systems, procedures and processes required to operationalise the changed ways of working. This will require close collaboration with internal stakeholders and teams to gain their support for the proposed changes and to then update/amend current procedures and processes

3\. Backstopping support to internal stakeholders / teams, supporting them to undertake their tasks to a high standard

4\. Updating the Federation Operating model, incorporating changes agreed during the Building Together change process

5\. Finalising a learning framework / approach for the Building Together change process and then leading the ongoing assessment of the change programme in line with this framework in order to:

a) Support real time decision making

b) Generate evidence and learning that can strengthen, support and guide future roll out

c) Determine the extent to which the change process is achieving its objectives and enable informed revisions and improvements to be made

6\. Facilitating learning and developing learning products, guides, tools, checklists etc that will support the wider roll out and replication of the pilots. These should be based upon our own learning and experience and also draw upon evidence, insights and existing materials and resources from within the sector.

7\. Supporting internal communications about the change process for the purpose of building understanding, awareness and support across the Federation. This will involve developing a clear communication strategy / approach; writing articles / papers; preparing and delivering presentations to different groups, including senior leadership and Board; and providing guidance and support to colleagues, who will communicate to their teams.

8\. Preparing ‘decision papers’ for any proposed changes which require approval. This could include papers for the Board, senior leadership or other decision-making fora within the Federation.

9\. Developing and then project managing a roll out plan.

10.Proposing changes to wider Federation approaches, ways of working and structures etc, which would enable the Building Together change process to achieve the greatest impact.

**Key internal stakeholders**

To achieve the Building Together outcomes, the Transformation Manager will be required to interface effectively with entities and teams across the Federation, including:

- Teams within the Secretariat responsible for operational processes and procedures, in particular the Finance and Global Online teams
- The MEAL team
- The Secretariat Institutional Fundraising team
- Other entities within the CBM Global Federation, in particular Members, Technical teams and Country Teams

**Key outcomes expected from this role**

1\. Organization wide understanding and buy in for the change process.

2\. Successful delivery of the 2 pilots and other currently planned related activities

3\. Development and successful delivery of a wider roll out plan, based upon learning from the pilots.

4\. Improved and more efficient systems and procedures, aligned to the new ways of working

5\. A suite of learning products, guides, tools and checklists.

**? Who We’re Looking For**

Experience and knowledge

1. A minimum of 5 years’ experience at a senior management level in an international development or humanitarian organisation with a track-record of leading successful organisation change and transformation.
2. Significant experience of designing, delivering and leading systems level, programmatic approaches, with deep practical experience of successfully applying these approaches.
3. Strong understanding of localisation and approaches to achieving successful power shift
4. Experience developing organisational processes and procedures, particularly related to grant management and the project cycle
5. Experience working in a Federated organisation
6. Knowledge of disability issues and a rights based approach. Lived experience of disability an advantage.

**Skills/competencies/personal qualities**

1. Excellent project management skills.
2. Outstanding interpersonal, relationship building skills with a track-record of building and managing effective relationships across an organisation
3. Persuasive and a good influencer
4. A self-starter. Proactive, resourceful and entrepreneurial.
5. Flexible and comfortable with complexity and uncertainty.
6. Able to operate both strategically and operationally, with a willingness and ability to lead and influence at a strategic level, whilst also getting involved in the day to day operational detail.
7. Diligent, persistent with a can-do, positive attitude.
8. Open, clear and inclusive communicator, with the ability to clearly articulate and win support for ideas.
9. Committed, excited, and passionate about disability inclusion and the rights of people with disabilities.
10. Alignment to our CBM Global values ([Our Vision, Mission and Values | CBM Global](https://cbm-global.org/about-us/who-we-are/vision-mission-values)) and our Safeguarding Policy (CBM-Global-Policy-Safeguarding.pdf) and Code of Conduct (CBM-Global-Code-of-Conduct.pdf)

**We welcome and encourage applications from people with lived experience of disability.**

We proactively work on achieving a diverse and inclusive work environment for people from all backgrounds and abilities.

**? Why work with Us?**

1. A chance to be part of a global movement pursuing an inclusive world for people with disabilities.
2. A supportive, flexible, and inclusive work environment.
3. Flexible working arrangements.

6. Competitive remuneration and benefits.

body:
**Médecins Sans Frontières,** founded in 1971, is an international medical humanitarian organization that provides emergency medical assistance to people affected by conflict, epidemics, disasters or exclusion from health care. Our teams are made up of tens of thousands of medical professionals, logistics, administrative and various other professions, all guided by our medical ethics and our principles of impartiality, independence and neutrality.

**MSF WaCA,** created in 2019, is the first MSF headquarters in Africa, and responds to the desire to reinvent the MSF movement after 50 years of humanitarian actions in the world, for more access to care, more reactivity and proactivity for greater medical coverage of affected populations in the world.

**Why join us?**

You are preparing to become a member of the MSF family, with over 50 years of emergency medical action that earned the Nobel Peace Prize in 1999.

We are an inclusive organization that considers social and professional well-being a right for all and provides an environment that considers the diversity of each member.

**MSF WaCA** claims an African anchorage that considers the local expertise with which it contributes to the implementation of its activities and makes each member, a key actor of the new dynamics of the humanitarian action in the world.
