title: HEAD OF PEOPLE SAFEGUARDING AND INCLUSION
body:
**Médecins Sans Frontières,** founded in 1971, is an international medical humanitarian organization that provides emergency medical assistance to people affected by conflict, epidemics, disasters or exclusion from health care. Our teams are made up of tens of thousands of medical professionals, logistics, administrative and various other professions, all guided by our medical ethics and our principles of impartiality, independence and neutrality.

**MSF WaCA,** created in 2019, is the first MSF headquarters in Africa, and responds to the desire to reinvent the MSF movement after 50 years of humanitarian actions in the world, for more access to care, more reactivity and proactivity for greater medical coverage of affected populations in the world.

**Why join us?**

You are preparing to become a member of the MSF family, with over 50 years of emergency medical action that earned the Nobel Peace Prize in 1999.

We are an inclusive organization that considers social and professional well-being a right for all and provides an environment that considers the diversity of each member.

**MSF WaCA** claims an African anchorage that considers the local expertise with which it contributes to the implementation of its activities and makes each member, a key actor of the new dynamics of the humanitarian action in the world.

**Diversity, Inclusion & Safe Recruitment**

MSF offers equal recruitment and development opportunities without any form of discrimination based on gender, religion, sexual orientation, ethnicity, geographical origin, physical disability or any other discriminatory ground.

**Female candidates who meet the requirements are strongly encouraged to apply.**

***Persons with disabilities are strongly encouraged to apply, and reasonable accommodations are available upon request.***

**MSF is committed to applying Safe Recruitment principles, ensuring transparent, fair, and respectful recruitment processes that protect candidates, the organization, and its beneficiaries.**

**Missions**

Under the leadership of the Deputy General Director, the Head of People Safeguarding and Inclusion provides strategic leadership and organizational assurance on safeguarding, including the inclusion and the protection of people across MSF WaCA. The position is accountable for ensuring that appropriate safeguarding and inclusion systems, standards, risk management mechanisms and reporting arrangements are in place and effectively implemented across MSF WaCA. The Head of People Safeguarding and Inclusion acts as an independent source of expertise, advice and challenge leadership, management and operational teams, while working closely with Human Resources, Operations, Medical and other relevant functions. The role does not replace the respective accountabilities of HR, Medical or Operations, but ensures that safeguarding and inclusion risks are identified, addressed and appropriately escalated across the organization.

**Objectives**

Provide strategic leadership on safeguarding and inclusion across MSF WaCA. Ensure safeguarding risks are systematically identified, assessed, monitored and mitigated. Promote a culture based on respect, dignity, equity, accountability and inclusion. Ensure accessible and trusted reporting and feedback mechanisms for staff, patients and communities. Oversee the appropriate management and governance of safeguarding concerns and investigations. Ensure that learning from cases, investigations and risks informs organisational improvement. Support Operations and other departments in integrating safeguarding and inclusion into their strategies, plans and practices. Provide strategic advice to the General Director, Leadership Team and Board on safeguarding, inclusion and related organisational risks. Ensure appropriate coordination with HR, Medical, Operations and SHU on matters falling within their respective mandates.

**Main responsibilities**

1. **Safeguarding Strategy, Prevention and Mainstreaming:**

Develop, maintain and oversee the implementation of the MSF WaCA safeguarding strategy and annual priorities; define safeguarding objectives, milestones and key results; ensure integration into safer recruitment, emergency response, safer programming, prevention and awareness, risk management and Safeguarding Focal Points; establish and maintain safeguarding risk management framework; represent MSF WaCA in movement forums; ensure standards, policies and training are implemented; promote safe reporting culture.

Ensure all relevant materials including safeguarding policy, local reporting procedure, training manuals, publication and related tools are in place and properly disseminated to staff, partners and representatives.

**2. Safeguarding Case Management, Investigations and Accountability:**

Ensure reporting mechanisms; oversee case management framework; ensure investigation governance, investigator selection and conflict management; oversee investigations; ensure confidentiality, fairness and protection from retaliation; communicate findings; monitor recommendations; escalate high-risk cases; maintain reporting to Leadership Team and Board; ensure donor/movement reporting requirements.

**3. Inclusion, Diversity, Equity and People Voice:**

Lead inclusion and DEI agenda; advise leadership on barriers; promote inclusive leadership; monitor indicators; integrate gender/diversity/equity/inclusion into HR processes; address barriers for under-represented groups; promote staff feedback mechanisms; support patient/community voice and accountability mechanisms; liaise with movement structures.

**4. Safeguarding and Protection of People in Operations:**

Provide safeguarding expertise to Operations; support risk identification in programme design and emergency response; integrate safeguarding standards into field and emergency operations; participate in field missions; ensure risks from visits/audits/reviews are documented and followed up.

**5. Staff Protection, Psychosocial Support and Wellbeing:**

Provide oversight on staff protection and psychosocial support; ensure support mechanisms with HR/medical functions; ensure access to information/support/referrals; promote psychological safety, dignity and respect; ensure coordination across safeguarding, HR and staff health; support operational/medical responses for staff wellbeing implications.

**6. Medical and Other Professional Governance Interfaces:**

Ensure referral of medical errors/quality-of-care concerns to medical governance; address safeguarding implications from medical incidents; coordinate with Medical teams; contribute to organisational learning.

**7. Data Protection and Confidentiality:**

Oversee safeguarding aspects of people-related data protection; ensure case information handling per confidentiality and data protection requirements; work with HR/Medical/IT; ensure records and systems are fit for purpose.

**8. Governance, Reporting and Risk Management:**

Provide strategic analysis and recommendations; maintain safeguarding and inclusion dashboard; report to Board; reflect risks in organisational risk management; monitor corrective/preventive actions; contribute to audits/reviews/assessments; ensure documentation and compliance evidence; track movement-wide developments and standards.

## **Job requirements**

**Education**

**Essential**

· University degree in Law, Psychology, Social Sciences, International Development, Risk Management, Human Resources, Protection, or another relevant field.

· Specialized training and/or certification in Safeguarding, PSEA, Protection, Investigations, or a related field.

**Desirable**

· Certification in investigation, safeguarding, or protection.

· Training in psychosocial support or trauma-informed approaches.

· Training in risk management or compliance.

**Competencies**

· Excellent understanding of international principles and standards regarding safeguarding, PSEA, and the prevention and protection against abuse.

· Proficiency in survivor-centered and victim-centered approaches, the “do no harm” principle, and confidentiality.

· Strong skills in case management and risk management.

· Ability to develop and maintain safe, accessible, and confidential reporting mechanisms.

· Ability to conduct risk assessments and implement mitigation measures.

· Good knowledge of the principles of investigation, due process, evidence management, and documentation.

· Ability to analyze data and identify trends and systemic risks.

· Excellent skills in drafting policies, procedures, reports, and recommendations.

· Ability to develop safeguarding KPIs and dashboards.

· Good understanding of the interactions between Safeguarding, HR, Legal, Risk, Operations, and Senior Management.

· Very strong training, facilitation, and communication skills.

**Professional experience required**

· Minimum 7 years of relevant professional experience, preferably including substantial experience within a humanitarian or international organisation;

· Significant experience in safeguarding, protection, investigations, prevention or related fields;

· Experience designing and implementing safeguarding systems and strategies;

· Experience in complex humanitarian or operational environments;

· Risk management and organisational change; Cross-department work and senior stakeholder influence;

· Managing sensitive and confidential cases;

· Minimum 3 years of people management experience, preferably in senior/strategic position; DEI/inclusion/organisational culture experience highly desirable;

· Medical, protection or social work experience

· Experience in conducting investigations

· MSF movement experience is an asset.

**Languages Skills**

· Working proficiency in English and French (Required)

**Computer Skills**

· MS Office suite (mainly MS Word, Excel and Powerpoint)

· Familiarity with online communication and collaboration platforms, including Microsoft Teams, Zoom, SharePoint, etc.

\-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*N.B.: This job description provides a framework for the main responsibilities and primary activities of the position. It is not exhaustive. Therefore, the responsibilities and activities of the position may differ from those described in this job description due to organizational and operational needs.*

**Deadline: 09th October 2026 18:00 GMT**

body:
## ABOUT US...

**Desired start date: 15/11/2026**  
**Duration of the mission: 6 months**  
**Location: Kabul**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## ABOUT THE MISSION

SOLIDARITÉS INTERNATIONAL activities are implemented in Nimroz, Farah, Herat, Helmand, Bamyan, Kandahar, Uruzgan, Zabul and Kunduz, provinces, with emergency activities that can be deployed all over the country. Operational bases are Nimroz, Farah, Herat and Bamyan provinces.

The team is now made of 125 national and 9 international employees with an annual budget of around 5.5 M EUR. SI currently implements WASH and Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR)/Natural Resource Management (NRM) programs.

There are currently 3 grants under implementation:

\- CDCS (French MoFA): in Bamyan, focusing on DRR/NRM and disability inclusion; this project is in consortium with Humanity & Inclusion (HI).

\- ECHO consortium: with Save the Children (lead), INTERSOS and Humanity & Inclusion. The project responds to the returnees crisis at informal settlements and areas of return. SI response focuses on WASH, MPCA and winterization.

\- ECHO consortium: with INTERSOS (lead), and MdM. Tthe project provides comprehensive WASH, Health and Nutrition response in underserved areas in 6 provinces... SI response focuses on WASH.

The SI team consists of 36 national staff in Nimroz, 13 national staff in Bamyan, 39 national staff and 1 international staff member across the south-west region, and 37 national staff and 8 international staff based at the coordination office in Kabul.

## ABOUT THE JOB

**GENERAL OBJECTIVES**

In close collaboration with the Country Director (CD), the DCD-P prime objectives are to provide leadership and management of the strategic programming, strengthening of SI’s programme development, quality and accountability. The DCD ensures the internal coherence between program activities and is responsible for ensuring that programs are driven by needs, based on evidence, adaptable to contextual changes and conflict sensitive, monitored closely and resourced appropriately. The position holder will require high levels of flexibility, strategic thinking and adaptibility

**ISSUES AND SPECIFIC CHALLENGES**

1 - Ensure high quality programing and timely implementation of projects amidst tight deadlines.   
2- Continued capacity building of the Program and MEAL teams in coordination and bases.   
3- Support the development of new proposals for 2027 & beyond, specifically humanitairan-development nexus programming.

**PRIORITIES ON THE 2-3 FIRST MONTHS**

1-In coordination with the CD, establish strong working relations with different stakeholders, including Donors, partner NGOs, clusters, OCT....etc., to support SI Positioning .   
2-Strengthen program quality in terms of implementation and MEAL interventions, streamline crosscutting priorities, and ensure compliance with SI standards and donor requirements.  
3-Support Proposal Development in coordination with the Grants Manager and Program and MEAL teams.  
4- Ensure that the operational HR setup is fit for purpose and aligned with programmatic objectives.

**SECURITY CONSTRAINTS**

For expats : Limited possibility of movement in Kabul: guest houses of other NGOs, UN Campounds, 3 supermarkets / malls are validated. As well as several restaurants.

Missions on the field are possible to all SI operational bases

Security situation is stable, but close monitoring is on-going as it could become volatile again

For women expatriate few specific security rules are implemented

## YOUR PROFILE

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCE**

- Diploma : Master degree in humanitarian field and related topics
- Experience in the humanitarian sector : 5 years and more
- Experience on a similar position : 0/2 years

**SKILLS**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1\. Project management: Experience planning, coordinating and monitoring projects, and assessments.

2\. Analysis and reporting: Ability to analyse information and produce clear reports, recommendations and other technical documents.

3\. Digital and data management: Good computer skills (Microsoft Office); experience with Kobo or other digital data collection tools is an asset.

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1\. Communication and stakeholder engagement: Strong interpersonal skills and ability to build effective relationships with partners and stakeholders.

2\. Organisation and problem-solving: Ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently and adapt to changing circumstances.

3\. Leadership and teamwork: Ability to coordinate teams, facilitate collaboration and support capacity building.

**LANGUAGES**

1\. Proficiency in English is mandatory

2\. Proficiency in Dari and/or Pashto or French will be an asset

## SI WILL OFFER YOU...

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 3080 gross per month (2800 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 600.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every two months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

Office and Guest House conditions: guest houses and offices are in two separate building within the same campound. Office are fully equiped, guest house are equipped with nice bedrooms having individual bathrooms. Common spaces are the kitchen, terrasses, one salon and one dining room. TV installed, and gym equipment in the basement of the guest house. each building is equiped with hibernation room.   
Internet and telephone network: internet connection OK, 4 G globally available without issue in Kabul.  
Restaurant & social life: few restaurant are validated and available for deliveries with a good diversity.   
Social life is possible in other NGO guest houses (or SI guest house as well) with a limited number of people gathering and UN couponds.   
4 Supermarkets / Malls are validated and located close to SI coumpound. Possibility to eat the food of the cook for lunch and dinner during the working days.   
Security level is 2 in Kabul, there is limited movement by foot allowed outside the coupound and movement by car described as above.   
Due to these conditions, the rotation cycle is one RnR each 2 months.   
Winter temperatures in Kabul are negative (untill minus 15 °c) and around 35 °c in summer. Maximum of 45 ° in Nimroz during summer.   
Living conditions in the field are often harsher (limited access to electricity, harsher weather conditions, isolation, etc.) and acces to the field is possible in the frame of the movement plans.

title: Research Analyst
body:
Laterite is looking for a new Research Analyst with an understanding of data analysis and a strong motivation to work in social and economic research to join our office in Dar es Salaam. This role combines research design, data analysis, project management support, and fieldwork coordination in a collaborative and fast-paced environment.

**This position is open exclusively to Tanzanian nationals.**

**WHO WE ARE**

Laterite is a data, research, and analytics firm working on complex development challenges. We partner with universities, global think tanks, international NGOs, multilateral donors, and government ministries. Our clients include the World Bank, TechnoServe, the Mastercard Foundation, and others.

We operate across the Netherlands, Rwanda, Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Sierra Leone, and Peru, with 90+ full-time staff and more than 2,000 enumerators. We believe meaningful impact requires being on the ground, building local teams, and establishing long-term trust. Our office culture is collaborative and gives people autonomy to grow into their roles.

**THE ENVIRONMENT YOU’RE STEPPING INTO**

You will join our Tanzania team in a high-trust environment. We are low on bureaucracy but high on individual accountability. You won’t be micromanaged here—we want you to use your judgment to solve problems, support our fast-paced field teams, and actively improve the systems you work with.

Laterite was founded in 2010 in Kigali, and our office in Dar es Salaam opened in 2021. Our project portfolio in Tanzania is varied and ranges from data collection (including mixed-methods studies) to full-cycle research projects. The Tanzania team works across all our key sectors with the majority of projects in education, public health and agriculture topics. Our team in Tanzania currently consists of 5 team members.

While based in our Dar es Salaam office, you will support Laterite’s Uganda team, contributing to projects in both countries. The Uganda portfolio is just as varied, combining data collection with full-cycle research studies, and spans the agriculture, public health, education and energy sectors. You will collaborate with the Uganda team remotely.

**HOW YOU’LL MAKE AN IMPACT**

**1 Supporting research projects**

- Support the ethical approval process, research design, and development of research instruments.
- Conduct quantitative and qualitative data analysis.
- Draft sections of reports and presentations for clients.
- Support communication with clients and internal project teams on project progress.

**2 Contributing to data collection**

- Code survey instruments using SurveyCTO and other ODK-based platforms.
- Collaborate with field teams to develop training materials and support enumerator trainings.
- Participate in field visits to understand and improve data collection processes.

**3 Strengthening data quality and analysis**

- Monitor, clean, and validate incoming survey data.
- Work closely with field teams to resolve data quality issues.
- Support statistical analysis and interpretation of findings.
- Contribute to consultancy-quality reports and data-driven insights.

**4 Contributing to business development (Optional)**

If you are interested, there is also room to contribute to our business development efforts, either through proactive business development or by contributing to the development of technical and financial proposals.

**WHAT YOU BRING**

We are looking for a colleague with strong quantitative data analysis skills and a motivation to work on socio-economic development research. Specifically, you have:

- A completed Master’s degree in Economics, Public Health, Development or related fields.
- At least one year of professional experience in similar roles or tasks. (We welcome experience gained through internships, dissertation work, or participation in an academic research group, provided you can demonstrate how this experience meets the requirements of the role.)
- Strong quantitative data analysis skills and proficiency in Stata.
- Excellent written and oral communication skills in English and Kiswahili.

*In addition, we welcome:*

- Experience working with ODK-based platforms (e.g., SurveyCTO).
    - Previous work experience in Tanzania.
    - Organizational and interpersonal skills, self-motivation and drive to work in a collaborative environment.

**WHAT YOU’LL LEARN AND DEVELOP**

- Technical research design, including sampling and impact evaluation methodologies.
- Project management and client communication.
- Advanced data analysis, statistical techniques, and coding skills.
- Report writing and presentation of findings in a consultancy-quality format.

**WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU**

- **Competitive compensation. TZS 7,311,684 - TZS 9,704,383** gross monthly salary (exact grade determined by experience/interviews), medical insurance, pension contribution, and 21 days of annual leave.
- **Professional growth.** We are also committed to supporting our staff’s learning, providing an annual learning budget of up to USD 1,000 per person and 10 days of time off for professional learning each year.
- **Flexibility.** We also provide remote work options in accordance with Laterite’s remote work policy.

title: Project Manager – HLGSC Procurement TWG (Global Humanitarian Procurement Collaboration and Performance Initiative)
body:
**Title:** Project Manager: HLGSC Procurement TWG (Global Humanitarian Procurement Collaboration and Performance Initiative)

**Date:** As soon as possible

**Concerned Project(s):** Global Procurement Forum

**ToR Reference Number:** HULO-HQ-PROC-2026-001

This Call for Interest is open to all eligible consultants, in accordance with hulo’s procedures and principles.

**Context of the consultancy:**

The Humanitarian Logistics Cooperative, also known as “hulo”, is the first humanitarian European Cooperative Society (SCE) created in June 2021. Hulo now regroups 19 organisations: ACTED, Action contre la Faim (ACF), Bioport, Care International, Fleet Forum, the French Red Cross (FRC), Handicap International / Humanity & Inclusion (HI), International Federation of the Red Cross and Red Crescent (IFRC), Intersos, International Rescue Committee (IRC), Médecins du Monde (MDM), Mercy Corps, Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC), Oxfam Intermón, Plan International, Première Urgence International (PUI), Save the Children International, Solidarités International (SI), and Welthungerhilfe (WHH).

Its objective is to increase the impact of humanitarian aid by strengthening links and solidarity between humanitarian logistics actors and improving performance through the pooling of logistics and supply chain resources and expertise.

hulo is co-lead, alongside WFP and NRC, of the Global Humanitarian Procurement Collaboration and Performance Initiative, a 12-month action (1 September 2026 – 31 August 2027) funded by DG ECHO that operationalises the reform priorities identified by the Humanitarian Leadership Group on Supply Chain (HLGSC) and its Procurement Thematic Working Group (TWG). The action establishes a Global Procurement Forum, develops and tests targeted procurement cooperation guidance, strengthens procurement integration into organisational and project-level decision-making, and develops and pilots a board-level procurement KPI framework, engaging around 30 organisations and 60 practitioners across the humanitarian procurement ecosystem.

**Overall scope of work expected from the Consultant:**

The Project Manager leads day-to-day implementation of the Global Humanitarian Procurement Collaboration and Performance Initiative, under hulo’s administrive contract, reporting to and managed by the Co-Leads Steering Committee, coordinating delivery of the action's four results – the Global Procurement Forum, targeted procurement cooperation guidance, procurement integration tools, and the board-level procurement KPI framework – across WFP, hulo, NRC, the Procurement TWG and around 30 participating organisations.

The Consultant is expected to:

**1. Establish overall project coordination and management**

- Maintain the consolidated implementation calendar, deliverable register, risk register and budget tracker across the four results.
- Coordinate and report to the WFP-hulo-NRC Steering Committee and monthly management reviews, and support timely escalation of material changes to WFP for donor communication.
- Ensure proper consultation, and inclusion of the participating organisation

**Expected Deliverable:** Operational calendar, deliverable and risk registers, and a functioning Steering Committee coordination framework.

**2. Drive delivery of the Global Procurement Forum**

- Coordinate consolidation of the procurement coordination landscape and gap analysis, and development of the Forum's governance and operating package (mandate, membership, decision-making, accountability, links to existing structures).
- Coordinate targeted consultation and validation through the Procurement TWG, and preparation of the package for the relevant HLGSC leadership process and its subsequent operationalisation.

**Expected Deliverable:** Validated Forum governance and operating package, and a leadership-ready briefing.

**3. Coordinate procurement cooperation guidance, integration tools and the KPI framework**

- Manage and coordinate the Procurement Expert(s), Data Specialist, Academic Expert and other contributors in consolidating evidence, developing guidance, tools and KPIs, and steering technical review through the Procurement TWG.
- Coordinate the selection and onboarding of pilot organisations to conduct activities, and consolidate pilot learning into refined, final outputs.

**Expected Deliverable:** Validated procurement cooperation guidance, procurement-integration tool package, and board-level KPI package, each supported by documented pilot and testing evidence.

**4. Manage stakeholder engagement, cross-TWG and donor coordination**

- Act as the senior coordination focal point with the Procurement TWG, other HLGSC working groups (Digitalization, Environmental Sustainability, Preparedness/Localization) and the HLGSC Donor Group.
- Coordinate community-management, communication and visibility activities in line with ECHO requirements, including institutional announcements, knowledge products and social-media content.

**Expected Deliverable:** Documented cross-TWG touchpoints and Donor Group engagement records, and a completed visibility and communication plan.

**5. Consolidate monitoring, reporting and the implementation roadmap**

- Consolidate technical inputs for WFP's quarterly consolidated results and budget reviews and for DG ECHO reporting requirements.
- Lead development of the final implementation roadmap, consolidating outputs, pilot learning, unresolved technical matters and future priorities, including inputs to the wider Supply Chain Charter process.

**Expected Deliverable:** Consolidated monitoring inputs and a final implementation roadmap.

**Qualifications and Experience:**

Interested Consultants should possess the following qualifications and experience:

- Master’s degree in project management, supply chain/logistics, international development, business administration or a related field.
- Significant experience (7+ years) in project or programme management, ideally leading multi-stakeholder or donor-funded (ECHO/UN) actions.
- Strong knowledge of humanitarian supply chain and/or procurement systems, networks and coordination structures.
- Proven experience coordinating consortia or co-led actions involving UN agencies, international NGOs and technical working groups.
- Excellent stakeholder management, facilitation, representation and consensus-building skills.
- Strong budgeting, risk-management and results-monitoring skills; experience with donor reporting (ECHO Single Form) is a strong asset.
- Organised, autonomous and able to manage delivery within a compressed 12-month timeline.
- Languages: English and French (essential).

**Management and Reporting Lines:**

The Project Manager works under the direct line management of hulo’s designated supervisor and is functionally accountable to the WFP-hulo-NRC Steering Committee for delivery of the action.

The Project Manager works under the direct line management and contractual authority of hulo’s designated supervisor, collaborates day to day with the WFP and other dedicated technical focal points on this project, and functionally accountability to the WFP–hulo–NRC Steering Committee for operational delivery.

The Project Manager is in charge of managing and structuring the work of the Procurement Expert(s), Data Specialist, Community Manager and Academic Expert, and of coordinating with the Procurement Thematic Working Group.

**Schedule:**

This consultancy targets 100% time engagement over the 12-month action period (1 September 2026 – 31 August 2027).

**Application & Contracting Process:**

The selected consultant will be contracted by hulo for the duration indicated above, on a full-time (100%) basis for the length of the action. He/She is expected to outline the main key steps of the process as part of the Expression of Interest (EOI). While the role is based full-time on the action, tasks can be carried out remotely where appropriate, with in-person participation expected for key hulo, TWG or Forum events.

Hulo invites applications for the provision of services described above. Interested candidates must submit their EOI outlining their financial offer (daily rate with clarifications on other cost covering expectations, plus a proposed overall cost), proposal to meet the ToR, scheduling and CV providing information on capacity and experience, showing qualification for the technical skills required by the scope of work.

**Selection Criteria:**

Applications will be evaluated based on the following criteria:

1. Relevant experience and qualifications.
2. Quality and relevance of the technical proposal.
3. Financial offer.
4. Understanding of humanitarian and collaborative environments.

title: Community Manager (NGO) – HLGSC Procurement TWG / Global Procurement Forum
body:
**Title:** Community Manager (NGO) – HLGSC Procurement TWG (Global Humanitarian Procurement Collaboration and Performance Initiative) / Procurement Technical Working Group / Global Procurement Forum

**Date:** As soon as possible

**Concerned Project(s):** Global Humanitarian Procurement Collaboration and Performance Initiative

**ToR Reference Number:** HULO-HQ-PROC-2026-002

This Call for Interest is open to all eligible consultants, in accordance with hulo’s procedures and principles.

**Context of the consultancy:**

The Humanitarian Logistics Cooperative, also known as “hulo”, is the first humanitarian European Cooperative Society (SCE) created in June 2021. Hulo now regroups 19 organisations: ACTED, Action contre la Faim (ACF), Bioport, Care International, Fleet Forum, the French Red Cross (FRC), Handicap International / Humanity & Inclusion (HI), International Federation of the Red Cross and Red Crescent (IFRC), Intersos, International Rescue Committee (IRC), Médecins du Monde (MDM), Mercy Corps, Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC), Oxfam Intermón, Plan International, Première Urgence International (PUI), Save the Children International, Solidarités International (SI), and Welthungerhilfe (WHH).

Its objective is to increase the impact of humanitarian aid by strengthening links and solidarity between humanitarian logistics actors and improving performance through the pooling of logistics and supply chain resources and expertise.

hulo is co-lead, alongside WFP and NRC, of the Global Humanitarian Procurement Collaboration and Performance Initiative, a 12-month action (1 September 2026 – 31 August 2027) funded by DG ECHO that operationalises the reform priorities identified by the Humanitarian Leadership Group on Supply Chain (HLGSC) and its Procurement Thematic Working Group (TWG). The action establishes a Global Procurement Forum, develops and tests targeted procurement cooperation guidance, strengthens procurement integration into organisational and project-level decision-making, and develops and pilots a board-level procurement KPI framework, engaging around 30 organisations and 60 practitioners across the humanitarian procurement ecosystem.

**Overall scope of work expected from the Consultant:**

The Community Manager (NGO) and the WFP-hosted Community Manager (UN) are jointly responsible for representing their respective communities and for co-constructing the Global Procurement Forum, the future consolidating platform for humanitarian procurement coordination. The two Community Managers co-design the Forum’s methodology, jointly consult on and structure the transition of the Procurement Thematic Working Group (TWG) into the Forum, and build on existing initiatives and conclusions – including the Inter-Agency Procurement Group (IAPG) and the HLGSC’s own prior work – rather than duplicating what already exists. The Forum is the articulation point between the community and the action’s three other results (procurement cooperation guidance, procurement integration, and the KPI framework): the Community Managers maintain a collaborative system of consultation so that work under these results is shared with, and progressively validated by, the TWG/Forum.

The Consultant is expected to:

**1. Co-construct the Global Procurement Forum’s methodology and structure, jointly with the Community Manager (UN)**

- Jointly design the Forum’s methodology, structure and ways of working with the Community Manager (UN), building on existing networks and initiatives (e.g. IAPG) and on the HLGSC’s own prior conclusions, so that the Forum builds on what already exists rather than duplicating it.
- Contribute an NGO perspective to the consolidation of the procurement coordination landscape and gap analysis, co-validated with the Community Manager (UN).

**Expected Deliverable:** Jointly co-constructed Forum methodology and structure, and a shared coordination-landscape and gap analysis.

**2. Facilitate and manage the transition of the Procurement TWG into the Global Procurement Forum**

- Support consultation on, and structuring of, the TWG’s current ways of working, jointly with the Community Manager (UN), to inform the Forum’s future operating model.
- Jointly manage the practical transition from TWG to Forum, preserving continuity of membership, engagement and institutional knowledge.

**Expected Deliverable:** Documented TWG-to-Forum transition plan, co-developed with the Community Manager (UN).

**3. Coordinate the Forum as the articulation point between the community and the other teams working on the project**

- Establish and maintain, jointly with the Community Manager (UN), a system of consultation between the TWG/Forum and the teams delivering procurement cooperation guidance, procurement integration tools and the KPI framework, so this work is shared with and can be contributed to by the wider community.
- Support a collaborative approach whereby outputs from the three results are progressively shared and validated through TWG/Forum consultation, culminating in their consideration by the Forum.

**Expected Deliverable:** An operating system of consultation linking other teams to the TWG/Forum, jointly maintained with the Community Manager (UN).

**4. Support NGO participation in Forum governance design and validation**

- Support outreach, scheduling and facilitation of targeted consultations on Forum governance (mandate, membership, decision-making, accountability) with NGO members and networks, identifying NGO cooperation needs to feed into the Forum’s governance terms.
- Maintain participant records, comments, matrices and decision records for NGO-related consultations.

**Expected Deliverable:** Documented NGO consultation record and comments matrix, and NGO cooperation needs feeding into the Forum’s governance package.

**5. Support Forum operationalisation, value proposition and follow-up**

- Jointly with the Community Manager (UN), support establishment of the Forum’s consultation calendar, workplan and action-tracking mechanism.
- Support the definition of a clear, well-scoped Forum value proposition and set of outputs, recognising the limited time and resources of participating organisations.

**Expected Deliverable:** Operational Forum workplan and a clearly defined value proposition reflecting participants’ limited time and resources.

**6. Contribute to wider action communications and visibility**

- Support collection and coordination of NGO-related content for knowledge products, human-interest stories and social media aligned with the action’s visibility plan.
- Support maintenance of the participant and stakeholder register, ensuring accurate disaggregation by organisation type.

**Expected Deliverable:** NGO-related content contributions and updated stakeholder register entries.

**Qualifications and Experience:**

Interested Consultants should possess the following qualifications and experience:

- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in international relations, communications, humanitarian studies, or a related field.
- Experience in community management, stakeholder engagement or network coordination, ideally within humanitarian or NGO networks.
- Familiarity with humanitarian procurement or supply chain coordination structures is an asset.
- Strong organisational, facilitation, and written communication skills.
- Experience facilitating co-design or participatory methodology development with multiple stakeholders is an asset.
- Proficiency in MS Office and CRM (or equivalent) tools.
- Languages: English and French (essential).

**Management and Reporting Lines:**

The Community Manager (NGO) works under the direct line management of the Project Manager, HLGSC Procurement TWG.

The Community Manager (NGO) shares joint responsibility with the WFP-hosted Community Manager (UN) for representing their respective communities and for co-constructing the Global Procurement Forum; the two roles co-design methodology and jointly manage the TWG-to-Forum transition.

The Community Manager (NGO) also coordinates with the Facilitator and the Procurement Thematic Working Group, and liaises with the other teams working on the project so the Forum remains the articulation point between the community and the other objeectives of the project.

**Schedule:**

This consultancy targets 30% time engagement over the 12-month action period (1 September 2026 – 31 August 2027).

**Application & Contracting Process:**

The selected consultant will be contracted by hulo for the duration indicated above but is not expected to work full time throughout this period. He/She is expected to outline the main key steps of the process as part of the Expression of Interest (EOI). These tasks can be carried out remotely, with occasional in-person participation in hulo, TWG or Forum events where relevant.

Hulo invites applications for the provision of services described above. Interested candidates must submit their EOI outlining their financial offer (daily rate with clarifications on other cost covering expectations, plus a proposed overall cost), proposal to meet the ToR, scheduling and CV providing information on capacity and experience, showing qualification for the technical skills required by the scope of work.

**Selection Criteria:**

Applications will be evaluated based on the following criteria:

1. Relevant experience and qualifications.
2. Quality and relevance of the technical proposal.
3. Financial offer.
4. Understanding of humanitarian and collaborative environments.

This Call for Interest is open to all eligible consultants, in accordance with hulo’s procedures and principles.

**Context of the consultancy:**

The Humanitarian Logistics Cooperative, also known as “hulo”, is the first humanitarian European Cooperative Society (SCE) created in June 2021. Hulo now regroups 19 organisations: ACTED, Action contre la Faim (ACF), Bioport, Care International, Fleet Forum, the French Red Cross (FRC), Handicap International / Humanity & Inclusion (HI), International Federation of the Red Cross and Red Crescent (IFRC), Intersos, International Rescue Committee (IRC), Médecins du Monde (MDM), Mercy Corps, Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC), Oxfam Intermón, Plan International, Première Urgence International (PUI), Save the Children International, Solidarités International (SI), and Welthungerhilfe (WHH).

Its objective is to increase the impact of humanitarian aid by strengthening links and solidarity between humanitarian logistics actors and improving performance through the pooling of logistics and supply chain resources and expertise.

hulo is co-lead, alongside WFP and NRC, of the Global Humanitarian Procurement Collaboration and Performance Initiative, a 12-month action (1 September 2026 – 31 August 2027) funded by DG ECHO that operationalises the reform priorities identified by the Humanitarian Leadership Group on Supply Chain (HLGSC) and its Procurement Thematic Working Group (TWG). The action establishes a Global Procurement Forum, develops and tests targeted procurement cooperation guidance, strengthens procurement integration into organisational and project-level decision-making, and develops and pilots a board-level procurement KPI framework, engaging around 30 organisations and 60 practitioners across the humanitarian procurement ecosystem.

**Overall scope of work expected from the Consultant:**

The Academic Expert provides research and academic input to develop and pilot a concise, board-level procurement KPI framework for humanitarian organisations. Academic input is expected to be most structured under this workstream, particularly for the literature review and evidence synthesis, while procurement and data experts lead organisational data gathering and technical design.

In addition, the Academic Expert holds a cross-cutting role, remaining available to contribute expertise to other results as the action progresses, and providing consultation and sharing relevant academic input across workstreams depending on the topic at hand.

The Consultant is expected to:

**1. Consolidate existing KPI practice and relevant evidence**

- Conduct a literature review and evidence synthesis on strategic, board-level procurement performance measurement in the humanitarian sector and relevant comparable sectors.
- Identify indicators already used for leadership oversight, areas of emerging convergence, and the strengths and limitations of different measurement approaches.

**Expected Deliverable:** Literature review and evidence synthesis identifying candidate KPI domains and implementation considerations.

**2. Support development of the candidate KPI package**

- Provide academic and research input to the strategic relevance, clarity and comparability of candidate board-level KPIs developed jointly with procurement and data experts.
- Contribute to documenting known limitations, data-feasibility considerations and evidence gaps for each candidate indicator.

**Expected Deliverable:** Academic input to the draft candidate KPI package and data-feasibility assessment.

**3. Support technical validation and the leadership package**

- Support the Procurement TWG’s technical validation of the candidate KPI package with evidence-based input.
- Contribute academic framing and evidence references to the concise, leadership-ready KPI briefing.

**Expected Deliverable:** Evidence-based contribution to the technically validated KPI package and leadership briefing.

**4. Support pilot learning and refinement of the KPI package**

- Provide research input to the analysis of findings from the five core pilots and the wider validation and adoption group, covering data availability, definition consistency and comparability.
- Contribute to the final, refined KPI package and its supporting evidence base and implementation roadmap.

**Expected Deliverable:** Research-informed contribution to the refined, pilot-tested KPI package.

**Qualifications and Experience:**

Interested Consultants should possess the following qualifications and experience:

- PhD or advanced Master’s degree in supply chain management, logistics, public policy, economics or a related field, with a research or academic background.
- Demonstrated experience conducting literature reviews and evidence synthesis on procurement or supply chain performance.
- Familiarity with humanitarian procurement systems, KPI frameworks or performance measurement is a strong asset.
- Excellent analytical and academic writing skills.
- Languages: English required; French an asset.

**Management and Reporting Lines:**

The Academic Expert works in close collaboration with the Procurement Expert(s), the Data Specialist, Data Analyst(s) engaged, and the Procurement Thematic Working Group.

title: Fundraising Manager
source: Association for the Prevention of Torture
body:
## **Description**

Location: Geneva, Switzerland

Term: 100% (40 hours/week), open-ended contract

Projected start date: 16.11.2026 or earliest available

Application deadline: 7.10.26

The Association for the Prevention of Torture (APT) is seeking to recruit a Fundraising Manager to lead and strengthen the organisation's fundraising efforts and support the implementation of the APT's Strategic Plan.

**WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?**

We are looking for a dynamic and strategic fundraising professional with a proven ability to build strong donor relationships, secure institutional and individual funding and identify new fundraising opportunities. Combining excellent communication, representation and writing skills with strong organisational abilities and a collaborative approach, the successful candidate will lead APT's fundraising efforts while ensuring high-quality donor stewardship, grant management and reporting. If you are passionate about human rights, enjoy building and nurturing partnerships and are committed to supporting meaningful and sustainable impact, we encourage you to apply.

**ABOUT THE APT**

(to learn more: )

The Association for the Prevention of Torture (APT) is a Swiss international non-governmental human rights organisation established in 1977. APT works for societies without torture and ill-treatment, advocating at the international, regional and national levels with an approach based on cooperation, dialogue and partnerships. Our multicultural team of 16 staff comprises members working in Geneva and in different locations around the world.

Our vision: Societies without torture or ill-treatment. We implement this vision by:

• Influencing national, regional and international legal frameworks, standards, policies and practices to reduce the risks of torture and ill-treatment

• Supporting partners' efforts to advance torture prevention, contributing our respective expertise and resources to maximise impact

• Bringing people together in constructive dialogue to build support for torture prevention and identify practical solutions

**MAIN ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Fundraising Manager will lead the development and implementation of APT's fundraising strategy and steward relationships with existing and prospective donors.

This is a hands-on fundraising role in a small association. In close collaboration with other members of the APT team, the Fundraising Manager will take responsibility for the full fundraising cycle, from identifying opportunities and developing approaches to drafting applications and reports, coordinating internal inputs, maintaining donor information and ensuring administrative follow-up. The role therefore requires both strategic judgement and a willingness to take ownership of the detailed, practical aspects of fundraising.

Reporting to the Secretary General, they will work closely with APT Senior Advisers, the Head of Operations, the Finance Manager and the Communications Manager to secure resources that enable the association to deliver its mission and strategic objectives.

The Fundraising Manager will oversee a portfolio of institutional donors and foundations that currently support an annual organisational budget of approximately CHF 2,5 million.

Fundraising strategy and donor engagement

• Develop, implement and regularly review APT's fundraising strategy

• Maintain and strengthen relationships with existing institutional donors and other funding partners, supporting APT management with high-quality stewardship of donor relations

• Identify and pursue new funding opportunities, contributing to the diversification of APT's funding base

• Develop strategic engagement plans and tailored communications for existing and prospective donors

• Provide regular analysis and updates on APT's funding situation to support decision-making by senior management and governance bodies (Bureau, Board, General Assembly).

Grant management and donor accountability

• Lead the preparation and submission of donor applications, in close cooperation with all relevant colleagues

• Coordinate donor reporting processes and ensure timely, accurate and high-quality reporting

• Work closely with operations and finance colleagues to ensure compliance with donor contracts and other requirements

• Develop and maintain a donor and grant database, including donor requirements

• Keep track of fundraising and grant deadlines, requirements and follow-up actions, ensuring that these are completed in a timely manner

Organisational support and representation

• Contribute to the development of communication materials that support fundraising efforts

• Support the implementation of APT's monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning processes to strengthen evidence-based reporting to donors in accordance with APT’s measurement framework

• Develop and maintain a network of fundraising and philanthropy professionals

• Represent the APT in relevant meetings, conferences and events

• Supervise interns and external consultants supporting fundraising activities, as applicable

## **Requirements**

Education

• University degree or equivalent higher education qualification in fundraising, marketing, philanthropy, or related field e.g. international relations, project management, etc.

Experience

• A minimum of eight years of relevant professional experience in fundraising, donor relations, grant management or organisational development within the non-profit, international development or human rights sectors

• Demonstrated experience securing and managing funding from a variety of donors (public and private institutional donors, as well as individuals)

• Experience coordinating complex funding proposals and donor reports

• Experience working in an international and multicultural environment

Also an asset:

• A network within the donors and philanthropic communities in Switzerland

• Experience working autonomously in a small NGO, where responsibilities span both strategic and hands-on fundraising

Knowledge and skills

• Strong commitment to human rights values, as well as to dialogue and partnerships

• Proactive approach with a strong sense of autonomy and accountability

• Excellent writing, communication and relationship-building skills

• Strong strategic thinking, planning and organisational skills

• Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines

• Ability to work collaboratively across teams and functions

• Excellent analytical skills and confidence working with budgets and financial information

• Strong attention to detail

• Full professional proficiency (written and spoken) in English and French. Additional languages are an asset

• Availability to travel occasionally (mainly within Switzerland)

## **Benefits**

Salary: monthly CHF 7’500 to 8’000.- gross at 100% commensurate with qualifications and experience.

Benefits: Standard pension plan; 25 days of holidays per annum (at 100%) plus national holidays and additional days at the end of the year; compensation days related to mission travel; learning and development opportunities; option to work from home up to 2 days per week; free car parking space. We pay attention to private life – including family and work balance – and we emphasise well-being.

Working environment: Exceptional working environment in APT's eco-friendly building, in a green location near public transportation and the United Nations HQ building.

title: Head of Partnerships
body:
## **About ATNi**

ATNi (Access to Nutrition Initiative) is a global nonprofit actively challenging the food industry, investors and policymakers to shape healthier food systems. We analyse and translate data into actionable insights, driving partnerships, finance and innovations for market transformation so that all people have access to nutritious and sustainable food. ATNi is registered in the Netherlands and two dozen staff as well as over a dozen advisors and consultants. For more information on ATNi, please visit our website. [https://accesstonutrition.org/](https://accesstonutrition.org/)

## **About the role**

Partnerships are a critical component of ATNi's Strategy and Theory of Change (2023-2027) and a key lever for achieving systemic impact. This role ensures that ATNi effectively engages partners across the continuum of change, building strategic relationships that amplify the organisation's influence, impact and reach.

Working closely with the Executive Director, the Head of Partnerships will lead ATNi's Partnership Strategy, ensuring that ATNi collaborates with like-minded and complementary organisations that serve as change agents and strategic allies to accelerate action for improved access to nutrition. Geographically, ATNi works with global partners as well as regional and national partners in Europe, East Africa, West Africa, South and Southeast Asia.

ATNI’s Partnerships broadly fall into five categories: Research; Policy; Food Business and Innovation; Investments; and Funding. The postholder will oversee the first three. S/he will support Investment Partnerships working with the ATNi’s Capital4Nutrition Team, and will support Funding Partnerships which is led by ATNi’s Head of Business Development.

The Head of Partnerships reports to the Executive Director and is a member of ATNi's Extended Management Team. The Head of Partnerships contributes to strategic discussions, represents ATNi externally, and drives collaboration across the organisation to advance ATNi's mission. S/he will represent ATNi externally, contributing to its reputation through thought leadership, partnership development and strategic engagement.

## **Responsibilities**

**Partnership Strategy & Management**

· Develop and implement ATNi's Partnership Strategy in alignment with its mission, Theory of Change and strategic priorities.  
· Identify and pursue strategic partnership opportunities that advance ATNi's impact and influence.  
· Build and nurture relationships with government agencies, international organisations, private sector actors, investors, civil society organisations and other key stakeholders.  
· Monitor the effectiveness of partnerships and identify opportunities to increase collaboration and impact.  
· Represent ATNi in high-level meetings, conferences, webinars and industry events, advocating for strategic partnerships and collaboration opportunities.  
· Provide regular updates and strategic recommendations to the Management Team regarding partnership opportunities and risks.  
· As a member of the Extended Management Team, help develop ATNi’s next strategy (from 2028 onwards).

**Team Management**

· Lead and supervise the Partnerships team, fostering professional growth and collaboration within ATNi while ensuring alignment with the organisation's broader mission.  
· Plan and allocate resources effectively, including team capacity, project time allocation and support for business development activities.  
· Foster a collaborative and inclusive team culture.  
· Provide professional development opportunities for team members.  
· Strengthen partnership capabilities and practices across the organisation.

**Cross-functional Collaboration & Integration**

· Liaise with Project Leads to ensure partnership strategies align with ATNi's broader impact goals.  
· Work closely with other Heads and Directors (Research, Policy & Communications, MEL & Data and Business Development) to ensure partnership insights and opportunities are embedded across workstreams.  
· Support organisational planning processes by ensuring partnerships contribute meaningfully to ATNi's strategic objectives.  
· Facilitate knowledge sharing and collaboration across teams to maximise partnership value and impact.  
· Provide oversight of project budgets and delivery.

**Resource Mobilisation**

· Identify and pursue funding opportunities in collaboration with colleagues across the organisation.  
· Develop proposals and grant applications together with the fundraising team.  
· Support donor engagement, reporting and compliance requirements.  
· Cultivate relationships with existing and prospective funders and strategic partners.

## **Education & Experience**

· Master's degree in International Development, Public Policy, Political Science, Business Administration, International Relations, Public Health, Nutrition or a related field.  
· At least 12 years of relevant professional experience in partnership development, stakeholder engagement, business development, resource mobilisation or programme management.  
· Demonstrated experience building and managing complex partnerships across sectors and geographies.  
· Experience working within international development, public health, nutrition, food systems or a related field.  
· Proven experience in fundraising, donor engagement and grant development is an advantage.  
· Experience leading and managing teams in an international environment.  
· Experience working in multicultural and international contexts, including field experience and/or extensive travel across Africa and Asia.  
· Highly desirable: experience in establishing, building and managing fundable partnerships in initiatives in East Africa or Europe; strong project management and budget experience.

## **Key Skills & Competencies**

· **Strategic Relationship Building**: Develops and maintains high-value partnerships that advance ATNi's mission and objectives.  
· **Negotiation & Influence**: Builds consensus, manages stakeholder relationships and secures strategic commitments.  
· **Strategic Thinking & Problem Solving**: Navigates complex stakeholder environments and identifies opportunities for impact.  
· **Public Engagement & Representation**: Represents ATNi effectively in external forums and high-level discussions.  
· **Flexibility & Adaptability**: Demonstrates resilience and effectiveness in diverse cultural, organisational and stakeholder contexts, adapting communication and engagement approaches to changing circumstances and emerging opportunities.  
· **Cross-functional Leadership**: Collaborates effectively across workstreams and projects to align partnerships with organisational strategy.  
· **People Leadership**: Leads, mentors and develops high-performing teams.  
· **Commitment to Mission**: Strong commitment to advancing healthier and more sustainable food systems.

## **Offer**

We offer a meaningful leadership role within an agile, mission-driven international organisation working to transform global food systems and improve access to nutrition worldwide.

This post is only open to individuals based in the Netherlands, Belgium, Kenya (Nairobi) or Tanzania (Dar es Salaam). (Hiring outside of the Netherlands will be undertaken by an employer of record or host organization.) Relocation support is not available. If already based in the Netherlands, HSM visa sponsorship may be possible.

· A full-time position (32-40 hours per week)  
· For Netherlands-based: Gross monthly salary of €5,000-€6,600 (full time). A cost of labor and cost of living adjustment will be made for successful applicants from outside of the Netherlands.  
· 26 days of annual leave (Netherlands; full-time basis), plus public holidays  
· Pension contribution and monthly health insurance allowance  
· Annual learning and development budget to support your professional growth  
· An initial one-year contract, with the intention to extend based on performance  
· Flexible and partly remote working arrangements that support work-life balance  
· A hybrid working model (50% office-based in Utrecht), with flexibility to support work–life balance

## **Diversity & Inclusion**

ATNi is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values and respects the importance of a diverse and inclusive workforce. It is the organisation's policy to recruit, hire, train and promote persons in all job titles without regard to race, colour, religion, gender, age, national origin, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation or gender identity. We recognise that diversity and inclusion are driving forces in the success of our organisation.
