**Terms of Reference (ToR)**

**Research Consultant: Gender- Environment Research, Transforming Masculinities Adaptation, and M&E System**

**I. Post Title:** Research Consultant for Gender-Environment Research, Transforming Masculinities Adaptation, and M&E System

**II. Contract Duration:** The total number of working days is 69

**Background**

Tearfund DRC plans to implement an initiative focused on the intersection of environment and gender-based violence in Aru territory, Ituri Province in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Environmental degradation, climate change, and resource scarcity in DRC significantly exacerbate risks of gender-based violence (GBV) and entrench harmful social norms. Tearfund DRC integrates gender transformation into environmental and humanitarian action as a standard practice. Building on previous TM adaptations (such as the Passages project), Tearfund seeks to go deeper by implementing gender-transformative approaches that directly address how environmental stressors fuel SGBV and marginalization. Tearfund DRC aims to collaborate with key research and institutional partners to adapt the Transforming Masculinities (TM) approach to promote environmental protection, sustainable natural resource management, and the reduction of GBV. This project aims to assess the feasibility and effectiveness of Transforming Masculinities in addressing environmental challenges and reducing GBV in vulnerable communities.

The “Transforming Masculinities” approach was developed and piloted in 2013 to work towards gender justice through a gender transformative model, founded on the principles and sacred texts of the world faiths that value the wellbeing and equality of all human beings. Transforming Masculinities (TM) is an evidence-based approach to transforming harmful concepts of gender and masculinities, and to promoting gender equality. Developed by Tearfund, TM has been adapted, scaled and implemented in multiple settings worldwide in efforts to reduce gender-based violence. In adapting and advancing the evidence on approaches that work across sectors and outcomes to reduce SGBV.

A core priority under Tearfund DRC’s environmental and protection pillar is mitigating GBV risks associated with natural resource access and climate change, while advancing equitable decision-making and gender equality. Emerging evidence highlights the reinforcing link between environmental degradation and entrenched social norms in heightening SGBV risks for women and girls in the DRC.

**VI. Objectives of the Research/Assessment (Scope of the work)**

❏ Conduct mixed-methods research (qualitative and quantitative landscape study on social norms at the intersection of gender, GBV and the environment), including the development of all research instruments (questionnaires, ethical protocols, etc.), data analysis, and reporting.

**VII. Objectives of the Adaptation, Monitoring and Evaluation and Learning**

❏ Adapt and contextualize the Transforming Masculinities model to address harmful norms and promote positive behaviors regarding environmental protection and GBV prevention in the DRC.

❏ Develop a robust Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) framework, including valid measures and instruments to assess shifts in social norms.

❏ Strengthen the evidence base and organizational learning concerning the intersection of environmental protection and GBV mitigation.

❏ Lead the drafting of technical papers, assessment reports, and evidence briefs based on research findings to inform advocacy and programming.

❏ Curate and synthesize relevant technical resources and literature, providing critical interpretation to enhance project implementation and contextual relevance.

The phases of testing and piloting are not considered for this Consultancy and might come after this (FY) period; the consultant may be contacted in the future to assist with the finalization of the materials.

**VIII. Competencies:**

● Research & Partnership Experience: Demonstrable experience in conducting high-quality research and successfully collaborating with local and international stakeholders within a consortium setting.

● M&E Framework Development: Proven expertise in designing, implementing, and managing monitoring and evaluation frameworks, tools, and methodologies.

● Data Analysis & Evaluation: Strong technical proficiency in quantitative and qualitative statistical data evaluation, interpretation, and reporting.

● Communication & Reporting: Excellent oral and written communication skills in English and French, with a demonstrated ability to synthesize complex data into actionable insights.

● Thematic Expertise: Substantial project experience across gender equality, environmental protection, climate adaptation, and sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV) prevention, preferably in the DRC or similar contexts.

**IX. Key Stakeholders and Participants**: This consultancy aims to engage a diverse range of stakeholders, including:

● Independent researchers and consultants

● Programme staff and organizational partners engaged in the environment and GBV research agenda

● Representatives from local, provincial or national ministries (Environment, Gender, etc.)

● Specialists in research translation, communication, and evidence uptake

● Advocacy professionals focused on influencing policy through research findings

**X. Reporting and Collaboration**

The consultant will operate under the direct supervision of the Tearfund DRC Country Director based in Goma. The assignment will involve close collaboration with Tearfund DRC Programme Sector Leads.

Additionally, the consultant will maintain communication with the Global SGBV Specialist (based in Goma, DRC) and the Global Leadership Team on Sexual and Gender-Based Violence to ensure alignment with global standards and strategic objectives.

**XI. Submission Guidelines**

Interested candidates are invited to submit a CV and a comprehensive technical proposal structured under the following headings:

1\. Contact Information ( scan of passport or ID)

2\. Relevant Experience (including 2–3 research samples from previous work, contract of previous work)

3\. Proposed Methodology

4\. Work Plan (including a detailed timeline aligned with the 69-day level of effort)

5\. Financial Proposal (including daily rate and itemized costs)

6\. References (two professional references with contact details and portfolio links to previous work, if available)

**XII. Financial Guidelines and Selection Criteria**

Applicants must submit a fully inclusive proposed daily rate. Financial proposals will be evaluated based on value for money. Eligible operational costs—including international travel, local transportation, and accommodation directly related to the execution of this assignment—will be covered by Tearfund, subject to prior approval.

**XIII. Evaluation Criteria & Weighting**

**1. Technical Proposal (70% / 70 points)**

- **Consultant's Experience and Qualifications (25 pts):** Proven experience in research, gender, GBV, environment, and mastery of transformative approaches (TM).
- **Proposed Methodology and Approach (30 pts):** Relevance of the mixed-methods research methodology, TM model adaptation, and Monitoring & Evaluation framework.
- **Work Plan and Timeline (15 pts):** Feasibility of the schedule relative to the 69-day level of effort and adherence to key deadlines (Nov 2026 – Mar 2027).

**2. Financial Proposal (30% / 30 points)**

- **Value for Money and Daily Rate (30 pts):** Competitiveness of the daily rate and transparency of the cost structure.

**XIV. Tender Schedule and Submission Details**

- **Call for Tenders Issued:** September 15th, 2026
- **Application Deadline:** Oct 07th, 2026, via email to **drc-procurement@tearfund.org**
- **Commencement of Assignment:** On or before November 1, 2026

**Proposal Formatting:** Maximum 5 pages for the tender document (excluding CVs, personal bibliography, and research samples)

**Note: Tearfund does not request or collect fees of any kind at any stage of the selection process (submission and processing of bids). Access to the Coupa platform is free of charge.**

**We urge you to remain vigilant and to categorically refuse any request for money regarding your submission from anyone claiming to be a "Tearfund agent." The only authorized personnel will contact you via the following email address: drc-procurement@tearfund.org**

title: Spécialiste Accès Humanitaire et Sécurité H/F/X - Lyon
body:
**Lieu : Lyon**  
**Date souhaitée de démarrage : mi-janvier 2027**  
**Durée : 3 mois dans le cadre d'un remplacement temporaire**

Handicap International / Humanité & Inclusion (HI) est une association de solidarité internationale indépendante et impartiale, qui intervient dans les situations de pauvreté et d’exclusion, de conflits et de catastrophes. Œuvrant aux côtés des personnes handicapées et vulnérabilisées, elle agit et témoigne pour répondre à leurs besoins essentiels et améliorer leurs conditions de vie. Elle s’engage à promouvoir le respect de leur dignité et de leurs droits fondamentaux. Depuis sa création en 1982, HI a mis en place des programmes de développement dans plus de 55 pays et intervient dans de nombreuses situations d’urgence. Aujourd'hui, nous avons un budget d'environ 200 millions d'euros, avec 4000 employés dans le monde.

Chez Handicap International, nous croyons fermement en l'importance de l'inclusion et de la diversité au sein de notre structure. C'est pourquoi nous sommes engagés dans une politique handicap afin de favoriser l'accueil et l'intégration de personnes en situation de handicap.

Merci d’indiquer si vous avez besoin d’un aménagement particulier, y compris pour participer aux 1ers entretiens.

Retrouvez plus d’informations sur l’association : [www.hi.org](http://www.hi.org/).

**OBJECTIFS DU POSTE :**

Sous la responsabilité du Manager Accès Humanitaire et Sécurité (AHS), le/la Spécialiste AHS contribue à développer l'accès humanitaire et la capacité d’intervention de l'organisation.

Il/Elle agit en tant que référent technique et soutient la ligne managériale (siège, région et pays) et les équipes AHS sur le terrain dans la mise en oeuvre des cadres AHS, la sécurité opérationnelle, la gestion des incidents/crises et la définition de stratégies d’accès.

Plus largement, il/elle participe à renforcer la culture de l'AHS au sein de l'organisation.

Dans ce cadre, vos principales fonctions seront :

STANDARDS ET EXPERTISES :

- Contribue à la définition, au déploiement et à la mise en application des normes et des standards relevant de l'AHS
- Veille à l'adaptation aux contextes et à la mise en place des outils de contrôle qualité (Standards Minimum de Sécurité, revue de sécurité, tableaux de bord…).

MISE EN ŒUVRE OPERATIONNELLE :

- Suivi de contexte et prospective : suit l'évolution des contextes, des tendances et des risques de son périmètre.
- Stratégie d'accès humanitaire : contribue à l’élaboration de la stratégie d’accès des programmes, à leur mise en œuvre et à leur suivi.
- Soutient les Directeurs dans le développement des stratégies opérationnelles (volet AHS) en conformité avec les cadres définis par l'organisation.
- Gestion de la sécurité opérationnelle :
    - Soutient la ligne managériale et les équipes AHS dans la gestion de la sécurité opérationnelle (analyses, dimensionnement, résolutions de problèmes, appui/ conseils…)
    - Assure un rôle d'alerte auprès de la ligne managériale et plus globalement de "check and balance" dans la gestion de la sécurité dans son périmètre.
- Gestion des incidents et des crises :
    - Veille à l'application du protocole de gestion de crise dans son périmètre.
    - Soutient les programmes dans la mise en place et la formation des membres des Equipes de Gestion des Incidents (EGI/IMT).
    - Participe à la gestion des crises sur son périmètre en tant que membre de l'Equipe de Gestion des Crises (EGC/CMT): analyse, appui technique, recommandations, mise en œuvre, reporting, exercice de leçons apprises…

DEVELOPPEMENT ET GESTION DES COMPETENCES

- Contribue à l'amélioration du savoir-faire technique AHS par le développement des exercices de leçons apprises et des expériences acquises sur son périmètre.
- Participe au recrutement, à la définition des objectifs, à la formation, au suivi et aux bilans annuels des Manager AHS pays de son périmètre.

PREPARATION ET REPONSES AUX URGENCES

- Contribue aux actions de préparation aux urgences et, lors d'une urgence, réorganise ses priorités en fonction de l'impératif humanitaire, afin d'assurer une réponse rapide et efficace.

**PROFIL REQUIS :**

- Vous possédez au moins 3 ans d’expérience sur le terrain au sein d’ONG humanitaires à des postes de Manager sécurité/ accès humanitaire en contextes d’urgence, complexes et instables ;
- Vous êtes expérimenté(e)s en gestion d’incident/de crise, en accès humanitaire et le renforcement des compétences.
- Vous maitrisez des concepts, outils et processus liés à la gestion de la sécurité et de l’accès humanitaire.
- Vous avez des connaissances en pédagogie et techniques de formation / transfert de compétence ;
- Vous avez le sens des priorités, grande capacité d'organisation et d'autonomie ;
- Vous maitrisez parfaitement le français et de l’anglais (lu, écrit et parlé).

**ACCESSIBILITE DU LIEU DE TRAVAIL :**

Les locaux sont facilement accessibles en transports en commun (bus, métro). Un parc à vélos est également à disposition. Au sein du bâtiment, des rampes d'accès et ascenseurs garantissent une meilleure circulation. Tous les postes de travail sont situés en Open Space mais des box sont disponibles à chaque étage pour travailler dans le calme si nécessaire. L’espace de travail est très lumineux.

Une référente handicap est présente pour répondre aux éventuelles questions et vous accompagner dans vos démarches. En fonction de vos besoins, le poste peut être aménagé.

**CONDITIONS DU POSTE :**

CDD de 3 mois à partir de mi-janvier 2027

**Ce que vous trouverez chez nous :**

**Des valeurs fortes :** Humanité, Inclusion, Engagement et intégrité ! Et une proximité avec le terrain via des conférences régulières.

**Statut cadre, 34 CP et 13 JRTT annuel**

**Une organisation flexible :** carte tickets resto (prise en charge 60% par HI), charte de télétravail : 8 jours de présentiel par mois minimum

**Transport :** un forfait mobilité durable existe. Prise en charge 50% des abonnements transports.

**Bien-être et santé :** mutuelle et prévoyance, sensibilisations internes diverses, un pôle Qualité de Vie et Conditions de Travail actif

**CSE et avantages sociaux** : Œuvres sociales du CSE pour améliorer votre quotidien.

**Une vie associative** culturelle, sportive et sociale dynamique

title: Malawi Extension Lead
body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Malawi program, founded in 2016, provides more than 670,000 farmers with quality farm supplies and training. Our office in Malawi is located in Zomba, in the country’s south. One Acre Fund works in Malawi’s southern region, which has the highest concentration of smallholder farmers in the country.

## **About the Role**

The Agronomy & Extension Lead will own the implementation of Malawi’s extension strategy, using HCD and SBC approaches to translate agronomic recommendations into simple, practical and adoptable support for farmers. The role will strengthen extension delivery, training and communication content, and use farmer feedback and impact data to continuously improve our approaches. They will work closely with Field Operations and Innovations to turn validated research into scalable farmer-facing solutions.

## **Responsibilities**

The role combines technical agronomy leadership with the design and management of a practical, farmer-centered extension system.

Own Malawi's agronomy and extension strategy

- Co-design and maintain a multi-year strategy aligned with Malawi’s impact priorities and farmers’ needs.
- Turn the strategy into annual OKRs, budgets, seasonal plans and clear ownership across teams.

Embed extension in Field Operations execution

- Build agronomy and extension priorities into the Field Operations seasonal calendar, training cascade, field tools and performance routines.
- Strengthen the technical capability of Field Managers, Field Officers and other delivery partners through training-of-trainers, coaching and practical support.
- Create clear feedback and support channels so field teams receive timely technical answers and can share implementation challenges and farmer responses.

Own the process of qualitative technical agronomic recommendations

- Use Human-Centred Design, farmer feedback and impact data to develop, test and refine agronomic recommendations.
- Work with Innovations, MEL and global technical teams to assess recommendations against local evidence, farmers’ realities and government guidance before they are scaled.
- Conduct formative research to understand farmers’ needs, behaviours and barriers to adoption.

Design farmer-centered extension and behavior-change interventions

- Translate technical recommendations into simple, memorable and actionable guidance for field teams and farmers.
- Develop extension approaches that use the right mix of group training, demonstrations, coaching and digital channels.
- Use the findings to design, test and improve extension approaches and communication content.
- Apply adult-learning, behavior-change and human-centered design approaches to understand barriers to adoption and ensure content works for different farmer profiles.

Monitor adoption, learning and impact

- Analyze results across farmer groups, locations and delivery channels to identify where recommendations or delivery approaches need to change.
- Lead seasonal learning reviews and maintain clear records of lessons and decisions to continue, adapt or stop interventions or crop offerings.

Build and manage a high-performing team

- Set clear goals, roles and decision-making responsibilities, and hold the team accountable for timely, high-quality delivery.
- Coach direct reports, strengthen the team’s technical expertise and support staff to take on greater ownership.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

Technical Expertise

- A bachelor's degree in Agronomy, Crop Science, Agricultural Systems, Agricultural Extension, Sociology, Anthropology, Design or a related field;
- A bachelor’s degree in Agricultural Extension, Behavioural Science, Communications, Anthropology, Sociology, Design or a related field.
- Experience working in the agricultural sector, ideally with smallholder farmers, is strongly preferred.
- At least 5+ years of relevant professional experience in Agricultural Extension, Human-Centred Design, Social Behaviour Change Campaigns, or Rural Marketing, with experience applying these approaches in the agricultural sector
- Demonstrated experience developing, testing or scaling agronomic recommendations or rural extension interventions.
- Experience using adult-learning, instructional-design, SBCC or human-centered design approaches is strongly preferred

Core skills

- Technical judgment: Able to assess agronomic evidence, identify limitations and translate it into responsible recommendations.
- Farmer-centered design: Able to understand farmer constraints and create practical interventions that improve understanding and adoption.
- Data and learning: Comfortable using qualitative and quantitative evidence to make decisions; strong Excel skills required, with R or Stata as an advantage.
- Strategy and project management: Able to prioritize, build critical paths and keep multiple seasonal workstreams on track.
- Communication: Able to make complex technical information simple and persuasive for field teams, farmers, leaders and external partners.
- Collaboration and influence: Able to work across Field Operations, Innovations, MEL and government-facing teams without relying solely on formal authority.
- People leadership: Able to set high standards, coach others and build a healthy, accountable team culture.

Cultural Fit & Communication

- Value Alignment: Deeply aligned with One Acre Fund values: *Farmers First*, *Work Hard*, *Grow Through Feedback*, and *Own Your Results*.
- Communication: Clear, compelling written and verbal style with a strong eye for data presentation and visual design (English required).
- Commitment: Willingness to relocate and commit to living in Africa (Malawi) for at least two years for a long-term career track.

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Zomba, Malawi

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

## **Eligibility**

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya, Malawi, Ethiopia, Uganda, Tanzania, Nigeria, Rwanda, Burundi, Zambia and the Democratic Republic of Congo.

## **Application Deadline**

16 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

title: Referral for Migrants and Mobile Populations Consultant
body:
Position Title : **Referral for Migrants and Mobile Populations Consultant**

Duty Station : IOM Philippines Country Office (Cotabato)

Classification: Consultant

Type of Appointment: Consultancy

Estimated Start Date: ASAP

Closing Date : 8 October 2026

**Project Context and Scope**

AThe International Organization for Migration (IOM)’s health program in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) aims at strengthening the resilience and responsiveness of the region’s health system and improving access to healthcare, as part of the organization’s strategy to alleviate the driver of unwanted migration and to reduce health-related risks during displacements and migration cycle. IOM has implemented various health-related projects that contributed to better health outcomes in the BARMM.

IOM’s project “Building Resilience through Inclusive Governance and Healthcare Transformation in BARMM (BRIGHT-BARMM), funded by Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA), aims to enhance the local capacity of Ministry of Health (MOH), the local provinces and cities/municipalities, to pursue key and cross cutting reforms in health systems. It will strengthen Health Systems (HS), particularly in areas of health governance and leadership, financing, and data and information, to provide a more conducive setting for implementing Safe Motherhood (SM), Adolescent Reproductive Health (ARH), and Global Health Security (GHS) programs.

Within the GHS component, IOM seeks to strengthen the capacity of the government, health workers, and frontline workers to promote inclusive, preventive, and culturally and gender appropriate health programs for returning migrants and mobile populations. This includes improving access to health information, strengthening referral pathways, and reducing the potential spread of infectious diseases through Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) materials, capacity-building of health workers at Points of Entry (PoEs), and the establishment of referral pathways to strengthen access to screening, counselling, and treatment for returnees and migrants. To support these efforts, IOM will engage a consultant to provide advisory and technical assistance with a focus on Referral Pathways for Returning Migrants and Mobile Populations.

Under the overall guidance of the Head of Sub-Office in Cotabato City, direct supervision of the National Migration Health Programme Coordinator, and in collaboration with the technical leads, the successful candidate will produce analytical papers, finalize the Referral Pathway Toolkit and SOP Manual, and facilitate the development of a Referral Pathway Institutionalization and Sustainability Plan. These outputs will contribute to strengthening national and local capacity to promote inclusive, preventive, and rights-based health programmes for returnees and host communities in areas of return and reintegration.

The objective of this consultancy is to strengthen migration health referral systems in ZamBaSulTa by refining and institutionalizing referral pathways, developing standardized referral tools and SOPs, building the capacity of stakeholders through training and mentoring, and establishing sustainable coordination and governance mechanisms to improve access to health, protection, and other essential services for Returning Filipinos from Sabah (ReFS), migrants and mobile populations.

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing**  
Migration Health Unit in Mindanao

BRIGHT BARMM: MA1161: 3:3:1:006-Consultancy (inc. CP) Migration Health

## **Responsibilities**

**Tasks to be performed under this contract**

**A**. **FIRST DELIVERABLES:** Migration Health Referral Pathway Refinement, Validation, and Operationalization Package

Building on the outputs and recommendations generated during the completed consultation and validation workshop, the consultant shall:

- Review existing and initially drafted health referral systems, protocols, service mapping outputs, and draft referral pathway tools developed under the project, identifying gaps, overlaps, and opportunities for strengthening alignment with national, BARMM, and local referral mechanisms.
- Refine and validate Migration Health Referral Pathway Package for ZamBaSulTa, ensuring that it is practical, context-specific, gender-responsive, protection-sensitive, and responsive to the health and protection needs of Returning Filipinos from Sabah (ReFs), migrants, and mobile populations. The package shall include, at a minimum:
    - Referral pathway flowcharts and process maps;
    - Standardized referral and feedback forms;
    - Referral tracking and monitoring tools;
    - Service mapping and directory templates;
    - Roles and responsibilities matrix for participating agencies and service providers; and
    - Referral coordination and reporting mechanisms.
- Prepare a draft Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) Manual to support the implementation and institutionalization of the referral pathway. The SOP shall clearly define procedures for:
    - Identification and screening of referral cases;
    - Referral initiation, acceptance, and case handover;
    - Follow-up and closure of referral cases;
    - Health, protection, and multisectoral referral coordination;
    - Confidentiality, informed consent, and data-sharing protocols;
    - Documentation, reporting, and referral monitoring requirements; and
    - Roles and responsibilities of Bangsamoro Migration Health Network (BMHN) members and other relevant stakeholders.

-Activities shall be completed by 30 October 2026, with all required deliverable reports submitted by email to IOM no later than 30 November 2026 (30% of overall contract value)

**B. SECOND DELIVERABLES:** Referral Pathway Training Package and Capacity Building

Building on the refined Migration Health Referral Pathway Package and draft SOPs, the consultant shall develop and deliver a comprehensive capacity-building programme to support the effective implementation, institutionalization, and sustainability of referral mechanisms for migrants, ReFs, and mobile populations in ZamBaSulTa.

The consultant shall:

- Co-develop with the RCCE Consultant the refinement of the training design, curriculum, agenda, and learning materials for the RCCE and Referral Pathway Training to strengthen the capacity of stakeholders serving returning migrants and mobile populations.
- Develop a comprehensive Migration Health Referral Pathway Training Package, ensuring that all materials are culturally sensitive, gender-/age-/ability-inclusive, and accessible to the diverse stakeholders involved in referral management and service delivery. The package shall include, at a minimum:
    - Facilitator's Guide
    - Participant's Manual
    - Presentation materials
    - Pre- and post-training assessment tools
    - Case studies and practical referral scenarios
    - Referral pathway simulation and tabletop exercises
- Conduct a training workshop for Bangsamoro Migration Health Network (BMHN) members, frontline POE workers, local health workers in referral facilities in ZamBaSulTa, and other service providers on referral pathways. Using the training materials and package developed, and referencing the IOM Health, Border, and Mobility Management (HBMM) framework, DOH/MOH referral structure, IOM Protection Handbook, and Sphere standards, the sessions shall cover, as applicable, the following topics:
- Understanding the migrant context and mobility patterns of ZamBaSulTa, including, informal and irregular movements of Returning Filipinos from Sabah (REFs)
- Health risk identification and prioritization, facilitating and institutionalizing referral pathways, and monitoring and tracking of referral cases.
- Monitoring and evaluation on the effectiveness of referral pathway, and implementing continuous improvement to maintain effective referral
- Prepare and submit a Training Completion Report summarizing the training methodology, participant profile, pre- and post-training assessment results, key findings, recommendations, and proposed actions to support the operationalization and institutionalization of the migration health referral pathway in ZamBaSulTa.

-Activities shall be completed by 30 November 2026, with all required deliverable reports submitted by email to IOM no later than 30 December 2026 (30% of overall contract value)

**C**. **THIRD DELIVERABLES:** Finalization, Institutionalization, and Handover Package

Building on the validated Migration Health Referral Pathway Package, SOPs, and capacity-building activities, the consultant shall finalize all technical outputs and support their institutionalization for sustained implementation by the BMHN and relevant stakeholders.

The consultant shall:

- Finalize and integrate all revisions arising from stakeholder consultations, validation workshops, training activities, and technical reviews into the Migration Health Referral Pathway Package, ensuring consistency, usability, and alignment with national, BARMM, and local referral systems.
- Finalize the Referral Pathway Toolkit, including referral flowcharts, standardized referral and feedback forms, referral tracking and monitoring tools, service mapping directories, coordination mechanisms, and roles and responsibilities matrices.
- Finalize the Referral Pathway SOP Manual and incorporate recommendations to support institutional adoption, implementation, monitoring, and sustainability of referral mechanisms for migrants, Returning Filipinos from Sabah (ReFs), and mobile populations in ZamBaSulTa.
- Develop a Referral Pathway Institutionalization and Sustainability Plan outlining recommended governance arrangements, coordination structures, monitoring and reporting mechanisms, capacity development needs, and actions required to support the long-term operationalization of the referral system through the partner agencies.
- Prepare and submit all final digital reports and outputs in editable formats to facilitate future reproduction, updating, dissemination, and utilization by BMHN, MOH-BARMM, local government units, and relevant stakeholders.
- Present the final referral pathway package and key recommendations to IOM through a turnover and dissemination session.

-Activities shall be completed by 30 December 2026, with all required deliverable reports submitted by email to IOM no later than 15 January 2027 (40% of overall contract value)

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

- The Consultant’s performance will be assessed based on the timely completion, quality, and comprehensiveness of the agreed deliverables, as well as the effectiveness of technical assistance, stakeholder coordination, and documentation and reporting.
- Percentage of task completion specified in the ToR based on supervisors’ performance evaluation. Tasks are divided into technical assistance (60%), coordination, liaison, and networking to National, Regional, and Local stakeholders and partners (10%), documentation and reporting (30%).
- Relevance of planning, organization and timeliness for managing and delivering progress reports and outputs.
- Practical applicability and institutional adoption by BMHN and relevant government partners.
- Timeliness and completeness of deliverable
- Feedback from stakeholders on the quality of work and reports.
- Contribution to achieving project goals and objectives in BARMM, such as strengthened operational and institutional capacity and guidelines or policies, BARMM application of new knowledge, and effective service delivery.

## **Qualifications**

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

- Master’s or Higher degree in Public Health, Health Systems Management, Global Health, Sociology, Communications, Emergency/ Disaster Management, Health Systems/Operations, or any related field from an accredited academic institution with ten years of relevant professional experience.
- Advanced knowledge and proven experience in public health, global health security and migration health.

Demonstrated experience on the following:

- Referral systems, health systems strengthening, case management, community health, health emergency preparedness and response, or related fields.

title: Data Analyst
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**This position is expected to end on 15 February 2027.**

**JOB OVERVIEW**

IRC has worked in Poland since February 2022, when it launched an emergency response to the war in Ukraine as part of its wider programming across Central and Eastern Europe. IRC Poland delivers its work both directly and through long-term partnerships with local civil society and has collaborated with more than 25 Polish non-governmental organisations, primarily in Warsaw, Wrocław, Katowice, and Poznań. In 2025, IRC Poland reached 39,930 clients, including 28,319 women, across 52 projects.

IRC Poland's work is organised around three programme areas: protection and access to rights; economic empowerment and livelihoods; and education and integration. The MEAL / Programmes team relies on robust, well-managed data systems, including CommCare, KoboToolbox and OpenFn, to monitor results, ensure accountability, and support evidence-based decision-making across the country programme.

**Position Purpose**

The Data Analyst supports IRC Poland's MEAL / Programmes function by connecting the organisation's data systems and turning them into clear, usable reports. The role is focused on three areas: setting up and maintaining data integrations in OpenFn, building a reliable connection between CommCare and Excel, and developing Excel-based reports that bring together CommCare and KoboToolbox data for use by partners and internal teams.

IRC Poland is one of the first offices in the organisation to use OpenFn, so the role also involves learning the platform from the ground up and establishing a working setup that others can build on in the future.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1. OpenFn Data Integration**

- Maintain integrations between KoboToolbox, CommCare and other programme databases through OpenFn, APIs and ETL processes.
- Monitor automated data flows and troubleshoot synchronisation, duplication and data-transfer issues as they arise.
- Document database structures, integrations, data flows and system changes to keep the integration clear and maintainable over time.
- Recommend and implement automation solutions that reduce manual data transfer and the risk of error.

**2. CommCare-to-Excel Connection**

- Establish and maintain a reliable connection between CommCare and Excel through APIs and ETL processes, ensuring CommCare data can be accessed and refreshed directly within Excel.
- Monitor the CommCare-to-Excel data flow on an ongoing basis and troubleshoot synchronisation or data-transfer issues as they arise.
- Ensure the connection continues to function accurately as CommCare forms, structures and reporting requirements evolve.

**3. Excel Reporting**

- Develop and maintain dashboards and reporting tools in Excel, combining data from CommCare and KoboToolbox so that reports remain live and up to date.
- Prepare regular reports on client reach, services delivered, results and progress against targets.
- Prepare datasets and tables to support monthly, quarterly, final and ad hoc reporting requirements.
- Organise reports so that partners and internal teams can use them effectively, presenting information such as indicator progress and registrations by region and by partner.
- Translate complex data into clear findings and recommendations for non-technical stakeholders.

**JOB REQUIREMENTS**

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

- University degree in data analysis, computer science, statistics, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).
- Advanced proficiency in Excel, including building reports and dashboards that pull in and organise data from external sources (e.g. Power Query, pivot tables, formulas).
- Practical experience with CommCare, or with a comparable digital data-collection or case-management platform.
- Familiarity with KoboToolbox, or the ability to learn it quickly.
- Experience with OpenFn, or a comparable data-integration / workflow-automation tool (e.g. Zapier, Make, Talend), is an advantage but not required. OpenFn is new to IRC Poland, so comfort learning independently matters more than prior hands-on experience with this specific tool.
- Strong attention to detail when consolidating and checking data from multiple sources.
- Ability to organise and present data clearly for different audiences, including non-technical colleagues and partners.
- Professional working proficiency in English and Polish; Ukrainian will be an advantage.

**Core Competencies**

- Strong Excel skills and comfort working with data drawn from multiple systems.
- Ability to learn new tools and platforms quickly and troubleshoot issues independently.
- High level of attention to detail and accuracy.
- Ability to organise and present data clearly for technical and non-technical audiences alike.
- Proactive, self-directed approach — comfortable being the first to figure something out.

**Performance Indicators**

- The OpenFn integration is functional, documented and properly maintained.
- CommCare data is reliably and accurately connected to Excel.
- Excel reports and dashboards are accurate, up to date, and easy for partners and internal teams to use.
- Data-integration and connection issues are identified and resolved promptly.

**Compensation:** (PLN100). Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: PALESTINE - MONITORING, EVALUATION, ACCOUNTABILITY AND LEARNING MANAGER - MEAL (M/F) - GAZA
body:
## ABOUT US

**Beginning of contract : 07/12/2026**

**Duration : 5 or 7 months, to be discussed**

**Localisation : Gaza / Deir el-Balah**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## THE MISSION

Solidarités International operates across the Gaza Strip and the West Bank, with operational teams in Deir el-Balah and Ramallah and mission coordination in Jerusalem (although some national coordination staff work out of Ramallah). The position works at coordination level and covers both Gaza and West Bank operations, ensuring consistent administrative, HR and financial support across the mission. SI delivers emergency and early-recovery WASH assistance, shelter and essential-item distributions, and is scaling up nutrition-sensitive FSL activities, including a EUR 1.3 million FIFSAN project with a Palestinian partner. The portfolio relies on close cooperation with local organizations and must continually adapt to volatile access, damaged infrastructure, fragile markets and supply constraints. The Palestinian context is a particularly volatile one, especially in recent months in the West Bank, and in Gaza there are for the moments no signs of a resolution to the political and humanitarian crisis engulfing the exclave and its 2 million residents.

## THE JOB

**General objective:**

The MEAL Manager ensures that the MEAL strategy is implemented by base teams throughout the project cycle. They guarantee the quality and relevance of MEAL activities, recommendations and analyses, and provide methodological support on MEAL plan design, qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis, indicator measurement, accountability to affected populations, evaluation, learning and capitalisation.

**The main challenges:**

1\) Establishing and harmonising robust MEAL and information-management systems across a rapidly evolving, multi-sector portfolio.

2\) Building the capacity and professional development of national staff through a structured plan and measurable outcomes.

3\) Improving accountability to and understanding of the Gazan community that SI serves, and working with Program to improve programming relevance.

4\) Embedding learning through maintained trackers, lessons-learnt exercises and systematic follow-up of recommendations.

**Priorities for the 2/3 first months:**

'1) Assess and harmonise existing MEAL and information-management systems.

2\) Agree a capacity-building plan for the national MEAL team, with baseline needs, milestones and expected outcomes.

3\) Create or consolidate learning and recommendation trackers, assign owners and establish a review rhythm.

4\) Facilitate an initial lessons-learnt exercise and agree priority actions with Program teams.

**Security constraints:**

Security constraints are extremely high in Gaza, with air, land and naval strikes, risks related to medium and light infantry weapons, and severe social tensions linked to war, deprivation and economic collapse. The position requires strong security awareness, strict adherence to protocols, and the ability to lead under pressure.

## YOUR PROFILE

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCE**

Diploma : Bachelor's or Master's degree in monitoring and evaluation, statistics, data management, international development, humanitarian studies or a related field.

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 5 years and more

Experience on a similar position : 3/4 years

**SKILLS**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1\. Strong command of MEAL strategy, project-cycle management and MEAL plan design

2\. Expertise in qualitative and quantitative data collection, indicator measurement, data quality, responsible data management and information-management systems

3\. Ability to design and manage accountability, complaints and feedback mechanisms that protect complainant data

4\. Experience creating and maintaining learning and recommendation trackers, facilitating lessons-learnt exercises and following up agreed actions

5\. Demonstrated capacity-building skills: assess needs, develop plans, coach staff and measure improvements in autonomy and work quality

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1. Experience working in Arab culture, and knowledge of how to approch and communicate with national staff
2. Excellent organization and prioritization skills, with the ability to meet multiple deadlines.
3. Ability to model good behavior and team work across a diverse team in a politically, socially, and religious complex context
4. Clear communication and ability to manage frustration in stressful situations
5. Ability to learn, with a strong growth mindset
6. High standards of rigor, integrity, accountability, discretion and confidentiality.
7. Adaptability, initiative and strong cross-department collaboration with Program, Access/Liaison and Coordination teams. Experience from other NGOs is welcomed; prior SI experience is not required.

**LANGUAGES**

1. English
2. Arabic is not mandatory but highly desirable and may compensate for some experience

## SI WILLE OFFER YOU

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2310 gross per month (2100 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

The position is based in Deir-el-Balah, where Solidarités International maintains its office and guesthouse, as do most INGOs. Since the ceasefire brokered on 10 October, living conditions have improved, and markets are gradually becoming more functional. At the time the position opened, most basic food items, including fruits and vegetables, were available in Gaza markets, although at high prices. Electricity at the SI office and guesthouse is entirely solar-powered, which, particularly in winter, may occasionally lead to temporary shortages. Internet is available at the GH and office with limited shortages. SI has one validated supermarket where expatriates can by most goods for everyday life.

title: Director, Technical - GUARD
body:
**JOB SUMMARY**

The Technical Director will provide strategic technical leadership and oversight for the project, ensuring the quality, coherence and effectiveness of program design, implementation, and technical assistance across all project objectives. As a member of the senior leadership team and classified as Key Personnel, the Technical Director will work in close collaboration with the Chief of Party, consortium partners, headquarters staff, and country missions to ensure alignment with donor priorities, global best practices, and adaptive management principles. This position reflects direct costs incurred by headquarters staff and requires both strategic vision and hands-on technical expertise in global health, infectious disease control, and health systems readiness.

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential function with or without reasonable accommodation.

**MAIN TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Strategic Technical Leadership**

Provide overarching strategic technical direction for all project activities, ensuring coherence, innovation, and impact across program objectives. Lead the refinement of the project's technical strategy, theory of change, and results framework. Ensure that technical approaches are evidence-based, context-appropriate, and aligned with the latest global health standards and guidelines, including those from CDC, and other relevant authorities.

**Program Design and Implementation Oversight**

Oversee the design, planning, and execution of all technical components of the project, including infectious disease surveillance, IPC, HCID readiness, screening and triage, safe isolation, and referral pathways. Ensure that program design is responsive to country contexts, operational realities, and security constraints. Monitor implementation progress from International Medical Corps (IMC) and consortium partners against workplans, identify bottlenecks, and propose corrective actions to ensure timely delivery of outputs and achievement of targets.

**Technical Assistance and Guidance**

Provide high-quality technical guidance to project staff, consortium partners, government counterparts, and other stakeholders. Develop and disseminate technical tools, standard operating procedures (SOPs), guidelines, and training materials. Support the Epidemiologist/ID and IPC Specialist and other technical staff in delivering targeted technical support to strengthen core alert-to-action and containment capacities at country and sub-national levels.

**Consortium Coordination and Partnership Management**

Support coordination across all consortium partners, fostering a collaborative, transparent, and results-oriented working environment. Facilitate regular technical meetings, working groups, and learning exchanges among partners. Ensure that each partner's technical contributions are well-integrated, complementary, and aligned with the overall project vision. Build and maintain strong relationships with consortium members, government agencies, and civil society organizations.

**Adaptive Management and Technical Quality Assurance**

Contribute to adaptive management processes by continuously monitoring the evolving epidemiological, operational, and security landscape. Lead technical quality assurance efforts, including the development and application of quality checklists, performance metrics, and work with M/E teams on updated M/E frameworks. Promote a culture of learning, reflection, and continuous improvement within the project team and across partners. Ensure that lessons learned and best practices are documented and disseminated.

**Capacity Building and Workforce Development**

Lead efforts to build the technical capacity of project staff, partners, and national counterparts. Design and oversee training programs, mentorship schemes, and on-the-job coaching initiatives. Ensure that capacity-building activities are tailored to the needs of diverse audiences, especially frontline health workers and subnational/national staff. Support the development of sustainable, locally owned technical expertise that extends beyond the project lifecycle.

**Representation and External Engagement**

Represent the project and organization in relevant technical forums, working groups, conferences, and coordination mechanisms at global, regional, and national levels. Engage with multilateral agencies, academic institutions, and private sector partners to leverage additional expertise, resources, and innovations. Serve as a thought leader and represent evidence-based approaches to infectious disease preparedness and response.

**Research, Innovation, and Knowledge Management**

Promote and support operational research, innovation, and knowledge management activities within the project. Identify opportunities for research partnerships, pilot initiatives, and the introduction of new technologies or methodologies. Ensure that project-generated knowledge is captured, analyzed, and shared through publications, conferences, and digital platforms to contribute to the global evidence base.

**Risk Management and Security**

In collaboration with the Chief of Party and security focal points, ensure that technical activities are planned and implemented with due consideration for operational and security risks. Develop contingency plans for technical aspects of the project in volatile or insecure environments. Ensure that staff and partners are equipped with the necessary skills and protocols to operate safely in complex settings.

Perform other duties as assigned. The duties and responsibilities listed in this document are representative of the nature and level of work assigned and not necessarily comprehensive.

**Job Requirements**

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

• Education: A Master's degree or higher in Public Health, Epidemiology, Infectious Disease, Health Systems, International Development, or a closely related field. A medical degree (MD) or doctoral degree (PhD, DrPH) is highly desirable.

• Experience: A minimum of 12 years of progressive experience in global health program management, with at least 7 to 8 years in a senior technical leadership role. Proven track record in infectious disease surveillance, outbreak and response, IPC, and HCID readiness. Demonstrated experience managing complex, multi-country health projects funded by major donors (e.g., U.S. Government, Global Fund, World Bank, bilateral agencies).

• Technical Expertise: Deep technical knowledge of infectious disease epidemiology, surveillance systems, infection prevention and control protocols, containment and mitigation, screening and triage methodologies, safe isolation practices, and referral pathways. Familiarity with International Health Regulations (IHR), WHO guidelines, and global health security frameworks. Experience with alert-to-action systems and rapid response mechanisms is essential.

• Leadership and Management: Demonstrated ability to lead multidisciplinary, multicultural teams in complex operational and security environments. Strong skills in strategic planning, adaptive management, and quality assurance. Proven ability to mentor, coach, and develop technical staff and partners.

• Partnership and Coordination: Extensive experience working with consortium partners, government ministries, international agencies, and civil society organizations. Strong diplomatic and negotiation skills. Ability to build consensus, manage conflicts, and foster productive collaboration across diverse stakeholders.

• Communication Skills: Excellent written and oral communication skills in English. Ability to produce high-quality technical reports, briefs, and presentations for diverse audiences. Proficiency in additional languages (e.g., French, Spanish, Arabic) is an asset.

• Analytical and Problem-Solving Skills: Strong analytical skills with the ability to synthesize complex technical information, identify trends, and develop practical solutions. Experience with data-driven decision-making, M/E frameworks, and performance measurement.

• Operational and Security Awareness: Experience working in fragile, conflict-affected, or otherwise challenging operational environments. Understanding of security protocols and risk management strategies for health programming in insecure settings.

• Computer Skills: Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and familiarity with data management and visualization tools. Experience with project management software and digital health platforms is an advantage.

• Strategic Thinking and Vision: Ability to articulate a compelling technical vision and translate it into actionable plans.

• Results Orientation: Commitment to achieving measurable outcomes and holding self and others accountable for results.

• Collaboration and Teamwork: Ability to work effectively across boundaries, build trust, and leverage collective expertise.

• Adaptability and Resilience: Capacity to navigate ambiguity, respond to changing circumstances, and maintain effectiveness under pressure.

• Integrity and Ethics: Unwavering commitment to ethical standards, transparency, and accountability in all aspects of work.

• Innovation and Learning: Openness to new ideas, willingness to experiment, and dedication to continuous professional and organizational learning.

**Ethical Conduct at International Medical Corps**

As part of a global, humanitarian team dedicated to saving lives, easing suffering, and building self-reliance, International Medical Corps staff are responsible for adhering to our *Code of Conduct and Ethics* and for knowing and abiding by International Medical Corps policies and standards. All staff play a vital role in preventing violations of our *Code of Conduct and Ethics*, including conflicts of interest, fraud, corruption, and any kind of exploitation or abuse. International Medical Corps is also committed to providing a safe and healthy work environment free of harassment, bullying, and other misconduct, enabling staff to build and maintain professional, respectful working relationships.

International Medical Corps prioritizes safeguarding the populations with whom we work from exploitation, neglect, or abuse of children and adults at risk, and/or any form of trafficking in persons. International Medical Corps is committed to engaging members of crisis-affected communities to participate in meaningful ways in a crisis response, including making informed decisions about the assistance they receive, mitigating potential risks, and holding us accountable for the commitments we make. All staff are expected to support International Medical Corps’ culture of accountability toward our stakeholders, particularly the crisis-affected communities and individuals we serve.

As part of International Medical Corps’ commitment to a speak-up culture and as one of the primary ways we collectively hold ourselves accountable for complying with the ethical principles and standards of conduct outlined in the *Code of Conduct and Ethics,* all staffare required to report suspected or actual misconduct or violations of organizational policies. Our *Code of Conduct and Ethics* and *Whistleblower Policy* prohibit any form of retaliation against whistleblowers or individuals who report a concern in good faith. Staff who violate these protections may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment or contractual relationship with International Medical Corps.

**Equal Opportunities**

International Medical Corps is proud to provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, age, disability or status as a veteran.

**Misconduct Disclosure Scheme**

All offers of employment at International Medical Corps are subject to satisfactory references and background checks. International Medical Corps participates in the Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme from the Steering Committee for Humanitarian Response (SCHR). In accordance with this, we will request information from an applicant’s previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her understanding of these recruitment procedures.

title: SOUTH SUDAN - Head of MEAL Department (M/F) - Juba
body:
## ABOUT US

**Desired start date:** ASAP  
**Duration of the mission:** 6 months  
**Location:** Juba

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## ABOUT THE MISSION

SOLIDARITÉS INTERNATIONAL (SI) has been operating in South Sudan since 2006, conducting activities in emergency and post emergency context, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas, including refugees/returnees and IDP camp settings.   
Context:  
\- Food insecurity is one of the highest in the world due to recurring shocks (consecutive years of widespread flooding, conflict-based displacement), and an ongoing protracted macro-economic crisis.  
\- The country also faces cholera outbreaks on a yearly basis, has very limited sanitation coverage and safe water access remain a challenge for most of the population.  
\- On top of these chronic situations, South Sudan has been highly impacted by the war that started in Sudan in April 2023. By end of 2025, more than 1,000,000 people had entered South Sudan, the vast majority entering through the Joda/ Wunthow border point in Renk County, Upper Nile State (northern part of South Sudan).   
\- More recently, resurgence of internal tensions have led to heightened conflict and analysts are worried that the peace conditions offered by the Peace Agreement may not hold.  
As a result, 9,3 million are in need of humanitarian assistance as of 2025.   
SI sectors of intervention:   
\- The portfolio includes both WASH & FSL activities. SI's expertise in running emergency WaSH intervention is highly acknowledged by all WaSH actors and donors and has been one of the first responders of the cholera response. Teh FSL component has become very important due to nwe grants that enlarged the portfolio of the mission  
Areas of operation:  
SI has a rapid emergency team based in Juba, who is being deployed following Rapid Needs Assessment in flood, epidemic or conflict induced displacement in the country. The teams will be deployed for up to 2 months per intervention adn the time in the coordination office only for limited time (sectors WASH and Cash). In additiomn, SI has three static offices in Malakal, Renk and Ulang, as well as 2 sub-offices in Fashoda and Baliet, always in Upper Nile.

## ABOUT THE JOB

**General objective:**

To strengthen the quality, accountability, monitoring, evaluation, and learning of humanitarian programmes through robust MEAL systems. The position supports effective monitoring, evidence-based decision-making, accountability to affected populations, data quality, programme adaptation, learning, and compliance with organisational and donor standards.

**The main challenges:**

**Key Issues and Challenges**

- Complex humanitarian access constraints due to conflict, insecurity, intercommunal violence, checkpoints, and bureaucratic impediments, with rapidly changing security conditions.
- High-risk public health environments, including cholera, Ebola, and other outbreaks, requiring strict health, safety, and infection prevention measures.
- Coordination with local authorities to facilitate access, approvals, movement authorisations, and operational continuity.
- Need for technical coordination across sectors, partners, and operational areas.
- Variable team capacity requiring mentoring, coaching, and technical support to ensure quality and compliance.
- Limited communication infrastructure affecting reporting, information management, and operational follow-up.
- Ongoing structuring of the emergency, FSL, and MEAL setup following the recent scale-up, including reinforcement of systems and field capacities.
- High operational pressure requiring flexibility, surge capacity, rapid adaptation, and reprioritisation.
- Logistical constraints including poor road access, flooding, air transport dependency, fuel availability, and emergency supply prepositioning.
- Staff welfare and duty of care concerns linked to deployments in austere and insecure environments.

**Priorities for the first 2–3 months:**

- Strengthen the MEAL department at coordination and field levels, harmonising systems, tools, processes, and reporting with organisational and donor requirements.
- Build MEAL and programme staff capacity through mentoring, training, supervision, and technical support, focusing on data quality, accountability, monitoring, and evidence-based programming.
- Reinforce and operationalise Feedback and Complaint Response Mechanisms (FCRM) and integrate community feedback into programme activities.
- Strengthen information management, data analysis, and reporting to provide timely and actionable information for decision-making.

**Security constraints:**

South Sudan remains a highly volatile humanitarian context marked by conflict, intercommunal violence, displacement, disease outbreaks, climatic shocks, and severe humanitarian needs. Conditions can deteriorate rapidly due to insecurity, political tensions, armed clashes, cattle raiding, flooding, and access constraints, particularly across Upper Nile, Jonglei, Unity, and Greater Equatoria. Bureaucratic impediments, poor infrastructure, and seasonal constraints further restrict access, requiring remote management and air transport.

Juba remains comparatively stable, with access to accommodation, medical services, communications, and facilities supporting staff welfare and coordination. Safety measures include movement tracking, communication protocols, security briefings, contingency planning, and coordination with security actors and local authorities.

Field conditions remain unpredictable. Ulang requires particular attention due to rapidly changing security and access conditions. Malakal and Renk are currently comparatively more stable, while continuous risk monitoring remains essential.

## YOUR PROFILE

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCE**

Diploma : BA in engineering, Biology, Water Resources Management, Humanitarian/Development/Political Studies, and similar

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 5 years and more

Experience on a similar position : 3/4 years

**SKILLS**

**Technical Skills**

1\. Strong knowledge of MEAL systems, methodologies, and tools in humanitarian and emergency response contexts.

2\. Proven experience in designing and implementing monitoring frameworks, indicator tracking systems, and data collection methodologies.

3\. Experience in developing and managing accountability mechanisms, including Feedback and Complaint Response Mechanisms (FCRM).

4\. Strong information management and data visualisation skills, including proficiency in Excel and data management platforms such as Kobo, ODK, Power BI, or similar tools.

**Transversal Skills**

1\. Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively in multicultural and multidisciplinary environments.

2\. Strong organisational and planning skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines simultaneously.

3\. Excellent reporting, drafting, and presentation skills.

**Languages**

1\. English mandatory

2\. Arabic is a bonus

## SI WILL OFFER YOU

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2860 gross per month (2600 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

The Head of MEAL Department lives in a shared guesthouse with the other international staffs (own bathrrom and bedroom but shared kitchen and shared spaces)

- Individual room, with electricity 24/7.
- Internet and Phone network available
- Restaurants and international food are available
- There is an internal curfew at night for international staffs - different zones are set (6-8-10PM). Curfew can be reduced based on security updates
- There is one driver available on evenings for movements out of office hours, 2 drivers during weekends daytime.
- Access to activities is possible for all (and encouraged!).
- In coordination, movements outside of Juba town (besides intervention location) for leisure are not permitted. When deployed in the field the conditions vary and can be challenging.

title: Responsable des programmes humanitaires (H/F)
body:
Rejoindre l’ONG Plan International France, c’est donner un sens à sa vie professionnelle en s’engageant dans la solidarité internationale et en adhérant aux valeurs de transparence, de respect, de durabilité, de communauté et d’inclusion.

Notre ONG est fière d’œuvrer pour un monde meilleur dans lequel les droits des enfants, et en particulier des filles, sont respectés. C’est ainsi qu’en 2025, le réseau Plan International a permis à 5,1 millions de filles dans le monde de bénéficier d’un meilleur accès à l’éducation.

Rejoindre notre ONG, c’est aussi intégrer une équipe conviviale d’une quarantaine de salarié·es et de bénévoles, aussi expert·es que passionné·es. Nous travaillons dans la bienveillance et la confiance, en gardant pour objectif le bien-être des salarié·es. Télétravail, flexibilité des horaires, grande autonomie sont autant d’aménagements qui favoriseront votre équilibre vie pro/vie perso. Vous trouverez une palette de métiers variés et une organisation qui s’inscrit dans une dynamique de progression.

Pour compléter cette belle équipe, nous recherchons des talents qui partagent nos valeurs et qui souhaitent apporter leur pierre à l’édifice. Venez donc nous rencontrer pour découvrir les belles missions qui nous animent et nous motivent.

## **Le poste que nous proposons** 

Au sein du département Programmes et partenariats stratégiques, la∙le Responsable des programmes humanitaires est en charge du développement de la programmation et du plaidoyer humanitaire de Plan International France en lien avec le plan stratégique de l’organisation centré sur les droits de l’enfant et l’égalité de genre.

Sous la responsabilité de la Directrice des programmes et partenariats stratégiques, la∙le Responsable des programmes humanitaires est chargé∙e de :

**Gérer le portefeuille des projets/programmes humanitaires**

Assurer la gestion des projets/programmes humanitaires, conformément aux procédures et au cadre de qualité de Plan International, et un reporting de qualité aux bailleurs en étroite collaboration avec les pôles/départements concernés.

Apporter un appui au Pôle Conformité et Finance de Plan International France pour assurer la conformité financière des projets/programmes et la réalisation des audits et du suivi des recommandations.

Assurer le partage d’informations sur les projets/programmes humanitaires au sein du département et avec les autres pôles/départements (rédaction de fiches de référence pour présentation et suivi des projets/programmes, organisation de comités de présentation, suivi et clôture, identification d’informations permettant d’alimenter la communication et le plaidoyer, etc).

En collaboration avec le département Communication et Collecte Individuelle, mettre en place un plan de communication, collecter des données, des informations et des témoignages sur les interventions humanitaires et assurer un reporting.

**Déployer la stratégie et la programmation humanitaire de Plan international France**

Développer et mettre en œuvre la programmation humanitaire en lien avec cette stratégie.

Appuyer les bureaux pays dans l’identification des besoins, assurer la coordination du développement de projets et la rédaction des propositions d’interventions en collaboration, le cas échéant, avec les pôles géographiques.

Développer/renforcer le dialogue avec les bailleurs de fonds pertinents (identifiés comme prioritaires) pour maintenir une connaissance approfondie de leur stratégie d’intervention, anticiper les opportunités de financement et positionner Plan International France comme un acteur humanitaire pertinent sur les thématiques des droits de l’enfant et des jeunesses et d’égalité de genre en situation de crises et de conflits.

Assurer une veille sur les situations de fragilités et de conflits et assurer la coordination entre les différents pôles et départements de la cellule d’urgence, le cas échéant

**Renforcer le savoir-faire de Plan International France en matière de programmation humanitaire en situation de crises ou de conflits**

Apporter de façon ad hoc aux bureaux pays et aux membres de l’équipe programmes une expertise sur les questions de la prévention et gestion des crises.

Apporter un appui à la Direction des programmes et partenariats stratégiques pour actualiser et faciliter la mise en œuvre de la procédure de sécurité de Plan International France, et assurer une veille des situations humanitaires et sécuritaires dans les pays d’intervention en situation de crises ou de conflits.

**Agir en tant que point focal sur les questions humanitaires au sein de Plan International France et du réseau Plan International**

Assurer l’interface entre Plan International France et le réseau Plan International sur les thématiques humanitaires identifiées comme prioritaires.

Participer activement aux plateformes de coordination du réseau sur les questions humanitaires et y représenter Plan International France dans les instances pertinentes.

Assurer une coordination avec le département communication et collecte individuelle et représenter Plan International France lors de prises de parole sur les questions humanitaires dans différentes instances.

**Piloter le déploiement d’un plaidoyer opérationnel humanitaire sur les pays identifiés comme prioritaires**

Faire remonter des données sur les atteintes aux droits de l’enfant et des jeunesses ains que sur les inégalités de genre dans les pays identifiés comme prioritaires pour alimenter les messages de plaidoyer.

Poursuivre la mise en œuvre des actions de plaidoyer opérationnelles humanitaires telles que prévues dans le plan d’action

Prendre une part active et représenter Plan International France dans les instances de coordination nationale et internationale, notamment auprès de l’ECT Enjeux Humanitaires de Coordination Sud.

## **Le profil que nous cherchons** 

Vous êtes titulaire d'un diplôme de niveau Master, idéalement en solidarité internationale, action humanitaire, relations internationales, sciences politiques (ou équivalent). Et vous justifiez d'au moins 5 ans d'expérience en coordination, développement et gestion de programmes humanitaires, incluant une expérience terrain. Également :

Expérience confirmée en montage, coordination (notamment sur la phase de développement) et gestion d’un portefeuille de projets financés par les bailleurs publics ou agences françaises (par exemple CDCS, MEAE, AFD – dont Minka, divisions techniques –, ECHO, Expertise France, etc.), idéalement dans les domaines prioritaires de Plan International. La gestion de projets multi-bailleurs est un plus.

Expérience dans le plaidoyer humanitaire et bonne compréhension de l’approche par les droits et de l’égalité de genre sont un plus

Parfaite maitrise du français et de l’anglais (oral, écrit) ; l’espagnol est un plus

Très bonne organisation et capacité à gérer les priorités et répondre à de courtes échéances
