title: Palestine - Program Coordinator (M/F) - Jerusalem
body:
## About us

**Desired start date: 15/10/2026**  
**Duration of the mission: 12 months**  
**Location: Jerusalem**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## La mission

In response to the attacks of 7 October 2023, the Israeli army launched a massive offensive in the Gaza Strip, beginning with a campaign of air strikes followed by a series of ground offensives that successively hit all the enclave's governorates. The intensity of the fighting, repeated strikes and successive evacuation orders have forced more than 1.7 million people to move, sometimes several times, to sites less directly affected by the fighting. The first displacements towards the south of Gaza, and more particularly the governorate of Rafah where 1.7 million Palestinians were displaced in April 2024, were followed by the displacement of more than 1 million people towards the central part of the Gaza Strip when the offensive on Rafah was launched in May 2024.

Displaced people are living in schools, organised sites and informal sites where it is more difficult to organise assistance. The destruction by the fighting of vital infrastructure, such as health facilities, water and electricity supplies, schools and other public services, is having a major impact on the displaced and host populations.

**SOLIDARITÉS INTERNATIONA**L teams have been working in Gaza since February 2024. Activities are currently being developed in the governorate of Deir el-Balah, in the centre of the Gaza Strip, where a base was opened in March.  
SI teams are implementing WASH activities, which include the installation and rehabilitation of water desalination plants to ensure the production of drinking water, the transport of water to displacement sites by tanker truck, and activities aimed at reducing health risks and improving the living conditions of displaced people through hygiene promotion sessions and the distribution of hygiene kits.

## Job description

**General objective:**

The Program Coordinator oversees the development and quality of SI’s programs, ensuring they are needs-driven, context-adapted, and impactful. S/He supports strategic planning, program monitoring, technical compliance, and coordination across teams, partners, and donors, while strengthening staff capacities and safeguarding ethical standards.

**The main challenges:**

1\) Developing strategy and defining SI value add for West Bank, including positioning on coordination architecture, and preparedness in the case of a medium-scale escalation.  
2\) Developing SI strategy and relevance in Shelter and FSL for Gaza.   
3\) Challenges include compliance, resource allocation, staff capacity, and integrating cross-cutting themes while mitigating operational and ethical risks.

**Priorities for the 2/3 first months:**

Support the structuration of the mission, including onboarding new staff, expanding activities, and developing new sectors and areas of intervention.   
Reinforce quality monitoring of program strategies and ensure the implementation and harmonization of SI’s frameworks, tools, and procedures across all teams.  
Implement the strategy of the mission and develop the activities of SI in the West Bank   
Continue to support the activities and Gaza to kept Gaza as a key Wash actor

**Security constraints:**

The mission faces no particular security constraints in Jerusalem, however, there are major security and access challenges in the Gaza Strip.

## Votre profil

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCE**

Master's degree in Humanitarian Action, human rights, social science (geography, sociology, anthropology, history) or Political Science is more preferable.

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 5 years

Experience on a similar position : 3/4 years

**SKILLS**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1\) Program strategy development

2\) Multi-sector program design (WASH, FSL ).

3\) Partnership development and coordination

4)External coordination: engagement with clusters, international partners, and national actors

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1)Leadership and team management

2)Coordination across multi-level teams

3)Capacity building and training

**LANGUAGES**

**- English**

**- Arabic is an asset**

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2860 gross per month (2600base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

To date, SI have a coordination office and a guesthouse in Jerusalem. The office is fully furnished, and the guesthouse is equipped with all necessary equipment (internet, kitchen, laundry facilities, living room, etc.). Jerusalem is generally very safe, and staff can move freely across most areas of East and West Jerusalem. Walking is permitted.

title: Mental health and psychosocial suppport coordinator (F/M) - Yemen
body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?

For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

## **MdM in Yemen**

Yemen remains one of the world's most severe humanitarian crises, after more than a decade of conflict, economic decline, climate shocks, and political instability. In 2026, over two-thirds of the population require humanitarian assistance, including 9.4 million people identified as most in need of life-saving support.

The health system is under extreme strain, with only 59.3% of health facilities fully operational and 19.3 million people requiring healthcare services, including more than 660,000 pregnant women in need of urgent care. Cholera continues to pose a major public health challenge, adding pressure to an already weakened system.

The operational environment remains highly volatile, marked by security incidents, service disruptions, funding cuts, and economic challenges that regularly affect humanitarian activities.

Médecins du Monde operates across northern and southern Yemen, with a coordination office in Sana’a and field offices in Aden and Marib. Its interventions focus on two strategic priorities:

- Supporting 29 health facilities to deliver primary healthcare services, including outpatient care, vaccination, nutrition, and reproductive health.
- Providing mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) through healthcare facilities and community-based networks trained in identification, referral, and awareness-raising activities.

## **About the role**

As MHPSS coordinator you will be in charge of overseeing all MdM’s MHPSS programming for the Yemen mission. You will contribute to proposal writing and development of new projects or concepts as per MdM’s mandate. You will also take part in the country strategy elaboration for the MHPSS sector, led by the general coordinator.

## **Who you’ll work with**

Under the supervision of the general coordinator and in close collaboration with the mental health advisor, you will provide technical leadership and functional management to the MHPSS Officers based in Sana’a, Aden and Marib.

Working closely with other MdM departments, local NGO partners and focal points within the Ministry of Public Health and Population (MoPHP), you will support the implementation, coordination and monitoring of activities aimed at integrating Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) components across MdM programmes.

## **What you’ll do**

? **MHPSS programme development and management**

- Lead the development, implementation and monitoring of the country MHPSS strategy and programme
- Ensure MHPSS activities are integrated into MdM-supported primary health care services and delivered in line with gender-sensitive and empowerment approaches
- Guarantee compliance with MdM and international MHPSS standards, and contribute to the development and review of training materials, SOPs, guidelines and reports in collaboration with the MHPSS Advisor
- Strengthen MHPSS referral pathways with partners and service providers, and support the mapping of needs, assessments and programme design to address identified gaps
- Ensure services remain culturally appropriate, responsive to changing contexts and emerging needs, and delivered according to quality standards
- Monitor programme implementation, budget utilisation and community-based MHPSS interventions

? **Capacity building and technical support**

- Participate in the recruitment, induction and onboarding of MHPSS staff, ensuring adequate orientation to MdM's MHPSS framework and tools
- Provide technical supervision and day-to-day support to MHPSS teams, including field-based officers, while contributing to performance management and staff development
- Develop and deliver capacity-building initiatives, including Training of Trainers (ToT) programmes on PFA, PM+ and other relevant MHPSS approaches
- Support the rollout of trainings for national staff and promote the integration of MHPSS standards across MdM teams

? **Coordination and representation**

- Foster close collaboration with health, protection and support teams to ensure integrated programme implementation
- Coordinate with local authorities, NGO partners, UN agencies and other stakeholders involved in MHPSS interventions within MdM areas of operation
- Represent MdM in relevant MHPSS coordination forums and technical working groups, contributing to information sharing, referral mechanisms, advocacy efforts and the promotion of good practices

? **Monitoring, reporting and evaluation**

- Oversee monitoring, evaluation and learning processes for MHPSS activities, including the development of tools, data collection and analysis
- Ensure regular review of programme performance and recommend corrective actions when required
- Act as the focal point for MHPSS reporting and contribute to donor reports, proposal development and fundraising efforts

## REQUIREMENTS

**You are the right match if you...**

- Hold a Master's degree in Psychology, Social Work, Public Health or a related field, complemented by training in MHPSS and project management
- Have proven experience managing MHPSS programmes in humanitarian settings, including programme design, quality assurance, monitoring and donor reporting
- Are confident integrating MHPSS into primary health care services and have a solid understanding of IASC and WHO MHPSS frameworks and interventions
- Can lead and support multidisciplinary teams, providing technical guidance, building capacities and fostering collaboration across locations and departments
- Are comfortable working with donors and budgets, and have experience developing proposals, reports and funding opportunities
- Excel at coordination and representation, building constructive relationships with authorities, partners, UN agencies and other stakeholders
- Combine strategic thinking with strong organisational skills, enabling you to adapt programmes to evolving humanitarian contexts and changing needs
- Communicate fluently in English, both verbally and in writing; knowledge of Arabic and experience in Yemen would be strong assets

**This role may not suit you if you...**

- Prefer working in highly predictable environments rather than responding to evolving humanitarian needs and priorities
- Are not comfortable balancing strategic leadership with hands-on technical support to field teams
- Find stakeholder engagement, coordination forums or external representation challenging
- Are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.  
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

## **EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS**

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: 3 392 €
- Fixed-term contract for 6 months starting in January 2027
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Sanaa but may be temporarily based in Aden depending on the security situation
- Regular field visits

**Benefits:**

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

**Essentials:**

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.  
If you are offically recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

title: Programs and Partnerships Coordinator / منسق البرامج والشراكات
body:
**Job Purpose:**

The Programs and Partnerships Coordinator is responsible for leading and coordinating the organization’s programs in Syria, while also developing and managing relationships with donors and local/international partners. This role aims to ensure efficient and effective program implementation, enhance funding and collaboration opportunities, and maintain compliance with donor requirements. The coordinator works closely with the Executive Director and senior management to achieve the organization’s strategic goals, while maintaining high standards of institutional performance and external communication.

**Duties & Responsibilities:**

**1. Program Management**

- Lead program strategy and develop integrated concepts within GAN’s sectors of work.
- Supervise Project Managers and ensure quality implementation and reporting.
- Prepare operational plans and monitor activities against budgets.
- Coordinate with finance teams to ensure budget compliance and adjustments as needed.
- Conduct regular field visits and submit reports to senior management.
- Develop and enforce program-related policies and procedures.

**2. Partnerships and Fundraising**

- Build strategic relationships with donors and partner organizations.
- Identify new funding opportunities and submit project proposals.
- Develop partnership management tools such as funding trackers, reporting calendars, templates, and compliance guidelines.
- Coordinate with technical teams to prepare high-quality proposals.
- Lead partnerships with Syrian NGOs, INGOs, and service providers.
- Maintain daily communication with partners and ensure smooth information flow.

**3. Representation and External Communication**

- Represent GAN in meetings, forums, and coordination bodies.
- Maintain strong relationships with government entities, donors, and other organizations.
- Support GAN’s external communication strategy and ensure updated media content.

**4. Team and Institutional Support Management**

- Oversee recruitment and training in coordination with HR.
- Ensure effective coordination among support departments (Finance, Logistics, Procurement, etc.).
- Develop capacity-building plans and improve institutional performance.

**5. Risk Management and Compliance**

- Regularly update the risk register and develop mitigation plans.
- Ensure program activities comply with donor policies and requirements.
- Contribute to contingency planning and ensure program readiness.

**Qualifications, Skills, and Experience**

- University degree in Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field; Master’s degree preferred.
- Minimum of 3 years of experience in program and partnership management within NGOs.
- Experience working with institutional donors (e.g., HF, DFID, ECHO, GIZ, UN agencies).
- Strong leadership, organizational, and team management skills.
- Excellent reporting and communication skills (written and verbal).
- Fluency in English (spoken and written); Turkish language is a plus.
- Ability to work under pressure and manage multiple tasks.

**الغرض الوظيفي**

يتولى منسق البرامج والشراكات مسؤولية قيادة وتنسيق برامج المنظمة داخل سوريا، وتطوير وإدارة علاقات الشراكة مع الجهات المانحة والمنظمات المحلية والدولية. يهدف هذا الدور إلى ضمان تنفيذ البرامج بكفاءة وفعالية، وتعزيز فرص التمويل والتعاون، وضمان التوافق مع متطلبات الجهات المانحة، مع الحفاظ على جودة عالية في الأداء المؤسسي والتواصل الخارجي. يعمل المنسق بشكل وثيق مع المدير التنفيذي وفريق الإدارة العليا لضمان تحقيق أهداف المنظمة الاستراتيجية.

المهام والمسؤوليات

**أولاً: إدارة البرامج**

قيادة استراتيجية البرامج وتطوير مفاهيم تكاملية ضمن القطاعات التي تعمل بها المنظمة

الإشراف على مديري المشاريع وضمان جودة التنفيذ والتقارير

إعداد الخطط التشغيلية ومتابعة تنفيذ الأنشطة مقابل الميزانيات

التنسيق مع الفرق المالية لضمان الالتزام بالميزانيات وتعديلها عند الحاجة

إجراء زيارات ميدانية دورية وتقديم تقارير للإدارة العليا

تطوير السياسات والإجراءات الخاصة بالبرامج وضمان تطبيقها

**ثانيًا: تطوير الشراكات والتمويل**

بناء علاقات استراتيجية مع الجهات المانحة والمؤسسات الشريكة

تحديد فرص التمويل الجديدة وتقديم مقترحات المشاريع

إعداد أدوات إدارة الشراكات مثل جداول التمويل والتقارير الزمنية والنماذج

التنسيق مع الفرق الفنية لتجهيز مقترحات عالية الجودة

قيادة الشراكات مع المنظمات السورية والدولية ومزودي الخدمات

متابعة التواصل اليومي مع الشركاء وضمان تدفق المعلومات بسلاسة

**ثالثًا: التمثيل والتواصل الخارجي**

تمثيل المنظمة في الاجتماعات والمنتديات والجهات التنسيقية

الحفاظ على علاقات قوية مع الجهات الحكومية والمانحين والمنظمات الأخرى

دعم استراتيجية الاتصال الخارجي للمنظمة وضمان تحديث المحتوى الإعلامي

**رابعًا: إدارة الفريق والدعم المؤسسي**

الإشراف على عمليات التوظيف والتدريب بالتنسيق مع قسم الموارد البشرية

ضمان التنسيق الفعال بين الأقسام الداعمة (المالية، اللوجستية، المشتريات...)

تطوير خطط بناء القدرات للفريق وتحسين الأداء المؤسسي

**خامسًا: إدارة المخاطر والامتثال**

تحديث سجل المخاطر بشكل دوري وتطوير خطط التخفيف

ضمان توافق الأنشطة مع سياسات الجهات المانحة ومتطلبات الامتثال

المساهمة في التخطيط للطوارئ وضمان جاهزية البرامج

**المؤهلات والمهارات والخبرة**

شهادة جامعية في إدارة الأعمال أو الهندسة أو مجال ذي صلة، ويفضل درجة الماجستير

خبرة لا تقل عن 3 سنوات في إدارة البرامج والشراكات في منظمات غير حكومية

خبرة في التعامل مع الجهات المانحة الدولية (مثل HF، DFID، ECHO، GIZ، UN)

مهارات قيادية وتنظيمية عالية، وقدرة على إدارة فرق متعددة

مهارات ممتازة في إعداد التقارير والتواصل الكتابي والشفهي

إجادة اللغة الإنجليزية تحدثًا وكتابة

قدرة على العمل تحت الضغط وتعدد المهام

title: Employment Specialist
body:
**Job Overview:**

The Employment Specialist helps newly arrived refugee clients achieve self-sufficiency through employment. This role delivers job readiness services, career coaching, and employer connections while supporting clients through the application and placement process. The Specialist maintains strong relationships with local employers, coordinates with other IRC staff, and ensures compliance with donor and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities may include, but are not limited to:

- Conduct intake and assessment for employment-eligible clients and develop individualized employment plans.
- Deliver job readiness orientations in both group and one-on-one settings, focusing on essential skills for employability.
- Cultivate and maintain relationships with area employers to identify appropriate opportunities for clients.
- Match clients to employment opportunities and guide them through applications, interviews, and hiring processes.
- Monitor job placements, wages, and satisfaction of both clients and employers, providing post-placement support.
- Assist clients with Unemployment Insurance applications and weekly claims when applicable.
- Maintain accurate case notes and data entry in required systems; prepare employment vouchers and other documentation.
- Participate in program meetings, trainings, and professional development activities; follow all IRC policies including safeguarding and confidentiality standards.
- Perform other related duties as assigned

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:**

- Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, workforce development, or related field strongly preferred; equivalent work experience may be considered.

**Work Experience:**

- At least 2 years of case management, employment, job placement, or business experience in a social services setting.
- Experience working with vulnerable or underserved populations strongly preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Knowledge of U.S. job search process and ability to coach clients through securing employment.
- Strong organizational and time-management skills; detail-oriented.
- Computer proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams).
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills; public speaking/presentation skills preferred.
- Proven ability to problem-solve, prioritize tasks, and meet goals independently or as part of a team.

**Language Skills:**

- Proficiency in English required; bilingual ability in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French, or other refugee/immigrant language preferred.

**Certificates or Licenses:**

- Valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, and access to reliable transportation.
- Must possess or be eligible for a fingerprint clearance card per Arizona state law.

**Working Environment*****:***

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.
- Must be able to lift 35 to 50 pounds (furniture, household supplies, and food boxes).

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $20.97/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Project Director - DRC Human Resources for Health (HRH)
body:
**Program:** Improve Human Resources for Health (HRH) through Implementing a Digital Health Worker Information System (iHRIS) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)

**Location:** Kinshasa, DRC (full-time, in-country)

**Reports to:** Sr. Program Manager (GST)

**Duration:** 36 months

**Please Note:** *This position is contingent upon award and donor approval. Start date will be determined upon award.*

**Overview:**

*Global Communities champions community-led solutions to complex challenges at the intersection of global health, humanitarian assistance, sustainable development, and financial inclusion. Together with our subsidiary IntraHealth International, we bring local and global insights together to save lives, expand opportunity, and build resilient health systems. We are the developer and global steward of iHRIS, the only free, open-source Human Resource Information System, used in more than 30 countries to manage over two million health worker records.*

Global Communities is seeking a full-time Project Director, based in Kinshasa, DRC, to lead a new project to improve health workforce planning, management, equity, and payment integrity in the DRC by establishing a government-owned, sustainable iHRIS. The project will support the Ministry of Public Health, Hygiene, and Social Welfare (MoH), the Agence Nationale d’Ingénierie Clinique (ANICNS), and other government stakeholders to design, implement, and institutionalize iHRIS in two provinces, interoperable with the national health worker payment system, as a model for scaling nationwide.

The Project Director will lead the change management in HRH and oversee all elements of the project, including providing strategic leadership and vision, guiding technical direction, ensuring financial and operational oversight, managing and mentoring the in-country team, and navigating a complex, multi-stakeholder political environment. Success requires strong political acumen, deep experience in health systems strengthening in the DRC, and the ability to build consensus across ministries, donors, and provincial authorities.

**Responsibilities:**

The Project Director is responsible for overall program implementation, strategic vision, and outcome achievement. The Project Director provides an integrated vision for the project and leads a team of senior staff and consultants to ensure the quality, timeliness, and efficiency of all products and activities. Specific responsibilities include the following:

**Strategic Leadership & Program Direction**

- Provide overall project leadership, strategic vision, and day-to-day direction, overseeing all technical, operational, and administrative elements of the project.
- Lead the co-design and co-creation process with government and other stakeholders to define system requirements, governance arrangements, and an iHRIS roadmap aligned with the MoH strategies.
- Apply adaptive, people-centered management and scaling approaches to build the conditions for improved HRH using iHRIS, sustainability, and scale from day one.
- Supervise, mentor, and manage the in-country team, including the Software Development Engineer, Capacity Strengthening Officer, and Finance & Administration Manager, and coordinate global technical support.

**Stakeholder Engagement & Change Management**

- Serve as the senior in-country representative for the project, building and sustaining strong relationships with the MoH, ANICNS, Ministère de la Fonction Publique, Ministries of Budget and Finance, provincial health authorities, the Central Bank, and other stakeholders.
- Oversee effective stakeholder engagement and change management in HRH, navigating a politically complex environment to build consensus, secure political backing, and drive sustained adoption of iHRIS.
- Convene and maintain a cross-government coordination structure and support the establishment of governance arrangements, MoUs, and accountability mechanisms across national and provincial levels.
- Coordinate with other key stakeholders, including donors, multi-lateral organizations, and other implementing partners.

**Technical Oversight**

- Support the review of human resources for health (HRH) and human resources management (HRM) policies and the implementation of consistent, transparent, and gender-equitable HRM practices across different levels of the health system.
- Build local capacity to use HRH data for decision-making and embed data use into routine HR practices, including workforce planning, deployment, supervision, gender analysis, equity, retention, and payment oversight.
- Oversee high-quality, evidence-based implementation across all project outcomes— assessment and co-creation, government accountability for iHRIS use, software development and payments interoperability, provincial implementation, and transition to scale.
- Ensure activities are aligned with national guidelines, WHO guidance, and donor requirements.

**Operational & Financial Management**

- Lead regular workplan, budget, and implementation reviews to ensure cost-effective and timely achievement of milestones, deliverables, and targets.
- Provide effective oversight of project operations, procurement, and partner management to ensure compliance and strong performance.
- Ensure sound financial management, documentation, and internal controls consistent with donor requirements and Global Communities policies.

**Monitoring, Evaluation, Learning & Sustainability**

- Support sustainability planning, including domestic financing, government ownership, hosting, and a structured transition of iHRIS operations to government stakeholders.
- Lead the project learning agenda and monitoring work, overseeing timely technical and financial reporting and ensuring accurate documentation of progress, achievements, and challenges.
- Capture lessons learned and translate evidence into actionable strategies, knowledge products, and recommendations to inform national scale-up and dissemination.

**Qualifications:**

**Minimum qualifications**

- Master’s degree or above in public health, health systems, human resources, international development, or a related field.
- A minimum of eight (8) years of professional experience including a demonstrated track record of leading projects of similar size, scope, and complexity, with strong strategic visioning and leadership capabilities.
- Strong expertise in health workforce management, human resources for health planning and data use.
- Experience in health systems strengthening in the DRC.
- Strong political acumen and demonstrated experience navigating complex systems, building consensus, and engaging government and donor stakeholders in the DRC.
- Skills in people-centered, adaptive management and supervision, with the ability to lead multi-disciplinary teams and drive results under deadlines.
- Fluency in French and English. Must have strong working proficiency in English (written and oral).

**Preferred qualifications**

- Experience implementing or managing health workforce information systems (e.g., iHRIS) or digital health / health information systems.
- Familiarity with health worker information systems, digital public infrastructure, and interoperability.
- Experience integrating gender equity into health workforce programming.
- Established relationships with the DRC government stakeholders.

**Global Communities’ Commitment**

*Global Communities positively welcomes and seeks applications from all sections of society. We are committed to a work environment that respects the dignity and worth of everyone and offers equal opportunity. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment.*

*Global Communities holds strict safeguarding principles and has a zero-tolerance policy for conduct of sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment. In the process of recruitment, selection, and appointment, Global Communities will conduct robust reference and background screening checks, including international vetting as a signatory of the Global Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, to ensure children and vulnerable adults are safeguarded and abuse is prevented. The incumbent is required to carry out their duties in accordance with Global Communities’ Safeguarding policy and Standards of Conduct.*

title: Senior Manager, Supply Chain Digitalization Benchmarking and Pilots
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Background/IRC Summary**

IRC is a co-lead of the Digitalization Thematic Working Group (TWG) of the Humanitarian Leadership Group on Supply Chain (HLGSC), alongside Help Logistics, data.org, World Economic Forum (WEF) and the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO). The TWG brings together 18 member organizations - UN agencies, INGOs, and local partners - to build a shared supply chain data governance framework, common data standards, and practical interoperability mechanisms across the humanitarian sector.

**Job Overview/Summary**

The TWG's work is organized around four results: a multi-stakeholder governance framework (Result 1), a common data standards and shared taxonomy (Result 2), a data-sharing and interoperability blueprint (Result 3), and a mapping of complementary initiatives already underway across the sector (Result 4). In the second half of the project, Results 1, 2, and 3 each move from design into live testing through a dedicated pilot: a governance pilot, a data standards pilot, and an interoperability pilot.

The Program Officer will lead the benchmarking work that underpins the data standards pilot and will support the design and delivery of all three pilots - governance, data standards, and interoperability -helping translate research and sector mapping into practical input for how each is built. This is a hands-on, delivery-focused role spanning three of the TWG's four workstreams, for someone who wants to help a sector-wide coalition move from agreement in principle to evidence in practice.

The position is funded through the HLGSC Digitalization TWG action (DG ECHO-funded), through project close in December 2027. The Program Officer, Supply Chain Digitalization Benchmarking and Pilots works closely with data.org, the TWG's facilitation partner, and reports to the Deputy Director for Business Development and Program Delivery within IRC's Global Supply Chain team.

**Major Responsibilities**

**Benchmarking (Result 2)**

- Lead benchmarking with the 3 TWG member organizations assessing their data systems against the TWG's agreed minimum viable data standards.
- Consolidate benchmarking results into a clear, decision-ready evidence base that directly informs the Result 2 data standards pilot.

**Pilot design, delivery & documentation (Results 1–3)**

- Support the design and launch of three pilots: a governance pilot (testing the endorsed governance framework, including rotating co-chair and decision procedures), a data standards pilot (testing the agreed taxonomy across benchmarked organizations), and an interoperability pilot (testing data-sharing and anonymization protocols across organizations at varying levels of digital maturity).
- Document each pilot as it unfolds, capturing lessons learned to support real-time, adaptive management.
- Author the pilot completion reports, prepared in a format agreed in advance with DG ECHO.
- Support identification of pilot opportunities under Result 3, working directly with participating organizations.

**Research translation (Result 4)**

- Translate findings from the Result 4 mapping report into concrete design inputs for the Results 1–3 pilots.

**Coordination & reporting**

- Participate in TWG meetings and relevant sub-group sessions.
- Provide regular progress updates to TWG co-leads.
- Help prepare materials for co-leads meetings and, where relevant, the HLGSC Coordination Board.

**Job Requirements**

**Education**

Bachelor's degree required in Supply Chain, Project Management, Data Science, International Development or related field required; Master's degree is an advantage.

**Work Experience**

3-6 years' experience in humanitarian supply chain, program monitoring and evaluation, or data systems work required, including direct responsibilities in pilot design or the testing of new operational mechanisms.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies**

**Required:**

- Strong project management skills, with the ability to keep multiple concurrent workstreams on track and within scope.
- Comfort working with data standards, benchmarking frameworks, or data governance concepts.
- Excellent written communication skills, with the ability to translate research and technical findings into clear, actionable recommendations for a non-technical audience.
- Demonstrated ability to work across multiple organizations and stakeholder groups.
- Fluency in English required; French or Arabic language skills is an advantage.

**Desirable:**

- Prior experience with data standards frameworks such as GS1 or UNSPSC.

**Working Environment**

Standard remote office environment. The TWG operates primarily through virtual engagement; occasional travel may be required for in-person convening.

title: Program Development and Award Advisor, Asia
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position will support business development and award management for institutional donors in the IRC’s Asia region, which includes programs in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Pakistan, and Thailand. Candidates who are from these countries and/or have significant experience in the region are strongly encouraged to apply. Candidates in IRC hub locations with overlapping time zones (London, Berlin, Nairobi) who have significant experience working in IRC Asia countries are also encouraged to apply.***

**Background**

Over the past 80 years, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has developed unparalleled expertise in responding to emergencies and helping uprooted communities to rebuild. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC’s mission is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster, including the climate crisis, to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. The IRC is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. In addition, through 28 regional offices in cities across the United States, the IRC also helps refugees resettle in the US. The IRC is committed to a culture of inclusivity and empowerment, humanitarian leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve.

**The Purpose of the Role**

The Program Development and Award Advisor (PDAA), Asia will support country programs to submit high-quality proposals, ensure compliance to donor rules and regulations and IRC systems and processes, lead on the review and submission of high-quality donor deliverables and ultimately support awards management in the Asia region. The PDAA also manages donor relationships with HQ donor counterparts as needed and advises country programs in relation to the implementation of IRC’s partnership management approach and system - the Partnership Excellence for Equality and Results (PEER) System.

The successful candidate will have a strong track record of working on humanitarian and international development programming with a range of multilateral and bilateral donors, as well as experience collaborating with local partner organisations.

The PDAA will support business development and award management for institutional donors in the IRC’s Asia region, which includes programs in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Pakistan, and Thailand. Candidates who are from these countries and/or have significant experience in the region are strongly encouraged to apply.

**Scope and Authority**

This position does not have any line management responsibilities.

**Working Locations**

This position is open for recruitment in Pakistan, Thailand, or other locations where IRC has an office presence. Candidates based in Asia are especially encouraged to apply.

**Key Working Relationships**

Reports to Director, Awards Management. Works closely with all Regional Program and Award Support team members, and across all teams within Awards Management Unit, Crisis Response Recovery and Development Department, Global Partnerships and Philanthropy, Global Supply Chain, Finance, Office of General Counsel, Technical Excellence, and other key departments within IRC. Donor and partner point of contact as applicable per region.

**Key Accountabilities:**

***Awards Management and Compliance***

- Manage a portfolio of awards for the Asia region. Main donors in portfolio will include USG, UN, GAC, World Bank, Australian DFAT, and Gulf donors, but may also include other donors as assigned.
- Review, provide substantive feedback and ensure timely submission of reports, collaborating with and ensuring input from relevant technical and financial staff.
- Guide country offices in partnership with other relevant departments in the design, production, and submission of and revise and quality assure award amendments and modifications.
- Serve as first point of contact for country program staff, to guide and advise country teams on all post-award issues and to act as a connecting point between country program and other HQ teams to facilitate the timely flow of key information between them.
- Review and lead negotiation of award agreements with donors, other IRC entities and partners according to IRC policies and internal processes.
- Guide and coach country offices in understanding policies, guidance and tools vis-à-vis working and managing local or international partners, ensuring that IRC’s PEER System is being followed and compliance rules from donors are cascaded to partners. Coordinate with compliance team as needed.
- Review and help processing sub-grants/partnership agreements in alignment with internal processes.
- Provide support to and monitoring of projects to ensure progress against objectives and compliance with donor guidelines and IRC internal requirements. Monitoring of awards can take the shape of monitoring visits, project implementation meetings and targeted calls following specific donor internal guidelines and IRC established processes.
- Provide technical advice to country offices on ad-hoc queries on donor compliance issues in coordination with the Compliance and Policy team on non-routine and high-level compliance matters and escalate to leadership for support as needed.
- Take part in regular meetings and calls with country teams to provide regular support and updates and collaborate closely on specific issues related to donor compliance, submissions and/or monitoring/award management.
- Ensure lessons learned from finalized projects are fed into the Business Development team.
- Stay informed about programmatic issues and security and political developments in the region and how they might affect program implementation.
- Advise and lead country programs appropriately to enable them to successfully follow internal IRC policies and procedures (e.g. OTIS, PEERS).
- Travel to provide additional support to or cover short-term gaps for awards and partnerships teams in the countries.
- Respond to data requests from other departments and accountability for portfolio-wide data needs.
- Coordinate with other members of the Program and Award Support Team and other AMU members for information sharing and to establish a coherent awards support.

***Proposal Development***

- In collaboration with the regional Business Development team, support business development in the region by providing effective proposal support, ranging from proposal management to comprehensive support and quality assurance.
- Provide quality assurance and quality compliance support on proposals, leading proposal development and coordination as needed. Ensure responsiveness to and compliance with solicitation documents and with IRC’s requirements.
- Review and advise on internal policy and donor requirements, budgets and supporting documentation for proposals in coordination with AMU and HQ Finance Department.
- Facilitate and/or participate in internal post-submission debrief sessions with country teams, technical units, regional team and other relevant stakeholders to collect lessons learned as needed.
- Maintain complete and accurate electronic files, including final submission packages and internal trackers, in coordination with the regional Business Development team.

***Donor Liaison and Representation***

- Manage donor relationships by maintaining communication on contractual issues, updates on program implementation and following up on compliance queries and securing changes and approvals as needed.
- Represent IRC externally at country/region-specific meetings, with donors and stakeholder networks.

***Capacity Building and Training***

- Support training of IRC in-country staff, as required and in coordination with PAS Leaders.
- In coordination with the DAM, develop and maintain work-processes and checklists for award implementation and report review, as well as record lessons learned.
- Support onboarding of country program Grants focal points and new Program and Award Support team to assigned donors, policies and/or IRC processes.

***Other Responsibilities***

- Contribute to AMU and regional strategic priorities and initiatives.
- Actively participate as a member of the Regional Team, engaging in strategy development and other initiatives as needed.
- Other duties as assigned by supervisor.

**Person Specifications**

**Essential**

***Skills, Knowledge and Qualifications:***

- Degree, preferably in a subject related to IRC’s work (International Relations, Refugee or Migration Studies, Development Studies, Public Policy) or equivalent experience
- Fluency in English, both spoken and written
- Experience with and a strong understanding of USG and UN donor requirements strongly preferred
- Understanding of other public donors is a plus
- Good understanding of humanitarian aid and development programming
- Ability to work collaboratively as part of a diverse team and handle a multifaceted workload
- Good financial management and budgeting skills
- Ability to analyze and synthesize information
- Proven organizational skills, detail-oriented, ability to prioritize tasks, and to learn quickly
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills: the ability to successfully and effectively liaise with people within and across departments in a multi-cultural environment.
- Ability to work independently in a very fast paced environment
- A flexible work attitude and a calm manner
- International work experience in the Global South is a plus
- Excellent IT skills (Word, Outlook, Excel)
- Ability to travel internationally, sometimes on short notice and to insecure areas

***Experience:***

- Experience in working at a distance and supporting field-based staff
- Experience writing, reviewing and editing narrative and financial reports and excellent attention to detail

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: MOZAMBIQUE - DEPUTY COUNTRY DIRECTOR PROGRAM (M/F) - PEMBA
body:
## About us

**Desired start date: ASAP**  
**Duration of the mission: 6 months**  
**Location: Pemba**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in some twenty countries, the SI teams – 2500 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

Solidarités International intervened in Mozambique in March 2019 for a few months following the passage of Cyclone Idai, which hit the Province of Sofala and the city of Beira hard. Operations were suspended after the emergency phase and the mission closed. The evolution of the situation in Cabo Delgado province, hit by several cyclones and severely affected by the violent actions of armed groups claiming to be IS, which caused the displacement of nearly 700 000 people, led to an assessment in May 2021 and to the reopening of the mission. The assessment carried out in the most affected district highlighted needs, particularly in the WASH sector, and the lack of emergency actors. The mission has opened in a complex security and administrative environment, where access is a major issue.

Solidarités International was one of the first INGO actors to respond to the growing crisis in Cabo Delgado, leading emergency response and distributions in hard-to-reach areas.

## About the job

**General objective:**

The Deputy CD for Programs (DCDP) ’s objectives are to provide leadership and management of the strategic programming, overseeing the strengthening of SI’s programs development, quality and accountability. The DCDP ensures the internal coherence between program activities and is responsible for ensuring that programs are driven by needs, based on evidence, adaptable to contextual changes and conflict sensitive, monitored closely and resourced appropriately.

**The main challenges:**

- Collaborate with the CD to implement the set country and program strategy.
- Support fundraising efforts and donor and partners’ relationship management and representation.
- Oversee Programme Development by providing cohesive leadership to SI programming, ensuring Support to program Coordination team and timely communication on program issues to the CD and HQ
- Provide guidance for the Quality management of the Programs by ensuring
- Quality Criteria and indicators are monitored and lead to decision making
- Ensure that procedures, guides and tools are updated and implemented in accordance with HQ recommendations.
- Support on lessons learning and using the findings to guide future strategic direction
- Being proactive in proposing New Activities based on the context evolution.

**Priorities for the 2/3 first months:**

- Prepare the proposals cycle of 2024 according to the 2022/2025 strategy developed
- Review the projects implemented during 2023 in order to draw the lesson learned and incorporate them into 2024 proposals
- Support the coordinators in strategy definition, implementation and in improving the quality of programming
- Support the implementation of the FSL strategy at mission level
- Review and strengthen SI emergency strategy set-up and mechanism in line with emergency fundings and in parallel to develop a strong second line response notably for returnees

## Your profile

**Education and experience background:**

- Master in humanitarian action, development, international law or any other technical area related to the humanitarian sector
- 3/4 years of experience in humanitarian sector.

**Technical skills :**

- Very good technical knowledge in project cycle management
- Very good strategic planning and coordination skills
- Ability to represent SI towards donors and partners

**Transversal skills :**

- Leadership and management
- Coordination with partners
- Planning and priorization

**Languages:**

- English (mandatory)
- Portuguese

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 3300 gross per month (EUR 3000 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

This position is based at the coordination office level in Pemba, offering an opportunity to work on a complex humanitarian emergency from a comfortable beach city. Pemba is a touristic city with beaches, several nice restaurants, and numerous grocery shops with imported goods.  
Visits to Mueda & Mocimboa will be required for supporting the team. Mueda has a market, a restaurant, and a bar; locally available ingredients are somewhat limited, but squid and fish, mangos (in season), and other seasonal items are readily available, with imported goods available to be sent up from Pemba.
