title: ESC Short-term Volunteering Greece (December-January)
body:
The organization was established in 2016 in response to the European refugee crisis and now manages cultural centers and residential programs for migrants and refugees in Spain and Greece. We are a small international team united by a commitment to breaking down barriers to social inclusion for migrants and refugees.

Our main projects in Greece include:

- Early childhood education center.
- Socio-educational activities with children and youth.
- Education activities for adults.
- Women Space.
- Transport and mobility projects to connect refugee camps to urban areas.
- European Union projects that foster social innovation and exchange of best practice.

For a period of **2 months**, starting in **early December 2026**, we are offering different volunteering positions within OCC Greece, focused on supporting the implementation of the projects in Polykastro.

**Main tasks**

Short-term volunteers will support and contribute to the implementation of one or more of the activities listed below:

- **Teaching for kids, youth or adults**: teaching English and/or Greek basic literacy to adult and/or minors.
- **Kindergarten**: working with minors of a really young age, organizing and implementing recreational activities around art, storytelling...
- **Women space**: organizing and implementing recreational/well-being activities for women and girls.
- **Monitoring and Evaluation**: administrative work for monitoring and evaluating our organization, in collaboration with the correspondent OCC manager.
- **Communications**: Use and editing of communications media via our communications equipment, administration of social media accounts, promotional campaigns, etc.
- **Bike Space:** technical support and administrative work in our bike rental service.
- **Computer/IT Classes**: teaching and promoting basic digital literacy skills i.e. use of Microsoft Office, setting up and email, etc to our beneficiaries’ community.
- **German Classes**: teaching German basic literacy to adults.

**Position requirements**

- Good command of English and/or Greek. Other languages are a plus (German, French, Arabic, Dari, Sorani, etc.).
- Experience with teaching and/or working with refugees is preferred.
- Being easy-going and eager to work in an intercultural, autonomous environment.
- Being motivated, proactive, open-minded, creative and self-reliant.
- Available for 2-month period starting early December.
- No problem with sharing an apartment/bedroom with other volunteers.

**Volunteer requirements established by ESC program (\*)**

- Candidates must be between 18 and 30 years old (preferably between 23 and 30).
- To have a legal residence permit in an EU country.

*(\*) Candidates that do not meet these requirements won't be able to be considered as potential candidates for the volunteer position.*

**What do we offer?**

The project is funded by the European Commission through the European Solidarity Corps program. This means that volunteering provides:

- **Travel costs coverage**: Up to the limits established in the Erasmus+ Guide distance calculator from the volunteer’s region of residency to our center, and back.
- **Free** **Accommodation:** Provided next to our activities center, in Polykastro, Greece with other volunteers. Houses are fully equipped (kitchen, bathrooms, washing machine, etc.). Note: be ready to share your bedroom with other volunteers of the same gender.
- **Monthly allowance:** 270 euros per month.
- **Insurance**: Henner
- **Free** **Language courses:** Online but also in person, according to availability.
- **Holidays:** two days per month.

title: RDC - DIRECTEUR.TRICE PAYS ADJOINT PROGRAMMES (H/F) - GOMA
body:
## Que faisons nous ...

**Date de début souhaitée: ASAP**

**Durée de la mission:** CDD, Durée : 12 mois

**Localisation**: Goma, RDC

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** est une association d’aide humanitaire internationale qui, depuis plus de 40 ans, porte secours aux populations victimes de conflits armés et de catastrophes naturelles en répondant aux besoins vitaux, boire, manger, s’abriter. Particulièrement engagée dans le combat contre les maladies liées à l’eau insalubre, première cause de mortalité au monde, SI met en œuvre par ses interventions une expertise dans le domaine de l’accès à l’eau potable, l’assainissement et la promotion de l’hygiène mais également dans celui, essentiel, de la sécurité alimentaire et moyen d’existence. Présentes dans plus de 20 pays, les équipes de SI, 2500 personnes au total, composées d’expatriés, de staffs nationaux, de permanents au siège, de quelques bénévoles…- interviennent avec professionnalisme et engagement dans le respect des cultures.

## La mission

Solidarités International intervient en RDC depuis 2001, afin de répondre aux besoins humanitaires des populations impactées par les conflits et les catastrophes naturelles et participer à la lutte contre les épidémies.  
La mission est active dans les domaines de la sécurité alimentaire et moyens d’existence (SAME), de l’eau hygiène et assainissement (EHA), et de l’assistance en transferts monétaires multisectoriels (cash direct ou coupons). Chacune des activités inclut une composante protection (transversale, ou « stand alone » via un partenaire d’implémentation). Les programmes couvrent la réponse d’urgence, via des programmes de réponse rapide (RRM) et de « deuxième ligne ». Toutefois, ils incluent également des activités de relèvement et de développement dans les zones stabilisées. Cette approche illustre la stratégie choisie par la mission, à savoir le maintien d’une capacité forte de réponse d’urgence tout en développant des solutions plus durables aux problématiques qui affectent les populations de l’est du pays.  
La mission est composée d’une coordination et de bases opérationnelles situées dans les provinces du Nord Kivu, Ituri et Sud Kivu. Dans le cadre de sa stratégie pluriannuelle, Solidarités International en RDC a l’ambition d’ouvrir de nouvelles sous-bases et de développer son portofolio programmatique. En 2026, le volume financier se situe à plus de 25M USD. Les équipes terrain mettent en oeuvre différents projets tout en menant des évaluations multisectorielles dans le but d'obtenir des financements additionnels et de poursuivre le soutien aux populations vulnérables.

La mission RDC emploie en moyenne 210 employés, dont 21 expatriés. Le département Programme au niveau de la coordination est composé: d'un Directeur Pays Adjoint aux Programmes, d'un Coordinateur SAME, d'un Coordinateur EHA, d'un Coordinateur MEAL. Le recrutement d'un adjoint Coo EHA est en cours de finalisation.

## Descriptif du poste

**OBJECTIF GENERAL**

Le/la Directeur.trice Pays Adjoint Programmes (DPAP) soutient la Directrice Pays (DP) dans la mise en oeuvre et le suivi de la stratégie programmatique ainsi que de l'engagement bailleurs. Il/elle est responsable du fonctionnement de l'ensemble des programmes et du contrôle des projets dans le respect des procédures internes et contractuelles ainsi que du suivi de la qualité de toute la programmation de SI en RDC. Il/elle coordonne l'équipe de coordination technique et s’assure du meilleur management et encadrement. Il/elle apporte les éléments programmatiques à la stratégie pays, en soutien au DP et peut soutenir la DP dans toutes les tâches inhérentes à sa fonction au besoin.

**ENJEUX ET DEFIS SPECIFIQUES**

\- SI souhaite rester un acteur majeur de la réponse d'urgence en RDC  
\- Positionnement stratégique sur la réponse d'urgence : en lien avec la négociation de l'accès humanitaire (mandat de SI : aller là où les autres ne vont pas) mais également prise en compte de la dimension intercommunautaire dans la stratégie d'intervention et de positionnement  
\- Augmentation du volume opérationnel : diversification des financements et extension des zones d'intervention  
\- Engagement bailleurs à assurer en continu avec une participation cohérente et une prise de hauteur de manière à alimenter les bailleurs avec des briefings sur la stratégie programmatique  
\- Developpement des activités de relèvement précoce (et possiblement développement)  
\- Continuer le suivi de qualité et aspects transversaux (compétences en protection mainstreaming, aspects environnementaux, genre etc.)  
\- Prise de hauteur concernant la stratégie programmatique (vision stratégique)  
\- Maîtrise de langue anglaise essentielle

**PRIORITE SUR LES 2/3 PREMIERS MOIS**

-S'imprégner de la stratégie programmatique pays qui sera déjà finalisée lors de la prise de poste  
-Assurer le suivi de mise en place des differents plans d'action des coordinateurs techniques dans le développement de la stratégie programmatique  
-Lead dans les groupes operationnels des consortia, par exemple SAFER (OCU)  
-Lead programmatique dans l'engagement bailleurs (visites, briefing en ligne, etc.), y compris tournée bailleurs à Kinshasa prévue au mois d'octobre  
-Lead programmatique lors de l'écriture des propositions de projet en coordination avec les coordinateurs techniques du departement  
-Suivi des chantiers mission en lien avec les coordianteurs techniques (Protection transversale, NEAT+...)  
-Assurer l'interim de la Directrice Pays pendant ses congés

**CONTRAINTES SECURITAIRES**

L'ensemble de l'Est de la RDC est catégorisé en zone de sécurité de niveau 4 et toutes les zones d'opération restent particulièrement volatiles. Pour ce qui est des contraintes sécuritaires majeures : 1. instabilité persistante de la zone liée à la présence et à l'activité de plusieurs groupes armés ; 2. contraintes logistiques dues à l'impraticabilité des routes, et nécessité d'accompagner le développement de la zone avec un renforcement de la structure logistique afin de réduire les risques sécuritaires lors des missions terrain ; 3. acceptance auprès des communautés généralement très bonne, mais nécessité de poursuivre l'engagement communautaire en continu afin de maintenir cette acceptance ; 4. désinformation médiatique constante qui peut accroître la psychose dans la zone et doit être diffusée rapidement ; 5. A cela s'ajoute l'actuelle épidémie de MVE qui sévit l'Est de la RDC, en particulier les trois provinces où SI est présent et opérationnel, avec des évidentes contraintes sécu/accès sur lesquelles les partenaires travaillent.

## Votre profil

Master en relations internationales, coopération au développement et action humanitaire, sciences politiques (ou équivalent)

Expérience dans le secteur humanitaire +5 ans

Expérience sur poste équivalent: 3-4 ans

1.Excellentes capactités de représentation et coordination dans les instances, auprès des bailleurs, communauté hum, consortia et clusters

2\. Excellente vision stratégique et bonne connaissance des mécanismes de réponse rapide

3\. Excellentes compétences en communication et en rédaction de différents documents

1\. Excellente capacité managériale

2\. Bonne capacité d'analyse de contexte et des besoins humanitaires

3.Très bonne connaissance des enjeux de redevabilité et protection transversale

1\. Français (MUST) - maîtrise

2\. Anglais (MUST) - très bonnes compétences

## SI vous offrira les conditions suivantes

**Un poste salarié :** Selon l'expérience, à partir de EUR 3300 bruts par mois (3000 salaire de base + 10% d'indemnité de congé annuel versée mensuellement) et un Per Diem mensuel de USD 800.

SI couvre également les frais de logement et les frais de déplacement entre le pays d'origine de l'expatrié et le lieu d'affectation.

**Breaks :** Pendant la mission, un système d'alternance entre travail et congés est mis en place à raison de 7 jours ouvrables tous les trois mois (avec USD 850 alloués par Solidarités International). A ces périodes de pause, s'ajoute un jour de repos supplémentaire par mois travaillé.

**Couverture sociale et médicale :** Les expatriés bénéficient d'une assurance qui rembourse tous les frais de santé (y compris les frais médicaux et chirurgicaux, les soins dentaires et ophtalmologiques, le rapatriement) et d'un système de prévoyance incluant les risques de guerre. Les frais de vaccination et de traitement antipaludéen indispensables sont remboursés.

**CONDITIONS DE VIE :**

- Logement dans des Guest House avec chambre et salle de bain privée.  
    Cuisiniers disponibles et accès à une nourriture relativement variée, de qualité et adaptable aux différents régimes.
- Certaines activités disponibles (restaurants et bars. Possibilité éventuelle de faire du sport).
- Règles sécuritaires évolutives suivant le contexte avec des couvre-feu qui changent en fonction de la zone.
- NB : à cause de l'épidémie MVE, certaines restrictions appliquent à l'heure actuelle en ville de Goma où le poste est basé. Toutefois, ces règles sont revues au fur et à mesure que la situation se stabilise.

title: Program Support Director - Francophone & Lusophone Africa
body:
This position is 100% remote. Candidates may work remotely from any of the following countries: Burundi, Chad, Benin, Madagascar, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Cote d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Kenya/Alliance locations, Malawi, Mozambique, Nigeria, South Africa, and Zambia. Candidates in West Africa are preferred.

The Program Support Director (PSD) is a senior leadership position within Ipas’s Global Program Support Team. The PSD serves as strategic thought partner to the Regional Directors (RDs), Country Directors (CDs) and other leaders across the Ipas network, helping strengthen organizational effectiveness, program quality, risk management and leadership capacity. The PSD provides strategic leadership, technical guidance, and operational oversight to 4–5 regional or country programs. This role supervises 3-5 direct reports which include CDs and RDs as well as Senior Program Managers (SPMs), who are part of the global Program Support Team. Reporting to the Deputy Chief Operating Officer (DCOO), the PSD ensures alignment with Ipas strategy and quality standards, donor and award compliance, and risk mitigation. The PSD serves as a bridge between Ipas global teams and regional / country offices, promoting cross learning and providing supportive supervision and thought partnership to country team leaders.

The PSD will bring significant team and program leadership experience, cross cultural knowledge, relevant language skills, a focus on user-centered approaches, and a dedication to shared leadership. The job responsibilities include working collaboratively with country program staff to ensure strong program results and strong project and risk management. The PSD provides high level stewardship and serve an “internal control” function with assigned regional and country programs, to ensure compliance with Ipas’s quality standards and as a steward of the Ipas’s global reputation. The position contributes significantly to addressing programmatic challenges and problem solving; ensuring we achieve desired goals, donor satisfaction and compliance with award terms and conditions, strengthening systems to improve value for money, organizational learning; and promoting a positive and empowering work culture.

The PSD has a strong commitment to reproductive justice and Ipas’s mission. Demonstrates a strong commitment to the individuals and communities we serve, acting with a sense of urgency and providing candid timely support and guidance to their team and peers.

Job Description

## **Primary Responsibilities:**

## Strategic Leadership

- Partner with regional and country leadership to advance organizational priorities, strengthen strategic decision-making, and promote alignment with Ipas's mission, values, strategic framework, global standards, policies and shared leadership practices.
- Support leaders in monitoring organizational, programmatic, and financial performance and in addressing emerging challenges, risks, and opportunities
- Participate in global strategic initiatives and other organizational development efforts to strengthen the Ipas Network, such as global strategic planning, expanding implementation of shared leadership practices and risk management.
- Represent Ipas on national or regional Boards of Directors, as needed.
- Support and provide thought leadership to regional and country leadership in translating organizational strategy into high-quality, contextually relevant program strategies.

## Program Quality, Stewardship and Support

- Provide high-level strategic inputs and assistance in project and program management with a focus on addressing challenges and problem solving with assigned regional and country teams.
- Facilitate periodic reviews with country and regional leaders to strengthen compliance, program quality, organizational learning, and accountability towards Ipas policies and quality standards, donor requirements, local laws and regulations, and standard accounting and business practices.
- Lead or support special assessments or learning initiatives, as needed.

## Regional and Country Program Support

- Serve as a trusted advisor to RDs and CDs, supporting leadership effectiveness, adaptive management, and cross-organizational collaboration
- Provide supportive supervision and thought partnership with RDs and CDs.
- Promote strong communication, collaboration, and cross learning among Ipas network technical and support units, and other country programs to strengthen programmatic and operational results.
- Support RDs, CDs and SPMs in addressing implementation challenges, risk management, and adaptive programming.
- Contribute to developing/updating and implementing strong regional/country strategic plans as requested, ensuring alignment with the Ipas mission and strategic framework.
- Provide coaching and support to RDs and CDs in recruiting and developing a high functioning team that practices shared leadership and maintains a positive and effective work culture.
- Provide strategic input on annual work plans, annual operating budgets, reports, and high-priority deliverables, as requested and needed.
- Oversee the strengthening of a variety of mechanisms to support a positive and effective work culture, organizational learning, sharing, and peer support across teams.
- Support start-up, scale-up, and close-out of country programs.

## Staff Management & Capacity Strengthening

- Foster a culture of shared leadership, accountability, learning, trust, and inclusion by empowering staff to contribute expertise, exercise leadership, and make informed decisions appropriate to their roles.
- Provide supportive supervision and manage the performance of direct reports, including RDs, CDs and Program Support Team staff.
- Support capacity strengthening of regional/country teams in program management, donor compliance and risk management.
- Promote organizational training and other capacity strengthening efforts as needed.

## Donor Engagement & Compliance

- Support RDs and CDs in managing complex donor-funded portfolios by strengthening systems, decision-making, compliance practices, and cross-node coordination.
- Ensure programs comply with donor requirements and organizational policies.
- Contribute to resource mobilization efforts by contributing to proposal development, donor briefings, and strategic partnerships as requested and needed.
- Work with program leaders to ensure that new business efforts and proposals are aligned with the country/region’s strategic plan, Ipas strategic framework, technical excellence and innovation, good stewardship of funding, and optimal cost recovery.
- Represent Ipas in donor meetings, technical forums, and external engagements as required.

## Risk Management & Safeguarding

- Ensure timely identification and mitigation of programmatic, operational, and reputational risks, working with country/regional program leaders.
- Promote safeguarding, protection from sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), and ethical programming across all supported programs.
- Conduct regular reviews and work with country / regional leaders to ensure adherence with organizational policies on safeguarding, gender equality, and inclusion.
- Guard Ipas interests and reputation through oversight on adherence to policies, performance against the annual operating budget, addressing audit findings and ethical issues, and compliance with donor requirements.
- Work closely with regional and country leaders and other Ipas units to ensure adequate internal controls to reduce the risk of fraud and mismanagement of funds;
- Play an internal control function where needed, such as to reduce perceived or actual conflicts of interest.

## Monitoring, Evaluation, Learning & Accountability (MEL)

- Promote strong monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning practices across assigned regional and country programs.
- Support the use of data for decision-making, learning, and program improvement.
- Encourage documentation of best practices, innovations, and lessons learned across all projects.

Minimum Requirements:

## Essential

- Commitment to sexual and reproductive health and rights, especially safe abortion and access to contraception, and an understanding of principles, policies, and best practices related to sexual and reproductive health, and related intersectionalities.
- Knowledge of the issues and context of women's sexual and reproductive health and rights in the Africa region, including demonstrated experience working with NGOs in Africa, preferably having worked in an Ipas implementing country in the West Africa region.
- Demonstrated commitment to shared leadership principles, with experience fostering distributed leadership, collaboration, accountability, and trust across geographically dispersed teams
- Proven ability to lead and motivate teams and create a positive work environment through supportive supervision, strong communication and teamwork, and shared leadership approaches, including demonstrated successes in program management, team leadership, strategic planning and problem solving.
- Proven ability to build and maintain positive working relationships with a variety of partners, including government officials, regional or global donors and partner organizations.
- Ability to work across cultures and manage complex relationships remotely.

## Minimum

- At least 15 years of increasing responsibility in non-profit leadership and program management in the international development or NGO-sector.
- Minimum of 7 years of senior program leadership experience overseeing multiple country programs and proven ability to provide strategic and technical leadership across diverse country contexts.
- Strong experience managing donor-funded programs (e.g., bilateral, multilateral, foundations) including budgetary management.
- Demonstrated experience supporting organizational risk management, compliance monitoring, and implementation of internal control systems
- Relevant post-graduate degree (e.g., MBA, MIA, MPH).
- Respect and credibility as an advocate for reproductive health and rights
- Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.
- Fluency in French required. Knowledge of Portuguese will be an added advantage and of other local languages will be an asset.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, Word, SharePoint, etc.

Travel Requirements:

Estimated 20%-25\*\*%\*\* time travel to regional and country programs and regional/global meetings.

Compensation for this position will be determined by the prevailing market rate in the employee's country and the applicable statutory laws, in addition to Ipas's own pay philosophy and other factors, such as the employee's experience level and expertise.

title: US Response Team Lead - Emergency Response Roster
body:
- **Job Purpose**
    
    CORE (Community Organized Relief Effort) is a crisis response organization that brings immediate aid and recovery to underserved communities across the globe. Our mission is simple: save lives and strengthen communities impacted by or vulnerable to crisis. Wherever the crisis is and whenever people are in need, we are there. CORE’s ability to impact communities is directly emboldened by each member of our staff and leadership.
    
    We are seeking experienced and mission-driven Response Team Leads to join our emergency response roster for limited-term deployments within the United States. This role leads CORE's response operations on the ground while serving as a key relationship builder — cultivating and managing institutional partnerships with emergency management agencies, VOAD networks, local governments, and community-based organizations. The Team Lead oversees site functions and programmatic teams (such as distribution, home repair, community hubs, or resource navigation), executes CORE's response strategy, and helps position CORE for funding and partnership opportunities across the domestic disaster landscape.
    
    The Team Lead acts as CORE's primary field leader and external representative, responsible for coordination, safety, quality control, and effective communication across all functions. They serve as the primary point of contact for government agencies, VOAD and coalition partners, local implementing partners, support agencies, and internal leadership throughout the response. This position requires exceptional leadership and relationship-building skills, decisiveness, and the ability to adapt under rapidly evolving conditions.
    
    **Roster work is available on an as-needed basis (it is not full-time or continuous).**
    
    Roster members may be activated based on needs arising from emergencies and must be prepared for rapid deployment, sometimes on short notice, for durations ranging from 2 to 10 weeks.
    
    Main Responsibilities
    
    **Institutional Partnerships and Relationship Building**
    
    
    - Serve as CORE's primary relationship holder with government emergency management agencies at the federal, state, and local levels (FEMA, state EMAs, county/municipal emergency management), building trust and positioning CORE as a go-to response partner.
    - Develop and sustain active membership and engagement with **VOAD networks** (National VOAD and relevant State VOADs) and other disaster coalitions, representing CORE in member meetings, committees, and working groups.
    - Cultivate partnerships with local governments, community-based organizations, faith-based networks, long-term recovery groups, and other implementing partners to expand CORE's reach and access.
    - Establish CORE's presence and credibility in new response geographies by proactively connecting with local and regional stakeholders ahead of and during deployments.
    - Represent CORE in EMA-led coordination structures, ESF (Emergency Support Function) briefings, and multi-agency coordination calls.
    
    **Funding and Business Development**
    
    
    - Identify, track, and pursue funding opportunities relevant to US disaster response, including government grants, foundation funding, and private donor opportunities.
    - Build relationships with institutional donors and funders active in the domestic disaster space, positioning CORE for both rapid-response and longer-term recovery funding.
    - Support the development of concept notes, proposals, and letters of intent in coordination with CORE's Development and Partnerships teams.
    - Monitor the funding landscape and flag emerging opportunities tied to declared disasters, anticipatory action, and recovery programming.
    
    **Project Leadership and Implementation**
    
    
    - Oversee the planning, execution, and real-time adjustment of emergency response programs, including but not limited to tarping, home repair, debris removal, WASH, case management, relief distributions, infrastructure repair, and community engagement.
    - Lead rapid and ongoing needs assessments to inform program strategy and prioritize interventions.
    - Ensure program activities are grounded in contextual analysis, community feedback, and operational feasibility.
    
    **Deployment and Operational Oversight**
    
    
    - Serve as CORE's senior-most representative in the field, providing strategic and operational leadership across all scopes of work.
    - Ensure quality, safety, and accountability standards are upheld across all response activities.
    - Represent CORE in coordination meetings with government agencies, humanitarian actors, and local partners.
    - Ensure compliance with internal protocols, donor requirements, and humanitarian standards.
    
    **Interdepartmental Coordination**
    
    
    - Facilitate coordination between field operations and HQ departments including Communications, Partnerships, Development, Finance, and Logistics.
    - Ensure timely flow of accurate data, narrative updates, and documentation for internal and external stakeholders.
    
    **Team Supervision and Training**
    
    
    - Supervise and support field-based staff, roster members, and volunteers across programmatic and operational roles.
    - Lead onboarding, mentoring, and just-in-time training for incoming team members.
    - Support the adaptation and dissemination of SOPs, assessment tools, and training materials specific to the deployment context.
    - Promote a culture of safety, inclusivity, and continuous learning among field teams.
    
    **Administrative and Reporting Duties**
    
    
    - Ensure accurate tracking of project outputs, deliverables, and key performance indicators.
    - Contribute to donor and HQ reporting, including situation reports, lessons learned, and end-of-deployment summaries.
    - Support documentation of program impact, gaps, and recommendations to inform transition to recovery and long-term programming.
    
    Scope and Travel
    
    
    - Supervises: Program Managers, Program Coordinators, Roster members, local hires, and/or volunteers assigned to specific projects
    - Travel nationwide to U.S.-based emergencies as assigned
    - Called upon with short notice for deployments of 2-12 weeks as needed
- Requirements
    - Relevant experience in emergency response, humanitarian aid, community development, or related fields.
    - A bachelor's degree is welcomed but not required—equivalent experience, including lived or professional experience in disaster-affected communities or crisis settings, is strongly valued.
    - Demonstrated ability to lead teams, manage projects, and work across diverse communities and partners during emergency or high-pressure situations.
    - Commitment to CORE's mission and a strong understanding of the challenges faced by underserved or crisis-impacted populations.
    - Proven experience in US emergency operations or volunteer management.
    - Excellent communication and coordination abilities, with experience working across multiple departments and teams.
    - Flexibility to deploy to various locations in response to disasters and humanitarian crises.
    - Minimum 3 years of professional experience in US emergency response, humanitarian aid, or related program implementation.
    - Prior experience leading teams or managing response projects in humanitarian contexts.
    - Familiarity with construction, distribution, CVA, or other sectoral experience is a plus.
    - Valid Driver’s License and clean driving history
    - Spanish or other secondary language proficiency preferred

title: Tupande Cashew Extension & Aggregation Officer (Fixed-term)
body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Kenya program, founded in 2006, operates under the local brand Tupande. Close to 500 staff in our Kakamega headquarters support 1,747 field staff and serve more than 1 million farmers. In Nairobi, around 50 staff support global functions like procurement, recruitment, government relations, and communications.

## About the Role

Seeking a hands-on Extension and Aggregation Officer to run a cashew buying centre and aggregate raw cashew nuts on Kenya's coast — building market access opportunities for smallholder farmers in a scaling program.

## Responsibilities

Manage the buying center:

- Operate it during scheduled hours.
- Keep it clean, organised, and secure.
- Handle, dry, and store RCN according to Tupande standard operating procedures.

Aggregate accurately and with integrity:

- Weigh RCN accurately.
- Quality control each purchase (sorting damaged, moldy, or poor-quality nuts).
- Process payments via FieldPro and ensure compliance (i.e., KRA/eTIMS).
- Escalate any disputes, discrepancies, or irregularities to your Supervisor immediately.

Support farmers in the field:

- Deliver agronomic training to farmers in your assigned location.
- Communicate purchase and quality requirements.
- Executive field visits and prepare field reports for your Supervisor.
- Coordinate with Tupande Agents and Zone Supervisors to mobilize farmers.

Collect accurate data:

- Interview farmers and brokers.
- Record data on time using provided digital tools (i.e., stock take, farmer/broker scouting).
- Escalate any data-quality issues to your Supervisor.

Coordinate logistics:

- Work with loaders, Tupande’s logistics team, and your Supervisor to schedule and execute RCN collection.

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You'll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You'll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

Required:

- Demonstrable prior experience with an agricultural, aggregation, trading, or comparable operations employer (verifiable references or employment record).
- Ability to read and write in English/local language and perform basic arithmetic.
- Demonstrated integrity and accountability in handling agricultural goods, weighing, and record-keeping.
- Fluency in Kiswahili and familiarity with local coastal language(s).
- Computer literacy and comfortable with tablet/smartphone data-collection tools.
- High attention to detail in quality control, record-keeping, and payment processing.
- Independent, proactive, problem-solving - comfortable operating with limited daily supervision.
- Willingness and ability to travel across the assigned area, and to do hands-on RCN handling.
- Strong connection to the local farming community

Nice to have:

- Prior experience in Cashew and/or the Coast
- Prior experience operating a buying or collection center
- Familiarity with Tupande

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Lamu, Kenya

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Contract Duration

8 months

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

## Application Deadline

10 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization's mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

title: Associate, Global Donation Operations
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Background:**

The External Relations (ER) department was created in February 2020 and is comprised of 3 main but complementary functional areas: Private Fundraising, Communications and Advocacy. The ER department is at the beginning stages of creating a new radical and ambitious strategy that will enhance IRC’s ability to ‘punch above its weight’ in private income, advocacy and brand awareness. The main objective of the department is to enable this organization of more than 12,000 staff to have the resources needed to continue serving 18 million people worldwide in places affected by war and disaster, shape the humanitarian sector by influencing key policies and reforms and build and grow IRC’s reputation.

**Job Overview:**

The Global Donation Operations (GDO) Associate is part of the team responsible for timely and efficient processing of donations; creating and maintaining accurate donation records; importing/exporting donation data; upholding donation data integrity through quality controls; and maintaining department protocols. The GDO team is flexible and responsive to the evolving expectations as our systems, and the teams we support, grow and evolve.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Batch, scan, process, and deposit daily donations (checks, credit cards, etc.);
- Create and update donation records;
- Review daily/weekly quality control reports and develop new reports as needed;
- Perform data hygiene tasks on a daily basis;
- Complete incoming department cases;
- Carry out data imports and exports from our various donation platforms;
- Work with our caging vendor to ensure smooth entry and processing of donations;
- Collaborate with our Supporter Care team to update matching and sustainer gifts per donor requests;
- Fulfill refund and chargeback requests as they are received;
- Maintain up-to-date knowledge of advancements in current and new technologies;
- Build reports to support overall fundraising objectives;
- Participate in special projects as needed

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Senior Manager, US Gift Processing  
**Position directly supervises:** N/A

**Other key internal and/or external contacts:**

***Internal:*** Colleagues in IRC Finance and fundraising departments; colleagues working in the areas of digital technology and global fundraising across External Relations

***External:*** Coordinate with third party mail processing vendor regularly, and other key Data & Analytics vendors

**Impact of work:**

Accurate donor and gift records are the cornerstone for reporting and forecasting and facilitates a better donor experience. This in turn supports the IRC’s ability to cultivate, solicit, and thank our donors.

**Job Requirements:**

***Work Experience:***

- Minimum: 2 years of clerical/admin support positions.
- Preferred: 2 years of work experience preferably in a fundraising, development operations, advancement services or customer service or related field, particularly in a non-profit environment.

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Accuracy and attention to detail a must; sensitivity when working with highly confidential information and ability to maintain complete discretion at all times.
- Excellent computer skills: facility with MS Word, Excel, and email/internet software.
- Solid organizational skills: the ability to work efficiently in a fast-paced, thorough, and collaborative environment and the ability to independently manage a multi-faceted workload and meet strict deadlines.
- Excellent oral and written communication and interpersonal skills: possess the ability to communicate and liaise effectively with colleagues and vendors and works well within a team environment.
- Ability to identify areas to increase efficiency of our systems.
- Proven ability to plan and manage a variety of projects and high work volume: must work well under pressure, prioritize, show flexibility, and solve problems creatively.

**Preferred:**

- Previous experience and understanding of fundraising and CRM management is helpful; Salesforce NPSP experience is preferred.
- Demonstrated skills for analyzing and interpreting data and systems: ability to identify areas to increase efficiency a plus.

**Working Environment:**

 Standard office work environment. Two days in office and three days work from home.

**Commitment to Diversity and Inclusivity:** IRC is committed to building a diverse organization and a climate of inclusivity. We strongly encourage applications from candidates who can demonstrate that they can contribute to this goal.

**US Benefits:**

We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days (depending on role and tenure), medical insurance starting at $145 per month, dental starting at $7 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare, childcare, and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with up to 4.5% immediately vested matching contribution, plus a 3-7% base IRC contribution (3 year vesting), disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

**Compensation:** ($23.50-$24.50). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Director of Research
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

The Airbel Impact Lab -- the International Rescue Committee's (IRC's) research and innovation team -- designs, tests, and scales life-changing, cost-effective solutions for people affected by conflict and disaster. By applying deep technical expertise and field experience with a range of skills from research to human-centered design, we take a multi-disciplinary approach to problem solving in humanitarian contexts. We are a leading contributor of impact evaluations and other research in humanitarian settings. Our portfolio consists of nearly 300 research and innovation projects across 40 countries; and we've collectively published over 150 journal articles in peer-reviewed publications on education, nutrition, violence prevention, health and economic programs. We use this research to increase the IRC's impact and to change the way humanitarian aid is delivered around the world.

The Director of Research will be a strategic and technical leader on conducting research to improve impact and scale across IRC programs and influence the humanitarian sector to take up research results and findings. They will continue to build organizational capacity and systems for research, drive ambitious research agendas across IRC technical sectors, and lead research teams and projects to answer the most pressing questions to improve humanitarian impact and scale.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Oversee research agendas and manage select research teams to deliver high quality research.**

- Provide oversight and strategic direction to research agendas across select outcome areas (e.g. health, climate and economic recovery and development and protection)
- Engage with IRC technical units and research teams to generate and use evidence to improve impact, equity, influence and scale across outcomes.
- Lead high performing research teams to develop research projects and deliver on ambitious workplans to carry out research agendas.
- Oversee workforce planning to deliver select research agendas and proactively identify and fill staffing gaps where needed.
- Cultivate and support passionate team members, creating a space of belonging, professional development, and research excellence across a geographically dispersed team.
- Oversee community of practice for research across IRC countries.

**Lead strategic, cross-sectoral research projects.**

- Lead flagship cross-sectoral strategic projects, driving evidence generation for scale.
- Identify and shape new cross-sectoral research and funding opportunities that advance IRC's Impact at Scale priorities.
- Serve as PI on key research projects, generating evidence on high impact humanitarian solutions and advancing cutting edge methods in humanitarian settings.

**Strengthen organizational systems to carry out high quality, ethical analysis making responsible use of data .**

- Serve as IRC's Institutional Review Board Chair. Support teams to maintain high ethical standards in research.
- Drive adoption of AI and data science tools across the research lifecycle -- design, data collection, cleaning, analysis, and dissemination -- to increase the speed and rigor of evidence generation.
- Support country and regional program teams to streamline and carry out high quality data collection for research priorities.
- Strengthen and continuously improve our research systems, including standards and support for high quality data collection, cleaning, coding, analysis, writing and dissemination, including to participants and communities involved in research.
- Strengthen systems for data storage, cleaning, sharing and analysis, as well as for version control and reproducibility.

**Develop strong partnerships and represent research internally and externally.**

- Develop and maintain effective partnerships for research priorities at country, regional and global level that will amplify IRC's ability to generate evidence and influence targeted policy and practice.
- Present, publish and represent IRC research and innovation at events and meetings to influence key stakeholders.
- Cultivate strong relationships across departments within IRC. Represent the Airbel Impact Lab with senior leaders across the organization.
- Collaborate with Technical Units, Communications and Advocacy on strong research communications to key audiences.

**Fundraise and ensure strong financial management of research team.**

- Raise funds needed to support IRC's research agenda and research systems.
- Oversee budgets and the financial health of select research teams, initiatives and projects. Identify and communicate gaps or concerns in a timely manner, and proactively seek out viable solutions.

**Job Requirements:**

- **Education:** Ph.D. in field related to development and humanitarian intervention (e.g., economics, epidemiology, political science).
- **Work Experience:** 10+ years in research, with significant experience in humanitarian or development contexts.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Extensive experience in designing research and managing research teams in low resource environments.
- Fluency in translating the use of empirical evidence to support technical and implementing teams to know what works best to achieve meaningful results for people.
- Demonstrated fluency with AI- and data-science-enabled research methods, and a track record of using them to modernize or accelerate research processes.
- Demonstrated success in business development for research projects with public and private donors.
- Experience developing and driving research strategy and learning agendas across a large, complex international organization.
- Strong record of publication and authorship/co-authorship of peer-reviewed articles.
- An existing and strong professional network in humanitarian and development research communities.
- Very strong leadership and management competencies including the ability to bring people from diverse backgrounds along with a stated vision and strategy, and capacity to communicate effectively with IRC leadership, technical peers, and colleagues in fundraising, communications and advocacy.
- Excellent public speaking and writing skills.

**Language Skills**: Fluency in English is required; Proficiency in French, Arabic or Spanish is a plus.

**Working Environment:**

Travel up to 25% of the time

**Compensation USA :** ($165,000–$185,000). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Compensation UK:** (GBP 80,502–GBP91,872). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Medical coordinator (F/M) - Yemen
body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?  
For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

**MdM in Yemen**

Yemen remains one of the world's most severe humanitarian crises, after more than a decade of conflict, economic decline, climate shocks, and political instability. In 2026, over two-thirds of the population require humanitarian assistance, including 9.4 million people identified as most in need of life-saving support.

The health system is under extreme strain, with only 59.3% of health facilities fully operational and 19.3 million people requiring healthcare services, including more than 660,000 pregnant women in need of urgent care. Cholera continues to pose a major public health challenge, adding pressure to an already weakened system.

The operational environment remains highly volatile, marked by security incidents, service disruptions, funding cuts, and economic challenges that regularly affect humanitarian activities.

Médecins du Monde operates across northern and southern Yemen, with a coordination office in Sana’a and field offices in Aden and Marib. Its interventions focus on two strategic priorities:

- Supporting 29 health facilities to deliver primary healthcare services, including outpatient care, vaccination, nutrition, and reproductive health.
- Providing mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) through healthcare facilities and community-based networks trained in identification, referral, and awareness-raising activities.

**About the role**

You will be responsible for designing, implementing, adapting and reporting the quality medical program activities for the Yemen mission. You will ensure the relevance and quality delivery of all medical activities, and practices, with a particular focus on health data analysis. You are the technical supervisor for the medical team (MdM or implementing partners) within the mission.

You will take part in the country strategy elaboration for the medical sector led by the general coordinator.

**Who you’ll work with**

Under the supervision of the General coordinator, you will work alongside the deputy general coordinator, the HQ desk officer, the HQ medical, mental health, and protection advisors/referents. You will be the technical supervisor for the medical team: health activity managers, Marib medical supervisor and pharmacy advisor.

**What you’ll do**

Under the supervision of the General coordinator, your main responsibilities are the following:

- Participate in the definition of the country strategy led by the general coordinator and drive the medical and technical aspects in the development of this strategy
- Design, plan, implement, adapt and monitor the programme’s health activities
- Ensure the quality and relevance of health activities, supervise the collection and analysis of medical data
- Recruit, manage, train, and motivate the medical team
- Ensure the management of pharmaceutical products
- Carry out health needs assessments and evaluations of medical partners
- Cooperate with the administration team regarding budgeting and supervise the medical purchase process
- Represent MdM with authorities, partners and other NGOs on health issues
- Participate in the writing of proposals and reports

## REQUIREMENTS

**You are the right match if you...**

- Hold an MD qualification or an advanced degree in Public Health, Nursing, Midwifery, or another relevant health discipline. Additional training in public health, epidemiology, project management, or humanitarian programme management is a strong asset
- Have proven experience in humanitarian and/or development contexts, with at least 2 years in a similar role involving programme development, proposal writing, donor reporting, budget management, and donor compliance
- Demonstrate strong technical knowledge in nutrition and sexual and reproductive health and rights, combined with a solid understanding of results-based management approaches, logical frameworks, and strategic planning
- Are skilled in developing high-quality funding proposals, technical reports, and impact narratives in English, and have experience working with institutional donors and multi-donor funding mechanisms
- Combine strong analytical, organisational, and coordination skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities, work autonomously, build capacity within teams, and collaborate effectively in multicultural environments
- Speak English fluently. Arabic is highly appreciated.

**This role may not suit you if you...**

- Are uncomfortable working in complex, unstable, or rapidly evolving humanitarian contexts that require flexibility, resilience, and adaptability
- Prefer close supervision and highly structured processes rather than taking initiative, anticipating needs, and working independently
- Do not have strong written English skills or experience producing donor proposals, narrative reports, and other high-quality programme documentation
- Are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.  
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

## **EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS** 

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: 3 663 €
- Fixed-term contract for 6 months starting in December 2026
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Sanaa but may be temporarily based in Aden depending on the security situation
- Regular field visits

**Benefits:**

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

**Essentials:**

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.  
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

title: HR Systems Analyst (Security & Integrations)
body:
**Background/IRC Summary:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries and 22 U.S. cities, we restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. The IRC leads the way from harm to home.

This position will be located in Nairobi, Kenya. - TBC

**Job Overview/Summary:**

The HR Systems Analyst (Security & Integrations) owns the functional design, build, and maintenance of Workday's integration layer and security configuration in support of all Workday users. This role is responsible for designing, testing, and hardening integrations between Workday and downstream systems, and for configuring Workday's security groups and policies in line with IRC's data classification standard. The role also builds rule-based automation for high-volume, structured P&C processes, and escalates complex, cross-functional design decisions to the Global HR Systems Product Manager.

This position requires hands-on experience with Workday integration tools (EIB, Core Connectors, Studio, and ideally Orchestrate) and a working understanding of Workday's security framework.

**Key Responsibilities:**

- Design, build, test, and maintain Workday integrations using EIB, Core Connectors, Studio, and Orchestrate to connect Workday with payroll, benefits providers, and other third-party systems
- Own the functional design process for Workday security and integrations, escalating complex cross-functional decisions to the Global HR Systems Product Manager
- Configure and maintain Workday security groups, business process security policies, and domain security policies aligned to IRC's data classification standard
- Build and maintain rule-based automation for high-volume, structured processes (bulk data loads, account provisioning, permissions, location and hierarchy setup) using Orchestrate and EIBs.
- Proactively monitor integration health, troubleshoot failures, and resolve root-cause issues ahead of ticket escalation
- Test and validate integrations and security configurations during Workday releases and functional area changes
- Gather requirements from HR and non-HR partners; map data elements as needed
- Collaborate with HRIS colleagues, Payroll, Finance, and IT to identify opportunities for process improvement and efficiency within IRC's current Workday usage, including cross-functional considerations
- Produce reporting and dashboards related to integration performance and security compliance
- Perform other special projects as needed

**Key Working Relationships:**

Position Reports to: Global HR Systems Product Manager

Position directly supervises: n/a

Indirect Reporting: n/a

Internal: Human Resources, Payroll, Finance, IT, Information Security

External: Workday, Cornerstone, ADP, and other third-party vendors

**Job Requirements:**

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent with 4+ years of professional experience managing data sharing/integrations between enterprise software applications
- Hands-on experience building and maintaining Workday integrations using EIB, Core Connectors, and Workday Studio; working knowledge of Workday Orchestrate a strong plus
- Working understanding of Workday's security framework: security groups, domain and business process security policies
- Working knowledge of data security/classification frameworks (e.g., GDPR or equivalent)
- Experience working with large datasets, in-depth understanding of data relationships, and data cleansing practices
- Intermediate understanding of relational database concepts
- Exceptional problem-solving skills with attention to detail, excellent time management, organizational skills, and ability to prioritize work
- Self-motivated with the ability to work both independently and in a team environment
- Excellent customer service, communication (written and verbal), and cross-group collaboration skills required
- Flexibility in daily schedule, and ability to understand and react quickly to changing priorities
- Experience working in a globally distributed environment a plus
- Experience working with a helpdesk ticketing system a plus

**Preferred Additional Qualifications**

- Workday Pro certification in Integrations or Security a strong plus
- Experience with an international nonprofit in the delivery of systems across varying IT infrastructure and low/intermittent bandwidth scenarios
- Experience with data migration and systems integration projects

**Working Environment:**

Standard office work environment with the ability to work a hybrid office/remote schedule.

The IRC and IRC workers must adhere to the values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. These are Integrity, Service, and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Beneficiary Protection from Exploitation and Abuse, Child Safeguarding, Anti Workplace Harassment, Fiscal Integrity, and Anti-Retaliation.

IRC et les employés de IRC doivent adhérer aux valeurs et principes contenus dans le IRC WAY (normes de conduite professionnelle). Ce sont l'Intégrité, le Service, et la Responsabilité. En conformité avec ces valeurs, IRC opère et fait respecter les politiques sur la protection des bénéficiaires contre l'exploitation et les abus, la protection de l'enfant, le harcèlement sur les lieux de travail, l'intégrité financière, et les représailles.

title: Fertilizer Procurement Associate
body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

## **About the Role**

Seeking a procurement professional to lead fertilizer procurement, ensuring cost-efficient sourcing and reliable on-time delivery. Drive strong individual execution and contribute to team success. In this role, your focus will be dedicated to deep-dive data analysis to determine optimal purchasing windows, and managing and executing the entire procurement process independently.

## **Responsibilities**

Execute Procurement with Excellence

- Strategy & Delivery: Support the creation and execution of seasonal procurement strategies to deliver +90% OTIF (On-Time, In-Full) delivery, market-competitive costs, and 5% year-on-year cost savings.
- Quality Assurance: Ensure absolute quality control, achieving 0 quality issues reaching the farmer, and maintain an +80% on-time payment rate for suppliers.
- Supply Chain Reliability: Proactively address future supply gaps by evaluating farmer needs against global market trends, supplier capacity, and current inventory levels.
- Process Optimization: Drive lead-time improvements through streamlined delivery and process automation. Regularly improve key operations like the goods receipt process and loading quality control.
- Data & Analytics: Spend time developing, maintaining, and continuously improving complex Google Sheets data models to track global market trends and landed costs. Use this data to provide crucial decision support on when to purchase (or not purchase) fertilizers to maximize cost savings.

Build Partnerships & Market Liaisons

- Strategic Relationships: Help build and maintain deep partnerships with fertilizer suppliers and industry organizations beyond seasonal procurement needs.
- Country Team Collaboration: Act as a critical business partner for our country operations teams, actively identifying and sharing opportunities to improve our offering to farmers.
- Industry Representation: Serve as a representative for One Acre Fund externally with suppliers and market actors to drive long-term, systematic supply chain improvements.

People Management

- People Management: Manage and mentor a small team, setting clear goals, providing timely feedback, and conducting high-quality career coaching and performance reviews.
- Team Growth:Contribute to staffing, recruitment, and succession planning to build a high-performing procurement unit.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

Professional & Technical Competencies:

- Supply Chain Expertise: Solid foundational knowledge of global procurement processes, international shipping, and supply chain operations.
- Data Fluency: An advanced analytical mindset with high proficiency in Google Sheets to build pricing, forecasting, and decision-support models. Comfortable spending half of your time analyzing data to help make decisions.
- Language: Fluency in written and spoken English is required.

Management & Execution Skills:

- Relationship Builder: Exceptional collaboration and negotiation skills, with the ability to influence both internal stakeholders and external global suppliers.
- Project Management: Strong organizational skills with a proven track record of managing multiple projects simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.
- Solution-Oriented: An innovative thinker who approaches obstacles with a results-driven mindset and is comfortable making data-driven decisions under medium-risk conditions.

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Nairobi, Kenya

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

## **Eligibility**

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

## **Application Deadline**

16 October 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

title: ADJOINTE OU ADJOINT COORDINATEUR OU COORDINATRICE RMM-TCHAD
body:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Rattaché.e au Coordinateur Mécanisme de réponse rapide, ce poste a pour objectif de renforcer les capacités d'analyse du consortium RRM en structurant les Systèmes de Gestion de l'Information et en développant une composante relative aux Systèmes d'Information Géographiques. Vous serez en charge plus spécifiquement de:  
La gestion et l'analyse des données  
Le développement des solutions de visualisation et de reporting sous Power BI  
La cartographie et SIG  
Le reportng et la diffusion de l'information  
la coordination et le renforcement de capacités

  
Profile :

 Titulaire d'un diplôme Bac+4/5 en géographie, géomatique, SIG, statistiques, data science, informatique décisionnelle, gestion de l'information humanitaire ou domaine équivalent, vous disposez d'une solide expertise en gestion et analyse de données.  
Vous matrisez les outils de collecte et de traitement de données (Excel avancé, SQL, KoboCollect, ODK) et idéalement DHIS2. Une expertise confirmée en Business Intelligence est requise, notamment sur Power BI, Power Query, DAX, la modélisation de données et l'automatisation des reportings.  
Une connaissance des outils de cartographie et systèmes d'information géographique (ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, QGIS) constitue un atout important, ainsi qu'une expérience en analyse spatiale, géoréférencement et web mapping.  
Vous êtes reconnu pour votre capacité à produire des tableaux de bord, infographies et supports visuels de haute qualité, adaptés à des besoins décisionnels ou opérationnels.  
Enfin, des compétences en analyse statistique et l'utilisation d'outils tels que SPSS, R ou Python sont appréciées.  
.

title: Head of support services (F/M) - Lebanon
body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?

For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

## **MdM in Lebanon**

MdM has been working in Lebanon for 30 years and actively contributed to respond to needs of the most vulnerable communities as the context unfolded (2011 Syrian crisis, 2019 severe economic crisis, 2020 Beirut Blast) and the current period since October 7th, 2023 – especially as the war resumed in Lebanon since March 2nd, 2026.

MdM’s intervention in Lebanon aims to strengthen the national health system and increase access to quality healthcare.

MdM is recognized in Lebanon as a major actor in the areas of mental health (MHPSS) and sexual and reproductive health (SRH). MdM supports several health centers and mobile clinics in the South, Beirut Mount Lebanon, Bekaa, and Baalbek Hermel; and works with other partners.

Despite the June 2026 ceasefire, the situation remains highly volatile and high needs remain, particularly in the South of the country. MdM continues to closely monitor the situation to ensure an appropriate, timely and flexible intervention, always in line with the needs of the various conflict-affected populations.

## **About the role**

You are responsible for the overall strategy and compliance, through the management of logistics, human resources and finance departments in the MdM Lebanon mission.

You ensure support services are fully compliant with MdM policies, donor requirements, national authorities' regulations, and applicable legislation.

## **Who you’ll work with**

Under the line management of the General coordinator, and the technical management of the Desk manager, you work in close collaboration with the other departments: Program, Medical/MHPSS, Grants, Security-Safety-Access, MEAL.

## **What you’ll do**

**Support services leadership & strategic planning**

- Provide strategic leadership and guidance to the General Coordinator and Country Management Team on all support-related matters
- Contribute to country strategy development, annual planning and financial planning processes
- Lead support services planning and ensure alignment between operational and programme priorities
- Anticipate operational challenges and oversee contingency planning to ensure humanitarian response continuity

**Development & reporting**

- Ensure support functions contribute effectively to proposal development, reporting and donor-related processes
- Coordinate the timely provision of analyses and support inputs required for programme development and decision-making

**Support services management & quality**

- Oversee the quality, compliance and performance of all support functions in accordance with organizational policies, donor requirements and local regulations
- Ensure sound resource management, accountability and legal compliance across the mission
- Monitor support systems, identify risks and corrective actions, and strengthen tools and procedures to support informed decision-making
- Promote effective integration and collaboration between Finance, HR, Logistics and programme teams

**Risk management, compliance & internal control**

- Strengthen internal control systems and ensure appropriate management of mission resources
- Identify and mitigate financial, operational, compliance, safeguarding, fraud and corruption risks
- Lead or coordinate audits, investigations and follow up on recommendations in collaboration with relevant stakeholders
- Promote adherence to anti-fraud, anti-corruption and safeguarding policies across the mission

**Team management & capacity building**

- Recruit, manage and develop the support services team through coaching, performance management and capacity-building initiatives
- Foster effective coordination, communication and information sharing across teams
- Identify learning and development needs and ensure access to appropriate technical support and resources

**Coordination & representation**
