title: Responsable Adjoint·e – Recrutement et Mobilité – SIEGE- basé à FRA-Asnieres-sur-Seine
body:
## **Contrat à durée déterminée (CDD) de 6 mois à compter du 16/11/2026**

## **Deadline for application : 09/10/2026**

## **PUI aux quatre coins du monde**

**Forte de ses 40 années d’expérience, Première Urgence Internationale :**

Vient en aide à près de **6** millions de bénéficiaires

Avec un budget de plus de **100** Millions € par an

Répartis dans **24** pays, sur **5** continents

Grâce à l’implication et l’engagement de :

- Plus de **2500**collaborateurs nationaux
- Environ **225** expatriés de 50 nationalités différentes
- Et **120** salariés au siège

PUI œuvre dans 10 secteurs d’intervention et se distingue par la mise en place d’une approche intégrée dans sa réponse. Cette méthode vise à identifier et comprendre l’ensemble des besoins des personnes touchées par une crise. Nos équipes se mobilisent pour apporter une réponse globale à l’ensemble des besoins fondamentaux des populations victimes de crises humanitaires dans l’urgence jusqu’à leur permettre de retrouver autonomie et dignité.

Pour en savoir plus sur [notre histoire](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/notre-histoire/), [nos valeurs](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/notre-valeurs/), [nos domaines d’intervention.](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/nos-domaines-d-intervention/)

## **Zoom sur le Service Recrutement et Développement des Compétences**

La branche Recrutement et Mobilité (R&M), intégrée à la Direction des Ressources Humaines et au Service Recrutement et Développement des Compétences, créé en 2024 au sein de Première Urgence Internationale, contribue à structurer et accompagner les parcours professionnels et les besoins en recrutement de l’organisation. Elle est composée de 5 Chargés de Recrutement et Mobilité, qui assurent la mise en œuvre des processus de recrutement, de mobilité interne et d’accompagnement des parcours.

## **Et le Responsable Adjoint·e – Recrutement et Mobilité dans tout ça?**

**En tant que Responsable Adjoint·e – Recrutement et Mobilité, sous la supervision du Responsable Recrutement & Développement des Compétences, vous serez le manager de l’équipe Recrutement & Mobilité.**

A cet effet, vos responsabilités seront les suivantes :

- Management : vous serez responsable du recrutement, de l’accompagnement et du suivi de l’équipe Recrutement & Mobilité (5 personnes), vous contribuerez aux plans d’action en cohérence avec la stratégie pluriannuelle et piloterez leur déploiement.
- Recrutement et mobilité : vous managerez l’activité de l’équipe Recrutement & Mobilité, organisée par filière métier.
- Renforcement des capacités : vous serez en charge de la montée en compétences en termes de recrutement pour l’ensemble des acteurs RH et non RH, vous participerez à la définition de formations par filière métier, en coordination avec l’équipe Formation et Développement des Compétences.
- Relations extérieures et communication RH : vous participerez au développement de la Marque Employeur de l’Association, vous piloterez les relations avec les écoles et travaillerez en lien avec l’équipe communication.
- Développement des procédures et outils : en matière de recrutement, d’intégration, de gestion de vivier et de la mobilité, vous contribuerez à la mise en œuvre de politiques RH innovantes pour améliorer nos pratiques internes.

## **Les défis qui vous attendent :**

Ce poste joue un rôle central dans la performance et l’évolution du recrutement international de l’association. Il s’agit d’accompagner et de faire grandir le Chargé de Recrutement tout en garantissant la qualité et l’efficacité des processus. Le poste doit également permettre d’anticiper les besoins en talents, notamment sur les profils stratégiques et lors des périodes de forte activité. Il contribue à faire évoluer les pratiques, outils et politiques de recrutement pour répondre aux enjeux futurs. Il participe enfin au renforcement de la Marque Employeur et de l’attractivité de PUI, en développant les réseaux et les partenariats. Un rôle à la fois managérial, stratégique et opérationnel, au cœur des enjeux RH de l’association.

## **Ce qu’il vous faudra pour réussir**

- **Formation**

Vous pouvez justifier d’un diplôme supérieur (Master 2 ou équivalent) en Ressources Humaines.

- **Expérience**

Vous êtes fort d’une expérience d’au moins 5 ans en Recrutement et Mobilité, en ONG internationale (terrain et/ou siège) ainsi qu’en management. C’est indispensable pour ce poste !

- **Compétences**

Vous disposez de solides connaissances en recrutement, et gestion de la mobilité ? Ce poste est fait pour vous !

- **Qualités requises**

Vous montrez un excellent relationnel, une facilité de communication, tant à l’écrit qu’à l’oral, et de bonnes capacités de négociation. Vous êtes force de proposition, faites preuve d’une grande rigueur, d’organisation, d’empathie et de curiosité. Vous avez le goût du travail en équipe ainsi qu’une bonne résistance au stress.

- **Langues**

Vous parlez le français et l’anglais couramment ? Tant mieux, c’est indispensable pour ce poste ! La maitrise de l’espagnol sera également appréciée.

## **Le mot du manager**

*« Rejoignez Première Urgence Internationale et prenez part à un poste au cœur des enjeux de recrutement et de développement des talents. Vous piloterez des recrutements internationaux à fort impact, contribuerez à faire évoluer nos pratiques et nos outils RH, développerez notre Marque Employeur et accompagnerez les Chargées de Recrutement au quotidien. Un rôle responsabilisant, varié et stratégique, au sein d’une équipe engagée et au service d’une mission humanitaire concrète. »*

## **PUI vous proposera**

- \*\*Statut :\*\*Cadre
- **Salaire : 3500 euros**
- **Couverture médicale : 100**% de la mutuelle Santé et Prévoyance
- \*\*Prise en charge :\*\*Prise en charge à hauteur de 50% du titre de transport et à hauteur de 60% des Tickets Restaurant (d’une valeur faciale de 10€)
- **Repos** : 5 semaines de congés payés par an + 1 RTT par mois (37h/semaine)
- Une **politique de télétravail**flexible, basée sur trois modalités.

## **Nos engagements**

Première Urgence Internationale (PUI) s’engage à prévenir tout type de comportement indésirable au travail, y compris le harcèlement, l’exploitation et l’abus sexuels, le manque d’intégrité et l’inconduite financière, et à promouvoir le bien-être des enfants et des adultes avec lesquels PUI est en contact. PUI attend de toutes les personnes employées qu’elles s’acquittent de leurs tâches et responsabilités professionnelles conformément au Cadre Éthique de PUI.  
Toutes les personnes employées par PUI suivront des formations appropriées, et s’engagent dans la promotion, la diffusion et le respect des principes édictés dans sa charte éthique.  
Le/la titulaire de ce poste aura potentiellement accès à des données personnelles concernant des enfants et des adultes vulnérables dans le cadre de son travail (catégorie 2 dans la classification de risques du recrutement sûr). Ainsi, toutes les offres de postes seront soumises à des références satisfaisantes et à des vérifications appropriées, qui peuvent inclure des vérifications du casier judiciaire et du financement du terrorisme.  
Première Urgence Internationale considère la diversité des nationalités, genres, croyances, profils et statuts au sein de ses Ressources Humaines comme un atout majeur pour son action humanitaire, et s’astreint donc au strict respect du principe de non-discrimination tout au long de son processus de recrutement.  
Nous nous engageons à garantir la diversité et l’égalité des genres au sein de notre organisation et encourageons les personnes candidates issues de milieux divers à postuler.  
Veuillez noter que Première Urgence Internationale ne sollicitera en aucun cas une participation financière pour des frais administratifs liés au recrutement. Toute information allant dans ce sens serait frauduleuse, merci de ne pas en tenir compte.

Vous vous reconnaissez dans ce profil et vous adhérez à nos engagements ? Vous vous sentez prêt·e à relever le **challenge et** à rejoindre la grande **famille PUI ?**

title: Tupande Zone Supervisor - Mtaragon
body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions.To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Kenya program, founded in 2006, operates under the local brand Tupande. Close to 500 staff in our Kakamega headquarters support 1,747 field staff and serve more than 1 million farmers. In Nairobi, around 50 staff support global functions like procurement, recruitment, government relations, and communications.

## About the Role

As a Zone/Duka Supervisor, you are directly responsible for sales in your retail zone. You will play a key role in understanding the needs of our customers/farmers and help shape the future of businesses across all channels and use technology to connect with customers/farmers. You will develop an execution strategy for your assigned market and work both individually, and with your Sales team and to prospect, qualify, develop, and close new customer/farmer opportunities

## Responsibilities

- Achieve sales, repayment, and impact targets for your zone.
- Manage multiple sales channel performance through the entire business cycle simultaneously, working with cross-functional teams as necessary, and serve as the primary contact for all zonal performance.
- Provide technical support and training to Shop Assistants and Field Agents by setting up and facilitating weekly meetings.
- Define and manage task planning for Duka Assistants and Tupande Agents
- Oversee the management of the tree nursery in the zone with a dotted reporting line to the Tree Advisor
- Oversee and execute inventory ordering, data entry and merchandising.
- Oversee the operation control environment at the Duka
- Actively build your teams through hiring, training and performance management
- Supporting planning and implementation of promotion programs for your zone.
- Assist customers in understanding their needs, articulate key differentiators and typical customer buying journeys, and generally display a passion for our program.
- Support your team to create sales opportunities for customers

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- 1+ years of experience in a sales, partner or channel manager role.
- Demonstrated ability to work towards strategic goals consistently.
- Knowledge in Data analysis and inventory management
- Knowledgeable in Google Sheets or MS Excel.
- Work in a team
- Effective strategic and analytical thinking skills.

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Mtaragon - Rift Region, Kenya

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

## Application Deadline

08 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

title: Field Coordinator
body:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Under the supervision of the Country Director, your missions will be as follows :  
Contribute to Action Against Hunger country strategy development and program design  
Coordinate Field Operations and Integrated Program Implementation  
Strengthen Local Partnerships, Community Engagement and Localization at Field level  
Manage the team at field level with technical support from Head of Departments  
Facilitate Effective Coordination and Collaboration with the Coordination Team  
Security and Access

  
Profile :

 You hold a degree in a related field such as Humanitarian Action, International Relations, Development Studies, or a related field.  
You have a minimum of 3 years experience in a senior management role with humanitarian and/or development organisations, in a similar context.  
You have experience in project management.  
You have strong managerial competencies including: strategic planning and operational management; budget and resource management; security and access management; communication, coordination, facilitation.  
You have negotiation skills; leadership, people management, coaching, and team development skills.  
ACF is committed to people with disabilities and actively fights against all forms of discrimination.  
  
Conditions d'emploi  
  
National applications :   
6-months contract according to the internal and national salary conditions of ACF in Afghanistan  
International applications :  
Fixed term contract under French legislation: 6 months  
Monthly gross salary from 2597 to 2968euros upon experience, including 13th month  
Reimbursement of the pension insurance for non-French citizens: 16% of the gross monthly salary  
Annual salary increase: 6% increase after and each 12 months of continuous contract  
Monthly per diem and living allowance: 682euros net, field paidMonthly country allowance: 450euros  
Cold allowance: Reimbursement for the purchase of winter equipment for a maximum of 380euros per person per year in severe cold contexts  
Child allowance: 1500euros per year per child present in the country of origin (maximum 6000euros/year)  
Transportation and accommodation: Coverage of transportation costs and guest house  
Medical coverage: ACF covers 100% of the health and repatriation insurance agreement fees, for your medical expenses, and up to 1 month after the end of your contract.  
Salary sustainment measures (sickness, paternity, maternity)  
Leaves and RnR: 25 days of paid leaves per year, 20 RnR per year, airfare reimbursement with a ceiling to get to the chosen break destination, and 215 euros for each RnR period  
Accompaniment and trainings:Follow-up and support for career development  
Free and unlimited access to the e-learning platform Talentsoft

title: Tchad : Volontaire Sécurité Pays – N’Djaména
source: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
body:
**Volontariat (CEV) | 6 mois | ASAP**

## Acted

Acted travaille avec 19 millions de personnes dans 43 pays au carrefour de l’humanitaire, du développement, et des programmes climatiques et environnementaux. Grâce à une connaissance poussée des contextes et l’adoption de technologies émergentes, nous sauvons des vies, allégeons les souffrances, et protégeons et restaurons notre planète. Travaillant avec un écosystème croissant de partenaires locaux, nationaux et internationaux, nous poursuivons un objectif commun : un monde 3Zéro : Zéro Exclusion, Zéro Carbone, Zéro Pauvreté.

## Acted Tchad

Présente au Tchad, Acted intervient en faveur des populations vulnérables des Provinces du Lac et du Ouaddai, et à Ndjamena. En 2025, l’organisation a mis en oeuvre 11 projets pour un budget de 10.5 millions d’euros. Ses opérations sont coordonnées depuis NDjamena et implémentées à travers 4 bases terrain à Bol et Daboua au Lac, Adré et Chokoyan au Ouaddai.

Au Lac, Acted soutient les personnes déplacées internes suite aux attaques des groupes armés à travers le mécanisme RRM, dont elle est co-lead, et assure l’assistance en sécurité alimentaire. Elle participe aussi à renforcer la résilience des populations dans le cadre de projets d’éducation, d’eau hygiène assainissement ou de moyens d’existence.

Au Ouaddai, Acted s’est redéployée dès avril 2023 pour répondre à l’afflux sans précédent de réfugiés soudanais et retournés tchadiens fuyant les combats au Soudan. A travers une approche multisectorielle d’urgence en abris/AME, CCCM et Protection, Acted répond aux besoins vitaux des déplacés sur les sites informels et les camps d’accueil. Depuis 2025, Acted participe à renforcer la résilience économique des réfugiés Soudanais avec l’aide des communautés hôtes dans la préfecture de Chokoyan.

Les actions d’Acted au Tchad reposent sur une expertise technique multisectorielle reconnue, une capacité de déploiement rapide, une approche basée sur les données, une forte acceptance locale, et la participation accrue des communautés.

Au Ouaddai, Acted s’est redéployée dès avril 2023 pour répondre à l’afflux sans précédent de réfugiés soudanais et retournés tchadiens fuyant les combats au Soudan. A travers une approche multisectorielle d’urgence en abris/AME, CCCM et Protection, Acted répond aux besoins vitaux des déplacés sur les sites informels et les camps d’accueil.

Enfin, Acted intervient régulièrement en réponse aux chocs cycliques, tels que la soudure et les inondations, particulièrement dévastatrices.

Les actions d’Acted au Tchad reposent sur une expertise technique multisectorielle reconnue, une capacité de déploiement rapide, une approche basée sur les données, une forte acceptance locale, et la participation accrue des communautés.

## Rôle et responsabilités principales

Le Volontaire Sécurité Pays soutient directement le Directeur Pays/Responsable Sécurité Pays dans l’établissement de rapports sur l’analyse du contexte, la rédaction de documents de sécurité et le respect des normes de sécurité. Il/elle sera chargé(e) de soutenir dans la rédaction des documents de sécurité d’Acted demandés dans le cadre de l’activité du département Sécurité.

***Principales Responsabilités***

1\. Collecte d’information et analyse du contexte

2\. Évaluations de sécurité, audit et soutien opérationnel

3\. Reporting

## Qualifications et compétences requises

Formation : Cursus universitaire en Relation ou politique internationale, Sciences Po, écoles de commerce ou similaire  
Niveau d’études requis : BAC+4/5  
Approche rigoureuse et méticuleuse du travail  
Dynamique, autonome et force de proposition  
Capacité de communication et de reporting  
Excellent niveau en anglais, écrit et parlé (contacts quotidiens avec les équipes locales)  
Intérêt pour les programmes d’aide d’urgence et de développement internationaux  
Intérêts pour les questions relatives à la sécurité et à la sureté

**Volontariat (CEV) | 6 mois | Octobre 2026**

## Acted

Acted travaille avec 19 millions de personnes dans 43 pays au carrefour de l’humanitaire, du développement, et des programmes climatiques et environnementaux. Grâce à une connaissance poussée des contextes et l’adoption de technologies émergentes, nous sauvons des vies, allégeons les souffrances, et protégeons et restaurons notre planète. Travaillant avec un écosystème croissant de partenaires locaux, nationaux et internationaux, nous poursuivons un objectif commun : un monde 3Zéro : Zéro Exclusion, Zéro Carbone, Zéro Pauvreté.

## Acted République Démocratique du Congo

La République Démocratique du Congo fait face à une crise humanitaire prolongée, marquée par la persistance des conflits armés, des déplacements massifs de populations, des chocs climatiques et des chocs épidémiques récurrents, tels que le choléra, le mpox ou la rougeole. Ces dynamiques combinées affectent durablement les conditions de vie des populations déplacées, retournées et hôtes, en particulier dans les provinces de l’Est et certaines zones de l’Ouest du pays.

Dans ce contexte, Acted intervient principalement dans les provinces du Sud-Kivu, Nord-Kivu, Tanganyika, Nord-Ubangi et Sud-Ubangi, à travers des projets financés notamment par le Department of State / US, ECHO, FCDO, SDC, le Fonds Humanitaire, ainsi que le CDCS, afin de répondre aux besoins humanitaires immédiats et aux vulnérabilités persistantes des populations les plus affectées. Afin de renforcer la couverture et la complémentarité de ses interventions, Acted intervient en coordination avec plusieurs partenaires opérationnels, et est membre de consortiums humanitaires.

Cette coordination permet à Acted de mettre en œuvre des réponses d’urgence rapides et multisectorielles pour couvrir les besoins vitaux liés aux conflits, aux déplacements forcés, aux catastrophes naturelles et aux crises sanitaires. Les interventions portent notamment sur l’assistance alimentaire, les abris et articles ménagers essentiels, l’Eau, Hygiène et Assainissement (EHA), la gestion et coordination des sites (CCCM) ainsi que l’éducation en situation d’urgence, avec une attention particulière portée, dès le premier kilomètre humanitaire, à la protection et à la dignité des personnes vulnérables. Au Sud-Kivu, Acted est par ailleurs un acteur clé du Mécanisme de Réponse Rapide (RRM), contribuant à des réponses rapides et coordonnées en lien avec les déplacements de populations et aux chocs soudains.

En parallèle, Acted développe des interventions visant à renforcer la résilience des communautés, à travers le soutien aux moyens d’existence, la relance agricole, la sécurité alimentaire et la relance économique locale, afin de réduire la vulnérabilité face aux chocs récurrents.

Acted apporte également un appui structurant aux organisations de la société civile (OSC) en renforçant leurs capacités organisationnelles et opérationnelles. Cet accompagnement inclut l’appui à la structuration des initiatives locales ainsi que la mise en place de mécanismes de financement en cascade, permettant aux OSC de développer des activités directement liées aux problématiques locales et aux priorités identifiées par les communautés.

Enfin, Acted intègre progressivement dans ses programmes des approches sensibles à l’environnement, visant à la préservation des écosystèmes et des aires protégées, à la réduction de l’empreinte environnementale des interventions et à la promotion de solutions à faible émission de carbone. À travers l’appui aux communautés, Acted encourage le développement d’activités génératrices de revenus durables et d’une économie locale plus verte, contribuant à la protection des ressources naturelles tout en renforçant les moyens d’existence.

## Rôle et responsabilités principales

Sous l’autorité du Responsable/Chargé (s’il y a) pays Transparence et Conformité, le Volontaire Transparence et Conformité facilite la mise en œuvre des processus conformité d’Acted dans le pays concerné.

Il/Elle devra se conformer et s’assurer de la conformité au code de conduite audit.

***Principales responsabilités***

1\. Faciliter la mise en œuvre des guides standards Acted et du système FLATS dans le pays

2\. Faciliter la préparation des audits externes et des due diligences

3\. Contribuer à la mise en œuvre du plan d’audit interne national validé.

4\. Sessions de formation/ leçons apprises / Meilleures pratiques

- *Formation et renforcement des compétences*
- *Leçons apprises*
- *Travail d’équipe*

## Qualifications et compétences requises

- Diplôme supérieur en Audit, Finance, Contrôle de Gestion, Relations internationales, droit ou en lien avec le volontariat proposé ;
- Capacités de synthèse, d’écriture, de communication et de reporting ;
- Sens de l’analyse et capacité à proposer des solutions aux problèmes rencontrés ;
- Savoir faire preuve de flexibilité, de dynamisme, d’autonomie ;
- Intérêt pour les programmes d’aide d’urgence et de développement internationaux ;
- Connaissance des problématiques de contrôle interne et d’audit ;
- Excellent niveau en anglais, écrit et parlé

body:
**CDD | 6 mois | ASAP**

## Acted

***Qui sommes-nous***

Acted travaille avec 19 millions de personnes dans 43 pays au carrefour de l’humanitaire, du développement, et des programmes climatiques et environnementaux. Grâce à une connaissance poussée des contextes et l’adoption de technologies émergentes, nous sauvons des vies, allégeons les souffrances, et protégeons et restaurons notre planète. Travaillant avec un écosystème croissant de partenaires locaux, nationaux et internationaux, nous poursuivons un objectif commun : un monde 3Zéro : Zéro Exclusion, Zéro Carbone, Zéro Pauvreté.

***Qui cherchons-nous***

Vous apportez les compétences clefs attendues d’un travailleur humanitaire et de développement, mais également une conscience climatique et environnementale active, et vous pouvez naviguez les défis qui émergent lorsque les souffrances environnementale et humaine se rencontrent. Vous avez l’esprit entrepreneurial : vous décelez les opportunités, connectez les points, adaptez votre approche aux différents environnements, et vous prenez des risques mesurés dans la poursuite de résultats. Vous alliez les principes au pragmatisme, et l’ambition à l’humilité.

## Acted Tchad

Acted intervient au Tchad depuis novembre 2004, et au Lac depuis 2011, où elle y conduit des interventions d’urgence et de résilience auprès des populations réfugiées, déplacées, retournées et hôtes vulnérables. Acted compte près de 120 employés et dirige ses opérations depuis sa base de coordination nationale à N’Djamena.

Dans le Lac, avec une base de coordination régionale à Bol et une sous-base à Daboua, la stratégie d’Acted allie une réponse d’urgence au sein du consortium de mécanisme de réponse rapide (RRM) à travers une assistance alimentaire (programmes de distribution de vivres/cash et non vivres, de nutrition), en CCCM et en abris ainsi qu’un soutien au relèvement précoce à travers des programmes de lutte contre la malnutrition, et par la mise en œuvre d’un projet multisectoriel en Eau, Hygiène et Assainissement (EHA), éducation en urgence (EiE), et de réduction des risques de catastrophes (RRC).

Dans le Ouaddai, Acted a une base à Adré et une sous-base à Chokoyan, et intervient en faveur des populations réfugiées, retournés et hôtes à travers un appui multisectoriel en CCCM, abris, Résilience, NFI, WASH et Protection.

**L’outil CATALYST**

Le programme CATALYST (Capacity Assessment, Technical Assistance, and Learning for Sustainable Transformation) d’Acted est un outil méthodologique destiné à renforcer les capacités des organisations de la société civile (OSC) et des organisations communautaires de base (OCB). **Cet outil, dans le cadre du projet concerné, sera utilisé à destination des Organisation Non gouvernementales Nationales (ONG-N) partenaires du Consortium**. Il s’agit d’un processus structuré d’évaluation, d’accompagnement technique et d’apprentissage visant à favoriser une transformation durable et alignée sur les objectifs 3ZERO (Zéro Exclusion, Zéro Carbone, Zéro Pauvreté).

## Rôle et responsabilités principales

Le/la Coordinateur.rice Technique CATALYST est responsable de la mise en œuvre efficace du programme CATALYST d’Acted et en accordance avec les indicateurs de renforcement de capacités attendus. Cela inclut l’accompagnement des organisations partenaires du consortium du projet, la facilitation des processus de renforcement des capacités et la promotion de l’innovation en cohérence avec les objectifs 3ZERO. Le rôle garantit que les activités du programme sont menées selon les standards et contribuent à des résultats durables.

1. **Coordination et mise en œuvre du programme avec les partenaires**

- Coordonner l’ensemble du cycle CATALYST (identification, évaluation, planification, développement des capacités, soutien financier, réévaluation).
- Élaborer et suivre des plans de travail détaillés.
- Assurer la communication entre les partenaires, consultants, mentors et équipes internes.
- Suivre les progrès et résoudre les défis de mise en œuvre.
- Documenter toutes les étapes et activités du programme.

1. **Intégration et évaluation des ONG-N**

- Organiser des sessions d’intégration et de formation sur l’outil CATALYST.
- Appuyer les ONG-N dans leurs auto-évaluations et analyser les résultats pour identifier forces, faiblesses et priorités.

1. **Développement des capacités et formations techniques**

- Co-créer des plans de développement adaptés pour chaque ONG-N.
- Identifier les besoins communs et organiser des formations collectives.
- Adaptation et conduite des formations spécifiques en lien avec les plans de développement spécifiques.
- Évaluer la qualité et l’impact des interventions grâce à des indicateurs SMART.
- Faciliter le mentorat et le coaching, promouvoir l’apprentissage entre pairs.
- Faciliter la mise en œuvre d’un manuel de procédures FLATS pour les ONG-N.

1. **Coordination MEAL**

- Collaborer avec les équipes MEAL pour les évaluations de base, intermédiaires et finales.
- Appuyer la collecte de données et l’implication des ONG-N.
- Utiliser les résultats pour adapter le programme.
- Contribuer aux rapports internes et bailleurs.

1. **Apprentissage, assurance qualité et capitalisation**

- Garantir la qualité et la cohérence du soutien apporté.
- Recueillir et analyser les retours des ONG-G.
- Documenter les leçons apprises et bonnes pratiques.
- Contribuer au partage de connaissances et à l’amélioration de la méthodologie CATALYST.

1. **Partenariats et développement de l’écosystème**

- Identifier et engager des partenaires pertinents (experts, réseaux, institutions, secteur privé).
- Renforcer les liens entre ONG-N et acteurs de l’écosystème.
- Représenter le programme lors de réunions et événements externes.

1. **Autres**

- Fournir des mises à jour régulières sur les progrès, défis et risques.
- Assurer la conformité avec les politiques et valeurs d’Acted.
- Exécuter toute autre tâche assignée par le/la responsable hiérarchique.

## Qualifications et compétences requises

- Diplôme dans un domaine d’expertise pertinent;
- Au moins 5 ans d’expérience dans la mise en œuvre de projets sur le terrain, de préférence dans un contexte international;
- Avoir un fort esprit d’équipe;
- Familiarité avec le système d’aide et capacité à comprendre les exigences des donateurs et des gouvernements;
- Excellentes compétences en matière de communication et de rédaction;
- Capacité à coordonner et à gérer le personnel et les activités du projet;
- Capacité avérée à travailler de manière créative et indépendante, tant sur le terrain qu’au bureau;
- Capacité à organiser et à planifier efficacement;
- Capacité à travailler avec des groupes de personnes de cultures différentes;
- Capacité à voyager et à travailler dans des conditions difficiles et sous pression ;
- L’anglais courant est requis ;

## Conditions

- Salaire défini par la grille des salaires Acted en fonction du niveau d’études, de l’expertise, du niveau de sécurité et du niveau d’expérience : entre 3100 et 3200€ net mensuel (avant impôts sur le revenu)
- Indemnité mensuelle de frais de vie 300$
- Logement en guesthouse et nourriture pris en charge par Acted
- Sécurité sociale, mutuelle (MSH) et assistance rapatriement (SOS International) pris en charge par Acted
- Transport vers la mission et billet retour totalement pris en charge tous les 6 mois (vers l’adresse spécifiée sur le contrat de travail)
- Frais de visa pris en charge par Acted
- Une semaine de préparation au départ comprenant 4 jours de formation sécurité en immersion

- Soutien psychologique (rendez-vous avec un.e professionnel.le)

title: Program Manager, Altadena Rebuild Fund
body:
**Job Purpose:**

The Program Manager, Altadena Rebuild Loan Fund will support the implementation and day-to-day coordination of CORE's responsibilities within the Altadena Rebuild Loan Fund partnership. This position will lead community outreach, homeowner engagement, resource navigation, workshop coordination, survivor support, and partnership-building efforts designed to connect wildfire-impacted homeowners with rebuilding resources and gap financing opportunities. Working from the Altadena Recovery Hub, the Program Manager will serve as a trusted guide for survivors throughout the recovery process, helping homeowners navigate recovery challenges and connect with appropriate recovery, rebuilding, and loan fund partners. The ideal candidate will possess strong program management skills, experience working with disaster-affected communities, and a commitment to equitable recovery, housing stability, and community resilience.

**Main Responsibilities:**

- Lead CORE's implementation and operational activities related to the Altadena Rebuild Loan Fund.
- Track data related to ARF program and author internal and external reports as needed.
- Direct community outreach efforts to increase awareness of available rebuilding resources and loan fund opportunities.
- Conduct homeowner engagement activities through workshops, community events, recovery meetings, and one-on-one survivor interactions.
- Build and maintain relationships with community organizations, recovery partners, local government agencies, funders, and other stakeholders.
- Serve as a trusted point of contact for wildfire-impacted homeowners seeking information about rebuilding resources and recovery options.
- Provide resource navigation support and connect homeowners with appropriate recovery programs, community resources, and partner organizations.
- Facilitate warm handoffs and referrals to partners to support homeowner access to loan fund programs and related services.
- Assist homeowners in understanding the loan fund process, eligibility requirements, and available support services without providing underwriting, credit, or lending determinations.
- Coordinate and support educational workshops, community information sessions, outreach campaigns, and homeowner resource fairs.
- Coordinate with partners to identify barriers to participation, support homeowner progression through the rebuilding process, and strengthen program effectiveness.
- Provide logistical support for loan closing appointments conducted at the Altadena Recovery Hub, including assisting homeowners, coordinating with partners, and supporting notary activities.
- Monitor outreach, referral, and homeowner engagement activities and maintain program metrics for reporting and continuous improvement.
- Analyze homeowner needs, recovery trends, and community concerns and provide recommendations to program leadership and fund partners.
- Support philanthropic engagement, community-facing fundraising efforts, and related outreach activities.
- Deliver services in a culturally responsive, equitable, and trauma-informed manner.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Scope and Travel:**

- Hybrid position based at the Altadena Recovery Hub with local travel to partner organizations and events.

**Qualifications:**

- Bachelor's degree in Public Administration, Business Administration, Community Development, Emergency Management, Social Work, Urban Planning, Communications, or a related field required; equivalent professional experience may be substituted.
- Knowledge of disaster recovery, housing recovery, community engagement, nonprofit program administration, or related fields preferred.
- Familiarity with wildfire recovery resources and community-based recovery efforts preferred.

**Experience:**

- Minimum three (3) years of experience in program management or program coordination, disaster recovery, community development, housing programs, nonprofit operations, or related fields.
- Experience working directly with disaster-affected, vulnerable, or underserved populations.
- Experience managing projects or programs involving multiple stakeholders, partners, and competing priorities.
- Experience building and maintaining community partnerships and collaborative relationships.
- Experience planning and facilitating workshops, community meetings, outreach events, and stakeholder engagement activities.
- Experience monitoring program performance, tracking outcomes, and preparing reports for leadership, funders, or external stakeholders.
- Familiarity with Los Angeles County communities and recovery networks preferred.

**Skills & Competencies:**

- Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
- Strong organizational, program management, project management, and problem-solving abilities.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining attention to detail.
- Strong public speaking, facilitation, and community engagement skills.
- Ability to build and maintain effective relationships with homeowners, community partners, funders, and stakeholders.
- Strong partnership development, collaboration, and stakeholder management skills.
- Demonstrated cultural humility and commitment to serving diverse communities.
- Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced and evolving recovery environment.
- Experience with data collection, reporting, performance measurement, and program evaluation.
- Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, CRM systems, and database management platforms.

**Physical Requirements:**

- Ability to sit, stand, and use a computer for extended periods.
- Ability to travel locally as required for community outreach events, workshops, partner meetings, and stakeholder engagement activities.
- Ability to occasionally lift and carry materials weighing up to 25 pounds.

title: Investor Relations Specialist (Renewable)
body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions.

To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

## **About the Role**

One Acre Fund relies on grant funding to support our operations, but also takes on debt to finance our working capital needs. This role is on the Investor Relations (IR) team, which manages our debt needs, identifies and grows relationships with lenders, and advises on capital structure and liquidity management. The Specialist will support the IR team across loan compliance and reporting, lender due diligence, team operations, and analytical projects.  
The IR team is a team of 4 people, based in Kenya and the U.S. and part of the larger Finance Division. You will report to the Investor Relations Senior Specialist.

This is a strong opportunity for someone interested in finance, impact investing, or accounting to gain hands-on experience working with global lenders and investors in a fast-paced social enterprise environment.

## **Responsibilities**

- Loan Reporting and Compliance: You will help prepare financial and operational reports for lenders, support internal reporting for senior leadership, and assist with interest payments and reconciliations.
- Investor Relations Operations: You will maintain lender records and loan documentation, support the signing and closing of new loans, and help improve the systems and processes that support the Investor Relations team.
- Lender Relationship Management and Due Diligence: You will support current and prospective lenders by coordinating due diligence requests, gathering information across teams, and preparing summaries, spreadsheets, and presentations.
- Financial Analysis and Strategic Projects: You will support financial modeling, dashboards, research, and special projects that help the Finance and Investor Relations teams make decisions and communicate key insights.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. title: Burundi Field Operations Associate
body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Burundi program, founded in 2011, operates under the local brand Tubura. 1662 staff serve close to 400,000 hard-working farmers. Our Burundi headquarters in Muramvya is supported by two regional offices in Gitega and Ngozi, and a small support office in Bujumbura. One Acre Fund works in the center and north of Burundi, in the provinces of Muramvya, Gitega, Ngozi, Kayanza, and Mwaro.

## **About the Role**

As a Program Associate, you will have the opportunity to learn from field operations and to help improve our program. Your proposed initial role will focus on execution of our core program as well as general program innovation, but the exact makeup of your work will depend on staffing and program needs, as well as your own interests.

## **Responsibilities**

**Operations management**

The FOP Associate will focus on delivering services to farmers. He/She begins as generalists, with overall responsibility for executing our program within a given region of operation in Burundi. Over time, He/she can continue to grow as a general leader, potentially managing Field Operations for an entire country. He/She may also choose to specialize, for example in designing and rolling out training programs.

Program associates also build the infrastructure necessary to sustain and scale the program. These teams proactively remove barriers to scale across a wide range of areas, processing millions of payments made by farmers, communicating with farmers through tens of millions of SMS messages, recruiting hundreds of new staff each year, and physically transporting more than 20,000 tons of agricultural inputs to various delivery sites. Program Associates also drive continuous improvements to accelerate growth, for example by implementing mobile money system integration at the country level.

**Core program execution and operations management**

- Own end-to-end execution of the core program across an assigned region and functional area (exemple of core activities can be farmers training, enrollment, distribution, repayment, expansion…), ensuring services reach farmers on time and at quality.
- Ensure seasonal objectives and KPIs are communicated and in line with country and department priorities, monitor performance against them, and intervene where results deviate.
- Ensure operational processes are documented, standardized and cost-efficient, and that spend stays within budget.

**Project and portfolio management**

- Lead a portfolio of 1–3 medium-to-large projects from design through field execution, defining objectives, work plans, timelines and success measures with limited manager support.
- Coordinate delivery across departments (Impact, Systems, Logistics, Business Operations, People) and with external partners, keeping stakeholders aligned and decisions timely.
- Produce analysis, post-mortems and reporting that inform leadership decisions on whether to continue, scale or discontinue an approach.

**Team management and development**

- Manage and mentor a team of direct reports (Senior Field Directors, Specialists, Coordinators) and the wider structure beneath them, driving both performance and professional growth.
- Recruit, onboard and develop staff using One Acre Fund's experiential recruitment approach, and progressively delegate as the team strengthens.
- Maintain performance follow-up systems and remove day-to-day barriers so field teams can consistently deliver quality service to farmers.

**Innovation and continuous improvement**

- Identify opportunities to improve farmer impact, program quality or cost efficiency, and translate them into structured trials or pilots.
- Design and run trials with field teams and farmers, analyze results, and recommend refinements to products, training or the operating model.
- Champion adoption of improved systems, tools and ways of working across the department, ensuring changes are embedded and sustained.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Project management: Able to design and lead medium-to-large projects with a high degree of independence, navigating ambiguity with limited manager support.
- Planning and prioritization: Creates and executes work plans independently. Work is characterized by a high degree of collaboration, higher visibility, and longer-term impact on the team and department.
- People management and coaching: Able to recruit, develop and manage a multi-level team, set clear performance expectations, give effective feedback, and progressively delegate as deputies grow.
- Data analysis: Strong analytical ability, using data to drive decisions and monitor performance against KPIs.
- Communication and stakeholder management: Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to influence without authority and coordinate across country teams, global departments and external partners.
- Innovation and process improvement: Leads innovation and process improvement within the department, from identifying opportunities through to embedding change.
- Budget and resource management: Able to build an annual budget, monitor budget versus actuals, and identify cost-efficiency opportunities without compromising program quality.
- Judgment and execution: Able to make interpretive decisions with incomplete information in a fast-moving field environment, and to keep detail-heavy operations on track.
- Technical proficiency: Strong Excel/Google Sheets skills and comfort with the digital systems used to run operations at scale.
- Languages: English required; French strongly recommended; Kirundi preferred.

As soon as possible

Muramvya, Burundi

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. ## **About the Role**

We are seeking a highly skilled and passionate Senior Agronomist with in-depth expertise and at least 6 years of experience in Conservation Agriculture and deploying farmer training in these practices in the field.

## **Responsibilities**

Conservation Agriculture Strategy & Extension Development

- Develop and continuously improve scalable conservation agriculture advisory models in collaboration with farmer advisory and field teams.
- Design practical extension materials, training manuals, visual guides, and digital tools tailored to diverse farmer needs and contexts.
- Translate technical concepts including cover cropping, minimum tillage, agroforestry, and integrated pest management into practical field-based curricula.
- Adapt advisory approaches and materials based on climate, soil, socioeconomic conditions, farmer feedback, and field learning.

Farmer Training, Field Deployment & Adoption

- Evaluate and refine conservation agriculture practices to improve soil health, water retention, biodiversity, productivity, and farmer profitability.
- Collaborate with R&D teams to design and oversee field assessments of soil health, crop performance, and environmental outcomes.
- Analyze field evidence and farmer feedback to identify high-impact practices and recommend improvements to conservation agriculture programming.
- Translate research findings and field learning into practical recommendations, extension content, and scalable implementation models.

Partnership & Cross-Functional Project Leadership

- Proven experience developing agricultural extension materials and leading farmer-facing training, capacity building, or advisory programs.

Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chili.

## About the Role

Seeking an exceptional poultry production and veterinary professional with 3 years of experience to drive flock performance, minimise mortality, and maximise feed efficiency across One Acre Fund growing broiler outgrower network.

## Responsibilities

Production Management

- Lead broiler production from placement to harvest; track FCR, mortality, and live weight targets while managing feed quality, stocking density, and harvest schedules.

Flock Health & Veterinary Oversight

- Serve as primary clinical authority for diagnostics, treatments, post-mortems, and vaccinations, while maintaining disease calendars, health logs, and regulatory compliance.

Harvest Compliance & Food Safety

- Enforce drug withdrawal periods to certify residue-free flocks and manage harvest-day veterinary documentation and processing facility inspections.

Biosecurity & Housing Management

- Enforce biosecurity protocols using scoring tools, set environmental parameters (ventilation, temp), and issue seasonal guidance for environmental risk management.

Data, SOPs & Coordination

- Oversee field team record-keeping, deliver performance reports analyzing key variances, and continuously update program SOPs based on cycle learnings.

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- At least 3 years of experience in poultry production, broiler performance, and flock health strategy.
- Bachelor’s Degree in Veterinary Medicine, veterinary technolody, Animal Science, or a related field.
- Valid RCVD (Rwanda Council of Veterinary Doctors) license.
- Demonstrated ability to translate veterinary protocols for non-technical field staff and farmers.
- Proven track record managing production across a geographically dispersed outgrower network.

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Bugesera, Rwanda

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

6 months

## Eligibility

02 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

title: Credit and Portfolio Analyst
body:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**JOB SUMMARY**  
Habitat for Humanity International (HFHI) is seeking a motivated Credit & Portfolio Analyst to join Habitat Capital (HCap), a nationally certified Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI), certified in 2017. Habitat Capital is a wholly-owned entity of HFHI and was created to serve our more than 900 US-based Habitat for Humanity affiliates. HCap provides an array of financial services and products to Habitat affiliates to support their work as affordable mortgage originators, real estate developers, home-builders, sellers, and partners for housing and community solutions. To date, HFHI and HCap has provided over $400MM in capital to its US domestic affiliate network via enterprise-level, secured project-level, bridge and structured financing for affordable housing and community development projects as well NMTC allocation for homeownership initiatives. Additionally, HCap seeks to develop and provide permanent mortgage financing products. HCap values creativity and flexibility in developing financial products for our customers and working with capital partners who share our mission.

**About the Program and Role**  
The HCap Analyst Program ("the Program") is a new intentional effort between HFHI and HCap to recruit and train early-stage professionals to succeed in mission-driven financial services roles. In this two-year program, participants will support HCap's efforts to attract and deploy capital to create and increase the production of affordable housing and greater community development across the US. The Analyst will possess and develop strong financial, entrepreneurial, program management and analytical skills while providing communications and research to advance housing and community development initiatives and support broader strategic initiatives and operations.

Supporting HCap Directors, the Analyst's primary responsibilities will include financial analysis and modelling, transaction underwriting, portfolio management, investor relations, marketing and communications, and supporting new programmatic initiatives. While the analyst will have broad responsibilities, there will be a primary focus on credit and underwriting.

Participants will receive training designed to foster mission-alignment, understanding of the housing and community development finance sectors, development of technical skills, and other ongoing enrichment. This 2-year program with the potential for a 3rd year to be evaluated at the end of year 2. The Program is committed to diversity and inclusion and encourages diverse candidates to apply.

These positions are strongly preferred to be based at our headquarters office in downtown Atlanta (Remote considered) and involves up to 10% travel within the US.

**Loan Origination and Underwriting (50%)**

- Conduct credit analysis, due diligence and structuring for investment and real estate transaction
    - Financial statement analysis
    - Project-level analysis and diligence
    - Impact analysis
    - Term sheet creation
- Support the creation of written investment memo for internal investment committee
- Interface with multiple internal and external to support all aspects of deal lifecycle from prospecting through closing
- Conduct financial modelling of new financial products that are innovative, socially responsible, fiscally responsible and attractive to the investing community.
- Provide technical assistance, as needed, to potential or current applicants

**Portfolio Management (20%)**

- Provide support to Portfolio Management Associate to monitor and provide analysis on the existing loan portfolio
- Support monthly, quarterly and semi-annual reporting requirements, collateral substitutions and loan prepayments
- Support investor financial and impact reporting requirements
- Interface with trustees, paying agents and internal finance to ensure timely and accurate satisfaction of debt service obligations

**Research & Analysis (20%)**

- Provide reliable borrower, property, and market-level data by using available third-party and internal resources to conduct research.
- Support the creation and analysis of models, charts, tables, templates, maps and other resources related to lending and programmatic initiatives
- Conduct market research, portfolio and impact data analysis related to historical and future lending work in advancing affordable homeownership, racial equity and climate resiliency

**General Operations (10%)**

- Develop investor and management presentations and reports as well as support training and educational materials for HFHI affiliates
- Prospecting and research in support of broader strategic initiatives and new products and programs

**Cross Functional Capabilities**

Employees in multiple divisions with different skillsets work together to achieve Habitat for Humanity International’s mission and common strategic goals.

Key aspects of cross-functional responsibilities in a global non-profit include: Strategic planning, program design and implementation, communication and branding, monitoring and evaluation, and compliance and risk management.

At Habitat, our work is guided by three core values:

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

## About the Role

Tupande Procurement Senior Coordinator plays a critical role in ensuring smooth and efficient execution of procurement projects by closely aligning with business units (BUs) needs, controlling spend, and improving procurement processes. This role involves managing the full procurement lifecycle for assigned BU procurement projects, supporting supplier and stakeholder relationships, driving process improvements, and maintaining strict contract management and compliance. The coordinator also provides performance tracking and reporting to facilitate strategic decision-making and continuous enhancement of procurement activities.

## Responsibilities

Targeted process and performance improvement

- Support cross-functional improvement initiatives by helping develop templates, SOPs, and training materials.
- Coordinate periodic reviews with assigned Business Units to clear aged Procurement Requests (PRs) and Purchase Orders (POs).
- Perform root cause analysis to identify bottlenecks and improve PR to PO turnaround time.
- Identify capability gaps and propose practical, incremental improvements to strengthen processes and team performance.
- Facilitate effective collaboration between BU and PRO teams to ensure alignment on priorities, timelines, and deliverables.
- Promote proactive communication between BU units and PRO to support timely planning, coordination, and issue resolution.

Strategic sourcing responsibilities

- Define the scope and profile of assigned procurement categories.
- Conduct comprehensive spend analysis, market analysis, and profile demand/supply markets to identify opportunities.
- Develop strategic sourcing strategies, setting clear objectives for cost savings, quality improvement, risk mitigation, and determining appropriate tactics.
- Identify, evaluate, and pre-qualify potential suppliers based on strategic needs.
- Lead RFx processes, including negotiation of pricing, Service Level Agreements (SLAs), payment terms, delivery windows, and change management processes, while integrating selected suppliers into planning systems.
- Finalize and execute contracts, ensuring all terms and conditions are clearly defined and favorable.
- Monitor supplier performance against contract terms, drive continuous improvement initiatives, and hold regular business review meetings to ensure costs are consistently driven down.

Reporting and documentation

- Prepare routine reports and dashboards on procurement project progress, highlighting status updates, risks, and key actions for timely decision-making.
- Support data collection and analysis, including responding to ad-hoc market research requests that inform sourcing decisions and category strategies.
- Capture and document supplier performance data to help drive improvements in service levels, quality, and on-time delivery.
- Analyse cost drivers by Business Unit, identifying short-, medium-, and long-term trends to support planning and spend management.
- Work with other BU coordinators to promote standardization and consolidation of requirements, helping reduce duplication and improve sourcing efficiency across BUs.
- Monitor KPI performance for assigned procurement projects and follow up on corrective actions when targets are not met.
- Maintain clear, organized, and audit-ready documentation for all procurement transactions to support compliance and transparency.
