The HBD also works closely with country program teams, collaborates with other teams within the Awards Management Unit, including the Compliance and Policy (C&P), and Awards management Systems (AMS) teams; the wider Crisis Response Recovery and Development Department including Technical Excellence; External Relations; Finance; Global Supply Chain; Finance; Office of General Counsel; and other key departments within IRC who contribute to regional business development efforts. The HBD serves as point of contact with external donor and partner stakeholders during the pre-award stage, as applicable per region.

**Direct Reports:**

-Program Development Advisor (PDA)

**KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES AND RESPONSABILITIES**

***Planning and Strategic Leadership***

- Provide strategic vision on regional BD efforts in support of country program Strategy Action Plans (SAP), in collaboration with regional and AMU leadership.
- Maintain visibility on the overall pipeline across all public and institutional donors, in collaboration with regional Program Development & Awards Advisors as well as private donors, in close collaboration with the Senior Advisor, Private Partnerships
- Maintain up to date knowledge of donor funding priorities and geographical interests relevant to IRC’s areas of work.
- Provide advice, analysis and guidance to AMU, Regional and Country leadership on BD trends, target-setting, donor engagement, and support needs in the region, ensuring leaders have the right level of information to make decisions.
- Lead and support BD strategy development efforts and planning at regional and country level, to establish clear funding priorities and targets, to support decision making and enable effective positioning and resource planning.
- Coordinate support to country teams in the identification, tracking and pursuit of new business opportunities across a variety of technical sectors and donors, including ensuring that technical brainstorming, partner, and competitor landscape analysis and win theme sessions with technical and country staff are occurring.
- Support country BD strategy development, BD and donor engagement planning and delivery.
- Maintain regional pipeline information and analysis. Lead pipeline monitoring routines at regional level, including but not limited to Quarterly Pipeline Calls. Coordinate with Regional Finance Director on and contribute to the Operating Budget process ahead of Business Development projection-setting.

***End to End Program Development***

- Provide BD summary of new opportunities (Cat A-C but excluding UN) and support CPs in analyzing opportunities (Cat A-D) to inform Go/No Go decisions.
- Support effective and timely Go/No Go decisions, including sharing initial assessment of new opportunities and providing insight and input based on donor knowledge, likelihood of success and experience.
- Plan and manage effective division of bid leadership across the portfolio at capture and live stages of development to ensure appropriate support on all opportunities.
- At the early stage of opportunity identification, work with country teams, DAM and BD leadership in identifying and addressing escalated support needs.
- Act as the regional business development focal point for escalated bid opportunities, providing regional advice and coordinating escalated support when needed.
- Collaborate with other Business Development colleagues, Business Development Specialist team members and technical staff on high demand opportunities and multi-country and Technical Units-led bids.
- Maintain visibility of all opportunities in the region throughout the proposal development process. Contribute to critical bids (Cat D) prioritization, decision-making and bid resourcing; provide relational support.
- Ensure the following Bid Leadership responsibilities are performed consistently and effectively by the assigned BD Lead (HBD, PDA, or other) on each public opportunity in the regional portfolio:
    - Collaborate with technical units, country offices, and other colleagues to support conceptualization of winning program and bid designs, including support to building effective partnerships and consortia.
    - Provide effective proposal support, ranging from proposal management to comprehensive support, confirming responsiveness to and compliance with solicitation documents and with IRC’s requirements. Ensure required reviews and approvals are secured prior to submission to donor.
    - Provide guidance on donor policies and ensure project design is responsive and compliant with donor expectations, rules, and regulations.
    - When providing proposal management support, coordinate concept note and/or proposal development, including sharing initial assessment of new opportunities, reviewing timelines, ensuring the proposal team adheres to deadlines, supporting recruitment, assisting in budget development, ensuring document completion, organizing meetings, and compiling notes, and drafting and proofreading proposal sections. This includes support to country office teams in the management and maintenance of IRC’s award management system.
    - Review agreements, in coordination with relevant RPAS post-award focal point, to ensure accuracy and highlight key compliance requirements, in coordination with post-award, Compliance & Policy and country Grants teams.
    - Facilitate internal After-action Reviews with country teams, technical units, regional team, and other relevant stakeholders to collect lessons learned. Support efforts to share feedback beyond the region as part of IRC’s wider business development learning agenda.
    - Work across teams to ensure successful handover from pre-award to post-award, that lessons learned are captured, and best practices are shared, in support of improved knowledge management and through the development of relevant tools.
    - Maintain complete and accurate electronic files, including final submission packages and internal trackers.

***Donor and Partner Engagement***

- In line with IRC’s Partnership Ambition, contribute to increasing the volume and equity of IRC's work with local and regional partners (with a focus on women-led national organizations) by coordinating support to country programs in identifying partnership opportunities, identifying strong partners, and finalizing teaming arrangements.
- Support partnering conversations with international partner HQs where needed.
- Support countries and the region in planning effective donor, partner, and peer engagement, collaborating with relevant Partnerships/Strategic Partnerships and post-award colleagues.
- Representing IRC externally to donors, peers, and partners.
- Partner with CPs and regional leadership and colleagues on donor engagement and stewardship for prioritized donors.
- Support countries in donor engagement by translating information and intelligence received at the global level into regional and country priorities.
- Support donor mapping and targeting at country and regional levels, as well as positioning and capturing for a limited set of priority opportunities.
- Contribute to donor briefings for country teams, in collaboration with Global BD, as needed.

***Capacity Building and Training***

- Collaborate with other HBDs and stakeholders to share best practices and lessons learned, and to develop and improve tools.
- Contribute to developing, updating, and delivering business-development related training for the region, including roll-out and refreshers of the IRC Business Development Process training.
- Develop, strengthen, and share capacity of other IRC staff - including direct reports, IRC country and regional teams - to identify opportunities and develop strong program design and proposals, including BD processes.
- Support in recruiting, onboarding, and training of new country and regional grants and partnerships team members in collaboration with RPAS team members.

***Staff Management, Learning, and Development***

- Supervise and mentor direct reports, including communicating clear expectations, providing regular and timely performance feedback, document and discussing performance issues if needed, and delivering high-quality documented annual performance reviews.
- Ensure direct reports are trained on all relevant IRC processes and donor regulations
- Support direct reports in achieving annual objectives, acting as a trusted and accountable manager, mentor, and professional resource, including promoting collaboration, enabling adequate resourcing, and ensuring accountability.
- Together with the Director of Awards Management, the Head of Business Development and other members of the team, ensure Regional Program Awards and Support team cohesion, identify team needs and continuous improvements in ways of working, strengthen communication and foster cross-portfolio experience-sharing and learning, as well as other relevant decision-making processes and practices in support of effective team management and well-being.

***Other Responsibilities***

- Contribute to AMU and regional strategic priorities and initiatives.
- Support with French/English translation when necessary.
- Participate in special projects, working groups and other tasks as assigned.

**PERSON SPECIFICATION**

**Essential**

Skills, Knowledge, and Qualifications:

- Substantial experience and a successful track record leading large proposal teams on complex, multi-year, multi-partner proposals with minimal supervision.
- Experience developing and supporting humanitarian and development proposals for NGOs.
- Strong proficiency in English and French.
- Experience with strategies and proposal processes of key government/statutory donors – US Government (USAID and Department of State), FCDO, EU institutions (ECHO, INTPA), and other donors (GAC, Sida, GFFO, BMZ, SDC, etc.).
- Experience collaborating with and supporting national and community-based partners.
- Experience in proposal budgeting is a plus.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to effectively collaborate across a variety of relationships in a multicultural environment.
- Demonstrated ability to collaborate equally effectively with colleagues in remote and diverse teams, including as team leader for proposals.
- Clear, compelling writing skills, preferably with previous experience with proposal writing.
- Ability to multi-task and prioritize effectively.
- Ability to travel internationally (approximately 20% of time).

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

***Ce poste est ouvert aux candidats internes de la région WACAR ou d’autres sites de l’IRC situés dans les fuseaux horaires GMT et EAT, qui possèdent une expérience significative de travail dans les pays d’Afrique de l’Ouest et d’Afrique centrale. Les candidats basés dans ces pays sont encouragés à postuler.***

**CONTEXTE**

**L’International Rescue Committee** (IRC) intervient face aux pires crises humanitaires mondiales et aide les personnes dont la vie et les moyens de subsistance ont été bouleversés par les conflits et les catastrophes à survivre, à se reconstruire et à reprendre le contrôle de leur avenir. Fondé en 1933 à la demande d’Albert Einstein, l’IRC travaille auprès des personnes contraintes de fuir la guerre, les conflits et les catastrophes, ainsi qu’auprès des communautés d’accueil qui les soutiennent, sans oublier celles qui restent chez elles et au sein de leur communauté. Présent aujourd’hui dans plus de 40 pays et 22 villes des États-Unis, nous redonnons sécurité, dignité et espoir à des millions de personnes déracinées qui luttent pour survivre. L’IRC montre la voie pour passer de la détresse au retour chez soi.

**Le département « Réponse aux crises, relèvement et développement » (CRRD)**

Le département Réponse aux crises, relèvement et développement (CRRD) gère un portefeuille croissant de programmes d’aide humanitaire, de relèvement post-crise et de développement relevant de sa compétence. Ce travail concentre son soutien sur cinq domaines clés : garantir la sécurité face aux dangers, améliorer la santé, accroître l’accès à l’éducation, améliorer le bien-être économique et veiller à ce que les personnes aient le pouvoir d’influencer les décisions qui affectent leur vie. Dans tous ces programmes, un effort particulier est déployé pour répondre aux besoins spécifiques des femmes et des filles (qui représentent la majorité des personnes déplacées) – ainsi qu’aux obstacles universels auxquels elles sont confrontées.

**L’Unité de gestion des subventions (AMU)**

Créée en janvier 2016, l’Unité de gestion des subventions (AMU) est un service mondial chargé d’identifier, d’obtenir et de gérer l’ensemble des financements provenant de bailleurs de fonds statutaires ou gouvernementaux. L’AMU fait le lien entre les bailleurs de fonds et les programmes nationaux : elle fournit des conseils techniques spécialisés aux équipes nationales, tout en assurant une visibilité au niveau du portefeuille afin de garantir la cohérence et la conformité et de gérer les risques. Cette unité veille à ce que les politiques et procédures de conformité des bailleurs de fonds soient mises en œuvre de manière cohérente et apporte son soutien à l’ensemble du personnel intervenant tout au long du cycle de gestion des subventions pour tous les financements soumis à des restrictions provenant de sources gouvernementales mondiales.

**Aperçu régional de l’Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre :**

**La région Afrique de l’Ouest et centrale (WACAR)** soutient la mise en œuvre de programmes efficaces, performants et de haute qualité en renforçant les capacités en matière de résultats pour les clients, de qualité des programmes, de positionnement stratégique et de développement des activités. Elle s’attaque aux défis humanitaires et de développement qui se recoupent — conflits, gouvernance défaillante et dégradation de l’environnement — par le biais d’approches intégrées et à fort impact.

WACAR priorise l’apprentissage lié à l’innovation et à des stratégies techniques harmonisées, en particulier dans les zones où les besoins sont importants. Elle assure la continuité des soins et la coordination de la prestation de services pour les clients en déplacement, tout en favorisant un engagement stratégique des bailleurs de fonds grâce à une collecte de fonds cohérente et à une collaboration régionale.

La région répond rapidement aux besoins des programmes nationaux, en comblant les lacunes critiques et en surmontant les contraintes d’accès, les situations d’urgence et les changements en matière de sécurité. Elle amplifie la voix des clients et des acteurs de première ligne pour éclairer le plaidoyer mondial et favorise une forte cohésion d’équipe afin d’améliorer la mise en œuvre des programmes. Le WACAR privilégie des approches rentables et adaptatives face à l’évolution du paysage humanitaire et des bailleurs de fonds, en mettant clairement l’accent sur le financement des programmes nationaux.

La WACAR regroupe le Burkina Faso, le Burundi, le Cameroun, la République centrafricaine, le Tchad, la Côte d’Ivoire, la République démocratique du Congo, le Mali, le Niger et le Nigeria.

**Objectif du poste**

Sous la responsabilité du Directeur de la Gestion des Subventions (DAM) et en étroite collaboration avec la direction de la mobilisation des ressources Globale, le/la Responsable de la Mobilisation des Ressources (HBD), WACAR dirige les efforts de mobilisation des ressources de l'IRC en soutien aux bureaux pays de la région WACAR et constitue un élément clé de l'équipe mondiale de mobilisation des ressources de l'IRC, représentant la région dans l'élaboration et la mise en œuvre de la stratégie mondiale de mobilisation des ressources de l'IRC. Le/la HBD joue un rôle stratégique dans la planification, l'identification et la recherche de nouveaux financements, en cohérence avec les Plans d'Action Stratégiques (SAP) des bureaux pays. Le soutien du/de la HBD couvre toutes les phases du processus de mobilisation des ressources, notamment la planification stratégique, la sensibilisation et l'engagement des bailleurs, le pré-positionnement (capture), les partenariats, le développement de propositions, la diligence raisonnable, les lettres de problèmes et la négociation d'accords.

Le/la HBD est chargé(e) de maintenir une supervision au niveau régional de l'ensemble de la mobilisation des ressources auprès des bailleurs institutionnels dans la région WACAR de l'IRC.

**Portée et responsabilité**

Le/la Responsable de la Mobilisation des Ressources exerce la direction générale de la mobilisation des ressources dans la région et assure la gestion hiérarchique du/de la Conseiller(ère) en Développement de Programmes régional(e) (PDA). Le poste supervise le pipeline régional et soutient les stratégies et la planification de la mobilisation des ressources au niveau des bureaux pays, notamment en examinant le pipeline et les opportunités individuelles et en veillant à l'allocation adéquate des ressources pour des soumissions de candidatures réussies, en coordination avec le/la Conseiller(ère) Régional(e) Principal(e) en Programmes et Subventions (SPAA), selon les besoins. Le/la HBD assure la supervision du développement des opportunités assignées à la région et sert de point focal régional clé pour les opportunités mondiales, soutenues par l'équipe de Mobilisation des Ressources.

Relations de travail clés

Le/la HBD gère le/la (les) Conseiller(ère)(s) en Développement de Programmes régional(aux) (PDA) et travaille en étroite collaboration avec l'équipe de direction régionale (RMT), tous les membres de l'équipe régionale de Soutien aux Programmes et Partenariats (RPAS), et l'équipe mondiale plus large/globale de Mobilisation des Ressources. Le/la HBD travaille également en étroite collaboration avec les équipes des bureaux pays, collabore avec d'autres équipes au sein de l'Unité de Gestion des Subventions (AMU), notamment les équipes de Conformité et Politiques (C&P) et de Systèmes de Gestion des Subventions (AMS) ; le Département Réponse aux Crises, Relèvement et Développement (CRRD) au sens large, y compris l'Excellence Technique ; les Relations Extérieures ; la Finance ; la Chaîne d'Approvisionnement Mondiale ; le Bureau du Conseiller Général ; et d'autres départements clés de l'IRC qui contribuent aux efforts de mobilisation des ressources régionaux. Le/la HBD sert de point de contact avec les bailleurs et partenaires externes lors de la phase pré-partenariat, selon les besoins propres à chaque région.

**Subordonnés directs :**

\- Conseiller(ère) en Développement de Programmes (PDA)

**PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILITÉS ET MISSIONS**

***Planification et leadership stratégique***

- Définir une vision stratégique des efforts de mobilisation des ressources régionaux en soutien aux Plans d'Action Stratégiques (SAP) des bureaux pays, en collaboration avec les directions régionale et AMU.
- Maintenir une visibilité sur le pipeline global auprès de l'ensemble des bailleurs publics et institutionnels, en collaboration avec les Conseiller(ère)s régionaux/ales en Développement de Programmes et Subventions (PDA), ainsi qu'auprès des bailleurs privés, en étroite collaboration avec le/la Conseiller(ère) Principal(e) en Partenariats Privés.
- Maintenir une connaissance actualisée des priorités de financement et des intérêts géographiques des bailleurs pertinents pour les domaines d'intervention de l'IRC.
- Apporter conseils, analyses et orientations à l'AMU et aux directions régionales et nationales sur les tendances de la mobilisation des ressources, la fixation d'objectifs, l'engagement des bailleurs et les besoins en soutien dans la région, en veillant à ce que les dirigeants disposent d'informations suffisantes pour prendre des décisions éclairées.
- Diriger et soutenir les efforts de développement stratégique et de planification de la mobilisation des ressources aux niveaux régional et national, afin d'établir des priorités de financement et des objectifs clairs, de faciliter la prise de décision et de permettre un positionnement et une planification des ressources efficaces.
- Coordonner le soutien aux équipes de pays dans l'identification, le suivi et la recherche de nouvelles opportunités de financement dans divers secteurs techniques et auprès de différents bailleurs, notamment en veillant à ce que des séances de réflexion technique, d'analyse du paysage des partenaires et de la concurrence, et des sessions sur les thèmes porteurs se tiennent avec les équipes techniques et de pays.
- Soutenir le développement de la stratégie de mobilisation des ressources des bureaux pays, la planification et la mise en œuvre de l'engagement avec les bailleurs.
- Maintenir les informations et analyses du pipeline régional. Diriger les routines de suivi du pipeline au niveau régional, notamment les Appels Trimestriels sur le Pipeline. Coordonner avec le/la Directeur/trice Régional(e) des Finances et contribuer au processus budgétaire opérationnel en amont de la définition des projections de mobilisation des ressources.

***Développement de programmes de bout en bout***

- Fournir un résumé des nouvelles opportunités de mobilisation des ressources (Cat A-C, à l'exclusion des Nations Unies) et soutenir les bureaux pays dans l'analyse des opportunités (Cat A-D) pour éclairer les décisions d'engagement (Go/No Go).
- Soutenir des décisions Go/No Go efficaces et rapides, notamment en partageant une évaluation initiale des nouvelles opportunités et en apportant des éclairages et des contributions fondés sur la connaissance des bailleurs, la probabilité de succès et l'expérience.
- Planifier et gérer une répartition efficace de la direction des offres dans l'ensemble du portefeuille aux stades de la capture et du développement actif, afin de garantir un soutien approprié à toutes les opportunités.
- Dès la phase initiale d'identification des opportunités, travailler avec les équipes de pays, le/la DAM et la direction de la mobilisation des ressources pour identifier et répondre aux besoins de soutien renforcé.
- Servir de point focal régional de la mobilisation des ressources pour les opportunités d'offres nécessitant un soutien renforcé, en fournissant des conseils régionaux et en coordonnant ce soutien lorsque nécessaire.
- Collaborer avec d'autres collègues de la Mobilisation des Ressources, les membres de l'équipe Spécialistes en Mobilisation des Ressources Globale et le personnel technique sur les opportunités à forte demande et les offres multinationales et portées par les Unités Techniques.
- Maintenir une visibilité sur toutes les opportunités dans la région tout au long du processus de développement des propositions. Contribuer à la priorisation des offres critiques (Cat D), à la prise de décision et à l'allocation des ressources ; assurer un soutien relationnel.
- Veiller à ce que les responsabilités suivantes de Direction d'Offre soient exercées de manière cohérente et efficace par le/la Responsable BD désigné(e) (HBD, PDA ou autre) pour chaque opportunité publique a travers le portefeuille régional :
    - Collaborer avec les unités techniques, les bureaux pays et d'autres collègues pour soutenir la conceptualisation de programmes et de conceptions d'offres gagnants, notamment en soutenant la construction de partenariats et consortiums efficaces.
    - Apporter un soutien efficace à la proposition, allant de la gestion de la proposition à un soutien complet, en confirmant la conformité aux documents de sollicitation et aux exigences de l'IRC. Veiller à ce que les révisions et approbations requises soient obtenues avant soumission au bailleur.
    - Fournir des orientations sur les politiques des bailleurs et veiller à ce que la conception du projet soit conforme aux attentes, règles et réglementations des bailleurs.
    - Lors de la fourniture d'un soutien à la gestion des propositions, coordonner le développement des notes conceptuelles et/ou des propositions, notamment en partageant l'évaluation initiale des nouvelles opportunités, en examinant les calendriers, en veillant au respect des délais par l'équipe de proposition, en soutenant le recrutement, en contribuant à l'élaboration des budgets, en assurant la complétude des documents, en organisant les réunions et en rédigeant des comptes rendus, ainsi qu'en rédigeant et en révisant les sections des propositions. Cela comprend le soutien aux équipes des bureaux pays dans la gestion et la maintenance du système de gestion des partenariats de l'IRC.
    - Examiner les accords, en coordination avec le point focal après-subvention (post-award) de l'RPAS concerné, afin de garantir leur exactitude et de mettre en évidence les exigences clés de conformité, en coordination avec les équipes post-award, de Conformité et Politiques et des Partenariats des bureaux pays.
    - Faciliter les Revues post-action internes avec les équipes des bureaux pays, les unités techniques, l'équipe régionale et les autres parties prenantes concernées pour collecter les leçons apprises. Soutenir les efforts de partage des retours d'expérience au-delà de la région dans le cadre de l'agenda d'apprentissage en mobilisation des ressources de l'IRC.
    - Travailler avec les équipes pour assurer une passation réussie des dossiers de la phase pré-subvention (pre-award) à la phase après-subvention (post-award), veiller à ce que les leçons apprises soient documentées et que les meilleures pratiques soient partagées, en soutien à l'amélioration de la gestion des connaissances et à travers le développement d'outils pertinents.
    - Maintenir des fichiers électroniques complets et précis, incluant les dossiers de soumission finaux et les tableaux de bord internes.

***Engagement avec les bailleurs et les partenaires***

- Conformément à l'Ambition Partenariale de l'IRC, contribuer à augmenter le volume et l'équité du travail de l'IRC avec les partenaires locaux et régionaux (avec un accent sur les organisations nationales dirigées par des femmes) en coordonnant le soutien aux bureaux pays dans l'identification des opportunités de partenariat, l'identification de partenaires solides et la finalisation des arrangements d'équipe.
- Soutenir les discussions de partenariat avec les sièges de partenaires internationaux si nécessaire.
- Soutenir les pays et la région dans la planification d'un engagement efficace avec les bailleurs, partenaires et pairs, en collaborant avec les collègues concernés des Partenariats/Partenariats Stratégiques et après-subvention (post-award).
- Représenter l'IRC en externe auprès des bailleurs, pairs et partenaires.
- Collaborer avec les bureaux pays, la direction régionale et les collègues sur l'engagement et la fidélisation des bailleurs prioritaires.
- Soutenir les bureaux pays dans l'engagement avec les bailleurs en traduisant les informations et renseignements reçus au niveau mondial en priorités régionales et nationales.
- Soutenir la cartographie et le ciblage des bailleurs aux niveaux national et régional, ainsi que le positionnement et la capture pour un ensemble limité d'opportunités prioritaires.
- Contribuer aux séances d'information pour les bailleurs à l'intention des équipes de pays, en collaboration avec l’équipe de Mobilisation des Ressources Mondiale (Global BD), selon les besoins.

***Renforcement des capacités et formation***

- Collaborer avec les autres HBD et parties prenantes pour partager les meilleures pratiques et les leçons apprises, et pour développer et améliorer les outils.
- Contribuer au développement, à la mise à jour et à la dispensation de formations liées à la mobilisation des ressources pour la région, notamment le déploiement et les actualisations de la formation sur le Processus de Mobilisation des Ressources de l'IRC.
- Développer, renforcer et partager les capacités des autres membres du personnel de l'IRC — y compris les rapports directs, les équipes des bureaux pays et régionales — pour identifier les opportunités et élaborer des conceptions de programmes et des propositions solides, notamment les processus de mobilisation des ressources.
- Participer au recrutement, à l'intégration et à la formation des nouveaux membres des équipes de subventions et de partenariats des bureaux pays et régionaux, en collaboration avec les membres de l'équipe RPAS.

***Gestion du personnel, apprentissage et développement***

- Superviser et encadrer les rapports directs, notamment en communicant des attentes claires, en fournissant un retour d'information régulier et ponctuel sur les performances, en documentant et en discutant des problèmes de performance si nécessaire, et en réalisant des évaluations annuelles de performances documentées et de haute qualité.
- Veiller à ce que les rapports directs soient formés à tous les processus pertinents de l'IRC et aux réglementations des bailleurs.
- Soutenir les rapports directs dans la réalisation de leurs objectifs annuels, en agissant en tant que manager, mentor et ressource professionnelle de confiance et responsable, notamment en favorisant la collaboration, en garantissant des ressources adéquates et en assurant la responsabilisation.
- Avec le/la Directeur/trice de la Gestion des Subventions, le/la Responsable de la Mobilisation des Ressources et les autres membres de l'équipe, veiller à la cohésion de l'équipe régionale de Soutien aux Programmes et Subventions (RPAS), identifier les besoins de l'équipe et les améliorations continues dans les modes de travail, renforcer la communication et favoriser le partage d'expériences et l'apprentissage transversal, ainsi que d'autres processus et pratiques décisionnels pertinents en soutien à une gestion d'équipe efficace et au bien-être.

***Autres responsabilités***

- Contribuer aux priorités et initiatives stratégiques de l'AMU et de la région.
- Apporter un soutien en traduction français/anglais si nécessaire.
- Participer à des projets spéciaux, groupes de travail et autres tâches assignées.

**PROFIL RECHERCHÉ**

**Compétences Essentielles**

Compétences, connaissances et qualifications :

- Expérience substantielle et un solide bilan dans la direction de grandes équipes de propositions sur des propositions complexes, multi-annuelles et multi-partenaires avec une supervision minimale.
- Expérience dans le développement et le soutien de propositions humanitaires et de développement pour des ONG.
- Maîtrise solide de l'anglais et du français.
- Expérience avec les stratégies et processus de propositions des principaux bailleurs gouvernementaux/institutionnels — Gouvernement américain (USAID et Département d'État), FCDO, institutions de l'UE (ECHO, INTPA), et autres bailleurs (GAC, Sida, GFFO, BMZ, SDC, etc.).
- Expérience de collaboration et de soutien aux partenaires nationaux et communautaires.
- Expérience en budgétisation de propositions est un atout.
- Excellentes compétences en communication et relations interpersonnelles, notamment la capacité à collaborer efficacement dans le cadre de relations diversifiées dans un environnement multiculturel.
- Capacité démontrée à collaborer efficacement avec des collègues dans des équipes à distance et diversifiées, notamment en tant que chef d'équipe pour des propositions.
- Compétences rédactionnelles claires et convaincantes, de préférence avec une expérience préalable dans la rédaction de propositions.
- Capacité à gérer plusieurs tâches simultanément et à prioriser efficacement.
- Disponibilité à voyager à l'international (environ 20 % du temps).

**Employeur garantissant l'égalité des chances** : L'IRC est un employeur garantissant l'égalité des chances. L'IRC évalue tous les candidats sur la base du mérite, sans distinction de race, de sexe, de couleur de peau, d'origine nationale, de religion, d'orientation sexuelle, d'âge, de situation matrimoniale, de statut d'ancien combattant, de handicap ou de toute autre caractéristique protégée par la législation en vigueur.

**Normes professionnelles** : Tous les collaborateurs de l’International Rescue Committee (IRC) doivent adhérer aux valeurs et principes fondamentaux énoncés dans le document « IRC Way – Normes de conduite professionnelle ». Nos normes sont l’intégrité, le service, l’égalité et la responsabilité. Conformément à ces valeurs, l’IRC met en œuvre et applique des politiques relatives à la protection des personnes, aux conflits d’intérêts, à l’intégrité financière, au signalement des irrégularités et à la protection contre les représailles. L’IRC s’engage à prendre toutes les mesures préventives nécessaires et à créer un environnement où chacun se sent en sécurité, ainsi qu’à prendre toutes les mesures nécessaires et correctives en cas de préjudice. L’IRC constitue des équipes de professionnels qui favorisent la réflexion critique, le partage des responsabilités, le débat et l’objectivité afin d’offrir les meilleurs services possibles à nos bénéficiaires.

title: Deputy Director, Supply Chain Business Development and Program Delivery
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
**Job Overview**

The Deputy Director, Supply Chain Business Development and Program Delivery is a senior global role responsible for making IRC's supply chains fit for scale across its most ambitious health and humanitarian programming commitments. The role is designed to translate strategic program targets into operational supply chain solutions that work at country level and ensuring country realities shape global supply chain strategy in return.

The role has three integrated areas of responsibility.

It serves as a primary GSC lead and contributor to business development: identifying, designing, and positioning supply chain funding opportunities with institutional and non-traditional donors, and leading supply chain sections of competitive proposals.

It provides support across IRC's Impact at Scale (I@S) thematic supply chains, driving end-to-end performance from demand planning and forecasting through sourcing, pre-positioning, and last-mile delivery.

It builds country and regional capacity to sustain health supply chain improvements over time, providing direct technical support, deploying to high-priority contexts, and harmonizing tools and SOPs across country programs in collaboration with Regional Supply Chain Directors (RSCDs) and other relevant Global Supply Chain (GSC) units and IRC stakeholder departments.

Reporting to the Director of Emergency and Health Supply Chain, the Deputy Director works in close collaboration with the Health Technical Unit, Global Procurement, Regional Supply Chain Directors, Country Programs, IT, Finance, and external partners including UNICEF, WHO, ECHO, and peer INGOs.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Leadership for Program Delivery**

- The Deputy Director plays an active role in GSC’s business development (BD) function. Supply chain is an increasingly fundable programming area, with institutional donors such as ECHO, SIDA, Gates and non-traditional donors explicitly framing requirements around operational efficiency, commodity management, and supply chain innovation. Additionally, private and corporate donors have expressed specific interest in funding the optimization of health and emergency supply chains.
- Act as the primary GSC focal point within I@S agile working groups and cross-functional scaling teams, ensuring supply chain planning is embedded in program design from the outset and not treated as a downstream implementation task.
- Implement the strategic direction for cross-cutting supply chain enablers including pooled procurement, global pre-positioning frameworks, harmonized delivery models, and digital systems and oversee their development and rollout across priority country programs.
- Provide supply chain leadership and oversight for the addition of any new I@S Ready to Scale thematic areas, ensuring new commodities and delivery models are integrated into IRC's global supply chain architecture without creating fragmentation or duplication.
- Serve as GSC's coordinating focal point with the Research and Innovation Department, contributing to supply chain innovations including AI-enabled solutions.

**2. Business Development & Resource Mobilization**

- Is responsible for operationalizing the BD strategy, assembling inputs to create compelling bids, gap filling in the BD process as needed/relevant, and driving ultimate bid success through correct donor intel and positioning, strong bid submission, and effective cross-functional collaboration.
- Flag, track and route relevant funding opportunities to GSC Leadership and work closely with internal stakeholders to plan for staff needs and business development capacity requirements to successfully write and budget for winning bids based on the pipeline
- Lead or co-lead the technical design of supply chain sections for proposals where GSC has a primary role, including narrative writing, logical framework development, and supply chain costing.
- Collaborating with program and business development leads to embedding supply chain considerations into program design, with specific attention paid to Impact at Scale initiatives
- Contribute to bid assessment, probability-of-winning analysis, and positioning strategy for supply chain funding opportunities with specific focus on I@S thematic areas
- Develop and maintain GSC supply chain capability statements and value propositions relevant to I@S programming areas, for use in capture and proposal development.
- Participate in the BD review cycle for proposals with significant supply chain components, ensuring technical quality and alignment with IRC’s global supply chain strategy.
- Mobilize opportunities with non-traditional partners such as Airlink to improve program delivery and increase cost savings
- Take the lead with External relations and other fundraising teams to enable increased use of GIK goods and services, enabling program delivery whilst making IRC more cost effective.
- Build and maintain donor intelligence on supply chain funding streams
- Support pre-award activities including donor engagement, capture visits, and key personnel recruitment where relevant to I@S supply chain opportunities.
- Coordinate with Regional Supply Chain Directors and country programs to ensure country-level supply chain needs and evidence are reflected in proposals.
- Contribute to after-action reviews following award decisions to capture lessons and improve future supply chain BD submissions.
- Identify and evaluate opportunities for business development & partnerships with academic or research centers, with Research & Innovation colleagues as appropriate.

**3. Implementation of Strategic Initiatives Supporting Impact @ Scale**

- Strengthening global forecasting and demand planning systems for key health commodities.
- Collaborate with Global Procurement to define sourcing strategies, monitor supplier performance, and ensure security of supply.
- Lead global visibility efforts by consolidating country-level data on demand, pipeline status, consumption, and stock risks. Collaborate with GSC Systems and Data to digitalize as many aspects of this as possible in a timely manner.
- Work with country teams to improve quantification, storage, distribution planning, and last-mile delivery.
- Translate I@S targets into actionable supply chain plans with milestones, KPIs, and risk controls.
- Design and support the rollout of cross-country improvements (e.g., pooled procurement feasibility, centralized pre-positioning, LMIS integration, preferred vendor strategies, emergency surge mechanisms, harmonized delivery models).
- Support the implementation of the supply chain I@S bodies of work.
- Escalate and advise GSC Leadership on global priorities, risks, and mitigation strategies impacting success of I@S activity plans.

**4. Capacity Building, Country Support & Operational Strengthening**

- Provide specialized technical support to country supply chain and health teams.
- Strengthening country practices in forecasting, contingency planning, supplier management, and stock-out prevention.
- Support countries facing pipeline risks or operational bottlenecks; deploy to high-priority locations as needed.
- Promote best practices and harmonize tools, guidance, and SOPs across all countries, regions and departments.
- Train country and departmental staff as required. Develop e-training as funding permits.

**5. Monitoring, KPIs, Reporting & Knowledge Management**

- Develop supply chain KPIs aligned to IRC’s LMIS, BD and I@S objectives.
- Produce timely reports on global health supply chain performance, risks, and mitigation actions.
- Document lessons learned and drive continuous improvement.
- Maintain updated knowledge of global markets, procurement trends, supplier landscapes, regulatory shifts, and donor funding priorities relevant to supply chain programming.

**Qualifications**

**Education**

- Master's degree in public health, pharmacy, supply chain management, strategy development, , international development, international relations, or relevant field or equivalent combination of education and work experience background is required or related field.

**Work Experience**

- Experience in supply chain management in humanitarian settings, preferably with demonstrable experience in health supply chains, especially immunization, nutrition and sexual and reproductive health (SRH).
- Proven experience in departmental or organizational strategy development in operations / supply chain in humanitarian organizations.
- Expertise in forecasting, strategic sourcing, procurement, quality assurance, and distribution of health commodities including in the context of vaccine storage and distribution.
- Experience in conducting assessments and evaluations of supply chain systems.
- Experience engaging in business development processes, including writing and project design, proposal development, donor positioning, or capture for supply chain or health programming is strongly preferred.
- Experience in developing and managing project concepts and funding proposals for humanitarian / development work with the ability to turn concepts and strategy into measurable action
- Strong capacity to understand the humanitarian system and operating context and coordinate the relevant technical inputs from within and outside GSC
- Familiarity with donor landscapes for supply chain programming (e.g., ECHO, SIDA, USAID, Gates) and ability to contribute to donor engagement and positioning.
- Familiarity with managing large-scale, complex portfolio and experience using strategic insights and data from varied sources to support portfolio management, pivoting and alignment to organizational and sectoral goals
- Experience in building partnerships for development and humanitarian funding as well as negotiation of programmatic and financial contractual arrangements with donors and partners
- Experience and comfort interrogating partnership practices and familiarity with emerging developments including growing attention to power-shifting, localization and technical assistance models for INGOs

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

- Proficiency in data analysis, visualization tools (Power BI), and performance monitoring.
- Excellent attention to detail and problem-solving skills and ability to analyses trends based on a diverse set of data and insights
- Digital supply chain literacy: familiarity with LMIS platforms, supply chain technology ecosystems, and data interoperability standards in humanitarian or low-resource settings. Experience with using AI-enabled solutions preferred.
- Ability to identify fundable supply chain programming opportunities and experience in business development writing and proposal design
- Ability to translate operational supply chain experience into compelling proposal narratives and capability statements.
- Demonstrated ability to work with stakeholders at multiple levels and influence decision making
- Knowledge of public and private fundraising - appetite and curiosity about building collaborative pathways with philanthropy and private sector
- Fluent in English (required); proficiency in French, Spanish or Arabic.

**Competencies**

- Strong project management and coordination skills.
- Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, particularly in supply chain optimization.
- Good organizational skills and ability to prioritize competing priorities effectively.
- Excellent communication and stakeholder management abilities; skills; ability to work cross-functionally and across cultures.
- A sense of curiosity about how things can be done, and a willingness to get creative on solutioning.
- Attention to detail and ability to identify and address potential risks proactively.
- Commitment to ethical standards and accountability.

**Key Relationships**

**Reports to:**

Director, Emergency & Health Supply Chain

**Directly Supervises:** N/A

**Internal:** Global Supply Chain, Health Technical Unit, IT, Regional Supply Chain Directors, Health Coordinators/teams and Supply Chain Coordinators/Teams; Pharmacists; GOAT BD Coordinator; GSC BD pipeline monitoring

**External:** Peer INGOs, UN agencies (UNICEF, WHO), institutional donors (ECHO, SIDA, Unitaid, USAID), implementing partners, HLGSC members

**Additional Information**

- Frequent travel to program countries will be required up to 20%.
- This position may involve collaboration with government agencies, international NGOs, private-sector partners, and institutional donors.
- The role actively participates in IRC’s BD process, including pipeline monitoring, capture, and proposal development for supply chain funding opportunities.

**Working Environment**

- Remote work / standard office (location dependent)

***This is a remote position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in United Kingdom, Kenya, and Lebanon.***

**Compensation:** (UK Pay Rate: £58,476-£69,440/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Administrative & Department Manager, CRRD
body:
**The Crisis Response, Recovery, and Development (CRRD) Department**

The CRRD Department houses all the IRC’s Country Programs that implement our work, within a four-pillar department structure:

- Program Delivery, comprised of 5 Regions with more than 30 Country Programs. These are our implementing and management teams delivering our programs.
- Technical Excellence, comprised of 5 Technical Units supporting sector-specific and cross-cutting program quality, as well as program design and strategic leadership.
- Awards Management, leading our processes and implementation around business development, grants management, compliance, and donor engagement and awards management strategies.
- Emergencies, leading stand-alone emergency responses in crisis-affected areas, as well as supporting existing teams with surge support and resources if emergencies break out in their contexts.

All four pillars of CRRD collaborate closely with Country Program staff on the frontlines of program delivery to provide high-quality programming with impactful results for the people we serve.

**JOB OVERVIEW**

The Administrative and Department Manager for CRRD will be responsible for providing high quality, core administrative support to the Senior Vice President (SVP) of CRRD and for leading on the overall administrative work of the department. For the SVP they will be responsible for coordinating calendars, meetings and events; coordinating travel arrangements; coordinating media and external engagements; and tracking expenses. For the department, they will provide wider coordination of meetings and events; document management; internal communications support; AV and logistical support; org charts; email lists; and for supporting events or changes in the HQ office space. Working directly with the SVP and alongside the department’s senior leadership, they will be a trusted member of the central administrative team – sitting in on senior meetings and entrusted with sensitive information. The role demands tremendous discretion, and in return it offers an unusually close view of how a global, fast-moving humanitarian organization runs and how decisions get made at the most senior level. This role requires very strong organization, communication, and interpersonal skills.

**Growth, Access, and Opportunity**

This role sits at the center of a global department and comes with unusual access: direct exposure to the SVP and senior leaders, a front-row seat in high-level meetings, and a network that reaches across the IRC’s work. There are multiple career paths this role can lead to, and the team will actively help you find and navigate the ones that fit your strengths and interests (specific next roles are earned not guaranteed). If you are someone who spots a problem, gets excited about solving it, and wants to grow, this is a place to do exactly that. A successful candidate will bring a can-do attitude and a collaborative team spirit, ready to support the diverse needs of a small and efficient executive team.

**MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Executive Leadership Support**

- Manage SVP calendar and communicate with meeting participants regarding internal and external meetings
- Support SVP speaking event and other travel coordination (logistics, travel documentation, partnering with others on speaking content, registrations, visas, etc.)
- Support media requests including last-minute schedule requests
- Organize, schedule, and support HQ meetings including room reservations, light AV support, and catering if applicable
- Prepare documents and other types of meeting materials, present slides and disseminate meeting materials
- Maintain and update shared calendars and trackers to document SMT and Executive Board travel and leave
- Submit credit card reconciliations and reimbursements on behalf of the SVP, as appropriate
- Support teams in obtaining signatures and approvals from the SVP

**Information / Document Management and Internal Communications**

- Work with Strategy & Performance team to maintain files and disseminate resources from pillar, departmental, and inter-departmental meetings
- Support pillar document formatting and meeting preparation
- Organize Box (online storage) folders and support collaboration and archival organization across CRRD
- Update organizational charts monthly, alongside departmental teams’ org charts as needed
- Oversee regular Distribution List updates and ensure accuracy of mailing lists
- Update the Emergency Contact List Card in coordination with Safety & Security colleagues
- Support onboarding for new CRRD hires that include scheduling time with pillar leaders

**Systems, Process Improvement, and Ownership Opportunities**

- Take ownership of discrete strategic planning and coordination tasks in partnership with the SVP’s office and the wider team, with scope that can grow to match your strengths and interests
- Identify and lead administrative process improvements that streamline how the department works
- Support the roll-out of new software, tools, and protocols – potentially from testing through to adoption

**Special Events and Special Projects**

- Support with annual Core Humanitarian Standards audits (uploading policies and documents, tracking relevant materials and emails)
- Arrange workshops and conferences with assistance from others (venue procurement, travel logistics arrangements and tracking, information dissemination with participants, hotel liaising and management)
- Plan and facilitate special occasions (e.g. birthdays, baby showers, retirements, welcome or farewell parties, etc.)
- Other duties as requested

**Position Reports to:** Senior Director, Strategy & Performance, CRRD

**JOB REQUIREMENTS**

- Bachelor’s degree, Associate’s degree, or equivalent, with 2–3 years of professional experience in an administrative role
- Excellent organizational skills, including the ability to juggle competing priorities and manage time for yourself and others
- Service-oriented and flexible, commitment to help and support in a fast-paced, fast-changing environment
- Sound judgment and discretion in handling confidential and sensitive information
- A proactive, ownership mindset: you anticipate needs, spot problems before they escalate, and are energized by the chance to make things work better
- Poise and confidence working directly with senior leaders and external stakeholders
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills: the ability to successfully and effectively liaise with people, within and across departments in a multi-cultural environment
- Strong computer acumen including proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, Power Point and Outlook
- Ability to work independently, resourcefully, and to own initiative, with flexibility to changing priorities and an eagerness to learn
- French, Arabic, Spanish or other relevant language skills an advantage
- Optimism and good humor warmly welcomed

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $68,000-$74,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Finance/Ops Lead - FCDO-funded Technical Assistance
body:
**Background and Objectives of the FCDO-funded Technical Assistance Programme in Pakistan**

IRC is preparing to bid for an upcoming long-term FCDO-funded Technical Assistance programme in Pakistan. The programme will provide sustained technical and advisory support to strengthen the capacity of government counterparts and partners, with delivery structured against agreed results and milestones in line with FCDO's payment-by-results (PBR) requirements. The Finance/Ops Lead will play a central role in ensuring the programme's financial management, operations and PBR-linked reporting are robust, compliant and responsive to the needs of the technical team throughout the life of the contract.

The Finance/Ops Lead will be responsible for overseeing financial management, operations and financial reporting for the FCDO-funded Technical Assistance programme in Pakistan. Acting as the principal finance and operations business partner to the Project Director and other Senior Management team, the Finance/Ops Lead provides the leadership and management necessary to ensure the project has the appropriate financial and operational infrastructure and systems in place to support smooth project implementation, including robust tracking and reporting against payment-by-results (PBR) milestones. The Finance/Ops Lead will ensure the assistance complies with FCDO rules and regulations and host country labor, tax, and other relevant laws. S/he will contribute to the development of the Project’s strategic and operational plans and be accountable for ensuring and monitoring delivery against the financial and PBR plans through targeted and comprehensive financial analytical review. Additionally, the Finance/Ops Lead will coordinate their work with IRC Finance Unit to enforce internal controls over the programme.

**Job Responsibilities:**

- Ensures that all policies and procedures are in compliance with IRC and FCDO policies, procedures, and requirements.
- Establishes project’s finance and supporting function policies, systems and procedures, and directs or performs their development, documentation, and implementation.
- Manages project finance activities and schedules to meet the financial reporting requirements and deadlines specified by IRC HQ and FCDO. Prepares quarterly accrual reports, expenditure reporting, and burn rate projections.
- Provides project management and program staff with monthly actual-to-budget expenditure reports and analysis for project funds and facilitate the review and discussion.
- Ensures balance sheet reconciliations are completed monthly and on a timely basis and review final reconciliations and trial balances with the Project Director.
- Closely monitors all financial activities, and keeps the Project Director advised of all situations which have the potential for a negative impact on internal controls or financial performance.
- Directs the preparation of and approval of all FCDO financial reports in respect to accounting, legal and contractual requirements and ensures the review of such reports by the Project Director and HQ prior to submission.
- Enforces internal control policies and procedures.
- Maintains current knowledge of local government requirements related to financial matters and ensures compliance with tax regulations and other legal requirements.
- Establishes project finance roles and responsibilities matrix; ensures job descriptions are current; recruits and maintains qualified staff to perform finance functions.
- Develops and implements a training program for the project’s finance staff.
- Ensures constructive performance reviews are completed on a timely basis and facilitates discussion of performance and career options with project finance staff.
- Supervises all project office bank relations and bank account activities including negotiation of fees, interest and currency exchange rates.
- In compliance with IRC policy, establishes policies regarding cash holding limits, cash movements and foreign currency holdings of the project.
- Oversees the timely preparation, review and approval of all monthly bank account and cash reconciliations.
- Designs, implements, and monitors systems, procedures and reporting necessary to maintain on current basis accurate forecasts of cash requirements for meeting future spending, including commitments entered into and which obligate IRC to future spending.
- Supervises the preparation of Cash Transfer Requests to IRC HQ and ensures that appropriate cash balances are maintained to facilitate project implementation.
- Assists with the preparation and revision of project budgets.
- Prepares the annual and monthly cash budgets based on approved funding.
- Prepares monthly pipeline analysis (spending forecast) on the project in coordination with the technical team.
- Coordinates and reconciles spending forecasts with Project Director to reflect realistic data.
- Leads on operational management of the project office, including logistics, procurement, and administrative/HR coordination, ensuring operations are efficient and compliant with FCDO and IRC requirements.
- Leads on the financial tracking, verification, and reporting of Payment by Results (PBR) milestones and disbursement-linked indicators, ensuring accurate and timely submissions to FCDO.

**Requirements:**

- A bachelor’s degree from an accredited university in Accounting, Business Administration, Commerce or Finance with a recognized professional certificate in accounting such as CPA, or a master’s degree in Accounting.
- Minimum of 10 years in similar financial, compliance, or operational role in managing and supporting $7 million or larger FCDO funded projects and other Institutional Donor projects in similar contexts;
- Experience with budgeting and financial reporting requirements on $7 million or larger FCDO, or other Institutional Donor funded projects;
- Experience with financial management and reporting on projects with substantial subaward components;
- Strong knowledge of generally accepted accounting practices, financial reporting standards, financial management processes and procedures
- Familiarity with FCDO rules and regulations including applicable laws.
- Prior experience working on FCDO Technical Assistance programmes and/or with commercial contractors delivering FCDO/ODA-funded assistance, with a solid understanding of the associated compliance, procurement and reporting requirements.
- Strong background in the Payment by Results (PBR) approach, including designing and tracking results-based milestones and disbursement-linked indicators, and financial reporting against PBR schedules.
- Extensive experience in working with computerized accounting systems (ERP), standard spreadsheet and database programs, and advanced and demonstrated/practical skills in Microsoft Excel.
- Must have a proven track record of proactively identifying and communicating potential problems and proposing solutions.
- Excellent interpersonal communication skills and professional patience and be able to interact, partner and thrive in a diverse environment.
- Strong negotiation skills and the ability to develop relations with diverse teams.
- Good written and verbal skills in English.

***Recruitment for this role is contingent upon the successful award of the project to the IRC. The final applicant's selection is subject to FCDO approval.***

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.
