title: Regional Health Advisor - Latin America and the Caribbean (Consultant)
body:
Corus International is the parent organization of a family of world-class organizations working to deliver comprehensive, lasting solutions to end extreme poverty. We are a global leader in international development, with 150 years of combined experience across our different entities. Our subsidiaries include IMA World Health, Lutheran World Relief, CGA Technologies, Ground Up Investing, and Farmers Market Brands. Our more than 400 employees around the world are dedicated experts serving vulnerable populations.

Corus International has a longstanding presence and network of relationships across Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC), with particular experience in Central America. As the health funding landscape continues to evolve, Corus seeks to strengthen its positioning for emerging health opportunities funded by the U.S. Department of State (DOS), the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), and other bilateral, multilateral, philanthropic, and private-sector donors.

The region continues to face complex health challenges, including infectious disease threats, gaps in public health surveillance and laboratory systems, health workforce constraints, migration-related health needs, maternal and child health challenges, and disparities in access to quality health services. At the same time, evolving donor priorities create opportunities to strengthen health security, disease prevention and response, health systems, laboratory capacity, workforce development, and locally led approaches.

**Role:** Regional Health Advisor - Latin America and the Caribbean (Consultant)

**Location:** Latin America and the Caribbean, with a particular focus on Central America

**Supervision:** Managing Director, Technical Business Unit / Designated Corus Technical and Business Development Leadership

**Position Type:** Consultant

**CONSULTANCY SUMMARY**

The Regional Health Advisor will provide strategic and technical leadership to strengthen Corus International's positioning for health opportunities across Latin America and the Caribbean, with a particular focus on Central America.

The Advisor will develop an in-depth understanding of the regional health landscape, donor priorities, Corus' existing capabilities and relationships, and emerging health funding opportunities. Working closely with Corus' Technical Business Unit, business development teams, country and regional staff, and organizational leadership, the Advisor will identify priority opportunities, strengthen relationships with key stakeholders and potential partners, and help shape competitive technical approaches for future health programming.

A major focus of the consultancy will be positioning Corus for opportunities from the U.S. Department of State, CDC, private sector and other priority donors. The Advisor will provide regional intelligence, technical input, partner mapping, capture support, and proposal design leadership, while helping Corus refine a clear health growth strategy for the region.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

1. **Regional Health Strategy and Technical Positioning (20%)**

- Develop a strong understanding of the health landscape across LAC, with particular attention to Central America, including major health challenges, government priorities, donor investments, and gaps that align with Corus' technical capabilities.
- Support development and refinement of a regional health growth strategy aligned with Corus' global strategy, organizational capabilities, geographic presence, and anticipated donor priorities.
- Identify priority technical areas where Corus can establish a differentiated and competitive position, which may include:
    - Global health security and health emergency preparedness and response
    - Infectious disease prevention, detection, surveillance, and response
    - Laboratory systems strengthening and diagnostic capacity
    - Public health surveillance and health information systems
    - Health workforce development
    - Community health and primary health care
    - Maternal, newborn, child, and reproductive health
    - Migration and cross-border health
    - One Health
    - Infection prevention and control
    - Supply chain and access to essential health commodities
    - Digital health and data use for decision-making
- Provide technical guidance on regional and country-specific health trends and help translate these trends into actionable positioning and program development strategies.
- Identify areas where Corus' existing global technical capabilities and experience can be adapted or leveraged for the LAC context.

1. **Donor Engagement, Opportunity Identification, and Business Development (40%)**

- Monitor and analyze the regional health funding landscape, with particular emphasis on anticipated opportunities from the U.S. Department of State, CDC, and other priority donors.
- Identify and communicate emerging health opportunities, donor priorities, procurement trends, and potential changes in the funding environment that could affect Corus' regional strategy.
- Develop donor and opportunity intelligence to help Corus prioritize investments in upcoming health procurements.
- Support early positioning and capture planning for priority opportunities, including analysis of:
    - Donor objectives and priorities
    - Competitive landscape
    - Potential prime and subcontracting opportunities
    - Corus' comparative advantages and capability gaps
    - Key technical requirements
    - Geographic priorities
    - Government and stakeholder interests
- Support development of opportunity-specific capture strategies and recommend actions needed to strengthen Corus' competitive position before solicitations are released.
- Participate in donor, government, partner, and stakeholder meetings, as appropriate, to strengthen Corus' visibility and understanding of emerging priorities.
- Help position Corus as a credible technical partner in regional health programming through targeted engagement with donors, governments, regional institutions, implementing organizations, academic institutions, and other relevant stakeholders.

1. **Partnership Development and Regional Relationship Building (20%)**

- Map relevant international, regional, national, and local organizations that could serve as strategic partners for priority health opportunities.
- Assess prospective partners based on technical capabilities, geographic presence, government relationships, donor experience, organizational capacity, and strategic fit with Corus.
- Develop and strengthen relationships with ministries of health, national public health institutes, U.S. Government stakeholders, regional health organizations, local civil society organizations, universities, research institutions, private-sector actors, and other relevant stakeholders.
- Identify high-value local and regional partners that can strengthen Corus' ability to design and implement locally led health programs.
- Support discussions with prospective partners regarding teaming arrangements and opportunity-specific collaboration.
- Recommend partnership strategies for priority countries and anticipated procurements.
- Help Corus strengthen relationships with relevant regional institutions and networks, including organizations supporting regional disease surveillance, laboratory strengthening, health security, migration health, and public health capacity development.

1. **Proposal and Program Design Support (15%)**

- Play a technical leadership role in the design of priority health proposals in the LAC region.
- Support proposal teams in developing technically sound and competitive approaches responsive to donor requirements and regional needs.
- Lead or contribute to the development of:
    - Technical strategies and approaches
    - Theories of change
    - Results frameworks and logical frameworks
    - Technical narratives
    - Implementation models
    - Partner roles and responsibilities
    - Monitoring, evaluation, research, learning, and adaptation approaches
- Ensure proposed approaches reflect current evidence, donor priorities, country context, government strategies, and Corus' institutional strengths.
- Participate in proposal design workshops, color team reviews, and other business development processes as requested.
- Identify technical experts, institutions, and other resources that may strengthen priority proposals.

1. **Learning, Representation, and Knowledge Development (5%)**

- Document relevant regional health trends, donor intelligence, lessons learned, and recommendations to support Corus' ongoing regional positioning.
- Identify and share relevant research, policies, technical guidance, and regional developments that may influence Corus' health strategy.
- Support development of capability statements, technical briefs, presentations, and other positioning materials highlighting Corus' relevant health experience.
- Represent Corus, as appropriate, at technical meetings, conferences, donor consultations, and other regional forums.
- Facilitate knowledge sharing between Corus' global technical experts and regional teams to strengthen organizational understanding of LAC health priorities and opportunities.

**EXPECTED DELIVERABLES**

The consultant's specific deliverables will be agreed upon with Corus leadership and may include:

- A regional health landscape and opportunity assessment focused on LAC, with deeper analysis of priority Central American countries.
- A recommended LAC health growth and positioning strategy identifying priority countries, donors, technical areas, and near- and medium-term opportunities.
- A pipeline of priority health opportunities, including anticipated DOS, CDC, and other donor procurements.
- Donor and stakeholder mapping for priority countries and technical areas.
- Partner mapping and recommendations for strategic teaming relationships.
- Opportunity-specific capture and positioning plans for selected priority procurements.
- Technical input and leadership for concept notes, expressions of interest, proposals, and other business development materials.
- Regular briefings to Corus leadership regarding regional health trends, funding opportunities, competitive intelligence, and recommended actions.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

**Education:** Master's degree or higher in public health, medicine, epidemiology, global health, health systems, health economics, international development, or a related field.

**Experience:**

- Minimum of 8 years of progressively responsible experience in international health, public health, or global health programming.
- Significant experience working in Latin America and the Caribbean, with strong knowledge of Central America preferred.
- Demonstrated experience with U.S. Government-funded health programs, particularly programs funded by CDC, the U.S. Department of State, USG, or other relevant U.S. Government agencies.
- Demonstrated experience supporting business development, capture, proposal design, or strategic positioning for donor-funded health opportunities.
- Experience developing or maintaining relationships with government ministries, donors, regional institutions, implementing partners, and local organizations.
- Experience in one or more priority technical areas such as global health security, infectious disease surveillance, laboratory strengthening, epidemiology, health systems strengthening, health workforce development, primary health care, or community health.

**Skills:**

- Strong understanding of the health and donor landscape in Latin America and the Caribbean.
- Strong strategic thinking, opportunity analysis, and business development skills.
- Demonstrated ability to translate complex public health challenges into competitive program strategies and technical approaches.
- Excellent relationship-building and stakeholder engagement skills.
- Strong proposal writing, technical writing, and presentation skills.
- Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with geographically dispersed and multicultural teams.
- Ability to rapidly analyze new technical areas, donor priorities, and funding opportunities.

**Languages:** Professional fluency in English and Spanish required.

**Other:**

- Existing professional networks within the health sector in Central America and the broader LAC region strongly preferred.
- Ability and willingness to travel within Latin America and the Caribbean and internationally, as required.
- Familiarity with locally led development and partnership approaches strongly preferred.

**PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE**

The anticipated period of performance will be determined based on Corus' business development and regional positioning needs. The consultancy may involve a combination of defined deliverables and ongoing advisory support.

title: Finance Manager, Budgeting and Reporting
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**DESCRIPTIF DU POSTE :**

Le/La Manager Finance Budgeting & reporting assistera le Finance and Emergency Deputy Director of Finance dans les questions Budgétaires et rapportage du bureau national IRC-RDC. Le poste sera responsable de la gestion financière des projets, du suivi des budgets, des rapports financiers aux donateurs, des prévisions de trésorerie et prévision des dépenses, de la formation du personnel/des partenaires et renforcement des capacités sur les questions budgétaires et rapportage.

**RESPONSABILITES :**

**Comptabilité**

- S'assurer que les budgets sont postes dans le système Integra en temps opportun et à jour. Qu’il s’agisse des budgets de nouveaux projets mais aussi des réalignements des projets en cours

**Budgets et rapports des donateurs**

- Travailler avec le personnel du programme et grants pour préparer des budgets de subventions pour soutenir de nouvelles propositions ou réalignements afin d'assurer une couverture adéquate des coûts de fonctionnement du pays et des coûts directs et indirects du Siege.
- Procéder à l'attribution des codes D2 sur les lignes budgétaires de chaque subvention en collaboration avec les chefs de projet et la chaine d’approvisionnement.
- Préparer le premier draft du rapport financier à soumettre au Coordinateur Financier et Budget.
- Mener la préparation des prévisions et des plans de dépenses pour les réunions de subvention. Participer à toutes les réunions de subventions (réunion d’ouverture, réunion de revue de mise en œuvre, réunions de clôture).
- Analyser les dépenses réelles par rapport aux prévisions budgétaires pour garantir une utilisation maximale des montants budgétés et pour fournir des recommandations de réalignement au besoin en vérifiant les dépassements / sous-dépenses sur le budget.
- Assister le Finance coordinateur en charge de la comptabilité dans le processus de répartition des coûts de support sur différents projets en signalant a temps des projets a risque de dépassement.
- S'assurer que les réglementations des donateurs sont respectées pour tous les aspects des opérations.
- Identification des problèmes de procédure ou de formation à résoudre pour améliorer la qualité des données des différents rapports.
- Préparation des rapports des donateurs en temps opportun conformément aux accords et contrats des donateurs.

**Partenariats/Gestion des sous-subventions**

- Superviser l’Officier partenariat suivi budgétaire et Finance et s'assurer que les listes de contrôle et les procédures sont suivies pour les examens systématiques des rapports financiers ainsi que les commentaires sur le rapport sont partagés avec les partenaires.
- Assurer la liaison avec le responsable financier et le responsable du partenariat pour identifier les lacunes en matière de renforcement des capacités des partenaires.
- Suivi des examens de pré-évaluation pour déterminer les besoins en capacités des sous-bénéficiaires.
- Examiner la demande de trésorerie des sous-subventions et assurer le transfert des fonds en temps opportun.
- Examen des montants des avances de sous-subvention par rapport aux dépenses déclarées, assurer un rapprochement régulier du compte d'avance dans Intégra et Power Bi.

**Analyse financière et suivi des dépenses**

- Fournir une analyse financière régulière des dépenses charges sur les projets et préparer les journaux de corrections qui permettent à ce que les lignes budgétaires sont charges uniquement de dépenses y afférentes.
- S’assurer que les données sur l’application Power BI sont à jour et exact en ce qui concerne les budgets des projets.
- Assurer les intérims du Coordinateur Financier et Budget en cas d’absence.

**Audit**

- Assurer un bon archivage des FACE form/Factures ainsi que tous les rapports financiers soumis aux bailleurs et les rendre disponible à la demande des auditeurs.
- Assister le Département Finance e cas d’audit.

**PROFIL REQUIS**

- Diplôme universitaire en Finance, ou Economie ;
- Des connaissances en informatique avec une expérience significative dans Excel, la connaissance d’un Système Entreprise Ressource Planning (ERP) sera un atout supplémentaire ;
- Minimum trois années d’expériences dans un poste de Budgeting and reporting ;
- La connaissance des règles et règlementations des différents bailleurs ;SIDA ,OCHA….
- Bonne expression orale et écrite en français et une bonne connaissance de l’anglais est un atout.

**Note pour le personnel de terrain IRC :** “Engagement envers les clients : En s'engageant à mettre en œuvre une programmation axée sur le client, l'IRC place les personnes qu'elle sert - ses clients - au centre de sa programmation et de ses services. Le personnel de l'IRC a un rôle important à jouer pour soutenir la mise en œuvre d'une programmation axée sur le client en sensibilisant la communauté et les clients aux mécanismes de retour d'information existants et à la manière de les utiliser, y compris les processus de réponse, l'accès et l'éligibilité aux services, et en contribuant à la création d'une culture institutionnelle qui incite le personnel à écouter les clients, à communiquer et à répondre à leurs demandes, à leurs commentaires et à leurs plaintes.”

**Normes de conduite professionnelle** : Les travailleurs de l’IRC doivent respecter les valeurs et les principes énoncés dans l’IRC WAY - Standards de conduite professionnelle. Il s’agit de l’Intégrité, du Service, de la Responsabilité et de l’Egalité.

**Conformément à la sauvegarde, l’IRC applique des politiques sur la protection des bénéficiaires/clients contre l’exploitation et les mauvais traitements, la protection des enfants, l’Anti-harcèlement dans le milieu du travail, l’intégrité fiscale et la lutte contre les représailles.**

**Employeur de l’égalité des chances : L’IRC est un employeur de l’égalité des chances. L’IRC considère tous les demandeurs d’emploi sur la base du mérite sans égard à la race, au sexe, à la couleur, à la nationalité, à la religion, à l’orientation sexuelle, à l’âge, à l’état matrimonial, au statut d’ancien combattant, au handicap ou à toute autre caractéristique protégée par la loi.**

**Diversité, Inclusion et Egalite Genre : IRC reconnaît et honore la valeur fondamentale et la dignité de tous les individus. Nous sommes un employeur offrant l'égalité des chances et considérons tous les candidats sur la base du mérite sans égard à la race, le sexe, la couleur, l'origine nationale, la religion, l'orientation sexuelle, l'identité de genre, l'âge, l'état matrimonial, le statut d'ancien combattant ou le handicap. IRC s'est également engagé à réduire l'écart entre les sexes dans les postes de direction. Nous offrons des avantages qui offrent un environnement propice aux femmes pour participer à notre main-d'œuvre, y compris un congé parental, des protocoles de sécurité sensibles au genre et d'autres avantages de soutien.**

title: Employment Specialist
body:
**IRC Background:**

Founded in 1933, the IRC is a leading nonsectarian, voluntary organization providing relief, protection and resettlement services for refugees and victims of oppression or violent conflict. One aspect of the IRC is to provide assistance to refugees resettling in the United States. The IRC opened an office in Phoenix, Arizona in 1994 to provide reception and placement services to newly arrived refugees. The office resettles refugees and provides numerous program services to assist refugees from their arrival through citizenship.

**Job Overview:**

The Employment Specialist is responsible for managing the provision of services to assist newly arrived refugee clients to attain self sufficiency through employment. Specifically, the Employment Specialist provides services that include employer and market development, employment search, client and employer preparation, job placement, career enhancement, job training and assessment and follow-up, and enrollment assistance with Arizona Unemployment Insurance benefits. They are also charged with maintaining accurate and timely data collection for employment services and reporting on program deliverables.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities may include, but are not limited to:

- Providing intake, assessment, and pre-employment/job readiness orientation to clients eligible for employment services.
- Developing comprehensive employment plans for each employable adult.
- Providing both group and one-on-one intense job readiness orientations that provide clients with the basic skills required to enhance their employability.
- Developing and cultivating long term relationships with area employers in order to identify appropriate employment opportunities for clients.
- Determining specific employment opportunities appropriate to clients and assisting clients in accessing these opportunities by guiding them through the hiring process.
- Monitoring job performance, wage level, and employer/employee satisfaction.
- Assisting clients and employers as necessary with post placement issues and continuing employment needs.
- Assisting clients with applying for Unemployment Insurance benefits and filing weekly claims.
- Ensuring timely and accurate compliance to all reporting requirements.
- Participating in all program meetings, staff development activities, and fully engaging as a member of the team.
- Complying with all policies, procedures and protocols of the agency.
- Other related duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Employment Supervisor   
**Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

***Internal:*** IRC staff, interns and volunteers

***External:*** Community partners, employers

**Job Requirements:**

- At least two years of related experience in case management, employment, job placement and/or business.
- Demonstrated experience with the US job search process and the ability to coach clients effectively through the nuanced process of securing employment.
- Knowledge of the Tucson job market strongly preferred.
- Excellent communication skills, with fluency in written and spoken English. Bilingual ability in one of the predominant languages of the local client base is desired.
- Proven ability to contribute both independently and as a key team member, self- starter with excellent problem solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook) and strong keyboarding skills and internet usage and research skills
- Proven success achieving goals and working effectively with all levels of staff in a multicultural environment.
- Valid driver’s license, reliable vehicle with current insurance, and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area.
- Must have or be eligible to receive a Fingerprint Clearance Card.

**Compensation**: (Pay Rate: $20.97). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Working Environment:**

- Standard office work environment, coupled with travel in and around the service delivery area.
- Work outside of traditional office hours may be required on occasion.

**Benefits:** We offer our employees phenomenal benefits such as paid parental leave, generous time off, and excellent medical, dental, and vision options.

**Commitment to Diversity and Inclusivity:** IRC is committed to building a diverse organization and a climate of inclusivity. We strongly encourage applications from candidates who can demonstrate that they can contribute to this goal.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation. #LI\_GR1

title: New Roots Farm Coordinator
body:
**IRC Background:**

Founded in 1933, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) is a leading nonsectarian, voluntary organization providing relief, protection and resettlement services for refugees and victims of oppression. For over 20 years our Phoenix office has provided a range of services including resettlement and economic empowerment services, immigration, community gardening and case management.

Our strength and success lie within our core values of Service, Accountability, Equality, and Integrity. We are strongly motivated by our clients and are dedicated to delivering high-impact and quality programs.

**Job Summary**

The Farm Coordinator manages the day-to-day operations of New Roots farm sites and supports the Urban Farm and Community Gardening Program. The role coordinates farmer activities, training, production, market participation, volunteers, equipment, infrastructure, and access to resources. The Farm Coordinator also supports safe and sustainable farming practices, program data collection, and community partnerships. This position reports to the New Roots Program Manager.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Farm Operations, Infrastructure, and Safety**

- Manage farm equipment, vehicles, tools, irrigation systems, and wash stations, including maintenance and inventory.
- Manage aquaponics greenhouse operations, including tilapia production.
- Develop and carry out land management plans covering soil fertility, farm inputs, irrigation, apiculture, and composting.
- Coordinate farm planning with New Roots staff and participating farmers.
- Implement farm and food safety plans and maintain GHP/GAP compliance at New Roots farm sites.
- Support land acquisition and site development, including soil remediation, infrastructure installation, farm layout, and irrigation.

**Farmer Training and Technical Assistance**

- Develop and deliver group and one-on-one training on sustainable agriculture, including crop planning, soil health, pest and weed management, irrigation, post-harvest handling, and food safety.
- Visit partner farm sites regularly to assess needs and provide technical assistance.
- Coordinate partner-led training and resources related to land management, crop production, food safety, business development, and marketing.

**Program Monitoring**

- Track farm production data, including crop plans, harvests, and farmer sales.
- Monitor soil health through testing and track soil amendments, tillage, and crop rotations.
- Track aquaponics production, harvests, system maintenance, pH levels, system health, and tilapia sales.
- Maintain accurate participant files and document farmer progress and skill development.
- Work with the Program Manager to maintain data for grant and donor deliverables and contribute to grant proposals and reports.

**Community Relations and Resource Development**

- Develop and maintain partnerships with organizations such as the University of Arizona Cooperative Extension, Local First Arizona, and the Natural Resources Conservation Service.
- Represent New Roots at community events and coordinate outreach activities and volunteer days.
- Support fundraising, development activities, and the acquisition of in-kind and financial resources.

**Additional Responsibilities**

- Support seasonal markets, produce deliveries, urban farm activities, community gardens, and other New Roots projects.
- Follow all IRC policies and procedures, including the IRC Way and Child Safeguarding requirements.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Position Reports to: New Roots Program Manager**  
**Position coordinates: Interns and program volunteers**

**Other Internal and External Contacts:**

***Internal:*** IRC staff, interns, and volunteers

***External:*** Community partners, donors, vendors

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Undergraduate degree in agricultural sciences, agronomy, environmental sciences, agricultural business, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

***Work Experience:***

- At least three years of agriculture-related experience. Experience with diversified vegetable and sustainable or organic production is preferred.

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Ability to safely operate and maintain farm vehicles and equipment, including tractors, tillers, mowers, and trimmers.
- Strong organization and time-management skills, with the ability to prioritize work and operate independently.
- Fluency in spoken and written English; bilingual ability is preferred.
- Ability to communicate effectively with people who have limited English proficiency and work across cultures.
- Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, Teams, and Outlook. Experience with web-based data systems is preferred.

***Certificates or Licenses:***

- Valid driver's license, active automobile insurance, and access to reliable transportation are required.
- Must possess or be eligible to obtain an Arizona fingerprint clearance card.

**Working Environment*****:***

Work is performed in farm office and outdoor urban farm settings, with regular travel throughout the service area. Some Saturday and weekday evening work is required. The role requires working outdoors in varying weather conditions and safely lifting up to 50 pounds.

**Compensation**: (Pay Rate: $26.78). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $120 per month, dental starting at $7 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Project Manager-Local Position (Re-advertised)
body:
**English:**

1. **DESCRIPTION OF THE AGENCY**

**Expertise France** is the French public agency responsible for designing and implementing international technical cooperation projects. The agency operates around four priority areas:

- Democratic, economic and financial governance;
- Peace, stability and security;
- Climate, agriculture and sustainable development;
- Health and human development.

In these areas, Expertise France provides project engineering and implementation support, contributes to capacity-building initiatives, mobilises technical expertise, and acts as a project integrator bringing together public expertise and private-sector know-how.

The **Lebanon-Jordan Country Direction**, established on 1 January 2025, provides the strategic and operational framework for managing Expertise France’s activities in both countries. Led by a Country Director based in Beirut, the Country Direction brings together approximately 70 staff members across Lebanon and Jordan. In Lebanon, the team includes around 30 staff members, including 4 project-based expatriates and 5 International Technical Experts (ITEs).

1. **PROJECT BACKDROUNG AND DESCRIPTION**

Lebanese citizens routinely face administrative procedures that lack transparency, traceability and predictability. Many services involve significant administrative discretion, weakly documented and hard to audit. This opacity feeds informal practices: reliance on intermediaries (wasta), informal payments, and access to information that depends on personal connections. The reliance on physical stamps and paper-based authentication further weakens the integrity of public documents, which can be falsified, lost or contested without effective recourse.

Lebanese public administrations face a severe capacity deficit, deepened by the prolonged economic crisis. The departure of qualified staff, the erosion of salaries and the limited renewal of the workforce have left many institutions structurally weakened. Internal processes are often outdated, training in digital tools and modern management is uneven, and change management capacity is limited. These administrations therefore need sustained external support to design, deploy and operate digital services that are genuinely user-centered and integrity-driven.

In this context, AI-assisted public services respond directly to the human resources constraint. By compensating for the shortage of qualified staff, taking over repetitive high-volume tasks, and improving the efficiency and responsiveness of service delivery, they free up administrative capacity for higher-value work while improving the citizen experience.

Digitalization has emerged as a strategic priority across government reform agendas. Efforts are underway to modernise public administration through the adoption of digital tools, the development of e-government platforms, and the introduction of more efficient and transparent service delivery mechanisms. Key areas of focus include the digitization of core administrative processes, the expansion of online public services, and the strengthening of digital infrastructure and connectivity across institutions.

Within this framework, the initiative led by the Office of the Minister of State for Information Technology and Artificial Intelligence (OMSITAI) plays a central role in advancing Lebanon’s digital transformation agenda. OMSITAI is actively supporting the development of national digital government priorities, promoting interoperability between public institutions, and guiding the rollout of key e-government services aimed at improving accessibility, efficiency, and transparency. OMSITAI has developed Lebanon’s Digital and AI Roadmap and identified a portfolio of priority e-services to be digitalised in pilot administrations.

Despite a vibrant technology sector in Beirut, the Lebanese GovTech ecosystem remains underleveraged in the public sector transformation agenda. Incubators, accelerators and start-ups hold strong technical skills and entrepreneurial energy, but their engagement with public administrations on service delivery is limited. Access to financing is constrained, particularly in the post-crisis context. As a result, opportunities to mobilise local capabilities for public services digitalisation are missed, and the ecosystem’s potential to anchor a sustainable transformation - including through viable, revenue-generating models - is not yet realised.

To address these challenges, the proposed action intends to support the deployment of user-centred digital public services designed to improve accessibility, transparency, and efficiency for citizens and businesses. Adopting a “quick wins” approach, the action prioritizes the digitalisation of high-impact services capable of delivering tangible benefits within a short timeframe, while demonstrating the value of digital transformation and building momentum for broader reforms.

Accordingly, a new EU Action, starting in September 2026 *(to be confirmed)* will be implemented to support anti-corruption efforts through processes' reforms and digitalisation of high-impact public services.

The Action is implemented by a consortium led by Expertise France, acting as the pillar-assessed entity and the e-Governance Academy (eGA) is the consortium partner responsible for leading the trust services component.

The action is structured around four complementary outputs, each led by one of the two consortium partners with cross-contributions where the complementarity of expertise adds operational value:

1. **Output 1 (EF lead).** Accessible, user-centered and integrity-enhancing digital public services developed and deployed.
2. **Output 2 (EF lead).** Pilot administrations' capacities strengthened for transparent and integrity-driven service delivery.
3. **Output 3 (eGA lead).** Cybersecurity frameworks, European trust services and integrity standards implemented for digital public services.
4. **Output 4 (EF lead).** Lebanese GovTech ecosystem strengthened and mobilised in support of public services digitalisation, towards the long-term financial sustainability of digitalised services.
5. **MISSION DESCRIPTION:**

For the implementation of the project, Expertise France is currently recruiting a Project Manager.

The Project Manager will be responsible for ensuring the effective implementation of the three project outputs under the responsibility of Expertise France. The Project Manager will report to the Governance Portfolio Manager and will work in close coordination with the e-Governance Academy (eGA) team to ensure alignment between the different components, maximize synergies, and support the overall successful implementation of the Action.

The Governance Portfolio Manager provides the strategic oversight of the action, ensuring its overall quality, coherence and alignment with Expertise France’s governance portfolio in Lebanon, particularly the Public Administration Reform (PAR) programme.

He/she will be responsible for the following tasks:

**3.1. Project Leadership and Management**

- Provide overall leadership, strategic guidance, and operational oversight for the successful implementation of the project.
- Ensure effective planning, coordination, implementation, and monitoring of project activities in line with the work plan, budget, contractual obligations, and expected results.
- Anticipate implementation challenges, identify risks and opportunities, monitor the political, institutional, and regulatory context, and recommend appropriate mitigation measures.
- Provide timely strategic alerts and recommendations to the Portfolio Manager on key risks, delays, or issues affecting project implementation.

**3.2. Technical Supervision, expert management and Quality Assurance**

- Provide technical leadership and supervision to the Project Officer, Long-Term Experts (LTEs), and Short-Term Experts (STEs).
- Lead the preparation of Terms of Reference for project experts, ensuring alignment with project objectives, contractual requirements, and expected results.
- Ensure effective coordination of experts’ contributions and alignment with project objectives.
- Guarantee the quality, relevance, consistency, and timely delivery of project outputs and key deliverables.
- Review, provide guidance on, and validate key technical documents, including work plans, reports, dashboards, and communication materials.
- Support, together with the Project Officer, the planning, coordination, and follow-up of expert missions to ensure their effective implementation and alignment with project objectives.

**3.3. Stakeholder Engagement and Partnership Coordination**

- Establish and maintain effective working relationships with project partners (eGA), beneficiaries, institutional stakeholders, civil society organisations, development partners, and other donor-funded initiatives.
- Facilitate coordination, dialogue, and synergies among stakeholders to maximize project impact and sustainability.
- Represent the project in strategic meetings, conferences, workshops, technical working groups, and other relevant forums.
- Support the Portfolio Manager in maintaining effective communication and coordination with the European Union representatives and relevant donor counterparts, including through the provision of timely updates on project progress, implementation challenges, and key risks.

**3.4. Project Planning, Monitoring, and Reporting**

- Under the supervision of the Governance Portfolio Manager, lead the coordination of internal project planning and operational management processes, including work planning, budget forecasts, project reviews, dashboards, and management reporting ; and the preparation, consolidation, quality assurance, and timely submission of donor reports in compliance with contractual requirements and Expertise France procedures.
- Coordinate with the MEAL Officer on the implementation of the Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) system and ensure regular analysis and reporting of project progress, results, risks, and challenges.
- Ensure that monitoring findings inform decision-making and support continuous improvement of project implementation.

1. **REQUIRED PROFILE**

**Qualifications and skills**

- Master’s degree or equivalent in international development, public administration, governance, political science, economics, project management, law, digital transformation, or a related discipline.
- Proven ability to coordinate a project with ambitious indicators
- Strong management skills
- Ability to work in a team and bring out ideas and operational solutions;
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills;
- Proactive, with a sense of responsibility;
- Organizational skills and attention to detail;
- Strong Institutional representation capacity;
- Demonstrated autonomy, flexibility, and responsiveness;
- Analytical mindset and ability to synthesize information;
- Proficiency in office tools (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.);
- Diplomatic and discreet approach;
- Demonstrated ability to work in a multicultural environment;
- Demonstrated ability to work in a complex context;
- Trilingual candidates (Arabic, English and French) are favored.

**Professional experience**

- Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in project management and/or international cooperation in the field of public reforms, the fight against corruption and digitalisation;
- Proven experience in leading and managing complex, multi-stakeholder projects, preferably in an international cooperation context.
- Proven experience working with Lebanese public institutions, including ministries, government agencies, and public administrations, and understanding of the institutional and regulatory environment in Lebanon.
- Demonstrated experience managing donor-funded projects in Lebanon or the wider Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, particularly projects involving public institutions and government counterparts.
- Demonstrated experience in governance, institutional strengthening, digital transformation, public sector reform, or related areas.
- Strong project management skills, deadline compliance, high quality of internal and external documents.

1. **ADDITIONAL INFORMATION**

The position is available from September 2026, contingent upon the signature of the project.

The Project Manager will be based in Beirut and will report directly to the Governance portfolio manager, based in Beirut.

Competitive package.

French:

1. **PRÉSENTATION DE L’AGENCE**

**Expertise France** est l’agence publique française chargée de la conception et de la mise en œuvre de projets de coopération technique internationale. L’agence intervient autour de quatre axes prioritaires :

- Gouvernance démocratique, économique et financière ;
- Paix, stabilité et sécurité ;
- Climat, agriculture et développement durable ;
- Santé et développement humain.

Dans ces domaines, Expertise France assure l’ingénierie de projets et l’appui à leur mise en œuvre, contribue aux initiatives de renforcement des capacités, mobilise une expertise technique et joue un rôle d’intégrateur de projets en associant expertise publique et savoir-faire du secteur privé.

La **Direction Pays Liban-Jordanie**, créée le 1er janvier 2025, constitue le cadre stratégique et opérationnel de gestion des activités d’Expertise France dans les deux pays. Dirigée par un(e) Directeur/Directrice Pays basé(e) à Beyrouth, la Direction rassemble environ 70 collaborateurs répartis entre le Liban et la Jordanie. Au Liban, l’équipe compte environ 30 collaborateurs, dont 4 expatriés sur projets et 5 Experts Techniques Internationaux (ETI).

1. **CONTEXTE ET DESCRIPTION DU PROJET**

Les citoyens libanais sont régulièrement confrontés à des procédures administratives manquant de transparence, de traçabilité et de prévisibilité. De nombreux services impliquent une marge de discrétion administrative importante, faiblement documentée et difficile à auditer. Cette opacité alimente des pratiques informelles : recours à des intermédiaires (wasta), paiements informels et accès à l’information dépendant de relations personnelles. Le recours aux tampons physiques et à l’authentification sur support papier fragilise en outre l’intégrité des documents publics, qui peuvent être falsifiés, perdus ou contestés sans recours efficace.

Les administrations publiques libanaises font face à un déficit de capacités sévère, aggravé par la crise économique prolongée. Le départ de personnel qualifié, l’érosion des salaires et le faible renouvellement des effectifs ont structurellement affaibli de nombreuses institutions. Les processus internes sont souvent obsolètes, la formation aux outils numériques et au management moderne est inégale, et la capacité de conduite du changement est limitée. Ces administrations ont donc besoin d’un appui externe soutenu pour concevoir, déployer et exploiter des services numériques réellement centrés sur l’usager et fondés sur l’intégrité.

Dans ce contexte, les services publics assistés par l’IA répondent directement à la contrainte de ressources humaines. En compensant le manque de personnel qualifié, en prenant en charge des tâches répétitives à fort volume et en améliorant l’efficacité et la réactivité de la prestation de services, ils libèrent de la capacité administrative pour des tâches à plus forte valeur ajoutée tout en améliorant l’expérience du citoyen.

La digitalisation s’est imposée comme une priorité stratégique dans l’ensemble des agendas de réforme gouvernementale. Des efforts sont en cours pour moderniser l’administration publique par l’adoption d’outils numériques, le développement de plateformes d’e-gouvernement et l’introduction de mécanismes de prestation de services plus efficaces et transparents. Les principaux axes de travail incluent la digitalisation des processus administratifs essentiels, l’extension des services publics en ligne et le renforcement de l’infrastructure et de la connectivité numériques entre les institutions.

Dans ce cadre, l’initiative portée par le Bureau du Ministre d’État chargé des Technologies de l’Information et de l’Intelligence Artificielle (OMSITAI) joue un rôle central dans l’avancement de l’agenda de transformation numérique du Liban. L’OMSITAI soutient activement l’élaboration des priorités nationales en matière de gouvernement numérique, promeut l’interopérabilité entre institutions publiques et guide le déploiement de services d’e-gouvernement clés visant à améliorer l’accessibilité, l’efficacité et la transparence. L’OMSITAI a élaboré la feuille de route numérique et IA du Liban et identifié un portefeuille de services numériques prioritaires à digitaliser au sein d’administrations pilotes.

Malgré un secteur technologique dynamique à Beyrouth, l’écosystème GovTech libanais demeure sous-exploité dans l’agenda de transformation du secteur public. Incubateurs, accélérateurs et start-up disposent de compétences techniques solides et d’une forte énergie entrepreneuriale, mais leur engagement auprès des administrations publiques sur la prestation de services reste limité. L’accès au financement est contraint, en particulier dans le contexte post-crise. Il en résulte que les opportunités de mobiliser les capacités locales pour la digitalisation des services publics sont manquées, et que le potentiel de l’écosystème à ancrer une transformation durable - y compris via des modèles viables et générateurs de revenus - n’est pas encore réalisé.

Pour répondre à ces enjeux, l’action proposée vise à soutenir le déploiement de services publics numériques centrés sur l’usager, conçus pour améliorer l’accessibilité, la transparence et l’efficacité pour les citoyens et les entreprises. Adoptant une approche de « gains rapides », l’action donne la priorité à la digitalisation de services à fort impact capables de produire des bénéfices tangibles dans un délai court, tout en démontrant la valeur de la transformation numérique et en créant une dynamique en faveur de réformes plus larges.

Ainsi, une nouvelle action de l’UE, débutant en septembre 2026 *(à confirmer)*, sera mise en œuvre pour soutenir les efforts de lutte contre la corruption à travers la réforme des processus et la digitalisation de services publics à fort impact.

L’action est mise en œuvre par un consortium mené par Expertise France, agissant en tant qu’entité pillar-assessed, l’e-Governance Academy (eGA) étant le partenaire du consortium chargé de la composante services de confiance.

L’action s’articule autour de quatre produits complémentaires, chacun piloté par l’un des deux partenaires du consortium, avec des contributions croisées lorsque la complémentarité des expertises apporte une valeur opérationnelle :

1. **Produit 1 (piloté par EF).** Des services publics numériques accessibles, centrés sur l’usager et renforçant l’intégrité sont développés et déployés.
2. **Produit 2 (piloté par EF).** Les capacités des administrations pilotes sont renforcées pour une prestation de services transparente et fondée sur l’intégrité.
3. **Produit 3 (piloté par l’eGA).** Des cadres de cybersécurité, des services de confiance européens et des normes d’intégrité sont mis en œuvre pour les services publics numériques.
4. **Produit 4 (piloté par EF).** L’écosystème GovTech libanais est renforcé et mobilisé à l’appui de la digitalisation des services publics, en vue de la pérennité financière à long terme des services digitalisés.
5. **DESCRIPTION DE LA MISSION :**

Pour la mise en œuvre du projet, Expertise France recrute actuellement un(e) Chef(fe) de Projet.

Le/la Chef(fe) de Projet sera responsable de la mise en œuvre effective des trois produits du projet placés sous la responsabilité d’Expertise France. Il/elle sera rattaché(e) au/à la Responsable de Portefeuille Gouvernance et travaillera en coordination étroite avec l’équipe de l’e-Governance Academy (eGA) afin d’assurer la cohérence entre les différentes composantes, de maximiser les synergies et de soutenir la réussite globale de la mise en œuvre de l’action.

Le/la Responsable de Portefeuille Gouvernance assure la supervision stratégique de l’action, en garantissant sa qualité globale, sa cohérence et son alignement avec le portefeuille gouvernance d’Expertise France au Liban, en particulier le programme d’Appui à la Réforme de l’Administration Publique (PAR).

Il/elle sera chargé(e) des tâches suivantes :

**3.1. Leadership et gestion de projet**

- Assurer le leadership global, l’orientation stratégique et la supervision opérationnelle pour la réussite de la mise en œuvre du projet.
- Assurer une planification, une coordination, une mise en œuvre et un suivi efficaces des activités du projet, conformément au plan de travail, au budget, aux obligations contractuelles et aux résultats attendus.
- Anticiper les difficultés de mise en œuvre, identifier les risques et opportunités, suivre le contexte politique, institutionnel et réglementaire, et recommander des mesures d’atténuation appropriées.
- Fournir en temps utile au/à la Responsable de Portefeuille des alertes stratégiques et des recommandations sur les risques majeurs, retards ou difficultés affectant la mise en œuvre du projet.

**3.2. Supervision technique, gestion des experts et assurance qualité**

- Assurer le leadership technique et la supervision du/de la Chargé(e) de Projet, des Experts Long Terme (ELT) et des Experts Court Terme (ECT).
- Piloter la préparation des termes de référence des experts du projet, en assurant leur cohérence avec les objectifs du projet, les exigences contractuelles et les résultats attendus.
- Assurer une coordination efficace des contributions des experts et leur alignement avec les objectifs du projet.
- Garantir la qualité, la pertinence, la cohérence et la livraison dans les délais des produits et livrables clés du projet.
- Revoir, orienter et valider les documents techniques clés, notamment les plans de travail, rapports, tableaux de bord et supports de communication.
- Appuyer, avec le/la Chargé(e) de Projet, la planification, la coordination et le suivi des missions d’experts afin d’en assurer la mise en œuvre effective et l’alignement avec les objectifs du projet.

**3.3. Engagement des parties prenantes et coordination des partenariats**

- Établir et entretenir des relations de travail efficaces avec les partenaires du projet (eGA), les bénéficiaires, les parties prenantes institutionnelles, les organisations de la société civile, les partenaires au développement et les autres initiatives financées par des bailleurs.
- Faciliter la coordination, le dialogue et les synergies entre les parties prenantes afin de maximiser l’impact et la pérennité du projet.
- Représenter le projet lors de réunions stratégiques, conférences, ateliers, groupes de travail techniques et autres forums pertinents.
- Appuyer le/la Responsable de Portefeuille dans le maintien d’une communication et d’une coordination efficaces avec les représentants de l’Union européenne et les autres bailleurs concernés, notamment par la transmission régulière et en temps utile d’informations sur l’avancement du projet, les difficultés de mise en œuvre et les risques majeurs.

**3.4. Planification, suivi et reporting du projet**

- Sous la supervision du/de la Responsable de Portefeuille Gouvernance, piloter la coordination de la planification interne du projet et des processus de gestion opérationnelle, notamment la planification du travail, les prévisions budgétaires, les revues de projet, les tableaux de bord et le reporting de gestion ; ainsi que la préparation, la consolidation, l’assurance qualité et la soumission dans les délais des rapports aux bailleurs, conformément aux exigences contractuelles et aux procédures d’Expertise France.
- Coordonner avec le/la Chargé(e) MEAL la mise en œuvre du système de Suivi, Évaluation, Redevabilité et Apprentissage (MEAL) et assurer l’analyse régulière et le reporting de l’avancement, des résultats, des risques et des difficultés du projet.
- Veiller à ce que les résultats du suivi éclairent la prise de décision et contribuent à l’amélioration continue de la mise en œuvre du projet.

1. **PROFIL RECHERCHÉ**

**Qualifications et compétences**

- Diplôme de master ou équivalent en développement international, administration publique, gouvernance, sciences politiques, économie, gestion de projet, droit, transformation numérique, ou discipline connexe.
- Capacité avérée à coordonner un projet doté d’indicateurs ambitieux
- Solides compétences en management
- Capacité à travailler en équipe et à faire émerger des idées et des solutions opérationnelles ;
- Excellentes compétences relationnelles et de communication ;
- Sens des responsabilités et esprit proactif ;
- Sens de l’organisation et souci du détail ;
- Solide capacité de représentation institutionnelle ;
- Autonomie, flexibilité et réactivité démontrées ;
- Esprit analytique et capacité de synthèse ;
- Maîtrise des outils bureautiques (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.) ;
- Approche diplomatique et discrétion ;
- Capacité démontrée à travailler dans un environnement multiculturel ;
- Capacité démontrée à travailler dans un contexte complexe ;
- La préférence est donnée aux candidats trilingues (arabe, anglais et français).

**Expérience professionnelle**

- Minimum de 10 ans d’expérience progressive en gestion de projet et/ou coopération internationale dans le domaine des réformes publiques, de la lutte contre la corruption et de la digitalisation ;
- Expérience avérée dans la direction et la gestion de projets complexes impliquant de multiples parties prenantes, de préférence dans un contexte de coopération internationale.
- Expérience avérée de travail avec les institutions publiques libanaises, notamment les ministères, agences gouvernementales et administrations publiques, et bonne compréhension de l’environnement institutionnel et réglementaire au Liban.
- Expérience démontrée dans la gestion de projets financés par des bailleurs au Liban ou dans la région Moyen-Orient et Afrique du Nord (MENA) au sens large, en particulier des projets impliquant des institutions publiques et des homologues gouvernementaux.
- Expérience démontrée en gouvernance, renforcement institutionnel, transformation numérique, réforme du secteur public, ou domaines connexes.
- Solides compétences en gestion de projet, respect des délais, documents internes et externes de haute qualité.

1. **INFORMATIONS COMPLÉMENTAIRES**

Le poste est disponible à partir de septembre 2026, sous réserve de la signature du projet.

Le/la Chef(fe) de Projet sera basé(e) à Beyrouth et rattaché(e) directement au/à la Responsable de Portefeuille Gouvernance, basé(e) à Beyrouth.
